## Psalm 55 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 55 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 55:1–23 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (v.8 backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The overwhelmed inner being — between *flight* and *casting*.** Psalm 55's findings: under a flood of dread the inner being's impulse is **escape** — "wings like a dove… I would fly away" (vv.4–8); the deepest wound is **betrayal by the intimate** who shared its confidential counsel (vv.12–14); the betrayer's **heart is at war behind smooth speech** (v.21); and the resolution is to **cast the burden** on God rather than flee ("he will sustain you," v.22). Two responses to being overwhelmed — *fly away* or *cast-and-be-held*.

## The reading

**I. The overwhelming, and the impulse to flee (vv.4–8).**
"My **heart** (H3820, the seat — M47) is in **anguish** (H2342, *chul*) within me; the **terrors** (H0367, M01, *emah*) of death have fallen upon me. **Fear** (H3374, M01) and **trembling** (H7461, M01, *raad*) come upon me, and **horror** (H6427, M01, *pallatsuth*) overwhelms me. And I say, 'Oh, that I had **wings like a dove**! I would **fly away** (H5774) and be at **rest** (H7931); I would **wander** (H5074, M18) far away… find a **shelter** from the raging wind'" (vv.4–8). The finding: a **fourfold flood of dread** (terrors, fear, trembling, horror — a dense M01 cluster) overwhelms the inner being *(stated)*, and its immediate impulse is **escape** — the wish for wings, to *fly away*, to *be elsewhere and at rest* *(stated)*. The operation: under extreme anguish the inner being **longs to flee its situation entirely** — an honest escape-fantasy, the desire to *not be here* *(inferred: the "oh, that I had wings… I would fly away" is the overwhelmed self's reflex toward flight)*.

**II. The deepest wound — betrayal by the intimate who shared the *sod* (vv.12–14).**
"For it is **not an enemy** who taunts me — then I could bear it… **But it is you**, a man **my equal**, **my companion** (H0441, *alluph*), my familiar friend. We used to take **sweet counsel** (H5475, M17, *sod*) together; within God's house we walked in the throng" (vv.12–14). The finding: the wound's depth is **the intimacy betrayed** — "an enemy I could bear, but *you*" *(stated)*. The gem: what was shared was the **sod** — the *confidential counsel*, the very word Ps 25:14 uses for the **friendship of the LORD** given to those who fear him *(stated)*. So the betrayal violated the **innermost circle of shared confidence** *(inferred: the sod is the intimate-confidence bond, here turned)*. The operation: **the depth of trust shared sets the depth of the wound when it turns** — betrayal by an *equal/companion* who held one's confidence cuts as an enemy's assault cannot (cf. Ps 41:9's bread-sharing friend) *(inferred)*.

**III. The war-heart behind smooth speech (v.21).**
"His speech was **smooth** (H2505, *chalaq* — the flatterer's verb, as in Ps 36:2) as butter, yet **war** (H7128) was in his **heart** (H3820, M47); his words were softer than oil, yet they were drawn swords" (v.21). The finding: the betrayer's **heart is at war while the mouth speaks peace** — smooth words masking the heart's true content *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being can be **divided against its own speech** — war within, butter without; the heart's real state (hostility) concealed by the tongue's oil (the concealing-speech mechanism of Ps 28:3, 50:19) *(inferred: the "smooth speech… yet war in his heart" names the split)*.

**IV. Casting the burden — the alternative to flight (v.22).**
"**Cast your burden** (H3053, *yehav* — your lot, what is given you) on the LORD, and **he will sustain** (H3557, *kul*) you; he will never permit the righteous to be **moved**" (v.22). The gem-resolution: against the earlier wish to **fly away** (vv.6–8), the inner being is told to **cast its burden on God**, who *sustains* *(stated)*. The finding — the psalm's key contrast: **the two responses to being overwhelmed are *escape* (fly away, vv.6–8) and *transfer* (cast the burden, be held, v.22)** — and the psalm moves from the flight-wish to the burden-casting *(inferred: v.22's "cast your burden… he will sustain" answers vv.6–8's "I would fly away")*. What the self cannot carry it **hands over** rather than **runs from** — and is *sustained* and *not moved* *(inferred)*. The close confirms the settled posture: "But I will **trust** in you" (v.23).

## What Psalm 55 says about the inner being
- **Under a flood of dread, the inner being's impulse is *flight* (vv.4–8).** A fourfold overwhelming (terrors, fear, trembling, horror) drives the honest wish to fly away, to be elsewhere and at rest — the reflex to *not be here*.
- **Betrayal by the intimate is the deepest wound (vv.12–14).** The depth of shared confidence — the *sod*, the same word for God's own friendship — sets the depth of the injury when it turns. An enemy could be borne; the equal-companion cannot.
- **The heart can be at war behind smooth speech (v.21).** The inner being divided against its own tongue — war within, butter without; the heart's true hostility concealed by the mouth's oil.
- **Casting the burden is the alternative to flight (v.22).** The two responses to being overwhelmed are *escape* and *transfer*; the inner being moves from the wish to fly away to casting its burden on God — what it cannot carry it hands over rather than runs from, and is sustained and not moved.

## Honest notes
- **"sweet counsel" (H5475, *sod*, v.14)** correctly M17 — and notably the **same word as Ps 25:14's "friendship of the LORD"**; the reading foregrounds that the betrayed bond was the *sod* (innermost confidence). A strong cross-psalm datum for the *sod* thread.
- **The M01 dread-cluster (vv.4–5)** — *emah*/*yirah*/*raad*/*pallatsuth* all M01 — is a good convergence for the fear cluster (the fourfold overwhelming as one operation).
- **"Cast your burden" (H3053, *yehav*) / "sustain" (H3557, *kul*)** captured gate-2; the transfer-vs-flight operation read from the pairing against vv.6–8. Candidate to note a *burden-casting* inner operation.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp at vv.1, 22; bearer=David/LORD bleed via superscription incl. the enemies' *strife* mis-assigned in vv.9–11; backfilled v.8 now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *give-ear* (H0238, M41, v.1); *hide* (H5956, M14, v.1); *heart* (H3820, M47, vv.4,21); *terrors/fear/trembling/horror* (H0367/H3374/H7461/H6427, M01, vv.4–5); *wander* (H5074, M18, v.7); *strife* (H7379, M02, v.9); *counsel/sod* (H5475, M17, v.14); *trust* (implied v.23).

## Psalm 56 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 56 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 56:1–13 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Trusting *while* afraid, and the tenderly-recorded grief.** Psalm 56's findings: the inner being **trusts *in* the fear, not after it** — "when I am afraid, I put my trust in you" (vv.3–4); its grief is **precisely counted and treasured** by God — tossings numbered, tears bottled, all booked (v.8); trust **re-sizes the threat** ("what can flesh do to me?", vv.4, 11); and the delivered soul's end is to **walk before God in the light of life** (v.13).

## The reading

**I. Trust performed *in* the fear (vv.3–4, 10–11).**
"When I am **afraid** (H3372, M01), I put my **trust** (H0982, M19) in you. In God… I **trust**; I shall **not be afraid**. What can **flesh** (H1320, seat=flesh — mortal weakness) do to me?" (vv.3–4; repeated vv.10–11). The gem-finding: the inner being **does not wait for the fear to pass before trusting — it trusts *when* afraid** *(stated: "when I am afraid, I put my trust in you")*. The operation, with its mechanism: **afraid → trust → not afraid** — trust is what the self *does with* the fear, and the doing dissolves the fear's grip *(inferred: the sequence runs from "when I am afraid, I trust" to "I shall not be afraid")*. Fear is the **occasion** for trust, not its obstacle; the two coexist and the trusting is the resolving act *(inferred)*.

**II. Trust re-sizes the threat (vv.4, 11).**
"What can **flesh** (H1320) do to me?… What can **man** do to me?" (vv.4, 11). The finding: the trusting inner being **re-measures its attackers** — they are mere *flesh* (basar, the word of mortal frailty) *(stated)*. The operation: trust **shrinks the threat to its true size** — what looked overwhelming (v.1, "man tramples on me all day long") is re-seen as *flesh*, unable to reach the self that trusts God *(inferred: the rhetorical "what can flesh do?" follows the trusting, re-sizing the same attackers of v.1)*.

**III. The tenderly-recorded grief — tossings counted, tears bottled (v.8).**
"You have kept **count** of my **tossings** (H5112, *nod* — restless turnings/wanderings); put my **tears** (H1832, M03, *dimah*) in your **bottle** (*nod* — a wordplay). Are they not in your **book** (H5612)?" (v.8). The gem-finding: the inner being's suffering is **not ignored but preciously recorded** — every sleepless *tossing* numbered, every *tear* stored in a bottle, all written in a book *(stated)*. The operation: the self's grief is **seen and treasured** by God with tender precision — the restless nights counted, the tears kept as something of value *(inferred: counting the tossings and bottling the tears makes the grief precious data, not overlooked pain)*. The Hebrew wordplay (*nod* = wandering / *nod* = skin-bottle) binds the two: **the wanderings counted, the tears kept in the wanderer's flask** *(inferred)*.

**IV. The delivered soul walks in the light of life (v.13).**
"For you have delivered my **soul** (H5315, the seat — M47) from **death**… my feet from falling, that I may **walk** before God in the **light of life** (H0216 + H2416)" (v.13). The finding: the deliverance's **end is not mere survival but a *walk before God in the light of life*** — the restored soul lives *in God's presence and light* *(stated)*. The operation: rescue is **for** relationship — the soul brought out of death to *walk before God*, in the light (the light-of-life, cf. Ps 36:9) *(inferred: the "delivered… that I may walk before God" makes the presence-walk the purpose of the rescue)*.

## What Psalm 56 says about the inner being
- **Trust is performed *in* the fear, not after it (vv.3–4).** "When I am afraid, I put my trust in you" — the inner being trusts *while* afraid; the trusting is what it does with the fear, and the doing dissolves the fear's grip. Fear is the occasion for trust, not its obstacle.
- **Trust re-sizes the threat (vv.4, 11).** The attackers who "trample all day long" are re-seen as mere *flesh* — trust shrinks the threat to its true size, unable to reach the God-trusting self.
- **Grief is precisely counted and treasured (v.8).** Every restless tossing numbered, every tear bottled, all booked — the inner being's suffering is seen and kept as something of value, not overlooked.
- **Rescue is *for* the presence-walk (v.13).** The soul delivered from death is delivered *to* walk before God in the light of life — survival's end is relationship, life in God's presence and light.

## Honest notes
- **The *nod* wordplay (v.8)** — *tossings/wandering* (H5112) and *bottle/skin* (H4997) — captured across gate-2 spans; the reading foregrounds the tender-recording operation (grief treasured) read from the counting/bottling/booking. A candidate for a "grief-seen-and-kept" inner-being datum.
- **"flesh" (H1320, *basar*, seat=flesh, vv.4)** correctly captured — read here as *mortal frailty* (the threat re-sized), the object trust shrinks; the same basar was the assaulted body in Ps 27:2.
- **The afraid/trust refrain** (vv.3–4, 10–11) is the psalm's spine — *yare* (M01) and *batach* (M19) paired twice; a clean datum for the fear→trust→not-afraid mechanism.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (heavy prohibition over-stamp across the "not afraid" refrain and v.8's questions; bearer=David/LORD bleed via the long superscription; "life" H2416 tagged M44 where M25 fits) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *afraid* (H3372, M01, vv.3,4,11); *trust* (H0982, M19, vv.3,4,11); *flesh* (H1320, M47, v.4); *tears* (H1832, M03, v.8); *soul/life* (H5315, M47, vv.6,13); *praise* (implied, "whose word I praise", vv.4,10).

## Psalm 57 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 57 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 57:1–11 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **From the bowed soul to the steadfast heart, and the self that rouses itself.** Psalm 57's findings: refuge as a **temporary sheltering "till the storm passes"** (v.1); the movement from a **soul bowed down** to a **heart *fixed* / steadfast** (vv.6–7); and the inner being **rousing *itself* to praise** — "awake, my glory!" (v.8), the positive mode of self-address.

## The reading

**I. Refuge as a sheltering *until* the storm passes (v.1).**
"For in you my **soul** (H5315, the seat — M47) **takes refuge** (H2620, M19, *chasah*); in the shadow of your **wings** I will take refuge, **till the storms of destruction pass by**" (v.1). The operation: the inner being **takes cover under the wings for the *duration* of the danger** — refuge here is explicitly **temporal**, a sheltering *until* the storm passes *(stated)*. The finding: refuge is not a permanent hiding but an **active waiting-out** — the soul lodges under the wings *through* the danger, expecting it to pass *(inferred: the "till the storms pass by" makes the refuge a bounded, waited-out shelter)*.

**II. From the bowed soul to the fixed heart (vv.6–7).**
"They set a net for my steps; my **soul** (H5315, M47) was **bowed down** (H3721, *kaphaph* — pressed low). They dug a pit… But now: **My heart** (H3820, the seat — M47) is **steadfast** (H3559, *kun*/*nakon* — fixed, established), O God, my heart is steadfast!" (vv.6–7). The gem-finding: the inner being moves from a **soul *pressed low*** (v.6) to a **heart *fixed and established*** (v.7) — and the affirmation is **doubled** for emphasis *(stated: "my heart is steadfast… my heart is steadfast")*. The operation: the same inner being **shifts from bowed to settled** — *nakon* names a heart that no longer wavers, a **fixed core** *(inferred: the bowed soul of v.6 and the fixed heart of v.7 are the one self, moved from pressed to established)*. And the fixity is the **ground of praise**: "my heart is steadfast… **I will sing and make melody**" — the settled heart *issues in* song *(stated)*.

**III. "Awake, my glory!" — the inner being rousing itself (v.8).**
"**Awake** (H5782, M25, *ur*), my **glory** (H3519, M22, *kabod* — here the inner self/soul, as Ps 30:12)! Awake, O harp and lyre! **I will awake the dawn**!" (v.8). The gem-operation: the inner being **commands *itself* to wake** — "awake, my glory" is self-address in the **positive mode**, the self *rousing* its own inner being to praise *(stated)*. The finding: where Ps 42's self-address *interrogated* a downcast soul, here the inner being **stirs itself to action** — waking its "glory" (the God-facing inner self) and even, in eagerness, **waking the dawn itself** rather than being woken by it *(inferred: "I will awake the dawn" reverses the usual order — the roused self outruns the morning)*. The steadfast heart (v.7) does not wait to feel like praising; it **rouses itself** *(inferred)*.

## What Psalm 57 says about the inner being
- **Refuge is a sheltering *until* the storm passes (v.1).** The inner being takes cover under the wings for the duration of the danger — an active waiting-out, not a permanent hiding; it expects the storm to pass.
- **The inner being can move from *bowed* to *fixed* (vv.6–7).** From a soul pressed low to a heart *steadfast* (*nakon*) — doubled — the same self shifting from pressed to settled; and the fixed heart is the ground from which song issues.
- **The inner being can rouse *itself* to praise (v.8).** "Awake, my glory!" — self-address in the positive mode; the steadfast heart stirs its own inner self to action rather than waiting to feel like it, outrunning even the dawn.

## Honest notes
- **Self-address, positive mode:** "awake, my glory" (v.8) pairs with Ps 42's "why are you cast down, O my soul" — the same dialogical structure (an "I" addressing its own inner being), here *rousing* rather than *interrogating*. A strong datum for the self-address/self-government operation (cf. Ps 42–43, 103's "bless the LORD, O my soul").
- **"steadfast" (H3559, *kun*, vv.7)** captured gate-2 standalone; the *fixed-heart* operation read from the doubled affirmation. The heart's *fixity* (nakon) is a recurring inner-state worth a characteristic (cf. Ps 51:10 "renew a *nakon* spirit", 112:7 "his heart is *nakon*, trusting").
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=Saul/LORD bleed via the long superscription; intensity *all*; the enemies' *lions/teeth/swords* v.4 are the external arena) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *soul* (H5315, M47, vv.1,4,6); *take-refuge* (H2620, M19, v.1); *steadfast-love* (H2617, M05, vv.3,10); *glory* (H3519, M22, vv.5,8,11 — v.8 = the inner self); *heart* (H3820, M47, v.7); *make-melody* (H2167, M42, v.7); *awake* (H5782, M25, v.8).

## Psalm 58 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 58 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 58:1–11 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (v.8 + others backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The wicked inner being — manufactured from origin, self-sealed against correction.** Psalm 58's findings: injustice is **devised in the *heart*** before the hands execute it (v.2); the wicked's disorder reaches to **origin** — estranged from the womb (v.3); and the inner being **makes itself *deaf*** — the adder stopping its own ear against the charmer (vv.4–5), the inverse of Ps 40's opened ear.

## The reading

**I. The heart is the workshop of injustice (v.2).**
"No, in your **hearts** (H3820, the seat — M47) you **devise** (H6466, *pa'al* — work, fabricate) **wrongs** (H5766, M10, *avel*); your hands deal out **violence** on earth" (v.2). The operation: injustice is **manufactured in the heart *first*** — the heart *works* the wrong, and only then do the hands *deal it out* *(stated: in the heart wrongs are devised; the hands dispense them)*. The finding: the **heart is the workshop** — the inner being fabricates the wrong inwardly before it becomes outward violence; the deed is the heart's output *(inferred: the "hearts devise… hands deal out" sequence makes the heart the origin, the hands the delivery)*.

**II. Disorder from the womb — corruption at origin (v.3).**
"The wicked are **estranged** (H2114, *zur* — made strange, alienated) from the **womb**; they **go astray** (H8582, *ta'ah*) from **birth**, speaking **lies**" (v.3). The finding: the wicked's disorder reaches **all the way to origin** — *estranged from the womb, astray from birth* *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's corruption is presented as **congenital, not merely acquired** — a strangeness present from the beginning *(inferred: "from the womb… from birth" locates the estrangement at origin)*. (The same depth Ps 51:5 owns of *itself* — "in sin conceived" — here diagnosed of the *wicked* from outside; the penitent's confession and the diagnosis meet at the origin-point.)

**III. The willful self-deafness — the adder that stops its own ear (vv.4–5).**
"They have **venom** (H2534, M02, *chemah* — the same word as *wrath*) like the venom of a serpent, like the **deaf** (H2795) **adder** that **stops its ear** (H0241), so that it does **not hear** the voice of **charmers**" (vv.4–5). Two findings. First, the venom is *chemah* — **the serpent's poison is *stored wrath*** (the M02 anger word): the inner being's malice is a treasured heat *(inferred: chemah names the venom as wrath, so the poison is the heart's stored anger)*. Second, the gem: the wicked inner being **makes itself deaf** — like an adder **stopping its own ear** against the charmer's voice *(stated)*. The operation: a **willful, self-induced deafness** — the inner being **actively closes the faculty of hearing** against what would correct or charm it *(inferred: the adder "stops its ear so that it does not hear" — a deliberate self-sealing)*. This is the exact inverse of Ps 40's **"dug/opened ear"** (God-given receptivity): here the ear is **self-stopped** — the refusal of instruction as an active operation *(inferred)*.

## What Psalm 58 says about the inner being
- **The heart is the workshop of injustice (v.2).** Wrongs are *devised* in the heart before the hands deal them out — the deed is the heart's manufactured output, not a first cause.
- **The wicked's disorder reaches to origin (v.3).** Estranged from the womb, astray from birth — corruption presented as congenital, not merely acquired. (The penitent owns this of himself in Ps 51:5; here it is diagnosed of the wicked.)
- **The inner being can make itself *deaf* (vv.4–5).** Like an adder stopping its own ear against the charmer, the wicked self *actively closes* the faculty of hearing against correction — a willful self-deafening, the inverse of Ps 40's opened ear.
- **Malice is *stored wrath* (v.4).** The venom is *chemah* — the poison the inner being carries is treasured heat/anger.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** the imprecation (vv.6–9) and the righteous' response to vindication (vv.10–11) are the arena; the inner-being weight is the wicked's *manufacture* and *self-sealing* (vv.2–5).
- **"venom" = *chemah* (H2534, M02)** correctly a characteristic in the *anger* cluster — the reading foregrounds the venom-as-stored-wrath link (a good M02 datum: malice as treasured heat, cf. Ps 37's self-kindling fire).
- **"stops its ear" (H0241, v.4)** captured via gate-2 *deaf/ear* spans; the self-deafening operation read from the adder image — a clean inverse of Ps 40:6's dug ear. Candidate to note a *self-stopped ear* inner mechanism.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=David/LORD bleed via superscription; *estranged/astray/devise* gate-2 verbs; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *right/judge* (H6664/H8199, M26, v.1); *hearts* (H3820, M47, v.2); *wrongs* (H5766, M10, v.2); *venom* (H2534, M02, v.4). *estranged/astray/lies* (H2114/H8582/H3577) captured gate-2 — the origin-corruption read from these.

## Psalm 59 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 59 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 59:1–17 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (v.15 + others backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **God as the self's *own* strength — watched-for and sung-to.** A deliverance psalm (the howling-dog enemies are the arena); its inner-being findings: the self **watches for God** as its fortress (v.9); it names God as **"my Strength"** — its strength located outside itself (vv.9, 17); and its **morning-song** stands against the enemies' never-filled **evening-prowl** (vv.6, 14–16).

## The reading

**I. "I will watch for you" — vigilant Godward expectancy (v.9).**
"O my **Strength** (H5797, M23, *oz*), I will **watch** (H8104, M30, *shamar* — keep watch, guard) for you, for you, O God, are my **fortress**" (v.9). The operation: the inner being **keeps watch *for* God** — a vigilant, expectant waiting *(stated)*. The finding is sharpened by the superscription's inversion: Saul's men *watch* (*shamar*) the house *to kill* (v.1), while the psalmist *watches* (*shamar*) *for God* to deliver — **the same watching-faculty turned Godward** *(inferred: the enemy's lethal watching and the psalmist's expectant watching are the same verb, oppositely aimed)*.

**II. "O my Strength" — the self's strength located in God (vv.9, 17).**
The refrain names God as the inner being's **own strength** — "*my* Strength" — twice (vv.9, 17) *(stated)*. The finding: the self's strength is **not intrinsic but relocated** — its *oz* is God, its fortress is God *(inferred: "*my* Strength… *my* fortress" places the self's power outside itself, in God)*. The inner being draws its stability from a source it does not generate (cf. Ps 46:1's "refuge and strength").

**III. The morning-song against the evening-prowl (vv.6, 14–16).**
Twice: "Each **evening** they come back, **howling like dogs** and prowling about the city… They **wander about** for food and **growl if they do not get their fill**" (vv.6, 14–15). Against this: "But I will **sing** of your **strength**; I will **sing aloud** (H7442, M42) of your **steadfast love** (H2617, M05) **in the morning**" (v.16). The gem-finding: two **temporal rhythms of the inner being** — the wicked's **restless, never-satisfied *evening* prowling** (they *growl* when not filled), versus the psalmist's **satisfied *morning* song** *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's disposition **shows in its rhythm** — the God-strengthened self *sings at dawn* (settled, satisfied), while the God-less self *prowls at dusk* (restless, unfilled) *(inferred: the evening-howl and the morning-song mark the two inner states by their hour)*.

## What Psalm 59 says about the inner being
- **The self *watches for* God with vigilant expectancy (v.9).** The same watching-faculty the enemies aim lethally, the psalmist turns Godward — expectant waiting for the fortress.
- **The self's strength is located in God (vv.9, 17).** "O my Strength" — the inner being's power is not intrinsic but relocated; it draws stability from a source it does not generate.
- **Disposition shows in the inner being's *rhythm* (vv.6, 14–16).** The wicked prowl and growl at evening, never filled; the God-strengthened self sings at morning, satisfied. The hour reveals the state.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** the howling-dog enemies (vv.6–7, 14–15), the imprecation (vv.11–13), and God's derision (v.8) are the arena; the inner-being weight is the watching, the located strength, and the morning-song (vv.9, 16–17).
- **"watch" (H8104, *shamar*, v.9)** correctly M30 — the reading foregrounds the *watching-for-God* sense and its inversion of the enemies' lethal watching (superscription). A clean datum for the watch/wait family.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=Saul/LORD bleed via the long superscription; intensity *all*; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *watch* (H8104, M30, v.9); *strength* (H5797, M23, vv.9,16,17); *steadfast-love* (H2617, M05, vv.10,16,17); *sing-aloud* (H7442, M42, v.16); *distress* (H6887, M24, v.16).

## Psalm 60 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 60 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 60:1–12 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (v.8 backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The staggering self, and confidence relocated from man to God.** A national lament (the territorial oracle, vv.6–9, is the arena). Two inner-being findings: the self **disoriented — reeling as from wine** under judgment (v.3); and the recognition that **human help is *vain***, valour itself relocated to God (vv.11–12).

## The reading

**I. The staggering inner being under judgment (v.3).**
"You have made your people see hard things; you have given us **wine to drink that made us stagger** (H8653, *tar'elah* — reeling)" (v.3). The operation: the inner being is **destabilised** — made to *reel*, as if drunk *(stated)*. The finding: under judgment the self loses its footing inwardly — a **disorientation, a loss of steadiness**, the ground no longer firm beneath it *(inferred: the reeling-from-wine image names an inner unsteadiness, not merely an outward defeat)*.

**II. "Vain is the salvation of man" — valour relocated to God (vv.11–12).**
"Oh, grant us **help** against the foe, for **vain** (H7723, *shav* — empty) is the **salvation of man**! **With God** we shall do **valiantly** (H2428, M23, *chayil*); it is he who will tread down our foes" (vv.11–12). The gem-finding: the inner being recognises **human help as *empty*** — *shav*, vain — and relocates its confidence to God *(stated)*. The operation: even **valour is relocated** — "**with** God we shall do valiantly": the self's strength-in-action is *not its own* but done *with* God *(inferred: the "vain is the salvation of man… with God we do valiantly" moves the source of both help and valour from man to God)*. The staggering self (v.3) finds its footing not by recovering its own strength but by lodging its confidence outside itself *(inferred; cf. the confidence-placement thread, Ps 20:7, 33:16, 44:6)*.

## What Psalm 60 says about the inner being
- **Judgment destabilises the inner being (v.3).** The self is made to *reel* — a loss of inner footing, the ground no longer firm; disorientation, not merely defeat.
- **Human help is recognised as *vain*, and valour relocated to God (vv.11–12).** The inner being learns its own and human resources are empty (*shav*), and that even its valour is done *with* God — confidence lodged outside itself. The reeling self finds footing not by recovering its own strength but by relocating its trust.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** the territorial oracle (vv.6–9, God portioning Shechem/Moab/Edom) and the corporate defeat (vv.1–2, 10) are the arena; the inner-being weight is the staggering (v.3) and the vain-help/relocated-valour (vv.11–12). Thin psalm, noted plainly.
- **"stagger" (H8653, *tar'elah*, v.3)** captured gate-2 standalone; the inner-disorientation read from the reeling image. Candidate for a *destabilised/reeling* inner-state datum.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer bleed severe via the very long superscription — Edom/Salt mis-assigned; prohibition at v.10; backfilled v.8 now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *fear* (H3373, M01, v.4); *valiantly* (H2428, M23, v.12). *stagger* (H8653) and *vain* (H7723, *shav*) captured gate-2 — the disorientation and the vain-help read from these.

## Psalm 61 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 61 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 61:1–8 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (v.6 backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The faint heart reaching for a ground higher than itself.** Psalm 61's finding: when the inner being is **overwhelmed**, it seeks a refuge that **exceeds its own reach** — "lead me to the rock that is *higher than I*" (v.2) — a ground it cannot attain alone but must be *led* to; and it longs to **dwell** sheltered under the wings (v.4).

## The reading

**I. The faint heart and the rock *higher than I* (v.2).**
"From the end of the earth I call to you when my **heart** (H3820, the seat — M47) is **faint** (H5848, *ataph* — overwhelmed, enveloped). **Lead me to the rock that is higher than I**" (v.2). The gem-finding: the **overwhelmed** inner being seeks a ground **above its own reach** — a rock *higher than itself* *(stated)*. The operation: the faint self recognises it needs a refuge that **exceeds its own capacity** — not a foothold it can climb to but one it must be **led** to, higher than it can attain alone *(inferred: "the rock that is higher than I… lead me" makes the refuge beyond the self's own reach, requiring guidance to it)*. The finding is precise: the inner being at the *end of its own resources* ("the end of the earth", "my heart is faint") reaches **upward and beyond itself**, not inward *(inferred)*.

**II. The longing to dwell, sheltered under the wings (vv.3–4).**
"For you have been my **refuge** (H4268, M19, *machseh*), a strong tower… Let me **dwell** in your **tent forever**! Let me **take refuge** (H2620, M19, *chasah*) under the shelter of your **wings**" (vv.3–4). The finding: the inner being's refuge-longing is for a **permanent dwelling** — not a passing shelter but "your tent *forever*", under the *wings* *(stated)*. The operation: the faint self, having reached for the higher rock, wants to **stay** there — its desire is not merely rescue but *abiding* in the refuge *(inferred: "dwell… forever" makes the longing a permanent home, not a momentary cover; cf. Ps 23:6, 27:4)*.

## What Psalm 61 says about the inner being
- **The overwhelmed self reaches for a ground *higher than itself* (v.2).** The faint heart seeks a refuge that exceeds its own reach — a rock "higher than I," which it must be *led* to, not climb to. At the end of its own resources, the inner being reaches upward and beyond itself, not inward.
- **Its refuge-longing is to *dwell*, not merely to shelter (vv.3–4).** The inner being wants to *abide* in the refuge — "your tent forever," under the wings — a permanent home, not a passing cover.

## Honest notes
- **"the rock that is higher than I" (v.2)** captured via gate-2 spans (*rock*/*higher*); the finding — a refuge *exceeding the self's own reach* — read from the phrase. A clean datum: the inner being's ground is *above* itself, attained by being led, not by self-effort. Candidate for a distinct inner-being operation (refuge-beyond-the-self).
- **"faint" (H5848, *ataph*, v.2)** captured gate-2 standalone; the overwhelmed-heart state read from the verb (enveloped/fainting). Pairs with the *heart* (M47) span.
- **Scope honesty:** the royal petition (vv.6–7) is a distinct movement (for the king); the inner-being weight is vv.2–4 (the faint heart, the higher rock, the dwelling).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer bleed via superscription; backfilled v.6 now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *heart* (H3820, M47, v.2); *refuge/take-refuge* (H4268/H2620, M19, vv.3,4); *fear* (H3373, M01, v.5).

## Psalm 62 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 62 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 62:1–12 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (v.3 backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The soul's silent, exclusive waiting — held with outpouring and non-attachment.** Psalm 62's findings: the inner being's posture is a **silent, exclusive waiting for God *alone*** — and the self **commands itself** into that silence (vv.1, 5); alongside the silence, it **pours out its heart** before God (v.8); and it **governs where the heart attaches** — "set not your heart" on riches (v.10). The through-line is an **exclusive orientation** ("God alone / he only") maintained by silence, outpouring, and non-attachment.

## The reading

**I. The soul waits in silence for God *alone* — and commands itself to (vv.1, 5).**
"For God **alone** (*ak* — only) my **soul** (H5315, the seat — M47) **waits in silence** (H1747, *dumiyah*)… For God alone, **O my soul, wait in silence** (H1826, M33, *damam*), for my **hope** (H8615, M18) is from him" (vv.1, 5). Two findings. First, the inner being's posture is a **silent, exclusive waiting** — the *silence* here is **positive** (unlike Ps 32's guilty silence or Ps 28's dreaded divine silence): the soul's **quiet stillness** before God *(stated)*. Second, the self-government: v.5 turns to **self-address** — "*O my soul*, wait in silence" — the inner being **commands *itself*** into the stillness *(stated: the "I" tells "my soul" to be silent, cf. Ps 42, 57)*. The operation: the soul **silences itself and waits, exclusively** ("God *alone*"), and it can *direct itself* into that posture *(inferred: the repeated *ak* fixes the object as God only, and v.5's imperative makes the silence self-willed)*.

**II. Pour out the heart — outpouring held with the silence (v.8).**
"**Trust** (H0982, M19) in him at all times, O people; **pour out your heart** (H3824, the seat — M47) before him; God is a **refuge** (H4268, M19)" (v.8). The finding: alongside the *silent waiting*, the inner being **pours itself out** before God (*shaphak*-heart, cf. Ps 42:4) *(stated)*. The operation: silence and outpouring **coexist** — the soul is *quiet* toward the world's clamour (vv.3–4) yet *empties its heart* toward God; the stillness is not emptiness but an **exclusive channelling** — all the heart's content directed to the one object *(inferred: the silent-before-all yet pour-out-to-God pairing makes the silence a *focusing*, not a muteness)*.

**III. Governing the heart's attachment (v.10).**
"Put no **trust** in extortion… if **riches** (H2428, M23) increase, **set not your heart** (H3820, M47) on them" (v.10). The finding: the inner being's heart **can attach itself to things** — and the command is **not to fix it on wealth** *(stated)*. The operation: the heart has an **attachment-faculty** that must be *governed* — "set not your heart" — kept from lodging on riches, so it stays free for its exclusive object (God alone) *(inferred: the "set not your heart on them" governs where the heart's weight settles, guarding the exclusivity of vv.1–7)*.

**IV. The split blessers and the weightless self-estimate (vv.4, 9).**
Two supporting findings. The enemies "**bless with their mouths, but inwardly they curse**" (v.4) — the concealing split, outward blessing / inward cursing (cf. Ps 28:3, 55:21) *(stated)*. And the right-sizing: "those of low estate are but a **breath**; those of high estate a **delusion**… in the balances they go up; together lighter than a breath" (v.9) — man **weighed and found weightless** *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being **re-sizes human importance** as *breath* (*hevel*, cf. Ps 39), which is *why* the heart is not to be set on riches or high position — they weigh nothing *(inferred: the weightlessness of v.9 grounds the non-attachment of v.10)*.

## What Psalm 62 says about the inner being
- **The soul's posture is *silent, exclusive* waiting (vv.1, 5).** A positive silence — quiet stillness before God *alone* — and the inner being can *command itself* into it ("O my soul, wait in silence").
- **Silence and outpouring coexist (v.8).** The soul is quiet toward the world's clamour yet *pours out its heart* to God — the stillness is a *focusing*, an exclusive channelling of the heart's content to one object, not a muteness.
- **The heart's *attachment* must be governed (v.10).** The heart can fix itself on things; "set not your heart on riches" keeps it free for its exclusive object. The attachment-faculty is directed, not left to settle where it will.
- **Re-sizing man as *breath* grounds the non-attachment (v.9).** Human estate weighed is weightless — which is *why* the heart is not set on it.

## Honest notes
- **Two silence words:** *dumiyah* (H1747, v.1) and *damam* (H1826, M33, v.5) — both the *positive* stillness-before-God; a clean datum distinguishing this from the guilty silence (Ps 32) and the dreaded divine silence (Ps 28). Self-commanded in v.5 (self-government, cf. Ps 42, 57).
- **"pour out your heart" (v.8)** and **"set not your heart" (v.10)** are the two heart-operations; the outpouring captured via *heart* (H3824) + gate-2 *shaphak*, the attachment via *heart* (H3820) + gate-2 *sim*. Both read from the phrases.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=David/LORD bleed via superscription; prohibition at vv.6, 10; backfilled v.3 now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *soul* (H5315, M47, vv.1,5); *silence* (H1826, M33, v.5); *hope* (H8615, M18, v.5); *refuge* (H4268, M19, vv.7,8); *heart* (H3824/H3820, M47, vv.8,10); *trust* (H0982, M19, vv.8,10); *riches* (H2428, M23, v.10); *steadfast-love* (H2617, M05, v.12).

## Psalm 63 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 63 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 63:1–11 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **From whole-being thirst to satisfaction to clinging.** Psalm 63 traces a **trajectory of the inner being toward God**: a **total, bodily thirst** (soul *and* flesh, v.1); the **re-valuation of God's love above life itself** (v.3); the thirst resolving into **satisfaction** as at a rich feast (v.5); **night-meditation** on the bed (v.6); and the soul **clinging/cleaving** to God (v.8). The movement runs *craving → filling → adhering*.

## The reading

**I. The whole-being thirst — soul *and* flesh (v.1).**
"O God, you are my God; earnestly I **seek** (H7836, *shachar* — seek at dawn) you; my **soul** (H5315, the seat — M47) **thirsts** (H6770) for you; my **flesh** (H1320, seat=flesh, *basar*) **faints** (H3642) for you, as in a **dry and weary land where there is no water**" (v.1). The finding: the desire for God engages the **whole person** — not the soul alone but the **flesh faints** too *(stated)*. The operation: the craving is a **total, bodily thirst** — the entire self, soul and body, is the *desert-thirst*, a survival-appetite in a waterless land *(inferred: the soul *thirsts* and the flesh *faints* — the whole organism craves as a body deprived of water; cf. Ps 42's deer-panting)*.

**II. Steadfast love valued *above life* (v.3).**
"Because your **steadfast love** (H2617, M05) is **better than life** (H2416, M25), my lips will praise you" (v.3). The gem-finding: the inner being holds God's *chesed* as **more valuable than life itself** — the most basic good is *outranked* *(stated)*. The operation: a **re-ordering of the value-hierarchy** — the inner being can esteem *something above its own life*, and here that something is God's steadfast love *(inferred: "better than life" is a supreme re-valuation, placing chesed at the top of the self's value-order)*.

**III. Thirst resolves into satisfaction (vv.4–5).**
"So I will **bless** you as long as I live; in your name I will **lift up my hands**. My **soul** (H5315, M47) will be **satisfied** (H7646, *saba*) as with **fat and rich food**, and my mouth will praise you with joyful lips" (vv.4–5). The gem-finding: the *thirst/faint* of v.1 **resolves into fullness** — the soul **fed and satisfied** as at a rich feast *(stated)*. The operation: the movement is **craving → filling** — the inner being's appetite, having sought God, is **met and filled to satisfaction** *(inferred: the same soul that *thirsts* in v.1 is *satisfied as with fat* in v.5 — the desert-thirst answered by a feast)*. (Contrast the never-filled prowling of Ps 59:15 — there the appetite growls unmet; here it is filled.)

**IV. Night-meditation on the bed (v.6).**
"When I **remember** (H2142, M41) you upon my **bed**, and **meditate** (H1897, M42, *hagah*) on you in the **watches of the night**" (v.6). The finding: the **bed and the night-watches are the place of God-ward meditation** — the inner being *remembers* and *ponders* God through the sleepless hours *(stated)*. The operation: night-meditation as a **God-ward** act (*hagah* on God) — the same bed that is the wicked's *plotting*-workshop (Ps 36:4) is here the **place of remembering God** *(inferred: the bed/night, elsewhere the workshop of evil devising, is turned to God-ward meditation; cf. Ps 16:7's night-instructed heart)*.

**V. The soul *clings* to God (vv.7–8).**
"For you have been my help, and in the shadow of your **wings** I will sing for joy. My **soul** (H5315, M47) **clings** (H1692, *dabaq* — cleaves, adheres) to you; your right hand **upholds** (H8551, *tamak*) me" (vv.7–8). The gem-finding: the trajectory ends in **cleaving** — the soul *dabaq* to God, the same verb for a man cleaving to his wife (Gen 2:24) *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being **adheres/clings** to God — an active *holding-fast* — and it is **mutual**: the soul clings *while* God's hand *upholds* *(inferred: "my soul clings… your right hand upholds" pairs the self's cleaving with God's sustaining — the clinging is held from the other side)*. The craving (v.1), once satisfied (v.5), becomes **attachment** (v.8) *(inferred)*.

## What Psalm 63 says about the inner being
- **Desire for God is a *whole-being*, bodily thirst (v.1).** Soul *and* flesh crave — the entire self is the desert-thirst, a survival-appetite in a waterless land.
- **God's love can be valued *above life itself* (v.3).** The inner being re-orders its value-hierarchy, placing *chesed* over its own most basic good — the supreme re-valuation.
- **Thirst resolves into *satisfaction* (v.5).** The craving, having sought God, is met and filled as at a rich feast — the soul satisfied "as with fat." (Contrast the never-filled appetite of the God-less, Ps 59:15.)
- **The bed and night are turned to God-ward meditation (v.6).** The inner being *remembers* and *ponders* God through the sleepless watches — the same place that is the wicked's plotting-workshop is here the place of remembering God.
- **The trajectory ends in *clinging* (v.8).** The soul *cleaves* (*dabaq*) to God — an active holding-fast — and it is mutual: the soul clings *while* God's hand upholds. Craving → filling → adhering.

## Honest notes
- **The trajectory** (thirst v.1 → behold v.2 → chesed>life v.3 → satisfied v.5 → meditate v.6 → cling v.8) is the psalm's spine; a strong worked example of the inner being's *movement* toward God (the process the study seeks). Worth marking as an exemplar of a multi-stage inner operation.
- **"clings" (H1692, *dabaq*, v.8)** captured gate-2 standalone; the soul-cleaving operation read from the verb (the Gen 2:24 cleaving-word). Candidate for a *cleaving/adhering* inner-being characteristic (a distinct attachment mode from *chasah* refuge or *batach* trust).
- **"flesh faints" (H1320 basar + H3642, v.1)** — the *whole-being* thirst read from soul+flesh in parallel; basar correctly seat=flesh. A clean datum: desire engaging the body, not the soul alone.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=Judah/LORD bleed via superscription; *seek/satisfied/clings/upholds* gate-2 verbs) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *soul* (H5315, M47, vv.1,5,8); *steadfast-love* (H2617, M05, v.3); *life* (H2416, M25, v.3); *remember* (H2142, M41, v.6); *meditate* (H1897, M42, v.6); *seek* (H1245, M41, v.9). *thirsts/flesh/faints/satisfied/clings* captured gate-2 — the thirst→satisfaction→clinging trajectory read from these.

## Psalm 64 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 64 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 64:1–10 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (v.7 backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The depth of the heart as a hiding-place — trusted as unsearchable, but reached.** Psalm 64's findings: "**the inward mind and heart of a man are deep**" (v.6) — the inner being's unfathomable interior, here the **hiding-place of schemes** the wicked trust to conceal them ("who can see them?"); their **holding fast to an evil purpose** (v.5); and the arrow that **reaches even the deep heart** (v.7).

## The reading

**I. The heart's *depth* as a hiding-place (vv.5–6).**
"They **hold fast** to their evil purpose; they talk of laying snares secretly, thinking, '**Who can see them?**' They search out injustice… For the inward mind and **heart** (H3820, the seat — M47) of a man are **deep** (H6013, *amoq*)" (vv.5–6). The gem-finding: the inner being has **depth** — the "inward part and heart" of a man is an **unfathomable interior** *(stated)*. The operation, in the wicked's use: they **trust that depth to conceal their schemes** — the heart is deep enough that "who can see them?" *(stated: they scheme secretly, thinking themselves unseen, *because* the heart is deep)*. The finding: the heart's depth is a **real hiddenness** — a place where plots (or anything) can be lodged out of sight of others; the wicked **bank on its unsearchability** *(inferred: "who can see them?… the heart is deep" makes the depth the ground of their confidence in concealment)*.

**II. Holding fast to an evil purpose (v.5).**
"They **hold fast** (H2388, M23, *chazaq* — strengthen themselves) to their evil purpose" (v.5). The finding: the inner being can **fortify itself in a resolve** — *chazaq*, strengthening its grip on a purpose (here evil) *(stated)*. The operation: a **self-hardening commitment** — the will *strengthening itself* around its chosen aim, making the purpose firm and held-fast *(inferred: chazaq is the self-strengthening in the resolve, the inner being consolidating its intent)*.

**III. The secret *counsel* turned conspiratorial (v.2).**
"Hide me from the **secret plots** (H5475, M17, *sod*) of the wicked" (v.2). The finding: the *sod* — the word for **intimate, confidential counsel** (God's friendship, Ps 25:14; the betrayer's shared counsel, Ps 55:14) — is here the wicked's **conspiratorial inner circle** *(stated)*. The operation: the same faculty of *confidential fellowship* can be **godly or conspiratorial** by its content — the sod's range spans God's confidence and the plotters' huddle *(inferred: sod is the shared-secret bond, its valence set by whom it binds and for what)*.

**IV. The arrow that reaches the deep heart (v.7).**
"But God **shoots his arrow** at them; they are **wounded suddenly**" (v.7). The finding: the depth the wicked trusted as unsearchable is **not beyond God's reach** — God's arrow finds them *(stated)*. The operation: the heart's hiddenness is real to *men* but **not to God** — the deep interior that concealed the schemes is **penetrated** *(inferred: the "who can see them?" of v.5 is answered by God's arrow in v.7 — the depth hides from man, not from God; cf. Ps 44:21's "secrets of the heart", 7:9's heart-testing)*.

## What Psalm 64 says about the inner being
- **The heart is *deep* — an unfathomable interior (v.6).** "The inward mind and heart of a man are deep" — a real hiddenness, a place where plots (or anything) can be lodged out of others' sight.
- **The wicked *trust* the heart's depth to conceal them (vv.5–6).** They scheme secretly, "who can see them?", banking on the interior's unsearchability — the depth is the ground of their confidence in hiding.
- **The inner being can *hold fast* to a purpose (v.5).** *Chazaq* — the will strengthening its grip, self-hardening around its aim; here around evil.
- **Confidential counsel (*sod*) is valenced by its content (v.2).** The same intimate-fellowship faculty is God's friendship (25:14) or the plotters' huddle (here) — the bond's worth is set by whom it binds and for what.
- **The deep heart is hidden from *men*, not from God (v.7).** The depth trusted as unsearchable is penetrated by God's arrow — the interior that hides schemes from others is open to God.

## Honest notes
- **"deep" (H6013, *amoq*, v.6)** captured gate-2 standalone; the heart's-depth finding read from "the inward mind and heart of a man are deep." A strong datum for the inner being's *unfathomability* (with the God-still-searches counter). Candidate for a *heart-depth* characteristic.
- **"secret plots" (H5475, *sod*, v.2)** correctly M17 — the reading foregrounds the *sod* range (godly confidence ↔ conspiratorial plot), a good cross-psalm datum (25:14, 55:14, here).
- **Scope honesty:** God's counter-action (vv.7–8), the resulting awe (v.9), and the righteous' response (v.10) are the arena; the inner-being weight is the deep heart, the held-fast purpose, and the sod (vv.2, 5–6).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed; the tongue-arrow recoil v.8 is the external pole; backfilled v.7 now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *secret-plots/sod* (H5475, M17, v.2); *hold-fast* (H2388, M23, v.5); *heart* (H3820, M47, vv.6,10); *righteous/upright* (H6662/H3477, M26/M13, v.10). *deep* (H6013) captured gate-2 — the heart-depth read from it.

## Psalm 65 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 65 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 65:1–13 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (v.13 backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Iniquities that overpower, answered by atonement; the chosen self brought near.** A thanksgiving/creation psalm (the provision of the earth, vv.5–13, is the arena). Its inner-being findings: **praise as a silent waiting** (v.1); **iniquities that *overpower* the self**, covered by God's atonement (v.3); and the **chosen self brought *near* and *satisfied*** (v.4).

## The reading

**I. Praise as a silent waiting (v.1).**
"**Praise** (H8416, M22) is **due** (H1747, *dumiyah* — silence, silent waiting) to you, O God, in Zion" (v.1). The finding: praise here is a **poised, silent readiness** — *dumiyah*, the same silence-word as Ps 62:1's waiting soul *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's praise **waits in stillness** for God — a readiness held in silence before it sounds *(inferred: dumiyah frames the praise as a waiting quiet, not yet noise)*.

**II. Iniquities *overpower* the self — answered by atonement (v.3).**
"When **iniquities prevail** (H1396, M23, *gabar* — overpower, are too strong) against me, you **atone** (H3722, M38, *kaphar* — cover) for our **transgressions** (H6588, M10)" (v.3). The gem-finding: the inner being's iniquities can be **stronger than the self can master** — they *prevail*, *overpower* *(stated)*. And the resolution comes **from outside**: God *atones/covers* *(stated)*. The operation: sin as **more than the inner being can handle** → **God's atonement**, not the self's effort *(inferred: "iniquities *prevail* against me… *you* atone" places the mastery of sin beyond the self and in God)*. The self does not overcome its own overwhelming iniquity; it is *covered* *(inferred; cf. Ps 40:12 "iniquities overtook me", 38's crushing weight — here the resolution named as atonement)*.

**III. The chosen self brought *near*, and satisfied (v.4).**
"**Blessed** is the one you **choose** (H0977, M37, *bachar*) and **bring near** (H7126, *qarab*), to **dwell** in your courts! We shall be **satisfied** (H7646, *saba*) with the goodness of your house" (v.4). The finding: the inner being's blessedness is a **three-fold movement — chosen, brought near, satisfied** *(stated)*. The operation: the self is **drawn near** (not self-approaching but *brought*) and there **filled** — "satisfied with the goodness of your house" *(inferred: "you choose and bring near… we shall be satisfied" makes the nearness God-initiated and the satisfaction its fruit; the satisfaction thread, Ps 17:15, 63:5)*.

## What Psalm 65 says about the inner being
- **Praise can be a *silent waiting* (v.1).** *Dumiyah* — a poised readiness held in stillness before it sounds; praise as a waiting quiet (with Ps 62:1).
- **Iniquities can *overpower* the self, and are covered by God's atonement (v.3).** Sin can be stronger than the inner being can master ("prevail against me"); its resolution is God's *atoning/covering*, not the self's effort. The self does not overcome its own overwhelming iniquity — it is covered.
- **The blessed self is *chosen, brought near, satisfied* (v.4).** A God-initiated movement — the inner being is *drawn* near (not self-approaching) and there *filled* with the goodness of God's house.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** vv.5–13 (God stilling the seas, watering the earth, crowning the year) are the creation/provision arena; the inner-being weight is vv.1, 3, 4. Thin psalm, noted plainly.
- **"iniquities" (v.3)** — the lexical span tagged H1697 (*davar*, word/matter) appears to mis-span the *iniquity* term; read from the text as the overpowering *avon/transgression*. Minor span note; the *prevail* (H1396, *gabar*) and *atone* (H3722, *kaphar*) tags carry the finding.
- **"praise is due" (H1747, *dumiyah*, v.1)** captured gate-2; read as the *silent-waiting* praise (with Ps 62). A neat datum linking praise to the positive-silence family.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=David/Zion/LORD bleed via superscription; backfilled v.13 now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *praise* (H8416, M22, v.1); *prevail* (H1396, M23, v.3); *atone* (H3722, M38, v.3); *transgressions* (H6588, M10, v.3); *choose* (H0977, M37, v.4). *near/dwell/satisfied* captured gate-2 — the drawn-near-and-satisfied movement read from these.

## Psalm 66 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 66 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 66:1–20 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (v.13 + others backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The self refined through trial, and the condition of being heard.** Psalm 66's two inner-being findings: the inner being **tested and smelted like silver** — affliction as *purposive refining* issuing in abundance (vv.10–12); and the **condition of being heard** — *cherished* iniquity in the heart blocks the prayer (v.18).

## The reading

**I. The self tested and smelted like silver (vv.10–12).**
"For you, O God, have **tested** (H0974, *bachan*) us; you have **tried** (H6884, *tsaraph* — smelted) us **as silver is tried**. You brought us into the net; you laid a **crushing burden** (H4157, M03) on our backs; you let men ride over our heads; we went through **fire** and through **water**; **yet you have brought us out to a place of abundance**" (vv.10–12). The gem-finding: the trials are **God's *refining* of the inner being** — *tsaraph*, the smelting of silver *(stated)*. The operation: the affliction is **purposive, not random** — the inner being is *passed through* fire and water **as a refining process**, and the process has an **outcome: abundance** *(inferred: "tried as silver… yet brought out to abundance" frames the trial as a smelting with a purposed end, not mere suffering)*. The self is **refined**, not merely afflicted *(inferred; cf. Ps 12:6's refined silver, 17:3's night-testing — here the *self* is the metal)*.

**II. Cherished iniquity in the heart blocks being heard (vv.16–18).**
"Come and hear… I will tell what he has done for my **soul** (H5315, the seat — M47). I **cried** to him with my mouth… If I had **cherished** (H7200, *ra'ah* — regarded, kept looking upon [with favour]) **iniquity** (H0205, M10, *aven*) in my **heart** (H3820, the seat — M47), the Lord would **not have listened** (H8085)" (vv.16–18). The gem-finding: being-heard is **conditional on the heart** — *if* iniquity were **cherished** in the heart, God would **not listen** *(stated)*. The operation: **harboured, un-renounced iniquity in the heart *blocks* the prayer** *(inferred)*. And the verb is precise: *ra'ah* — not merely *having* sin but **regarding it, keeping it in view with favour**, *harbouring* it *(inferred: "cherished" = to look upon/regard, so the block is the heart's *attachment* to the sin, not the sin's mere presence)*. The finding is a **mechanism of communion**: the heart's **secret harbouring of sin closes the channel** — the cry does not get through while the heart cherishes iniquity *(inferred: the "if I had cherished… he would not have listened / but truly he has listened" makes the un-cherishing the condition of the answered prayer)*.

## What Psalm 66 says about the inner being
- **Affliction can be a *purposive refining* of the self (vv.10–12).** The inner being is *tested and smelted like silver* — passed through fire and water as a refining process with a purposed end (abundance). The self is refined, not merely afflicted.
- **Being heard is conditional on the heart (v.18).** *Cherished* iniquity — sin *regarded, kept in view with favour, harboured* — blocks the prayer. The block is the heart's *attachment* to the sin, not the sin's mere presence; the secret harbouring closes the channel of communion.
- **The testimony centres on the *soul* (v.16).** "What he has done for my soul" — the inner being is the beneficiary of the refining and the answered prayer.

## Honest notes
- **"cherished" (H7200, *ra'ah*, v.18)** captured gate-2 standalone; the reading foregrounds the *regard/harbour* sense (not mere having) — the mechanism of harboured sin blocking being-heard. A precise inner-being datum; candidate for a *harbouring/cherishing* operation (the heart's attachment to sin, cf. Ps 24:4's "lift the soul to falsehood", 62:10's "set the heart on riches").
- **"tried as silver" (H6884, *tsaraph*, v.10)** captured gate-2; the *refining* operation read from the smelting image. A clean datum: the self as the metal refined (with 12:6, 17:3).
- **Scope honesty:** vv.1–7 (universal praise, God's deeds), vv.13–15 (offerings) are the arena; the inner-being weight is the refining (vv.10–12) and the condition-of-being-heard (vv.16–18).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp at vv.9, 18, 20; bearer=LORD bleed; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *soul* (H5315, M47, vv.9,16); *crushing-burden* (H4157, M03, v.11); *iniquity* (H0205, M10, v.18); *heart* (H3820, M47, v.18); *steadfast-love* (H2617, M05, v.20). *tested/tried/cherished/listened* captured gate-2 — the refining and being-heard read from these.

## Psalm 67 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 67 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 67:1–7 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (v.2 backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **A short harvest/blessing psalm — honestly scoped.** Its body (the peoples praising, the earth's increase) is the arena. Its one genuine inner-being finding: **blessing received is *centrifugal* — given not to terminate in the self but to flow outward** so others may know and be glad (vv.1–4).

## The reading

**I. Blessing flows outward — received to be spread (vv.1–4).**
"May God be **gracious** (H2603, M39) to us and **bless** (H1288, M39) us and make his **face to shine** upon us… **that** your way may be **known** on earth… Let the nations be **glad** (H8055, M04) and **sing for joy** (H7442, M42)" (vv.1–4). The finding: the blessing received by the inner being is **instrumental, not terminal** — "bless us **that** your way may be known" *(stated)*. The operation: the self is blessed **so that the blessing may flow outward** — the inner being's reception of grace is oriented toward **others' knowing and gladness**, not held as its own possession *(inferred: the purpose-clause "that your way may be known… let the nations be glad" makes the blessing centrifugal — received to be spread)*. And the fruit is a **widening gladness** — the nations *glad and singing for joy* *(stated)*.

**II. The shining face upon the self (v.1).**
"Make his **face to shine** upon us" (v.1) — the lit face of the Aaronic blessing (cf. Ps 31:16, 4:6). The finding: the inner being's blessedness is being **under God's *shining* face** — the illuminated favour resting on it *(stated)*; a brief but real datum in the light-of-the-face thread.

## What Psalm 67 says about the inner being
- **Blessing received is *centrifugal* (vv.1–4).** The inner being is blessed *so that* the blessing flows outward — grace received is oriented toward others' knowing and gladness, not held as its own possession. Its fruit is a widening joy among the nations.
- **The blessed self is under the *shining* face (v.1).** God's lit, favourable face resting on the inner being (with Ps 31:16, 4:6).

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** a short liturgical blessing largely about the nations' praise and the earth's increase (the arena); the inner-being content is limited to the centrifugal blessing and the shining face. Noted plainly, not inflated.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (intensity *all* on the repeated "let all the peoples praise"; backfilled v.2 now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *gracious/bless* (H2603/H1288, M39, vv.1,6,7); *praise* (H3034, M22, vv.3,5); *glad* (H8055, M04, v.4); *sing-for-joy* (H7442, M42, v.4). *face/shine* captured gate-2 — the shining-face read from these.

## Psalm 68 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 68 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 68:1–35 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (vv.22 + others backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **A long triumphal procession — honestly scoped.** Most of it (God marching, scattering enemies, ascending on high, the parade through the sanctuary) is the *arena* of theophany. Its genuine inner-being findings cluster in a few verses: God who **settles the solitary in a home** (v.6); God who **daily bears the self up** (v.19); and the **threefold exultant gladness** of the righteous (v.3).

## The reading

**I. God settles the *solitary* in a home (vv.5–6).**
"**Father of the fatherless** and protector of widows is God… God **settles the solitary** (*yachid* — the alone/isolated) in a **home** (H1004); he leads out the **prisoners** to prosperity" (vv.5–6). The gem-finding: the inner being's **isolation** — the *solitary*, the *fatherless*, the *widow* — is answered by being **set in a home**, given belonging *(stated)*. The operation: God **places the lonely self into a family** — the isolated inner being (the *yachid* of Ps 25:16, the parent-forsaken of Ps 27:10) is not left alone but **homed** *(inferred: "settles the solitary in a home" makes belonging the answer to isolation)*. And the *prisoner* is led out to freedom — the bound self released *(stated)*.

**II. God who *daily bears the self up* (v.19).**
"Blessed be the Lord, who **daily bears us up** (*amas* — loads onto himself, carries); God is our **salvation**" (v.19). The gem-finding: God **carries the self *daily*** — not a single rescue but a **continual bearing-up** *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being is **borne** by God **day by day** — *amas*, the word for loading a burden onto oneself: God takes the self's weight onto himself, continually *(inferred: "daily bears us up" makes the carrying ongoing, God shouldering the self's load each day)*.

**III. The threefold exultant gladness (v.3).**
"But the righteous shall be **glad** (H8055, M04); they shall **exult** (H5970) before God; they shall be **jubilant** with **joy** (H8057, M04)!" (v.3). The finding: the inner being's joy before God is **superlative and layered** — *glad, exult, jubilant with joy*, three joy-words stacked *(stated)*. The operation: joy here is **not single but compounded** — the inner being's gladness intensifies through several registers at once *(inferred: the three joy-terms pile up to name a maximal exultation)*.

## What Psalm 68 says about the inner being
- **The isolated self is given a *home* (vv.5–6).** God settles the *solitary* — the fatherless, the widow, the alone — into belonging; isolation is answered by being homed, and the bound self is led out to freedom.
- **The self is *carried daily*, not just rescued once (v.19).** God *bears the self up* day by day — *amas*, loading the self's weight onto himself continually. The inner being is borne, not merely delivered.
- **Joy before God is *compounded* (v.3).** Glad, exult, jubilant — the inner being's gladness intensifies through several registers at once, a layered exultation.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** the bulk (vv.1–2, 7–18, 21–34 — the march, the scattering, the ascent, the sanctuary procession) is the theophany arena; the inner-being weight is vv.3, 5–6, 19. Long psalm, read for its inner-being moments, not verse-by-verse.
- **"settles the solitary in a home" (v.6)** and **"daily bears us up" (v.19)** captured via gate-2 spans; the *homing-the-isolated* and *daily-carrying* operations read from the phrases. Both connect to threads: isolation-answered (25:16, 27:10) and the upheld/carried self (54:4 *samak*, 55:22 *kul*, here *amas*).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed pervasive; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *glad/joy* (H8055/H8057, M04, v.3); *power/strength* (H5797/H5810, M23, v.35). *solitary/home/bears-up* captured gate-2 — the homing and daily-carrying read from these.

## Psalm 69 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 69 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 69:1–36 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (vv.35 + others backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The overwhelmed and *consumed* inner being.** Psalm 69's findings: the self **wearied by prolonged waiting** — "eyes grow dim with waiting" (vv.1–3); **zeal that *consumes* and *isolates*** the inner being (vv.8–9); the heart **broken by reproach into despair, with *no comforter*** (v.20); resolving into the **revived hearts of the humble** (v.32).

## The reading

**I. The fatigue of prolonged waiting (vv.1–3).**
"Save me… the waters have come up to my **neck** (H5315, *nephesh* — throat/soul, seat=soul)… I am **weary** (H3021, *yaga*) with my crying out; my throat is parched. My **eyes grow dim** with **waiting** (H3176, M18, *yachal*) for my God" (vv.1–3). The finding: the inner being is **exhausted by the *length* of the waiting** — "my eyes grow dim with waiting" *(stated)*. The operation: the waiting itself **wears the self out** — the prolonged, unanswered cry *fatigues* the inner being (weary, parched, eyes failing) *(inferred: the eyes "grow dim *with waiting*" — the fatigue is the cost of protracted hope, not of the danger alone)*. The self is worn down not only by the flood but by **how long** it must wait for God *(inferred)*.

**II. Zeal that *consumes* and *isolates* (vv.8–9).**
"I have become a **stranger** (H2114, *zur*) to my brothers, an alien to my mother's sons. For **zeal** (H7068, M02, *qinah*) for your house has **consumed** (H0398, *akal* — eaten) me" (vv.8–9). The gem-finding: **zeal *eats* the inner being** — *qinah* (an intense heat, in the M02 passion cluster) has **consumed/devoured** the self *(stated)*. The operation: zeal is a **consuming inner fire** — a passion so intense it *eats up* the one who holds it *(inferred: akal makes zeal a devouring, the self burned through by its own intensity)*. And it has a **cost: isolation** — the zeal-consumed self becomes "a *stranger* to his brothers" *(stated)*: the very passion for God **alienates the inner being from its own kin** *(inferred: the "stranger to my brothers… for zeal has consumed me" links the alienation to the zeal — the fire isolates)*.

**III. The heart broken by reproach — despair with no comforter (v.20).**
"**Reproaches** (H2781, M06, *cherpah*) have **broken** (H7665, *shabar*) my **heart** (H3820, the seat — M47), so that I am in **despair** (H5136, M24). I looked for **pity**, but there was none, and for **comforters**, but I found none" (v.20). The gem-finding: the heart **broken by reproach → despair**, and — the aggravation — the search for **pity and a comforter that *fails*** *(stated)*. The operation: the wound is **doubled** — the reproach breaks the heart, *and* the absence of any comforter compounds it *(inferred)*. The finding is the **wound of un-comforted suffering**: the inner being, already broken, **looks outward for pity and finds none** — the loneliness of the unshared break is itself part of the injury *(inferred: "broken my heart… I looked for comforters but found none" makes the missing comforter a second wound on the first)*.

**IV. The revived heart of the humble (vv.29–32).**
"But I am **afflicted** and in pain… I will **praise** the name of God with a song… When the **humble** see it they will be glad; you who **seek** God, **let your hearts revive** (H2421, *chayah* — live)" (vv.29–32). The finding: against the *broken* heart of v.20, the seeking/humble inner being's heart is **revived** — brought back to life *(stated)*. The operation: the heart can **move from broken to revived** — the same organ shattered by reproach (v.20) is *made to live again* in the seeking humble (v.32) *(inferred: "broken my heart" v.20 and "let your hearts revive" v.32 are the two poles — the light-rekindled/heart-revived thread, cf. Ps 22:26)*.

## What Psalm 69 says about the inner being
- **Prolonged waiting *fatigues* the inner being (vv.1–3).** The self is worn out not only by the flood but by *how long* it must wait — "eyes grow dim with waiting." The cost of protracted, unanswered hope is exhaustion of the very faculties of seeing and crying.
- **Zeal can *consume* and *isolate* the self (vv.8–9).** *Qinah* eats the inner being — a passion so intense it devours the one who holds it — and it alienates: the very zeal for God makes the self a stranger to its own kin.
- **The broken heart is doubled by the absent comforter (v.20).** Reproach breaks the heart into despair; the search for pity and a comforter that *fails* is a second wound — the loneliness of un-comforted suffering.
- **The heart can move from *broken* to *revived* (vv.20, 32).** The organ shattered by reproach is made to live again in the seeking humble — broken-heart and revived-heart are the two poles.

## Honest notes
- **"zeal" (H7068, *qinah*, M02)** correctly a characteristic in the passion/jealousy cluster — the reading foregrounds the *consuming* sense (*akal*, "eaten"): zeal as a devouring heat with an isolating cost. A strong M02 datum (zeal, like the anger of Ps 37/58, is an intense heat — here God-directed yet self-consuming).
- **"despair" (H5136, v.20)** captured M24; the broken-heart-without-comforter operation read from the verse. Candidate for an *un-comforted-break* inner datum (the missing comforter as a second wound).
- **Scope honesty:** the long imprecation (vv.22–28) and the enemy-description are the arena (external pole); the inner-being weight is vv.1–3, 8–10, 20, 29–32.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=David/LORD bleed via superscription; backfilled vv. now full-text; "neck" H5315 = nephesh/throat, seat=soul, correctly captured) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *soul/neck* (H5315, M47, vv.1,10,18); *waiting* (H3176, M18, v.3); *reproach* (H2781/H2778, M06, vv.7,9,10,19,20); *zeal* (H7068, M02, v.9); *heart* (H3820, M47, v.20); *despair* (H5136, M24, v.20). *weary/consumed/broken/revive* captured gate-2 — the fatigue, consuming, and revival read from these.
