## Psalm 70 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 70 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 70:1–5 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter. **A near-duplicate of Ps 40:13–17** (id 438) — the *urgent-plea* portion of Ps 40, standing alone without that psalm's "I waited patiently" frame. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Urgency and acknowledged neediness.** Two inner-being findings: the **pressing, time-sensitive urgency** of the plea — "make haste… do not delay" (vv.1, 5); and the **self-acknowledgment of poverty** — "I am poor and needy" (v.5).

## The reading

**I. Urgency — the inner being at the limit (vv.1, 5).**
"**Make haste** (H2363, *chush*), O God, to deliver me! O Lord, **make haste** to help me!… **hasten** to me, O God!… O Lord, **do not delay**!" (vv.1, 5). The finding: the inner being's need is **time-sensitive** — the *haste*-word tolls three times, closing on "do not delay" *(stated)*. The operation: the self is **at the limit of what it can bear**, pressing not merely for help but for **speed** — the urgency itself discloses an inner being that **can wait no longer** *(inferred: the repeated "make haste… do not delay" makes the *timing* the burden, the self unable to sustain further delay)*. (Notably, where Ps 40 framed this same plea with an opening "I *waited patiently*", Ps 70 is the plea **stripped to its urgency** — the same words at a different inner moment.)

**II. Acknowledged neediness (v.5).**
"But I am **poor** (H6041, *ani*) and **needy** (H0034, *evyon*); … You are my **help** and my **deliverer**" (v.5). The finding: the inner being **names its own poverty** — *poor and needy* — as the ground of its appeal *(stated)*. The operation: the self approaches God **not from strength but from acknowledged lack** — its neediness is the very basis on which it asks *(inferred: "I am poor and needy… you are my help" makes the confessed poverty the reason God is appealed to; cf. Ps 40:17, 34:6)*.

## What Psalm 70 says about the inner being
- **Urgency itself is a disclosure (vv.1, 5).** The threefold "make haste… do not delay" reveals an inner being at the limit — pressing for *speed*, unable to sustain further delay. The *timing* is the burden. (The same plea Ps 40 framed with patient waiting, here stripped to its urgency.)
- **The self appeals from acknowledged *lack* (v.5).** "I am poor and needy" — the inner being approaches God not from strength but from confessed poverty, which is the very ground of its asking.

## Honest notes
- **Near-duplicate of Ps 40:13–17** (id 438); read as the *urgent-plea* fragment standing alone. The pair is worth noting in any cross-chapter reading — the contrast (Ps 40's patient-waiting frame vs Ps 70's bare urgency) is itself a datum about the inner being at different moments.
- **SANITY-CHECK CATCH (recurring) — "love" (H0157, *aheb*, v.4) gate-2 standalone** — the eighth occurrence ("those who love your salvation"); the **aheb-reclassification** remains the decided pending fix.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=David/LORD bleed via superscription; prohibition at v.5 "do not delay") — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *put-to-shame/shame* (H0954/H1322, M07, vv.2,3); *rejoice* (H7797, M04, v.4); *great* (H1431, M22, v.4); *love* (H0157, v.4 — see catch). *make-haste/poor/needy* captured gate-2 — the urgency and neediness read from these.

## Psalm 71 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 71 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 71:1–24 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (v.12 + others backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The psalm of old age — lifelong leaning and growing hope.** Psalm 71's findings: the inner being's **lifelong, continuous dependence** — leaning on God from the womb through youth into old age (vv.5–6); the **aging self's vulnerability** as strength fails, and its desire to *transmit* to the next generation (vv.9, 18); **hope that *increases*** "yet more and more" (v.14); and the expectation of **revival — brought up *again*** from the depths (vv.20–21).

## The reading

**I. Lifelong leaning — dependence across the whole lifespan (vv.5–6).**
"For you, O Lord, are my **hope** (H8615, M18), my **trust** (H4009, M19), from my **youth**. Upon you I have **leaned** (H5564, *samak* — propped myself) from before my birth; you are he who took me from my mother's womb" (vv.5–6). The gem-finding: the inner being's dependence is **continuous across the entire lifespan** — *from the womb, from youth*, and (vv.9, 18) *into old age* *(stated)*. The operation: the self has **leaned** on God — *samak*, propping its whole weight — **as a single unbroken posture from before birth onward** *(inferred: "leaned… from before my birth… from my youth" makes the dependence one continuous lean, not a series of episodes; cf. Ps 22:9–10)*. The same verb (*samak*) that named God *upholding* the self in Ps 54:4 is here the self's *leaning* — the two sides of one relation *(inferred)*.

**II. The aging self's vulnerability — and its desire to transmit (vv.9, 18).**
"**Do not cast me off** in the time of **old age** (H2209); **forsake me not** when my **strength** (H3581, M23) is **spent**… So even to old age and gray hairs, O God, do not forsake me, **until I proclaim your might to another generation**" (vv.9, 18). The finding: the aging inner being's specific fear is that **as its strength fails, it may be abandoned** *(stated)*. The operation: the self **at the end of its own strength** seeks *continued holding* — dependence intensifies precisely as self-sufficiency runs out *(inferred: "forsake me not when my strength is spent" ties the plea to the failure of the self's own resources)*. And it has a **forward aim**: the old self wants to *last long enough to* **transmit** — "until I proclaim your might to *another generation*" — its remaining desire is **handing on** what it knows before it goes *(stated; cf. Ps 48:13's observe-to-tell)*.

**III. Hope that increases (v.14).**
"But I will **hope** (H3176, M18, *yachal*) continually and will praise you **yet more and more**" (v.14). The finding: the inner being's hope is **not static but *growing*** — "yet more and more" *(stated)*. The operation: hope **accumulates and increases** — the aging self's hope is *larger*, not smaller, with the years; it grows rather than wears out *(inferred: "hope continually… yet more and more" makes hope an increasing quantity, gaining across a lifetime of proof)*.

**IV. Revival — brought up *again* from the depths (vv.20–21).**
"You who have made me see many troubles and calamities **will revive me again** (H2421, M25, *chayah*); from the **depths of the earth** you will **bring me up again**. You will **increase** my greatness and **comfort me again**" (vv.20–21). The gem-finding: the inner being, brought low through many troubles, expects to be **revived *again*** — the word *again* tolls three times *(stated)*. The operation: the self reads a **repeating pattern — down, then up; brought low, then revived** — and expects its recurrence *(inferred: "revive me *again*… bring me up *again*… comfort me *again*" makes the down-then-up a known cycle the self trusts will repeat)*. Hope's confidence rests on the **remembered pattern** of God's past revivals *(inferred)*. And it terminates in the soul: "my **soul** (H5315, M25/M47) also, **which you have redeemed**" (v.23) — the inner being, redeemed, joins the praise *(stated)*.

## What Psalm 71 says about the inner being
- **Dependence is *lifelong and continuous* (vv.5–6).** The inner being leans on God as one unbroken posture — from the womb, through youth, into old age. The self's *leaning* (*samak*) answers God's *upholding* (*samak*, Ps 54:4).
- **The aging self's dependence *intensifies* as strength fails (vv.9, 18).** Its specific fear is being cast off when it can no longer sustain itself; and its forward desire is to *last long enough to transmit* — to hand on what it knows to another generation before it goes.
- **Hope *increases* with the years (v.14).** "Yet more and more" — the inner being's hope grows rather than wears out, larger across a lifetime of proof.
- **The self expects *revival — again* (vv.20–21).** Brought low, it trusts to be brought up *again*; hope rests on the remembered pattern of God's past revivals — a known cycle of down-then-up.

## Honest notes
- **"leaned" (H5564, *samak*, v.6)** captured gate-2 standalone; the *lifelong-leaning* operation read from the verb — the same *samak* that is God's *upholding* in Ps 54:4. A clean two-sided datum (the self leans / God upholds).
- **The "again" pattern (vv.20–21)** — revive/bring-up/comfort *again* — captured across gate-2 spans; the down-then-up cycle read from the repetition. Candidate for a *revival-again / remembered-pattern* inner datum (hope grounded in God's past cycle).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp at vv.9, 18; bearer=LORD bleed; backfilled vv. now full-text; two trust/hope words — *mivtach* M19, *tiqvah*/*yachal* M18) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *take-refuge* (H2620, M19, v.1); *hope/trust* (H8615/H4009/H3176, M18/M19, vv.5,14); *strength* (H3581, M23, v.9); *revive* (H2421, M25, v.20); *soul* (H5315, M47, v.23); *joy* (H7442, M42, v.23). *leaned/old-age/spent/again* captured gate-2 — the lifelong leaning, aging vulnerability, and revival read from these.

## Psalm 72 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 72 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 72:1–20 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (closes Book II; vv.16 + others backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **A royal psalm — honestly scoped.** Its body (the king's just, wide, prosperous reign) is the arena. Its one genuine inner-being finding: the just ruler's **inner disposition toward the vulnerable** — *pity* on the weak, and the *valuing of their life as precious* (vv.12–14).

## The reading

**I. The ruler's inner regard for the vulnerable (vv.12–14).**
"He delivers the **needy** (H0034, *evyon*) when he calls, the **poor** (H6041, *ani*) and him who has **no helper**. He has **pity** (H2347, M05, *chus* — spares, feels compassion) on the weak and the needy… From oppression and violence he **redeems their life**, and **precious is their blood in his sight**" (vv.12–14). The finding: the righteous ruler's *justice* is not merely external policy but an **inner disposition** — **pity** (chus) toward the weak, and a **valuing of the vulnerable's life as *precious*** *(stated)*. The operation: the just self **regards the helpless with compassion and holds their life as of great worth** — "precious is their *blood* in his sight" makes the valuation an *inner seeing*, an esteem lodged in how he *regards* them *(inferred: "precious in his sight" locates the justice in the ruler's inner valuing, not only his acts)*. Right rule flows from a **heart that pities and prizes the powerless** *(inferred)*.

## What Psalm 72 says about the inner being
- **Just rule flows from an inner disposition of *pity and valuing* (vv.12–14).** The righteous ruler *feels compassion* (*chus*) for the weak and holds the vulnerable's life as *precious in his sight* — the justice is lodged in how he *regards* the powerless, not only in what he does. Right conduct toward the weak has an inner root: a heart that pities and prizes them.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** the great bulk (the king's wide dominion, long life, the earth's prosperity, the nations' homage) is the royal/external arena; the inner-being weight is the ruler's *disposition* toward the vulnerable (vv.12–14). Thin psalm, noted plainly (memory `feedback_no_stats_trends_review_fabricated_data`).
- **"pity" (H2347, *chus*, M05)** correctly a characteristic (compassion cluster); "precious… in his sight" captured via gate-2 — the inner-valuation read from the phrase. A datum: justice rooted in inner regard (cf. Ps 41:1's *sakal* attention to the poor).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=Solomon/LORD bleed via superscription; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *justice/righteousness* (H4941/H6666/H6664/H6662, M26, vv.1–3,7); *pity* (H2347, M05, v.13). *precious/blood/sight* captured gate-2 — the inner valuing read from these.

## Psalm 73 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 73 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 73:1–28 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (vv.19 + others backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The anatomy of an inner crisis — envy, resolved by re-perception and re-valuation. A cornerstone.** Psalm 73 traces a **whole crisis of the inner being**: **envy** at the wicked's prosperity nearly *toppling* the self (vv.2–3); bitterness **reducing it to a brute** (vv.21–22); the crisis **resolved by a shift of vantage** in the sanctuary — *discerning the end* (vv.16–17); and the great pivot into desiring **God himself as the supreme good and portion** (vv.23–28). The movement is *destabilised → brutish → re-seeing → re-valuing*.

## The reading

**I. Envy nearly topples the inner being (vv.2–3).**
"But as for me, my **feet had almost stumbled** (H5186), my steps had nearly **slipped** (H8210). For I was **envious** (H7065, M02, *qana*) of the arrogant when I saw the **prosperity of the wicked**" (vv.2–3). The finding: **envy nearly overthrew the self's footing** — the feet almost slipped *(stated)*. The operation: seeing the wicked prosper set off *qana* (envy — the same passion-word as zeal, M02), and that envy **destabilised the inner being to the brink of falling** *(inferred: the "feet almost stumbled… for I was envious" makes the envy the cause of the near-collapse; the very thing Ps 37 warned against — "be not envious")*.

**II. Bitterness reduces the self to a brute (vv.13, 21–22).**
The envy fed a grievance: "**All in vain** have I kept my **heart** (H3824, the seat — M47) **clean**" (v.13). And its inner effect, seen in retrospect: "When my **soul** was **embittered** (H2556, *chamets* — soured), when I was **pricked** in **heart** (kidneys), I was **brutish** (H1198, M16, *baar*) and **ignorant**; I was **like a beast** toward you" (vv.21–22). The gem-finding: **bitterness reduced the inner being to a *beast*** — brutish, without understanding *(stated)*. The operation: the **soured soul loses its understanding** — envy-fed bitterness **strips the inner being of the very faculty (understanding) that raises it above the animals** (Ps 49:20's "man without understanding is like the beasts") *(inferred: "embittered… brutish… like a beast" chains the souring to the loss of understanding)*.

**III. The turn in the sanctuary — a shift of vantage (vv.16–17).**
"But when I **thought** how to **understand** this, it seemed a **wearisome** task, **until I went into the sanctuary** of God; then I **discerned** (H0995, M15, *bin*) their **end** (H0319, *acharith*)" (vv.16–17). The gem-finding: the crisis is **not resolved by reasoning alone** (which *wearied* him) but by **entering God's presence**, where the inner being gains a **new perception — discerning the wicked's *end*** *(stated)*. The operation: a **shift of vantage** — from the immediate view (the wicked prosper *now*) to the **end-view** (their trajectory and destruction) — and this reframing **dissolves the envy** *(inferred: the "wearisome… until I went into the sanctuary… then I discerned their end" makes the resolution a change of *where the self stands to see*, not new information reasoned out)*. Perception, reframed in God's presence, is the turn.

**IV. The great pivot — God as the supreme desire and portion (vv.23–26).**
"**Nevertheless**, I am **continually with you**; you hold my right hand. You **guide** me with your **counsel**… **Whom have I in heaven but you?** And there is **nothing on earth that I desire besides you**. My **flesh** and my **heart** (H3824, M47) may **fail**, but God is the **strength of my heart** and my **portion** forever" (vv.23–26). The gem-finding — the psalm's peak: the crisis resolves into a **re-valuation** — the inner being discovers it **desires God above everything** ("nothing on earth I desire besides you") and that **God is its portion** *(stated)*. The operation: the envy (which prized the wicked's *stuff*) is answered by a **re-ordered desire** that finds its all in God himself *(inferred: the "nothing I desire besides you" directly reverses the envy of v.3 — the object of desire is re-set)*. And even when the inner being's own resources give out — "my flesh and my **heart** may **fail**" — **God is the *strength of the heart*** beyond the heart's own failing: the self is upheld at the very point of its collapse *(stated; the heart sustained past its own end)*.

**V. "The nearness of God is my good" (v.28).**
"But for me it is **good to be near God**; I have made the Lord GOD my **refuge** (H4268, M19)" (v.28). The finding: the inner being's **supreme good is re-defined as *nearness* to God** — not prosperity (the wicked's), but *proximity* *(stated)*. The operation: the whole crisis terminates in a **redefinition of the good** — the self's *good* is being *near* God, and that nearness is where the envy finally has no more hold *(inferred: "it is good *to be near God*" names the resolved value — nearness itself is the good, over against the wicked's goods)*.

## What Psalm 73 says about the inner being
- **Envy destabilises the inner being (vv.2–3).** Seeing the wicked prosper nearly *toppled* the self — the feet almost slipped. *Qana* (envy, the M02 passion) can bring the inner being to the brink of falling.
- **Bitterness reduces the self to a *brute* (vv.21–22).** The soured soul loses its understanding — envy-fed bitterness strips the very faculty that raises the inner being above the beasts.
- **The crisis is resolved by a *shift of vantage*, not by reasoning (vv.16–17).** Entering God's presence gives a new perception — discerning the wicked's *end* — and the reframed view dissolves the envy. Perception, re-sited in the sanctuary, is the turn.
- **Resolution is a *re-ordered desire* (vv.23–26).** The envy that prized the wicked's stuff is answered by desiring *God himself* above all — "nothing on earth I desire besides you"; God is the *portion*, and the *strength of the heart* even when the heart fails.
- **The good is re-defined as *nearness* to God (v.28).** The whole crisis ends in a redefinition of the good — proximity to God, not prosperity. Where the self is near God, the envy has no hold.

## Honest notes
- **A cornerstone crisis-anatomy** (destabilised → brutish → re-seeing → re-valuing → nearness); a strong worked exemplar of an *inner process*, alongside Ps 51 (re-creation) and Ps 63 (thirst→satisfaction→clinging). Worth flagging for the movements/emergence focus of the study.
- **"envy" (H7065, *qana*, M02)** correctly a characteristic — the passion cluster; here the destabilising envy (with Ps 37:1's "be not envious", 69:9's consuming zeal — the same root turned differently).
- **"brutish" (H1198, *baar*, M16)** correctly a characteristic (folly cluster) — the beast-reduction read with it; ties to Ps 49:20.
- **DISK-FULL incident (this run):** the DB backup-copy step filled the disk mid-run; Ps 73's Phase-1 had to be re-run after freeing space. See session note; `backups/` is oversized (flag to researcher). Ps 73 lexical is now correctly written.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=Asaph/Israel/LORD bleed via superscription; *stumbled/slipped/embittered/pricked/desire/fail* gate-2 verbs; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *good* (H2896, M04, vv.1,28); *heart* (H3824, M47, vv.1,13,21,26); *envious* (H7065, M02, v.3); *discerned* (H0995, M15, v.17); *brutish* (H1198, M16, v.22); *refuge* (H4268, M19, v.28). *slipped/desire/portion/near* captured gate-2 — the destabilising, re-valuing, and nearness read from these.

## Psalm 74 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 74 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 74:1–23 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (vv.16 + others backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **A community lament over the ruined sanctuary — honestly scoped.** The desolation itself (the burned temple, the scoffing foe) is the arena. Its inner-being findings: the anguish of **not knowing *how long*** (vv.9–10); the pivot to **remembered, ancient faith** amid the ruins (v.12); and the self figured as a defenceless **dove** (v.19).

## The reading

**I. The "how long" — and the anguish of *not knowing the duration* (vv.9–10).**
"We do not see our signs; there is **no longer any prophet**, and there is **none among us who knows how long**. **How long**, O God, is the foe to scoff?" (vv.9–10). The finding: the inner being's anguish is sharpened by **not knowing *how long* the affliction will last** — and by the **absence of any word** (no prophet) to tell it *(stated)*. The operation: the self can bear affliction, but the **unbounded, un-datable duration** — "none knows how long" — is its own torment; the inner being reaches for an *end-point* and finds none *(inferred: "none knows how long… how long, O God?" makes the *not-knowing-the-end* the specific weight, compounding the affliction; cf. Ps 13's fourfold "how long")*.

**II. The pivot to remembered, ancient faith (v.12).**
"**Yet** God my King is **from of old**, working salvation in the midst of the earth" (v.12). The finding: against the present desolation, the inner being **anchors on the *ancient*, remembered God** — "from of old" *(stated)*. The operation: the "**yet**" turns the self from the *present ruin* to the *remembered, long-established faithfulness* of God — memory of God's ancient works becomes the ground the inner being stands on when the present gives nothing *(inferred: the "yet… from of old" pivots from desolation to remembered antiquity, the self reaching back past the present)*.

**III. The self as a defenceless dove (v.19).**
"Do not deliver the **soul** (H5315, the seat — M47) of your **dove** to the wild beasts; do not forget the **life** of your poor forever" (v.19). The finding: the inner being is figured as a **defenceless dove** — the fragile, vulnerable *soul* exposed to beasts *(stated)*. The operation: the self names its own **helplessness** — a dove among predators — as the ground of its plea *(inferred: "the soul of your dove" casts the inner being as small and defenceless, the vulnerability itself the appeal; cf. Ps 55:6's dove-longing)*.

## What Psalm 74 says about the inner being
- **Not knowing *how long* is its own torment (vv.9–10).** The inner being can bear affliction, but the un-datable, unbounded duration — "none knows how long," no word to tell it — is a distinct weight; the self reaches for an end-point and finds none.
- **The self anchors on *remembered, ancient* faith amid ruin (v.12).** The "yet" turns the inner being from the present desolation to God's long-established works — memory of the ancient becomes the ground when the present gives nothing.
- **The self names its own defencelessness (v.19).** Figured as a *dove* among beasts, the vulnerable soul makes its very helplessness the ground of its plea.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** the bulk (the burned sanctuary, the enemy's desecration, the creation-recital vv.13–17) is the community/external arena; the inner-being weight is vv.9–10, 12, 19. Thin psalm, noted plainly.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp across the "do not… let not…" petitions vv.19,21,23; bearer=Asaph/LORD bleed; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *soul* (H5315, M47, v.19); *shame* (H3637, M07, v.21); *remember* (H2142, M41, vv.2,18,22). *how-long/dove/from-of-old* captured gate-2 — the not-knowing, the vulnerable self, and the remembered-faith pivot read from these.

## Psalm 75 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 75 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 75:1–10 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (v.3 backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The futility of self-exaltation.** A psalm of God's judgment (the cup, vv.1–3, 8, is the arena). Its inner-being finding: the wicked's **self-exaltation** — "lift up your horn… haughty neck" (vv.4–5) — is *futile*, because **"lifting up" is God's prerogative alone**, not self-generated (vv.6–7).

## The reading

**I. Self-exaltation warned against (vv.4–5).**
"I say to the **boastful** (H1984, M16, *halal* — in its boasting sense), 'Do not **boast**,' and to the **wicked** (H7563, M10), 'Do not **lift up your horn**; do not lift up your horn on high, or speak with **haughty neck**'" (vv.4–5). The finding: the wicked inner being's characteristic posture is **self-elevation** — *raising its own horn* (its power/status) and the *stiff, haughty neck* *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being **exalting itself** — lifting its own horn, arrogant-necked — is the disposition named and forbidden *(inferred: "lift up *your* horn… haughty neck" is the self raising its own standing)*.

**II. "Lifting up" is God's, not the self's (vv.6–7, 10).**
"For **not** from the east or from the west and **not** from the wilderness comes **lifting up** (H7311, *rum*), **but it is God** who executes judgment, **putting down one and lifting up another**… the horns of the wicked I will **cut off**, but the horns of the righteous shall be **lifted up**" (vv.6–7, 10). The gem-finding: **exaltation cannot be self-generated** — "lifting up" comes from **no direction and no self, but from God alone** *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's self-raising is **futile** — the horn it lifts for itself will be **cut off**, while the horn it does *not* raise (the righteous', *lifted up* passively, *by God*) is the one that rises *(inferred: the self-raised horn "cut off" vs the righteous' horn "lifted up" [by God] contrasts self-exaltation with God-given exaltation — only the latter stands)*. The finding: **the self cannot elevate itself; elevation is God's to give or withhold** *(inferred)*.

## What Psalm 75 says about the inner being
- **Self-exaltation is the wicked's characteristic posture (vv.4–5).** Lifting its own horn, haughty-necked — the inner being raising its own standing.
- **Exaltation cannot be *self-generated* (vv.6–7, 10).** "Lifting up" comes from God alone, not from the self or any direction; the self-raised horn is cut off, while the righteous' horn — *not* self-raised — is lifted up by God. The inner being cannot elevate itself; elevation is God's prerogative.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** the frame (God's appointed judgment, the pillars of the earth, the cup of wine, vv.1–3, 8) is the arena; the inner-being weight is the self-exaltation vs God-given exaltation (vv.4–7, 10).
- **"boast" (H1984, *halal*, M16)** — the *halal* root spans praise (M22), pride (M08), and here *boasting/madness* (M16); a per-occurrence note on the root's range (praise God-directed vs boast self-directed).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp at vv.4–5; bearer=Asaph/LORD bleed; backfilled v.3 now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *give-thanks* (H3034, M22, v.1); *judge* (H8199, M26, v.2); *boastful/boast* (H1984, M16, v.4); *wicked* (H7563, M10, vv.4,8,10). *horn/haughty/neck/lifting-up* captured gate-2 — the self-exaltation and God-given exaltation read from these.

## Psalm 76 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 76 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 76:1–12 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (v.6 backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Awed stillness, and wrath overruled.** A Zion/victory hymn (God's terrifying power in judgment is the arena). Its inner-being findings: the **fearful stillness** before God's overwhelming power — the self unable to *stand* (vv.7–8); and the striking datum that **man's wrath is turned to God's praise** (v.10).

## The reading

**I. Awed stillness — the self unable to stand (vv.7–8).**
"But you, **you are to be feared**! **Who can stand** before you when once your **anger** is roused? From the heavens you uttered judgment; the earth **feared and was still**" (vv.7–8). The finding: the fitting response to God's overwhelming power is **fear**, and before it the self **cannot stand** — "who can stand before you?" *(stated)*. The operation: God's roused judgment reduces the inner being (and the whole earth) to **fearful *stillness*** — "the earth feared and *was still*", fell silent *(stated)*. The awe is not noise but **a silenced hush** — the self stopped, unable to remain standing or speaking before the majesty *(inferred: "feared and was still" pairs the fear with a falling-silent; cf. Ps 46:10's "be still and know", here the involuntary stillness of awe)*.

**II. Man's wrath turned to God's praise (v.10).**
"Surely the **wrath of man** shall **praise** you; the remnant of wrath you will **put on like a belt**" (v.10). The gem-finding: even the inner being's **hostile passion — the *wrath of man*** — ends up **serving God's praise** *(stated)*. The operation: human wrath, the very rage that *opposes* God, is **overruled and co-opted to his glory** — and its *remnant* is **restrained** (girded on like a belt) *(inferred: "the wrath of man shall praise you… the remnant you will put on" makes the opposing passion an occasion for God's praise, its excess bound)*. The finding: the rebellious inner being's rage **does not thwart God but is turned to serve him** *(inferred)*.

## What Psalm 76 says about the inner being
- **God's roused power reduces the self to *fearful stillness* (vv.7–8).** The fitting response is fear; before God's judgment the inner being cannot *stand* — "the earth feared and was still". Awe is a silenced hush, the self stopped before the majesty.
- **Man's wrath is turned to God's *praise* (v.10).** Even the inner being's hostile passion — the wrath that opposes God — is overruled and co-opted to his glory, its remnant restrained. Rebellious rage does not thwart God but ends up serving him.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** the bulk (God known in Zion, the shattered weapons, the stunned warriors, God's judgment to save the humble) is the victory/judgment arena; the inner-being weight is the awed stillness (vv.7–8) and the wrath-turned-praise (v.10).
- **"the earth… was still" (v.8)** captured gate-2; the *awed silence* read from it — a distinct note from the positive stillness of Ps 46:10/62:1 (there chosen, here involuntary before majesty).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=Asaph/Judah/LORD bleed via superscription; backfilled v.6 now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** the human-response terms (*feared*, *stand*, *wrath*, *praise*, *still*, *vows*) are largely gate-2 in this God-focused hymn; the two inner-being findings (awed stillness, wrath-turned-praise) are read from vv.7–8, 10. *save the humble* (v.9) notes the vulnerable as the beneficiaries.

## Psalm 77 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 77 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 77:1–20 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (vv.19 + others backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The inconsolable soul, resolved by the *willed redirection of memory*.** Psalm 77's findings: a **soul that refuses to be comforted** (v.2); the paradox that at the crisis, **remembering and meditating *aggravate*** the anguish (v.3); and the resolution — a **deliberate, willed turn** of the very same faculties from brooding on the present to recalling God's *ancient deeds* (vv.10–12). The meditative faculty's effect **depends on its object**.

## The reading

**I. The soul that refuses comfort (v.2).**
"In the day of my trouble I **seek** the Lord… my **soul** (H5315, the seat — M47) **refuses to be comforted** (H5162, M05, *nacham*)" (v.2). The gem-finding: the inner being **actively *refuses* consolation** — not that none is offered, but that the soul **turns it away** *(stated)*. The operation: grief can reach a pitch where the inner being **rejects comfort** — an active refusal, not merely an absence of comforters (contrast Ps 69:20's *found none*; here comfort is refused) *(inferred: "refuses to be comforted" is the soul's own act of declining consolation)*.

**II. Remembering *aggravates* — the crisis phase (vv.3, 6–9).**
"When I **remember** (H2142, M41) God, I **moan**; when I **meditate** (H7878, M15, *siach*), my **spirit** (H7307, the seat) **faints** (H5848)" (v.3). The gem-finding, paradoxical: at the crisis, the God-ward operations — *remembering, meditating* — **do not soothe but worsen** the anguish; "I meditate and my spirit *faints*" *(stated)*. The operation: turned on the *present* distress, memory and meditation **intensify** the pain, feeding the doubting questions: "Will the Lord spurn forever? Has his steadfast love forever ceased? Has God forgotten to be gracious?" (vv.7–9) *(stated)*. The finding: **the meditative faculty, aimed at the unanswered present, breeds despair** — the same brooding that Ps 39 found builds heat, here builds a fainting spirit *(inferred)*.

**III. The willed turn — redirecting memory to God's *ancient deeds* (vv.10–12).**
"Then I **said**, 'I will **appeal** to this, to the **years of the right hand** of the Most High.' **I will remember** (H2142, M41) the deeds of the LORD… I will **ponder** (H1897, M42, *hagah*) all your work, and **meditate** (H7878, M15, *siach*) on your mighty deeds" (vv.10–12). The gem-finding — the psalm's hinge: a **deliberate, *willed* decision** — "**I will** remember… **I will** ponder" — to redirect the very same faculties *(stated)*. The operation: the same *remember/meditate/ponder* that **aggravated** when aimed at the present (v.3) are now **deliberately aimed at God's *past* deeds** — and *that* redirection resolves the crisis *(inferred: the identical verbs (zakar, siach, hagah) reappear, now with a *past-deeds* object, and the fainting turns to appeal)*. The finding: **the meditative faculty's effect depends on its *object*** — brooding on the unanswered present breeds despair; recalling God's *proven past* steadies the self. The resolution is not new feeling but a **willed change of what memory dwells on** *(inferred)*.

## What Psalm 77 says about the inner being
- **The soul can *refuse* comfort (v.2).** Grief can reach a pitch where the inner being actively declines consolation — a refusal, not merely an absence of comforters.
- **Remembering/meditating on the unanswered present *aggravates* (vv.3, 7–9).** Aimed at the crisis, the meditative faculty breeds despair — "I meditate and my spirit faints" — and feeds the doubting questions.
- **The crisis is resolved by a *willed redirection of memory* (vv.10–12).** A deliberate decision — "I *will* remember… ponder… meditate" — turns the very same faculties from the present to God's *ancient deeds*. The resolution is not new feeling but a willed change of what memory dwells on.
- **The meditative faculty's effect depends on its *object* (vv.3, 11–12).** The same *remember/meditate/ponder* breeds despair on the present and steadies the self on God's proven past. What the inner being *dwells on* determines whether meditation wounds or heals.

## Honest notes
- **The same-verbs-different-object structure** (zakar/siach/hagah aggravating in v.3, healing in vv.11–12) is the psalm's spine — a strong worked datum: the meditative faculty is *neutral*; its *object* sets its effect (with Ps 1:2 delight-meditation, 39:3 fire-fanning meditation, here despair vs steadiness). Worth flagging for the study's movements focus.
- **"refuses to be comforted" (v.2)** — *nacham* (M05) captured as a characteristic (comfort), here *refused*; the active-refusal-of-comfort operation read from the negation. Candidate for a distinct inner datum (grief declining consolation).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp at v.2; bearer=Asaph/LORD bleed via superscription; *faints/appeal* gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *soul* (H5315, M47, vv.1,2); *comforted* (H5162, M05, v.2); *remember* (H2142, M41, vv.3,6,11); *meditate/ponder* (H7878/H1897, M15/M42, vv.3,6,12); *appeal* (H2470, M03, v.10). *spirit* (H7307, seat=spirit) + *faints* captured gate-2 — the aggravation read from these.

## Psalm 78 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 78 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 78:1–72 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (vv.60 + others backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **A long historical-teaching psalm — honestly scoped.** Its bulk (the recital of Israel's rebellions and God's dealings across the exodus and settlement) is the *arena*. Its inner-being findings cluster in a few recurring notes: the **unsteady, unfaithful heart** of the rebellious (vv.8, 37); the **mouth–heart split** (vv.36–37); the **craving heart that tests God** (v.18); the tender **"he remembered that they were but flesh"** (v.39); and the **transmission of hope and memory** to the next generation (vv.7–8).

## The reading

**I. The unsteady, unfaithful heart (vv.8, 37).**
The rebellious generation is diagnosed inwardly: "a generation whose **heart** (H3820, the seat — M47) was **not steadfast** (H3559, *nakon* — fixed, established), whose **spirit** (H7307, the seat) was **not faithful** (H0539, M13, *aman*) to God" (v.8); and again, "their **heart** was **not steadfast** toward him; they were **not faithful** to his covenant" (v.37). The gem-finding: the mark of the rebellious inner being is a heart that **will not stay *fixed*** (*nakon*) and a spirit that **will not stay *faithful*** *(stated)*. The operation: **instability** — the heart keeps *shifting*, never established toward God *(inferred: "not steadfast/nakon" names an unfixed heart, the opposite of Ps 57:7's doubled "my heart is *nakon*" and 112:7's fixed heart)*. Rebellion is, at root, a heart that **won't hold still** toward God *(inferred)*.

**II. The mouth–heart split (vv.36–37).**
"But they **flattered** (H6601, *patah*) him with their **mouths**; they **lied** to him with their tongues. Their **heart** was not steadfast toward him" (vv.36–37). The finding: the inner being can **flatter God with the mouth while the heart is unfixed** — outward words masking an unsteady heart *(stated)*. The operation: the **speech–heart disjunction** (cf. Ps 12, 28:3, 62:4) — the tongue's flattery contradicting the heart's instability *(inferred: the "flattered with mouths… heart not steadfast" pairs false speech with an unfixed heart)*.

**III. The craving heart that tests God (v.18).**
"They **tested** (H5254, *nasah*) God **in their heart** (H3824, M47) by demanding the food they **craved** (H8378, M28, *ta'avah*)" (v.18). The finding: the inner being's **craving** (*ta'avah* — the appetite/desire) **drove it to *test* God** — putting God on trial out of appetite *(stated)*. The operation: disordered **craving becomes a testing** — the demanding desire turns the inner being against God, making it *try* him rather than trust him *(inferred: "tested God in their heart… the food they craved" makes the appetite the engine of the testing)*.

**IV. "He remembered that they were but flesh" (v.39).**
"He **remembered** (H2142, M41) that they were but **flesh** (H1320, the seat — M47, *basar*), a **wind** that passes and comes not again" (v.39). The gem-finding: God's compassion is grounded in his **accounting of the self's frailty** — he *remembered* they were "but flesh," a passing wind *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's **weakness** (flesh, wind) is **factored in** by God — his restraint flows from *remembering* how frail the creature is *(inferred: "he remembered they were but flesh" makes the divine compassion turn on a reckoning of human frailty; a tender datum — the self's weakness is *seen and allowed for*, cf. Ps 103:14 "he knows our frame")*.

**V. Transmission — that the next generation set its *hope* and not *forget* (vv.7–8), and the upright-hearted shepherd (v.72).**
"So that they should **set their hope** in God and **not forget** the works of God… and that they should **not be like their fathers**" (vv.7–8). The finding: the point of handing on the story is that the next inner being **set its hope** and **not forget** — hope and memory are the inner things transmitted *(stated; cf. Ps 48:13, 71:18)*. And the psalm closes on the counter-image of the unsteady heart: "With **upright heart** (*tom levav*) he shepherded them" (v.72) — the shepherd's **integrity of heart** against the people's instability *(stated)*.

## What Psalm 78 says about the inner being
- **Rebellion is, at root, an *unsteady heart* (vv.8, 37).** A heart not *fixed* (*nakon*) and a spirit not *faithful* — the inner being that will not hold still toward God. Instability is the mark, against the steadfast/fixed heart (57:7, 112:7).
- **The mouth can flatter while the heart is unfixed (vv.36–37).** Outward words mask an unsteady heart — the speech–heart disjunction.
- **Craving turns to *testing* God (v.18).** Disordered appetite drives the inner being to *try* God rather than trust him — the demanding desire the engine of the testing.
- **God accounts for the self's *frailty* (v.39).** His compassion is grounded in *remembering* the inner being is "but flesh," a passing wind — the self's weakness is seen and allowed for.
- **Hope and memory are what is transmitted (vv.7–8).** The story is handed on so the next inner being sets its *hope* and does not *forget* — against the counter-image of the shepherd's *upright heart* (v.72).

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** the great bulk (the exodus signs, the wilderness rebellions, the plagues, the settlement, the choice of Zion and David) is the historical/national arena; the inner-being weight is the recurring heart-diagnosis (vv.7–8, 18, 36–39, 72). A 72-verse psalm read for its inner-being notes, not verse-by-verse (not stanza-structured; standard reading, unlike the planned Ps 119 handling).
- **"steadfast/nakon" (H3559)** recurs (vv.8, 37) gate-2; the *unfixed-heart* operation read from the negation — a clean contrast with the *fixed* heart elsewhere (candidate for a heart-fixity characteristic, both poles).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (heavy prohibition over-stamp across the "not steadfast / not faithful / not forget" negations; bearer=Asaph/LORD bleed via superscription; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *heart* (H3820/H3824, M47, vv.8,18,37,72); *faithful* (H0539, M13, vv.8,37); *craved* (H8378, M28, v.18); *flesh* (H1320, M47, v.39); *covenant* (H1285, M44, v.37); *remember* (H2142, M41, v.39). *steadfast/flatter/tested* captured gate-2 — the instability, flattery, and testing read from these.

## Psalm 79 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 79 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 79:1–13 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (vv.10 + others backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **A community lament over ruined Jerusalem — honestly scoped.** The desolation and the plea for vengeance are the arena. Its inner-being finding: the appeal to be **met by compassion rather than by the record** — "do not remember our iniquities… let your compassion come to *meet* us" (v.8), grounded in being **brought very low**.

## The reading

**I. Met by compassion, not by the record (vv.8–9).**
"**Do not remember** (H2142, M41) against us our **former iniquities** (H5771, M10); let your **compassion** (H7356, M05, *racham*) come speedily **to meet** us, **for we are brought very low**… **atone** (H3722, M38) for our **sins** (H2403, M10)… for your name's sake" (vv.8–9). The finding: the inner being appeals to be **met by *compassion*, not remembered by its *iniquities*** — it asks God's memory to turn *from* the record *to* mercy *(stated)*. The operation: the plea is for compassion to **come out and *meet* the self** (a prevenient movement, cf. Ps 21:3's *qadam*, "meet"), and its ground is **the self's own lowness** — "for we are brought very low" *(stated)*. The finding: the inner being pleads **its lowness, not its merit** — and asks that its *sin be atoned* on God's *name's sake*, not its own standing *(inferred: "brought very low… atone… for your name's sake" makes the appeal rest on the self's need and God's name, not the self's worth; cf. Ps 25:7's "remember not the sins of my youth", 65:3's overpowering iniquities atoned)*.

## What Psalm 79 says about the inner being
- **The inner being appeals to be *met by compassion*, not by its record (vv.8–9).** It asks God's memory to turn from its iniquities to mercy — compassion coming out to *meet* it — and grounds the plea on its own *lowness* and God's *name*, not on any merit. To be brought very low is itself the ground of the appeal.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** the great bulk (the defiled temple, the slaughter, the taunting nations, the plea for vengeance, vv.1–7, 10–12) is the community/external arena; the inner-being weight is the compassion-not-record plea (vv.8–9). Thin psalm, noted plainly.
- **"compassion come to meet us" (v.8)** — *racham* (M05) captured as a characteristic; the *prevenient-meeting* read from the phrase (with Ps 21:3's *qadam*). The appeal-from-lowness is a clean datum (with 25:7, 65:3).
- **"how long… angry forever" (v.5, *anaph* H0599, M02)** — the duration-dread noted (cf. Ps 13, 74); the arena's "how long" rather than a distinct new inner operation.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp at v.8; bearer=Asaph/LORD bleed; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *angry* (H0599, M02, v.5); *remember* (H2142, M41, v.8); *iniquities/sins* (H5771/H2403, M10, vv.8,9); *compassion* (H7356, M05, v.8); *atone* (H3722, M38, v.9); *give-thanks* (H3034, M22, v.13).

## Psalm 80 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 80 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 80:1–19 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (vv.16 + others backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The face-shine as the means of restoration; grief as the self's food.** A community lament with a threefold refrain (the vine of Israel is the arena). Its inner-being findings: the self's **restoration comes through God's *shining face*** (vv.3, 7, 19); and the inner being's grief is figured as its **food and drink** — the *bread of tears* (v.5).

## The reading

**I. The shining face as the means of restoration (vv.3, 7, 19).**
The refrain, three times: "**Restore us**, O God; let your **face shine** (H0215, *or*), that we may be **saved**!" (vv.3, 7, 19). The finding: the inner being's **restoration and salvation are tied to God's *face shining* upon it** *(stated)*. The operation: the self is not restored by its own effort but by the **turning of God's lit, favourable face toward it** — "let your face shine… *that we may be saved*" makes the face-shine the *means* of the saving *(inferred: the shining face is the cause, the salvation the effect; the light-of-the-face thread, Ps 4:6, 31:16, 67:1)*. The refrain's repetition makes it the psalm's one persistent request — everything hinges on the face *(inferred)*.

**II. The bread of tears — grief as the self's sustenance (v.5).**
"You have fed them with the **bread of tears** (H1832, M03, *dimah*) and given them tears to **drink in full measure**" (v.5). The gem-finding: the inner being's **grief becomes its food and drink** — fed *with tears*, drinking tears *in full measure* *(stated)*. The operation: sorrow so pervasive it is the self's **entire intake** — grief is not an interruption of nourishment but *is* the nourishment; the inner being *lives on* its tears *(inferred: "bread of tears… tears to drink in full measure" makes grief the whole diet, filling both bread and cup; cf. Ps 42:3 "my tears have been my food")*.

## What Psalm 80 says about the inner being
- **Restoration comes through God's *shining face* (vv.3, 7, 19).** The inner being is saved not by its own effort but by God turning his lit, favourable face toward it — the face-shine is the *means* of the restoration, and the psalm's one persistent plea.
- **Grief can become the self's *food and drink* (v.5).** Fed with the bread of tears, drinking tears in full measure — sorrow so pervasive it *is* the inner being's sustenance, its whole intake.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** the vine-allegory (Israel brought out of Egypt, planted, ravaged, vv.8–16) and the plea for the man of God's right hand are the community/external arena; the inner-being weight is the face-shine refrain (vv.3, 7, 19) and the bread of tears (v.5).
- **"face shine" (H0215/H6440)** captured gate-2; the *face-shine-as-means-of-restoration* read from the refrain — a strong recurrence of the light-of-the-face thread (4:6, 31:16, 67:1).
- **"bread of tears" (H1832, *dimah*, M03)** — *tears* correctly a characteristic (sorrow cluster); the grief-as-diet read from the bread/drink pairing (with 42:3, 102:9).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=Joseph/Manasseh/LORD bleed via superscription; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *tears* (H1832, M03, v.5). *face/shine/saved/life/call* captured gate-2 — the face-shine restoration and the bread of tears read from these.

## Psalm 81 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 81 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 81:1–16 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (vv.13 + others backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The listening self versus the one given over to its stubborn heart.** Psalm 81's findings turn on *listening*: the refusal to listen results in being **given over to one's own stubborn heart** (vv.11–12) — abandonment to the self as the judgment; while **receptivity — "open your mouth wide" — is met by God's *filling*** (v.10); and not-listening **forfeits the good God longed to give** (v.16).

## The reading

**I. Refusal to listen → given over to the stubborn heart (vv.11–12).**
"But my people **did not listen** (H8085) to my voice; Israel **would not submit** (H0014, *abah*) to me. So **I gave them over to their stubborn hearts** (H8307, M30, *sheriruth* + H3820, the seat — M47), to follow their **own counsels** (H4156, M17, *moetsah*)" (vv.11–12). The gem-finding: the judgment on the non-listening inner being is to be **handed back to its own hardened heart** — "given over to their stubborn hearts, to follow their own counsels" *(stated)*. The operation: **refusal to listen → abandonment to the self** — God's deepest response to the closed ear is not to force it but to **let it follow its own stubborn heart**, which *is* the punishment *(inferred: "would not submit… so I gave them over to their stubborn hearts" makes the being-left-to-oneself the consequence of the not-listening — a self-perpetuating captivity to one's own hardness)*. To not listen is to be **shut up in one's own counsels** *(inferred)*.

**II. Receptivity met by filling — "open your mouth wide" (v.10).**
"I am the LORD your God, who brought you up out of Egypt. **Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it**" (v.10). The gem-finding: the inner being that **opens itself wide** to God is **filled** by him *(stated)*. The operation: **receptivity is the condition of being filled** — the *open* mouth is met by God's abundance, the exact inverse of the *closed*, stubborn heart of v.12 *(inferred: the "open wide → I will fill" of v.10 contrasts the un-submitting, self-following heart of vv.11–12 — the open self is filled, the closed self is left empty to itself)*. The self's part is simply to **open**; the filling is God's *(inferred; cf. Ps 40:6's dug ear — receptivity as the thing God seeks)*.

**III. The forfeited good — God's thwarted longing (vv.13, 16).**
"**Oh, that my people would listen to me**, that Israel would walk in my ways!… But he would **feed** you with the **finest of the wheat**, and with honey from the rock I would **satisfy** you" (vv.13, 16). The finding: God **yearns** for the self to listen — "*oh, that* my people would listen" — because a **satisfaction is waiting** that the not-listening forfeits *(stated)*. The operation: the refusal to listen **forfeits the good God longed to give** — the finest wheat, honey from the rock, a satisfaction held out but not received *(inferred: the "oh that… I would feed/satisfy you" names the thwarted good, lost by the closed ear)*. The inner being's non-listening does not merely disobey; it **loses the feast** *(inferred)*.

## What Psalm 81 says about the inner being
- **The judgment on the non-listening self is to be *given over to its own stubborn heart* (vv.11–12).** God's response to the closed ear is not to force it but to let it follow its own hardened counsels — abandonment to the self, a self-perpetuating captivity to one's own stubbornness. To not listen is to be shut up in one's own heart.
- **Receptivity — the open self — is met by *filling* (v.10).** "Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it." The inner being's part is simply to open; the filling is God's. The open self is filled; the closed, stubborn self is left empty to itself.
- **Not-listening *forfeits the waiting good* (vv.13, 16).** God yearns for the self to listen because a satisfaction — the finest wheat, honey from the rock — is held out; the refusal loses the feast, not merely disobeys.

## Honest notes
- **"stubborn heart" (H8307, *sheriruth*, M30 + H3820, M47)** — the *hardened, self-willed heart* captured (seat=heart); the *given-over-to-the-self* operation read from vv.11–12. A strong datum: the judgment on the closed ear is *abandonment to one's own heart* (a distinct mechanism — cf. the self-deafening adder of Ps 58:4, here the consequence of it).
- **"open your mouth wide… fill it" (v.10)** captured gate-2; receptivity-met-by-filling read from it — the inverse of the stubborn heart (with Ps 40:6's dug ear).
- **Scope honesty:** the festival call (vv.1–5) and the exodus recital (vv.6–7) are the arena; the inner-being weight is the listen/stubborn-heart/open-mouth material (vv.8–16).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp at vv.11; bearer=Egypt/Israel/LORD bleed via superscription; *listen/submit/fill/feed* gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *stubborn/hearts* (H8307/H3820, M30/M47, v.12); *counsels* (H4156, M17, v.12). *listen/submit/open/fill/feed/satisfy* captured gate-2 — the not-listening, the given-over, and the filling read from these.

## Psalm 82 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 82 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 82:1–8 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; **aheb-fix build**). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Injustice rooted in inner blindness.** A psalm of God judging the unjust "gods"/rulers (the divine-council scene is the arena). Its one inner-being finding: injustice flows from a **failure of inner *perception*** — "they have neither knowledge nor understanding; they walk about in darkness" (v.5).

## The reading

**I. Injustice flows from inner blindness (v.5).**
Against the charge to "give **justice** (H8199, M26) to the weak… rescue the needy" (vv.3–4), the unjust are diagnosed inwardly: "They have **neither knowledge nor understanding** (H0995, M15, *bin*), they **walk about in darkness**; all the foundations of the earth are shaken" (v.5). The finding: injustice is not merely bad policy but a **failure of the inner faculty of understanding** — "neither knowledge nor understanding" *(stated)*. The operation: the unjust inner being **lacks perception** — it cannot *see* (walks in darkness), and from that inner blindness the outward injustice flows, until "the foundations… are shaken" *(inferred: "no understanding… walk in darkness… foundations shaken" chains the inner lack to the cosmic disorder — the failure of inner sight destabilises the world; cf. Ps 36:1–4's self-enclosed wicked, 14:2's God scanning for the understanding)*. Injustice has an **inner root: a darkened, un-understanding self** *(inferred)*.

## What Psalm 82 says about the inner being
- **Injustice is rooted in a *failure of inner perception* (v.5).** The unjust "have neither knowledge nor understanding" and "walk about in darkness" — a darkened, un-understanding self, from which the outward injustice flows and the world's foundations are shaken. The inner lack of *sight* is the root.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** the divine-council scene (God arraigning the unjust "gods", their mortality, vv.1–4, 6–8) is the arena; the inner-being weight is v.5's diagnosis of inner blindness. Short psalm, noted plainly.
- **"understanding" (H0995, *bin*, M15)** correctly a characteristic (here negated — its *absence*); the inner-blindness operation read from "no knowledge/understanding… walk in darkness" (with Ps 14:2, 36:1–4).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp at v.5 "neither… nor"; bearer=Asaph/LORD bleed; intensity *all*) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *give-justice* (H8199, M26, v.3); *understanding* (H0995, M15, v.5, negated). *knowledge/darkness/shaken* captured gate-2 — the inner blindness read from these.

## Psalm 83 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 83 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 83:1–18 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (vv.14 + others backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **An imprecatory community lament — honestly scoped.** The list of conspiring nations and the plea for their overthrow are the arena. Two inner-being findings: the enemies' **united heart** in conspiracy (v.5); and the **redemptive aim** hidden in the imprecation — that shame drive them to *seek* God (v.16).

## The reading

**I. The enemies' *one heart* in conspiracy (v.5).**
"For they **conspire** (H3289, M15, *yaats* — take counsel, devise) **with one heart** (H3820, the seat — M47, *leb* — 'one accord'); against you they make a **covenant** (H1285, M44)" (v.5). The finding: the wicked's hostility is a **united inner disposition** — a *single heart* devising against God *(stated)*. The operation: the conspiring inner beings are **welded into one heart** — a corporate unison of malice, bound by a mutual covenant *(inferred: "conspire with one heart" makes the hostility a shared, unified inner posture, not scattered individual grudges)*.

**II. The redemptive aim of shame — "that they may seek your name" (v.16).**
"Fill their faces with **shame** (H7036, M07), **that they may seek** (H1245, M41) your name, O LORD" (v.16). The gem-finding: even the imprecation carries a **redemptive purpose** — the shame is aimed at the enemies' eventual **seeking** of God *(stated)*. The operation: shame is **not the end but the means** — "that they may *seek* your name" — the humbling of the hostile inner being is directed toward its **turning to God** *(inferred: the "shame… that they may seek" makes the shame instrumental to the enemies' seeking/knowing, v.18; the imprecation bends toward their conversion)*.

## What Psalm 83 says about the inner being
- **Hostility can be a *united heart* (v.5).** The conspiring wicked are welded into "one heart" — a corporate unison of malice bound by covenant, not scattered grudges.
- **Shame can be aimed at *seeking* (v.16).** Even the imprecation carries a redemptive purpose — the humbling of the hostile self is directed toward its turning to seek God's name; shame the means, seeking the end.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** the great bulk (the roll-call of enemy nations, the plea for their overthrow like Midian/Sisera, vv.2–4, 6–18) is the external/imprecatory arena; the inner-being weight is the one-heart conspiracy (v.5) and the redemptive aim of shame (v.16).
- **"one heart" (H3820, v.5)** correctly a characteristic (seat=heart) — the *unified-hostile-heart* read from "with one accord/heart"; a datum on corporate inner disposition (contrast the individual's divided heart, Ps 12).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp at v.1; bearer=Asaph/LORD bleed via superscription; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *still* (H8252, M33, v.1); *conspire* (H3289, M15, v.5); *accord/heart* (H3820, M47, v.5); *covenant* (H1285, M44, v.5); *shame/put-to-shame* (H7036/H0954, M07, vv.16,17); *seek* (H1245, M41, v.16).

## Psalm 84 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 84 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 84:1–12 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The longing for God's dwelling, and the pilgrim self with the way in its heart.** Psalm 84's findings: a **whole-being longing** — soul faints with yearning while heart and flesh sing (v.2); the **pilgrim-roads carried *within the heart*** (v.5); a journey that **accumulates strength** and turns the valley of tears to springs (vv.6–7); and the **re-valuation** — a day/threshold near God outweighs a thousand elsewhere (v.10).

## The reading

**I. Whole-being longing — ache and joy together (vv.1–2).**
"How **lovely** is your dwelling place… My **soul** (H5315, the seat — M47) **longs** (H3700, M18, *kasaph* — yearns), yes, **faints** for the courts of the LORD; my **heart** (H3820, M47) and **flesh** (H1320, seat=flesh — M47) **sing for joy** (H7442, M42) to the living God" (vv.1–2). The finding: the longing for God's presence-place engages the **whole person** — *soul* and *flesh* — and it holds **ache and joy at once** *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's desire is **total and consuming** ("faints" — spent with yearning) *and simultaneously* breaks into **song** — the soul *aches* while the heart and flesh *sing* *(inferred: "longs… faints… sing for joy" combines the consuming yearning and the joy in one movement; cf. Ps 63:1's soul-thirsts/flesh-faints, here with the added *joy*)*.

**II. The pilgrim-roads *within the heart* (v.5).**
"Blessed are those whose **strength** (H5797, M23) is in you, in whose **heart** (H3824, the seat — M47) are the **highways** (H4546, *mesillah* — the pilgrim-roads) to Zion" (v.5). The gem-finding: the inner being can carry the **roads to God's dwelling *inside* the heart** — "in whose *heart* are the highways to Zion" *(stated)*. The operation: the pilgrimage is **interiorised** — the *way* to God is set *within* the inner being, the heart already **oriented toward and travelling** the road to the dwelling *(inferred: "the highways… in the heart" locates the journey in the interior — the heart is on the way before the feet are)*. The self whose *strength* is in God has the *road* in its heart.

**III. A journey that *accumulates* strength (vv.6–7).**
"As they go through the **Valley of Baca** (weeping) they make it a place of **springs**… They go **from strength to strength** (H2428, M23); each one appears before God in Zion" (vv.6–7). Two findings. The inner being **turns the valley of tears into springs** as it passes — it *transforms* the place of weeping in the going *(stated)*. And it goes **"from strength to strength"** — the God-ward journey **accumulates rather than depletes** strength *(stated)*. The operation: unlike ordinary travel that tires, the pilgrim inner being **grows stronger as it goes** — the journey toward God is *strengthening*, and even its valleys become sources *(inferred: "Valley of Baca… springs… strength to strength" makes the road a place of increasing, not diminishing, power; cf. Ps 71:14's hope "more and more")*.

**IV. The re-valuation — a day, a threshold, outweighs a thousand (v.10).**
"For a **day** in your courts is better than a **thousand** elsewhere. I would rather be a **doorkeeper** in the house of my God than dwell in the tents of wickedness" (v.10). The gem-finding: the inner being's value-hierarchy is **re-ordered** — *proximity* to God, even *briefly* (a day) and at the *lowest place* (a doorkeeper, the threshold), **outweighs abundance and status elsewhere** *(stated)*. The operation: the self prizes **nearness over quantity and position** — a day at the threshold near God is worth more than a thousand days, a doorkeeper's place worth more than dwelling among the wicked *(inferred: "a day… better than a thousand… doorkeeper rather than dwell in wickedness" re-values nearness above duration and rank; cf. Ps 63:3 chesed>life, 73:28 nearness is my good)*.

## What Psalm 84 says about the inner being
- **The longing for God's dwelling is *whole-being* — ache and joy at once (vv.1–2).** Soul and flesh together; the soul *faints* with yearning while the heart and flesh *sing* — the consuming desire and the joy held in one movement.
- **The pilgrim-roads can be carried *within the heart* (v.5).** The way to God's dwelling is interiorised — the heart is on the road before the feet are; the self whose strength is in God has the journey set within it.
- **The God-ward journey *accumulates* strength (vv.6–7).** Unlike ordinary travel, it goes "from strength to strength" — the inner being grows stronger as it goes, and even the valley of tears is turned to springs in the passing.
- **Nearness outweighs quantity and rank (v.10).** A day at the threshold near God is worth more than a thousand elsewhere; the doorkeeper's lowest place outweighs dwelling among the wicked. The value-hierarchy is re-ordered around proximity.

## Honest notes
- **A strong longing-and-journey exemplar** (whole-being longing → the way in the heart → strength-to-strength → re-valuation); a good worked datum for the study's *movement* focus, alongside Ps 63 and 42–43.
- **"longs" (H3700, *kasaph*, M18)** correctly a characteristic (the yearning); "highways in the heart" (H4546) and "strength to strength" (H2428) captured — the interiorised journey and accumulating strength read from these.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=Korah/LORD bleed via superscription; *faints/highways/springs/doorkeeper* gate-2) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *soul* (H5315, M47, v.2); *longs* (H3700, M18, v.2); *heart* (H3820/H3824, M47, vv.2,5); *flesh* (H1320, M47, v.2); *sing-for-joy* (H7442, M42, v.2); *strength* (H5797/H2428, M23, vv.5,7); *uprightly* (H8549, M12, v.11).

## Psalm 85 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 85 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 85:1–13 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The listening posture, poised for God's word of peace.** A community restoration psalm (the reconciled attributes — steadfast love and faithfulness meeting, vv.10–13 — are the arena). Its inner-being finding: the deliberate posture of **listening for what God will speak**, expecting *peace*, with the caution not to relapse into folly (v.8).

## The reading

**I. "Let me hear what God will speak" — the listening posture (v.8).**
"**Let me hear** (H8085, *shama*) what God the LORD will **speak**, for he will speak **peace** (H7965, M33, *shalom*) to his people, to his saints; **but let them not turn back to folly** (H3690, M19, *kesel*)" (v.8). The finding: the inner being takes up a deliberate posture of **attentive listening** — *waiting to hear* what God will say — and it **expects peace** *(stated)*. The operation: the self **quiets and attends for God's word** — the receptive listening-stance (the exact opposite of Ps 81's people who "would not listen" and were given over to their stubborn hearts) *(inferred: "let me hear what God will speak" is the self poising itself to receive, expecting shalom)*. And the caution completes it: the listening must not **relapse into *folly*** ("let them not turn back") — the receptive posture is guarded against sliding back *(stated)*.

## What Psalm 85 says about the inner being
- **The inner being can take up a *listening posture*, poised for God's word (v.8).** "Let me hear what God will speak" — the self quiets and attends, expecting *peace*; the receptive stance that is the opposite of the stubborn, non-listening heart (Ps 81). And it is *guarded* — the listening must not relapse into folly.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** the restoration plea (vv.1–7, incl. "revive us again", v.6) and the reconciled attributes (steadfast love/faithfulness meet, righteousness/peace kiss, vv.10–13) are the arena; the inner-being weight is the listening posture (v.8).
- **"folly" (H3690, *kesel*, M19)** — *kesel* spans "confidence/loins" and "folly/stupidity"; here the negative sense (relapse into folly), a per-occurrence note; the *listening-guarded-against-relapse* read from v.8.
- **Cross-psalm:** v.8's *listening* is the positive counterpart to Ps 81's *refusal to listen* → given over to the stubborn heart. Recorded as a thread.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp at vv.6, 8; bearer=LORD bleed) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *revive* (H2421, M25, v.6); *steadfast-love* (H2617, M05, v.10); *peace* (H7965, M33, vv.8,10); *faithfulness* (H0571, M13, vv.10,11); *righteousness* (H6664, M26, vv.10,11,13). *hear/speak* captured gate-2 — the listening posture read from these.

## Psalm 86 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 86 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 86:1–17 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (v.8 backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The divided heart made one.** Psalm 86's key finding: the plea **"unite my heart to fear your name"** (v.11) — the inner being is *divided/scattered* and asks God to **gather it into a single focus**; and the fruit is thanks with the **whole heart** (v.12). Around this: the soul **lifted up** to God (v.4).

## The reading

**I. "Unite my heart" — the divided heart gathered into one (v.11).**
"Teach me your way, O LORD, that I may walk in your **truth** (H0571, M13); **unite** (*yachad* — make one, join together) my **heart** (H3824, the seat — M47) to **fear** (H3372, M01) your name" (v.11). The gem-finding: the inner being asks to have its heart **made *one*** — which implies the heart is **divided, scattered** and needs **gathering** *(stated: "unite my heart" presupposes a heart not yet single)*. The operation: the **unification of a fragmented heart** — the many pulls of the inner being drawn together into **a single focus, the fear of God's name** *(inferred: yachad "unite/make one" gathers the divided heart from its scatter into one object; the inverse of the "double heart" of Ps 12)*. And crucially, the self **cannot do this to itself** — it *asks God* to unite it: the gathering of the divided heart is **God's work requested**, not the self's achievement *(inferred: "*unite* my heart" is a petition, the self handing its fragmentation to God to be made whole)*.

**II. Thanks with the *whole* heart — the fruit (v.12).**
"I give **thanks** (H3034, M22) to you, O Lord my God, **with my whole heart** (H3824, M47), and I will glorify your name forever" (v.12). The finding: the response is from the **whole, undivided heart** — the *fruit* of the unification asked in v.11 *(stated)*. The operation: the **united heart issues in whole-hearted thanks** — where v.11 asked for the heart to be made one, v.12 gives thanks from that oneness; the gathered heart is a heart that can worship *entire*, not in fragments *(inferred: "unite my heart" (v.11) → "with my whole heart" (v.12) — the petition and its fruit)*.

**III. The soul lifted up to God (v.4).**
"Gladden the **soul** (H5315, the seat — M47) of your servant, for **to you, O Lord, do I lift up my soul** (H5375, M19, *nasa nephesh*)" (v.4). The finding: the inner being **lifts up its soul to God** — the aspiration/longing directed upward *(stated; the *nasa-nephesh* idiom of Ps 25:1, 143:8)*. The operation: the self **raises its whole inner being toward God** as the ground of its gladdening — "gladden my soul, *for* to you I lift it up" *(inferred: the lifted soul is the posture within which it asks to be gladdened)*.

## What Psalm 86 says about the inner being
- **The heart can be *divided*, and needs to be *united* (v.11).** "Unite my heart to fear your name" presupposes a scattered heart pulled many ways; the operation is its *gathering* into a single focus on God. And the self *cannot unify itself* — it asks God to make it one; the wholeness is God's work requested.
- **The united heart issues in *whole-hearted* thanks (v.12).** Where v.11 asks for oneness, v.12 gives thanks "with my whole heart" — the gathered heart can worship *entire*, not in fragments. Petition and fruit.
- **The inner being *lifts up its soul* to God (v.4).** The whole self raised toward God — the posture within which it asks to be gladdened.

## Honest notes
- **A cornerstone-level datum:** "unite my heart" (v.11) names the inner being's *fragmentation* and the operation of its *unification* — a key disclosure for the study's movements focus (the divided heart, its gathering; with the "double heart" of Ps 12, the "whole heart" thread of 9:1, 111:1, 119:2).
- **"unite" (*yachad*, v.11)** captured gate-2; the *make-one/gather* operation read from the verb. Candidate to promote a *heart-unification / divided-heart* inner mechanism.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed pervasive; intensity *all/many*; *unite/lift* gate-2; backfilled v.8 now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *life/soul* (H5315, M47, vv.2,4,13); *godly* (H2623, M05, v.2); *lift-up* (H5375, M19, v.4); *truth* (H0571, M13, v.11); *heart* (H3824, M47, vv.11,12); *fear* (H3372, M01, v.11); *give-thanks* (H3034, M22, v.12); *steadfast-love* (H2617, M05, vv.5,13,15).
