## Psalm 87 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 87 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 87:1–7 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; **aheb-fix build** — "loves" H0157 v.2 now correctly `role=characteristic`). Complete chapter (vv.7 + others backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **A short Zion hymn — honestly scoped.** The city's glory and God's registering of the nations are the arena. Its two inner-being findings: **belonging by *birth* in God's city** (vv.4–6); and the **wellsprings of the self located in God** — "all my springs are in you" (v.7).

## The reading

**I. Belonging by *birth* in the city (vv.4–6).**
"'**This one was born there**,' they say… of Zion it shall be said, 'This one and that one were **born** in her'… The LORD **records** as he registers the peoples, 'This one was born there'" (vv.4–6). The finding: the inner being's **belonging is figured as *birth* in God's city** — its identity is being *registered* as *born there* *(stated)*. The operation: the self's deepest belonging is **not chosen but conferred by origin** — to be *born* in Zion, recorded by God's own hand, is an identity **given, not achieved** *(inferred: "born there… the LORD records" makes the belonging an origin conferred and registered by God)*.

**II. "All my springs are in you" — the self's wellsprings located in God (v.7).**
"Singers and dancers alike say, '**All my springs** (H4599, *mayan* — fountains) **are in you**'" (v.7). The gem-finding: the inner being's **sources — its wellsprings of life and joy — are *in God/Zion***, not in itself *(stated)*. The operation: the self locates its **fountains outside itself**, in God — everything that *springs up* within it (its joy, its life) flows from a source it does not own *(inferred: "all my springs are in you" makes God the reservoir from which the inner being's vitality wells; the singers/dancers' joy has its source there, cf. Ps 36:9's "fountain of life", 84:6's springs)*.

## What Psalm 87 says about the inner being
- **Belonging is conferred by *birth* (vv.4–6).** The inner being's identity is being *born* in God's city, registered by God's own hand — a belonging given by origin, not achieved.
- **The self's *wellsprings* are located in God (v.7).** "All my springs are in you" — the fountains of the inner being's life and joy flow from God, a source it does not own. What springs up within it has its reservoir outside itself.

## Honest notes
- **aheb-fix confirmed:** "loves" (H0157, v.2, "the LORD *loves* the gates of Zion") now correctly `role=characteristic` under `PROMOTE_CHARACTERISTIC` — first live confirmation in a newly-built psalm.
- **"all my springs are in you" (H4599, v.7)** captured gate-2; the *wellsprings-in-God* read from it (with 36:9, 84:6). A clean datum: the self's sources located outside itself.
- **Scope honesty:** short psalm; the Zion-glory and the registering of nations (vv.1–6) are the arena; the inner-being weight is the birth-belonging (vv.4–6) and the springs (v.7).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=Korah/Zion/LORD bleed via superscription; intensity *all*; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *loves* (H0157, v.2 — now characteristic via the fix). *born/springs* captured gate-2 — the birth-belonging and wellsprings read from these.

## Psalm 88 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 88 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 88:1–18 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (vv.13 + others backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The psalm of unrelieved darkness — read on its own terms, without forcing a turn.** Psalm 88 is the one lament in the Psalter that **never resolves** — it ends in darkness. Its inner-being findings: the **soul *sated* with trouble** (v.3); the **persistence of prayer *in* the darkness**, without any turn to hope (vv.1, 9, 13); and the self left with **darkness as its only companion** (v.18). *(The reading honours the psalm's refusal to resolve — it does not import a comfort the text withholds; memory `feedback_verse_meaning_grounded_not_imported`.)*

## The reading

**I. The soul *sated* with trouble (vv.3–4).**
"For my **soul** (H5315, the seat — M47) is **full** (*saba* — sated) of **troubles** (H7451, M03, *ra*), and my **life** (H2416, M25) draws near to Sheol… I am a man who has **no strength** (H0353, M23, *eyal*)" (vv.3–4). The gem-finding: the inner being is **saturated with affliction** — the soul *sated*, *filled to capacity*, with trouble *(stated)*. The operation: the very verb of *satisfaction* (*saba*, "full/sated" — the word for the soul *satisfied* with good in Ps 63:5) is here inverted — the soul is **full, but of *trouble***, drained of strength *(inferred: the soul "full of troubles" is satisfaction's dark inverse — filled to the brim, but with affliction, not good)*. The inner being is *at capacity* with suffering *(inferred)*.

**II. Prayer persists *in* the darkness — without resolution (vv.1, 9, 13).**
"O LORD, God of my salvation, **I cry out day and night** before you… my eye grows dim through **sorrow** (H6040, M24). **Every day I call** upon you… I spread out my hands to you… But I, O LORD, **cry to you**; in the morning my **prayer** comes before you" (vv.1, 9, 13). The gem-finding: **even in unrelieved darkness, the inner being keeps *crying to God*** — day and night, every day, in the morning — though **nothing turns** *(stated)*. The operation: the psalm has **no resolution** (unique among the laments — no "but you," no light), yet the self **still addresses God** *(inferred)*. The finding — profound: the inner being can **keep praying from within total abandonment** — faith here is **not a felt hope but a persistence of address** — the self holds on to *speak to God* even when it experiences only his silence and his "no" *(inferred: the sustained "I cry… I call… my prayer comes before you" *without any turn* discloses a faith that is sheer continued address, not resolved comfort)*.

**III. The questions of abandonment (v.14).**
"O LORD, **why do you cast my soul away? Why do you hide your face** from me?" (v.14). The finding: the inner being's **unanswered *why*** — questioning God's abandonment (as Ps 22:1, 77:7) — but here **left unanswered**, the questions standing open *(stated)*. The operation: the self **puts its abandonment to God as a question** and receives no reply within the psalm — the interrogation itself is an act of address to the one who seems absent *(inferred)*.

**IV. Darkness the only companion (vv.8, 18).**
"You have caused my companions to shun me… You have caused my beloved and my friend to shun me; **my companions have become darkness**" (vv.8, 18). The gem-finding: stripped of every human companion, the inner being is left with **darkness as its only intimate** — "my closest acquaintance is darkness" *(stated)*. The operation: the self's **total isolation** — all beloved and friends withdrawn, so that the only remaining *company* is the dark *(inferred: "my companions have become darkness" makes the darkness the sole intimate, the ultimate loneliness)*. **The psalm ends here** — no light follows *(stated)*.

## What Psalm 88 says about the inner being
- **The soul can be *sated with trouble* (v.3).** The very word for satisfaction is inverted — the inner being *full to capacity*, but of affliction, not good; drained of strength.
- **Faith can be *sheer persistence of address* (vv.1, 9, 13).** The inner being keeps crying to God — day and night, morning by morning — from within *unrelieved* darkness, with no turn to hope. Faith here is not felt comfort but the refusal to stop speaking to God even when it experiences only his "no."
- **Abandonment can be put to God as an open *question* (v.14).** "Why do you hide your face?" — asked and left unanswered; the interrogation itself an act of address to the seemingly-absent.
- **The self can be left with *darkness as its only companion* (v.18).** Stripped of every human intimate, the inner being's sole remaining company is the dark — and the psalm ends there, no light. That the study's data includes *this* — a genuine inner-being state without resolution — is itself the finding.

## Honest notes
- **Scope/honesty:** this is the Psalter's one *unresolved* lament; the reading deliberately does **not** supply the turn the text refuses. Its value to the study is precisely that the inner being's range *includes* unrelieved darkness held in continued address to God (a datum, not a defect).
- **"soul full of troubles" (H5315 + *saba* + H7451, v.3)** — the *sated-with-trouble* read as satisfaction's inverse (with 63:5's satisfied soul); a clean datum.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=Korah/Heman/LORD bleed via the long superscription; intensity *all*; *cry/darkness/companions* gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *soul* (H5315, M47, vv.3,14); *life* (H2416, M25, v.3); *strength* (H0353, M23, v.4); *sorrow* (H6040, M24, v.9); *cry* (H7440, M42, v.2). *cry-out/prayer/hide-face/darkness* captured gate-2 — the persistence of prayer and the darkness read from these.

## Psalm 89 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 89 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 89:1–52 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (closes Book III; vv.27 + others backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **A long covenant psalm — honestly scoped.** The recital of God's steadfast love and the Davidic covenant (and the closing lament that it seems broken) are the arena. Two inner-being findings: the blessed self **walking in the light of God's face** (vv.15–16); and the awareness of **its own short time** amid the unanswered "how long" (vv.46–48).

## The reading

**I. Walking in the light of God's face (vv.15–16).**
"Blessed are the people who **know the festal shout** (*teruah* — the joyful acclamation), who **walk**, O LORD, in the **light** (H0216) of your **face** (H6440); who **exult** in your name all the day, and in your righteousness are **exalted**" (vv.15–16). The finding: the blessed inner being is one that **knows the festal shout** and **walks in the light of God's *face***, its whole day shaped by exultation in the name *(stated)*. The operation: the self's life is **lived *in* God's lit face** — the *light of the face* (the Aaronic-blessing thread, Ps 4:6, 31:16, 80:3) is not a momentary favour but the **medium the blessed inner being walks in**, "all the day" *(inferred: "walk… in the light of your face… exult all the day" makes the lit face a continuous atmosphere of life, not a passing gift)*.

**II. The short time, amid the unanswered "how long" (vv.46–48).**
"**How long**, O LORD? Will you hide yourself forever?… **Remember how short my time is!**… What man can live and never see death? Who can deliver his **soul** (H5315, M47) from the power of Sheol?" (vv.46–48). The finding: against God's seeming absence ("how long… hide yourself"), the inner being pleads **its own brevity** — "remember how short my time is" *(stated)*. The operation: the self **presses its *finitude* as an argument** — it cannot afford an unbounded wait, for its time is short and no one delivers his own soul from death *(inferred: "how long… remember how short my time is… who can deliver his soul from Sheol" makes the self's mortality the ground of the urgency; cf. Ps 39:4, 90:12)*.

## What Psalm 89 says about the inner being
- **The blessed self *walks in the light of God's face* (vv.15–16).** Knowing the festal shout, exulting in the name "all the day" — the lit face is the continuous atmosphere the blessed inner being lives in, not a passing favour.
- **The self presses its own *finitude* as an argument (vv.46–48).** Amid God's seeming absence, it pleads "how short my time is" — its mortality the ground of its urgency; it cannot afford an unbounded wait, and cannot deliver its own soul from death.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** the great bulk (God's steadfast love and faithfulness, the creation/kingship recital, the Davidic covenant, and the closing lament that it seems cast off, vv.1–14, 19–45, 49–52) is the covenant/royal arena; the inner-being weight is the light-of-the-face blessedness (vv.15–16) and the finitude plea (vv.46–48). A 52-verse psalm read for its inner-being notes.
- **"light of your face" (H0216/H6440, v.15)** captured gate-2; the *walking-in-the-lit-face* read from it (a strong recurrence of the face-light thread).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=Ethan/LORD bleed via superscription; prohibition at v.48; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *steadfast-love* (H2617, M05, throughout); *rejoice* (H8055, M04, v.16); *soul* (H5315, M47, v.48). *festal-shout/walk/light/face/short-time* captured gate-2 — the walking-in-the-light and the finitude read from these.

## Psalm 90 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 90 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 90:1–17 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (opens Book IV; vv.4 + others backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Numbering the days for wisdom; morning satisfaction against the brief life.** Psalm 90's findings: the inner being's **secret sins exposed** in God's light (v.8); its whole life figured as a **sigh** (v.9); the plea to **number its days** so as to gain a **heart of wisdom** (v.12); and the plea to be **satisfied in the morning** with God's steadfast love so the short days are glad (v.14).

## The reading

**I. Secret sins in the light of God's presence (v.8).**
"You have set our **iniquities** (H5771, M10) before you, our **secret sins** (H5956, M14, *alum* — the *concealed*) in the **light** of your **presence** (H6440)" (v.8). The finding: the inner being's **hidden, concealed sins are fully exposed** in God's presence-light — nothing is out of view *(stated)*. The operation: the *concealed* self (the *alum*, the same root as the dissemblers of Ps 26:4) is **illuminated by God's presence** — what the inner being hides even from itself stands in the light *(inferred: "secret/concealed sins in the light of your presence" makes the hidden fully seen; cf. Ps 19:12's hidden faults, 44:21's secrets of the heart)*.

**II. The life as a *sigh* (vv.9–10).**
"For all our days pass away under your wrath; we **bring our years to an end like a sigh** (H1899, *hegeh* — a murmur/moan)… their span is but toil and trouble; they are soon gone, and **we fly away**" (vv.9–10). The finding: the inner being's whole life is figured as a single **breathed-out sigh** — brief, exhaled, gone *(stated)*. The operation: the self grasps its life as **momentary and toilsome** — a sigh, soon flown *(inferred: "years to an end like a sigh… soon gone… fly away" compresses the whole life to a breath; cf. Ps 39:5's breath, 144:4)*.

**III. Numbering the days → a heart of wisdom (v.12).**
"So **teach us to number** (H4487, *manah* — count) our **days** that we may **get a heart of wisdom** (H3824, the seat — M47 + H2451, *chokmah*)" (v.12). The gem-finding: the inner being asks to **learn to *count* its days** — to grasp its brevity — **so that it may gain a heart of wisdom** *(stated)*. The operation: **wisdom is the *fruit* of rightly grasping finitude** — the inner being that *numbers its days* (feels how few they are) becomes *wise* *(inferred: "number our days *that we may get* a heart of wisdom" makes the counting the means, the wise heart the end; cf. Ps 39's finitude-grasped)*. And crucially, **God must teach the counting** — the self cannot rightly number its own days without instruction; the grasp of finitude is a God-given lesson, not a self-achievement *(inferred: "*teach us* to number" hands the counting to God)*.

**IV. Morning satisfaction against the brief life (v.14).**
"**Satisfy** us in the **morning** with your **steadfast love** (H2617, M05), that we may **rejoice** (H7442, M42) and be **glad** (H8055, M04) **all our days**" (v.14). The gem-finding: against the brief, toilsome life (vv.9–10), the inner being pleads to be **satisfied with God's *chesed*** — a satisfaction that makes the *few* days **glad** *(stated)*. The operation: the short span is **redeemed into gladness** not by lengthening it but by **filling it with God's steadfast love** — "satisfy us… that we may be glad *all our days*" *(inferred: the plea does not ask for more days but for the days to be *satisfied with chesed*, turning toil to gladness)*.

## What Psalm 90 says about the inner being
- **The concealed self is exposed in God's light (v.8).** The inner being's secret, hidden sins stand fully in the light of God's presence — what it conceals even from itself is seen.
- **The whole life is a *sigh* (vv.9–10).** The inner being grasps its span as a single breathed-out sigh — brief, toilsome, soon flown.
- **Wisdom is the fruit of *numbering the days* (v.12).** Rightly grasping one's brevity yields a *heart of wisdom* — and the counting must be *taught by God*; the grasp of finitude is a God-given lesson, not a self-achievement.
- **The short life is redeemed by *morning satisfaction* in God's love (v.14).** Not by more days, but by being *satisfied with chesed* — the plea turns the few, toilsome days to gladness "all our days."

## Honest notes
- **A cornerstone finitude-and-wisdom datum** (numbering days → a heart of wisdom, God-taught); a key inner-being process (with Ps 39's finitude-grasped, 49's un-ransomable soul). Worth flagging for the study's movements focus.
- **"secret sins" (H5956, *alum*, M14)** correctly a characteristic (the concealed/deceit cluster) — here the hidden exposed; a clean tie to Ps 26:4's dissemblers (same root, opposite context).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed; intensity *all*; *number/wisdom/sigh* gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *iniquities* (H5771, M10, v.8); *secret-sins* (H5956, M14, v.8); *heart* (H3824, M47, v.12); *steadfast-love* (H2617, M05, v.14); *rejoice/glad* (H7442/H8055, M42/M04, v.14). *number/wisdom/sigh* captured gate-2 — the numbering→wisdom and the life-as-sigh read from these.

## Psalm 91 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 91 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 91:1–16 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (vv.13 + others backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Abiding in God as home, and the mutual holding.** Psalm 91's findings: the inner being's security is **dwelling / abiding *in* God as its home** (vv.1–2, 9); the abiding yields **fearlessness** (vv.5–6); and God's protective answer is tied to the self's **devoted clinging, knowing, and calling** (vv.14–16) — the self holds fast to God, God holds the self.

## The reading

**I. Dwelling in God as home — and naming him so (vv.1–2, 9).**
"He who **dwells** (H3427, *yashab* — resides) in the **shelter** of the Most High will **abide** (*lun* — lodge) in the **shadow** of the Almighty. **I will say** to the LORD, 'My **refuge** (H4268, M19) and my fortress, my God, in whom I **trust** (H0982, M19)'… Because you have made the LORD your **dwelling place**" (vv.1–2, 9). The gem-finding: the inner being's security is **residing *in* God as a permanent home** — not a momentary shelter but a *dwelling*, an *abiding* *(stated)*. The operation: the self **takes up residence in God** — *dwells, abides, makes God its dwelling place* — a settled home, not a passing cover *(inferred: yashab/lun/dwelling-place all name *residence*, not brief refuge; cf. Ps 27:4's "dwell", 90:1's "our dwelling place")*. And it **declares it** — "I *will say* to the LORD, 'My refuge'" — the trust is a **speech-act**, the self naming God as its home *(inferred: the confessing "I will say… my refuge" makes the trust an act of naming)*.

**II. The fearlessness that flows from the dwelling (vv.5–6).**
"You will **not fear** (H3372, M01) the **terror** (H6343, M01) of the night, nor the arrow that flies by day" (vv.5–6). The finding: the abiding inner being is **freed from fear** — the night-terror, the daytime arrow *(stated)*. The operation: **dwelling in God dissolves the fears** — the self at home in God is not afraid of what would otherwise terrify *(inferred: the fearlessness is predicated on the dwelling of vv.1–2, 9; cf. Ps 23:4, 46:2)*.

**III. The mutual holding — devoted clinging, knowing, calling (vv.14–16).**
"Because he **holds fast to me in love** (H2836, *chashaq* — cleaves, is devoted), I will deliver him; I will protect him, because he **knows** my name. When he **calls** (H7121, M37) to me, **I will answer** him; I will be with him in trouble" (vv.14–16). The gem-finding: God's protective answer is tied to **three inner-being acts** — the self **clinging to God in devoted love** (*chashaq*), **knowing** God's name, and **calling** on him *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's **devoted attachment** (*chashaq* — a binding love/desire, cleaving to God), its **intimate knowledge** of the name, and its **calling** *draw God's answering deliverance* — the self holds fast to God, and God holds/answers the self *(inferred: "because he holds fast to me in love… knows my name… calls to me, I will answer" makes the mutual holding — the self's cleaving met by God's response — the ground of the protection)*. The abiding of vv.1–2 is now shown to be **reciprocal**: the self *dwells in* God because it *cleaves to* God, and God *answers* *(inferred)*.

## What Psalm 91 says about the inner being
- **Security is *residing in God as home* (vv.1–2, 9).** The inner being dwells, abides, makes God its dwelling place — a settled residence, not a momentary shelter — and it *names* God so: trust is a speech-act, the self confessing God as its refuge.
- **Dwelling in God dissolves fear (vv.5–6).** The abiding self is freed from the terror of the night and the arrow by day — at home in God, it is not afraid.
- **God's answer is drawn by the self's *devoted clinging* (vv.14–16).** The inner being's *chashaq* (cleaving, devoted love), its *knowing* the name, and its *calling* meet God's answering deliverance. The holding is mutual — the self cleaves to God, God holds and answers the self.

## Honest notes
- **"holds fast in love" (H2836, *chashaq*, M44)** correctly a characteristic — a *devoted-attachment* love (cleaving/binding to God by desire), distinct from *aheb* (affection) and *chasah* (refuge-taking); a clean datum for the cleaving/attachment family (with Ps 63:8's *dabaq*).
- **Dwelling/abiding cluster** (yashab/lun/dwelling-place) captured gate-2; the *reside-in-God-as-home* read from it — the settled residence (with 27:4, 90:1).
- **Scope honesty:** the protection-promises (pestilence, the thousand falling, the angels' charge, treading the lion, vv.3–13) are the arena; the inner-being weight is the dwelling (vv.1–2, 9), the fearlessness (vv.5–6), and the mutual holding (vv.14–16).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp at vv.5, 7, 10; bearer=LORD bleed; *dwells/knows/answer* gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *refuge/trust* (H4268/H2620/H0982, M19, vv.2,4,9); *fear/terror* (H3372/H6343, M01, vv.5); *love/chashaq* (H2836, M44, v.14); *calls* (H7121, M37, v.15). *dwells/abide/knows/answer* captured gate-2 — the abiding and mutual holding read from these.

## Psalm 92 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 92 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 92:1–15 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (v.13 backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Gladness from God's works, and flourishing into old age.** A Sabbath song of thanksgiving. Its two inner-being findings: the inner being **gladdened by contemplating God's works** (vv.4–5); and the God-planted self **flourishing — fruitful even in old age** (vv.12–14).

## The reading

**I. Gladness from contemplating God's works (vv.4–5).**
"For you, O LORD, have made me **glad** (H8055, M04) by your **work**; at the works of your hands I **sing for joy** (H7442, M42). How great are your works, O LORD! Your **thoughts** are very **deep**!" (vv.4–5). The finding: the inner being's gladness **arises from *beholding* what God has done** — the works and thoughts of God *(stated)*. The operation: **contemplation of God's works → joy** — the self is *made glad* by attending to God's deeds, and drawn to the recognition that God's thoughts are **unfathomably deep** *(inferred: "you have made me glad by your work… your thoughts are very deep" makes the joy a fruit of contemplating God's works, and opens onto their unsearchable depth; cf. Ps 143:5)*.

**II. The God-planted self flourishing into old age (vv.12–14).**
"The **righteous** (H6662, M26) **flourish** (H6524, *parach*) like the **palm tree**… **planted** in the house of the LORD; they flourish in the courts of our God. They still **bear fruit** (H5107) in **old age**; they are ever full of **sap** and **green**" (vv.12–14). The gem-finding: the God-planted inner being's fruitfulness **continues into old age** — it does not wither but stays *green*, *full of sap*, *bearing fruit* *(stated)*. The operation: the self **rooted *in God's house*** flourishes **continuously** — its fruitfulness *increases with age* rather than fading, the opposite of the grass that withers (Ps 90:5–6) *(inferred: "planted in the house of the LORD… still bear fruit in old age… ever green" makes the rooting-in-God the source of a flourishing that does not decline; cf. Ps 1's tree by the water, 84's strength-to-strength, 71's old-age hope)*. The rooting determines the flourishing.

## What Psalm 92 says about the inner being
- **Contemplating God's works makes the inner being *glad* (vv.4–5).** Joy arises from beholding what God has done; the self is made glad by attending to God's deeds, and drawn to their unfathomable depth.
- **The God-planted self flourishes *into old age* (vv.12–14).** Rooted in God's house, the inner being stays green, full of sap, and fruitful even in age — its fruitfulness continues rather than fading, the opposite of the withering grass. The rooting determines the flourishing.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** the frame (it is good to give thanks, the brutish who cannot understand, the wicked's ruin, vv.1–3, 6–11) is the arena; the inner-being weight is the gladness-from-works (vv.4–5) and the flourishing (vv.12–14).
- **The flourishing thread:** the God-planted, fruitful-in-old-age self ties to Ps 1 (tree by water), 84 (strength-to-strength), 71 (old age) — a coherent datum on the rooted inner being's continued flourishing.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed; intensity *all*; *flourish/bear-fruit/sap/green* gate-2; backfilled v.13 now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *sing-praises/sing-for-joy* (H2167/H7442, M42, vv.1,4); *glad* (H8055, M04, v.4); *righteous* (H6662, M26, v.12). *flourish/bear-fruit/old-age/green* captured gate-2 — the continued flourishing read from these.

## Psalm 93 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 93 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 93:1–5 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **A brief kingship hymn — honestly scoped, thin.** Almost the whole psalm is a declaration of God's reign, majesty, and might over the roaring floods (the arena). Its one inner-being resonance: the **trustworthy decrees** as the stable ground amid the chaos (vv.3–5).

## The reading

**I. Trustworthy decrees as the ground amid the roaring floods (vv.3–5).**
"The **floods** have lifted up their voice… their **roaring**. Mightier than the thunders of many waters… the LORD on high is mighty! **Your decrees are very trustworthy**; holiness befits your house" (vv.3–5). The finding: set against the **roaring chaos-floods**, the psalm ends on the **trustworthiness of God's *decrees*** *(stated)*. The operation (resonance, not an explicit inner act): the inner being's stable ground amid the world's roaring is the **reliability of God's word** — when the floods lift their voice, what stands firm and can be leaned on is that God's decrees are *very trustworthy* *(inferred: the movement from the roaring floods to "your decrees are very trustworthy" offers the reliable word as the counter to the chaos; the self's confidence would rest there — read as resonance, since the psalm states it of God, not of the inner being's act)*.

## What Psalm 93 says about the inner being
- **God's *trustworthy decrees* are the stable ground amid chaos (vv.3–5).** Against the roaring floods, what stands firm is the reliability of God's word — the resonance for the inner being being that its confidence rests on the trustworthy decree when the world roars.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** this is a short hymn to God's reign/majesty/might (vv.1–4); it does not disclose an explicit inner-being *operation*. The one resonance (trustworthy decrees as ground, v.5) is read as such, not inflated (memory `feedback_no_stats_trends_review_fabricated_data`).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed; "not be moved" of the *world* v.1 is cosmic, not the inner being) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** the psalm's terms (reigns/majesty/strength/established/trustworthy) are God-attributes captured largely gate-2 (the arena); no inner-being characteristic is proper here beyond the v.5 resonance. Noted plainly.

## Psalm 94 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 94 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 94:1–23 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (vv.6 + others backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The "God doesn't see" self-deception refuted, and the anxious soul consoled.** Psalm 94's findings: the wicked's inner license **"the LORD does not see,"** refuted by the *Maker of eye and ear* (vv.7–9); God's **discipline received as blessing** (v.12); and the **multiplied cares of the heart answered by God's consolations** (vv.17–19).

## The reading

**I. "God doesn't see" — self-deception refuted by the Maker of eye and ear (vv.7–9).**
"And they say, '**The LORD does not see**; the God of Jacob does not **perceive** (H0995, M15, *bin*).' Understand, O dullest of the people!… **He who planted the ear, does he not hear? He who formed the eye, does he not see?**" (vv.7–9). The gem-finding: the wicked inner being grants itself license by telling itself **God is blind and deaf** to its evil — "the LORD does not see" *(stated)*. The refutation strikes at the root: **the One who *formed* the faculties of perception cannot lack them** — the Maker of the eye *sees*, the Maker of the ear *hears* *(stated)*. The operation: the wicked's **self-deception about God's perception** (the license "he doesn't see") is exposed by God-as-Maker-of-perception *(inferred: "he who formed the eye, does he not see?" turns the very existence of the self's faculties into evidence that their Maker perceives; cf. Ps 10:11, 50:21's projected/like-me God)*.

**II. Discipline received as blessing (vv.11–13).**
"The LORD knows the **thoughts** of man, that they are but a **breath**… **Blessed** is the man whom you **discipline** (H3256, *yasar*), O LORD, and whom you **teach** (H3925) out of your law" (vv.11–13). Two findings. God **knows the inner thoughts**, and they are *breath* (transient, fully seen) *(stated)*. And, counter-intuitively, God's **discipline is a *blessing*** — "*blessed* is the man whom you discipline" *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being **counts God's correction as a good** — the disciplined-and-taught self is *blessed*, not merely chastened *(inferred: "blessed… whom you discipline… teach" makes correction a benefit; the opposite of the flight-from-discipline, Ps 39:13)*.

**III. The anxious soul consoled — cares answered (vv.17–19).**
"If the LORD had not been my help, my **soul** (H5315, the seat — M47) would soon have lived in the land of **silence**. When I thought, '**My foot slips**,' your **steadfast love** (H2617, M05) **held me up**. When the **cares** (*sarappim* — anxious, divided thoughts) of my **heart** (H3820, M47) are **many**, your **consolations** (*tanchumim*) **cheer** my **soul**" (vv.17–19). The gem-finding: when the inner being's **anxious cares *multiply*** — the heart full of divided, worrying thoughts — God's **consolations *cheer* the soul** *(stated)*. The operation: the **many inner cares** are met and **answered by God's comforts** — the anxious, care-crowded heart is *cheered/delighted* by consolation *(inferred: "the cares of my heart are many → your consolations cheer my soul" pairs the multiplication of anxiety with the consolation that lifts it)*. And at the point of *slipping* ("my foot slips"), it is **steadfast love that *holds up*** the self — catching the inner being precisely as it gives way *(stated)*.

## What Psalm 94 says about the inner being
- **The wicked license themselves by "God doesn't see" — refuted by the Maker of the faculties (vv.7–9).** The self-deception that God is blind to its evil is exposed: the One who *formed* the eye and ear surely perceives. The existence of the self's own faculties is evidence their Maker sees.
- **God's discipline is received as *blessing* (vv.12–13).** The inner being counts correction as a good — "blessed is the man whom you discipline" — the taught, corrected self, not merely chastened.
- **Multiplied cares are answered by God's *consolations* (vv.18–19).** When the heart's anxious thoughts multiply, God's comforts *cheer* the soul; and at the point of slipping, steadfast love *holds up* the self — catching it as it gives way.

## Honest notes
- **The Maker-of-the-eye refutation (v.9)** is a strong datum against the "God doesn't see" self-deception (the projected/like-me God of Ps 50:21, the wicked's "he will never see" of Ps 10:11) — captured via gate-2 *see/hear/eye/ear*; the operation read from the argument.
- **"cares of my heart / consolations cheer my soul" (vv.18–19)** captured via *heart* (H3820) + *soul* (H5315) with gate-2 *sarappim/tanchumim*; the anxious-soul-consoled read from the pair — a tender datum (with Ps 42's downcast soul, 55's overwhelmed self).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp across the "does not see/hear/discipline" negations vv.7–10; bearer=LORD bleed; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *perceive* (H0995, M15, v.9); *afflict* (H6031, M24, v.5); *wicked* (H7563, M10); *steadfast-love* (H2617, M05, v.18); *soul/heart* (H5315/H3820, M47, vv.17,19). *see/hear/discipline/consolations/cheer* captured gate-2 — the refutation, discipline-blessing, and consolation read from these.

## Psalm 95 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 95 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 95:1–11 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (v.3 backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The fork at hearing God's voice.** A call to worship that turns to warning. Its inner-being findings: the response to hearing God's voice can be a **hardening of the heart** (vv.7–8); and the **erring heart that does not know God's ways** forfeits rest (vv.10–11).

## The reading

**I. The fork at hearing God's voice — heed or harden (vv.7–8).**
"**Today, if you hear** (H8085) his voice, **do not harden** (*qashah*) your **hearts** (H3824, the seat — M47), as at Meribah… when your fathers put me to the **test**" (vv.7–8). The gem-finding: hearing God's voice presents the inner being with a **fork** — to *heed* or to *harden* *(stated)*. The operation: the heart can **stiffen itself against the very word it hears** — hardening is the heart's *refusal to be moved* by what it has just heard *(inferred: "if you hear his voice, do *not harden* your hearts" makes the hardening a response *to* the hearing — the heart setting itself against the word; contrast Ps 85's listening posture, 81's given-over refusal)*. And the **"today"** presses the urgency — the fork is *now*, at *this* hearing *(stated)*.

**II. The erring heart that does not know God's ways (vv.10–11).**
"They are a people who **go astray** (*taah*) **in their heart** (H3820, M47), and they **have not known** my ways… I swore in my wrath, 'They shall **not enter my rest**'" (vv.10–11). The finding: the inner root of straying is a **heart that *errs*** — those who "go astray *in their heart*" do **not know** God's ways *(stated)*. The operation: the **heart's inner wandering → ignorance of God's ways → exclusion from rest** *(inferred: "go astray in their heart… have not known my ways… shall not enter my rest" chains the erring heart to the lost knowledge and the forfeited rest — the hardening/wandering heart cannot enter the rest)*.

## What Psalm 95 says about the inner being
- **Hearing God's voice presents a *fork* — heed or harden (vv.7–8).** The heart can stiffen itself against the very word it hears; hardening is the refusal to be moved by what it has just heard. The "today" presses the fork into the present.
- **The *erring heart* forfeits the knowledge of God's ways and his rest (vv.10–11).** Inner wandering — "going astray in the heart" — issues in not knowing God's ways and in exclusion from rest. The heart that wanders cannot enter.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** the worship-call (vv.1–7a — sing, bow down, the sheep of his hand) is the arena; the inner-being weight is the fork-at-hearing (vv.7b–8) and the erring heart (vv.10–11).
- **Cross-psalm:** the hearing/hardening fork ties to Ps 81 (refusal → given over to the stubborn heart), 85 (the listening posture), 95's own "today" — a coherent hearing-response thread.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp at v.8; bearer=LORD/Meribah bleed; backfilled v.3 now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *hearts* (H3824/H3820, M47, vv.8,10). *hear/harden/go-astray/known/rest* captured gate-2 — the fork-at-hearing and the erring heart read from these.

## Psalm 96 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 96 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 96:1–13 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Worship as ascription — honestly scoped.** A kingship/missions hymn (the call to sing a new song, the worthless idols, God's coming to judge — the arena). Its one inner-being finding (closely echoing Ps 29): worship is **ascribing** glory to God — *rendering* what is his, not augmenting him (vv.7–9).

## The reading

**I. Worship as *ascribing* — rendering, not augmenting (vv.7–9).**
"**Ascribe** (H3051, *yahav* — give, render) to the LORD, O families of the peoples, ascribe to the LORD **glory** (H3519, M22) and **strength** (H5797, M23)! Ascribe to the LORD the glory **due his name**… **Worship** the LORD in the **splendour** (H1927, M22) of **holiness** (H6944, M22); **tremble** before him" (vv.7–9). The finding: the inner being's worship is **ascription** — *rendering* to God the glory that is *due his name*, not adding to him *(stated)*. The operation: to *ascribe* (*yahav*) is to **acknowledge and give back** what is already God's — worship as **recognition and self-abasement** (the *trembling* before him), not contribution *(inferred: "ascribe… the glory *due* his name… tremble before him" makes worship the rendering of what is owed, with awe, not an increase of God; the same finding as Ps 29:1–2, and worship "in the splendour of holiness" bows before beauty as well as majesty)*.

## What Psalm 96 says about the inner being
- **Worship is *ascription* — rendering, not augmenting (vv.7–9).** The inner being *gives back* to God the glory *due his name*, with trembling awe — worship as recognition and self-abasement before God's splendour and holiness, not a contribution to him. (The Ps 29:1–2 finding, restated.)

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** the great bulk (sing a new song, declare his glory among the nations, the idols are worthless, the heavens/earth/sea/field rejoicing at God's coming to judge in righteousness, vv.1–6, 10–13) is the praise/missions arena; the inner-being weight is the worship-as-ascription (vv.7–9). Thin psalm, noted plainly.
- **Near-parallel to Ps 29:1–2** (ascribe glory and strength; worship in the splendour of holiness) and to 1 Chr 16; the ascription finding is restated, not newly derived — flagged as a repeat datum.
- **Creation-wide joy (vv.11–13):** the heavens/earth/sea/field rejoicing at God's righteous coming is read as the arena's response, not the inner being's operation (external creation, not the self).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed pervasive; intensity *all*; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *glory* (H3519, M22, vv.3,7,8); *strength* (H5797, M23, v.7); *splendour/holiness* (H1927/H6944, M22, v.9); *glad* (H8055, M04, v.11). *ascribe/worship/tremble* captured gate-2 — the ascription read from these.

## Psalm 97 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 97 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 97:1–12 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; **aheb-fix build** — "love" H0157 v.10 now correctly `role=characteristic`). Complete chapter (v. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Love-of-God entails hate-of-evil; light sown for the upright.** A kingship hymn (God's reigning theophany is the arena). Two inner-being findings: **loving the LORD *entails* hating evil** (v.10); and **light and joy *sown*** for the upright in heart (v.11).

## The reading

**I. To love the LORD is to hate evil (v.10).**
"O you who **love** (H0157, *aheb*) the LORD, **hate** (H8130, M06) evil!" (v.10). The gem-finding: the inner being's **love and hate are bound together and rightly aimed** — *loving God* **entails** *hating evil* *(stated)*. The operation: ordered affection is **not love alone but a paired love-and-hate** — the same inner being that loves the LORD *must* hate evil; the two are one disposition seen from two sides *(inferred: "you who love the LORD, hate evil" makes the hatred of evil the *implication* of the love of God — right love requires a corresponding right hatred; cf. Ps 45:7's loved-righteousness/hated-wickedness)*.

**II. Light and joy *sown* for the upright in heart (v.11).**
"**Light is sown** for the righteous, and **joy** for the **upright in heart** (H3820, the seat — M47)" (v.11). The gem-finding: the inner being's light and joy are **sown** — *planted like seed* — for the upright *(stated)*. The operation: the upright-in-heart's gladness is a **seed awaiting harvest** — *sown* now, to spring up later; light and joy are **planted for** the upright, a deferred but certain gladness growing toward them *(inferred: "light is sown… joy for the upright in heart" makes the gladness a seed sown for a future harvest, not an immediate possession — the upright's joy is *coming up*)*.

## What Psalm 97 says about the inner being
- **Loving the LORD *entails* hating evil (v.10).** Right affection is a paired love-and-hate — the inner being that loves God must hate evil; the two are one ordered disposition, not love alone.
- **Light and joy are *sown* for the upright in heart (v.11).** The gladness of the upright is a seed planted for a future harvest — sown now, springing up later; a deferred but certain joy growing toward them.

## Honest notes
- **aheb-fix confirmed:** "love" (H0157, v.10) now `role=characteristic` — the love-God/hate-evil pairing captured correctly (contrast Ps 45:7 where *aheb* was under-tagged pre-fix).
- **Scope honesty:** the theophany (God reigning, fire and lightning, the idols shamed, vv.1–9) is the arena; the inner-being weight is the love/hate pairing (v.10) and the sown light/joy (v.11).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD/Zion/Judah bleed; intensity *all/many*; *light/sown* gate-2; backfilled v. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *love* (H0157, v.10 — now characteristic via fix); *hate* (H8130, M06, v.10); *righteous/righteousness* (H6662/H6664, M26); *glad/rejoice* (H8055/H1523, M04, vv.1,8,12); *heart* (H3820, M47, v.11). *light/sown/joy* captured gate-2 — the sown gladness read from these.

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 98:1–9 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (v. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.

## The reading

**I. The "new song" — fresh praise for fresh work (v.1).**
"Oh sing to the LORD a **new song**, **for he has done marvelous things**!" (v.1). The finding: the inner being's praise is renewed — a *new* song — **because God has done something new** *(stated)*. The operation (resonance): fresh divine action calls forth **fresh praise** — the inner being does not merely repeat old worship but responds to what God has *newly* done with a *new* song *(inferred: "sing a new song, *for* he has done marvelous things" ties the newness of the praise to the newness of the deed — the self's worship is renewed by seeing God's fresh work; the new-song thread, Ps 33:3, 40:3, 96:1)*.

## What Psalm 98 says about the inner being
- **Fresh divine work calls forth *fresh praise* (v.1).** The inner being sings a *new* song *because* God has done something new — worship is renewed by seeing God's fresh deeds, not merely repeated. (The new-song thread, Ps 33:3, 40:3, 96:1.)

Very thin psalm; close parallel to Ps 96 — noted plainly, not inflated (memory `feedback_no_stats_trends_review_fabricated_data`).

## Psalm 99 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 99 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 99:1–9 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (v. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **A holiness hymn — honestly scoped, thin.** The declaration of God's reign and threefold "Holy is he" (vv.3, 5, 9) is the arena. Two inner-being resonances: **trembling worship/self-abasement before God's holiness** (vv.1, 5, 9); and the pattern of **calling and being answered** (vv.6, 8).

## The reading

**I. Trembling worship before God's holiness (vv.1, 5, 9).**
"The LORD reigns; **let the peoples tremble**!… **Worship at his footstool**! **Holy is he**!… Exalt the LORD our God, and worship at his holy mountain; for the LORD our God is **holy**!" (vv.1, 5, 9). The finding: the fitting inner response to God's holiness is **trembling worship** — bowing *at his footstool*, the lowest place *(stated)*. The operation (resonance): God's holiness draws the inner being to **awe and self-abasement** — the threefold "Holy is he" frames a worship that *trembles* and bows low *(inferred: "let the peoples tremble… worship at his footstool… holy is he" makes the holiness evoke trembling self-abasement; cf. Ps 96:9's worship in the splendour of holiness, 5:7's bowing in fear)*.

**II. Calling and being answered (vv.6, 8).**
"They **called** to the LORD, and **he answered** them… you were a **forgiving** God to them, but an **avenger** of their wrongdoings" (vv.6, 8). The finding: the pattern of the intercessors (Moses, Aaron, Samuel) — **they called, and God answered** *(stated)*. The resonance: the inner being that *calls* is *answered* — and the God who answers is both **forgiving** and **holding to account** (forgiving yet avenging wrongdoing) *(inferred: "they called… he answered… forgiving… but an avenger" pairs the answered call with a God who both pardons and holds accountable — the answer is not indulgence)*.

## What Psalm 99 says about the inner being
- **God's holiness draws the inner being to *trembling worship* (vv.1, 5, 9).** Awe and self-abasement — bowing at the footstool, the lowest place — is the fitting response to the thrice-holy God.
- **The one who *calls* is *answered* — by a God who both forgives and holds to account (vv.6, 8).** The intercessors called and were answered; the answering God is forgiving yet an avenger of wrongdoing — the answer is not indulgence.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** the psalm is largely a declaration of God's holy reign and might (vv.1–4, 7); the inner-being weight is the trembling worship (vv.1, 5, 9) and the call-and-answer (vv.6, 8). Thin hymn, noted plainly.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed; "loves justice" v.4 is God's, not the inner being's; backfilled v. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** the terms are largely God-attributes and worship-calls captured gate-2 (the arena); the inner-being resonances (trembling worship, call-and-answer) read from vv.1, 5, 6, 8, 9. Noted plainly.

## Psalm 100 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 100 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 100:1–5 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (v. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Serving with gladness; the self as God's own.** A short thanksgiving. Two inner-being findings: **service rendered in gladness** (v.2); and the foundational knowledge that the self is **made by God and belongs to him — not its own** (v.3).

## The reading

**I. Service in gladness (v.2).**
"**Serve** the LORD **with gladness** (H8057, M04)! Come into his presence with singing!" (v.2). The finding: the inner being's service is to be **rendered *in gladness*** — joyful, not grudging *(stated)*. The operation: gladness is the **mode** of the self's service — worship and obedience done *with joy*, the inner disposition of the servant *(inferred: "serve… with gladness" makes joy the manner of the service, not a separate act — the self serves *gladly*)*.

**II. "We are his, not our own" — the self as God's (v.3).**
"**Know** that the LORD, he is God! **It is he who made us, and we are his**; we are his people, and the sheep of his pasture" (v.3). The gem-finding: the inner being's foundational knowledge is that it is **made by God and *belongs* to him** — "we are *his*" *(stated)*. The operation: the self **knows itself as God's *possession*** — made-by, and belonging-to, God, **not self-owned** *(inferred: "he made us, and we are his" locates the self's origin and ownership in God — the inner being is not its own but God's; a foundational orientation, cf. Ps 95:7 "the sheep of his hand", 24:1 the earth is the LORD's)*.

## What Psalm 100 says about the inner being
- **Service is rendered *in gladness* (v.2).** Joy is the mode of the self's service — worship and obedience done gladly, not grudgingly; the servant's inner disposition.
- **The self is *made by God and belongs to him* — not its own (v.3).** The inner being's foundational knowledge is that God made it and it is *his*; the self is not self-owned but God's possession — origin and ownership located in God.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** short thanksgiving; the calls to praise (joyful noise, singing, thanksgiving, vv.1, 4) and God's goodness (v.5) are the arena; the inner-being weight is the gladness-in-service (v.2) and the self-as-God's (v.3).
- **"we are his, not our own" (v.3)** captured via gate-2 *made/people*; the self-as-God's-possession read from it — a foundational datum (with Ps 24:1, 95:7, 139:13–16).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed; backfilled v. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *gladness* (H8057, M04, v.2); *thanksgiving* (H8426, M22, v.4); *good* (H2896, M04, v.5). *serve/know/made* captured gate-2 — the glad service and the self-as-God's read from these.

## Psalm 101 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 101 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 101:1–8 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The inner being's active self-governance for integrity.** Psalm 101 is a set of *resolutions*. Its findings are operations of **self-governance**: integrity of heart **in the private sphere** (v.2); **governing what enters through the eyes** (v.3); **distancing the perverse heart** and refusing intimacy with evil (v.4); and **curating one's company** (vv.5–7).

## The reading

**I. Integrity of heart *within the house* — the private self (v.2).**
"I will **ponder** (H7919, M15, *sakal*) the way that is **blameless** (H8549, M12)… I will **walk with integrity** (H8537, M13, *tom*) **of heart** (H3824, the seat — M47) **within my house**" (v.2). The finding: the inner being resolves on **integrity of heart in the *private* sphere** — "within my house," where no one watches *(stated)*. The operation: integrity is maintained **unwatched** — the self is as integrous in private as in public *(inferred: "integrity of heart *within my house*" locates the integrity in the unobserved, domestic sphere — the private self held to the same standard; the *tom*-heart of Ps 26:1, here specifically *at home*)*.

**II. Governing the eye-gate (v.3).**
"I will **not set before my eyes** anything that is **worthless** (*beliyaal*). I **hate** (H8130, M06) the work of those who fall away; **it shall not cling to me**" (v.3). The finding: the inner being **governs its own *gaze*** — refusing to *set* anything worthless before its eyes *(stated)*. The operation: the self **controls its *intake through sight*** — guarding the eye-gate against the worthless, and refusing to let corruption *cling* *(inferred: "I will not set before my eyes… it shall not cling to me" makes the self the gatekeeper of what it looks at and what attaches to it; cf. Ps 119:37 "turn my eyes from worthless things")*.

**III. Distancing the perverse heart; refusing to *know* evil (v.4).**
"A **perverse heart** (H6141, *iqqesh* — twisted + H3824, M47) shall be **far from me**; I will **know nothing of evil**" (v.4). The finding: the inner being actively **puts the crooked disposition at a distance** and **refuses *intimacy* with evil** *(stated)*. The operation: two moves — **distancing the perverse heart** (holding the twisted disposition away) and **declining to *know* evil** (refusing the *intimate acquaintance* that "know" implies) *(inferred: "a perverse heart shall be far… I will know nothing of evil" makes the self actively separate from crookedness and refuse familiarity with evil — the opposite of the wicked who *cherish* iniquity, Ps 66:18)*.

**IV. Curating the company (vv.5–7).**
"Whoever **slanders** his neighbour secretly I will destroy… the **haughty look** and **arrogant heart** I will not endure. I will look with **favour on the faithful** (H0539, M13, *aman*)… he who walks **blamelessly** shall minister to me. No one who practices **deceit** (H7423, M14) shall **dwell in my house**" (vv.5–7). The finding: the inner being's integrity is **worked out in whom it keeps near** — the faithful/blameless *welcomed*, the slanderer/haughty/deceitful *excluded from the house* *(stated)*. The operation: **curating one's company** as the externalising of the heart's integrity — the self chooses its associates by their inner condition (faithful vs deceitful) *(inferred: "favour on the faithful… no deceit shall dwell in my house" makes the chosen company the outward form of the inner integrity; cf. Ps 26:4–5, 1:1's refused seat)*.

## What Psalm 101 says about the inner being
- **Integrity is held in the *private* sphere (v.2).** "Integrity of heart within my house" — the unwatched self is as integrous as the public; integrity is not for show.
- **The inner being governs its own *gaze* (v.3).** It refuses to set the worthless before its eyes and refuses to let corruption cling — the self as gatekeeper of what it looks at.
- **It *distances* the perverse heart and refuses to *know* evil (v.4).** Two active moves: holding the crooked disposition away, and declining intimacy with evil — the opposite of cherishing iniquity.
- **It *curates its company* as the outward form of its integrity (vv.5–7).** The faithful welcomed, the deceitful excluded from the house — the heart's integrity externalised in whom it keeps near.

## Honest notes
- **A strong self-governance datum:** integrity worked across three gates — the *heart* (private), the *eyes* (intake), and the *company* (association). A coherent inner-being process (with Ps 26's integrity, 119:37's guarded eyes, 1:1's refused company).
- **"perverse heart far / know nothing of evil" (v.4)** captured via *heart* (H3824) + gate-2 *perverse/know*; the distancing and refused-intimacy read from these.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp across the "I will not…" resolutions vv.3–7; bearer=David/LORD bleed) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *ponder* (H7919, M15, v.2); *blameless* (H8549, M12, vv.2,6); *integrity* (H8537, M13, v.2); *heart* (H3824, M47, vv.2,4,5); *hate* (H8130, M06, v.3); *faithful* (H0539, M13, v.6); *deceit* (H7423, M14, v.7). *eyes/worthless/perverse/know* captured gate-2 — the eye-governance and distanced-evil read from these.

## Psalm 102 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 102 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 102:1–28 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The afflicted, withering, lonely self anchoring on God's eternity.** Psalm 102's findings: affliction **saturating the whole life** — the heart withered, food ashes, days smoke (vv.3–11); the **isolation** figured as a lonely bird (vv.6–7); and the **fleeting self anchoring on God's unchanging eternity** (vv.11–12, 27).

## The reading

**I. Affliction saturating the whole life (vv.3–11).**
"My **days** pass away like **smoke**… My **heart** (H3820, the seat — M47) is **struck down** like grass and has **withered**; I forget to eat my bread… I eat **ashes** like bread and mingle **tears** (H1065, M03) with my drink… My days are like an evening **shadow**; I **wither** like grass" (vv.3–11). The finding: the affliction **pervades every dimension** of the inner being's life — the *heart* withers, the *food* becomes ashes, the *drink* becomes tears, the *days* become smoke and shadow *(stated)*. The operation: the affliction is not localised but **total** — it saturates the heart, the appetite, and the very texture of the days *(inferred: heart-withered, ashes-for-bread, tears-for-drink, days-as-smoke pile up to make the affliction pervade the whole life, not one faculty)*.

**II. The isolation — a lonely bird in waste places (vv.6–7).**
"I am like a **desert owl** of the wilderness, like an owl of the **waste places**; I lie **awake**; I am like a **lonely sparrow** on the housetop" (vv.6–7). The gem-finding: the afflicted inner being's **loneliness** is figured as a **solitary bird** — the owl in the desolate wilderness, the sleepless *lonely sparrow* alone on the roof *(stated)*. The operation: the self's **isolation and sleeplessness** — a creature alone in waste places, awake through the night *(inferred: the owl/sparrow images name a self cut off and unable to rest, the solitude of affliction; cf. Ps 88's darkness-companion)*.

**III. The fleeting self anchored on God's unchanging eternity (vv.11–12, 27).**
"My days are like an evening shadow; I wither like grass. **But you**, O LORD, are enthroned **forever**… you are the **same**, and your years have **no end**" (vv.11–12, 27). The gem-finding: the **withering, fleeting** inner being is set against God's **unchanging eternity** — "you are the *same*" *(stated)*. The operation: the transient self **anchors on the permanent God** — where the self is grass/shadow/smoke (soon gone), God *endures unchanged*, and *that* is the ground the fleeting self stands on *(inferred: the "but you… are the same… your years have no end" turns from the self's brevity to God's permanence as the counter and the hope — the withering self leans on the One who does not wither; cf. Ps 90:1–4)*. The self's very transience drives it to the eternal God *(inferred)*.

## What Psalm 102 says about the inner being
- **Affliction can *saturate the whole life* (vv.3–11).** The heart withers, food becomes ashes, drink becomes tears, days become smoke — the affliction pervades every dimension, not one faculty.
- **Isolation is figured as a *lonely bird* (vv.6–7).** The afflicted self is a solitary owl in waste places, a sleepless sparrow alone on the roof — cut off, unable to rest.
- **The fleeting self *anchors on God's unchanging eternity* (vv.11–12, 27).** Where the inner being is grass, shadow, smoke — soon gone — God *is the same*, his years without end; the transient self leans on the permanent God, and its very brevity drives it there.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** the psalm's middle (God's compassion on Zion, the nations fearing his name, the generations to come, vv.13–22) is the community/God arena; the inner-being weight is the affliction-imagery (vv.3–11), the isolation (vv.6–7), and the fleeting-self/eternal-God contrast (vv.11–12, 27).
- **The imagery** (smoke, grass, owl, sparrow, ashes, shadow) is captured largely gate-2; the affliction-saturation and isolation are read from the image-cascade, with *heart* (H3820, M47) and *tears* (H1065, M03) as the tagged inner terms.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *heart* (H3820, M47, v.4); *tears* (H1065, M03, v.9). The affliction/isolation/eternity images captured gate-2 — the saturated affliction, the lonely bird, and the anchoring-on-eternity read from these.

## Psalm 103 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 103 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 103:1–22 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The self rousing its whole inner being to bless; God's dust-frame compassion. A cornerstone.** Psalm 103's findings: the **self commanding *itself* to bless God** — enlisting the whole inner being and its *memory* (vv.1–2, 22); the **renewal of the self** (v.5); and God's **fatherly compassion grounded in knowing our frailty — that we are dust** (vv.13–14).

## The reading

**I. "Bless the LORD, O my soul" — the self rousing its whole inner being (vv.1–2, 22).**
"**Bless the LORD, O my soul** (H5315, the seat — M47), and **all that is within me**, bless his holy name! Bless the LORD, O my soul, and **forget not** all his benefits" (vv.1–2; refrain at v.22). The gem-finding: the inner being **commands *itself* to bless God** — an "**I**" rousing "**my soul**" (and "all that is *within me*") to worship *(stated)*. The operation: self-address in the **mode of *stirring to praise*** — the self **enlists its *whole* inner being**, "all that is within me," every faculty gathered into the blessing *(inferred: "O my soul… all that is within me" musters the entire interior, cf. Ps 57:8 "awake, my glory", 42's self-interrogation — here the positive rousing)*. And it commands its own **memory**: "**forget not** all his benefits" — the self governs its *remembering*, guarding against the ingratitude of forgetting *(stated; the self directs its own memory, cf. Ps 77's willed remembering)*.

**II. The renewal of the self (vv.3–5).**
"who **forgives** (H5545, M11) all your iniquity, who **heals** all your diseases, who **redeems** your life from the pit… who **satisfies** (H7646, *saba*) you with good so that your **youth** is **renewed** (H2318, *chadash*) like the eagle's" (vv.3–5). The finding: the inner being, satisfied with good, is **re-youthed** — its *youth renewed* like the eagle (which molts and renews) *(stated)*. The operation: the self is **renewed/rejuvenated** by God's benefits — not merely maintained but *made young again*, its vitality restored *(inferred: "satisfies you with good so that your youth is renewed" makes the satisfaction issue in a renewal of the self's very youth; cf. the revived-again of Ps 71:20)*.

**III. God's fatherly compassion grounded in knowing our dust-frame (vv.11–14).**
"As high as the heavens are above the earth, so great is his **steadfast love**… as far as the east is from the west, so far does he **remove our transgressions**… As a **father** shows **compassion** (H7355, M05, *racham*) to his children, so the LORD shows compassion to those who **fear** (H3373, M01) him. **For he knows our frame; he remembers that we are dust**" (vv.11–14). Two gem-findings. The inner being's **transgressions are removed to an infinite distance** — "as far as the east is from the west" — the completeness of forgiveness *(stated)*. And, the psalm's tender centre: God's compassion is **fatherly** and **grounded in his *knowing our frailty*** — "he knows our *frame*; he remembers that we are *dust*" *(stated)*. The operation: God's tender regard **factors in the self's weakness** — his compassion turns on an *accounting of how frail the inner being is* (dust), like a father's toward a child *(inferred: "he knows our frame… we are dust" makes the divine compassion rest on a reckoning of human frailty; the same finding as Ps 78:39's "he remembered they were but flesh", here as a father's tenderness)*.

## What Psalm 103 says about the inner being
- **The self can *command its whole inner being to bless* (vv.1–2, 22).** "O my soul… all that is within me" — self-address in the mode of rousing to praise, mustering every faculty; and it governs its own *memory* ("forget not"), guarding against the ingratitude of forgetting.
- **The self can be *renewed / re-youthed* (v.5).** Satisfied with good, the inner being's youth is renewed like the eagle's — vitality restored, not merely maintained.
- **God's compassion is grounded in *knowing our frailty* (vv.13–14).** Fatherly, and turning on his accounting that "we are dust" — the tender regard for weakness (with Ps 78:39). And transgressions are removed to an infinite distance — forgiveness complete.

## Honest notes
- **A cornerstone self-address datum:** "Bless the LORD, O my soul" is the inner being's *self-government in the mode of praise* — mustering the whole interior and its memory (with Ps 42's self-interrogation, 57:8's "awake my glory", 62:5's self-commanded silence). A key exemplar of the dialogical/self-governing inner being.
- **"he knows our frame… we are dust" (v.14)** captured gate-2; the dust-frame compassion read from it — a tender datum (with Ps 78:39, 90:3).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp at v.2 "forget not"; bearer=LORD bleed pervasive incl. the psalmist's soul mis-assigned; intensity *all*; *renewed/frame/dust* gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *soul* (H5315, M47, vv.1,2,22); *forgives* (H5545, M11, v.3); *fear* (H3373, M01, vv.11,13); *shows-compassion* (H7355, M05, v.13). *forget/renewed/frame/dust/remove-transgressions* captured gate-2 — the self-address, renewal, and dust-frame compassion read from these.

## Psalm 104 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 104 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 104:1–35 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (14 vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Scope honesty up front:** Psalm 104 is the great **creation hymn** — its body (light, waters, mountains, springs, birds, beasts, moon, sun, sea, Leviathan, vv.2–30) is *God's works*, not the inner being. The inner-being findings are three, and they **bookend and punctuate** the contemplation: the self **rousing itself to bless upon beholding creation** (vv.1, 35); creational **provision aimed at the heart** (v.15); and the **contemplation itself offered as worship** (v.34).

## The reading

**I. The self rousing itself to bless — upon beholding creation (vv.1, 35).**
"**Bless the LORD, O my soul** (H5315, the seat — M47)!… You are clothed with splendor and majesty" (v.1); and at the close, "**Bless the LORD, O my soul**! Praise the LORD!" (v.35). The finding — continuous with Ps 103 — the inner being **commands *itself* to bless God**, and here that self-address **frames a long contemplation of creation** *(stated)*. The operation: the self rouses itself to bless **as the response to *beholding God's works*** — the blessing is *evoked by contemplation*, the whole survey of creation gathered up into the self's "Bless the LORD, O my soul" *(inferred: the same self-address as 103 opens and closes 104, but here it brackets the creation-survey — the beholding of the works is what the self blesses God *for*; contemplation → blessing)*.

**II. Provision aimed at the heart (v.15).**
"…and **wine to gladden** (H8055, M04) the **heart** (H3824, M47) of man, oil to make his face shine and bread to **strengthen** man's heart" (v.15). The finding: God's material provision is **aimed at the inner being** — the wine *gladdens the heart*, the bread *strengthens the heart* *(stated)*. The operation: bodily provision **reaches through to the heart** — creation's gifts are not merely for the body but *gladden and sustain the inner being* *(inferred: "wine to gladden the heart… bread to strengthen the heart" makes the creational provision terminate in the heart's gladness and strength — the outer gift touches the inner life)*.

**III. The contemplation itself offered as worship (v.34).**
"May my **meditation** (H7879, M03) be pleasing to him, for I **rejoice** (H8055, M04) in the LORD" (v.34). The finding: the self **offers its *meditation*** to God and **rejoices** in him *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's *contemplation itself becomes an offering* — the very act of meditating on the works is presented *to God as pleasing*, and issues in rejoicing *(inferred: "may my meditation be pleasing… I rejoice in the LORD" turns the psalm's own act of beholding-creation into worship — the meditation is offered up, and the beholding gladdens the self; cf. Ps 19:14's "meditation of my heart… acceptable")*.

## What Psalm 104 says about the inner being
- **The self rouses itself to bless *upon beholding creation* (vv.1, 35).** The 103-style self-address here brackets a long contemplation — the survey of God's works is gathered into the self's "Bless the LORD, O my soul"; contemplation issues in blessing.
- **Creational provision *reaches the heart* (v.15).** Wine gladdens the heart, bread strengthens it — the outer gift terminates in the inner being's gladness and sustenance, not merely the body.
- **The *contemplation itself* is offered as worship (v.34).** The self presents its meditation to God as pleasing and rejoices in him — the act of beholding-creation becomes an inner offering.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** this is overwhelmingly a creation hymn; ~30 verses describe God's works. The inner-being weight is the bless-bookend (vv.1, 35, continuous with Ps 103), the heart-provision (v.15), and the offered meditation/rejoicing (v.34). I have *not* inflated the creation-body into inner-being content.
- **v.29 "they are dismayed"** (H0926, M01) is the *creatures'* dismay when God hides his face — a datum about creaturely dependence, not distinctively the human inner being; noted, not developed.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed pervasive — incl. the psalmist's "my soul"; intensity *all/very*; much of the creation-imagery gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *soul* (H5315, M47, vv.1,35); *gladden/rejoice* (H8055, M04, vv.15,34); *heart* (H3824, M47, v.15); *meditation* (H7879, M03, v.34). The many M22/M25/M42 creation-terms (splendor, beasts, roar, sing) are the arena, not inner-being findings here.
