## Psalm 105 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 105 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 105:1–45 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (13 vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Scope honesty up front:** Psalm 105 is a **historical recital** — God's covenant faithfulness through Abraham, Joseph, Egypt, and the Exodus (vv.7–45). Most of it narrates *God's dealings*, not the inner being. The inner-being findings are three, concentrated in the opening call and two narrative touch-points: the **rejoicing of the *seeking heart*** and the disposition to seek/remember (vv.3–5); **Joseph *tested by the word* until it came to pass** (vv.18–19); and a **heart *turned* to hate** (v.25).

## The reading

**I. The rejoicing of the seeking heart; the disposition to seek and remember (vv.3–5).**
"Glory in his holy name; **let the hearts** (H3820, the seat — M47) **of those who seek the LORD rejoice** (H8055, M04)! **Seek** (H1875, M41) the LORD and his strength; seek his presence continually! **Remember** (H2142, M41) the wondrous works that he has done" (vv.3–5). The gem-finding: the inner being that **seeks the LORD** is the one whose **heart *rejoices*** — seeking and gladness are joined *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being is summoned to a **posture of *continual seeking and remembering*** — "seek his presence *continually*," "*remember* the wondrous works" — and in that seeking the heart finds its joy *(inferred: "let the hearts of those who seek… rejoice / seek continually / remember" makes seeking-and-remembering the disposition, and gladness its fruit — the heart is glad *in the seeking*, not only in the finding; cf. Ps 27:8 "your face, LORD, do I seek")*.

**II. Joseph tested by the word until it came to pass (vv.18–19).**
"His feet were hurt with fetters; his **neck** (H5315 — *nephesh*, the self/soul — M47) was put in a collar of iron; until what he had said came to pass, **the word of the LORD tested him**" (vv.18–19). The gem-finding: in the fettered, imprisoned Joseph, "the word of the LORD **tested him**" — the *self* held under trial until the promise was fulfilled *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being is **proved / refined by *the word* over a long delay** — the interval between promise and fulfilment is itself the testing, the self held in iron until the word "came to pass" *(inferred: "until what he had said came to pass, the word… tested him" makes the *waiting on the word* the crucible — the self is tested precisely in the gap; cf. the purposed/tested heart of Ps 17:3, here stretched across years)*.

**III. A heart *turned* to hate (v.25).**
"He **turned their hearts** (H3820, M47) **to hate** (H8130, M06) his people, to deal craftily with his servants" (v.25). The finding: the Egyptians' **hearts were *turned* to hate** *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's disposition can be **turned** — the heart is here *moved into hate* within God's sovereign ordering of the history *(inferred: "he turned their hearts to hate" presents the heart's hostility as something into which it was *turned*, a datum on the heart's turnability; noted, not developed — the arena is the Exodus narrative, cf. Ex 1's oppression)*.

## What Psalm 105 says about the inner being
- **The *seeking heart rejoices* (vv.3–5).** Seeking and gladness are joined — the inner being summoned to continual seeking and remembering finds its joy *in the seeking*, not only the finding.
- **The self is *tested by the word* across a long delay (vv.18–19).** Joseph, fettered, is proved in the gap between promise and fulfilment — the waiting on the word is itself the crucible.
- **The heart can be *turned* (v.25).** The disposition is turnable — here turned to hate — a datum on the heart's malleability within the ordering of events.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** this is overwhelmingly a historical recital; ~35 verses narrate God's covenant dealings (Abraham, Joseph, plagues, Exodus, wilderness). The recurring "he **remembered** his covenant/promise" (vv.8, 42) is *God's* faithful memory driving the history — the arena, not the human inner being. The inner-being weight is the seeking-heart call (vv.3–5), Joseph's testing (vv.18–19), and the turned heart (v.25).
- **v.19 "the word of the LORD tested him"** is the psalm's richest inner-being touch-point — the long testing of Joseph in the gap; the "neck/soul" of v.18 (H5315) anchors the self under trial.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer bleed — Lord/Israel/Egypt/Aaron; intensity *all*; prohibition over-stamp at vv.14–15 "allowed no one… harm"; much recital gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *hearts* (H3820, M47, vv.3,25); *rejoice/glad* (H8055, M04, vv.3,43); *seek* (H1875, M41, v.4); *remember* (H2142, M41, vv.5,8,42); *neck/soul* (H5315, M47, v.18); *hate* (H8130, M06, v.25); *dread* (H6343, M01, v.38, of Egypt). The many M22/M23/M44 recital-terms (thanks, strength, covenant) are the arena.

## Psalm 106 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 106 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 106:1–48 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (7 vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The anatomy of a forgetting, craving, impatient heart — set against a God who remembers.** Psalm 106 is a **confession of Israel's rebellions**, and — unlike a bare recital — it is unusually rich on the inner being, because it *diagnoses* the failures. Its findings are operations of a **failing inner life**: the **failure of memory that breeds rebellion** (vv.7, 13); the **collapse of belief into forgetting** (vv.12–13); the **refusal to *wait* for counsel** (v.13); the **wanton craving that tests God — and is answered to its ruin** (vv.14–15); and the **despising of the gift through unbelief** (v.24).

## The reading

**I. The failure of memory that breeds rebellion (vv.7, 13).**
"Our fathers… **did not consider** (H7919, M15) your wondrous works; **they did not remember** (H2142, M41) the abundance of your steadfast love, but **rebelled** by the sea" (v.7); "But they soon **forgot** his works" (v.13). The gem-finding: the root of the rebellion is a **failure of memory** — *not considering, not remembering* God's works and love — *out of which* the rebellion grows *(stated; "did not remember… but rebelled")*. The operation: the inner being's **lapse of memory is the *seedbed of rebellion*** — when the recollection of God's works and steadfast love goes dark, the self turns to revolt; memory-failure *precedes and enables* the sin *(inferred: the "did not remember… but rebelled" structure makes forgetting the *cause*, not a side-effect — the whole psalm reads rebellion as un-remembering; cf. Ps 78:11 "they forgot his works")*.

**II. The collapse of belief into forgetting (vv.12–13).**
"Then they **believed** (H0539, M13) his words; they sang his praise. **But they soon forgot** his works" (vv.12–13). The gem-finding: faith and praise are **real but short-lived** — belief and song at the Red Sea collapse into forgetting *"soon"* after *(stated)*. The operation: the aroused inner being is **transient** — a genuine belief-and-praise that does not *hold*, dissolving almost at once into forgetfulness *(inferred: "they believed… they sang… but they soon forgot" names the tragic brevity of the roused heart — the problem is not the absence of faith but its *failure to endure*; cf. the stony ground of later Scripture, and Ps 78:36–37 "their heart was not steadfast")*.

**III. The refusal to *wait* for counsel (v.13).**
"they **did not wait** (H2442, M18) for his counsel" (v.13). The finding: the inner being **would not *wait*** for God's counsel *(stated)*. The operation: **impatience** — the self runs *ahead* of God's guidance, unwilling to hold still for the counsel that would order its steps *(inferred: "did not wait for his counsel" makes the failure a refusal to *wait* — the impatient heart that will not defer to God's timing or direction; the negative of the wait-on-the-LORD of Ps 27:14, 40:1)*.

**IV. The wanton craving that tests God — answered to its own ruin (vv.14–15).**
"But they had a **wanton craving** (H8378 / H0183, M28) in the wilderness, and **put God to the test**… he **gave them what they asked**, but sent a **wasting** disease among them" (vv.14–15). The gem-finding: the inner being's **craving** was so intense it **tested God** — *demanding* — and the answer is terrible: *the craving was granted, and it hollowed them out* ("he gave them what they asked, but sent a wasting disease") *(stated)*. The operation: **disordered craving is self-destructive even when satisfied** — the appetite that demands and tests God is *answered*, but the granting itself becomes the judgment, the fulfilled craving wasting the very self that craved *(inferred: "he gave them what they asked, but sent a wasting" welds the *granting* to the *wasting* — the got-what-it-wanted craving is the ruin; cf. Ps 78:29–31, the KJV "leanness into their soul")*.

**V. Despising the gift through unbelief (v.24).**
"Then they **despised the pleasant** (H2532, M28) land, **having no faith** (H0539, M13) in his promise" (v.24). The finding: the inner being **despised the good gift** — the pleasant land — *because it had no faith* in the promise *(stated)*. The operation: **unbelief turns the good gift *contemptible*** — the self, not trusting the promise, *despises* the very thing promised; faith and desire are linked, and where faith fails, the desirable becomes despised *(inferred: "despised the pleasant land, having no faith" makes the unbelief the ground of the contempt — the heart that will not trust cannot value the gift; cf. Num 14)*.

## What Psalm 106 says about the inner being
- **Forgetting is the *seedbed of rebellion* (vv.7, 13).** When the memory of God's works and steadfast love goes dark, the self turns to revolt — the psalm reads rebellion as fundamentally *un-remembering*.
- **The roused inner being is *transient* (vv.12–13).** Belief and praise are real but do not hold — they collapse "soon" into forgetting; the problem is faith's *failure to endure*, not its absence.
- **Impatience refuses to *wait* for counsel (v.13).** The self runs ahead of God's guidance, unwilling to hold still for the counsel that would order its steps.
- **Disordered craving is *self-destructive even when satisfied* (vv.14–15).** The appetite that demands and tests God is answered — and the granting itself becomes the judgment; the fulfilled craving wastes the craver.
- **Unbelief turns the good gift *contemptible* (v.24).** The heart that will not trust the promise despises the very thing promised — faith and valuing are linked.

## Honest notes
- **This closing psalm is *rich*, not thin** — because it is a *diagnostic* confession (not a bare recital like 105). It names the inner mechanisms of failure: un-remembering, transient faith, impatience, craving, unbelief. A cornerstone catalogue of the *failing* inner being (the shadow-side counterpart to the seeking/blessing heart of 103–105).
- **The frame — a God who remembers against a people who forget:** the human failure is un-remembering (vv.7, 13, 21); the resolution is that "he **remembered** his covenant, and relented according to the abundance of his steadfast love" (v.45). The contrast (human forgetting vs divine remembering) is the psalm's architecture — God's memory is the arena/hope against which the inner-being findings are set.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp pervasive across the "did not…" confessions vv.7,13,24,25; bearer bleed — Egypt/Aaron/Phinehas/Ham mis-assigned; intensity *all*; much recital gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *consider* (H7919, M15, v.7); *remember/forgot* (H2142, M41, vv.7,13); *believed/faith* (H0539, M13, vv.12,24); *wait* (H2442, M18, v.13); *wanton/craving* (H8378/H0183, M28, v.14); *pleasant* (H2532, M28, v.24); *jealous/wrath/provoked/angered* (M02, of the people/God). The many M22/M10/M26 recital-terms (praise, sinned, righteousness) frame the confession.

## Psalm 107 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 107 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 107:1–43 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (8 vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The soul at the end of itself cries out and is heard — four times over. Book V opens.** Psalm 107 is built on a fourfold refrain: four portraits of the self *in extremity*, each turning on "**Then they cried to the LORD in their trouble, and he delivered them**" (vv.6, 13, 19, 28). Its findings are operations of the **inner being pressed to its limit** — the *fainting/longing* soul (vv.5, 9), the *bowed-down* heart (v.12), the soul that *loathes food* at death's gate (v.18), the *melting, wits'-end* self in the storm (vv.26–27) — and the single move that answers each: **the cry that is heard**.

## The reading

**I. The cry from extremity that is heard — the fourfold refrain (vv.6, 13, 19, 28).**
Four times: "**Then they cried** (H2199, *zaaq*) **to the LORD in their trouble, and he delivered them** from their distress" (vv.6, 13, 19, 28). The gem-finding: the one operation that recurs at every depth is the **cry of the self at the end of itself** — and it is *always heard* *(stated)*. The operation: **extremity drives the inner being to cry out, and the cry is the hinge of deliverance** — wanderer, prisoner, fool, sailor all reach the point where nothing is left *but* to cry, and *that* cry turns the whole vignette *(inferred: the refrain makes the cry-from-the-bottom the universal inner-being move — not strength or merit but the honest cry of the undone self; cf. Ps 34:6 "this poor man cried")*.

**II. The fainting, longing soul satisfied (vv.5, 9).**
"hungry and thirsty, their **soul** (H5315, M47) **fainted** within them" (v.5)… "For he **satisfies** the **longing** soul, and the hungry soul he **fills** with good things" (v.9). The gem-finding: the *longing* soul — fainting with hunger and thirst — is **satisfied and filled** *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being has a **capacity of *longing* that only God fills** — the fainting, craving soul is not rebuked but *satisfied*, its emptiness met with good *(inferred: "he satisfies the longing soul… fills the hungry soul with good" makes the soul's longing the very thing God meets; the appetite is answered, not shamed — contrast the disordered craving of Ps 106:15; here the honest longing is filled)*.

**III. The bowed-down heart; the soul that loathes food at death's gate (vv.12, 18).**
"So he **bowed** their **hearts** (H3820, M47) **down** (H3665) with hard labor; they fell down, with none to help" (v.12); and of the fools in their affliction, "their **soul loathed** (H8581, M06) any kind of food, and they drew near to the gates of death" (v.18). The finding: affliction **bows the heart down** and drives the soul to **loathe food** — the body's sustenance made repellent by inner distress *(stated)*. The operation: extremity **reaches into the inner being's very *appetites*** — the heart is pressed low, and the soul's aversion to food marks a self so afflicted it turns from life itself, at the gates of death *(inferred: "their soul loathed any food… near the gates of death" shows distress reaching down into appetite — the afflicted self loses even the will to eat; cf. Ps 102:4 "I forget to eat my bread")*.

**IV. The melting, wits'-end self in the storm (vv.26–27, 30).**
"They mounted up to heaven; they went down to the depths; their **courage** (H5315, *nephesh* — the self/soul — M47) **melted away** in their evil plight; they **reeled and staggered** like drunken men and were **at their wits' end**" (vv.26–27); then, delivered, "they were **glad** (H8055, M04) that the waters were quiet, and he brought them to their **desired** (H2656) haven" (v.30). The gem-finding: the storm-tossed self's **very courage *melts*** — the inner being unstrung, reeling, *at its wits' end* — and after the cry, made **glad** at the hushed sea, brought to its *desired* haven *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being can be **dissolved past its own competence** — "at their wits' end," every inner resource exhausted — and the cry from *that* place is answered with stillness and gladness *(inferred: "their courage melted… at their wits' end" names the total exhaustion of the self's coping, the precise point where the cry becomes the only move; the "glad… desired haven" is the inner rest on the far side; cf. Ps 46:10 the stilled)*.

## What Psalm 107 says about the inner being
- **The *cry from the bottom* is the universal move — and it is heard (vv.6, 13, 19, 28).** At every depth the one operation left to the undone self is the honest cry, and that cry is the hinge of deliverance; not strength or merit but the cry of the end-of-itself self.
- **The soul's *longing* is met, not shamed (vv.5, 9).** The fainting, hungry soul is satisfied and filled with good — the inner being's honest appetite answered by God.
- **Affliction reaches into the *appetites* (vv.12, 18).** The heart is bowed down; the soul loathes food at death's gate — distress penetrates to where the self turns from life itself.
- **The self can be *dissolved past its own competence* (vv.26–27).** Courage melts, the self reels "at its wits' end" — and from that exhaustion the cry is answered with stillness and gladness, brought to its desired haven.

## Honest notes
- **A coherent inner-being architecture:** four states of the self at its limit (fainting / bowed / loathing / melting), each resolved by the *same* cry-and-deliverance. The psalm is practically a *taxonomy of the inner being in extremity* — a strong Book-V-opening datum, and it closes urging the wise to "consider the steadfast love of the LORD" (v.43).
- **"soul/courage" (H5315)** carries much of the weight (vv.5, 9, 18, 26) — the *nephesh* as the self that faints, longs, loathes, and melts; a rich cluster of soul-language.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed; intensity *all/very*; some vignette-imagery gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *soul/courage* (H5315, M47, vv.5,9,18,26); *cried* (H2199, M42, vv.6,13,19,28); *hearts / bowed-down* (H3820/H3665, M47/M09, v.12); *loathed* (H8581, M06, v.18); *glad* (H8055, M04, v.30); *desired* (H2656, M04, v.30); *affliction* (H6040, M24, v.10). The M22 thanks-terms frame the four deliverances.

## Psalm 108 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 108 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 108:1–13 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Scope honesty up front:** Psalm 108 is a **composite** — its two halves are lifted from Ps 57:7–11 and Ps 60:5–12. The back half (vv.6–13) is the national petition/military plea of Ps 60 (the arena). The inner-being findings are concentrated in the opening (vv.1–3): the **steadfast/fixed heart** and the **self rousing its whole being to praise — waking the dawn itself**.

## The reading

**I. The steadfast/fixed heart, ready to praise (v.1).**
"My **heart** (H3820, the seat — M47) is **steadfast**, O God! I will sing and make melody with **all my being** (H3519 — *kabod*, glory/the honoured self)!" (v.1). The gem-finding (continuous with Ps 57:7): the inner being is **settled, fixed** — a *steadfast heart* — and *out of that settledness* it praises with its *whole self* *(stated)*. The operation: the heart's **fixed/anchored condition is the ground of wholehearted praise** — not a scattered or divided heart but a *settled* one, from which the song rises with "all my being" *(inferred: "my heart is steadfast… I will sing with all my being" makes the steadiness the precondition — the fixed heart can give itself *entire* to praise; cf. Ps 57:7, 112:7 "his heart is firm")*.

**II. Rousing the whole being to praise — waking the dawn (vv.1–2).**
"…I will sing and make melody with **all my being**! **Awake**, O harp and lyre! **I will awake** (H5782) **the dawn**!" (vv.1–2). The gem-finding: the self **musters its "glory" (its whole inner being) for praise** and is so eager it will **wake the dawn** — rouse the very morning to worship *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being **stirs *itself* (and even the day) into praise** — a self-rousing so ardent it precedes and summons the dawn, the whole self and its world called up to worship *(inferred: "with all my being… I will awake the dawn" makes the praise an act of self-arousal that overflows onto creation — the eager self will not wait for the morning but *wakes* it; cf. Ps 57:8, 103:1's "all that is within me")*.

## What Psalm 108 says about the inner being
- **The *steadfast/fixed heart* is the ground of wholehearted praise (v.1).** A settled, anchored heart — not scattered or divided — can give itself *entire* to worship, singing "with all my being."
- **The self *rouses its whole being (and the dawn) to praise* (vv.1–2).** A self-arousal so ardent it summons the very morning — the inner being stirring itself, and its world, up to worship.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** a composite psalm; the second half (vv.6–13, "give us help against the foe… with God we shall do valiantly") is the national/military petition of Ps 60 — the arena, not the inner being. The inner-being weight is the steadfast heart and the self-rousing praise (vv.1–3), continuous with Ps 57.
- **Provenance note:** because 108 reuses 57 and 60, its inner-being findings are *not new* to the corpus — they re-attest the steadfast heart (57:7) and the awaking self (57:8). Recorded as re-attestation, not fresh discovery.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=David/LORD/Ephraim bleed; intensity *all*; military-imagery gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *heart* (H3820, M47, v.1); *being/glory* (H3519, M22, vv.1,5); *make melody / sing praises* (H2167, M42, vv.1,3); *awake* (H5782, M25, v.2); *faithfulness* (H0571, M13, v.4). The M23 military-terms (valiantly, helmet) are the arena.

## Psalm 109 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 109 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 109:1–31 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (6 vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The wronged self that will not retaliate but *gives itself to prayer*; the stricken heart.** Psalm 109 is the great imprecatory psalm — a long, terrible curse (vv.6–20). But its *inner-being* findings are not the curse-content; they are the operations of the **wronged self**: love repaid with hatred, met by **giving oneself to prayer** rather than revenge (vv.4–5); the **poor, needy, *stricken* heart** (v.22); and the self **physically wasted by grief and scorn** (vv.23–25).

## The reading

**I. Love repaid with hatred — met by *giving oneself to prayer* (vv.4–5).**
"In return for my **love** (H0160, M05) they accuse me, but **I give myself to prayer**. So they reward me evil for good, and **hatred** (H8135, M06) for my love" (vv.4–5). The gem-finding: to being *accused in return for love*, the self's response is not counter-attack but **prayer** — Hebrew literally "I *am* prayer" *(stated)*. The operation: the wronged inner being **converts its grievance into *prayer*** — where love has been repaid with hatred, the self does not retaliate in kind but *turns the whole matter Godward*, becoming prayer itself *(inferred: "in return for my love they accuse… but I give myself to prayer" makes the self's move a *handing-over to God* rather than revenge — the injustice is prayed, not avenged; this is the frame that makes even the fierce imprecation an act committed to God's court, cf. Rom 12:19, Ps 35:13)*.

**II. The poor, needy, *stricken* heart (v.22).**
"For I am **poor and needy**, and my **heart** (H3820, M47) is **stricken** (H2490 — pierced/wounded) within me" (v.22). The gem-finding: the self names itself *poor and needy*, its **heart *wounded within*** *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being under sustained assault is **pierced at its core** — not merely troubled but *wounded within*, a heart stricken through *(inferred: "my heart is stricken within me" locates the injury *inside* — the persecution has reached the heart itself; the self's poverty/neediness is the honest confession of its emptied condition, the very ground on which it appeals; cf. Ps 34:18 "the brokenhearted," 69:20 "reproach has broken my heart")*.

**III. The self physically wasted by grief and scorn (vv.23–25).**
"I am gone like a **shadow** at evening; I am **shaken off** like a locust. My **knees are weak** through fasting; my **body** (H1320, the flesh — M47) has become **gaunt**… I am an object of **scorn** (H2781, M06) to my accusers; when they see me, they **wag their heads**" (vv.23–25). The finding: grief has **wasted the body** — knees weak, flesh gaunt, the self a fading shadow — and the scorn is *felt*, the wagging heads registering as reproach *(stated)*. The operation: inner distress **writes itself on the body** and the self **absorbs the contempt of others** — the fasting-worn flesh and the felt scorn are the outward form of a self ground down *(inferred: "knees weak… body gaunt… an object of scorn… they wag their heads" shows the affliction embodied and the mockery internalised — the self diminished to a shadow, cf. Ps 102:3–11, 22:6–7)*.

## What Psalm 109 says about the inner being
- **The wronged self *becomes prayer* rather than retaliating (vv.4–5).** Love repaid with hatred is met not by counter-attack but by handing the whole matter to God — the self *is* prayer; the grievance is committed to God's court, not avenged in kind.
- **The persecuted heart is *stricken within* (v.22).** The assault reaches the core — a heart *pierced/wounded* inside; the self's confessed poverty and neediness is the honest ground of its appeal.
- **Inner distress *writes itself on the body* and *absorbs others' scorn* (vv.23–25).** Grief wastes the flesh gaunt, the self fades like a shadow, and the mockery is felt as reproach — affliction embodied and contempt internalised.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty — the imprecation:** the long curse (vv.6–20, "may his days be few… may his children be fatherless") is aimed at the enemy; read morally it is *what the wronged self prays*, and its inner-being significance is precisely that — the rage is **committed to God in prayer** (v.4's frame), not enacted by the self's own hand. I have *not* treated the curse-content as inner-being findings; the finding is the self's recourse to prayer.
- **v.31 "he stands at the right hand of the needy one"** resolves the psalm — the answered hope of the stricken self; the arena of the plea.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=David/LORD bleed; prohibition over-stamp at vv.12–16 "no one to… did not remember"; intensity *very/many*; curse-imagery gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *love* (H0160, M05, vv.4,5); *hate/hatred/scorn* (H8135/H2781, M06, vv.3,5,25); *heart* (H3820, M47, v.22); *body/flesh* (H1320, M47, v.24); *brokenhearted* (H3512, M20, v.16); *put-to-shame/dishonor/shame* (H0954/H3639/H1322, M07, vv.28–29). The M10/M14/M26 terms (wicked, deceitful, condemn) frame the accusation.

## Psalm 110 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 110 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 110:1–7 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Scope honesty up front:** Psalm 110 is the **royal / priest-king enthronement** psalm ("The LORD says to my Lord, Sit at my right hand"). It is almost wholly about the *enthroned King-Priest* and his victory (the arena) — not the human inner being. There is **one** inner-being touch-point: the people's **willing self-offering** (v.3).

## The reading

**I. The willing self-offering of the people (v.3).**
"Your people will **offer themselves freely** (H5071 — *nedabot*, freewill offerings) on the day of your power, in holy garments" (v.3). The finding: on the day of the King's power, the people **give themselves *freely* / *willingly*** *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's **glad, un-coerced *willingness*** — the self offered *freely*, not conscripted; a volunteered devotion *(inferred: "offer themselves freely" (nedabot = freewill) names a willing inner disposition — the people give *themselves*, and give *gladly*; the offering is of the will, cf. the "willing heart" of Ex 35:5, Ps 54:6 "with a freewill offering I will sacrifice")*.

## What Psalm 110 says about the inner being
- **The self can be *offered freely / willingly* (v.3).** A glad, un-coerced devotion — the people give *themselves*, and give *gladly*; the offering is of the will, not conscription.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** this is overwhelmingly a royal/messianic enthronement psalm — the right hand, the sceptre, the priest "after the order of Melchizedek," the shattering of kings (vv.1–2, 4–7) are all about the *King-Priest*, the arena. The only inner-being weight is the willing self-offering of v.3. I have *not* inflated the enthronement-content into inner-being findings.
- **v.4 "will not change his mind"** (H5162, *nacham*) is *God's* unwavering oath — his constancy, not a human inner-being operation; noted as arena.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=Zion/LORD bleed; royal-imagery gate-2) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *offer-freely* (H5071, v.3, the sole inner-being datum); the M23 power/rule terms and M22 holy/garments are the enthronement arena; *mind* (H5162, M11, v.4) is God's constancy.

## Psalm 111 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 111 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 111:1–10 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Whole-hearted thanks; the works *studied by those who delight*; the fear of the LORD as *the beginning of wisdom*.** Psalm 111 is an acrostic hymn to God's works and character (the arena). Its inner-being findings are three, framing that praise: **thanks with the *whole heart*** (v.1); the works **studied by all who *delight* in them** (v.2); and the cornerstone — **the fear of the LORD is *the beginning of wisdom*** (v.10).

## The reading

**I. Thanks with the whole heart (v.1).**
"Praise the LORD! I will give thanks to the LORD with my **whole heart** (H3824, the seat — M47), in the company of the upright" (v.1). The finding: the thanksgiving is ***whole-hearted*** — the entire heart engaged, nothing withheld *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being praises **undividedly** — "whole heart" naming a self *gathered entire* into the thanks, not partial or distracted *(inferred: "with my whole heart" makes the thanks total — the undivided heart, cf. Ps 9:1, 138:1; the wholeness is itself the inner-being datum)*.

**II. The works *studied by those who delight* in them (v.2).**
"Great are the works of the LORD, **studied** (H1875 — *darash*, sought out) by all who **delight** (H2656, M04) in them" (v.2). The gem-finding: God's works are *sought out / studied* — and specifically by those who **delight** in them *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's **delight *drives inquiry*** — those who take pleasure in God's works *search them out*; delight and study are joined, the loved thing pondered *(inferred: "studied by all who delight in them" links affection to investigation — the self that delights *seeks out*; the works are searched *because* they are loved; cf. Ps 1:2 "his delight… on his law he meditates", 119:2 "seek him with their whole heart")*.

**III. The fear of the LORD — *the beginning of wisdom* (v.10).**
"The **fear** (H3373, M01) of the LORD is the **beginning of wisdom**; all those who practice it have a **good understanding**. His praise endures forever!" (v.10). The gem-finding — a cornerstone of the whole study: **wisdom *begins* with the fear of the LORD** *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's **first and foundational orientation is reverent fear** — wisdom is not first intellect but a *right awe*, and out of that fear grows *good understanding*; the fear is the *starting-point*, the root from which the wise inner life develops *(inferred: "the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom… all who practice it have good understanding" makes reverent fear the foundation and *practice* the path — wisdom is a posture before it is knowledge; the master-datum linking M01 fear and M15 wisdom, cf. Prov 9:10, Ps 25:12,14, 34:11)*.

## What Psalm 111 says about the inner being
- **Thanks is *whole-hearted* (v.1).** The entire heart engaged, undivided — the self gathered *entire* into the praise, nothing withheld.
- **Delight *drives study* (v.2).** Those who delight in God's works *seek them out* — affection and inquiry joined; the loved thing is searched out *because* it is loved.
- **The fear of the LORD is *the beginning of wisdom* (v.10).** The inner being's first, foundational orientation is reverent awe — wisdom is a *posture* before it is knowledge, and good understanding grows from *practising* that fear. A master-datum linking fear and wisdom.

## Honest notes
- **v.10 is a cornerstone** — the hinge-verse of the biblical wisdom tradition, here in the Psalter. It roots the whole M15 (wisdom) cluster in M01 (fear): the inner being becomes wise not by cleverness but by *reverent fear practised*. A key cross-cluster datum for the study (with Ps 25, 34, 112:1, Prov 1:7, 9:10).
- **Scope honesty:** most of the psalm (vv.2–9) describes God's works and character — great, majestic, gracious, faithful, redeeming (the arena). The inner-being weight is vv.1, 2, 10.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed pervasive — incl. the psalmist's "whole heart"; intensity *all*; God's-works terms gate-1 but arena) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *heart* (H3824, M47, v.1); *studied* (H1875, M41, v.2); *delight* (H2656, M04, v.2); *fear* (H3373, M01, v.10). The M22/M26/M39 terms (praise, righteousness, gracious) describe God — the arena.

## Psalm 112 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 112 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 112:1–10 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The firm, steady heart that does not dread — and the melting heart of the wicked as its foil.** Psalm 112 (acrostic companion to 111) portrays the one who fears the LORD. Its inner-being findings: **fear of the LORD issuing in *delight* in his commandments** (v.1); the **firm/steady heart that will *not be afraid*, because it trusts** (vv.7–8); and, as foil, the **wicked's *melting* heart of angry, thwarted desire** (v.10).

## The reading

**I. Fear of the LORD issuing in delight (v.1).**
"Praise the LORD! Blessed is the man who **fears** (H3373, M01) the LORD, who **greatly delights** (H2654, M04) in his commandments!" (v.1). The gem-finding (extending 111:10): the one who *fears* the LORD **greatly *delights*** in his commandments — reverent fear and glad delight *held together* *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's fear **is not dread-of but *delight-in*** the LORD's commands — the fear that begins wisdom (111:10) *matures into pleasure* in God's will, the same self that reveres also *loves* the commandments *(inferred: "fears the LORD… greatly delights in his commandments" joins awe and delight — the fear is not aversive but issues in love for God's word; cf. Ps 1:2, 119:16,47)*.

**II. The firm/steady heart that will not be afraid — because it trusts (vv.7–8).**
"He is **not afraid** (H3372, M01) of **bad news**; his **heart** (H3820, M47) is **firm** (H3559 — *nakon*, established/fixed), **trusting** (H0982, M19) in the LORD. His heart is **steady** (H5564 — *samuk*, supported/upheld); he will not be afraid, until he looks in triumph on his adversaries" (vv.7–8). The gem-finding: the heart is **firm and steady** — *established, upheld* — and therefore **unafraid even of bad news**, because it *trusts* *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being is **stabilised against fear *by trust*** — the "firm/steady heart" is not native fearlessness but a heart *anchored* in the LORD; because it leans on God it does not lurch at bad news, it holds *(inferred: "not afraid of bad news; his heart is firm, trusting… his heart is steady" makes the fearlessness a *derived* stability — the heart is fixed *because* it trusts, upheld *because* it leans on God; the one who fears the LORD fears nothing else; cf. Ps 27:3, 46:2, 57:7)*.

**III. The foil — the wicked's *melting* heart of thwarted desire (v.10).**
"The wicked man sees it and is **angry** (H3707, M02); he **gnashes his teeth** and **melts away** (H4549 — *masas*); the **desire** of the wicked will perish!" (v.10). The finding: over against the steady heart, the wicked's inner being is **angry, gnashing, *melting away*** — its *desire* coming to nothing *(stated)*. The operation: the un-anchored inner being **dissolves** — where the trusting heart is *firm* (nakon), the wicked heart *melts* (masas); the contrast is exact, and the wicked's very *desire* perishes *(inferred: the "melts away… desire will perish" is the deliberate antonym of the "firm/steady" heart of vv.7–8 — the self not anchored in trust has no inner stability, it dissolves in impotent rage; cf. Ps 58:7, 68:2)*.

## What Psalm 112 says about the inner being
- **Fear of the LORD *matures into delight* (v.1).** The reverent fear that begins wisdom issues in *glad pleasure* in God's commandments — the self that reveres also loves God's word; awe and delight held together.
- **Trust *stabilises the heart against fear* (vv.7–8).** The firm, steady heart is not native fearlessness but a heart *established and upheld by trust* — it does not dread bad news because it leans on the LORD; the one who fears God fears nothing else.
- **The un-anchored heart *melts* (v.10).** The exact foil: where the trusting heart is *firm*, the wicked heart *melts away* in angry, thwarted desire — no trust, no inner stability, it dissolves.

## Honest notes
- **A precise firm-vs-melting contrast:** the psalm builds its whole anthropology on *nakon* (established) vs *masas* (melting) — inner stability is a function of *trust*, and its absence a function of its lack. A clean datum on what *anchors* the inner being (with Ps 111:10, 27:1–3, 46).
- **Scope honesty:** the middle (vv.2–6, 9 — descendants blessed, wealth, generosity, righteousness enduring) describes the *blessed life* of the God-fearer (the arena/fruit); the inner-being weight is the fearing-delighting heart (v.1) and the firm/steady/unafraid heart vs the melting one (vv.7–8, 10).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed at v.1 "fears"; prohibition over-stamp at vv.7–8 "not afraid"; intensity *very*) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *fears/afraid* (H3373/H3372, M01, vv.1,7,8); *delights* (H2654, M04, v.1); *heart* (H3820, M47, vv.7,8); *trusting* (H0982, M19, v.7); *angry* (H3707, M02, v.10). The M39/M26/M46 terms (blessed, righteousness, wealth) describe the blessed life — the arena.

## Psalm 113 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 113 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 113:1–9 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Scope honesty up front:** Psalm 113 (opening the Hallel) is a hymn to the LORD who is *exalted above all* yet *stoops to the lowly* — the whole psalm describes *God's* character and action (the arena). Its one inner-being touch-point is the transformed condition of the lifted: the **barren made a *joyous* mother** (v.9), and the lowly raised to *sit with princes* (vv.7–8).

## The reading

**I. The lowly lifted; the barren made a *joyous* mother (vv.7–9).**
"He **raises the poor from the dust** and **lifts the needy from the ash heap**, to make them **sit with princes**… He gives the **barren woman a home**, making her the **joyous** (H8056, M04) **mother of children**" (vv.7–9). The finding: God's lifting of the lowly issues in the barren woman's **joy** — from desolation to a *joyous* motherhood *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's condition is **utterly reversed** — the self that was in the dust / on the ash heap / barren is raised to honour and *gladness*; the outward reversal *terminates in inner joy* ("joyous mother") *(inferred: "raises the poor from the dust… making her the joyous mother" traces God's condescension all the way into the lifted one's *inner state* — the reversal is felt as joy; the lowly self does not merely change place but is *gladdened*; cf. Ps 107:41, 1 Sam 2:8 Hannah's song)*.

## What Psalm 113 says about the inner being
- **God's lifting of the lowly *terminates in inner joy* (vv.7–9).** The self raised from dust, ash heap, barrenness is not merely relocated but *gladdened* — the barren becomes a *joyous* mother; the outward reversal is felt inwardly as joy.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** this is overwhelmingly a hymn about *God* — his name blessed, his exaltation above the heavens, his stooping to look on the lowly (vv.1–6). The inner-being weight is only the *joyous* mother of v.9 (the felt reversal). I have *not* inflated the God-description into inner-being findings.
- **The high-yet-stooping pattern** (vv.5–7) is a datum about *God's* posture toward human lowliness — the arena in which many inner-being reversals across the Psalter occur (with Ps 138:6, 34:18, 147:6).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed pervasive; praise-terms gate-1 but arena) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *joyous* (H8056, M04, v.9, the sole inner-being datum). The M22/M08/M07 terms (praise, high, brought-down) describe God's exaltation and condescension — the arena.

## Psalm 114 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 114 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 114:1–8 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (3 vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Scope honesty up front:** Psalm 114 is a compact Exodus hymn — the sea flees, Jordan turns back, the mountains skip like rams, the earth trembles at God's presence (the arena). It is about *creation's* response to God, **not the human inner being**. It yields **essentially no distinct inner-being finding**; the one transferable datum is the *appropriate posture of awe* modelled by the trembling creation (v.7).

## The reading

**I. Trembling at the presence — awe modelled by creation (v.7).**
"**Tremble**, O earth, at the presence of the LORD, at the presence of the God of Jacob" (v.7). The finding (by extension, not directly of the human inner being): the fitting response to God's presence is a *trembling awe* — here commanded of the *earth* and its mountains/sea *(stated of creation)*. The operation: the psalm holds up **reverent trembling as the *right* response to the divine presence** — creation's skipping and fleeing *models* the awe the inner being owes; the earth's tremor is the pattern of the reverent heart *(inferred — and cautiously: the psalm speaks of *creation*, not the human self; the inner-being relevance is only that the trembling-at-presence it dramatises is the same awe the reverent self is elsewhere called to, cf. Ps 96:9 "tremble before him," 99:1, 33:8)*.

## What Psalm 114 says about the inner being
- **(Indirect) Reverent *trembling* is the fitting response to God's presence (v.7).** The psalm dramatises this in *creation* — sea, river, mountains, earth — and only by extension models the awe the inner being owes; there is no direct human inner-being content here.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty — this is the thinnest psalm of the batch:** it is wholly an Exodus/creation-trembling hymn. I record *no* direct inner-being finding, and flag the v.7 "tremble" only as the arena's *model* of awe (with 96:9, 99:1) — not as a human inner-being operation observed in the text. To claim more would be to import.
- **A marker for the re-alignment sweep:** psalms like this (114, and parts of 110, 113) are legitimately *arena-only* — they belong to the corpus as context, contributing little to the inner-being findings. Noting the pattern honestly rather than inflating.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=Judah/Israel bleed; creation-imagery gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** none are human inner-being operations — *sanctuary* (H6944, M22), *dominion* (H4475, M23) describe the Exodus arena; *tremble* (v.7) is creation's, taken only as a model of awe.

## Psalm 115 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 115 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 115:1–18 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (3 vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Glory deflected from the self; *you become what you trust*; the threefold call to trust.** Psalm 115 opens with a self-effacing "Not to us… but to your name give glory," turns to a polemic against dead idols, and lands on a triple summons to trust. Its inner-being findings: the self **deflecting glory from itself to God** (v.1); the master-datum that **the worshipper is *conformed to* what he trusts** (v.8); and **trust as the fundamental posture**, with God as help and shield (vv.9–11).

## The reading

**I. Glory deflected from the self (v.1).**
"**Not to us**, O LORD, **not to us**, but to **your name give glory** (H3519, M22), for the sake of your steadfast love and your faithfulness!" (v.1). The gem-finding: the inner being **refuses glory *for itself*** and redirects it wholly to God — the doubled "not to us, not to us" *(stated)*. The operation: the self **deflects honour away from itself** — a deliberate *self-effacement* that will not let praise settle on the self but sends it to God's name; the inner move of *decreasing* so God is glorified *(inferred: the emphatic doubled "not to us" is an active turning-away of glory from the self — the inner being's humility enacted as a *refusal to receive* what belongs to God; cf. Ps 96:8, John 3:30; the opposite of the self-glorifying heart of Ps 10:3, 49:11)*.

**II. The master-datum — *you become what you trust* (vv.4–8).**
"Their **idols** (H6091, M27) are silver and gold, the work of human hands. They have mouths but do not speak, eyes but do not see… **Those who make them become like them; so do all who *trust* (H0982, M19) in them**" (vv.4–8). The gem-finding — one of the most important in the Psalter for the inner being: **the worshipper is *conformed to* the object of his trust** — those who make dead idols "*become like them*," and so do all who trust them *(stated)*. The operation: **trust/worship is *formative* of the self** — the inner being is *shaped into the likeness* of whatever it leans on; a lifeless, blind, deaf idol *deadens, blinds, and deafens* its worshipper; you *become what you trust* *(inferred: "those who make them become like them; so do all who trust in them" states a law of the inner life — the object of trust re-forms the truster into its own image; therefore trusting the living God *enlivens*, trusting dead things *deadens*; a master-datum for the whole study, cf. Ps 135:18, 2 Cor 3:18 "beholding… transformed")*.

**III. Trust as the fundamental posture — help and shield (vv.9–11).**
Threefold: "O Israel, **trust** in the LORD!… O house of Aaron, **trust** in the LORD!… You who **fear** (H3373, M01) the LORD, **trust** in the LORD! He is their **help and their shield**" (vv.9–11). The finding: the summons, pressed three times, is to **trust the LORD** — who is *help and shield* *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being is called to make **trust its *foundational stance*** — reiterated for every group (people, priests, God-fearers), the one posture on which all rest; and the God trusted is *protective* (help + shield) *(inferred: the triple "trust in the LORD… help and shield" makes trust the universal, non-negotiable inner posture — following directly from v.8, the point is *what* you trust determines what you become, so trust the *living* God; cf. Ps 118:8–9, 62:8)*.

## What Psalm 115 says about the inner being
- **The self can *deflect glory from itself* (v.1).** An active self-effacement — the doubled "not to us" — that refuses to let praise settle on the self and sends it wholly to God's name; humility enacted as a refusal to receive.
- **You are *conformed to what you trust* (v.8).** The master-datum: the object of trust re-forms the truster into its own likeness — dead idols deaden, blind, and deafen their worshippers; therefore what you lean on *makes* you. (So the living God *enlivens*.)
- **Trust is the *foundational inner posture* (vv.9–11).** Pressed three times for every group — the one stance on which all rest; and following v.8, the summons is precisely to trust the *living* God, who is help and shield.

## Honest notes
- **v.8 is a cornerstone** — "those who make them become like them; so do all who trust in them" states a *law of formation*: the inner being takes the shape of its object of trust/worship. This is a hinge datum linking M19 (trust) to the whole question of what forms the self (with Ps 135:18). I have foregrounded it as the psalm's central inner-being finding.
- **Scope honesty:** the idol-description (vv.4–7 — mouths/eyes/ears that do not work) is polemic *about the idols* (arena); its inner-being payload is only v.8's "become like them." The closing (vv.12–18, the LORD blesses, the dead do not praise) is liturgical arena.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD/Israel/Aaron bleed; intensity *all*; prohibition over-stamp at vv.5–7,17; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *give-glory* (H3519, M22, v.1); *trust* (H0982, M19, vv.8,9,10,11); *fear* (H3373, M01, vv.11,13); *idols* (H6091, M27, vv.4,8). The M39 bless-terms (vv.12–15) are liturgical arena.

## Psalm 116 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 116 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 116:1–19 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; **aheb-fix build** — v.1 "love" (H0157) correctly tags *characteristic*). Complete chapter (3 vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Love born of being *heard*; the self calling itself back to *rest*; faith held while afflicted.** Psalm 116 is a thanksgiving for deliverance from death. Its inner-being findings: **love arising *because* God heard** (vv.1–2); the self **commanding its soul to *return to its rest*** (v.7); **faith held even in the midst of affliction** (vv.10–11); and the **grateful self seeking what to *render*** (v.12).

## The reading

**I. Love born of being heard (vv.1–2).**
"**I love** (H0157, *aheb*, M05) the LORD, because he has **heard my voice** and my **pleas for mercy**. Because he **inclined his ear** to me, therefore I will **call** on him as long as I live" (vv.1–2). The gem-finding: the self's **love for God *arises from* having been *heard*** — "I love… *because* he has heard" *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's love is **evoked by God's *attentiveness*** — love as a *response* to being listened to; because God inclined his ear, the self both *loves* and resolves to *keep calling* — the answered prayer *generates ongoing devotion* *(inferred: "I love the LORD because he has heard… therefore I will call" makes the love reactive-and-generative — born of being heard, and issuing in lifelong calling; love here is not abstract but the grateful bond of one who has been *attended to*; cf. 1 John 4:19 "we love because he first loved")*.

**II. The self calling itself back to its rest (v.7).**
"**Return, O my soul** (H5315, M47), to your **rest**; for the LORD has dealt **bountifully** with you" (v.7). The gem-finding: the self **addresses its own soul, commanding it to *return to rest*** — on the ground that God has dealt bountifully *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being **governs itself back into *settledness*** — after the turmoil of near-death (vv.3, 8), the self *recalls its soul* from agitation to its "rest," grounding the command in God's proven bounty *(inferred: "Return, O my soul, to your rest… he has dealt bountifully" is self-address in the mode of *stilling* — the self leading its own soul back from distress to repose, the counterpart to the self-rousing of Ps 103:1; the settledness is *argued* from remembered goodness; cf. Ps 62:5 "for God alone, O my soul, wait in silence", 42:5)*.

**III. Faith held even in affliction; the alarmed judgment (vv.10–11).**
"**I believed** (H0539, M13), even when I spoke: 'I am greatly **afflicted** (H6031, M24)'; I said in my **alarm**, 'All mankind are liars'" (vv.10–11). The gem-finding: the self **kept believing *while* declaring itself greatly afflicted** — faith and honest complaint coexisting — and, in *alarm*, made a sweeping bitter judgment *(stated)*. The operation: **faith persists *through* affliction, not by denying it** — "I believed, *even when* I said 'I am greatly afflicted'"; the inner being holds trust and honest anguish *together*; and it notes its own *alarmed overstatement* ("all mankind are liars") as the distortion panic works *(inferred: "I believed, even when I spoke… I said in my alarm" shows faith surviving alongside voiced distress, and a self honest enough to flag its own panic-driven judgment as hasty; cf. Ps 31:22 "I had said in my alarm, I am cut off")*.

**IV. The grateful self seeking what to render (v.12).**
"**What shall I render to the LORD** for all his **benefits** to me?" (v.12). The finding: the delivered self asks what it can **give back** for all God's benefits *(stated)*. The operation: gratitude issuing in the impulse to **respond / reciprocate** — the inner being, overwhelmed by benefit, *searches for a fitting return* (the cup of salvation, the vows, the thanksgiving sacrifice, vv.13–17) *(inferred: "what shall I render… for all his benefits" is gratitude become active — the self not passive in receiving but moved to answer; cf. Ps 103:2 "forget not all his benefits", here the benefits provoke a *response*)*.

## What Psalm 116 says about the inner being
- **Love is *born of being heard* (vv.1–2).** The self loves God *because* he inclined his ear — love as the grateful response of one attended to, issuing in lifelong calling.
- **The self *calls its own soul back to rest* (v.7).** Self-address in the mode of stilling — leading the soul from near-death agitation back to its repose, grounded in God's proven bounty. (The counterpart to the self-*rousing* of 103:1.)
- **Faith *persists through* affliction (vv.10–11).** "I believed, even when I said 'I am greatly afflicted'" — trust and honest anguish held together; and the self flags its own alarmed overstatement as panic's distortion.
- **Gratitude seeks *what to render* (v.12).** The delivered self is not passive in receiving but moved to *answer* — searching for a fitting return for all God's benefits.

## Honest notes
- **A rich self-government datum:** v.7's "Return, O my soul, to your rest" is a prime example of the dialogical/self-governing inner being — here in the *stilling* register (with Ps 42:5, 62:5, 103:1). Cornerstone-adjacent for the self-address thread.
- **aheb-fix confirmed:** v.1 "I love the LORD" (H0157) now tags *characteristic* under the PROMOTE_CHARACTERISTIC rule — the love-born-of-being-heard finding rests on a correctly-typed term (with Ps 18:1, 31:23).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed at vv.6,15; intensity *very*; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *love* (H0157, M05, v.1 — aheb-fixed); *soul* (H5315, M47, vv.4,7,8); *believed* (H0539, M13, v.10); *afflicted* (H6031, M24, v.10); *distress/anguish/tears* (H6869/H3015/H1832, M03, vv.3,8); *call* (H7121, M37, vv.2,13,17). The M39/M22 gracious/thanksgiving terms frame the deliverance.

## Psalm 117 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 117 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 117:1–2 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Scope honesty up front:** Psalm 117 is the shortest psalm — a two-verse universal call to praise ("Praise the LORD, all nations!… for great is his steadfast love… his faithfulness endures forever"). It is a pure summons grounded in God's character (the arena). It yields **no distinct inner-being finding**; recorded honestly as an *arena-only* call to praise.

## The reading

**I. The call to praise, grounded in God's love and faithfulness (vv.1–2).**
"Praise the LORD, all nations! Extol him, all peoples! For great is his **steadfast love** toward us, and the **faithfulness** (H0571, M13) of the LORD endures forever" (vv.1–2). The finding (arena): the whole psalm is a *summons* to universal praise, its *ground* being God's steadfast love and faithfulness *(stated)*. There is no observed inner-being *operation* here — the psalm names *why* praise is owed (God's constancy), not a movement of the human self *(inferred, cautious: to read an inner-being process into a two-verse summons would be to import; the transferable point is only that praise's proper *ground* is God's steadfast love/faithfulness — the arena reason, not a self-movement)*.

## What Psalm 117 says about the inner being
- **(Arena-only) Praise is *grounded in God's steadfast love and faithfulness* (vv.1–2).** The psalm supplies the *reason* for praise (God's constancy), not a movement of the inner being; no distinct inner-being finding here.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** the shortest psalm, a pure call to praise. I record *no* inner-being finding rather than manufacture one from two verses — an honest arena-only marker (with the like note on Ps 114).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (praise-terms gate-1 but arena) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *faithfulness* (H0571, M13, v.2) describes *God* — the arena ground of praise; no human inner-being operation observed.

## Psalm 118 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 118 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 118:1–29 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (5 vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **From distress to fearlessness; the deliberate choice of refuge; God as strength *and song*.** Psalm 118 is the climactic Hallel thanksgiving. Its inner-being findings: the self **freed from the fear of man** by God's answer (vv.5–6); the **deliberate valuation that refuge in the LORD is *better* than trust in man** (vv.8–9); and God become the self's **strength *and song*** (v.14).

## The reading

**I. From distress to fearlessness (vv.5–6).**
"Out of my **distress** (H4712, M24) I **called** on the LORD; the LORD answered me and **set me free**. The LORD is on my side; **I will not fear** (H3372, M01). What can man do to me?" (vv.5–6). The gem-finding: the answered cry **converts distress into *fearlessness*** — "I will not fear; what can man do to me?" *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being, once God's presence is assured ("the LORD is on my side"), is **released from the fear of *man*** — the vertical security *cancels* the horizontal threat; the self reasons from God's nearness to its own fearlessness *(inferred: "the LORD is on my side; I will not fear. What can man do to me?" makes the fearlessness a *derived* conclusion — the assured presence of God *dissolves* the fear of what man can do; cf. Ps 27:1, 56:11 "in God I trust; I shall not be afraid. What can man do to me?", 112:7)*.

**II. The deliberate valuation — refuge in the LORD is *better* (vv.8–9).**
"It is **better** (H2896, M04) to **take refuge** (H2620, M19) in the LORD than to **trust** (H0982, M19) in **man**. It is better to take refuge in the LORD than to trust in **princes**" (vv.8–9). The gem-finding: the inner being makes a **comparative judgment** — refuge in the LORD is *better* than trust in man, even in *princes* *(stated)*. The operation: the self **deliberately weighs and *chooses* where to place its trust** — "better… than" is a *valuation*, ranking God above the strongest human recourse; the inner being sets its refuge by a reasoned preference, not drift *(inferred: the doubled "better to take refuge in the LORD than to trust in man/princes" is an act of *evaluation* — the self appraises its options and ranks God first; central verses of the Psalter (v.8 is its midpoint), and a clean datum on trust as a *chosen* orientation; cf. Ps 146:3 "put not your trust in princes", 40:4)*.

**III. God as strength *and song* (v.14).**
"The LORD is my **strength** (H5797, M23) **and my song** (H2176, M42); he has become my **salvation**" (v.14). The gem-finding: God is the self's **strength *and* its song** — both its power and its music *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being finds in God **both what *upholds* it and what it *sings*** — the source of its strength *is* the theme of its joy; power and praise converge in one object *(inferred: "my strength and my song" fuses the sustaining and the celebrating — God is not only the self's support but the *content* of its gladness; the strength that holds becomes the song that rejoices; cf. Ex 15:2, Isa 12:2)*.

## What Psalm 118 says about the inner being
- **God's assured presence *cancels the fear of man* (vv.5–6).** From distress the self calls, is set free, and reasons to fearlessness — "the LORD is on my side; what can man do to me?"; the vertical security dissolves the horizontal threat.
- **Trust is a *deliberately chosen* orientation (vv.8–9).** "Better to take refuge in the LORD than to trust in man/princes" — the inner being *weighs and ranks* where to place its refuge, choosing God above the strongest human recourse.
- **God is *strength and song* together (v.14).** The self finds in God both what upholds it and what it sings — the source of its power *is* the theme of its joy; strength and praise converge.

## Honest notes
- **vv.8–9 are the Psalter's centre** and a model of *trust-as-valuation* — the inner being appraising and choosing its refuge rather than drifting into it (with Ps 40:4, 146:3). Foregrounded as the psalm's key inner-being finding.
- **Scope honesty:** much of the psalm is corporate liturgy and the rejected-stone/gate-of-righteousness sequence (vv.19–29, the arena of thanksgiving procession). The inner-being weight is the fearlessness (vv.5–6), the chosen refuge (vv.8–9), and strength-and-song (v.14); the "rejoice and be glad" of v.24 is the corporate joy in God's day.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed pervasive; prohibition over-stamp at vv.6,17,18; procession-imagery gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *fear* (H3372/H3373, M01, vv.4,6); *distress* (H4712, M24, v.5); *take-refuge* (H2620, M19, vv.8,9); *trust* (H0982, M19, vv.8,9); *strength/song* (H5797/H2176, M23/M42, v.14); *rejoice/glad* (H1523/H8055, M04, v.24). The M22/M26 thanks/righteous terms frame the procession.
