## Psalm 119 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 119 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 119:1–176 (chapter-driven poetic build; 22 acrostic stanzas; 3,355 rows / 796 spans; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (14 vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`). Here the **word/Torah is the arena**, and the findings are the *movements of the self around it*.
- **The most sustained portrait in the Psalter of the inner being's *whole relationship to God's word*.** 176 verses, nearly every one naming the *word* under one of eight terms (law, testimonies, precepts, statutes, commandments, rules, word, promise). Read first-principles — not as a catalogue of the word's excellencies but as a **map of what the inner being *does* with it**: it *hides, seeks, delights in, longs for, is revived by, is enlarged and freed by, is taught by affliction toward, loves and grieves over, and rests in* the word — and confesses, at the end, that it still *strays*. This reading is organised by those movements.

## The reading

**I. The word *hidden in the heart* — internalised as the guard against sin (vv.10–11).**
"With my **whole heart** (H3820, M47) I **seek** you; let me not wander from your commandments! **I have stored up your word in my heart**, that I might **not sin** against you" (vv.10–11). The gem-finding: the self **takes the word *inside*** — "stored up in my heart" — precisely as a *preventive against sin* *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being **internalises the word as an inward *garrison*** — not external rule but treasure *hidden within*, working from inside to keep the self from sin; the whole-hearted seeking is the posture, the stored word the means *(inferred: "stored up your word in my heart, that I might not sin" makes internalisation *itself* the mechanism of holiness — the word kept *inside* guards from within, cf. v.9 "guarding it according to your word", Deut 6:6)*.

**II. *Delight, love, sweetness* — affection that outbids riches (vv.14, 72, 97, 103, 111, 162).**
"In the way of your testimonies I **delight** (H7797, M04) as much as in **all riches**" (v.14); "the law of your mouth is **better** to me than thousands of gold and silver" (v.72); "Oh how **I love** (H0157, *aheb*, M05) your law! It is my **meditation** all the day" (v.97); "How **sweet** are your words to my taste, **sweeter than honey**" (v.103); "your testimonies… are the **joy of my heart**" (v.111); "I **rejoice** at your word like one who finds **great spoil**" (v.162). The gem-finding: the inner being's stance toward the word is **positive *desire*** — delight, love, sweetness, joy — and it *outbids* every rival good (riches, gold, spoil, honey) *(stated)*. The operation: the self **prizes the word above all other treasure and *savours* it** — affection so strong it is measured against wealth and found greater, tasted like honey; love and pleasure, not mere duty, bind the self to the word *(inferred: the repeated valuations "better than gold… sweeter than honey… like great spoil… joy of my heart" make the word an *object of appetite and love*, ranked over every competing good; the self is bound to it by *delight*, cf. Ps 19:10, 1:2)*.

**III. *Longing* that consumes and pants — appetite for the word (vv.20, 81, 131).**
"My **soul** (H5315, M47) is **consumed with longing** for your rules at all times" (v.20); "My soul **longs** for your salvation; I **hope** (M18) in your word" (v.81); "I **open my mouth and pant**, because I **long** for your commandments" (v.131). The gem-finding: the self's desire for the word rises to a **bodily craving** — *consumed*, *panting*, *longing* *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being **hungers and thirsts for the word** as for food and breath — the longing is not calm preference but *ache*, the mouth opened and panting; a self *starving* for God's rules *(inferred: "consumed with longing… I open my mouth and pant" figures the desire as physical appetite — the word craved like air; the honest appetite of Ps 42:1, 63:1, here directed at the word)*.

**IV. *Affliction as teacher* — the redemptive reading of suffering (vv.50, 67, 71, 92).**
"This is my **comfort** in my **affliction** (H6040, M24), that your **promise gives me life**" (v.50); "**Before I was afflicted I went astray**, but now I keep your word" (v.67); "**It is good for me that I was afflicted, that I might learn** your statutes" (v.71); "If your law had not been my delight, I would have **perished in my affliction**" (v.92). The gem-finding — one of the psalm's deepest: the self **reads its own affliction as *good*** — the very thing that turned it from straying to keeping, the schooling by which it learned the statutes *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being **reinterprets suffering as *instruction*** — affliction is not merely endured but *received as teacher*, the discipline that corrected its wandering ("before I was afflicted I went astray") and drove it deeper into the word that then *kept it alive* ("I would have perished… had not your law been my delight") *(inferred: "it is good for me that I was afflicted, that I might learn" is a positive *valuation of pain* — the self sees its suffering as the means of its learning and the word as what sustained it *through* the suffering; a mature inner operation, cf. Heb 12:11, Ps 94:12)*.

**V. The word as *revival / life to the dust-clinging soul* (vv.25, 50).**
"My **soul clings to the dust**; **give me life** according to your word!" (v.25); "your promise **gives me life**" (v.50). The gem-finding: when the self is at its lowest — *clinging to the dust* — the word is what **revives** it *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being at the point of collapse **draws its very *life* from the word** — "revive me / give me life according to your word" is the recurring cry (vv.25, 37, 40, 50, 88, 107, 154, 156); the word is not only guide and delight but *resuscitation* for a soul in the dust *(inferred: the repeated "give me life according to your word" makes the word the *source of vitality* for the fainting self — where the soul cleaves to dust, the word raises it; cf. Ps 19:7 "reviving the soul")*.

**VI. The *enlarged heart* that runs; the *wide place* of freedom (vv.32, 45).**
"I will **run** in the way of your commandments when you **enlarge my heart**!" (v.32); "I shall **walk in a wide place**, for I have sought your precepts" (v.45). The gem-finding: obedience is experienced not as confinement but as **freedom** — a *wide place*, and a heart *enlarged* so it can *run* *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being finds the word ***liberating*** — the enlarged heart runs where a cramped one could only trudge; keeping the precepts opens a *wide place* rather than narrowing the self; a paradox where law is the ground of liberty *(inferred: "run… when you enlarge my heart… walk in a wide place" makes obedience the *expansion* of the self, not its restriction — the word frees; cf. Ps 18:19,36, James 1:25 "the law of liberty")*.

**VII. The word as *lamp and light* — guidance in the dark (v.105).**
"Your word is a **lamp to my feet** and a **light to my path**" (v.105). The finding: the self navigates by the word *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being **takes its *guidance* from the word** — a lamp for the single next step ("to my feet") and a light for the longer way ("to my path"); the self walks by it through the dark *(inferred: "lamp to my feet… light to my path" makes the word the self's *illumination* for both immediate step and onward direction; cf. Prov 6:23)*.

**VIII. *Love of the word and grief over its neglect* — moral passion (vv.113, 136, 165).**
"I **hate** (H8130, M06) the **double-minded**, but I **love** (H0157, M05) your law" (v.113); "My eyes shed **streams of tears**, because people do not keep your law" (v.136); "Great **peace** (M33) have those who love your law; **nothing can make them stumble**" (v.165). The gem-finding: the self's attachment to the word generates a whole **moral affect** — *hatred* of duplicity, *love* of the law, and *tears* over others' disobedience *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's love of the word **spills into passion for it in the world** — it *hates* what opposes the word (the double-minded), *weeps* that others break it, and enjoys a *great peace* that keeps it from stumbling; the word has become so much the self's own that its violation *grieves* the self *(inferred: "streams of tears because people do not keep your law" shows the word so internalised that others' neglect wounds the self — love of the word become grief over its dishonour; and "great peace… nothing shall make them stumble" the settled security it yields; cf. Ps 119:158, Jer 9:1)*.

**IX. The closing confession — the *lost sheep* that has not forgotten (v.176).**
"I have **gone astray like a lost sheep**; **seek your servant**, for I do not **forget** your commandments" (v.176). The gem-finding: after 175 verses of devotion, the self ends not on mastery but on **straying** — "I have gone astray like a lost sheep" — yet *still* holding the word ("I do not forget your commandments") *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's honest self-assessment is that it **remains a *straying* self even at its most devoted** — it cannot keep itself, and asks *God* to seek it; the devotion is real, but so is the wandering, and the final posture is *dependence*, not achievement *(inferred: ending the great word-psalm on "I have gone astray… seek your servant" is a profound humility — the most law-loving self in Scripture confesses it still strays and needs seeking; devotion and neediness held together to the last; cf. Ps 23:1, Isa 53:6, Luke 15:4)*.

## What Psalm 119 says about the inner being
- **The word is *internalised* as the guard against sin (vv.10–11).** Hidden in the heart, it works from *inside* — holiness by treasure stored within, not rule imposed without.
- **The self relates to the word by *delight, love, and appetite* — not mere duty (vv.14, 20, 72, 97, 103, 131, 162).** It prizes the word above riches and gold, tastes it like honey, and *longs / pants / is consumed* for it — bound by pleasure and craving.
- **Affliction is *received as teacher* (vv.67, 71, 92).** The self reads its suffering as *good* — the discipline that corrected its straying and drove it into the word that then kept it alive; a mature reinterpretation of pain.
- **The word is *revival* to the dust-clinging soul (vv.25, 50).** At its lowest the self draws its very *life* from the word — "give me life according to your word," the recurring cry.
- **Obedience is *freedom*, not confinement (vv.32, 45).** An *enlarged* heart that runs; a *wide place* — the word expands the self rather than cramping it.
- **Love of the word becomes *moral passion* (vv.113, 136, 165).** Hatred of duplicity, tears over others' neglect, and a *great peace* that keeps from stumbling — the word so owned that its violation grieves the self.
- **The devoted self is *still a straying self* (v.176).** The great word-psalm ends on "I have gone astray like a lost sheep; seek your servant" — devotion and neediness held together; the final posture is dependence, not mastery.

## Honest notes
- **The cornerstone word-psalm:** Psalm 119 is *the* sustained inner-being-and-the-word text in Scripture. Its findings are not about the word's properties (arena) but about the *self's operations around it* — internalising, desiring, being taught, revived, freed, grieved, and finally confessing dependence. A master-source for how the inner being *relates to God's revelation* (with Ps 1, 19:7–11).
- **Method honesty on scope:** at 176 verses I have read by *movement*, not verse-by-verse — grouping the recurring operations and grounding each in representative verses. This is faithful to the psalm's own design (the eight word-terms cycle throughout; the acrostic is formal, not thematic-sequential), but it means individual verses not cited still instance one of the named movements. No movement has been invented; each is attested repeatedly.
- **The "revive/give me life" refrain** (vv.25, 37, 40, 50, 88, 107, 149, 154, 156, 159) and the **"delight" refrain** (vv.14, 16, 24, 35, 47, 70, 77, 92, 143, 174) are the two most repeated inner-being motions — logged here as the psalm's spine.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed pervasive; prohibition over-stamp across the many "let me not… I do not…" petitions; intensity *all/whole*; eight word-terms mostly gate-1 but *arena*; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant, representative):** *whole-heart/heart* (H3820, M47, vv.2,10,11,32,34,36,58,69,111,112,145); *love* (H0157, M05, vv.47,48,97,113,119,127,159,163,165,167 — aheb-fixed); *delight/rejoice* (H7797/H8055, M04, vv.14,16,24,47,70,111,143,162,174); *soul/longing* (H5315, M47, vv.20,25,28,81,109,129,167,175); *affliction* (H6040, M24, vv.50,67,71,92,153); *hate* (H8130, M06, vv.104,113,128,163); *hope* (M18, vv.43,49,74,81,114,147,166); *peace* (M33, v.165); *tears* (M03, v.136). The eight word-terms are the arena in which every movement occurs.

## Psalm 120 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 120 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 120:1–7 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (2 vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The peaceable self worn down by dwelling among the hostile. The Songs of Ascents begin.** Psalm 120 opens the pilgrim songs in distress. Its inner-being findings: the cry from **distress that is answered** (v.1); and the ache of the **peace-loving self *worn out* by long dwelling among those who hate peace** (vv.5–7).

## The reading

**I. The cry from distress, answered (v.1).**
"In my **distress** (H6869, M03) I **called** to the LORD, and he **answered** me" (v.1). The finding: the pilgrim song begins where so many do — distress voiced, and *answered* *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being under pressure **turns its distress into a *call*** and finds it met — the settled testimony ("he answered me") that grounds the pilgrimage *(inferred: "in my distress I called… he answered" restates the cry-and-answer move as the pilgrim's starting confidence; cf. Ps 118:5, 107)*.

**II. The peaceable self worn by dwelling among peace-haters (vv.5–7).**
"Woe to me… **Too long** have I had my dwelling among those who **hate peace** (H7965, M33). **I am for peace**, but when I speak, they are for **war**!" (vv.5–7). The gem-finding: the self is **weary of a *prolonged* dwelling among the hostile** — "too long" — and names its own inmost alignment: "**I am for peace**" (Hebrew *"I — peace"*), set against a surrounding *war* *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being suffers the **friction of being *peaceable in a hostile environment*** — its own bent is toward peace, but every word meets war; the sustained exposure *wearies* the self, which longs to be elsewhere *(inferred: "too long… among those who hate peace; I am for peace, but… they are for war" makes the affliction *environmental and chronic* — the self's peaceable nature is ground down by prolonged company with the contentious; the weariness is the datum, cf. 2 Pet 2:8 Lot "worn out", Ps 55:6 "oh that I had wings")*.

## What Psalm 120 says about the inner being
- **Distress becomes a *call* that is answered (v.1).** The pilgrim's starting confidence — pressure voiced Godward and met.
- **The peaceable self is *worn down by hostile company* (vv.5–7).** "I am for peace… they are for war" — the inner being's own bent toward peace is ground down by *prolonged* dwelling among those who hate it; a chronic, environmental affliction, and a longing to be elsewhere.

## Honest notes
- **A distinctive datum:** the self *identifying itself with peace* ("I — peace") against a warlike environment, and the *weariness* of chronic exposure to hostility — an inner-being affliction that is relational/environmental rather than internal (with Ps 55, and the peace-thread of 34:14, 37:37).
- **Scope honesty:** the "deceitful tongue" and its judgment (vv.2–4) are the *arena* of the distress (the hostile speech that surrounds the self); the inner-being weight is the answered cry (v.1) and the worn peaceable self (vv.5–7).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer bleed; war/tongue-imagery gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *distress* (H6869, M03, v.1); *peace* (H7965, M33, vv.6,7); *called/answered* (M37, v.1). The M14 deceit-terms (lying lips, deceitful tongue) are the hostile arena.

## Psalm 121 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 121 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 121:1–8 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (1 v. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The self lifting its eyes and *locating its help*; the settled security of the kept.** Psalm 121 is the pilgrim's assurance psalm. Its inner-being findings: the self **questioning and answering itself about where help comes from — redirecting its gaze to God** (vv.1–2); and the **rest/security** of the one who knows himself *kept* by an unsleeping keeper (vv.3–8).

## The reading

**I. The self lifts its eyes and *locates its help* (vv.1–2).**
"I **lift up my eyes** to the hills. **From where does my help come?** My **help comes from the LORD**, who made heaven and earth" (vv.1–2). The gem-finding: the self **asks itself where its help is, and answers** — the lifted eyes moving past the hills to God *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being performs a **deliberate redirection of its gaze** — from the hills (whether threat or false refuge) to the LORD; a self-interrogation ("from where…?") resolved by a self-answer ("from the LORD") *(inferred: "I lift up my eyes… from where does my help come? My help comes from the LORD" is an inner dialogue of faith — the self questions its own dependence and *reorients* it to God, past every lesser source; the lifted eyes enact the turn, cf. Ps 123:1, 25:15 "my eyes are ever toward the LORD")*.

**II. The settled security of the kept (vv.3–8).**
"He who **keeps** (H8104, M30) you will not **slumber**… The LORD is your **keeper**… The LORD will keep your **life** (H5315, M47)… your going out and your coming in" (vv.3–8). The finding: the self is assured it is **kept** — comprehensively, by one who never sleeps *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being **rests in being *kept*** — the sixfold "keep" settles the pilgrim's anxiety into security; the self is not self-guarding but *guarded*, and can therefore be at rest *(inferred: the piling of "keeps… will not slumber… your keeper… keep your life… going out and coming in" functions to *quiet the self* — the effect on the inner being is settled security, the anxious pilgrim stilled by the unsleeping keeper; the keeping is God's arena-action, its inner-being fruit is rest; cf. Ps 4:8, 127:2)*.

## What Psalm 121 says about the inner being
- **The self *reorients its gaze* to locate its help (vv.1–2).** An inner dialogue of faith — "from where does my help come? From the LORD" — the lifted eyes moving past every lesser source to God; dependence questioned and *redirected*.
- **The inner being *rests in being kept* (vv.3–8).** Not self-guarding but guarded by an unsleeping keeper — the sixfold "keep" quiets the anxious pilgrim into settled security.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** most of the psalm (vv.3–8) is *God's* keeping — his action, the arena; its inner-being payload is the *rest* it produces. The distinct inner-being *operation* is the self's gaze-redirection and self-answer (vv.1–2). I have kept the keeping as arena and the security as its felt fruit, without turning God's action into a self-movement.
- **The eyes-thread:** "I lift up my eyes" (v.1) joins 123:1, 25:15, 141:8 — the inner being's *directed attention* as an act of faith (where the eyes go, the trust goes).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed pervasive; prohibition over-stamp at vv.3–6 "will not…"; backfilled v. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *keeps/keeper* (H8104, M30, vv.3,4,5,7,8 — God's action, arena); *life* (H5315, M47, v.7). The distinct inner-being datum is the lifted eyes / self-answer of vv.1–2.

## Psalm 122 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 122 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 122:1–9 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Gladness at the summons to worship; love that *seeks the good* of the place of worship.** Psalm 122 is the pilgrim's joy at arriving at Jerusalem. Its inner-being findings: the **gladness at being called to God's house** (v.1); and the **love that moves the self to *seek the good* and peace of the city — for others' sake and God's** (vv.6–9).

## The reading

**I. Gladness at the summons to worship (v.1).**
"I was **glad** (H8055, M04) when they said to me, 'Let us go to the **house of the LORD**!'" (v.1). The gem-finding: the invitation to worship *itself* produces **gladness** — the self rejoices not (yet) at arriving but at the *summons* to go *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being **delights in the *call* to God's presence** — the prospect of worship gladdens the self before the journey even begins; the house of the LORD is desired, so the word "let us go" lands as joy *(inferred: "I was glad when they said… let us go" locates the gladness in the *invitation* — the self's affection for God's house is such that being *called* to it is already joy; cf. Ps 27:4, 84:1–2,10)*.

**II. Love that *seeks the good* and peace of the place of worship (vv.6–9).**
"**Pray for the peace** (H7965, M33) of Jerusalem! May they be **secure who love** (H0157, *aheb*, M05) you!… For my brothers and companions' sake I will say, 'Peace be within you!' For the sake of the **house of the LORD** our God, **I will seek your good**" (vv.6–9). The gem-finding: the self's **love** for the city moves it to *pray for its peace* and *actively seek its good* — and it does so **for the sake of others** ("my brothers and companions") **and of God's house** *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's love issues in ***other-directed seeking*** — love become the will to *pursue the welfare* of the beloved place, motivated not by self-interest but by concern for the community and for God's dwelling; affection expressed as *active good-seeking* *(inferred: "for my brothers' sake… for the house of the LORD… I will seek your good" makes the love outward and self-giving — the self labours for the peace of what it loves, on others' behalf; love as pursuit-of-the-other's-good, cf. Ps 137:6, Neh 2:10)*.

## What Psalm 122 says about the inner being
- **The *summons* to worship gladdens the self (v.1).** The inner being's affection for God's house is such that being *called* to it is already joy — gladness at the invitation, before the arrival.
- **Love issues in *seeking the good* of what it loves (vv.6–9).** The self prays for and actively pursues the peace and welfare of the city — for its brothers' sake and God's house; affection become other-directed, self-giving labour.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** the description of Jerusalem — bound firmly together, the tribes going up, the thrones of judgment (vv.3–5) — is the *object* of the love (arena). The inner-being weight is the gladness at the summons (v.1) and the love-driven good-seeking (vv.6–9).
- **A love-in-action datum:** v.9's "I will seek your good" makes love *practical* — the inner being's affection becoming the will to pursue the beloved's welfare (with the delight-drives-inquiry of 111:2; here delight drives *labour*).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=David/LORD bleed; city-description gate-1 but arena) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *glad* (H8055, M04, v.1); *peace* (H7965, M33, vv.6,7,8); *love* (H0157, M05, v.6 — aheb-fixed); *seek-good* (v.9). The city-description (vv.3–5) is the arena/object.

## Psalm 123 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 123 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 123:1–4 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (1 v. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The servant's eyes fixed on the master's hand; the soul *sated with contempt*.** Psalm 123 is a short pilgrim cry. Its inner-being findings: the **attentive, waiting dependence** figured as a servant's eyes on the master's hand (vv.1–2); and the **soul that has had *more than enough* of scorn** (vv.3–4).

## The reading

**I. The servant's eyes on the master's hand — attentive waiting dependence (vv.1–2).**
"To you **I lift up my eyes**, O you who are enthroned in the heavens! Behold, as the **eyes of servants look to the hand of their master**… so our eyes look to the LORD our God, **till he has mercy** upon us" (vv.1–2). The gem-finding: the self's posture is a **fixed, waiting gaze** — the servant's eyes on the master's *hand*, watching for the least signal, *until* mercy comes *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being **attends on God in *patient dependence*** — not glancing but *fixed* on the hand that provides and directs, holding the look "*till* he has mercy"; a waiting that is both submission and expectant watchfulness *(inferred: "as the eyes of servants… to the hand of their master, so our eyes… till he has mercy" figures dependence as a *sustained watchful gaze* — the self reads the master's hand for its next provision, and does not look away until answered; attentive, patient, submissive expectancy; cf. Ps 25:15, 141:8, 130:6 "more than watchmen for the morning")*.

**II. The soul *sated with contempt* (vv.3–4).**
"Have mercy upon us… for we have had **more than enough of contempt** (H0937, M06). Our **soul** (H5315, M47) has had **more than enough** of the **scorn** of those who are at ease, of the **contempt of the proud**" (vv.3–4). The gem-finding: the **soul is *filled to satiety* with scorn** — "more than enough" (Hebrew *rab*, sated/glutted) *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being is **saturated past its capacity by contempt** — the scorn of the comfortable and proud has *filled the soul to overflowing*, and it is this *fullness of humiliation* that presses the cry for mercy *(inferred: "our soul has had more than enough of… contempt" makes the scorn a thing the soul has been *force-fed* until sated — the self glutted with humiliation, its endurance at its limit; the satiety is the datum, and the ground of the appeal; cf. Ps 69:20 "reproach has broken my heart", 44:13)*.

## What Psalm 123 says about the inner being
- **Dependence is an *attentive, patient watching* (vv.1–2).** The servant's eyes fixed on the master's hand, reading it for provision, holding the gaze "till he has mercy" — submission and expectant watchfulness together.
- **The soul can be *sated past capacity with contempt* (vv.3–4).** "More than enough" — the self glutted with scorn, filled to overflowing with humiliation; the fullness itself presses the cry for mercy.

## Honest notes
- **Two vivid inner-being images** in four verses: the *watching servant's eye* (dependence) and the *soul force-fed contempt* (humiliation at its limit). Both are strong, compact data — the eye-thread (with 121:1, 25:15) and the scorn-saturation (with 69:20, 44:13).
- **Scope honesty:** the "those at ease / the proud" (v.4) are the *source* of the scorn (arena); the inner-being weight is the watching gaze and the sated soul.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer bleed; imagery gate-2; backfilled v. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *soul* (H5315, M47, v.4); *contempt/scorn* (H0937, M06, vv.3,4). The lifted-eyes/servant's-gaze of vv.1–2 is the dependence datum.

## Psalm 124 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 124 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 124:1–8 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (2 vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Gratitude born of *reckoning what one was spared*; the exhilaration of escape.** Psalm 124 is a thanksgiving for narrow escape. Its inner-being findings: the **counterfactual reckoning** ("if not for the LORD… then…") that fuels gratitude (vv.1–5); and the **exhilarated relief of the self set free** — "the snare is broken, and we have escaped!" (vv.6–7).

## The reading

**I. Gratitude born of reckoning what one was spared (vv.1–5).**
"**If it had not been the LORD** who was on our side… then they would have **swallowed us up alive**… then the **flood** would have swept us away… the raging waters" (vv.1–5). The gem-finding: the self's thanksgiving is generated by **imagining the catastrophe it *narrowly missed*** — the swallowing, the flood, the raging waters that *would have* overwhelmed *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being **reckons its deliverance by contemplating the *counterfactual ruin*** — it looks back and *pictures what would have been* without God, and that vivid sense of near-destruction *fuels* the gratitude; thanksgiving deepened by *imagining the alternative* *(inferred: the repeated "if not for the LORD… then… then… then" is the self deliberately rehearsing the disaster it escaped — gratitude intensified by counterfactual imagination; the deeper the imagined ruin, the fuller the thanks; cf. Ps 124:6, 129:1–2)*.

**II. The exhilaration of the self set free (vv.6–7).**
"**Blessed be the LORD**, who has not given us as **prey to their teeth**! We have **escaped like a bird** from the snare of the fowlers; **the snare is broken, and we have escaped!**" (vv.6–7). The gem-finding: the deliverance breaks out in **exhilarated relief** — the doubled "we have escaped!" and the image of a bird flying free from a shattered snare *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being, once trapped and now free, is **flooded with the joy of *escape*** — the repetition ("escaped… escaped!") enacts the breathless relief; the self that was *prey* is suddenly *airborne*, and the freedom is *felt* as elation *(inferred: "escaped like a bird… the snare is broken… we have escaped!" is the affect of sudden liberation — the doubling and the flight-image carry the exhilaration; the self's relief at being sprung from the trap; cf. Ps 18:19, the wide place)*.

## What Psalm 124 says about the inner being
- **Gratitude is *fuelled by reckoning what one was spared* (vv.1–5).** The self rehearses the ruin it narrowly missed — "if not for the LORD, then…" — and the vivid counterfactual *deepens* the thanks; imagining the alternative intensifies gratitude.
- **Escape breaks out in *exhilarated relief* (vv.6–7).** The self once *prey* is suddenly *airborne* — "the snare is broken, and we have escaped!"; the doubled cry carries the breathless joy of sudden liberation.

## Honest notes
- **A gratitude-mechanism datum:** the psalm shows *how* thanksgiving is generated — by the counterfactual imagination ("if not… then…") that makes the deliverance vivid. A transferable inner-being operation (with Ps 129, and the "remember what you were spared" logic).
- **Scope honesty:** corporate/national ("let Israel now say"), and the flood/snare/teeth imagery is the *arena* of the danger; the inner-being weight is the reckoning (vv.1–5) and the exhilaration (vv.6–7).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD/Israel bleed; prohibition over-stamp at v.6 "not given"; flood/snare-imagery gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** the psalm's terms are largely arena-imagery (flood, snare, teeth) and the corporate "our side / our help"; the inner-being data are the counterfactual reckoning (vv.1–5) and the escape-exhilaration (vv.6–7), read from the structure and the bird-image.

## Psalm 125 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 125 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 125:1–5 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (1 v. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The trusting self *immovable* like a mountain; the encircled, secure self.** Psalm 125 is a pilgrim song of security. Its inner-being findings: **trust that makes the self *unshakable*** — like Mount Zion (v.1); the **self *surrounded* by God** (v.2); and the **upright heart** as the object of God's good (v.4).

## The reading

**I. Trust that makes the self *immovable* (v.1).**
"Those who **trust** (H0982, M19) in the LORD are like **Mount Zion, which cannot be moved**, but **abides forever**" (v.1). The gem-finding: the trusting self is **as *unshakable* as a mountain** — it "cannot be moved," it "abides" *(stated)*. The operation: **trust confers *rock-like stability* on the inner being** — the self that leans on the LORD takes on the immovability of Zion itself; not native steadiness but a *derived* permanence, the truster made as fixed as a mountain *(inferred: "those who trust… are like Mount Zion, which cannot be moved" makes trust the source of a *geological* stability of soul — the inner being anchored so that it neither topples nor shifts; the same law as 112:7's firm heart and 46:2's "we will not fear though the mountains be moved", here the *truster* becomes the unmoved mountain; cf. Ps 15:5, 16:8)*.

**II. The self *surrounded* by God (v.2).**
"As the **mountains surround Jerusalem**, so the **LORD surrounds his people**, from this time forth and forevermore" (v.2). The finding: the self is **encircled** by God as Jerusalem is ringed by mountains *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being rests in being ***enclosed / hemmed in* by God** — protected on every side, the divine presence a ring of security around the self *(inferred: "as the mountains surround… so the LORD surrounds his people" gives the felt security of being *encircled* — the self safe within a divine perimeter; the inner-being fruit is settledness, cf. Ps 34:7, 121:5)*.

**III. The upright heart as God's object of good (v.4).**
"Do good, O LORD, to those who are good, and to those who are **upright in their hearts** (H3820, M47)!" (v.4). The finding: the prayer distinguishes the ***upright in heart*** as those for whom good is sought *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's ***inward* uprightness** is what marks the self God favours — not outward conformity but the heart's straightness; the petition locates true goodness *in the heart* *(inferred: "the upright in their hearts" makes the heart's condition the criterion — the inner being's straightness, not mere behaviour, is what is prayed-for and favoured; cf. Ps 7:10, 11:2, 24:4 "pure in heart")*.

## What Psalm 125 says about the inner being
- **Trust makes the self *immovable* (v.1).** The truster takes on the rock-like stability of Mount Zion — "cannot be moved," "abides forever"; not native steadiness but a permanence *derived* from leaning on the LORD.
- **The self rests in being *surrounded* by God (v.2).** Encircled as Jerusalem by mountains — safe within a divine perimeter; the inner-being fruit is settled security.
- **Uprightness is *of the heart* (v.4).** The self God favours is marked by inward straightness, not mere outward conformity — true goodness located *in the heart*.

## Honest notes
- **A trust-yields-stability datum** (v.1) — the clearest mountain-image of the immovable trusting self in the Psalter, joining the nakon heart of 112:7 and the unmoved of 46, 16:8. Foregrounded as the key finding.
- **Scope honesty:** the sceptre of wickedness / the land / the crooked ways (vv.3, 5) are the *arena* (the moral-political setting); the inner-being weight is the immovable truster (v.1), the encircled self (v.2), and the upright heart (v.4).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed; prohibition over-stamp at v.3; land-imagery gate-2; backfilled v. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *trust* (H0982, M19, v.1); *heart* (H3820, M47, v.4); *upright* (M13, v.4). The Zion/mountains/land imagery is the arena.

## Psalm 126 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 126 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 126:1–6 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (2 vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Joy so great it feels *dreamlike*; tears *sown* that reap joy.** Psalm 126 is a pilgrim song of restoration. Its inner-being findings: the **overwhelming, dreamlike joy** of deliverance (vv.1–3); and the profound principle of **sorrow *sown* in tears that reaps a harvest of joy** (vv.5–6).

## The reading

**I. Joy so great it feels *dreamlike* (vv.1–3).**
"When the LORD restored the fortunes of Zion, **we were like those who dream**. Then our **mouth was filled with laughter**, and our tongue with **shouts of joy**… The LORD has done great things for us; **we are glad** (H8056, M04)" (vv.1–3). The gem-finding: the deliverance is so great that the joy feels ***unreal* — "like those who dream"** — overflowing into laughter and shouting *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's joy at a great restoration is **so overwhelming it borders on *disbelief*** — the self can hardly credit it ("like those who dream"), and the gladness spills past containment into laughter and shouts; a joy too big for the self to fully take in *(inferred: "we were like those who dream… our mouth filled with laughter" figures a delight that exceeds the self's capacity to believe it — the stunned, laughing joy of the too-good-to-be-true; cf. Gen 21:6 Sarah's laughter, Luke 24:41 "disbelieved for joy")*.

**II. Tears *sown* that reap joy (vv.5–6).**
"Those who **sow in tears** (H1832, M03) shall **reap with shouts of joy**! He who goes out **weeping**, bearing the seed for sowing, shall come home with **shouts of joy**, bringing his sheaves with him" (vv.5–6). The gem-finding — one of the Psalter's deepest: **sorrow *sown* becomes joy *reaped*** — the weeping that carries the seed returns as harvest-gladness *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's **grief, borne faithfully *through*, is *transformed* into future joy** — tears are not wasted but *sown*, an investment whose harvest is gladness; the self weeps *now* in hope of reaping *then*, and the sorrow itself is the seed of the coming joy *(inferred: "sow in tears… reap with shouts of joy; goes out weeping… comes home with shouts of joy" makes present sorrow a *seed* — grief endured in faithfulness yields a harvest of joy; the tears are not the end but the planting; a profound reframing of suffering as *fruitful*, cf. John 16:20–21, Ps 30:5 "weeping may tarry for the night, but joy comes with the morning")*.

## What Psalm 126 says about the inner being
- **Great restoration produces a *dreamlike, disbelieving joy* (vv.1–3).** A delight so overwhelming the self can hardly credit it — "like those who dream" — spilling past containment into laughter and shouts; joy too big to fully take in.
- **Sorrow *sown* is joy *reaped* (vv.5–6).** Grief borne faithfully *through* is transformed into future gladness — tears are not wasted but *planted*, an investment whose harvest is joy; the self weeps now in hope of reaping then.

## Honest notes
- **v.5–6 is a cornerstone reframing of suffering:** grief as *fruitful seed*, not dead loss — the tears-to-joy principle (with Ps 30:5, John 16:20). A key inner-being datum on how sorrow is *held* — in hope of harvest. Foregrounded.
- **Scope honesty:** the "restored fortunes of Zion / streams in the Negeb" (vv.1, 4) are the corporate/national arena of the restoration; the inner-being weight is the dreamlike joy (vv.1–3) and the sow-in-tears principle (vv.5–6).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD/Zion bleed; harvest-imagery gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *glad* (H8056, M04, v.3); *tears/weeping* (H1832, M03, vv.5,6); *shouts-of-joy* (M04/M42, vv.2,5,6). The Zion/Negeb-restoration imagery is the arena.

## Psalm 127 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 127 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 127:1–5 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (1 v. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The bread of anxious toil versus the sleep God gives his beloved.** Psalm 127 opens with the futility of self-reliant striving. Its inner-being finding: the contrast between the **self grinding itself in *anxious* over-work** and the **rest that God *gives* to his beloved** (vv.1–2).

## The reading

**I. Anxious toil versus God-given sleep (vv.1–2).**
"Unless the LORD builds the house, those who build it **labor in vain**… It is **in vain** that you rise up early and go late to rest, **eating the bread of anxious toil**; for he **gives to his beloved sleep**" (vv.1–2). The gem-finding: the self's frantic over-labour — early rising, late resting, "the bread of anxious toil" — is **futile**, while God *gives* his beloved **sleep** *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being is offered a choice between **anxious self-exhausting striving and *received rest*** — the "bread of anxious toil" names a self grinding itself in worry-driven effort *as if the outcome depended on it*, over against the *sleep* (rest, trust, release) that comes as a *gift* to the one God loves *(inferred: "eating the bread of anxious toil… for he gives to his beloved sleep" opposes two inner postures — the anxious self that over-works because it does not trust, and the beloved self that can *sleep* because it does; the sleep is the fruit and sign of released trust, the very opposite of anxious toil; cf. Ps 4:8 "in peace I will lie down and sleep", 3:5, Matt 6:25–34 "do not be anxious")*.

## What Psalm 127 says about the inner being
- **Anxious self-reliant striving is *futile*; rest is a *gift* to the trusting (vv.1–2).** The "bread of anxious toil" is a self grinding itself in worry-driven effort as if all depended on it — over against the *sleep* God gives his beloved, the fruit and sign of released trust. The inner being can exhaust itself in anxiety or *receive* rest.

## Honest notes
- **A rest-vs-anxiety datum:** "he gives to his beloved sleep" makes *sleep itself* the emblem of trust — the anxious inner being cannot rest; the beloved, trusting self can (with Ps 3:5, 4:8, 131:2). The finding is the *inner posture* the two breads reveal, not a doctrine of work.
- **Scope honesty:** vv.3–5 (children a heritage, arrows, the full quiver) are the *blessing/arena* — a distinct wisdom-datum about family, not an inner-being operation; noted, not developed. The inner-being weight is vv.1–2.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=Solomon/LORD bleed; prohibition/"in vain" over-stamp; family-imagery gate-2; backfilled v. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** the key datum is the *anxious-toil vs given-sleep* contrast (vv.1–2), read from "bread of anxious toil / he gives his beloved sleep"; *beloved* (M05) frames the rest as love-gift. vv.3–5 are arena/blessing.

## Psalm 128 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 128 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 128:1–6 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (1 v. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Scope honesty up front:** Psalm 128 is a wisdom-**blessing** on the God-fearer — his labour, wife, children, and length of days (the arena/fruit). Its one inner-being touch-point is the **root disposition of *fearing the LORD*** from which the blessed life flows (vv.1, 4).

## The reading

**I. The fear of the LORD as the root disposition (vv.1, 4).**
"**Blessed** is everyone who **fears** (H3373, M01) the LORD, who **walks in his ways**!… thus shall the man be blessed who **fears the LORD**" (vv.1, 4). The finding: the blessed life is rooted in **fearing the LORD** — the disposition that, joined to *walking in his ways*, issues in flourishing *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's **reverent fear is the *root* from which the ordered, blessed life grows** — as in 111:10 and 112:1, the fear is not a mood but the *foundational orientation* that shapes the walk and bears the fruit *(inferred: "blessed is everyone who fears the LORD, who walks in his ways" makes the fear the generating disposition — the inner posture that produces the outward flourishing; the fear-of-the-LORD thread again as the root, cf. Ps 111:10, 112:1, 25:12)*.

## What Psalm 128 says about the inner being
- **The fear of the LORD is the *root disposition* of the blessed life (vv.1, 4).** Joined to walking in his ways, reverent fear is the foundational orientation from which the ordered, flourishing life grows — not a mood but a generating posture (with 111:10, 112:1).

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** the substance of the psalm (vv.2–3, 5–6 — the fruit of one's labour, the fruitful wife, olive-shoot children, seeing Jerusalem's prosperity and one's grandchildren) is the *blessing/arena*, not inner-being operation. The inner-being weight is only the fear-of-the-LORD root (vv.1, 4) — a re-attestation of the 111:10/112:1 datum, not a fresh discovery.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed at v.1 "fears"; family/blessing-imagery gate-1 but arena; backfilled v. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *fears* (H3373, M01, vv.1,4); *peace* (M33, v.6). The labour/wife/children/prosperity terms are the blessing arena.

## Psalm 129 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 129 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 129:1–8 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (1 v. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The lifelong-afflicted yet *unconquered* self.** Psalm 129 is a pilgrim song of endurance. Its inner-being finding: the **resilience of a self afflicted *from its youth* yet *never overcome*** (vv.1–3).

## The reading

**I. Afflicted from youth, yet not prevailed against (vv.1–3).**
"Greatly have they **afflicted** (H6887, M24) me **from my youth**… yet **they have not prevailed** against me. The **plowers plowed upon my back**; they made long their furrows" (vv.1–3). The gem-finding: the self testifies to **lifelong affliction** — "from my youth," the back *plowed* into furrows — *and* to **not having been overcome** — "yet they have not prevailed" *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being holds together **long, scarring suffering and *unbroken survival*** — it does not deny the wounds (the plowed back) but declares its endurance: the affliction was *great* and *early* and *lasting*, yet it failed to *defeat* the self *(inferred: "greatly afflicted from my youth… yet they have not prevailed… plowers plowed upon my back" is the self's *defiant resilience* — the honest owning of deep, lifelong wounds *combined with* the testimony that they did not win; the scarred-but-standing self, cf. Ps 124:1–2, 2 Cor 4:8–9 "afflicted… but not crushed")*.

## What Psalm 129 says about the inner being
- **The self can be *lifelong-afflicted yet unconquered* (vv.1–3).** It owns the deep, early, lasting wounds — "the plowers plowed upon my back" — and *at the same time* testifies "they have not prevailed"; scarred, but standing. Endurance that neither denies the suffering nor is defeated by it.

## Honest notes
- **A resilience datum:** the psalm's inner-being value is the *combination* — honest acknowledgement of severe, lifelong affliction held together with unbroken survival (with Ps 124, 2 Cor 4:8–9). Not triumphalism (the wounds are real) but endurance.
- **Scope honesty:** corporate ("let Israel now say"), and the back half (vv.4–8 — the LORD cutting the cords, the imprecation on Zion's haters withering like rooftop grass) is the arena of judgment/vindication. The inner-being weight is the afflicted-but-unprevailed testimony (vv.1–3).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=Israel/LORD bleed; prohibition over-stamp at v.2 "not prevailed"; plowing/grass-imagery gate-2; backfilled v. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *afflicted* (H6887, M24, vv.1,2); the endurance ("not prevailed," v.2) is the key datum, read from the structure. vv.4–8 are the judgment arena.

## Psalm 130 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 130 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 130:1–8 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The cry from the depths; forgiveness that *makes God feared*; the soul waiting more than watchmen for the morning. A cornerstone.** Psalm 130 (De Profundis) is one of the Psalter's great inner-being texts. Its findings: the **cry from the lowest place** (vv.1–2); the profound insight that **forgiveness — not judgment — is what makes God *feared*** (vv.3–4); and the **whole soul *waiting and hoping*, straining toward God like a watchman for dawn** (vv.5–6).

## The reading

**I. The cry from the depths (vv.1–2).**
"**Out of the depths** I cry to you, O LORD! O LORD, **hear my voice**! Let your ears be **attentive** to the voice of my **pleas for mercy**!" (vv.1–2). The gem-finding: the self cries **from *the depths*** — the lowest place, drowning — and still reaches upward for a hearing *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being at its **absolute nadir *still cries*** — "the depths" (deep waters, the place of sinking) is not too low for the cry to rise; from the very bottom the self flings its voice up for mercy *(inferred: "out of the depths I cry… let your ears be attentive" makes even the lowest point a place from which prayer ascends — the self is submerged but not silenced; the depths are the *starting-place*, not the end; cf. Ps 69:1–2 "the waters have come up to my neck", Jonah 2:2 "out of the belly of Sheol")*.

**II. Forgiveness that *makes God feared* (vv.3–4).**
"If you, O LORD, should **mark iniquities**, O LORD, **who could stand?** But **with you there is forgiveness**, that you may be **feared** (H3372, M01)" (vv.3–4). The gem-finding — one of the most searching in the Psalter: the self first sees that *no one could stand* under a God who kept accounts — and then grasps that **forgiveness is precisely what makes God *feared*** *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being discovers that ***grace*, not judgment, generates reverent awe** — "there is forgiveness, *that you may be feared*"; a God who merely condemned would be *fled from*, but a God who *forgives* is *revered*; mercy does not cheapen awe but *creates* it, binding the pardoned self to God in grateful fear *(inferred: "with you there is forgiveness, that you may be feared" inverts the natural expectation — forgiveness might seem to *reduce* fear, but the psalm says it *produces* it; the self that has been spared what it could not survive is drawn into a deeper, love-shot reverence; the fear of the LORD here is the awe of the *forgiven*, cf. Ps 130:7, 1 Kgs 8:39–40, Rom 2:4 "God's kindness leads to repentance")*.

**III. The whole soul waiting more than watchmen for the morning (vv.5–6).**
"**I wait** (H6960, M18) for the LORD, **my soul** (H5315, M47) **waits**, and in his **word** I **hope**; my soul waits for the LORD **more than watchmen for the morning**, more than watchmen for the morning" (vv.5–6). The gem-finding: the **whole soul *waits and hopes*** — grounded in God's word — with a longing **more intense than a night-watchman's for dawn**, the phrase *repeated* to press the ache *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being **strains toward God in *expectant, hoping waiting*** — not passive delay but the taut, watchful longing of one who scans the dark for the first light, *sure it will come*; the self's whole weight leaned forward on God's word, waiting *(inferred: "my soul waits… more than watchmen for the morning, more than watchmen for the morning" fuses certainty and yearning — the watchman *knows* dawn comes yet *aches* for it; the doubled line enacts the straining; the waiting is anchored "in his word" (hope with a ground) and involves the *whole soul*, not a corner of it; cf. Ps 27:14, 40:1, 62:5 "for God alone, O my soul, wait in silence")*.

## What Psalm 130 says about the inner being
- **The self cries *from the depths* (vv.1–2).** No place is too low for prayer to rise — submerged but not silenced, the self flings its voice up from the very bottom; the depths are the *starting-place* of the cry, not its end.
- **Forgiveness *makes God feared* (vv.3–4).** The searching inversion: grace, not judgment, generates reverent awe. A God who only condemned would be fled; a God who *forgives* is *revered* — the fear of the LORD here is the awe of the *forgiven*, bound to God in grateful reverence.
- **The whole soul *waits and hopes*, straining for God (vv.5–6).** Expectant, watchful longing — "more than watchmen for the morning" — certainty and yearning fused, the self's whole weight leaned forward on God's word; waiting that *knows* the dawn comes yet aches for it.

## Honest notes
- **A cornerstone triad:** the *cry from the depths* (the lowest place still prays), *forgiveness generating fear* (grace produces awe — a profound anatomy of the forgiven heart), and the *watchman-waiting soul* (expectant hope with a ground). All three are prime inner-being data; v.4 in particular is a rare and deep insight into how *mercy shapes reverence* — foregrounded.
- **The waiting/hope thread** (vv.5–6) is a capstone of the Psalter's wait-on-the-LORD motif (with 27:14, 40:1, 62:5, 33:20) — here at its most intense (doubled watchman-line) and most grounded ("in his word I hope").
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed; prohibition/"who could stand" at v.3; depths/watchmen-imagery gate-2) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *feared* (H3372, M01, v.4); *wait/hope* (H6960, M18, vv.5,6,7); *soul* (H5315, M47, vv.5,6); *pleas-for-mercy* (M21, v.2); *forgiveness* (M11, v.4). The steadfast-love/redemption of vv.7–8 is the arena ground of the hope.

## Psalm 131 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 131 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 131:1–3 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The un-lifted heart; the soul *weaned* into stillness. A cornerstone of contentment.** Psalm 131 is three verses of profound inner peace. Its findings: the **heart that refuses to over-reach** — not lifted up, not straining after the too-great (v.1); and the **self actively *calming and quieting* its own soul, until it rests like a *weaned child*** (v.2).

## The reading

**I. The un-lifted heart that refuses to over-reach (v.1).**
"O LORD, my **heart** (H3820, M47) is **not lifted up**; my **eyes are not raised too high**; I **do not occupy myself with things too great and too marvelous** for me" (v.1). The gem-finding: the self declares a **heart *not lifted up*** — no pride of eye, no straining after matters beyond its measure *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being **deliberately keeps to its *scale*** — it renounces the over-reaching of pride (the "lifted-up" heart, the "raised" eyes) and the restless ambition to grasp "things too great"; a chosen *smallness*, a refusal to be inflated *(inferred: "my heart is not lifted up… I do not occupy myself with things too great" is an active *self-limiting* — the opposite of the proud heart (Ps 101:5, 18:27) and the over-reaching that troubles the self; the inner being renounces grasping beyond its bound and so finds rest; humility as *chosen proportion*, cf. Rom 12:3 "not to think of himself more highly than he ought")*.

**II. The self *calming and quieting* its own soul — the weaned child (v.2).**
"But I have **calmed and quieted** my **soul** (H5315, M47), **like a weaned child** with its mother; like a weaned child is my soul within me" (v.2). The gem-finding — one of the tenderest inner-being images in Scripture: the self has **actively *stilled* its own soul**, and the result is a soul like a ***weaned* child** at rest with its mother *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being **governs itself into *stillness*** — "I have calmed and quieted my soul" is a *deliberate act* of self-composing — and the image tells its quality: not the *nursing* child who cries and frets for the breast, but the ***weaned*** child, past the craving, content simply *to be with* the mother, wanting nothing but her presence *(inferred: "I have calmed and quieted my soul, like a weaned child" describes a self that has *outgrown restless craving* — weaning is the hard passage from demanding-what-I-want to resting-in-who-I'm-with; the soul no longer frets for gratification but is *satisfied by presence alone*; the self actively led its own soul through that weaning into peace, the stilling-register of self-address at its deepest, cf. Ps 62:5 "for God alone, O my soul, wait in silence", 116:7 "return, O my soul, to your rest", 42:5)*.

## What Psalm 131 says about the inner being
- **The heart can *refuse to over-reach* (v.1).** A chosen smallness — not lifted up, not straining after the too-great; the inner being keeps to its scale, renouncing the grasping of pride and restless ambition, and so finds rest. Humility as *chosen proportion*.
- **The self can *quiet its own soul* into contented stillness (v.2).** "I have calmed and quieted my soul, like a weaned child" — a deliberate act of self-composing whose fruit is a soul *past craving*, content simply to be with God, satisfied by presence alone. The self weaned off restless want into peace.

## Honest notes
- **A cornerstone of stillness/contentment:** Psalm 131's weaned-child is *the* image of the settled inner being — a self that has done the hard work of *weaning* itself off the fretful demand for gratification into rest in God's presence. It caps the self-quieting thread (62:5, 42:5, 116:7) with its most tender picture, and pairs the *inner* stillness (v.2) with the *renounced over-reaching* (v.1) that makes it possible. A prime datum on inner peace.
- **The two verses are one movement:** the un-lifted heart (v.1) and the quieted soul (v.2) are cause and fruit — you cannot still a soul that is still grasping "things too great"; humility of aim *enables* rest of soul.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=David/LORD bleed; prohibition over-stamp at v.1 "not lifted up… not raised"; weaned-child image gate-2) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *heart* (H3820, M47, v.1); *soul* (H5315, M47, v.2); *calmed/quieted* (M33-adjacent, v.2 — the stilling); *hope* (M18, v.3). The un-lifted-heart / weaned-child are the two inner-being data, read from vv.1–2.

## Psalm 132 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 132 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 132:1–18 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (2 vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Scope honesty up front:** Psalm 132 is largely the **Davidic–Zion covenant** — God's choice of Zion, his promises to David's line (the arena). Its one inner-being touch-point is David's **consuming, self-denying vow** — the single-minded resolve that refuses its own rest until God is honoured (vv.3–5).

## The reading

**I. The consuming vow that refuses its own rest (vv.2–5).**
"how he **swore** to the LORD and **vowed** to the Mighty One of Jacob, 'I will **not enter my house** or get into my bed, I will **not give sleep to my eyes** or slumber to my eyelids, **until I find a place for the LORD**'" (vv.2–5). The gem-finding: David binds himself by oath to **deny himself house, bed, and sleep** *until* God has a dwelling *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being is **wholly bent on a single God-ward purpose**, so that it *subordinates its own comfort and rest* to it — no house, no bed, no sleep "until"; a consuming, single-minded devotion that will not let the self rest while God is unhoused *(inferred: "I will not… I will not… until I find a place for the LORD" is the inner being *organised around one priority* — the self's own needs (rest, home) held in abeyance beneath the desire to honour God; devotion as *refusal of self-comfort* until the God-ward aim is met; cf. Ps 69:9 "zeal for your house has consumed me", 27:4)*.

## What Psalm 132 says about the inner being
- **The self can be *wholly bent on one God-ward purpose*, subordinating its own rest (vv.3–5).** David's vow denies house, bed, and sleep "until I find a place for the LORD" — a consuming, single-minded devotion that will not let the self rest while God is unhonoured; the inner being's needs held beneath the God-ward aim.

## Honest notes
- **A single-minded-devotion datum:** the inner being *organised around one priority*, refusing self-comfort until it is met (with Ps 69:9, 27:4) — the zeal that subordinates the self's rest to God's honour.
- **Scope honesty:** the bulk of the psalm (vv.6–18 — the ark brought up, the oath to David, God's choice of Zion as "my resting place forever," the horn for David, the crown) is the *covenant arena*, not inner-being operation. The inner-being weight is only the consuming vow (vv.3–5).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=David/LORD bleed; prohibition over-stamp at vv.3–4 "I will not…"; covenant-imagery gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** the *vow/resolve* of vv.2–5 (the sole inner-being datum), read from "swore… vowed… I will not… until." The Zion/David covenant terms are the arena.

## Psalm 133 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 133 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 133:1–3 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The delight in *unity* as good and pleasant.** Psalm 133 is a three-verse wisdom-song on harmony. Its inner-being touch-point: the self's **delight in and valuation of *unity* as "good and pleasant"** (v.1).

## The reading

**I. The delight in unity as good and pleasant (v.1).**
"Behold, how **good** (H2896, M04) and **pleasant** (H5273) it is when **brothers dwell in unity**!" (v.1). The finding: the self exclaims over unity as *good* and *pleasant* — a warm, appreciative valuation *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being **savours *relational harmony* as a delight** — not a duty observed but a *sweetness relished*; the "behold… how good and pleasant" is the self's *pleasure* in seeing brothers dwell together, an aesthetic-moral delight in concord *(inferred: "how good and pleasant… when brothers dwell in unity" registers unity as something the inner being *enjoys and prizes* — the self responds to harmony with warmth (good = morally-approved, pleasant = felt-as-sweet); the delight is the datum, cf. Ps 16:3 "the saints… in whom is all my delight", the love-of-community of 122)*.

## What Psalm 133 says about the inner being
- **The self *delights in and prizes unity* as good and pleasant (v.1).** Relational harmony is savoured, not merely approved — the inner being responds to concord with warmth: *good* (morally approved) and *pleasant* (felt as sweet); a delight in harmonious community.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** the two images (the precious oil running down Aaron's beard; the dew of Hermon on Zion, vv.2–3) *describe* the goodness of unity (arena/illustration) and end on God's commanded blessing. The inner-being weight is thin — the delight-in-unity of v.1 (a valuation/affect, with the community-love of 122, 16:3).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=David bleed; oil/dew-imagery gate-2) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *good* (H2896, M04, v.1); *pleasant* (H5273, v.1). The oil/dew images and Zion-blessing are the arena.

## Psalm 134 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 134 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 134:1–3 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (1 v. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Scope honesty up front:** Psalm 134 is the closing Song of Ascents — a three-verse liturgical call to the night-servants of the temple to bless the LORD, and a returning blessing. It is a *summons and benediction* (the arena of worship). It yields **no distinct inner-being finding**; recorded honestly as an arena-only call to praise.

## The reading

**I. The call to the night-watch to bless (vv.1–3).**
"Come, **bless the LORD**, all you servants of the LORD, who **stand by night** in the house of the LORD! **Lift up your hands** to the holy place and bless the LORD! May the LORD **bless you from Zion**" (vv.1–3). The finding (arena): a summons to those who serve *through the night* to bless God, answered by a benediction *(stated)*. There is no observed inner-being *operation* — the psalm calls for worship and pronounces blessing; the only transferable hint is that faithful, unseen *night*-service (standing "by night" in God's house) is itself an offering of worship *(inferred, cautious: to read an inner-being process into a three-verse liturgical call would be to import; the "stand by night" points only to steadfast, unglamorous devotion — a posture, not a self-movement observed in the text)*.

## What Psalm 134 says about the inner being
- **(Arena-only) No distinct inner-being finding.** The psalm is a call to worship and a benediction; the "stand by night" hints only at steadfast, unseen devotion as an offering — not an inner-being operation the text describes.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** an arena-only marker (with Ps 117, 114) — I record no inner-being finding rather than manufacture one from a liturgical call. The night-service of faithful worshippers is noted as a posture of quiet devotion, no more.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed; bless-terms gate-1 but arena; backfilled v. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** the bless-terms (M39/M22) are liturgical arena; no human inner-being operation observed.

## Psalm 135 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 135 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 135:1–21 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (7 vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Scope honesty up front:** Psalm 135 is a Hallelujah hymn — praise, a recital of God's works (creation, Exodus, conquest), and an idol-polemic (the arena). Its inner-being findings are two, both *re-attestations*: praise experienced as **pleasant** (v.3), and the master-datum that **you become what you trust** (v.18, = 115:8).

## The reading

**I. Praise experienced as *pleasant* (v.3).**
"Praise the LORD, for the LORD is **good** (H2896, M04); sing to his name, for it is **pleasant** (H5273)!" (v.3). The finding: praise is commended as *pleasant* — an act the self finds *sweet* *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being experiences worship **not as burden but as *pleasure*** — "sing… for it is pleasant" makes praise agreeable to the self, something enjoyed *(inferred: "sing to his name, for it is pleasant" locates a *sweetness* in the act of praise itself — worship as delight; cf. Ps 147:1 "it is pleasant, and a song of praise is fitting", 133:1)*.

**II. *You become what you trust* — re-attested (v.18).**
"Their idols are silver and gold… **Those who make them become like them; so do all who *trust* (H0982, M19) in them**" (vv.15–18). The gem-finding (re-attesting 115:8): the worshipper is **conformed to the object of his trust** — dead idols *deaden* their trusters *(stated)*. The operation: the same *law of formation* as Ps 115:8 — the inner being is *shaped into the likeness* of whatever it trusts; here re-stated verbatim, confirming the datum across two psalms *(inferred: the identical "those who make them become like them; so do all who trust in them" re-attests the formation-law — what you trust *makes* you; recorded as re-attestation, not fresh discovery; see the fuller treatment at Ps 115:8)*.

## What Psalm 135 says about the inner being
- **Praise is experienced as *pleasant* (v.3).** Worship is not burden but pleasure — "sing… for it is pleasant"; the self finds a sweetness in the act of praise itself.
- **You are *conformed to what you trust* (v.18, re-attesting 115:8).** The law of formation restated verbatim — dead idols deaden their trusters; what you trust *makes* you. (Fuller treatment at Ps 115:8.)

## Honest notes
- **Both findings are re-attestations**, not fresh discoveries: praise-as-pleasant (with 147:1, 133:1) and the become-like-what-you-trust formation-law (verbatim from 115:8). Recorded as corroboration — the formation-law appearing twice in the Hallel strengthens it as a corpus datum.
- **Scope honesty:** most of the psalm (vv.4–14 — God's choice of Jacob, the signs in Egypt, the smiting of nations, the LORD's name and vindication) is *God's works* (arena); the idol-description (vv.15–17) is polemic; the inner-being payload is v.3 and v.18.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD/Israel bleed; recital/idol-imagery gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *good/pleasant* (H2896/H5273, M04, v.3); *trust* (H0982, M19, v.18). The recital and idol terms are the arena.

## Psalm 136 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 136 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 136:1–26 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (11 vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Scope honesty up front:** Psalm 136 is the "Great Hallel" — an antiphonal litany rehearsing creation and the Exodus, every line answered by the refrain *"for his steadfast love endures forever"* (26×). It is corporate liturgy about *God's works and chesed* (the arena). Its only inner-being touch-point is the *formative discipline* the refrain works on the self (below) — otherwise arena-only.

## The reading

**I. The refrain as a discipline of *responsive gratitude* (throughout).**
Every act — creation, the Red Sea, the wilderness, the giving of the land, "he **remembered us in our low estate**" (v.23), "he **gives food to all flesh**" (v.25) — is answered: "**for his steadfast love endures forever**." The finding (subtle, and the only inner-being note): the antiphonal form **trains the self to attach *every* work of God to his steadfast love** *(stated of the liturgy)*. The operation: the inner being is *formed* by the repetition — schooled to **read all of history, and its own low estate, through the single lens of God's *chesed*** — every remembered act met with the same grateful confession, until the reflex is the self's own *(inferred, cautious: the psalm is liturgy, not a described self-movement; but the antiphonal structure *shapes* the worshipper — 26 repetitions drill the inner being to answer each divine act with "his steadfast love endures forever," forming a habit of reading everything as mercy; the formation is the only inner-being payload, cf. the become-what-you-rehearse logic, Deut 6:7)*.

## What Psalm 136 says about the inner being
- **(Formation, not a described movement) The refrain *trains the self to read everything through God's steadfast love* (throughout).** The 26-fold antiphon drills the inner being to answer every divine act — even "our low estate" — with the same grateful confession, forming a habit of seeing all of history as mercy. This is the psalm's only inner-being payload; the content is arena (God's works and chesed).

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** an essentially arena-only litany (with Ps 135's recital, 117, 134) — the substance is God's works and his enduring steadfast love. I record only the *formative* effect of the refrain, cautiously, rather than manufacture a self-movement the text does not describe.
- **v.23 "remembered us in our low estate"** is a tender arena-datum (God's attention to lowliness, with 113:7, 138:6) — noted, not developed as a human inner-being operation.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed pervasive; recital-imagery gate-2; the refrain repeated 26×; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** the terms are the recital arena (creation, Exodus) and the *chesed* refrain (God's); no distinct human inner-being operation observed — only the refrain's formative discipline.
