## Psalm 137 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 137 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 137:1–9 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (5 vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Grief that suspends song; the self-binding vow of memory. A cornerstone of sorrow.** Psalm 137 is the great exile lament. Its inner-being findings: the **grief that hangs up the harp and refuses to perform joy on command** (vv.1–4); and the **self-binding vow never to forget — setting Jerusalem above its highest joy** (vv.5–6).

## The reading

**I. Grief that suspends song and refuses to fake joy (vv.1–4).**
"By the waters of Babylon, there we **sat down and wept**, when we **remembered Zion**. On the willows there we **hung up our lyres**. For there our captors required of us songs… 'Sing us one of the songs of Zion!' **How shall we sing the LORD's song in a foreign land?**" (vv.1–4). The gem-finding: memory of Zion produces **tears**, the harps are **hung up** — music suspended — and the self **cannot and will not perform joy on demand** *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being in real grief **loses (and guards) its capacity for song** — it will not counterfeit mirth for its captors; the honest self *cannot* sing joy while the heart mourns, and refuses to *fake* it ("how shall we sing… in a foreign land?") *(inferred: "we hung up our lyres… how shall we sing the LORD's song in a foreign land?" makes grief *incompatible with performed joy* — the self keeps faith with its sorrow rather than manufacture gladness; the integrity of grief that will not lie; cf. Ps 42:3 "my tears have been my food", the refusal of hollow praise)*.

**II. The self-binding vow of memory — Jerusalem above the highest joy (vv.5–6).**
"**If I forget you, O Jerusalem**, let my **right hand forget its skill**! Let my **tongue stick to the roof of my mouth**, if I do not **remember you**, if I **do not set Jerusalem above my highest joy**!" (vv.5–6). The gem-finding: the self binds itself by **self-curse never to forget** — invoking loss of hand and tongue if it lets the memory lapse — and *ranks* Jerusalem **above its highest joy** *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being **governs its own memory by oath and *orders its affections*** — it commits, on pain of self-curse, to keep the beloved city in memory, and *sets* it at the very top of its hierarchy of joys ("above my highest joy"); memory here is a *willed fidelity*, and love a deliberate *ranking* *(inferred: "if I forget you… let my hand forget… if I do not set Jerusalem above my highest joy" makes remembrance a *vowed discipline* and love an *ordering of joys* — the self decides what its chief joy shall be and binds itself to it; the counterpart to the forgetting-breeds-rebellion of Ps 106, here memory guarded by oath; cf. Ps 42:6 "therefore I remember you", 84:2)*.

## What Psalm 137 says about the inner being
- **Real grief *suspends song and refuses to fake joy* (vv.1–4).** The mourning self hangs up its harp and will not perform mirth on command — it keeps faith with its sorrow rather than counterfeit gladness; the integrity of grief that will not lie.
- **The self *binds its own memory by vow and orders its affections* (vv.5–6).** On pain of self-curse it commits never to forget Jerusalem, and *sets* it "above my highest joy" — memory as willed fidelity, love as a deliberate ranking of joys; the self decides what its chief joy shall be.

## Honest notes
- **A cornerstone on grief and memory:** the *integrity of sorrow* (won't fake joy, vv.1–4) and the *vowed, ordered love* that ranks the beloved above the self's highest joy (vv.5–6) are prime inner-being data — memory as willed discipline, love as chosen hierarchy (with Ps 42, 84, and the anti-type of 106's forgetting). Foregrounded.
- **Scope honesty — the imprecation:** the terrible close (vv.7–9, against Edom and Babylon, "blessed shall he be who dashes your little ones") is the *rage of the violated* — read morally as 109's frame: the fury *voiced to God*, the raw cry of the traumatised, committed to God's justice rather than enacted. I do *not* treat the curse-content as an inner-being finding; the finding is the honest grief and the vowed memory. The verse records how real the wound was.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer bleed; prohibition over-stamp at vv.5–6 "if I forget… if I do not"; Babylon-imagery gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *wept/tears* (M03, v.1); *remembered/remember* (H2142, M41, vv.1,6); *joy* (H8057, M04, v.6, "highest joy"); *forget* (H7911, M41, vv.5,6). The Babylon/Edom imprecation (vv.7–9) is the rage-arena.

---

## Psalm 138 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 138 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 138:1–8 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (1 v. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Answered prayer that *strengthens the soul within*; the settled confidence that God completes his purpose.** Psalm 138 is David's thanksgiving. Its inner-being findings: **whole-hearted thanks** (v.1); the gem that God's answer **increased strength *in the soul itself*** (v.3); God's regard for the **lowly** (v.6); and the **settled confidence that God will fulfil his purpose** for the self (v.8).

## The reading

**I. Whole-hearted thanks (vv.1–2).**
"I **give you thanks**, O LORD, with my **whole heart** (H3820, M47); before the gods I sing your praise; I bow down toward your holy temple and give thanks… for your **steadfast love** and your **faithfulness**" (vv.1–2). The finding: the thanks is *whole-hearted*, the entire self engaged *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being praises **undividedly**, its thanks grounded in God's steadfast love and faithfulness *(inferred: "with my whole heart" as at 9:1, 111:1 — the gathered, entire self in thanks; recorded as re-attestation)*.

**II. Answered prayer that *strengthens the soul within* (v.3).**
"On the day I **called**, you **answered** me; **my strength of soul** (H5315, M47) **you increased**" (v.3). The gem-finding: God's answer to the cry did not only change circumstances — it **increased *strength in the soul*** *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being is **fortified *within* by God's response** — the answer works *inward*, emboldening and strengthening the *soul itself*, not merely resolving the outward trouble; prayer answered *builds up the inner self* *(inferred: "on the day I called, you answered… my strength of soul you increased" locates the fruit of answered prayer *inside* — the self is made *stronger, bolder within* by being heard; God's response is inner fortification, not only external rescue; cf. Ps 27:14 "let your heart take courage", Isa 40:29–31, Eph 3:16 "strengthened with power… in the inner being")*.

**III. God regards the lowly (v.6).**
"Though the LORD is **high**, he **regards the lowly**, but the **haughty** (M08) he knows from afar" (v.6). The finding: the high God *draws near the lowly* and holds the proud at a distance *(stated)*. The operation (inner-being-adjacent): the self's ***lowliness* is the posture God draws near to** — nearness to God correlates with humility, distance with pride; the inner condition determines the proximity *(inferred: "the high… regards the lowly, but the haughty he knows from afar" makes the *inner posture* (lowly vs haughty) the thing that opens or closes the distance to God; humility as the condition of nearness, cf. Ps 34:18, 51:17, Isa 57:15)*.

**IV. Settled confidence that God completes his purpose (v.8).**
"The LORD will **fulfill his purpose for me**; your steadfast love, O LORD, **endures forever**. Do not forsake the work of your hands" (v.8). The finding: the self rests in the assurance that God will *complete* what concerns it — while still pleading "do not forsake" *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being holds a **settled confidence in God's *completing purpose*** — trusting that God will *finish* his work in the self, yet honestly voicing the fear of abandonment alongside the trust *(inferred: "the LORD will fulfill his purpose for me… do not forsake the work of your hands" holds assurance and appeal together — confidence in God's perseverance with the self, coexisting with the honest plea; cf. Phil 1:6 "he who began a good work… will bring it to completion", Ps 57:2)*.

## What Psalm 138 says about the inner being
- **Answered prayer *strengthens the soul within* (v.3).** God's response works *inward* — "my strength of soul you increased" — fortifying and emboldening the inner self, not merely resolving the outward trouble; being heard *builds up* the self.
- **Lowliness is the posture God *draws near to* (v.6).** The inner condition — lowly vs haughty — opens or closes the distance to God; humility is the condition of nearness.
- **The self rests in God's *completing purpose* (v.8).** A settled confidence that God will *finish* his work in the self — held honestly alongside the plea "do not forsake."
- **(Re-attested) Thanks is *whole-hearted* (v.1).** The entire self gathered into praise.

## Honest notes
- **v.3 is the distinctive datum:** answered prayer as *inner strengthening* — the soul itself made stronger by being heard (with Eph 3:16, Isa 40:31). A valuable inner-being finding: God's answers fortify the *interior*, not only the circumstance. Foregrounded.
- **Scope honesty:** the "before the gods," the kings of the earth praising (vv.1, 4–5), and God's steadfast love/faithfulness are the arena; the inner-being weight is vv.3, 6, 8 (and the whole-heart of v.1).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=David/LORD bleed; prohibition at v.8 "do not forsake"; backfilled v. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *whole heart* (H3820, M47, v.1); *strength-of-soul* (H5315, M47, v.3); *lowly/haughty* (M24/M08, v.6); *called/answered* (M37, v.3). The steadfast-love/faithfulness and kings-praising terms are the arena.

## Psalm 139 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 139 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 139:1–24 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (5 vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The self fully *known*, inescapably *accompanied*, intricately *made* — and its final self-offering to be *searched*. A major cornerstone.** Psalm 139 is the Psalter's deepest meditation on the inner being *before God's knowledge*. Its findings: the self **exhaustively known from within** (vv.1–6); the self that **cannot flee God's presence** (vv.7–12); the self **formed and foreknown before birth** (vv.13–16); and the climactic move — the fully-known self **inviting God to search it further** (vv.23–24).

## The reading

**I. The self exhaustively known from within (vv.1–6).**
"O LORD, you have **searched me and known me**! You know when I sit down and when I rise up; you **discern my thoughts from afar**… you are **acquainted with all my ways**" (vv.1–3). The gem-finding: the inner being is **known utterly** — its sitting and rising, its *thoughts discerned from afar*, its every way traced *(stated)*. The operation: the self reckons that its ***interior is completely open* to God** — not behaviour only but *thoughts*, and those known "from afar" (before they surface); there is no hidden chamber, no unread thought; the inner being lives *wholly exposed* to a knowing that precedes even its own self-awareness *(inferred: "you discern my thoughts from afar… acquainted with all my ways" makes the self *transparent* to God — the interior fully read, the thought known before it is thought; "such knowledge is too wonderful for me" (v.6) is the self's awe at being *this* known; cf. Ps 44:21 "he knows the secrets of the heart", Heb 4:13)*.

**II. The self that cannot flee God's presence (vv.7–12).**
"Where shall I go from your Spirit? Or where shall I **flee from your presence**? If I ascend to heaven, **you are there**! If I make my bed in **Sheol**, you are there!… even the **darkness is not dark to you**" (vv.7–12). The gem-finding: there is **nowhere the self could go to escape God** — height, depth, darkness, the far sea — God is *there* *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being confronts the **impossibility of *hiding* from God** — and, in this psalm's key, receives it not as threat but as *inescapable accompaniment*; wherever the self flees, even to Sheol or darkness, it finds God *already there*, holding it ("your right hand shall hold me," v.10) *(inferred: "if I make my bed in Sheol, you are there… the darkness is not dark to you" turns the impossibility-of-flight into *presence-in-every-place* — the self can never be *alone* or *lost*; the same omnipresence that forbids hiding also guarantees company; cf. Ps 23:4, Rom 8:38–39)*.

**III. The self formed and foreknown before birth (vv.13–16).**
"For you **formed my inward parts**; you **knitted me together** in my mother's womb. I praise you, for I am **fearfully and wonderfully made**… your eyes saw my **unformed substance**; in your book were written… the **days that were formed for me**, when as yet there was none of them" (vv.13–16). The gem-finding: the self is God's **intimate handiwork** — knitted in the womb, *fearfully and wonderfully made* — and **foreknown before it existed**, its days written before one was lived *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being marvels at its own ***createdness and foreknownness*** — it did not make itself; it is *woven* by God, *wonderful* in its making, and *known from before its origin*; the self's very existence is God's craft and God's foreknowledge, and the fitting response is praise *(inferred: "you formed my inward parts… fearfully and wonderfully made… days written when as yet there was none" grounds the self's being in God's *forming and foreknowing* — the inner being is neither accident nor self-origin but intimate, praised handiwork; "my soul knows it very well" (v.14) is the self's inward assent to its own wonder; cf. Ps 119:73, Jer 1:5)*.

**IV. The fully-known self *invites the searching* (vv.23–24).**
"**Search me, O God, and know my heart** (H3824, M47)! **Try me and know my thoughts**! And **see if there be any grievous way in me**, and **lead me in the way everlasting**!" (vv.23–24). The gem-finding — the psalm's climactic turn: the self that *began* by marvelling it is searched and known (v.1) now **asks to be searched** — "search me… try me… see if there be any grievous way" *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's response to being fully known is **not to hide but to *open itself further*** — it welcomes, even *requests*, the divine examination, wanting its *own hidden faults exposed* for the sake of being *led rightly*; a self so secure in God's knowing-and-loving that it makes itself *voluntarily transparent*, inviting God to find and correct what the self cannot see in itself *(inferred: the movement from "you have searched me" (v.1, fact) to "search me" (v.23, invitation) is the whole psalm's arc — the self does not resent being known but *embraces* it, asking God to try it and expose any "grievous way"; transparency becomes *desirable* because the searcher is trusted and the aim is "the way everlasting"; the summit of trust — to want to be fully seen; cf. Ps 26:2 "prove me… try my heart", John 3:21)*.

## What Psalm 139 says about the inner being
- **The self is *exhaustively known from within* (vv.1–6).** Not behaviour only but *thoughts discerned from afar* — the interior wholly transparent to a knowing that precedes the self's own awareness; no unread thought, no hidden chamber.
- **The self *cannot flee God — and is never alone* (vv.7–12).** Nowhere (height, depth, darkness, far sea) is outside God's presence; the impossibility of hiding is also the guarantee of accompaniment — the self can never be lost, for God is *already there*, holding it.
- **The self is *formed and foreknown before birth* (vv.13–16).** God's intimate handiwork — knitted in the womb, *fearfully and wonderfully made*, its days written before one was lived; the inner being's existence is God's craft and foreknowledge, and praise is the fitting response.
- **The fully-known self *invites the searching* (vv.23–24).** The psalm's summit: from "you have searched me" to "*search* me" — the self opens itself further, *asking* God to try it and expose its hidden faults for the sake of being led rightly; the deepest trust is to *want* to be fully seen.

## Honest notes
- **A major cornerstone** — the Psalter's fullest anatomy of the inner being *coram Deo* (before God's face): known, accompanied, made, foreknown, and finally *self-offered to be searched*. The v.1→v.23 arc ("you have searched me" → "search me") is the key inner-being movement: being known, embraced rather than resented, turned into an *invitation*. Foregrounded as the study's prime datum on transparency-before-God.
- **Scope honesty — the imprecation:** vv.19–22 ("O that you would slay the wicked… I hate them with complete hatred") are the *zeal of the God-aligned self* against evil — read as 109/137's frame: fierce, honest, voiced to God; and note the psalm *immediately* turns that hatred back on *itself* in vv.23–24 ("search *me*… see if there be any grievous way in *me*"), submitting even its own zeal to God's examination. The finding is that self-submission, not the imprecation's content.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=David/LORD bleed pervasive; prohibition at vv.7–12; womb/darkness-imagery gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *heart* (H3824, M47, v.23); *thoughts* (vv.2,17,23); *searched/known* (M15/M41, vv.1,23); *soul* (H5315, M47, v.14); *praise* (M22, v.14, "fearfully and wonderfully made"). The omnipresence/womb-forming content is the arena in which the self is known and made.

## Psalm 140 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 140 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 140:1–13 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (2 vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The anchoring confession "You are my God"; the settled *knowing* that God vindicates the afflicted.** Psalm 140 is a lament for deliverance from violent men. Its inner-being findings: the self's **declaration of allegiance amid danger** — "You are my God" (v.6); and the **settled confidence that God will maintain the cause of the afflicted** (v.12).

## The reading

**I. The anchoring confession amid danger — "You are my God" (v.6).**
"I say to the LORD, **You are my God**; give ear to the voice of my **pleas for mercy**, O LORD!" (v.6). The gem-finding: encircled by violent men, the self makes a **declaration of belonging** — "You are my God" — before it even presses its plea *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being **anchors itself in an act of *allegiance*** — in danger it *names* whose it is ("you are my God"), and that confession is the ground from which it then asks for mercy; the self steadies itself by re-affirming its bond to God *(inferred: "I say to the LORD, You are my God… give ear" makes the confession of allegiance the *anchor* preceding the petition — the self locates its security in *belonging* to God before it asks anything; cf. Ps 31:14 "I trust in you… you are my God", 16:2)*.

**II. The settled *knowing* that God vindicates the afflicted (vv.12–13).**
"I **know** that the LORD will **maintain the cause of the afflicted** (H6041, M24), and will **execute justice for the needy**. Surely the **righteous shall give thanks**… the **upright shall dwell in your presence**" (vv.12–13). The gem-finding: the self declares a **settled *knowledge*** — "I know" — that God will uphold the afflicted's cause and give justice to the needy *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being rests on a **firm conviction about God's *character toward the oppressed*** — not a wish but a *known* certainty ("I know") that God takes up the afflicted's case; and it looks forward to *dwelling in God's presence*, the hope beyond the conflict *(inferred: "I know that the LORD will maintain the cause of the afflicted" is the self's *settled assurance* — the conviction that steadies it under assault is knowledge of God's bias toward the wronged; the confidence rests on God's nature, not the odds; cf. Ps 9:18, 12:5, 34:6)*.

## What Psalm 140 says about the inner being
- **The self *anchors in allegiance* amid danger (v.6).** Before pressing its plea, the inner being *names whose it is* — "You are my God" — steadying itself by re-affirming its bond; the confession of belonging is the ground of the petition.
- **The self rests on a *settled knowing* of God's justice (vv.12–13).** "I *know* the LORD will maintain the cause of the afflicted" — not a wish but a certainty about God's character toward the oppressed; the conviction that steadies the self under assault, with the hope of dwelling in God's presence beyond it.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** much of the psalm is the plea against evil/violent men and the imprecation on them (vv.1–5, 8–11 — the arena of the threat and the prayed judgment, cf. 109/137's frame). The inner-being weight is the anchoring confession (v.6) and the settled knowledge of God's justice (vv.12–13).
- **A trust datum:** "You are my God" (v.6) as the *self-steadying confession* (with 31:14, 16:2), and "I know" (v.12) as *conviction resting on God's character* — both anchor the self under assault.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=David/LORD bleed; prohibition/imprecation over-stamp at vv.8–11; violence-imagery gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *pleas-for-mercy* (M21, v.6); *afflicted/needy* (H6041, M24, v.12); *know* (M15, v.12); *righteous/upright* (M26/M13, v.13). The violent-men/imprecation terms are the arena.

## Psalm 141 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 141 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 141:1–10 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (1 v. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Praying God to guard the heart's *inclination*; the eyes fixed on God.** Psalm 141 is an evening prayer. Its inner-being findings: the plea for God to **guard both speech and the heart's *inclination toward evil*** (vv.3–4) — a self-suspicion joined to dependence; and the **eyes turned to God for refuge** (v.8).

## The reading

**I. Praying God to guard the heart's inclination (vv.3–4).**
"Set a **guard**, O LORD, over my **mouth**; keep watch over the door of my lips! **Do not let my heart** (H3820, M47) **incline to any evil**, to busy myself with wicked deeds… and let me **not eat of their delicacies**!" (vv.3–4). The gem-finding: the self asks God to guard not only its *speech* but the **inclination of its *heart*** — "do not let my heart incline to any evil" — and to keep it from the *appetite* for the wicked's "delicacies" *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being, **distrusting its own capacity to stay upright, asks God to *restrain its interior*** — it recognises that the heart can *incline / lean* toward evil and the appetite be drawn to forbidden pleasures, and so it seeks *divine* help to guard the very *bent* of the self; self-suspicion turned into a prayer for keeping *(inferred: "do not let my heart incline… let me not eat of their delicacies" is the self acknowledging its own *pull* toward evil and enlisting God to guard against it — the inner being does not trust itself to hold the line but asks God to keep its *heart* and *appetite*; a mature humility about the self's own reliability, cf. Ps 19:13 "keep back your servant from presumptuous sins", 119:36 "incline my heart… and not to selfish gain")*.

**II. The eyes turned to God for refuge (v.8).**
"But my **eyes are toward you**, O God, my Lord; in you I **seek refuge** (H2620, M19); leave me not **defenseless**!" (v.8). The finding: amid the snares of the wicked, the self keeps its **eyes fixed on God** and takes refuge in him *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being **directs its attention and dependence Godward** — "my eyes are toward you" enacts the turn from the surrounding threat to God as refuge; where the eyes go, the trust goes *(inferred: "my eyes are toward you… in you I seek refuge" re-attests the eye/refuge posture — the self's gaze deliberately held on God as its safety; cf. Ps 25:15, 123:1–2, 121:1)*.

## What Psalm 141 says about the inner being
- **The self asks God to *guard its heart's inclination* (vv.3–4).** Distrusting its own reliability, it prays God to restrain not only its speech but the *bent* of its heart toward evil and its appetite for forbidden pleasures — self-suspicion turned into a plea for keeping. A mature humility about the self's own capacity to stay upright.
- **The self *fixes its eyes on God for refuge* (v.8).** Amid snares, it directs its attention and dependence Godward — "my eyes are toward you"; where the gaze goes, the trust goes.

## Honest notes
- **A self-suspicion datum:** v.4's "do not let my heart incline to any evil" is a valuable inner-being finding — the self *knows its own pull* toward wrong and enlists God to guard its interior (with 19:13, 119:36). Not confidence in its own uprightness but dependence for keeping. Foregrounded.
- **Scope honesty:** the snares/traps of the wicked and the fate of evildoers (vv.5–7, 9–10) are the arena of the danger; the inner-being weight is the heart-guarding plea (vv.3–4) and the eyes-toward-God refuge (v.8). The "let my prayer be as incense" (v.2) is the liturgical frame.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=David/LORD bleed; prohibition over-stamp at vv.3–4 "do not let… let me not"; snare-imagery gate-2; backfilled v. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *heart* (H3820, M47, v.4); *take-refuge* (H2620, M19, v.8); *guard-mouth/lips* (M30, v.3). The snares/wicked terms are the arena.

## Psalm 142 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 142 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 142:1–7 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Pouring out the complaint; the fainting spirit still known; God as refuge and portion in abandonment.** Psalm 142 is David's prayer in the cave. Its inner-being findings: the self **pouring out its complaint before God** (v.2); the **fainting spirit that God still *knows*** (v.3); and, amid total abandonment, the declaration that **God is refuge and portion** (v.5).

## The reading

**I. Pouring out the complaint before God (v.2).**
"I **pour out my complaint** before him; I **tell my trouble** before him" (v.2). The gem-finding: the self *empties* its complaint and *tells* its trouble to God — full, unedited disclosure *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being **unburdens itself entirely before God** — "pour out" figures a *complete emptying* of what is inside, holding nothing back; the self brings its trouble to God not in tidy petition but as *outpoured complaint* *(inferred: "I pour out my complaint… I tell my trouble" is the honest, total unburdening — the inner being turned out before God like a vessel emptied; cf. Ps 62:8 "pour out your heart before him", 1 Sam 1:15 Hannah "pouring out my soul")*.

**II. The fainting spirit that God still knows (v.3).**
"When my **spirit** (H7307, M47) **faints** within me, **you know my way**!" (v.3). The gem-finding: even as the *spirit faints within*, the self affirms that **God knows its way** *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being at the point of *collapse* holds to **being *known* by God** — the fainting is real, but so is the confidence that God still *sees the path* the self cannot; being-known is the comfort *underneath* the fainting *(inferred: "when my spirit faints within me, you know my way" sets the self's inner collapse against God's undiminished knowledge — even fainting, the self is not lost to God, who knows the way through; the 139 datum (fully known) here as *comfort in extremity*; cf. Ps 143:4, 61:2 "when my heart is faint")*.

**III. God as refuge and portion in abandonment (vv.4–5).**
"Look to the right and see: there is **none who takes notice of me**; no refuge remains to me; **no one cares for my soul** (H5315, M47). I cry to you, O LORD; I say, '**You are my refuge** (H4268, M19), **my portion** in the land of the living'" (vv.4–5). The gem-finding: abandoned by all — "no one cares for my soul" — the self declares **God its *refuge* and its *portion*** *(stated)*. The operation: in total human abandonment the inner being **relocates its whole security and inheritance in *God alone*** — when no one takes notice and no refuge remains, the self names God as both its *shelter* (refuge) and its *allotted inheritance* (portion); the emptier the human field, the more entirely God becomes the self's all *(inferred: "no one cares for my soul… You are my refuge, my portion" makes the abandonment the very occasion for locating everything in God — refuge (safety) and portion (inheritance/possession) both found in him when all else fails; the portion-theme of 16:5, 73:26, here from the cave)*.

## What Psalm 142 says about the inner being
- **The self *pours out its complaint* before God (v.2).** A complete, unedited unburdening — the inner being emptied before God like a vessel, holding nothing back; trouble brought as outpoured complaint, not tidy petition.
- **The *fainting* spirit is still *known* (v.3).** At the point of collapse the self holds to being seen — "you know my way"; being-known by God is the comfort underneath the fainting, the path known even when the self cannot see it.
- **God is *refuge and portion* in total abandonment (vv.4–5).** When "no one cares for my soul," the inner being relocates its whole security *and* inheritance in God alone — the emptier the human field, the more entirely God becomes the self's all.

## Honest notes
- **A rich lament triad:** the *unburdening* (pour out, v.2), the *fainting-yet-known* spirit (v.3, linking to 139), and the *refuge-and-portion* found precisely in abandonment (v.5, linking to 16:5, 73:26). Prime inner-being data on how the self prays from the bottom.
- **Scope honesty:** the trap, the prison, the enemies (vv.3, 6–7) are the arena of the danger; the inner-being weight is the pouring-out (v.2), the fainting-but-known spirit (v.3), and the refuge/portion declaration (vv.4–5).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=David/LORD bleed; prohibition over-stamp at v.4 "none… no one"; trap/prison-imagery gate-2) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *spirit/faints* (H7307, M47, v.3); *soul* (H5315, M47, v.4); *refuge/portion* (H4268, M19, v.5); *complaint/trouble* (M03, v.2). The trap/prison terms are the arena.

## Psalm 143 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 143 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 143:1–12 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The fainting spirit that *deliberately remembers*; the thirsting soul lifted up to be taught.** Psalm 143 (the last penitential psalm) is a lament from the depths. Its inner-being findings: the self declining to plead its **own righteousness** (v.2); the **fainting, appalled spirit that *chooses to remember and meditate*** on God's works (vv.3–5); the **soul thirsting like a parched land** (v.6); and the self **lifting itself up to be taught and led** (vv.8, 10).

## The reading

**I. The self declines to plead its own righteousness (v.2).**
"**Enter not into judgment** with your servant, for **no one living is righteous** before you" (v.2). The finding: the self asks *not* to be judged on its merits, confessing that *no one living* is righteous before God *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being **renounces self-justification** — it does not come pleading its own uprightness but throws itself on mercy, owning that it could not stand under strict judgment *(inferred: "enter not into judgment… no one living is righteous before you" is the self *declining to claim righteousness* — the honest ground of appeal is mercy, not merit; cf. Ps 130:3, Rom 3:20)*.

**II. The fainting spirit that deliberately remembers (vv.3–5).**
"The enemy has… made me sit in darkness… Therefore my **spirit** (H7307, M47) **faints** within me; my **heart** (H3820, M47) within me is **appalled**. **I remember** (H2142, M41) the days of old; **I meditate** on all that you have done; **I ponder** the work of your hands" (vv.3–5). The gem-finding: with spirit *fainting* and heart *appalled*, the self makes a **deliberate turn to *remembering, meditating, pondering*** God's past works *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being in darkness **actively rehearses God's deeds as the *way through* despair** — it does not wait for the faintness to lift but *chooses* to remember, meditate, ponder; recollection of what God has done is the *counter-move* to the appalled heart *(inferred: the pivot "*therefore* my spirit faints… *I remember… I meditate… I ponder*" makes memory a *deliberate discipline against despair* — the self steadies itself by rehearsing God's works when its own spirit is failing; the willed remembering of 77:11, the counter to 143:4's faintness; cf. Ps 42:6)*.

**III. The soul thirsting like a parched land (v.6).**
"I **stretch out my hands** to you; my **soul** (H5315, M47) **thirsts** for you like a **parched land**" (v.6). The gem-finding: the soul's longing for God is a *thirst* — dry ground craving rain *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being **aches for God with the intensity of *drought*** — the parched-land image makes the desire a matter of *survival*, the soul cracked and dry, reaching (hands stretched) for the only water *(inferred: "my soul thirsts for you like a parched land" figures the longing as *life-and-death thirst* — the self desperate for God as dry ground for rain; cf. Ps 42:1–2, 63:1 "my soul thirsts for you… in a dry and weary land")*.

**IV. Lifting up the soul to be taught and led (vv.8, 10).**
"Let me hear in the morning of your steadfast love, for in you I **trust** (H0982, M19). Make me **know the way** I should go, for **to you I lift up my soul**… **Teach me** to do your will, for you are my God! Let your good Spirit **lead me** on level ground!" (vv.8, 10). The gem-finding: the self **lifts up its soul** to God, *trusting*, and asks to be **taught and led** *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being **offers itself up to God for *direction*** — "to you I lift up my soul" is a self-*presenting*, and the petitions ("make me know the way… teach me… lead me") ask God to *guide the self's steps and will*; the soul raised toward God is a soul asking to be *taught* *(inferred: "to you I lift up my soul… teach me to do your will… lead me" makes the lifted soul an act of *submission-for-guidance* — the self hands itself over to be directed, not just delivered; the desire is to be *taught God's will*, cf. Ps 25:1,4–5, 25:4 "make me know your ways")*.

## What Psalm 143 says about the inner being
- **The self *declines to plead its own righteousness* (v.2).** It throws itself on mercy, owning that no one living could stand under strict judgment — self-justification renounced.
- **The fainting spirit *deliberately remembers* (vv.3–5).** In darkness the self chooses to remember, meditate, and ponder God's past works — recollection as a willed discipline against despair, the counter-move to the appalled heart.
- **The soul *thirsts like a parched land* (v.6).** Longing for God as a matter of survival — dry, cracked ground reaching for the only water; desire at the intensity of drought.
- **The self *lifts itself up to be taught and led* (vv.8, 10).** "To you I lift up my soul… teach me to do your will… lead me" — a self-presenting for *direction*, handing itself over to be guided, not merely delivered.

## Honest notes
- **A rich lament-anatomy:** mercy-not-merit (v.2), *deliberate remembering* against despair (v.5, prime datum), *thirst* for God (v.6), and the *lifted-up soul asking to be taught* (vv.8, 10). Strong inner-being data on praying from the depths — the memory-as-discipline (v.5) especially valuable (with 77:11, 42:6).
- **Scope honesty:** the enemy's pursuit and the prayed judgment on foes (vv.3, 11–12) are the arena of the distress; the inner-being weight is the confession (v.2), the remembering (vv.3–5), the thirst (v.6), and the taught/led self (vv.8, 10).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=David/LORD bleed; prohibition at v.2 "enter not"; darkness/enemy-imagery gate-2) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *spirit/faints* (H7307, M47, v.4); *heart/appalled* (H3820, M47, v.4); *remember/meditate/ponder* (H2142, M41, v.5); *soul/thirsts* (H5315, M47, vv.6,8); *trust* (H0982, M19, v.8). The enemy/judgment terms are the arena.

## Psalm 144 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 144 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 144:1–15 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (5 vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The wonder that God *regards* transient man.** Psalm 144 is a royal battle-and-blessing psalm (the arena of warfare, deliverance, prosperity). Its one inner-being touch-point is the self's **astonished humility that God takes notice of frail, fleeting man** (vv.3–4).

## The reading

**I. The wonder that God regards transient man (vv.3–4).**
"O LORD, **what is man that you regard him**, or the son of man that you **think of him**? Man is like a **breath**; his days are like a **passing shadow**" (vv.3–4). The gem-finding: the self marvels that God should *regard* and *think of* man — and in the same breath owns man's *transience* ("like a breath… a passing shadow") *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being holds together **its own *smallness/fleetingness* and God's astonishing *attention*** — the self sees itself as breath and shadow, *and* is amazed that such a creature is *noticed* by God; humility (I am nothing lasting) and wonder (yet you think of me) fused *(inferred: "what is man that you regard him… man is like a breath" fuses the self's honest sense of its own transience with astonishment at being *regarded* — the same wonder as Ps 8:4; the inner being humbled by its brevity yet lifted by God's notice; cf. Ps 39:5, Job 7:17)*.

## What Psalm 144 says about the inner being
- **The self holds together its own *transience* and God's *astonishing regard* (vv.3–4).** Seeing itself as breath and passing shadow, the inner being is amazed that God *notices* it at all — humility (I am nothing lasting) and wonder (yet you think of me) fused in one recognition.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** the bulk of the psalm (vv.1–2, 5–11 — God trains the hands for war, the plea for rescue from foreign foes; vv.12–15 — the prayer for flourishing children, full barns, peace) is the *royal/battle/prosperity arena*, not inner-being operation. The inner-being weight is only the wonder-at-regard of vv.3–4 (a re-attestation of the 8:4 datum).
- **A transience-and-regard datum:** the fused humility-and-wonder (with Ps 8:4, 39:5) — the self small and fleeting, yet astonished to be noticed by God.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=David/LORD bleed; war/prosperity-imagery gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** the *what-is-man / breath / shadow* of vv.3–4 (the sole inner-being datum, read from the wonder-and-transience). The war/rock/deliverance/prosperity terms are the arena.

## Psalm 145 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 145 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 145:1–21 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (1 v. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Continual praise and meditation; the *desire* of every living thing satisfied; calling *in truth*.** Psalm 145 is the great acrostic hymn (the last psalm ascribed to David). Its inner-being findings: the **resolve of daily praise and meditation** (vv.1–2, 5); the **desire of every creature satisfied by God's open hand** (vv.15–16, 19); and nearness to those who **call in truth** (v.18).

## The reading

**I. The resolve of daily praise and meditation (vv.1–2, 5).**
"I will **extol** you, my God and King… **every day I will bless you**… On the glorious splendor of your majesty, and on your wondrous works, **I will meditate**" (vv.1–2, 5). The finding: the self commits to **continual praise** — *every day* — and to **meditating** on God's majesty and works *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being **sustains a settled habit of blessing and pondering God** — praise not as an occasional burst but a *daily resolve*, and meditation as the mind's dwelling on God's splendour *(inferred: "every day I will bless you… I will meditate" makes praise a *durable practice* and meditation the deliberate turning of the mind onto God's works; the self orders its days around blessing God, cf. Ps 34:1, 71:8)*.

**II. The *desire* of every living thing satisfied by God's open hand (vv.15–16, 19).**
"The **eyes of all look to you**, and you give them their food in due season. You **open your hand**; you **satisfy the desire** (H7522) of **every living thing**… He **fulfills the desire** of those who **fear** (H3373, M01) him; he also **hears their cry** and saves them" (vv.15–16, 19). The gem-finding: God **satisfies the *desire* of every creature** and **fulfills the desire of those who fear him** *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's ***desire* finds its answer in God** — the longing that runs through every living thing (and, more, through the God-fearer) is *met* at God's open hand; the self's appetite is not left gnawing but *satisfied* by the One to whom "the eyes of all look" *(inferred: "you open your hand, you satisfy the desire of every living thing… he fulfills the desire of those who fear him" makes God the *satisfier of longing* — the inner being's desire, when directed to God (the God-fearer's, v.19), is *fulfilled*; the appetite that Ps 107:9, 103:5, 63:5 track finds here its universal resolution — God as the answer to desire itself; and "the eyes of all look to you" (v.15) re-attests the dependent gaze)*.

**III. Calling *in truth* (v.18).**
"The LORD is **near to all who call on him**, to all who **call on him in truth**" (v.18). The finding: God's nearness is to those who call *in truth* — sincerely *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's ***sincerity* conditions the nearness** — not the mere form of calling but calling "in truth" (genuinely, without pretence) is what God draws near to; the honesty of the calling heart matters *(inferred: "near to all who call on him in truth" makes the *genuineness* of the appeal the thing — the self that calls without pretence finds God near; cf. Ps 51:6 "you delight in truth in the inward being", John 4:24)*.

## What Psalm 145 says about the inner being
- **Praise and meditation are a *daily resolve* (vv.1–2, 5).** The self orders its days around blessing God and pondering his works — praise as durable practice, not occasional burst; the mind deliberately dwelling on God's splendour.
- **The self's *desire* is *satisfied* by God (vv.15–16, 19).** The longing that runs through every living thing, and especially the God-fearer's, is *met* at God's open hand — the inner being's appetite not left gnawing but *fulfilled*; God as the answer to desire itself.
- **Nearness is to those who *call in truth* (v.18).** The *sincerity* of the appeal conditions the nearness — the honest, unpretending calling heart is what God draws near to.

## Honest notes
- **A desire-resolution datum:** v.16/19's "satisfy/fulfill the desire" is the Psalter's most universal statement that *God satisfies longing* — the resolution of the appetite-thread running through 107:9, 103:5, 63:5, 42:1. Foregrounded as a key inner-being finding (the desire *directed to God* is the desire *met*).
- **Scope honesty:** most of the psalm describes *God's* greatness, goodness, kingdom, and compassion (vv.3–4, 6–14, 17, 20 — the arena of praise-content). The inner-being weight is the self's daily-praise resolve (vv.1–2, 5), the satisfied desire (vv.15–16, 19), and calling-in-truth (v.18).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=David/LORD bleed pervasive; God's-attribute terms gate-1 but arena; backfilled v. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *extol/bless/meditate* (M22, vv.1–2,5); *desire-satisfied* (H7522, vv.16,19); *fear* (H3373, M01, v.19); *call-in-truth* (M37 + truth, v.18). The extensive God-attribute terms (gracious, merciful, righteous, etc.) are the praise arena.

## Psalm 146 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 146 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 146:1–10 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Trust redirected from mortal man to the enduring God. The final Hallel opens.** Psalm 146 begins the five closing praise-psalms. Its inner-being finding: the **deliberate redirection of trust/hope — away from mortal princes (whose plans perish) to the God whose help endures** (vv.3–5).

## The reading

**I. Trust redirected from mortal man to the enduring God (vv.3–5).**
"**Put not your trust in princes**, in a son of man, in whom there is **no salvation**. When his **breath departs**, he returns to the earth; on that very day his **plans perish**. **Blessed is he whose help is the God of Jacob, whose hope is in the LORD** his God" (vv.3–5). The gem-finding: the self is directed **not to trust mortal man** — because he *dies* and his plans *perish with him* — but to place its **hope in the LORD** *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being **redirects its trust by *reasoning from mortality*** — it *weighs* where to lean, sees that the strongest human helper is *breath that departs*, and so *relocates* its hope in the God who endures; trust as a *reasoned choice* informed by the transience of every human refuge *(inferred: "put not your trust in princes… his plans perish… blessed is he whose hope is in the LORD" is the self *choosing* its ground by reckoning that man is mortal and God is not — the deliberate redirection of 118:8–9, here argued from death; misplaced trust exposed by the grave, right trust anchored in the enduring God; cf. Ps 118:8, 62:9, 115:9–11)*.

## What Psalm 146 says about the inner being
- **Trust is *redirected by reasoning from mortality* (vv.3–5).** The self weighs where to lean, sees that even princes are "breath that departs" whose plans perish, and *relocates* its hope in the enduring God — trust as a reasoned choice informed by the transience of every human refuge.

## Honest notes
- **A trust-redirection datum** (re-attesting and deepening 118:8–9): here the choice is *argued from death* — the mortality of the human helper is the reason to place hope elsewhere (with 62:9, 115:9–11). Foregrounded.
- **Scope honesty:** the bulk of the psalm (vv.6–10 — God who made heaven/earth, keeps faith, executes justice, feeds the hungry, frees prisoners, opens blind eyes, lifts the bowed-down, loves the righteous, reigns forever) is *God's character and action* (the arena that *grounds* the redirected hope). The inner-being weight is the trust-choice of vv.3–5. v.8's "lifts up those who are bowed down" is God's action, its inner-being fruit relief.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed; prohibition at v.3 "put not"; God's-works terms gate-1 but arena) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *trust* (H0982, M19, v.3); *hope* (H7664, M18, v.5); *praise* (M22, vv.1–2). The God's-works terms (vv.6–10) are the arena grounding the hope.

## Psalm 147 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 147 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 147:1–20 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (5 vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The brokenhearted healed; God's pleasure in the *fearing, hoping* heart, not in strength.** Psalm 147 is a praise-psalm on God's care and power. Its inner-being findings: the **brokenhearted *healed* and their wounds bound** (v.3); and the searching datum that **God's pleasure is in the *fearing, hoping* heart — not in human strength** (vv.10–11).

## The reading

**I. The brokenhearted healed (v.3).**
"He **heals the brokenhearted** (H3820, M47) and **binds up their wounds**" (v.3). The gem-finding: God's care reaches the *broken heart* — he *heals* it and *binds up* its wounds *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's ***wounds are tended*** — the broken heart is not left to bleed but *bound up*, the healing directed precisely at the *inner* injury; God as physician of the wounded self *(inferred: "he heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds" makes the *inner* wound the object of God's tender repair — the shattered heart mended, the hurt bound like a physician dressing a wound; God's nearness to the broken, cf. Ps 34:18, 51:17, Isa 61:1)*.

**II. God's pleasure in the *fearing, hoping* heart, not in strength (vv.10–11).**
"His **delight is not in the strength of the horse**, nor his pleasure in the legs of a man, but the LORD **takes pleasure in those who fear** (H3373, M01) him, in those who **hope** (H3176, M18) in his steadfast love" (vv.10–11). The gem-finding: what *pleases* God is **not power** (horse, man's legs) but the heart that **fears him and hopes in his steadfast love** *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being learns that **its *reverent fear and hope*, not its strength, are what *delight* God** — the self's value before God lies not in might or capability but in the *inward* posture of fear-and-hope; the fearing, hoping heart is the thing God *takes pleasure in* *(inferred: "his delight is not in the strength of the horse… but in those who fear him, who hope in his steadfast love" contrasts *external power* with the *inner posture* and locates God's pleasure entirely in the latter — the inner being's worth is its fear and hope, not its force; a searching datum on what God actually values in the self, cf. Ps 33:16–18, 1 Sam 16:7, Mic 6:8)*.

## What Psalm 147 says about the inner being
- **The *brokenhearted* are *healed* (v.3).** God's care reaches the inner wound — the shattered heart mended, its hurt bound up like a physician dressing a wound; the broken self not left to bleed.
- **God's pleasure is in the *fearing, hoping* heart, not in strength (vv.10–11).** What delights God is not power (horse, man's legs) but the inward posture of reverent fear and hope in his steadfast love — the inner being's worth lies in its fear and hope, not its force.

## Honest notes
- **A what-God-values datum:** vv.10–11 is a searching inner-being finding — God's pleasure located entirely in the *inner* posture (fear + hope), explicitly *over against* external strength (with 33:16–18, 1 Sam 16:7). The self's value is its fearing-hoping heart. Foregrounded, alongside the healed brokenhearted (v.3).
- **Scope honesty:** most of the psalm (vv.2, 4–9, 12–20 — God builds Jerusalem, counts the stars, covers the heavens with clouds, gives snow and frost, sends his word) is *God's power and providence* (the arena). The inner-being weight is v.3 and vv.10–11.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed pervasive; prohibition at v.10 "not in"; weather/creation-imagery gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *brokenhearted* (H3820, M47, v.3); *fear* (H3373, M01, v.11); *hope* (H3176, M18, v.11); *pleasant* (v.1). The building/stars/weather terms are the providence arena.

## Psalm 148 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 148 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 148:1–14 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (2 vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Scope honesty up front:** Psalm 148 is the great cosmic doxology — every order of creation (angels, sun, moon, stars, sea creatures, weather, mountains, trees, beasts, kings, peoples, young and old) summoned to praise the LORD. It is a *universal call to praise* (the arena of worship). It yields **no distinct inner-being finding**; recorded honestly as an arena-only summons.

## The reading

**I. The universal summons to praise (throughout).**
"Praise the LORD from the heavens… Praise him, sun and moon… Praise the LORD from the earth… kings of the earth and all peoples… Young men and maidens together, old men and children! Let them praise the name of the LORD" (vv.1–13). The finding (arena): all creation, human and non-human, is called to praise — the human "young and old" taking their place in the cosmic chorus *(stated)*. There is no observed inner-being *operation* — the psalm *commands* praise across the whole created order; the only human-relevant note is that the self joins the *entire creation* in worship, one voice among all *(inferred, cautious: to read an inner-being process into a universal doxology would be to import; the transferable hint is only that the inner being's praise is *part of a cosmic whole* — the self takes its place in creation's chorus, not a self-movement the text describes)*.

## What Psalm 148 says about the inner being
- **(Arena-only) No distinct inner-being finding.** The psalm summons all creation — including "young and old" — to praise; the only human-relevant note is that the self's worship joins the *whole created order's*, one voice among all. Not an inner-being operation the text describes.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** an arena-only cosmic doxology (with Ps 117, 114, 134, 150) — I record no inner-being finding rather than manufacture one from a universal call to praise. The self's place *within* creation's chorus is noted, no more.
- **v.14 "the people… who are near to him"** is a positional/covenant note (nearness to God), not a described inner-being operation.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed pervasive; creation-catalogue gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** the terms are the creation-catalogue and praise-summons (arena); no human inner-being operation observed.

## Psalm 149 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 149 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 149:1–9 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (2 vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Joy in God that overflows to the private hours; the humble adorned.** Psalm 149 is a praise-psalm of the godly. Its inner-being findings: **gladness in God that exults even *on the bed*** (vv.2, 5); and God's **pleasure in his people, *adorning the humble*** with salvation (v.4).

## The reading

**I. Joy in God overflowing to the private hours (vv.2, 5).**
"Let Israel be **glad** (H8055, M04) in his **Maker**; let the children of Zion **rejoice** in their King!… Let the godly **exult** in glory; let them **sing for joy on their beds**" (vv.2, 5). The gem-finding: the joy in God is so full it **sings even *on their beds*** — in the private, resting, night hours *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's gladness in God **overflows past public worship into the *intimate and hidden*** — "on their beds" locates the joy where no one sees, at rest, in the night; a delight that does not need an audience but sings in solitude *(inferred: "let them sing for joy on their beds" carries the joy into the private place — the self so glad in its Maker that it exults even lying down, alone; the gladness has soaked through to the intimate hours, cf. Ps 42:8 "at night his song is with me", 63:6 "on my bed")*.

**II. God's pleasure in his people; the humble adorned (v.4).**
"For the LORD **takes pleasure in his people**; he **adorns the humble** (H6035, M24) with **salvation**" (v.4). The gem-finding: God *delights* in his people and **beautifies the humble** with salvation *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's ***humility* is what God *adorns*** — the lowly self is not despised but *decorated / crowned* with salvation; God's pleasure rests on his people, and his beautifying grace falls on *humility* *(inferred: "he adorns the humble with salvation" makes the humble inner being the object of God's *beautifying* — the self that is lowly is clothed with the ornament of salvation; humility is the condition God delights to dignify, cf. Ps 147:11, 138:6, 1 Pet 5:5 "God… gives grace to the humble")*.

## What Psalm 149 says about the inner being
- **Joy in God *overflows to the private hours* (vv.2, 5).** So full is the gladness in its Maker that the self sings "on their beds" — the joy soaked through past public worship into the intimate, resting, night hours; delight that needs no audience.
- **God *adorns the humble* (v.4).** The lowly self is not despised but *beautified* — clothed with salvation; humility is the condition God delights to dignify, his pleasure resting on his people.

## Honest notes
- **A private-joy datum:** "sing for joy on their beds" (v.5) — gladness that reaches the solitary, unwitnessed hours (with 42:8, 63:6); the joy is real enough to sing where no one sees. And the humble *adorned* (v.4) joins the humility-thread (147:11, 138:6).
- **Scope honesty:** the militant close (vv.6–9 — the two-edged sword, executing judgment on the nations) is the arena of vindication/judgment, not an inner-being operation; noted, not developed. The inner-being weight is the overflowing joy (vv.2, 5) and the adorned humble (v.4).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD/Israel bleed; sword/judgment-imagery gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *glad/rejoice/exult* (H8055, M04, vv.2,5); *humble* (H6035, M24, v.4). The sword/judgment terms (vv.6–9) are the arena.

## Psalm 150 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 150 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 150:1–6 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Scope honesty up front:** Psalm 150 is the Psalter's closing doxology — a tenfold "Praise him" summoning every instrument and "everything that has breath" to praise. It is *pure worship-summons* (the arena). It yields **no distinct inner-being finding**; but as the **capstone of the whole Psalter**, it carries a structural note worth recording (below).

## The reading

**I. The final summons — everything that has breath (vv.1–6).**
"Praise the LORD! Praise God in his sanctuary… Praise him for his **mighty deeds**… **Let everything that has breath praise the LORD!**" (vv.1–6). The finding (arena): the Psalter ends in *unqualified praise* — every instrument, every breathing creature called to worship *(stated)*. There is no observed inner-being *operation*; the psalm is doxology *(inferred, cautious: to read a self-movement into a six-verse summons would be to import)*. **The one honest structural note:** the entire Psalter — which has traversed *every* state of the inner being (fear, grief, guilt, longing, waiting, trust, doubt, rage, joy) across 150 psalms — resolves here into *sheer praise*; the inner being's long journey through its whole range *arrives* at "let everything that has breath praise the LORD." That *terminus* is the datum: praise is where the whole inner life is bound, at last, to land *(inferred, structural: the Psalter's editors close the book on praise after every darker note has been sounded — the movement of the whole collection is *toward* praise; the inner being's varied journey has this as its endpoint, cf. the Psalter's five-book doxological seams, 41:13, 72:19, 89:52, 106:48)*.

## What Psalm 150 says about the inner being
- **(Arena-only, with a structural note) No distinct inner-being finding.** The psalm is pure praise-summons. But as the Psalter's capstone it marks the *terminus* of the inner being's whole journey: after every state — fear, grief, guilt, longing, waiting, trust, rage, joy — the collection resolves into unqualified praise. Praise is where the whole inner life is, at last, bound to land.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** an arena-only doxology (with Ps 148, 117, 134) — I record no inner-being *operation* rather than manufacture one from a summons. The *structural* observation (the Psalter arriving at praise after traversing the full inner-being range) is offered as a reading of the collection's shape, not as a datum extracted from these six verses alone.
- **A fitting close to the chapter-run:** the inner-being journey this project has traced through all 150 psalms — the fearing, grieving, trusting, longing, waiting, rejoicing self — ends where the Psalter ends: in praise. Noted for the eventual cross-chapter synthesis.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed; instrument-catalogue gate-2) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** the terms are the praise-summons and instrument-catalogue (arena); no human inner-being operation observed — only the structural terminus-of-the-Psalter note.

## Psalm 1 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 1 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 1:1–6 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Lexicals only; cited; grounded in the verses. Every inference tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens (re-framed 2026-07-03):** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`). *Part B of the re-alignment sweep — process-lens re-frame + Lens bullet added; findings unchanged (this reading was already operation-focused).*
- **The chapter is multi-characteristic** (as expected for a poem): it works by **two ways** set in antithesis, and reads the inner being from several perspectives at once — **desire, cognition, moral condition, rootedness, and destiny**.

## The reading
Psalm 1 does not describe a deed so much as an **orientation of the inner being** — which way the whole person is turned — and it contrasts two.

**I. The blessed man — a desire that becomes meditation (vv.1–2).**
The blessed man is first defined by a **refusal**: he does *not* walk in the counsel of the wicked, nor stand in the way of sinners, nor sit in the seat of scoffers (v.1). The three verbs *walk → stand → sit*, paired with *counsel → way → seat*, read as a **deepening of association** *(inferred from the progression)* — from taking advice, to taking the road, to taking a seat among mockers. What he refuses is a settling-in with evil. Positively, his inner life is a **desire**: his *delight* (H2656, characteristic — M04) is in the law of the LORD (v.2). *Delight* is affection, not duty *(stated: the term is pleasure/delight)* — the law is what he *wants*. And that desire does not stay still: it becomes **meditation** (H1897, characteristic — M42), a low continual muttering *day and night* (v.2). So the inner sequence is **desire → rumination**: what the inner being loves, it dwells on *(inferred)*.

**II. The impact — rootedness, fruit, permanence (v.3).**
The effect of that inner orientation is given as a simile: he is *like a tree planted by streams of water.* Its lexical operations — it **yields** its fruit in season, its leaf does **not wither**, and *in all he does he prospers* — read as the **stability and fruitfulness** the delighting-meditating inner life produces *(inferred: the tree is the vehicle; the tenor is the man of vv.1–2)*. The inner being that is rooted in what it loves does not run dry; it bears in season and endures out of season.

**III. The other way — the wicked, rootless and driven (vv.4–5).**
*Not so the wicked* (v.4). Where the righteous is planted, the wicked (H7563, characteristic — M10) is *like chaff that the wind drives away* — the exact negation of rootedness: no soil, no water, no permanence, carried off by a breath *(stated: chaff/wind/drives)*. The consequence is inability to **stand**: the wicked will not stand in the judgment, nor sinners (H2400, characteristic — M10) in the congregation of the righteous (v.5). The inner condition that took its seat among scoffers has no standing when it counts *(inferred: the v.1 progression closes here)*.

**IV. The two destinies — knowing and perishing (v.6).**
The psalm resolves the two ways into two ends held by the LORD: he *knows* the way of the righteous (H6662, characteristic — M26), but the way of the wicked will *perish* (v.6). The righteous's way is **relationally known** — held, acknowledged *(stated: "the LORD knows")*; the wicked's way simply ends.

## What Psalm 1 says about the inner being
- The inner being is fundamentally **oriented** — turned one of two ways — and the psalm reads that orientation from several angles at once: **desire** (delight), **cognition** (meditation), **moral condition** (righteous / wicked–sinner–scoffer), **rootedness** (planted tree vs driven chaff), and **destiny** (endure/known vs perish).
- The generative core is **desire that becomes meditation**: the blessed inner life *loves* the law and therefore *dwells* on it continually — and that inner orientation, not any single act, is what roots the person into stability and fruitfulness.
- The wicked is drawn as the **privation** of this: not a rival root but *no* root — rootless, transient, unable to stand.
- **Blessedness** is thus presented as an inner state (a rooted, God-delighting, meditating orientation), not a reward for deeds.

## Honest notes
- **Characteristics** the chapter surfaces (sanity-checked roles): *delight* (M04), *meditation* (M42) — the righteous inner life; *wicked / sinners* (M10) and *righteous* (M26) — the two moral poles; the tree-simile operations *yields / does-not-wither* carried as the **fruitfulness/stability** expression of the righteous (kept as characteristic; read as the simile's tenor).
- **counsel** (v.1) and **judgment** (v.5) were sanity-checked to **process-qualifier** (they function adverbially — the *sphere* of the wrong walk, the *scene* of non-standing — not inner dispositions).
- **bearer** is unreliable across vv.2 and 6 (the nearest-proper heuristic attaches "LORD" to spans it does not govern) — flagged in D11; this reading does not lean on bearer (e.g. it is the *man*, not the LORD, who meditates in v.2).
- Residual mechanical noise (prohibition over-firing, manner/coupling over-welding) does not touch the reading's spine.

## Psalm 2 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 2 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 2:1–12 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). **Complete chapter** — verses 3–4 were absent from the corpus and were **backfilled** (measure-layer ingest) before this reading. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens (re-framed 2026-07-03):** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`). §II (the LORD's derision/wrath) is the *arena* — the drama's counter-voice — not itself a human inner-being finding; the findings are the human movements (defiant desire, glad awe, sheltering refuge). *Part B re-alignment sweep; findings unchanged.*
- **Multi-characteristic**, and structured as a **four-voice drama** — the nations, the LORD, the Anointed, and the psalmist's closing counsel — each disclosing a different movement of the inner being: **defiant desire, holy wrath, derision, and the fear/refuge that is the only safety.**

## The reading
Psalm 2 stages the inner being through **who speaks**, and reads it as a collision between human self-will and divine sovereignty.

**I. The nations — defiant desire that schemes (vv.1–3).**
The peoples **rage** and **plot** (H1897, characteristic — M42) "in vain" (v.1) — an inner scheming, the same lexical operation that is godly *meditation* in Psa 1:2, here turned to **conspiracy** *(inferred: valence from context; the operation is identical, the object opposite)*. The kings **set themselves** and take **counsel together** against the LORD and his Anointed (v.2). Their inner posture is then spoken aloud (v.3, backfilled): "let us **burst** their bonds and **cast** away their cords" — the desire underneath the plotting is **the throwing-off of restraint** *(stated: burst/cast the bonds/cords)*. The inner being here is **autonomy as appetite** — rule experienced as bondage, freedom imagined as revolt.

**II. The LORD — derision, then holy wrath (vv.4–6).**
The answer is first **laughter**: the One enthroned in the heavens **laughs**, holds them in **derision** (v.4, backfilled) — the rebellion is not met with alarm but with **contempt for its futility** *(inferred: derision as the measure of the threat)*. Then the mood turns: he will **speak** to them in his wrath and **terrify** them (H0926, characteristic — M01) in his **fury** (H2740, qualifier — M02) (v.5) — dread deliberately induced. And he asserts the settled fact they revolted against: "I have **set** my King on Zion, my **holy** hill" (v.6). *(holy here qualifies the place, not a human inner state — sanity-checked to standalone.)*

**III. The Anointed — sonship and the asking (vv.7–9).**
The King recites the **decree**: "You are my Son; today I have begotten you" (v.7) — an identity **received, not seized** *(inferred, against the nations' seizing)*. And the mode of his rule is **petition**: "**Ask** of me (H7592, characteristic — M21), and I will make the nations your heritage" (v.8) — dominion comes by **asking the Father**, the exact inverse of the kings who take counsel to grasp it. The rule itself is unbreakable (v.9, the iron rod).

**IV. The counsel — be wise; serve with fear; take refuge (vv.10–12).**
The psalmist turns to the rebels with an inner-being summons: "be **wise** (H7919, characteristic — M15), be warned" (v.10) *(rulers/judges here = a vocative address, sanity-checked to standalone).* The prescribed inner posture is **Serve the LORD** (H5647, characteristic — M36) **with fear** (H3374, qualifier — M01), and **rejoice** (H1523, characteristic — M04) **with trembling** (H7461, qualifier — M01) (v.11) — a striking weld: joy and dread held together, worship that is glad *and* awed. The alternative is his **anger** (H0599, characteristic — M02) kindled (v.12). The psalm closes where Psalm 1 began: "**Blessed** are all who **take refuge** (H2620, characteristic — M19) in him" — the inner being's only safety is **sheltering trust**, the opposite of the opening revolt.

## What Psalm 2 says about the inner being
- The chapter reads the inner being as a **contest of wills**, disclosed through four voices: **defiant desire** (the nations — autonomy felt as the throwing-off of restraint), **holy wrath and derision** (the LORD — the rebellion is contemptible, then dreadful), **received sonship that asks rather than seizes** (the Anointed), and the counselled posture of **fear-filled worship and sheltering refuge** (the close).
- Its sharpest disclosure is the **weld of opposites** in v.11: *serve with fear*, *rejoice with trembling* — the right inner orientation to God is **glad awe**, joy and dread inseparable.
- **Refuge/trust** (v.12) is named as the inner being's safety — and it stands as the exact inverse of the opening **revolt** (v.3): the whole psalm moves from "burst his bonds" to "take refuge in him."
- The **same operation carries opposite value by context**: *hagah* is *meditation* (Psa 1:2) and *plotting* (Psa 2:1) — the inner being's activity is morally weighted by its object, not its mechanism.

## Honest notes
- **Corpus completeness:** vv.3–4 were **backfilled** (they held no study term, so were absent) — without them the psalm would have lost the rebels' cry *and* the divine derision, its two hinges. Both are gate-2 content (no IB-cluster term tags them), read here as operations.
- **Characteristics** (sanity-checked): *plot* (M42), *terrify* (M01), *ask* (M21), *wise* (M15), *serve* (M36), *rejoice* (M04), *angry* (M02), *take-refuge* (M19); qualifiers *fury/fear/trembling* (M02/M01).
- **Reclassified** by sanity-check: *holy* (v.6, attribute of a place → standalone), *rulers/judges* (v.10, vocative address → standalone).
- **bearer** unreliable in vv.4,7,11 (nearest-proper "LORD" bleed) — flagged D11; the reading does not lean on it (the bearers of *serve/rejoice* are the kings, not the LORD).

---
