## Psalm 18 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 18 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 18:1–50 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (10 verses backfilled). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **The great deliverance psalm** (50 verses) — read here by **movement**, not verse-by-verse, tracing the inner being's arc from *love* through *rescue* to the psalm's deepest disclosure: **God is met according to the disposition one brings him.**
- **Lens (re-framed 2026-07-03):** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`). *Part B re-alignment sweep — Lens bullet added for consistency; this reading was already operation-focused (verified header-by-header). Findings unchanged.*

## The reading

**I. "I love you, O LORD" — the affectionate opening (vv.1–3).**
The psalm opens with the rarest note in the Psalter: "I **love** (H7355, M05 — *racham*) you, O LORD, my **strength** (H2391, M23)." The verb is one usually spoken *by* God (tender, womb-deep affection); here it is spoken by a person *to* God *(inferred: the direction of the verb is what makes it startling)*. And God is named in a cascade of shelter-words — rock, fortress, deliverer, shield, horn, stronghold (v.2). The inner being's first movement is not petition but **love**, and love that leans its whole weight on God *(stated)*.

**II. Distress, and the cry that is heard (vv.4–6).**
Then the depth from which it was rescued: "the **cords** of death encompassed me… the torrents of destruction assailed me" (vv.4–5). "In my distress I **called** (H7121, M37); to my God I cried for help. From his temple he **heard** (H8085, M41) my voice" (v.6). The inner being at the edge of death does one thing — *cry* — and is **heard** *(stated)*.

**III. The theophany — heaven convulses for one man (vv.7–15).**
What follows is disproportion: at that single cry, "the earth reeled and **trembled** (H7264, M01)… smoke went up from his nostrils… he bowed the heavens and came down" in fire, thunder, and thick darkness (vv.7–15). The astonishing inner-being note is the **scale of God's response to one person's distress** — the whole cosmos is moved to rescue a drowning man *(inferred: the storm is the measure of God's regard, not of the enemy)*.

**IV. Reached down, drawn out — because he delighted (vv.16–19).**
The rescue itself is a *stooping*: "he **reached down from on high**, he took me; he **drew me out of many waters**" (v.16). The inner being is saved not by climbing but by being **grasped** from above. "He brought me out into a **broad place**; he rescued me, **because he delighted in me**" (v.19). Two gems: deliverance is **spaciousness after constriction** — from the narrow grip of death into a *broad place* — and its ground is God's **delight**: he saves the one he *takes pleasure in* *(stated: because he delighted in me)*.

**V. The mirror — God met according to the inner posture (vv.20–27).**
Here is the psalm's deepest disclosure. After grounding vindication in kept integrity — "I have **kept** (H8104) the ways of the LORD… I was **blameless** (H8549) before him, and I kept myself from **guilt**" (vv.21–23) — comes the principle: "with the **merciful** (H2623, M05) you show yourself merciful; with the **blameless** you show yourself blameless; with the **purified** you show yourself pure; and with the **crooked** you make yourself seem tortuous. For you **save a humble people**, but the **haughty eyes** you **bring down** (H8213, M07)" (vv.25–27). God is a **mirror to the inner being's disposition**: the merciful *experience* him as merciful, the crooked *experience* him as crooked. Not that God changes — but that **what you bring to him shapes how you meet him** *(inferred: the reciprocity is about the inner being's own posture returning to it)*.

**VI. Lamp lit, made great by gentleness (vv.28–45).**
God then equips for life and battle: "you **light my lamp**; the LORD my God lightens my **darkness**" (v.28 — the inner light rekindled, as in Ps 13:3). He makes the feet sure, trains the hands, gives "the shield of your salvation" — and the summit: "your **gentleness** (H6037, M05) made me **great** (H7235)" (v.35). Not the psalmist's strength but God's **condescension/gentleness** is what exalts him *(stated: your gentleness made me great)*.

**VII. Praise (vv.46–50).**
"The LORD **lives**, and **blessed** (H1288, M39) be my rock!" (v.46). The arc closes in **praise** (H3034, M22) and **song** (H2167, M42), grounded in God's **steadfast love** (H2617, M05) (v.50).

## What Psalm 18 says about the inner being
- **It can love God, not merely need him.** The opening *racham* (v.1) — a tender, affectionate love usually God's toward us — turned back *toward* God, is the inner being at its warmest: leaning its whole weight on a God it *loves*.
- **God is met according to the disposition brought to him** (vv.25–27): the merciful find him merciful, the crooked find him tortuous. The inner being's own posture is, in a real sense, *returned* to it — how you come to God shapes how you experience God. This is the psalm's profoundest inner-being gem.
- **Rescue is being grasped, and grounded in delight** (vv.16, 19): the inner being is *reached down for* and *drawn out*, and the reason given is not merit but that God *delighted in* it — and the result is *spaciousness* ("a broad place") after the narrow grip of death.
- **Greatness comes from God's gentleness, not one's strength** (v.35): "your gentleness made me great" — the exalted inner being is exalted by God's *stooping*, not its own reaching.
- **The scale of God's regard** (vv.7–15): heaven itself convulses to answer one person's cry — the inner being matters enough to move the cosmos.

## Honest notes
- **Read by movement** (50 verses) rather than verse-by-verse — the mechanical Phase-1 build scaled fine (297 spans, 1255 rows); the reading groups the psalm's seven movements.
- **Stop-list working:** *choirmaster* (H5329), *enemies/enemy* (H0341) → standalone throughout.
- **Characteristics** (sanity-checked): *love* (M05), *strength*/*mighty*/*strong* (M23), *take-refuge* (M19); the theophany — *trembled* (M01), *angry* (M02); integrity — *blameless*/*kept*/*righteousness*; the mirror — *merciful* (M05), *bring-down* (M07); the summit — *gentleness* (M05); the close — *blessed* (M39), *praise* (M22), *sing* (M42), *steadfast-love* (M05).
- **Where the meaning lives:** the reaching-down rescue, "because he delighted in me," "broad place," and "light my lamp" are gate-2 — the reading carries them.
- **Residuals:** bearer=LORD bleed; manner/coupling over-weld; heavy repetition-tagging in the theophany (trembled/angry ×3).

---

## Psalm 19 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 19 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 19:1–14 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (2 verses backfilled). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **The psalm of two revelations.** Its own key is a movement **from the vast to the intimate**: the heavens' wordless speech to all the earth (vv.1–6), the perfect Torah that acts *on the inner being* (vv.7–11), and the response that ends at "the meditation of my heart" (vv.12–14).
- **Lens (re-framed 2026-07-03):** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`). *Part B re-alignment sweep — Lens bullet added for consistency; this reading was already operation-focused (verified header-by-header). Findings unchanged.*

## The reading

**I. The wordless speech of the heavens (vv.1–6).**
"The heavens **declare** the **glory** (H3519, M22) of God… Day to day pours out speech, and night to night reveals **knowledge** (H1847, M15). There is no speech, nor words, whose voice is not **heard** (H8085, M41). Their voice goes out through all the earth" (vv.1–4). A paradox: creation *communicates without language* — a voiceless testimony that nonetheless reaches everyone, everywhere *(inferred: the "no words" yet "voice heard" is the gem — a universal address below language)*. The sun, "like a bridegroom" and "a strong man," runs its course "with **joy** (H7797, M04)" (v.5). The inner being is *addressed by the cosmos* before a word is spoken.

**II. The perfect Torah that works on the soul (vv.7–11).**
Then the particular word, praised in six strokes, each naming an **effect on the inner being**: "The law of the LORD is **perfect** (H8549, M12), **reviving the soul** (H5315, M47); the testimony… **sure** (H0539, M13), making wise the simple; the precepts… **right** (H3477, M13), **rejoicing the heart** (H3820, M47); the commandment… **pure**, **enlightening the eyes**; the **fear** (H3374, M01) of the LORD… **clean** (H2889, M12), enduring forever; the rules… **true** (H0571, M13) and **righteous** (M26)" (vv.7–9). God's word does not merely inform — it **revives, gladdens, and illumines** the inner life *(stated: reviving the soul, rejoicing the heart, enlightening the eyes)*. And it is the object of **desire and delight**: "more to be **desired** (H2530, M28) than gold… sweeter than honey" (v.10) — the word is *craved and savoured*, not merely obeyed.

**III. Hidden faults, presumptuous sins, and the heart's meditation (vv.12–14).**
The response is self-examination that reaches below and above the conscious will: "Who can **discern** (H0995, M15) his **errors**? Declare me innocent from **hidden** faults. Keep back your servant also from **presumptuous** (H2086, M08) sins; let them not have **dominion** (H4910, M23) over me!" (vv.12–13). Two kinds of sin: the **hidden** (unknown, undetectable — "who can discern?") and the **presumptuous** (willful, seeking to *master* the person). The inner being needs God for both — it can neither *see* the one nor *resist* the other alone *(inferred: the pair maps sin below awareness and above the will)*. And the close turns wholly inward: "Let the **words of my mouth** and the **meditation** (H1902, M15) **of my heart** (H3820, M47) be **acceptable** (H7522, M29) in your sight" (v.14) — the inner being offers its very *private rumination* to God for approval.

## What Psalm 19 says about the inner being
- **The inner being is addressed before it speaks.** Creation's *wordless* voice (vv.1–4) reaches every person — a knowledge "poured out" day and night that the inner being "hears" without a syllable. Revelation meets it first as a silent, universal testimony.
- **God's word acts *on* the inner life, not just informs it** (vv.7–9): it *revives the soul*, *rejoices the heart*, *enlightens the eyes* — transformation, not data. And it is meant to be *desired and savoured* (v.10), sweeter than honey — the inner being is made to *relish* the word, not merely keep it.
- **Sin works both below awareness and above the will** (vv.12–13): "hidden faults" it cannot detect and "presumptuous sins" that would gain *dominion* over it. The inner being's self-knowledge is limited (it cannot discern its own errors) and its self-control is insufficient (it can be mastered) — so it needs God for both cleansing and restraint.
- **The heart's private meditation is offered to God** (v.14): the closing prayer aligns *outer speech* and *inner thought* — the inner being asks that even its silent rumination (*higgayon*, the meditating of Ps 1:2) be *acceptable*. What the heart turns over in private is presented for God's approval, as weighty as what the mouth says.

## Honest notes
- **Stop-list working:** *choirmaster* (H5329), *Psalm* (H4210) → standalone.
- **Characteristics** (sanity-checked): the Torah's qualities — *perfect*/*clean* (M12), *right*/*sure*/*true* (M13), *rules*/*righteous* (M26), *fear* of the LORD (M01); its effects — *reviving*/*rejoicing* with *soul*/*heart* (M47), *knowledge*/*discern*/*meditation* (M15); response to it — *desired* (M28), *keeping* (M30), *presumptuous*/*dominion* of sin (M08/M23), *acceptable* (M29); creation — *glory* (M22), *joy* (M04).
- **Where the meaning lives:** the wordless-speech paradox (vv.3–4) and "sweeter than honey" (v.10) are largely gate-2; the reading carries them.
- **Residuals:** bearer=LORD bleed (D11-flagged, very heavy in the Torah stanza); manner/coupling over-weld.

## Psalm 20 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 20 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 20:1–9 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **A royal, corporate psalm** — the people pray for the king before battle. Less introspective than the Davidic laments, but its centre is a sharp inner-being disclosure: **what you trust defines and decides you.**
- **Lens (re-framed 2026-07-03):** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`). *Part B re-alignment sweep — Lens bullet added for consistency; this reading was already operation-focused (verified header-by-header). Findings unchanged.*

## The reading
Psalm 20 is spoken *for* another — the congregation interceding — and its inner-being content lies in what it asks and where it locates confidence.

**I. Intercession — the heart's desire brought to God (vv.1–5).**
"May the LORD answer you in the day of **trouble** (H6869, M03)… May he **remember** (H2142, M41) all your offerings… May he **grant** (H5414, M12) you your **heart's desire** (H3824, the seat — M47) and **fulfil** all your **plans** (H6098, M17). May we shout for **joy** (H7442, M42) over your salvation" (vv.1–5). The inner being's deepest wishes — the *heart's desire* and *plans* — are **brought to God to be granted**, not seized by force *(inferred: the whole prayer treats desire as something entrusted for God to fulfil)*.

**II. The confession of confidence (v.6).**
"Now I **know** that the LORD **saves** his anointed; he will **answer** him… with the saving **might** (H1369, M23) of his right hand." Assurance rests on God's proven power, not the army's *(stated)*.

**III. The trust-contrast — name vs chariots (v.7).**
The centre: "Some **trust** in **chariots** and some in **horses**, but we **trust** (H2142, M41) in the **name** of the LORD our God." The Hebrew of "trust" here is *nazkir* — "we **invoke / call to mind**" — so the contrast is exact: others lean on *visible, tangible power* (chariots, horses); we *invoke the name* — God's revealed character and presence *(inferred: trust here is an act of remembering the Name, over against counting one's horses)*. **What the inner being leans on is what defines it.**

**IV. Two trusts, two ends (vv.8–9).**
"They **collapse** and **fall**, but we **rise** and **stand upright** (H5749, M11)" (v.8). The chariot-trusters *fall*; the name-invokers *stand*. The object of trust **decides the outcome** *(stated: they fall, we stand)*. The psalm closes: "O LORD, save the king! May he answer us when we **call** (H7121, M37)" (v.9).

## What Psalm 20 says about the inner being
- **What you trust defines you** (v.7): the inner being is revealed and shaped by *where it leans* — on visible power it can count (chariots, horses), or on the *name* it can only invoke. Trust is an act of *invoking* what one cannot see over against relying on what one can.
- **What you trust decides you** (v.8): the two trusts have two ends — collapse or standing. The ground of confidence is not neutral; leaning on might that fails *makes you fall*, leaning on the Name *makes you stand* (with the "never moved" of Ps 15–16).
- **The heart's desire is brought to God, not grasped** (v.4): even one's deepest wishes and plans are *entrusted* for God to grant — the inner being's proper posture toward its own longings is to lay them before God (setting up Ps 21's answer: "you have given him his heart's desire").

## Honest notes
- **Recurring reclassification — "holy of place":** *sanctuary* / *holy* (H6944, vv.2, 6, "holy heaven") → standalone (place attribute); handled at sanity-check.
- **Stop-list working:** *choirmaster* (H5329), *Psalm* (H4210) → standalone.
- **Characteristics** (sanity-checked): intercession — *remember*/*trust*-invoke (M41), *grant* (M12), *heart's-desire* (M47), *plans* (M17), *joy* (M42), *petitions* (M21), *favour* (M46); confidence — *might* (M23), *stand-upright* (M11), *call* (M37).
- **Note on "trust":** the tagged term is *zakar/nazkir* (invoke/remember, M41), not the usual *batach* — the psalm frames trust as *invoking the Name*. A per-occurrence sense worth keeping.
- **Residuals:** bearer=LORD bleed (D11-flagged); *all* intensity over-stamp.

## Psalm 21 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 21 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 21:1–13 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **A royal thanksgiving** — the companion and answer to Psalm 20. Where Ps 20 *asked* ("may he grant you your heart's desire", 20:4), Ps 21 *reports the giving* ("you have given him his heart's desire", 21:2). Its inner-being disclosure is not petition but **reception**: the trusting heart is a **receiving** heart, and everything it holds — joy, honour, life, security — it holds *derivatively*, from God.
- **Lens (re-framed 2026-07-03):** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`). *Part B re-alignment sweep — Lens bullet added for consistency; this reading was already operation-focused (verified header-by-header). Findings unchanged.*

## The reading
Psalm 21 divides cleanly: the king's joy in what God has **given** (vv.1–7), the rout of the enemy (vv.8–12, largely the external pole), and a closing doxology (v.13). The inner-being weight is almost all in the first movement, and it turns on one word in v.7.

**I. Joy that is wholly derivative (v.1).**
"O LORD, in **your strength** (H5797) the king **rejoices** (H8055, M04), and in **your salvation** how greatly he **exults** (H1523, M04)!" Two joy-verbs, intensified ("how greatly") — but note *where* the joy is located: **in your strength**, **in your salvation**. The lexical marks *strength* and *salvation* as process-qualifiers binding the rejoicing, not the king's own possessions. The inner being's gladness here has an **external ground**: it is joy *in* God's power and rescue, not joy in the self or the victory as the king's own achievement *(inferred from the "in your…" framing of both joy-verbs)*.

**II. The heart's desire — named and granted (v.2).**
"You have **given** (H5414, M12) him his **heart's** (H3820, the seat — M47) **desire** (H8378, M28) and have not **withheld** the **request** of his **lips**." The gem: the inner longing is not condemned, not merely tolerated, but **answered**. The *desire of the heart* (the seat's own wanting) and the *request of the lips* (its outward voicing) are set in parallel — inner longing and its expression — and **both are met** *(stated: given… not withheld)*. This is the exact hinge back to Ps 20:4's petition: what was asked *for* the king is here reported as **done** *(inferred from the verbal echo; not asserted as the psalm's own claim)*.

**III. Blessing that comes to meet him (v.3).**
"For you **meet** (H6923) him with **rich blessings** (H1293, M22); you **set** a **crown** of fine gold upon his head." The verb *qadam* (H6923) is "to come before, to anticipate, to go to meet." God does not merely respond when reached — he **comes out to meet** the king with good, ahead of the asking *(inferred: qadam carries the sense of anticipation)*. Blessing is **prevenient** — it arrives before it is earned or even fully sought.

**IV. Asked one thing, given more (v.4).**
"He **asked** (H7592, M21) **life** (H2416, M25) of you; you **gave** it to him, length of days forever and ever." He asked for *life*; he received **life extended past its own measure** — "forever and ever." The giving **exceeds the request** *(stated: he asked life; the answer is length of days forever)*. The inner being's petition is not merely granted but **overflowed**.

**V. Glory that is conferred, not self-generated (v.5).**
"His **glory** (H3519, M22) is great **through your salvation**; **splendor** (H1935, M22) and **majesty** (H1926, M22) you **bestow** on him." Three honour-words — glory, splendor, majesty — and every one is **derivative**: his glory is great *through your salvation*, splendor and majesty are what *you bestow*. The king's honour is real but **received**, never manufactured from within *(stated: "you bestow"; the glory is "through your salvation")*. (Cf. Ps 8 — worth is conferred by God's action, not intrinsic to the creature.)

**VI. The culmination is joy in the presence, not the gifts (v.6).**
"For you make him most **blessed** (H1293, M22) forever; you make him **glad** (H2302, M04) with the **joy** (H8057, M04) of your **presence** (H6440 — your *face*)." The movement of gifts (desire, crown, life, glory) does **not** terminate in the gifts — it terminates in **gladness in God's face**. The lexical binds *joy* and *presence* as the manner of the gladness: the deepest thing given is **joy in the presence itself** *(inferred: "the joy of your presence" makes the presence, not the benefits, the ground of the gladness)*. This is the same note struck in Ps 16:11 ("fullness of joy in your presence") and Ps 17:15 ("satisfied with your likeness") — a cross-psalm thread.

**VII. The hinge — WHY all of this: the king trusts (v.7).**
"For the king **trusts** (H0982, M19) in the LORD, and through the **steadfast love** (H2617, M05) of the Most High he shall **not be moved** (H4131)." The whole psalm turns here — *ki*, "for/because." The reason for the joy, the giving, the prevenient blessing, the conferred glory is **the king's trust**, met by **God's steadfast love**, issuing in "**not be moved**." The structure is exact: the **inner posture** (trust, *batach*) → **God's response** (steadfast love, *chesed*) → **the outcome** (immovability, *bal yimmot*). "Not be moved" is the same word as Ps 15:5 and 16:8 — the security of the one whose confidence is rightly placed *(stated: the king trusts; through steadfast love he is not moved)*. **The receiving of the first six verses rests entirely on the trusting of the seventh.**

**VIII. The enemy's inner scheming — and its futility (vv.8–12).**
The second movement turns outward to the enemies (largely the **external pole** — judgment, wrath, fire — not the inner being). But one inner-being note surfaces: "Though they **plan** evil (H7451, M27) against you, though they **devise** (H2803, M15) **mischief**, they will **not succeed**" (v.11). The enemies have an *inner life* too — they **plan** and **devise** (*chashab*, the same faculty of purposing/reckoning that is a good when stayed on God) — but here it is bent to **evil**, and its verdict is **"they will not succeed"** *(stated)*. The inner devising of the wicked against God **recoils into futility** *(inferred: the plan is real but comes to nothing)*.

**IX. The frame closes in praise (v.13).**
"Be **exalted**, O LORD, in **your strength**! We will sing and **praise** (H2167, M42) your **power** (H1369, M23)." The psalm opened with the king rejoicing *in your strength* (v.1) and closes with the community praising *your strength / power* (v.13) — an **inclusio on God's strength**. The inner being's final act, having received everything, is **praise of the Giver's power** *(stated)*. Reception completes itself in worship.

## What Psalm 21 says about the inner being
- **The trusting heart is a receiving heart (v.7 → vv.1–6).** All the psalm's giving is grounded, by its own *ki* in v.7, in the king's **trust** met by God's **steadfast love**. The inner posture that receives is trust; the security it gains ("not moved") is the same immovability as Ps 15–16.
- **Joy is wholly derivative (vv.1, 5, 6).** The inner being's gladness is located *in your strength*, *through your salvation*, in *the joy of your presence* — never in the self or the gift-as-possession. Honour too is **conferred** ("you bestow"), not self-generated.
- **The heart's desire is answered, not denied (v.2).** The seat's own longing and its voiced request are both met — the inner life's deepest wants, when brought to God (Ps 20), are **granted** and even **exceeded** (v.4, "length of days forever").
- **Blessing is prevenient (v.3).** God *comes to meet* (qadam) the inner being with good ahead of the asking — grace anticipates.
- **The gifts terminate in the Presence (v.6).** The chain of benefits resolves not in the benefits but in **joy in God's face** — the same thread as Ps 16:11 and 17:15.
- **The wicked's inner devising is futile (v.11).** The enemy's *planning* and *devising* (M15, the purposing faculty) bent to evil against God **does not succeed** — inner scheming against God recoils into nothing.

## Honest notes
- **DATA QUALITY — v.12 text garbled in DB.** `verse.verse_text` for Psa 21:12 ingested as fragments — "put flight you aim their faces bows" (a Phase-0 backfill artefact); the lexical spans (put/flight/aim/faces/bows) are intact. The verse is external (aiming bows at the enemies' faces), so it does not affect the inner-being reading, but the verse row should be repaired. **Flag for the researcher / a backfill re-run.**
- **bearer=LORD bleed (D11-flagged):** the Phase-1 lexical repeatedly stamped `bearer=Lord` on vv.1, 7, 9, 13 via the nearest-proper-noun heuristic, where the true bearer is the **king** (vv.1, 7) or the psalmist/community. Known residual (subject-agreement not parsed); does not affect the reading, which reads the bearers from the text.
- **Stop-list working:** *choirmaster* (H5329), *Psalm* (H4210), *David* (H1732) → standalone / superscription qualifiers (v.1).
- **Intensity over-stamp (residual):** *very* (v.1) and *all* (v.8) auto-stamped as intensity; cosmetic.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** reception — *given*/*gave* (H5414, M12), *heart's-desire* (H3820 M47 / H8378 M28), *asked* (H7592, M21), *life* (H2416, M25), *blessings*/*glory*/*splendor*/*majesty*/*most-blessed* (M22), *glad*/*joy* (M04); the hinge — *rejoices*/*exults* (M04), *trusts* (H0982, M19), *steadfast-love* (H2617, M05); the enemy — *devise* (H2803, M15); the close — *praise* (H2167, M42), *power* (H1369, M23).
- **Note on the M22 cluster (glory/splendor/majesty/blessing):** heavily represented here but every instance is **conferred** — a per-occurrence reading worth keeping (honour as received, not intrinsic).

## Psalm 22 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 22 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 22:1–31 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (vv.7, 12, 21 backfilled — see notes). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **The psalm of the forsaken sufferer.** A single 31-verse arc from the cry of dereliction (vv.1–21) to widening praise (vv.22–31). Its inner-being spine is **trust** (*batach*) — trust *remembered*, trust *constituted from the womb*, trust *mocked at its root*, and finally trust *vindicated*. The distinctive key: the sufferer feels **forsaken and unanswered**, yet the turn (v.24) discloses that God "has **not** hidden his face… **has heard**" — the felt-abandonment was real as experience but not final as reality.
- **A note on restraint:** this psalm is deeply resonant elsewhere in Scripture; the reading below stays with **the inner being the text itself discloses** — the sufferer's trust and dereliction — and does not build on imported meaning (memory `feedback_verse_meaning_grounded_not_imported`).
- **Lens (re-framed 2026-07-03):** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`). *Part B re-alignment sweep — Lens bullet added for consistency; this reading was already operation-focused (verified header-by-header). Findings unchanged.*

## The reading

**I. The cry of dereliction — forsakenness *prayed* (vv.1–2).**
"My God, my God, why have you **forsaken** (H5800) me? Why are you so **far** from saving me, from the words of my **groaning** (H7581, M42)?… by night, but I find **no rest** (H1747)." The extremity of the inner being: it experiences God's *absence* — far, unanswering, restless. Yet the whole cry is addressed **to** God — the doubled "my God, my God" is faith *clinging in the dark*: the inner being cries out even in the felt-forsakenness, and the crying is itself a holding-on *(inferred: the address "my God" persists through the sense of abandonment)*. Even the night yields "no rest" — not even the cessation of the cry *(stated)*.

**II. Trust that argues from history against present feeling (vv.3–5).**
"**Yet** you are **holy** (H6918, M22)… In you our fathers **trusted** (H0982, M19); they **trusted**, and you delivered them. To you they **cried** (H2199, M42) and were rescued; in you they **trusted** and were **not put to shame** (H0954, M07)." The inner being reasons *against its own experience*: three times "trusted," bracketed by God's holiness and the fathers' vindication. Trust here is **corporate memory** marshalled as evidence — *they* trusted and were not shamed, so the ground holds *(stated)*. **Shame** (*bosh*, M07) is named as the exact antithesis of vindicated trust — the fear the sufferer's trust might yet be "put to shame" *(inferred: the negation "not put to shame" makes shame the stake)*.

**III. The mockery aimed at the trust itself (vv.6–8).**
"But I am a **worm** and not a man, **scorned** (H2781, M06) by mankind and despised." Self-abasement — the loss of human standing. Then the taunt: "He **trusts** (H1556 — *galal*, 'rolls himself') in the LORD; let him deliver him… for he delights in him!" The deepest assault is not on the body but on the **trust**: the mockers weaponize the very act of *rolling oneself onto God*, throwing it back as proof it is useless *(stated: the mockers quote his trust as a reproach)*. The inner being is attacked at its foundation — the object of its confidence is turned into the instrument of its shame.

**IV. Trust constituted from the womb (vv.9–11).**
"**Yet** you are he who took me from the womb; you **made me trust** (H0982, M19) you at my mother's breasts… from my mother's womb you have been my God." The second "Yet." Now the ground shifts from corporate memory to **personal origin**: trust is not a late acquisition but **woven in from birth — and woven by God himself** ("*you* made me trust") *(stated)*. This is a strong disclosure of the inner being: the self is **oriented God-ward from infancy**, its trust native and God-given, not self-generated *(inferred)*. So the plea: "Be **not far**, for **trouble** (H6869, M03) is near, and there is none to help" (v.11).

**V. The dissolution of the whole person — the melting heart (vv.12–18).**
The encirclement (bulls of Bashan, the ravening **lion**, the **dogs**, the "company of **evildoers**" H7489/M27) presses in, and under it the whole person dissolves: "I am **poured out** like water; all my bones out of joint; my **heart** (H3820, the seat — M47) is like **wax**; it is **melted** within my breast; my **strength** (H3581, M23) is dried up… **you** lay me in the dust of death" (vv.14–15). The inner being (the heart) and the body **liquefy together** — the heart's resolve *melts like wax*, courage gone *(stated)*. And piercingly, the death is laid to **God's own hand** — "**you** lay me in the dust" — not only the enemies' *(stated)*; the sufferer traces even his undoing back to God.

**VI. The plea — the soul at stake (vv.19–21).**
"But **you**, O LORD, do not be **far off**! O you my **help** (H0360, M23), come quickly… **Deliver** my **soul** (H5315, the seat — M47) from the sword, my precious life from the power of the dog… Save me from the mouth of the lion." "Be not far" brackets the lament (v.11, v.19). What is at stake is named as the **soul / nephesh** — the very life of the inner being *(stated)*.

**VII. The turn — "he has *not* hidden his face… *has heard*" (vv.22–24).**
The hinge of the whole psalm. "I will tell of your **name** to my brothers; in the congregation I will **praise** (H1984, M22) you." Then the reason, answering vv.1–2 point for point: "For he has **not despised** or **abhorred** (H8262, M27) the **affliction** of the afflicted, and he has **not hidden his face** from him, but **has heard** (H8085, M41), when he cried" (v.24). The lament's "**why are you far** / you **do not answer**" is resolved: God did **not** hide his face; he **heard** all along *(stated)*. **The felt-forsakenness (v.1) was real as experience but was never the reality** — the turn is not a change in God but a disclosure of what was true through the silence *(inferred from the exact answering of the opening cry)*.

**VIII. The deliverance is generative — private rescue becomes public worship (vv.25–27).**
"**From you** comes my praise in the great congregation… The **afflicted** (H6035, M24) shall eat and be **satisfied**; those who **seek** (H1875, M41) him shall praise the LORD! **May your hearts** (H3824, the seat — M47) **live** (H2421, M25) forever!" (vv.25–26). The rescued sufferer's testimony **creates worship in others** — his praise is the fountain from which the afflicted are fed and their **hearts made to live** *(stated: the afflicted eat, are satisfied, their hearts live)*. Then the widening: "All the **ends of the earth** shall **remember** (H2142, M41) and **turn** (H7725, M45) to the LORD" (v.27) — the nations' inner **remembering and turning** *(stated)*.

**IX. The reach to the dying and the unborn — "he has done it" (vv.28–31).**
"**Kingship** belongs to the LORD… before him shall bow all who go down to the dust, even the one who **could not keep himself alive** (H5315, the soul — M47)" (vv.28–29). Worship extends even to those who **cannot preserve their own life** — the soul that could not save itself still bows *(stated)*. And it reaches forward: "Posterity shall **serve** (H5647, M36) him… they shall proclaim his **righteousness** (H6666, M26) to a people yet unborn, that **he has done it**" (vv.30–31). The accomplished work — "he has done it" (*asah*) — becomes the ground of the unborn's worship. The private rescue has become a testimony across the whole earth and every generation *(stated)*.

## What Psalm 22 says about the inner being
- **Forsakenness can be *prayed* (vv.1–2).** The inner being cries out even while experiencing God's absence; the doubled "my God, my God" is faith clinging through the felt-abandonment. The cry is itself an act of trust.
- **Trust is the spine, and it argues against feeling (vv.3–5, 9–10).** The inner being marshals *corporate memory* (the fathers trusted, were not shamed) and *personal origin* (trust from the womb) against its present sense of silence. **Shame** is the named antithesis of vindicated trust.
- **Trust is constituted from the womb (v.9).** "You made me trust you" — the self is oriented God-ward from birth, its confidence native and God-given, not self-produced. A strong claim about the inner being's original grain.
- **The deepest assault is on the trust itself (vv.7–8).** The mockery weaponizes the act of rolling oneself onto God — the inner being is attacked at its foundation, not merely its circumstances.
- **The heart melts; the whole person dissolves together (v.14).** Inner resolve liquefies "like wax"; body and heart collapse as one — and the sufferer traces even his undoing to God's hand ("*you* lay me in the dust").
- **The felt-forsakenness was not the reality (v.24).** God had "not hidden his face… has heard." The turn is a *disclosure*, not a reversal — what was true through the silence is finally seen.
- **A rescued inner being becomes generative (vv.25–31).** Private deliverance overflows: the afflicted are fed, their "hearts live forever," the ends of the earth remember and turn, the dying bow, the unborn are told — "he has done it." Testimony creates worship.

## Honest notes
- **DATA QUALITY — backfilled verses have fragmentary `verse_text`.** vv.7, 12, 21 were Phase-0 backfilled and their `verse.verse_text` stored as word-fragments (e.g. v.7 "All see mock make mouths wag heads"; standard text: "All who see me mock me; they make mouths at me; they wag their heads"). Same artefact seen at Psa 21:12. The lexical **spans are intact**; the verses here are external (mockery, bulls, lion), so the reading is unaffected — but this is now a **recurring backfill defect** worth a fix to the backfill script's verse_text assembly. **Flag for the researcher.**
- **"prohibition=forbidden (neg particle)" over-stamp (residual/D11).** The Phase-1 build stamps `prohibition=forbidden` on any span in a *negated* clause (vv.2, 5, 6, 24, 29). Most are plain **negation**, not prohibition — "you do **not** answer" (v.2), "**not** put to shame" (v.5), "he has **not** despised" (v.24). The prohibition flag should not fire on descriptive/asseverative negatives. **Rule-adjustment candidate.**
- **bearer=LORD bleed (D11-flagged):** pervasive here (vv.1, 8, 12, 19, 23, 26, 27, 28, 30) via the nearest-proper-noun heuristic — true bearers are the sufferer, the enemies, or the congregation. Known residual; the reading takes bearers from the text.
- **Intensity over-stamp (residual):** *all* / *many* auto-stamped (vv.7, 12, 14, 17, 23, 27, 29); cosmetic.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** the trust spine — *trusted* (H0982, M19, vv.4×2, 5, 9), *groaning*/*cried* (M42, vv.1, 5), *not-put-to-shame* (H0954, M07, v.5); the reproach — *scorned* (H2781, M06, v.6); dissolution — *heart* (M47, v.14), *strength* (M23, v.15); plea — *soul* (M47, v.20), *help* (M23, v.19); the turn — *heard* (H8085, M41, v.24), *abhorred* (H8262, M27, v.24, negated); the widening — *praise* (H1984/H8416, M22), *afflicted* (M24, v.26), *seek* (H1875, M41, v.26), *hearts/live* (M47/M25, v.26), *remember/turn* (M41/M45, v.27), *fear/awe* (H3373/H1481, M01, v.23), *serve* (M36, v.30), *righteousness* (M26, v.31).

## Psalm 23 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 23 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 23:1–6 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **The inner being at rest in the shepherd's keeping.** Six verses, one settled confidence. Read first-principles (not through its familiarity), the psalm's own key is a **movement of the inner being**: *want stilled* → *rest given and soul restored* → *fear answered by presence* → *honoured amid enemies* → *pursued by steadfast love into settled dwelling*. Its distinctive disclosures cluster on **what the shepherd does to the inner being**: he *makes* it rest, *restores* the soul, and — at the darkest point — the speech turns from *about* him to *to* him.
- **Lens (re-framed 2026-07-03):** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`). *Part B re-alignment sweep — Lens bullet added for consistency; this reading was already operation-focused (verified header-by-header). Findings unchanged.*

## The reading

**I. The wanting stilled (v.1).**
"The LORD is **my** shepherd; I shall **not want** (H2637)." The psalm opens with a statement about the inner being's *lack* — and declares it quieted. Not "I have all things" but "I shall not **want**": the *wanting itself* is stilled by the relationship *(inferred: the object of the claim is the verb "want", i.e. the inner state of lack)*. The confidence is **personal and relational** — "*my* shepherd" — not a doctrine about God but a bond *(stated)*.

**II. Rest that is *made*, and the soul *restored* (vv.2–3).**
"He **makes me lie down** (H7257) in green pastures. He **leads** me beside **still** (H4496, M33) waters. He **restores** (H7725) my **soul** (H5315, the seat — M47)." Two gems here. First, the rest is not self-achieved — the shepherd *makes* the sheep lie down, and the waters are literally the waters of **rest** (*menuchah*, M33): the inner being is **led into stillness** *(stated)*. Second, and central: "he restores my **soul**" — *shub nephesh*, the bringing-back of the inner being. The soul that flags is **turned/brought back** (the same *shub* that elsewhere is repentance) — the shepherd's core work on the inner being is **restoration** *(stated)*. And the guidance in "paths of **righteousness** (H6664, M26)" is grounded not in the sheep's merit but "**for his name's sake**" — the leading rests on the shepherd's own character *(stated)*.

**III. The turn to "you" — intimacy deepens in the valley (v.4).**
"Even though I **walk through** the valley of the shadow of death, I will **fear** (H3372, M01) **no evil**, for **you** are with me; your rod and your staff, they **comfort** (H5162, M05) me." The grammar itself preaches: vv.1–3 speak *about* the shepherd ("He… He… He"); at the valley the psalm turns to speak *to* him ("**you** are with me"). **The inner being draws nearest precisely at the darkest point** *(inferred from the He→You shift landing exactly on the valley)*. And the fearlessness is not stoicism but **relational** — "I will fear no evil, **for** you are with me": fear is answered by *presence*, not by the removal of the valley (he still *walks through* it) *(stated: the ground of no-fear is "you are with me")*. The rod and staff **comfort** (*nacham*, M05) — an inner consolation, not merely protection.

**IV. Honour and abundance in the enemies' presence (v.5).**
"You **prepare** (H6186, M26 — set in order) a table before me **in the presence of my enemies**; you **anoint** (H1878, M46) my head with oil; my cup **overflows**." The inner being is **satisfied and honoured in full view of the threat** — not after the enemies are removed *(stated: the table is set "in the presence of my enemies")*. The anointing (*dashen*, M46 — to make rich/fat) and the overflowing cup are **abundance lavished amid danger** *(inferred: the overflow signals more-than-enough)*.

**V. Pursued by steadfast love into settled dwelling (v.6).**
"Surely goodness and **mercy** (H2617, M05 — *chesed*) shall **follow** (H7291) me all the days of my life, and I shall **dwell** in the house of the LORD forever." The verb *radaph* (H7291) is **pursue / chase** — the word usually used of enemies hunting the sufferer. Here the one pursued is pursued instead by **goodness and steadfast love**: the inner being is **hunted down by chesed** *(inferred: radaph inverts the pursuit — mercy chases where foes used to)*. And the destination is not merely safety but **settled belonging** — "I shall **dwell** in the house of the LORD forever." The inner being's end is *dwelling with God* *(stated)*.

## What Psalm 23 says about the inner being
- **The inner being's *wanting* is stilled by the relationship (v.1).** The opening claim is about lack — and it is quieted not by possession but by "my shepherd."
- **Rest is *made*, not achieved (v.2).** "He makes me lie down"; the soul is *led* into stillness (the waters of *menuchah*). Rest is the shepherd's gift, worked on the inner being.
- **The soul is *restored* (v.3).** *Shub nephesh* — the flagging inner being is brought back; restoration is the shepherd's central inner-work, grounded "for his name's sake," not the sheep's merit.
- **Intimacy deepens in the dark (v.4).** The speech turns from *about* him to *to* him exactly at the valley — the inner being draws nearest at its lowest.
- **Fear is answered by presence, not by rescue from the valley (v.4).** He still *walks through* it; what changes is "you are with me." The rod and staff *comfort* — an inner consolation.
- **The inner being is satisfied *amid* enemies (v.5).** Honour and abundance are given in full view of the threat, not after its removal.
- **Steadfast love *pursues* (v.6).** *Radaph* inverts the hunt — the one chased by foes is now chased by *chesed*, into settled dwelling with God.

## Honest notes
- **"prohibition=forbidden (neg particle)" over-stamp (residual/D11).** Fired on v.1 "shall **not** want" and v.4 "fear **no** evil" — both plain **negation** (descriptive/asseverative), not prohibition. Same over-stamp flagged at Psa 22; **rule-adjustment candidate** (the prohibition flag should not fire on non-imperative negatives).
- **bearer=LORD/David bleed (D11-flagged):** v.1 via the nearest-proper heuristic; the reading takes bearers from the text.
- **Intensity over-stamp (residual):** *all* auto-stamped at v.6 ("all the days"); cosmetic.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *still*-waters = rest (H4496, M33, v.2); *soul* (H5315, M47, v.3); *righteousness* (H6664, M26, v.3); *fear* (H3372, M01, v.4, negated — "fear no evil"); *comfort* (H5162, M05, v.4); *prepare* (H6186, M26, v.5); *anoint* (H1878, M46, v.5); *mercy/chesed* (H2617, M05, v.6); *life* (H2416, M25, v.6).
- **Note (cross-psalm, not imported):** placed after Psa 22 (the forsaken sufferer whose "heart melts like wax"), Psa 23 reads as its counter-image — the same inner being now *restored* and *at rest*. Recorded as a thread for the later cross-chapter reading, not read into Psalm 23's own text.

## Psalm 24 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 24 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 24:1–10 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (v.2 backfilled). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **An entrance liturgy in two panels:** *who may approach* God (vv.3–6) and *who is approached* (vv.7–10, the King of glory), framed by the LORD's ownership of the whole earth (vv.1–2). The inner-being weight is the middle panel. Its own key — over against Ps 15, the other entrance liturgy — is that it presses past *deeds* to the **soul's aim**: the qualified worshipper is one who "does not **lift up his soul** to what is false," and the qualified are named as **seekers of God's face**.
- **Lens (re-framed 2026-07-03):** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`). *Part B re-alignment sweep — Lens bullet added for consistency; this reading was already operation-focused (verified header-by-header). Findings unchanged.*

## The reading

**I. The ground: the whole earth is the LORD's (vv.1–2).**
"The earth is the LORD's and the fullness thereof… for he has **founded** (H3245) it upon the seas and **established** (H3559) it upon the rivers." The panel of approach is set against **total divine ownership** — the One to be approached owns everything and everyone who dwells on the earth *(stated)*. The question of vv.3–6 therefore is not "may a creature come to a local deity" but "who may stand before the **Owner of all**" *(inferred)*.

**II. The question of ascent — who may stand before God (v.3).**
"**Who** shall ascend the hill of the LORD? And **who** shall stand in his **holy** (H6944, M22) place?" The inner being's **fitness to approach God** is the whole question *(stated)*. Not everyone who lives on the LORD's earth (v.1) may **stand in his holy place** — approach requires something the psalm is about to name.

**III. The answer — outward and inward, and the soul's aim (v.4).**
"He who has **clean** (H5355, M12) hands and a **pure** (H1249) **heart** (H3824, the seat — M47), who does **not lift up his soul** (H5375 *nasa* + H5315, the seat — M47) to what is **false** (H7723, *shav*), and does not swear **deceitfully** (H4820, M14, *mirmah*)." Four clauses, paired: **outward** ("clean hands" — deeds) and **inward** ("pure heart" — disposition) *(stated)*. But the psalm goes deeper than either: "does not **lift up his soul to what is false**." To *lift up the soul* (*nasa nephesh*) is to **set one's longing / aspiration upon** something — so the qualification is about **where the inner being directs its desire**: not toward *shav* (emptiness, vanity, falsehood) *(inferred: nasa-nephesh is the idiom of longing/aiming the self)*. And "swear deceitfully" (*mirmah*, M14) tests the **integrity of the inner being in speech**. **The heart's purity is located in the soul's aim** — not merely in clean acts but in a self whose longing is not fixed on the empty and false *(inferred)*.

**IV. Righteousness *received* (v.5).**
"He will **receive** (H5375, *nasa* — lift/carry away) **blessing** (H1293, M22) from the LORD and **righteousness** (H6666, M26) from the God of his salvation." Even the one with clean hands and pure heart does not *generate* his standing — he **receives righteousness from God** *(stated: "righteousness from the God of his salvation")*. The inner being's rightness before God is, at last, a **gift carried to it**, not a self-achievement *(inferred; cf. the conferred glory of Ps 21:5)*.

**V. The face-seeking generation (v.6).**
"Such is the **generation** of those who **seek** (H1875, M41, *darash*) him, who **seek** (H1245, M41, *baqash*) the **face** of the God of Jacob." Two seek-verbs intensify the point: the qualified inner being is defined not by a *state* but by a **direction** — it is a **seeker**, and what it seeks is not gifts but **the face of God himself** *(stated)*. The generation of the pure-hearted (v.4) *is* the generation of face-seekers (v.6) — purity and seeking are the same posture viewed twice *(inferred)*. (Thread: seeking/beholding the face — Ps 11:7, 16:11, 17:15, 21:6, 22:26.)

**VI. The King of glory — whom the seeker seeks (vv.7–10).**
"**Lift up** (*nasa*) your heads, O **gates**… that the **King of glory** (H3519, M22, *kabod*) may come in… Who is this King of glory? **The LORD**, strong and mighty… **The LORD of hosts** (H6635, M23), he is the King of glory!" *Glory* (*kabod*) tolls five times. Two things for the inner being. First, this panel **names the object of the seeking of v.6**: the face the pure-hearted seek is the face of **the King of glory now entering** — the movement resolves from *who may come to God* to *who this God is* *(inferred: v.6's "seek his face" and vv.7–10's revealed King answer each other)*. Second, a wordplay worth marking: the same verb *nasa* runs through the psalm — the worshipper must **not lift his soul** to what is false (v.4), and the gates **lift their heads** for the King (v.7). **What the inner being lifts itself toward is the whole question** — the soul that refuses to lift itself to vanity is the one prepared to lift its head to the King of glory *(inferred from the shared verb; offered as a structural observation, not asserted as the psalm's stated claim)*.

## What Psalm 24 says about the inner being
- **Fitness to stand before God is *inner* (vv.3–4).** The question of approach is answered by "clean hands **and** a pure heart" — deed and disposition together — but the decisive clause is about the **soul's aim**.
- **Purity is a matter of where the soul lifts its longing (v.4).** "Does not lift up his soul to what is false" — the inner being is qualified or disqualified by the *direction of its desire*, not only by its acts. Longing fixed on vanity disqualifies.
- **Integrity of the inner being in speech (v.4).** "Does not swear deceitfully" — *mirmah*; the honest heart shows in kept oaths (cf. Ps 15:4).
- **Righteousness is *received*, not achieved (v.5).** Even the pure-hearted "receive righteousness from the God of his salvation" — standing before God is finally a gift carried to the inner being.
- **The approaching self is a *seeker of the face* (v.6).** The qualified generation is defined by direction, not state — it seeks God himself, his *face*, not merely his gifts. Purity and seeking are one posture.
- **What the inner being *lifts itself toward* defines it (vv.4, 7).** The *nasa* wordplay: refuse to lift the soul to falsehood, and you are the one who lifts your head to the King of glory.

## Honest notes
- **"prohibition=forbidden (neg particle)" over-stamp (residual/D11).** Fired across v.4 ("does **not** lift up… **not** swear") — these negatives **define the character**, they are not prohibitions. Same over-stamp flagged at Psa 22, 23; **rule-adjustment candidate**.
- **bearer=LORD/David bleed (D11-flagged):** pervasive (vv.1, 3, 5, 8, 10) via the nearest-proper heuristic; the reading takes bearers from the text.
- **`nasa` (H5375) tagged M19/mixed:** the verb carries three senses across the psalm — *lift up the soul* (v.4, aim/long), *receive/carry* (v.5), *lift the head* (vv.7, 9). The Phase-1 tag (M19) is a per-occurrence approximation; the reading reads each occurrence from context. A **grain-split candidate** (memory `project_term_is_sense_not_lemma`).
- **DATA QUALITY — v.2 backfilled with fragmentary `verse_text`** ("for founded it upon seas established it upon rivers"); spans intact, verse is external (creation), reading unaffected. Recurring backfill defect (see Psa 21:12, 22:7/12/21).
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *holy* (H6944, M22, v.3); *clean* (H5355, M12) + *heart* (H3824, M47) + *soul* (H5315, M47) + *deceitfully* (H4820, M14, v.4); *blessing* (H1293, M22) + *righteousness* (H6666, M26, v.5); *seek* ×2 (H1875 *darash* / H1245 *baqash*, M41, v.6); *glory* (H3519, M22, ×5, vv.7–10); *hosts* (H6635, M23, v.10).

## Psalm 25 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 25 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 25:1–22 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (v.4 backfilled). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **An acrostic** (each verse begins with a successive Hebrew letter). The form is not a linear argument but a **comprehensive, A-to-Z circling** of the soul's postures before God — so the reading names the *recurring postures* rather than forcing a progression. Three intertwined needs braid through it — to be **taught**, to be **forgiven**, to be **delivered** — all carried by **trust** and **waiting** (*qavah*, which brackets the psalm at vv.3, 5, 21), and all grounded in God's *chesed*, name, and goodness, never the pleader's merit.
- **Lens (re-framed 2026-07-03):** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`). *Part B re-alignment sweep — Lens bullet added for consistency; this reading was already operation-focused (verified header-by-header). Findings unchanged.*

## The reading

**I. The soul lifted to God — and held in waiting (vv.1–5).**
"To you, O LORD, I **lift up my soul** (H5375 *nasa* + H5315, the seat — M47)" (v.1). The very idiom Psalm 24:4 used *negatively* ("does **not** lift up his soul to what is false") appears here *positively*: the inner being's longing and aspiration are **directed to God** — the soul offered up in dependence rather than fixed on vanity *(inferred: nasa-nephesh is the idiom of aiming/longing the self; here the object is "to you, O LORD")*. This is coupled at once with **trust** ("in you I **trust**", H0982, M19, v.2) and its stake, **shame** ("let me not be **put to shame**", H0954, M07) — shame is again named as the antithesis of vindicated trust *(stated)*. Then the frame-posture enters: "none who **wait** (H6960, M17, *qavah*) for you shall be put to shame… for you I **wait** all the day long" (vv.3, 5). The inner being's stance is **expectant waiting** — not passive but a sustained, all-day leaning *(stated)*.

**II. The plea to be *taught* — teachability as the soul's central request (vv.4–5, 8–9, 12).**
A dense cluster of guidance-verbs: "**Make me know** (H3045) your ways… **teach** (H3925) me your paths. **Lead** (H1869) me in your **truth** (H0571, M13)" (vv.4–5). The inner being's central petition is not merely rescue but **guidance** — to be *shown* and *led* *(stated)*. And the ones God teaches are named: "He **leads the humble** (H6035, M24, *anav*) in what is right, and **teaches the humble** his way" (v.9); "Who is the man who **fears** (H3373, M01) the LORD? Him will he **instruct** in the way he should **choose** (H0977, M37)" (v.12). **Teachability has preconditions — humility and the fear of the LORD** — and its fruit is a self able to *choose* rightly because it has been taught *(inferred: the taught man is instructed "in the way he should choose")*. The inner being that lowers itself and fears is the one led.

**III. The appeal to God's memory — remember mercy, remember not my sins, remember *me* (vv.6–7, 11, 18).**
A threefold play on **remember** (H2142, M41, *zakar*): "**Remember** your **mercy** (H7356, M05, *racham*)… and your **steadfast love** (H2617, M05, *chesed*)" — "**Remember not** the **sins** (H2403, M10) of my youth or my **transgressions** (H6588, M10)" — "according to your steadfast love **remember me**" (vv.6–7). The inner being asks God to remember **selectively**: his own mercy, and the pleader — but *not* the record *(stated)*. And the ground is entirely God's: "**for the sake of your goodness**" (v.7), "**for your name's sake**" (v.11). The most striking clause is v.11: "pardon my **guilt** (H5771, M10), **for it is great**." Not *pardon despite its greatness* but **pardon because it is great** — the inner being pleads **the very size of its need as the ground of grace**, because only such pardon magnifies God's name *(inferred: the "for it is great" is offered as the reason, not the obstacle)*. Forgiveness and affliction are sought as one breath: "Consider my affliction… and **forgive all my sins**" (v.18) — deliverance from trouble and from sin are not separate requests *(stated)*.

**IV. The fear of the LORD that becomes *friendship* (vv.12–14).**
The gem at the psalm's centre: "The **friendship** (H5475, M17, *sod*) of the LORD is for those who **fear** (H3373, M01) him, and he makes **known** (H3045) to them his covenant" (v.14). *Sod* is **intimate counsel — the confidential circle, the shared secret**. The fear of the LORD issues **not in distance but in intimacy**: God lets those who fear him **into his confidence** *(stated: the sod of the LORD is for those who fear him)*. The paradox is exact — *fear* opens *friendship*; the reverent inner being is the one taken into God's counsel *(inferred)*. And the fearing soul's future is secure: "His **soul** (H5315, M47) shall **abide** in well-being" (v.13).

**V. The fixed gaze and the enlarged heart (vv.15–19).**
"My **eyes** are **ever** toward the LORD, for he will pluck my feet out of the net" (v.15). The inner being's **continual orientation** — the gaze *ever* fixed Godward, a settled attentiveness even while trapped *(stated)*. Then the raw disclosure of distress: "Turn to me and be **gracious** (H2603, M39), for I am **lonely** (*yachid* — solitary) and **afflicted** (v.16). The **troubles** (H6869, M03) of my **heart** (H3824, the seat — M47) are **enlarged** (*rachab* — made wide); bring me out of my **distresses** (H4691, M03)" (v.17). Two things for the inner being: **loneliness** named outright — the solitary self — and the heart's troubles that **widen** rather than shrink, the inner straits *growing* under pressure *(stated: the troubles of the heart are enlarged)*. The gaze stays fixed (v.15) even as the heart's distress expands (v.17) — attentiveness and anguish coexist.

**VI. Integrity, refuge, and waiting as the frame (vv.20–22).**
"Oh, **guard** (H8104, M30) my **soul** (H5315, M47), and deliver me… for I **take refuge** (H2620, M19, *chasah*) in you" (v.20) — the refuge-posture again (cf. Ps 2, 3, 11, 16). Then: "May **integrity** (H8537, M13, *tom*) and **uprightness** (H3476, M26, *yosher*) **preserve** me, for I **wait** (H6960, M17) for you" (v.21). The inner qualities are asked to **function as guardians** — integrity and uprightness *preserve* the one who has them — and the ground is once more **waiting** *(stated)*. Waiting closes the psalm as it opened it (vv.3, 5 → 21); the whole is held between the soul lifted up (v.1) and the soul that waits (v.21).

## What Psalm 25 says about the inner being
- **The soul's aim can be lifted *to God* (v.1).** The positive counterpoint to Ps 24:4 — the inner being directs its longing to the LORD rather than to vanity. Aspiration Godward is the opening posture.
- **Waiting is the sustaining stance (vv.3, 5, 21).** *Qavah* brackets the psalm — an expectant, all-day leaning that is never put to shame.
- **Teachability is the soul's central request, and it has preconditions (vv.4–5, 9, 12).** The inner being asks above all to be *taught* and *led*; humility and the fear of the LORD are what make it teachable, and the fruit is a self able to choose rightly.
- **The inner being appeals to be remembered by grace, not by record (vv.6–7).** Remember your mercy, remember *not* my sins, remember *me* by steadfast love — a selective memory pleaded on God's own goodness and name.
- **The size of the need is pleaded as the ground of grace (v.11).** "Pardon my guilt, *for it is great*" — need magnified, not minimised, because grace answers to God's name.
- **Fear of the LORD becomes *friendship* (v.14).** *Sod* — the reverent inner being is admitted to God's confidential counsel. Fear opens intimacy, not distance.
- **The gaze stays fixed while the heart's troubles widen (vv.15, 17).** "Eyes ever toward the LORD" and "the troubles of my heart are enlarged" hold together — attentiveness and anguish coexist; loneliness is named.
- **Integrity and uprightness *preserve* the inner being (v.21).** Inner qualities function as guardians, and waiting is their ground.

## Honest notes
- **"prohibition=forbidden (neg particle)" over-stamp (residual/D11).** Fired at vv.2, 7, 20. Some are **jussive/volitional** negatives ("let me **not** be put to shame", "remember **not**") — closer to petition than the plain descriptive negatives flagged at Psa 22–24, but still not *prohibition*. The flag conflates negation, jussive-petition, and prohibition; **rule-adjustment candidate** (distinguish the three).
- **bearer=LORD bleed (D11-flagged):** pervasive via the nearest-proper heuristic; the reading takes bearers from the text.
- **`nasa` (H5375) again mixed:** *lift up the soul* (v.1, aim/long) vs *forgive/lift away* (v.18). Per-occurrence sense; **grain-split candidate** (memory `project_term_is_sense_not_lemma`), as flagged at Psa 24.
- **DATA QUALITY — v.4 backfilled with fragmentary `verse_text`** ("know ways Lord teach me paths"; spans intact). Recurring backfill defect (Psa 21:12, 22:7/12/21, 24:2). Also v.21 verse_text carries a stray "^" footnote marker (H3068 span). Cosmetic; flag for cleanup.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *lift-up-soul* (H5375/H5315, M19/M47, v.1); *trust* (H0982, M19, v.2); *wait* (H6960, M17, vv.3,5,21); *put-to-shame* (H0954, M07, vv.2,3,20); *truth/faithfulness* (H0571, M13, vv.5,10); *remember* (H2142, M41, vv.6,7); *mercy/steadfast-love* (H7356/H2617, M05, vv.6,7,10); *pardon* (H5545, M11, v.11) + *guilt/sins/transgressions* (H5771/H2403/H6588, M10); *fears* (H3373, M01, vv.12,14); *choose* (H0977, M37, v.12); *friendship/sod* (H5475, M17, v.14); *soul* (H5315, M47, vv.1,13,20); *gracious* (H2603, M39, v.16); *troubles/heart* (H6869/H3824, M03/M47, v.17); *affliction* (H6040, M24, v.18); *hatred/hate* (H8135/H8130, M06, v.19); *guard* (H8104, M30, v.20); *take-refuge* (H2620, M19, v.20); *integrity/uprightness* (H8537/H3476, M13/M26, v.21); *redeem* (H6299, M38, v.22).

## Psalm 26 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 26 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 26:1–12 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **The psalm of the inner being that offers itself to be tested.** "Prove me… try me… test my heart and my mind" (v.2). Read first-principles, its own key is a **tension held rightly**: the bold appeal for vindication ("I have walked in my integrity") is **not** self-righteousness in the psalm's own frame, because it is (a) grounded in God's *steadfast love kept before the eyes* (v.3), (b) worked out in *disassociation* from falsehood and *love for God's house* (vv.4–8), and (c) resolved into a plea for **grace** — "redeem me, and be gracious to me" (v.11). **The integrous inner being does not trust its integrity; it can invite testing precisely because its confidence rests on *chesed*, not on its own record.**

- **Lens (re-framed 2026-07-03):** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`). *Part B re-alignment sweep; already operation-focused (the self offered for assay; integrity resolved into grace). Aheb-fix substrate now applied — the v.8 "love the habitation" mis-tag flagged below is **RESOLVED** (H0157 now tags characteristic). Findings unchanged.*

## The reading

**I. The self offered for assay — "test my heart and my mind" (vv.1–2).**
"**Vindicate** (H8199, M26 — *judge* me) me, O LORD, for I have **walked in my integrity** (H8537, M13, *tom*), and I have **trusted** (H0982, M19) in the LORD **without wavering**" (v.1). Then the astonishing invitation: "**Prove** (H0974, *bachan* — assay) me, O LORD, and **try** (H5254, *nasah*) me; **test** (H6884, *tsaraph* — smelt/refine) my **heart** (H3820, the seat — M47) and my **mind** (*kilyah* — the kidneys, the inmost)." Three assaying verbs — assay, try, **smelt** — and the inner being offers its **deepest, most hidden parts** (heart and kidneys) **to the refiner's fire** *(stated: he asks God to test his heart and inmost)*. This is the opposite of hiding: where Ps 24 *states* the qualification for approach, Ps 26 **submits to being examined** — a confidence that welcomes the closest scrutiny *(inferred)*.

**II. The ground — chesed before the eyes (v.3).**
And here is why the confidence is not boasting: "For your **steadfast love** (H2617, M05, *chesed*) is **before my eyes**, and I **walk** in your **faithfulness** (H0571, M13, *emet*)" (v.3). The integrity is **not self-generated** — it is a *walking* **in God's faithfulness**, with God's *chesed* **kept constantly before the gaze** *(stated)*. The uprightness flows from **keeping God's love in view** (the fixed gaze again — cf. 25:15). The inner being's integrity is **responsive**, not autonomous: it walks in *God's* faithfulness, not its own *(inferred)*.

**III. The company that defines the inner being — the separations (vv.4–5).**
"I do **not sit** (H3427) with men of **falsehood** (*shav*), nor consort with **hypocrites** (H5956, M14 — *dissemblers*, the concealed); I **hate** (H8130, M06) the assembly of **evildoers** (H7489, M27), and I will **not sit** with the **wicked** (H7563, M10)" (vv.4–5). Integrity is partly defined by **disassociation** — the inner being's refusal to *sit / keep company* with falsehood *(stated)*. The "sitting" motif echoes Ps 1:1 ("sit in the seat of scoffers"): **the company one keeps shapes and reveals the inner being**. And the one directed *hatred* named here is a **hatred of the evildoers' assembly** — the inner being's aversion is aimed at evil-company, not persons abstractly *(inferred: the object is "the assembly of evildoers")*.

**IV. The positive counterpart — innocence and the *love* of God's house (vv.6–8).**
Over against the assembly he shuns stands the place he loves: "I **wash** my hands in **innocence** (H5356, M07, *niqqayon*) and go around your altar… **proclaiming thanksgiving** (H8426, M22, *todah*)… O LORD, I **love** (H0157, *aheb*) the **habitation** of your house and the place where your **glory** (H3519, M22, *kabod*) **dwells**" (vv.6–8). The gem: the inner being's positive orientation is **affection for God's dwelling** — "I *love* the habitation of your house" is a genuine **desire and delight** directed to where God's glory dwells *(stated)*. Purity of hands (v.6) and love of the presence (v.8) are the two faces of the same integrity — clean approach and glad affection *(inferred)*. (The *kabod* that "dwells" here is the glory whose King entered in Ps 24; thread noted, not imported.)

**V. The plea not to share the sinners' fate (vv.9–10).**
"Do **not sweep** my **soul** (H5315, the seat — M47) away with **sinners** (H2400, M10), nor my **life** (H2416, M25) with **bloodthirsty** men, in whose hands are evil devices… and whose right hands are full of **bribes**" (vv.9–10). The inner being fears **sharing the sinners' gathering / fate** — "do not gather my soul with theirs" *(stated)*. Note the **hands** motif: *his* hands washed in innocence (v.6) against *their* hands full of bribes (v.10) — the same body-part discloses two inner conditions *(inferred)*.

**VI. Integrity resolved into grace — the psalm's own key (v.11).**
"**But as for me**, I shall **walk in my integrity** (H8537, M13); **redeem** (H6299, M38, *padah*) me, and be **gracious** (H2603, M39, *chanan*) to me" (v.11). This is where the whole psalm shows its hand. The re-affirmed integrity ("I shall walk in my integrity") stands **in the same breath** as a plea for **redemption and grace** — "redeem me, be gracious to me" *(stated)*. **The integrous inner being does not plead its integrity as merit; it walks in integrity *and* casts itself on grace.** The opening "vindicate me, for I have walked in integrity" was therefore never self-righteousness — it ends on **being redeemed** *(inferred: v.11 reframes v.1 as a plea, not a boast)*.

**VII. The tested heart on level ground — the two assemblies (v.12).**
"My **foot stands** on **level ground** (*mishor* — evenness/uprightness); in the **great assembly** I will **bless** (H1288, M39, *barak*) the LORD" (v.12). From the *tested heart* (v.2) to the *foot on level ground* (v.12): the inner being that submitted to assaying now **stands firm and even** *(stated)*. And the private integrity issues in **public blessing** — "in the great assembly I will bless the LORD." The two assemblies **frame the psalm**: the *assembly of evildoers* he would not sit in (v.5) versus the *great assembly* where he blesses God (v.12). The inner being's chosen congregation discloses it *(inferred)*.

## What Psalm 26 says about the inner being
- **The inner being can *invite* God's examination of its inmost (v.2).** "Test my heart and my mind" — three assaying verbs offer the hidden self to the refiner. Confidence that welcomes the closest scrutiny.
- **That confidence is grounded in *chesed*, not in the self (v.3).** Integrity is a *walking in God's faithfulness* with his steadfast love kept before the eyes — responsive, not autonomous.
- **The company the inner being keeps defines it (vv.4–5).** Integrity includes *disassociation* — refusal to sit with falsehood; the one directed hatred is aimed at evil-company (echo of Ps 1:1's "seat").
- **Its positive orientation is *love for God's dwelling* (v.8).** "I love the habitation of your house" — genuine affection directed to where God's glory dwells; the counterpart to the assembly it shuns.
- **Integrity does not trust itself — it resolves into grace (v.11).** "I shall walk in my integrity; *redeem me, be gracious to me*." The integrous heart still rests on redemption. This is the psalm's key.
- **The tested heart ends on *level ground* and in *public blessing* (v.12).** The self that submitted to assay stands firm; private integrity overflows into blessing God in the great assembly.

## Honest notes
- **SANITY-CHECK CATCH — "love" (H0157, *aheb*, v.8) — ✓ RESOLVED (2026-07-03).** The original Phase-1 build marked *love* as `role=standalone` [gate-2]; this reading flagged it as a mis-tag (it is a genuine **inner-being characteristic** — affection/desire directed God-ward). The **aheb re-run** (PROMOTE_CHARACTERISTIC = {H0157}, Part A of the re-alignment sweep) has now corrected the substrate: v.8 "love" tags `role=characteristic`. The reading anticipated the fix; substrate and reading now agree.
- **"prohibition=forbidden (neg particle)" over-stamp (residual/D11).** Fired at vv.1, 4, 5, 9 — a mix the flag conflates: *descriptive* ("without wavering", v.1), *habitual resolve* ("I do not sit", vv.4–5), and *petition* ("do not sweep", v.9). None are prohibitions. Same over-stamp flagged Psa 22–25; **rule-adjustment candidate** (distinguish descriptive / resolve / jussive-petition / prohibition).
- **bearer=LORD bleed (D11-flagged):** pervasive (vv.1, 2, 8) via the nearest-proper heuristic; the reading takes bearers from the text (the speaker, not the LORD, walks in integrity and loves the house).
- **v.2 "mind" (kilyah, kidneys)** not separately surfaced in the lexical (only *heart* H3820 tagged); read from the text as the paired inmost organ. Minor coverage gap.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *vindicate* (H8199, M26, v.1); *integrity* (H8537, M13, vv.1,11); *trusted* (H0982, M19, v.1); *heart* (H3820, M47, v.2); *steadfast-love* (H2617, M05, v.3); *faithfulness* (H0571, M13, v.3); *hypocrites* (H5956, M14, v.4); *hate* (H8130, M06, v.5) + *evildoers/wicked* (H7489/H7563, M27/M10); *innocence* (H5356, M07, v.6); *proclaiming/thanksgiving/wondrous-deeds* (H8085/H8426/H6381, M41/M22/M04, v.7); *love* (H0157, v.8 — see catch); *glory* (H3519, M22, v.8); *soul/life* (H5315/H2416, M47/M25, v.9); *redeem/gracious* (H6299/H2603, M38/M39, v.11); *bless* (H1288, M39, v.12).
