## Psalm 27 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 27 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 27:1–14 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (v.10 backfilled). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **The psalm of the "one thing" and the seeking face.** Two movements that feel almost opposite — fearless confidence (vv.1–6) and urgent, exposed plea (vv.7–14) — are held together by **a single consuming desire**: to dwell with God and **gaze on his beauty** (v.4). Its two peaks are the *consolidation of all desire into one* (v.4) and the *heart's dialogue with God* (v.8, "Seek my face" / "Your face I seek"). The very face the inner being longs to gaze on (v.4) is the face it dreads to lose (v.9) — longing and dread of the same thing.
- **Lens (re-framed 2026-07-03):** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`). *Part B re-alignment sweep — Lens bullet added for consistency; this reading was already operation-focused (verified header-by-header). Findings unchanged.*

## The reading

**I. Fearlessness grounded in what God *is* to the inner being (vv.1–3).**
"The LORD is my **light** (H0216) and my **salvation**; whom shall I **fear** (H3372, M01)? The LORD is the **stronghold** (H4581, M19, *maoz*) of my life; of whom shall I be **afraid** (H6342, M01)?" The inner being's fearlessness flows not from the absence of threat but from **what God is to it** — light, salvation, stronghold *(stated)*. And it holds under siege: "Though an army encamp against me, my **heart** (H3820, the seat — M47) shall **not fear**… I will be **confident** (H0982, M19)" (v.3). The heart's steadiness is **trust** (*batach*) *(stated: "my heart shall not fear… I will be confident")* — fear answered by who God is, not by safety (cf. Ps 23:4).

**II. The ONE THING — all desire consolidated into beholding God (v.4).**
"**One thing** have I **asked** (H7592, M21) of the LORD, that will I **seek after** (H1245, M41, *baqash*): that I may **dwell** in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to **gaze** (H2372, *chazah*) upon the **beauty** (H5278, M04, *noam* — delight/pleasantness) of the LORD and to **inquire** in his temple." The distinctive gem of the psalm: the inner being's *many* desires collapse into **one** — not to *get* things from God but to **behold him**, to contemplate his **beauty** *(stated: "one thing… that I may… gaze upon the beauty of the LORD")*. This is the **peak of the face-beholding thread** running through Ps 11:7, 16:11, 17:15, 21:6, 24:6, 26:8: here the longing is named outright and made *singular* — the whole inner life gathered to one point, the contemplation of God's delightfulness *(inferred: "one thing" makes the beholding the consolidation of all wants)*.

**III. The hiding-place matches the longing (vv.5–6).**
"For he will **hide** me in his **shelter** in the day of **trouble** (H7451, M03); he will **conceal** me under the cover of his tent; he will lift me high upon a rock" (v.5). The one who longs to **dwell in God's house** (v.4) is **hidden in God's own shelter** (v.5) — desire and refuge are the same place *(inferred: the house he seeks is the shelter that hides him)*. And the response overflows: "my head shall be **lifted up** above my enemies… I will offer… sacrifices with **shouts of joy**; I will sing and **make melody** (H2167, M42)" (v.6). The hidden inner being **sings above the encircling enemies** *(stated)*.

**IV. The heart's dialogue with God — desire awakened by God's own call (vv.7–8).**
The hinge of the inner-being disclosure: "**Hear** (H8085, M41), O LORD, when I cry… be **gracious** (H2603, M39). You have said, '**Seek** (H1245, M41) my **face**.' My **heart** (H3820, M47) says to you, 'Your **face**, LORD, do I **seek**'" (vv.7–8). A two-way exchange: **God invites** ("Seek my face"), and **the heart answers by echoing God's own words back** ("Your face I seek") *(stated)*. The gem: **the inner being's longing to seek is itself a response to God's invitation** — the heart does not generate the desire from nothing but is **awakened by God's call** and conforms itself to it *(inferred: the heart's "I seek" repeats the LORD's "Seek")*. The face-seeking of the whole cluster here becomes **personal, heart-to-heart** — the inner being in dialogue.

**V. The confident heart still dreads the hidden face (vv.9–10).**
And now the underside of all the confidence surfaces: "**Hide not** your face from me… Cast me not off, **forsake** (H5800) me not, O God of my salvation!" (v.9). The very face the inner being longs to **gaze upon** (v.4) and answers that it **seeks** (v.8) is the face it now **dreads to lose** *(inferred: v.4/v.8 seek the face, v.9 pleads it not be hidden — longing and dread of the same object)*. **Confidence and need coexist** — the psalm refuses to resolve one into the other. Then the deepest belonging: "For my **father** and my **mother** have **forsaken** me, but the LORD will **take me in**" (v.10). The inner being's ultimate belonging is in God **beyond even family** — where the closest human bond fails, God gathers *(stated)*.

**VI. Teachability under threat, and belief as assured seeing (vv.11–13).**
"**Teach** me your way, O LORD, and **lead** me on a level path **because of my enemies**" (v.11) — the guidance-petition (cf. 25:4–5, 12), grounded here in the enemy-watch. "Give me not up to the **will** (H5315, *nephesh* — the desire — M47) of my adversaries; for **false** (H8267, M14) witnesses have risen… and they breathe out violence" (v.12). Then the sustaining conviction: "I **believe** (H0539, M13, *aman*) that I shall **look upon the goodness** of the LORD **in the land of the living**!" (v.13). The gem: the inner being's **faith** (*aman* — the root of *amen*/faithfulness) is **the assurance of future seeing** — "I believe that I shall *see*" — and the seeing is of God's **goodness in this life**, not only beyond it *(stated)*. Belief and beholding join: what the one thing longs to gaze on (v.4), faith is sure it will see (v.13).

**VII. The inner being exhorts its own heart to wait (v.14).**
"**Wait** (H6960, M17, *qavah*) for the LORD; be **strong** (H2388, M23), and let your **heart** (H3820, M47) **take courage** (H0553, M23); wait for the LORD!" The psalm ends with the inner being **addressing itself** — commanding its own **heart** to be strong and to wait, the doubled "wait for the LORD" framing the close *(stated)*. **Waiting is here an act of courage**, not passivity — the self governing the self, summoning its own heart to hold on *(inferred: "be strong… let your heart take courage… wait" is self-address)*. Waiting (the *qavah* thread from Ps 25) becomes the inner being's disciplined stance toward the delay of its one desire.

## What Psalm 27 says about the inner being
- **Fearlessness rests on what God *is* (vv.1–3).** Light, salvation, stronghold — the heart does not fear the encamped army because of *who God is*, not because the threat is gone.
- **All desire can be consolidated into one — beholding God (v.4).** The inner being's supreme, singular longing is not to *get* from God but to *gaze on his beauty*: the peak of the face-beholding thread.
- **The longing to seek is *awakened by God's invitation* (v.8).** "You said, 'Seek my face'; my heart says, 'Your face I seek'" — the heart answers by echoing God's own call; desire is response, not self-origination.
- **Longing and dread attach to the same face (vv.4, 8, 9).** What the inner being most wants to gaze on it most fears to lose; confidence and need coexist unresolved.
- **God is the belonging beyond family (v.10).** Where father and mother forsake, the LORD gathers — the inner being's final belonging is in God.
- **Faith is the assurance of future *seeing* (v.13).** "I believe that I shall look upon the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living" — belief and beholding join.
- **The inner being can command its own heart to wait (v.14).** Self-address: "be strong, let your heart take courage, wait" — waiting as courage, the self governing the self.

## Honest notes
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp at vv.3, 9; bearer=LORD bleed pervasive; backfilled v.10 fragmentary `verse_text`; intensity *all* at v.4) — all per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals* section; not re-detailed here. Readings take bearers/senses from the text.
- **v.8 is a notoriously hard Hebrew line;** the DB text ("You have said, 'Seek my face.' My heart says to you, 'Your face, LORD, do I seek'") is the interpretive base used — the reading follows it and does not resolve the textual crux.
- **`living` (H2416, v.13) tagged M44 (relational)** where elsewhere *life/chay* is M25 — a per-occurrence tag wobble ("land of the **living**"); minor, noted for grain consistency.
- **`chazah` (H2372, "gaze", v.4) and `baqash` (H1245, "seek")** carry the psalm's beholding/seeking weight but *gaze* is gate-2 standalone; the **inner-being act of contemplative gazing** is read from context. Candidate to promote *chazah*-upon-God to a characteristic (beholding).
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *fear/afraid* (H3372/H6342, M01, vv.1,3); *stronghold/confident* (H4581/H0982, M19, vv.1,3); *heart* (H3820, M47, vv.3,8,14); *asked/seek* (H7592/H1245, M21/M41, v.4); *beauty* (H5278, M04, v.4); *make-melody* (H2167, M42, v.6); *hear/cry/gracious* (H8085/H7121/H2603, M41/M37/M39, vv.7); *seek* (H1245, M41, v.8, ×2); *believe* (H0539, M13, v.13); *wait* (H6960, M17, v.14, ×2); *strong/take-courage* (H2388/H0553, M23, v.14).

## Psalm 28 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 28 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 28:1–9 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **The psalm of the dread of divine silence — answered by "he has heard."** Its spine: the inner being **cannot live if God is deaf** ("if you be silent to me, I become like those who go down to the pit," v.1); the whole psalm pivots on being **heard** (v.6, *"he has heard the voice of my pleas"*), and the answered cry issues in a heart that **trusts → is helped → exults** (v.7). Around this run two further disclosures: the wicked whose *lips and heart contradict* (v.3), and the personal rescue that **widens to the whole people** (vv.8–9).
- **Lens (re-framed 2026-07-03):** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`). *Part B re-alignment sweep — Lens bullet added for consistency; this reading was already operation-focused (verified header-by-header). Findings unchanged.*

## The reading

**I. The dread of God's silence — worse than the enemies (v.1).**
"To you, O LORD, I **call** (H7121, M37); my **rock**, be not **deaf** (H2814, M42) to me, lest, if you be **silent** (H2790, M33) to me, I become like those who go down to the **pit**." The inner being's deepest fear here is **not the enemies but God's non-response** *(stated)*. Divine silence is equated with **death** — "if you be silent… I become like those who go down to the pit." **The inner being's life depends on being heard; God's silence is itself a kind of dying** *(inferred: the unanswered cry is set equal to descent to the pit)*. God is named "my **rock**" — the stable ground under the dread *(stated)*.

**II. The lifted hands — the whole self oriented to the holy place (v.2).**
"Hear the voice of my **pleas for mercy** (H8469, M21, *tachanun*)… when I **lift up my hands** toward your most **holy** (H6944, M22) sanctuary." The inner being's plea is **embodied** — hands lifted toward God's dwelling. The whole self (voice, body, longing) **reaches toward the holy place** *(stated)*; the inner cry takes bodily posture.

**III. The wicked whose lips and heart contradict (vv.3–5).**
"Do not drag me off with the **wicked** (H7563, M10)… who speak **peace** (H7965, M33, *shalom*) with their neighbours **while evil** (H7451, M27) is in their **hearts** (H3824, the seat — M47)" (v.3). The gem: the wicked are defined by a **split** — *peace on the lips, evil in the heart* *(stated)*. The **heart is the true content**, and their speech **conceals** rather than reveals it (the "double heart" of Ps 12, inverted). The inner being pleads **not to be grouped with these heart-deceivers** *(inferred: "do not drag me off *with* them" fears the shared verdict)*. And the root of their condition is an inner failure: "Because they do **not regard** (H0995, M15, *bin* — discern/consider) the **works of the LORD**… he will tear them down" (v.5) — their downfall is grounded in a **failure to perceive God's action** *(stated)*; not-regarding is the inward blindness beneath the outward evil (cf. Ps 10:11).

**IV. The pivot — "he has heard" (v.6).**
"**Blessed** (H1288, M39) be the LORD! For he has **heard** (H8085, M41) the voice of my pleas for mercy." The hinge: the **dread of silence** (v.1) is answered by "**he has heard**" *(stated)*. The inner being moves in one verse from fearing the pit to blessing God — and the turn is on **being heard**, the same word Ps 22:24 turned on. **The answered cry is the resolution** *(inferred: v.6 directly reverses v.1's dread)*.

**V. The heart's cycle — trust → helped → exult → thanks (v.7).**
"The LORD is my **strength** (H5797, M23) and my **shield**; in him my **heart** (H3820, M47) **trusts** (H0982, M19), and I am **helped**; my heart **exults** (H5937), and with my song I **give thanks** (H3034, M22)." A compact inner sequence: the heart **trusts** → is **helped** → **exults** → **gives thanks** *(stated)*. The help *follows* the trust ("my heart trusts, **and** I am helped"), and the experienced help *issues* in exultation *(inferred: the order runs trust → help → joy)*. The **heart** is named twice — it is both the *organ of trust* and the *organ of exultation*; the whole cycle from confidence to joy runs through the inner being *(inferred)*.

**VI. The personal strength widens to the people (vv.8–9).**
"The LORD is the **strength** (H5797, M23) of his people… the saving **refuge** (H4581, M19, *maoz*) of his anointed. Oh, **save** your people and **bless** (H1288, M39) your heritage! Be their **shepherd** and **carry** them forever" (vv.8–9). The "**my** strength" of v.7 becomes "the strength of **his people**" (v.8) — the personal rescue **overflows into intercession for the whole community** *(stated)*. The inner being that was heard now prays that the people be shepherded and **carried forever** — its own experience of being upheld enlarged to a prayer for all *(inferred; the shepherd/carry image ties to Ps 23)*.

## What Psalm 28 says about the inner being
- **The inner being cannot live under God's silence (v.1).** Its deepest dread is not the enemy but the unanswered cry — "if you be silent… I become like those who go down to the pit." Being heard is life; silence is a kind of death.
- **The plea is embodied (v.2).** Lifted hands toward the sanctuary — the whole self, body and longing, orients to the holy place.
- **The heart is the true content, and speech can conceal it (v.3).** The wicked "speak peace… while evil is in their hearts" — the inner being's real state may contradict its words; the double heart.
- **The wicked's root is inner non-perception (v.5).** They "do not regard the works of the LORD" — a failure of attention/discernment underlies the outward evil.
- **Everything pivots on "he has heard" (v.6).** The dread of silence is answered; the inner being turns from the pit to blessing in a single verse.
- **The heart's cycle runs trust → helped → exult → thanks (v.7).** Help follows trust and issues in joy; the heart is both the organ of trust and of exultation.
- **The rescue widens (vv.8–9).** "My strength" becomes "the strength of his people"; being upheld overflows into praying the whole flock be carried forever.

## Honest notes
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp at vv.1, 3, 5 — all petition/descriptive, not prohibition; bearer=LORD bleed pervasive) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals* section; not re-detailed.
- **"peace" (H7965, M33, v.3) tagged characteristic** but here it is the wicked's **deceptive outward word** ("speak peace… while evil is in their hearts"), not a genuine inner peace. Read in context as the *concealing speech*, not a disposition — a per-occurrence sense (the same *shalom* is a real inner good elsewhere, so not a stop-list case). Sanity note, not a rule change.
- **`charash` homonyms (vv.1):** "deaf" (H2814) and "silent" (H2790) both carry the be-silent sense with different tags (M42/M33); the reading takes both as God's *non-response*, the object of the dread.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *call* (H7121, M37, v.1); *deaf/silent* (H2814/H2790, M42/M33, v.1 — God's silence, dreaded); *hear/heard* (H8085, M41, vv.2, 6); *pleas* (H8469, M21, vv.2, 6); *holy* (H6944, M22, v.2); *wicked/evil* (H7563/H0205/H7451, M10/M27, vv.3); *hearts* (H3824/H3820, M47, vv.3, 7); *regard/discern* (H0995, M15, v.5); *blessed/bless* (H1288, M39, vv.6, 9); *strength* (H5797, M23, vv.7, 8); *trusts* (H0982, M19, v.7); *give-thanks* (H3034, M22, v.7); *refuge* (H4581, M19, v.8).

## Psalm 29 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 29 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 29:1–11 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (v.6 backfilled). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **A storm theophany — the least introspective psalm of this run.** Its centre (vv.3–9) is a seven-fold hymn to "the voice of the LORD" over the waters, breaking cedars, flashing fire, shaking the wilderness — **overwhelmingly about God, not the inner being.** Read honestly, the psalm discloses the inner being at exactly three points, and they form its **frame**: the summons to **ascribe** glory and strength (vv.1–2), the awed cry "**Glory!**" (v.9), and — the gem — the same overwhelming power that shatters cedars turned into the people's **strength and peace** (v.11). *(Scope note: this reading is deliberately shorter and does not force inner-being content onto the theophany verses; memory `feedback_no_stats_trends_review_fabricated_data`, `feedback_each_chapter_first_principles_find_the_gems`.)*
- **Lens (re-framed 2026-07-03):** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`). *Part B re-alignment sweep — Lens bullet added for consistency; this reading was already operation-focused (verified header-by-header). Findings unchanged.*

## The reading

**I. Worship as *ascribing* — the creature's response to glory (vv.1–2).**
"**Ascribe** (H3051, *yahav* — give) to the LORD, O heavenly beings, ascribe to the LORD **glory** (H3519, M22) and **strength** (H5797, M23)… **worship** the LORD in the **splendour** (H1927, M22) of **holiness** (H6944, M22)" (vv.1–2). The proper posture of the inner being before overwhelming power is **worship — to *ascribe / give* glory** *(stated)*. The gem is that one cannot *add* to God's glory; to *ascribe* is to **acknowledge and render** what is already his — worship is **recognition and self-abasement**, not contribution *(inferred: yahav renders to God what is his, it does not augment him)*. And it is worship "in the splendour of holiness" — the inner being bows before **beauty as well as power** *(stated)*.

**II. The theophany — and the inner being as *hearer* who can only cry "Glory!" (vv.3–9).**
Seven times "the voice of the LORD" (*qol YHWH*) rolls through the psalm — over the waters, breaking the cedars, flashing flames of fire, shaking the wilderness (vv.3–9). These verses are **God's action, not the inner being's** *(honest note: the reading does not allegorise them)*. But the theophany has one human hinge: "and in his temple **all cry, 'Glory!'** (H3519, M22)" (v.9). The gem: the **only inner response the storm evokes is a single word** — *Glory!* The contemplation of God's overwhelming power **reduces the inner being to worship** — it cannot analyse or answer, only exclaim *(inferred: the cry is the sole response amid the theophany)*. This is Ps 8's movement in another key — majesty contemplated sizes the inner being rightly, and the awed heart's whole speech becomes praise *(inferred)*. And it **echoes the summons**: what vv.1–2 commanded (ascribe *glory*) the temple now spontaneously does (cries *Glory*) — the imperative has become the heart's own cry *(inferred)*.

**III. The gem — overwhelming power becomes the inner being's strength and peace (vv.10–11).**
"The LORD sits **enthroned** over the flood; the LORD sits enthroned as **king forever**. May the LORD **give** (H5414, M12) **strength** (H5797, M23) to his people! May the LORD **bless** (H1288, M39) his people with **peace** (H7965, M33, *shalom*)!" (vv.10–11). Here the psalm turns the storm **inward**. The same **strength** (*oz*) the worshippers were told to *ascribe* to God (v.1) God now **gives** to his people (v.11) — an **inclusio on strength**: ascribed in v.1, granted in v.11 *(stated)*. And the God whose voice **shatters cedars and shakes the wilderness** (vv.5, 8) **blesses his people with *peace*** *(stated)*. The gem: **the terrifying power resolves not in terror but in shalom** — the storm outside becomes **peace inside**; the inner being contemplates the overwhelming voice and receives, not dread, but **strength and settled peace** *(inferred: the theophany's payoff for the people is strength + peace, not fear)*. The God enthroned over the flood is the God who steadies the heart.

## What Psalm 29 says about the inner being
- **Before overwhelming power, the inner being's posture is worship-as-ascription (vv.1–2).** To *ascribe* glory is to acknowledge and render what is already God's — recognition and self-abasement, not contribution — and it bows before *beauty* ("splendour of holiness") as much as power.
- **Contemplation of majesty reduces the inner being to a single cry — "Glory!" (v.9).** The awed heart cannot analyse the storm, only exclaim; the imperative to *ascribe glory* (v.1) becomes the temple's spontaneous cry of *Glory* (v.9). (Ps 8's right self-sizing, in the storm's key.)
- **The overwhelming power resolves into the inner being's strength and peace (vv.10–11).** The same *strength* ascribed to God is *given* to his people (inclusio); the voice that shatters cedars blesses with *shalom*. The storm outside becomes peace inside — majesty contemplated ends not in terror but in a steadied heart.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** vv.3–9 are theophany — God's action on creation, not inner-being disclosure. They are read as the *object* the inner being contemplates (yielding the cry "Glory!"), not mined for inner content they do not carry. The psalm's genuine inner-being weight is its frame (vv.1–2, 9, 11).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed on nearly every span — appropriate-ish here since the LORD *is* the subject of the theophany, but still heuristic; intensity *many*/*all* at vv.3, 9; v.6 backfilled fragmentary `verse_text`) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **`worship` (shachah, v.2)** not surfaced as its own span (splendour/holiness tagged as its qualifiers); read from the text as the inner being's bowing.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *glory* (H3519, M22, vv.1,2,3,9); *strength* (H5797, M23, vv.1,11); *splendour/holiness* (H1927/H6944, M22, v.2); *powerful/majesty* (H3581/H1926, M23/M22, v.4); *give* (H5414, M12, v.11); *bless* (H1288, M39, v.11); *peace* (H7965, M33, v.11). Note the storm-verbs (thunders/breaks/shakes/flashes) are gate-2 standalone (God's action) — correctly *not* inner-being characteristics.

## Psalm 30 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 30 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 30:1–12 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (v.2 backfilled). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **The thanksgiving of the humbled heart.** A rescue-from-death psalm whose inner-being spine is a **confession of presumption**: the self grew complacent in ease ("I said… 'I shall never be moved'"), God **hid his face**, and the false security collapsed into **dismay** — until "you have turned my mourning into dancing." Its own key is the lesson the inner being learns: **its stability was never its own but God's favour.** The distinctive counter-note to the wider cluster: the "not moved" that was a *gift* in Ps 16:8 and 21:7 here becomes *presumption* (30:6) when the self claims it — and is exposed by the hidden face.
- **Lens (re-framed 2026-07-03):** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`). *Part B re-alignment sweep — Lens bullet added for consistency; this reading was already operation-focused (verified header-by-header). Findings unchanged.*

## The reading

**I. The soul drawn up from the pit (vv.1–3).**
"I will **extol** you, O LORD, for you have **drawn me up** (H1802, *dalah* — hauled up, as a bucket from a well)… you have brought up my **soul** (H5315, the seat — M47) from Sheol; you **restored me to life** (H2421, M25) from among those who go down to the pit" (vv.1–3). The inner being (the *soul*) is **hauled up from the depths** like water from a well — the rescue reaches the deepest, most helpless place *(stated; the dalah image gives it)*. The soul at the edge of death is lifted back to life *(stated)*.

**II. The proportion that consoles the inner being — a moment vs a lifetime, night vs morning (vv.4–5).**
"For his **anger** is but for a **moment**, and his **favour** (H7522, M29, *ratson*) is for a **lifetime**. **Weeping** (H1065, M03) may tarry for the **night**, but **joy** (H7440, M42) comes with the **morning**" (v.5). The great inner-being consolation: a **disproportion** the inner being learns to read by — God's anger measured in *moments*, his favour in *lifetimes*; grief is a **night-lodger** that gives way to morning joy *(stated)*. The inner being is taught to see its sorrow as **temporary and framed** — lodging for a night, not a permanent resident *(inferred: "tarry for the night… comes with the morning" makes weeping the transient guest)*.

**III. The confession of presumption — "I shall never be moved" (vv.6–7).**
The psalm's turn inward: "As for me, I said in my **prosperity** (*shalvah* — ease), 'I shall **never be moved** (H4131)'" (v.6). In ease the inner being grew **complacent and presumptuous** — and the very phrase "not moved," which is the *gift* of grounded trust elsewhere (Ps 16:8, 21:7), here is **self-attributed security** *(inferred: the same bal-yimmot, now claimed by the self in prosperity)*. Then the exposure: "By your **favour** (H7522, M29) you made my mountain stand strong; you **hid your face**; I was **dismayed** (H0926, M01 — *terrified*)" (v.7). The gem: the inner being **mistook God's gift for its own stability** — the mountain stood *by God's favour*, not by the self — and the **withdrawal of God's face collapsed the false security into terror** *(stated: "you hid your face; I was dismayed")*. The hidden face (the dread of Ps 27:9) here does **disciplinary** work — it teaches the presumptuous heart that its standing was always God's, never its own *(inferred)*.

**IV. The argument from the grave — life is *for* praise (vv.8–10).**
"To you, O LORD, I **cry** (H7121, M37)… 'What profit is there in my death…? Will the **dust** praise (H3034, M22) you? Will it tell of your **faithfulness** (H0571, M13)?… Hear (H8085, M41), O LORD… be my helper!'" (vv.8–10). The inner being pleads for its life on the ground of **praise** — dead dust cannot praise or testify, so *let me live to do it* *(stated)*. The distinctive inner-being logic: **the reason to want life is to praise God** — the self values its own continuance as a *voice for God's faithfulness* *(inferred: the argument makes praise the point of living)*.

**V. Mourning into dancing — the self restored *for* praise (vv.11–12).**
"You have **turned** for me my **mourning** (H4553, M03) into **dancing**; you have loosed my sackcloth and clothed me with **gladness** (H8057, M04), that my **glory** (H3519, M22 — *kevodi*, the inner self/soul) may **sing** (H2167, M42) your praise and **not be silent** (H1826, M33). O LORD my God, I will **give thanks** (H3034, M22) to you forever!" (vv.11–12). The reversal is total — mourning→dancing, sackcloth→gladness *(stated)*. And the **purpose clause** completes the argument of v.9: "**that my glory may sing… and not be silent**." "My glory" (*kevodi*) is the **inner self** — the honoured, God-facing part of the person — and the whole deliverance is **for this end: that the inner being may praise and not fall silent** *(stated: the purpose of the rescue is that the glory sing)*. The dust that could not praise (v.9) becomes the restored self that vows **never to be silent** *(inferred: v.9's silent dust answered by v.12's unsilent glory)*.

## What Psalm 30 says about the inner being
- **The soul can be hauled up from the deepest place (vv.1–3).** *Dalah* — the inner being drawn up from Sheol like a bucket from a well; the rescue reaches death's edge.
- **Grief is framed as a night-lodger (v.5).** The inner being learns the proportion — anger a moment, favour a lifetime; weeping tarries the night, joy comes in the morning. Sorrow is temporary and bounded.
- **"Not moved" is a gift, not a possession — and presumption forgets this (vv.6–7).** In ease the inner being claimed its own stability; the hidden face exposed that the mountain stood by God's favour. The same phrase that is trust-grounded elsewhere (16:8, 21:7) here is complacency, corrected by discipline.
- **The hidden face does disciplinary work (v.7).** God's withdrawal collapses false security into dismay — teaching the inner being its dependence.
- **Life is *for* praise (vv.9, 12).** The inner being argues for its own continuance as a voice for God's faithfulness ("will the dust praise you?"), and the deliverance's stated purpose is "that my glory may sing… and not be silent."
- **Restoration reverses the whole inner state (v.11).** Mourning→dancing, sackcloth→gladness — and the restored self vows never to fall silent in praise.

## Honest notes
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp at v.12 "not be silent" — purpose/descriptive; bearer=LORD bleed pervasive; v.2 backfilled fragmentary `verse_text`) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **"my glory" (kevodi, H3519, v.12)** is tagged M22 (glory cluster) but functions here as **the inner self / soul** (the praising faculty), not divine glory — a per-occurrence sense worth marking (the same lemma is God's *glory* elsewhere in this very run, e.g. Ps 29). Sanity note.
- **"not moved" (H4131, v.6)** left gate-2 standalone; read as the inner being's *presumptuous security claim* — the reading supplies the disposition from context (contrast the trust-grounded "not moved" of 16:8, 21:7). Candidate cross-reference for the "not moved" thread.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *soul* (H5315, M47, v.3); *restored-to-life/lifetime* (H2421/H2416, M25, vv.3,5); *sing* (H2167, M42, vv.4,12); *saints* (H2623, M05, v.4); *give-thanks/praise* (H3034, M22, vv.4,9,12); *favour* (H7522, M29, vv.5,7); *weeping/mourning* (H1065/H4553, M03, vv.5,11); *joy/gladness* (H7440/H8057, M42/M04, vv.5,11); *dismayed* (H0926, M01, v.7 — the hidden-face terror); *cry* (H7121, M37, v.8); *plead/merciful* (H2603, M39, vv.8,10); *hear* (H8085, M41, v.10); *glory* (H3519, M22, v.12 — the inner self); *silent* (H1826, M33, v.12, negated).

## Psalm 31 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 31 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 31:1–24 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **The psalm of entrustment.** A long lament-to-trust that oscillates between the depths (social death, whole-person wasting, "terror on every side") and renewed trust — held together by its signature act: **"Into your hand I commit my spirit" (v.5), "My times are in your hand" (v.15).** The inner being **deposits itself and its whole life-span into God's hand** rather than the enemy's. Its two peaks are that **entrustment** and the **panic-verdict overturned** — "I had said in my alarm, 'I am cut off from your sight.' But you heard" (v.22). Across it, the inner being is named by all three of its seats — **spirit** (v.5), **soul** (vv.7, 9), **heart** (v.24).
- **Lens (re-framed 2026-07-03):** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`). *Part B re-alignment sweep; already operation-focused (entrustment; trust at the lowest point). Aheb-fix substrate now applied — the v.23 "Love the LORD" mis-tag flagged below is **RESOLVED** (H0157 now tags characteristic). Findings unchanged.*

## The reading

**I. Entrustment — the spirit committed into God's hand (vv.1–5).**
"In you, O LORD, do I **take refuge** (H2620, M19)… Be a **rock** (H4581, M19) of refuge for me… **Into your hand I commit** (*paqad* — deposit for safekeeping) my **spirit** (H7307, the seat — *ruach*); you have **redeemed** (H6299, M38) me, O LORD, **faithful** (H0571, M13) God" (vv.1–5). The peak inner-being act: the innermost self (*ruach*) is **entrusted into God's hand as one deposits a treasure for safekeeping** *(stated; paqad is the entrusting word)*. And it rests not on the self's strength but on God's proven character — "you *have redeemed* me, faithful God" — the entrustment leans on **God's faithfulness already shown** *(stated)*.

**II. Trust against idols; the joy of being *seen and known* (vv.6–8).**
"I **hate** (H8130, M06) those who pay regard to worthless idols, but I **trust** (H0982, M19) in the LORD. I will **rejoice** (H1523, M04) and be **glad** (H8055, M04) in your **steadfast love** (H2617, M05), **because you have seen my affliction; you have known** (*yada*) the **distress** (H6869, M03) of my **soul** (H5315, M47)" (vv.6–7). The gem: the inner being's joy is grounded in **being seen and known** — "you have *known the distress of my soul*" *(stated)*. God's **intimate knowledge of the inner being's straits** is itself the reason for gladness (the God-sees thread, Ps 10:14) — *because* God has seen and known, the soul can rejoice *(inferred: the "because" makes being-known the ground of the joy)*.

**III. The whole-person wasting and the social death (vv.9–13).**
Then the plunge. "my **eye** is wasted from **grief** (H3708, M02, *kaas*); my **soul** (H5315, M47) and my **body**… my **life** (H2416, M25) is spent with **sorrow** (H3015, M03)… my **strength** (H3581, M23) **fails because of my iniquity** (H5771, M10); my bones waste" (vv.9–10). The inner being dissolves **whole** — eye, soul, body, strength, bones — and, tellingly, it **implicates itself**: the strength fails "because of my *iniquity*," not only from outward affliction *(stated: the wasting is tied to the self's own guilt)*. Then social annihilation: "I have become a **reproach** (H2781, M06)… an object of **dread** (H6343, M01) to my acquaintances; those who see me flee. I have been **forgotten** like one who is dead; like a **broken vessel** (v.12). For I hear the whispering of many — **terror** (H4032, M01) on every side!" (vv.11–13). The gem: the inner being's experience of being **reduced to a discarded thing** — dreaded, shunned, *forgotten as if dead*, a **broken/useless vessel** *(stated)*. This is the pain of the self erased from others' regard.

**IV. The pivot — "But I trust… You are my God"; my times in your hand (vv.14–16).**
Against all of it: "**But I trust** (H0982, M19) in you, O LORD; I **say**, 'You are my God.' My **times** are in your **hand**" (vv.14–15). The emphatic turn — trust declared **at the lowest point**, and made personal ("You are my God") *(stated)*. And the entrustment of v.5 widens: not only the *spirit* but the **times** — the whole course and moments of the life — are placed **in God's hand** *(stated)*. The **two hands** frame the psalm: the inner being commits itself and its times to *God's* hand (vv.5, 15) and pleads rescue from the *enemy's* hand (vv.8, 15) — **security is a matter of *whose hand* holds the self** *(inferred: the same "hand" motif opposes God's keeping to the enemy's grip)*. Then the counter to every hidden face: "Make your **face shine** on your servant; save me in your steadfast love" (v.16) — the plea for God's **lit** face (the inner-light thread, Ps 13:3, 18:28) *(stated)*.

**V. Goodness stored up; the inner being hidden in God's presence (vv.19–20).**
"How **abundant** is your **goodness**, which you have **stored up** (*tsaphan* — treasured/hidden) for those who **fear** (H3373, M01) you… In the cover of your **presence** you **hide** them from the plots of men; you store them in your **shelter** from the **strife** (H7379, M02) of tongues" (vv.19–20). Two gems. God's goodness is **treasured up in reserve** for the God-fearers — a laid-up store, not just present help *(stated)*. And the inner being is **hidden *in* God's presence** — sheltered "from the strife of tongues" not by the enemies' absence but by being **concealed in God's own presence** *(stated; the presence is the hiding-place, cf. Ps 27:5)*.

**VI. The panic-verdict overturned — "I am cut off" / "but you heard" (vv.21–22).**
"Blessed be the LORD, for he has **wondrously** (H6381, M04) shown his **steadfast love** (H2617, M05)… I had **said in my alarm** (*chaphaz* — panic), 'I am **cut off** from your sight.' **But you heard** (H8085, M41) the voice of my **pleas** (H8469, M21)" (vv.21–22). The gem: the inner being's **panic-driven verdict** — "I am cut off from your eyes" — is **a false read**, corrected by the reality "**but you heard**" *(stated)*. In alarm the self **hastily concludes God has abandoned it**, and that conclusion is overturned *(inferred: the "but" reverses the panic-verdict)*. Like Ps 30:6's presumption, this is a **fear-distorted misjudgement of God** — here the misjudgement is despair rather than complacency, and it too is answered by God's hearing (the "he has heard" turn of Ps 22:24, 28:6).

**VII. The closing exhortation — be strong, take courage, wait (vv.23–24).**
"**Love** (H0157, *aheb*) the LORD, all you his **saints** (H2623, M05)!… Be **strong** (H2388, M23), and let your **heart** (H3824, the seat — M47) **take courage** (H0553, M23), all you who **wait** (H3176, M18, *yachal*) for the LORD!" (vv.23–24). The inner being turns outward, **calling the community to the same postures it has learned** — to love, to be strong, to let the heart take courage, and to **wait** *(stated)*. As in Ps 27:14, the psalm ends with the self exhorting others' hearts to courage and waiting *(inferred: the self-address of 27:14 here becomes address to all the saints)*.

## What Psalm 31 says about the inner being
- **The inner being can *entrust itself* into God's hand (vv.5, 15).** "Into your hand I commit my spirit… my times are in your hand" — the innermost self and the whole life-span deposited with God for safekeeping, resting on his proven faithfulness. Security is a matter of *whose hand* holds the self — God's, not the enemy's.
- **Being *seen and known* is the ground of joy (v.7).** "You have known the distress of my soul" — the inner being rejoices *because* God intimately knows its straits.
- **Distress dissolves the whole person, and the self implicates itself (vv.9–10).** Eye, soul, body, strength, bones waste — and "my strength fails *because of my iniquity*": the wasting is not only from without.
- **The self can be reduced to a discarded thing (vv.11–12).** Reproach, an object of dread, forgotten as if dead, a broken vessel — the pain of erasure from others' regard.
- **Trust is declared at the lowest point (v.14).** "But I trust in you… You are my God" — the pivot against all the evidence of the depths.
- **The inner being is hidden *in* God's presence (v.20).** Sheltered from the strife of tongues not by the enemies' removal but by concealment in God's own presence; his goodness is treasured up in reserve.
- **Panic produces false verdicts about God — corrected by his hearing (v.22).** "I am cut off from your sight" is the alarm's misjudgement; "but you heard" overturns it (as complacency was overturned in Ps 30).
- **The inner being names itself by all three seats — spirit, soul, heart (vv.5, 7, 24)** — and, having learned to wait, calls others' hearts to strength and courage.

## Honest notes
- **SANITY-CHECK CATCH (repeat) — "love" (H0157, *aheb*, v.23) — ✓ RESOLVED (2026-07-03).** As at Ps 26:8, "**Love** the LORD" is a genuine inner-being characteristic (the commanded affection). The **aheb re-run** (PROMOTE_CHARACTERISTIC = {H0157}, Part A of the re-alignment sweep) has corrected the substrate: v.23 "Love" now tags `role=characteristic`. The reading anticipated the fix; substrate and reading now agree.
- **Three seat-terms in one psalm:** *ruach* (spirit, v.5, seat=spirit), *nephesh* (soul, vv.7, 9, seat=soul), *lebab* (heart, v.24, seat=heart) — the lexical captured all three seats; worth noting the inner being is addressed under each.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp at vv.1, 8, 17 — petition/descriptive; bearer=LORD bleed pervasive; intensity *all/very/many*) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **v.17 "go" (H1826, *damam*, M33)** = "let them go *silently* to Sheol" — the wicked *silenced* (external pole/imprecation, vv.17–18); read as the counter to the psalmist's own vow of praise, not inner-being disclosure of the self.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *take-refuge/rock/refuge* (H2620/H4581, M19, vv.1,2,4,19); *put-to-shame* (H0954, M07, vv.1,17); *redeemed* (H6299, M38, v.5); *faithful* (H0571/H0529, M13, vv.5,23); *hate* (H8130, M06, v.6); *trust* (H0982, M19, vv.6,14); *rejoice/glad* (H1523/H8055, M04, v.7); *steadfast-love* (H2617, M05, vv.7,16,21); *affliction/distress/sorrow/sighing* (H6040/H6869/H3015/H0585, M24/M03, vv.7,9,10); *soul* (H5315, M47, vv.7,9); *grief/strife* (H3708/H7379, M02, vv.9,20); *strength* (H3581, M23, v.10); *reproach/contempt* (H2781/H0937, M06, vv.11,18); *dread/terror/fear* (H6343/H4032/H3373, M01, vv.11,13,19); *flee/wait* (H5074/H3176, M18, vv.11,24); *lying* (H8267, M14, v.18); *righteous* (H6662, M26, v.18); *pride* (H1346, M08, vv.18,23); *heard/pleas* (H8085/H8469, M41/M21, v.22); *blessed/wondrously* (H1288/H6381, M39/M04, v.21); *saints* (H2623, M05, v.23); *strong/take-courage* (H2388/H0553, M23, v.24); *heart* (H3824, M47, v.24).

## Psalm 11 - inner-being reading

# Psalm 11 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 11:1–7 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens (re-framed 2026-07-03):** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`). §II–III describe *God's* discriminating inner life (arena); the human findings are trust-that-stays-put, the self steadied by being watched, and the telos of beholding God's face. *Part B re-alignment sweep. Aheb-fix substrate now applied: v.5 "one who **loves** violence" (H0157) tags characteristic — the wicked's **misdirected affection** (love aimed at violence, cf. Ps 4:2 "love vanity"), a human inner-being datum; v.7 "he **loves** righteous deeds" is God's love (arena). Findings otherwise unchanged.*
- **A short psalm of steadfast trust under the counsel of fear.** Its own key is **sight**: it moves from *"flee to your mountain"* (v.1) to *"the upright shall behold his face"* (v.7) — and the hinge between them is that **God sees and tests** from his throne.

## The reading
Psalm 11 begins by refusing an argument — and the refusal is the whole psalm.

**I. The refusal to flee (vv.1–3).**
"In the LORD I **take refuge** (H2620, M19); how can you say to my **soul** (H5315, the seat — M47), 'Flee like a bird to your mountain'?" (v.1). Against the psalmist stands a counsel of **panic**: the wicked shoot "in the **dark**" at the **upright** in **heart** (H3820, M47) (v.2), and the despairing question, "if the **foundations** are destroyed, what can the **righteous** (H6662, M26) do?" (v.3). The inner being's first act is to **decline the flight**: trust that refuses the mountain because its refuge is a Person, not a place *(inferred: 'how can you say' rejects the advice as a category error)*.

**II. The answer — God sees and tests from his throne (vv.4–5).**
The reply to despair is not a plan but a **gaze**: "The LORD is in his **holy** temple; the LORD's throne is in heaven; his **eyes see**, his eyelids **test** the children of man" (v.4). And the test discriminates: "the LORD **tests** the **righteous**, but his **soul** (H5315, M47) **hates** (H8130, M06) the wicked and the one who loves **violence**" (v.5). Two divine postures on one throne — the righteous **tested** (proved, not condemned), the violent **hated** — and remarkably, it is God's own *soul* that hates cruelty: the divine inner life is **morally engaged**, not neutral *(stated: his soul hates)*.

**III. The vision of the upright (vv.6–7).**
Judgment falls on the wicked as their "portion" and "cup" (v.6), but the psalm's last word is intimacy: "For the LORD is **righteous** (H6666, M26); he **loves** righteous deeds; the **upright** (H3477, M13) shall **behold his face**" (v.7). The reward of the one who refused to flee is to **see God** — the face turned toward him *(stated: the upright shall behold his face)*.

## What Psalm 11 says about the inner being
- **Trust can mean staying put.** The tempting inner move under threat is *flight* (v.1) and *despair* (v.3); faith's answer is to refuse both — not because the danger is unreal, but because the refuge is God, whom no mountain can better. Steadfastness is trust contradicting the survival instinct.
- **The cure for despair is God's attentiveness, not human action.** To "what can the righteous do?" (v.3) the psalm answers not with a strategy but with *God's seeing eyes* (v.4) — the inner being is steadied by being *watched over*, not by its own remedy. (This joins Ps 7:9, 10:14 — the "God sees" thread.)
- **The divine inner life discriminates** (v.5): God *tests* the righteous (to prove) and his *soul hates* the violent (to oppose) — two postures, so that being tested is not the same as being rejected. The trials of the righteous are assay, not abandonment.
- **The telos of the inner being is to behold God's face** (v.7): the psalm runs on sight — the wicked shoot *unseen from the dark* (v.2), God's eyes *see and test* (v.4), and the upright at last *see his face*. The reward of trust is vision.

## Honest notes
- **Recurring reclassification — "holy of place":** *holy* (H6944, v4 "his holy temple") is an attribute of the temple → standalone (not a human inner state); handled at sanity-check (Ps 2/3/5/11).
- **Characteristics** (sanity-checked): *take-refuge* (M19); *upright*/*righteous* (M13/M26); God's discriminating inner life — *hates* (M06, his soul's), with *soul* (M47) as its seat; *scorching* (M02) the wicked's portion. *test* (H0974, God's assay) sits gate-2 but is thematically central.
- **Note:** *hates* (H8130, v5) is **God's** moral hatred of violence (a divine inner posture), distinct from the enemies' hatred elsewhere — kept as characteristic here.
- **Residuals:** bearer=LORD bleed (D11-flagged); manner/coupling over-weld.

## Proverbs 1 - inner-being unit synthesis

# Proverbs 1 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Pro 1:1–33, read **per segmentation unit** (`segment_unit`, provenance `proverbs-segmentation-v1-20260703`). Complete chapter (3 vv. backfilled). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**; wisdom/God-relation is the arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Method (unit meaning-synthesis):** each unit is read for its inner-being meaning, and that reading **reads back and validates the Phase-1 lexical** — checking the roles, the **pairs** (bearer / manner / coupling) and flags for sensibility, and **isolating hidden or less-obvious characteristics** the provisional segmentation did not name. Validation catches (bearer=LORD bleed; prohibition over-stamp) are logged per unit, not re-derived.

---

## PRO-01-A · Prov 1:1–6 · [D, multi] — the formation of the inner being (wisdom's aims)

**The reading.** The book opens not with a command but with a *list of what wisdom builds in a person* — "to **know** wisdom… to **understand** words of insight… to **receive** instruction… to give **prudence** to the simple, **knowledge** and **discretion** to the youth" (vv.2–4). The finding is the **inner faculties wisdom is meant to form**: knowing, understanding, prudence, discretion, and the disposition to *receive* instruction *(stated: these are the stated aims)*. The operation the unit foregrounds is **receptivity that grows** — "let the wise **hear** and **increase** in learning" (v.5): even the already-wise are defined by a *continuing intake*, a self that keeps taking in *(inferred: the aims are not a fixed state but a faculty-set held open to increase)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** Sound. The lexical correctly tags *know, understand, insight, wise-dealing, prudence, knowledge, wise, hear, guidance* as **characteristics** — the faculty-cluster the reading rests on. One **pair-sensibility note:** *simple* (H6612, v.4) is tagged `process-qualifier` welding *give* (manner/coupling pair `simple→give`); it is really the **recipient/target** of "give prudence *to* the simple," not a manner — a minor role-slippage (recipient read as manner). It does not affect the reading (the simple is still the one being formed). The genre/superscription terms of v.1 (*proverbs, Solomon, David, king, Israel*) correctly sit `standalone`.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** (1) **Receptivity-as-increase** (v.5) — distinct from mere "reception"; the wise self *keeps growing*, a hidden characteristic under the "aims." (2) The **transmission of the inner life** — wisdom is aimed *from* teacher *to* the simple/youth (vv.4–5); formation is relational, handed on, not self-generated.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *formation/faculties of the inner being* (new to the corpus — Proverbs' distinctive); *receptivity / teachability* (shared w/ Ps); *the transmission of wisdom* (new).

---

## PRO-01-B · Prov 1:7 · [S] — the fear of the LORD as the beginning/root

**The reading.** The single most load-bearing line in the book, given its own unit by weight: "The **fear** of the LORD is the **beginning** of knowledge; fools despise wisdom and instruction." The finding: the inner being's **foundational orientation is reverent fear** — knowledge does not *start* with intellect but with awe *(stated)*. The operation: fear is the *root from which the whole faculty-cluster of PRO-01-A grows* — and its refusal ("fools **despise**") is the inner posture that forfeits it *(inferred: the motto grounds vv.2–6 in a prior disposition; cf. 9:10, and bookended by 31:30)*. This is the same cornerstone as Ps 111:10, here at the head of Proverbs.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** The key term *fear* (H3374) is correctly a **characteristic**. But this verse is a clear case of the **bearer=LORD bleed** — the nearest-proper heuristic wrongly stamps `bearer=Lord` on *beginning, knowledge, fools, despise, wisdom, instruction* (pairs `H3068→…`). Read straight from the lexical, it would say *the LORD despises wisdom* — plainly wrong: it is the **fools** who despise. The reading takes the bearers from the text, not the tags (the fools despise; the fear is the person's). A flagged residual, not a defect in the reading.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** The verse holds a **paired opposition** the segmentation named as one characteristic but which is really two: *reverent fear* (the root) **and** *the despising of wisdom* (its refusal) — the fool's contempt is a distinct inner-being operation (the closed, scornful self), worth its own thread across the book (scoffer/fool).

**Characteristics surfaced:** *the fear of the LORD (as root)* (shared cornerstone w/ Ps 111:10); *the despising/scorning of wisdom* (new thread — the scoffer's closed heart).

---

## PRO-01-C · Prov 1:8–19 · [D, multi] — filial receptivity; the self-destructive greedy heart

**The reading.** Two inner-being movements held together. First, **filial receptivity**: "**Hear**, my son, your father's instruction, and **forsake not** your mother's teaching" (v.8) — the self that *takes in* the handed-down word, worn like a garland (v.9) *(stated)*. Second, and the unit's gem, the **self-destructive greedy heart**: the enticers say "let us **lie in wait** for blood… we shall **fill our houses** with plunder" (vv.11–13), but the trap they set closes on *themselves* — "these men **lie in wait for their own blood**; they set an ambush for their **own lives**" (v.18). The operation: **greed recoils on the greedy** — "such are the ways of everyone who is **greedy for unjust gain**; it takes away the **life** of its possessors" (v.19); the appetite for plunder is *self-consuming* *(inferred: the "own blood/own lives" turns the ambush self-ward — the greedy heart digs its own pit; cf. Ps 7:15–16, 9:15)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** The characteristics carrying the reading — *hear* (v.8, receptivity), *graceful* (v.9) — are correctly tagged. **Prohibition over-stamp** on v.8: the negation "forsake **not**" wrongly stamps `prohibition=forbidden` onto *father's, instruction, forsake, mother's, teaching* — the whole clause, not the verb; a known neg-particle bleed (the line is an *appeal*, not a legal prohibition). The greed-recoil of vv.17–19 sits largely in gate-2 content (*ambush, plunder, blood, life*); the reading is read from the structure (own-blood/own-lives), correctly.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** The **greed-that-self-destructs** is the deeper find — not "greed" as a label but the *mechanism* by which the acquisitive inner being **becomes its own victim** (the appetite consuming its owner). This is a Proverbs sharpening of a Psalter theme (the pit-digger caught in his own pit) and belongs to a cross-book thread on **self-inflicted ruin**.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *filial receptivity* (shared); *the self-destructive greedy heart / appetite that consumes its owner* (new — sharper than anything in Ps); *self-inflicted ruin (the pit-digger)* (shared w/ Ps 7/9).

---

## PRO-01-D · Prov 1:20–33 · [D, multi] — the refusal of wisdom; the security of the one who listens

**The reading.** Wisdom personified cries in the street, and the unit anatomises the **inner being that refuses her**: "How long, O **simple** ones, will you **love** being simple? How long will **scoffers delight** in their scoffing and **fools hate knowledge**?" (v.22). Three refusing dispositions are named as *loves and delights* — the self that **loves its own simplicity**, **delights in scoffing**, **hates knowledge** *(stated)*: refusal is not neutral ignorance but an *affection for un-wisdom*. Its end is the terrible reciprocity of vv.24–31 — "because you **ignored all my counsel**… I will not answer when you call" — and the un-answerable regret of a self that would not listen when it could. Against it stands the unit's resolution: "whoever **listens** to me will **dwell secure** and will be **at ease, without dread** of disaster" (v.33) — the **inner security of the receptive self** *(inferred: the listening heart's reward is not information but *rest without dread*, the same fearless security as Ps 112:7, 3:24)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *love* (H0157, *aheb*, v.22 — "love being simple") is correctly a **characteristic** under the aheb-fix (PROMOTE_CHARACTERISTIC) — the *misdirected affection* toward simplicity, exactly parallel to Ps 4:2 "love vanity." *delight* and *hate* (v.22) likewise carry the refusing dispositions. The bearer/prohibition residuals recur (the "will not" of vv.24–28); the reading leans on the text. Pairs are sensible here.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** (1) **Refusal as *affection*** — the aheb-fix makes visible that the simple *love* their simplicity; un-wisdom is *desired*, not merely defaulted-to (a hidden characteristic the provisional "refusal of wisdom" flattened). (2) **The un-answerable regret** (vv.28–31) — a distinct inner state: the self that *finds no answer* because it refused to listen when answered (the mirror of the "he has heard" pivot in the Psalms — here, "I will not answer").

**Characteristics surfaced:** *the refusal of wisdom as misdirected affection (loving simplicity)* (new — surfaced by the aheb-fix); *the scoffer's delight / the closed scornful heart* (new thread); *the inner security of the listening self ("dwell secure, without dread")* (shared w/ Ps 112:7, 3:24).

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Validation summary:** Phase-1 substrate is sound for reading; two systemic residuals recur exactly as in the Psalter — **bearer=LORD bleed** (acute at v.7) and **prohibition over-stamp** on negated appeals (v.8, vv.24–28). One **pair note**: recipient-read-as-manner at v.4 (*simple*→*give*). None touch the readings' spine; all are candidates for the same rule-adjustments flagged in the Psalms run.
- **New characteristics this chapter (for the fork-b control table):** *formation/faculties of the inner being*; *the transmission of wisdom*; *the despising/scorning of wisdom (the scoffer's closed heart)*; *the self-destructive greedy heart (appetite consuming its owner)*; *refusal of wisdom as misdirected affection*. **Shared with the Psalter:** *fear of the LORD (root)*; *receptivity/teachability*; *self-inflicted ruin*; *the inner security of the listening/trusting self*.

---

## Proverbs 2 - inner-being unit synthesis

# Proverbs 2 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals (v1.1, construct-`specifier` + positional-`target` enriched) for Pro 2:1–22, read per `segment_unit`. Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**; wisdom/God is the arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Method:** unit reading + lexical read-back/validation (now with specifier/target pairs) + hidden-characteristic isolation + characteristics-surfaced.

---

## PRO-02-A · Prov 2:1–11 · [D, multi] — the seeking of wisdom; reception that reshapes the heart

**The reading.** One long conditional: *if* the self does something, *then* something happens *to* it. The condition is a fivefold **active seeking** — "**receive** my words… **making your ear attentive**… **inclining your heart**… **call out** for insight… **seek** it like **silver** and **search** for it as for hidden treasures" (vv.1–4). The finding: understanding is not passively received but **strenuously sought** — the self *inclines its own heart* (an act of the will) and *digs* for wisdom as for buried treasure *(stated)*. The consequence is the reception that **reshapes the interior**: "then you will understand the **fear of the LORD**… **wisdom will come *into* your heart**, and knowledge will be **pleasant to your soul**" (vv.5,10). The operation: wisdom, once sought, **enters and re-forms the inner being** — it *comes into* the heart and becomes *pleasant to the soul*, and thereafter its faculties (discretion, understanding) **watch over** the self from within (v.11) *(inferred: the movement is self-seeks → God-gives (v.6) → wisdom-indwells → wisdom-guards; the inner being is remade by what it went after)*.

**Lexical validation.** The v1.1 substrate now carries the reading well: *fear* (H3374) → **specifier = of Lord** (the object of the fear captured); *heart* → seat + **specifier = of understanding**; and the seeking-verbs carry their objects positionally — *understand* → target **righteousness**, *walk* → target **integrity**, *gives* → target **wisdom**. The "wisdom comes *into* the heart" weld appears as *heart* (v.10) `manner/coupling` to *come-into* — correctly reading the heart as the place wisdom enters. Sound; the enrichment materially sharpens the "reshapes the heart" finding.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** (1) **Inclining the heart as an act of will** (v.2) — the self *directs* its own heart toward understanding; a volitional operation (with the "give me your heart" thread, 23:26). (2) **Wisdom as an *indwelling guardian*** (v.11) — "discretion will watch over you, understanding will guard you": the acquired faculties become *internal protectors*, a personified inner-being characteristic. (3) The **reciprocity** — the self seeks, but "the LORD *gives* wisdom" (v.6): the sought-for good is also a gift.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *the active seeking of wisdom* (new — Proverbs-distinctive, cf. the Psalter's seeking-God's-face); *inclining/directing the heart (volition)* (new); *wisdom indwelling and reshaping the heart* (new); *wisdom as internal guardian* (new); *the fear of the LORD* (shared, now object-tagged).

---

## PRO-02-B · Prov 2:12–22 · [D, multi] — discretion guarding the self; deliverance from evil

**The reading.** The indwelling faculties (from v.11) now *act*: they are "**delivering you** from the way of evil, from men of **perverted speech**… from the **forbidden woman** with her **smooth words**" (vv.12,16). The finding: the inner being's acquired discretion **functions as a deliverer** — wisdom internalised *extracts* the self from the paths of the crooked and the seductive *(stated)*. The unit's sharpest inner-being note is the anatomy of the seductress's *inner* failure: "who **forsakes** the companion of her youth and **forgets the covenant of her God**" (v.17) — her outward danger springs from an inward **forsaking and forgetting** *(inferred: the enticement is traced to a prior inner defection — she has *forgotten* a covenant; evil is diagnosed as a failure of inner fidelity/memory, cf. the Psalter's forgetting-as-seedbed-of-rebellion, Ps 106:13)*.

**Lexical validation.** The enrichment is telling here: *forsakes* → target **covenant**, *forgets* → target **covenant**, and *covenant* → **specifier = of God** — so the substrate now captures precisely the object of her defection ("the covenant *of God*"), which the reading rests on. The two "ways" close the unit as the moral-poles frame (paths *of uprightness* vs *of darkness* — both now specifier-tagged). Sound.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** **Evil as inner infidelity** (v.17) — the seductress is defined not by her acts but by her *forgetting the covenant*; a hidden characteristic (the forgetting/forsaking heart) that the segmentation's "deliverance" framing didn't name, and which links to the Psalter's memory-and-fidelity thread.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *discretion as deliverer* (new); *evil as inner infidelity (forgetting the covenant)* (new — links to Ps memory thread); *the two ways* (shared frame).

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Validation summary:** the v1.1 substrate is markedly richer for reading — construct `specifier` now supplies the *objects* of the characteristics (fear-of-Lord, covenant-of-God, heart-of-understanding) and positional `target` supplies the *objects of the operations* (walk→integrity, forsakes→covenant). Recurring residuals unchanged (bearer=LORD bleed at v.6; prohibition over-stamp on the "do not forsake" negations). No new anomalies.
- **New characteristics (fork-b control table):** *active seeking of wisdom*; *inclining the heart (volition)*; *wisdom indwelling / reshaping the heart*; *wisdom as internal guardian*; *discretion as deliverer*; *evil as inner infidelity (forgetting the covenant)*. **Shared:** *fear of the LORD*; *the two ways*.

---

## Proverbs 4 - inner-being unit synthesis

# Proverbs 4 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 4:1–27, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation** (wisdom/God = arena).

---

**PRO-04-A · 4:1–9 · [D, multi] — the inherited, single-minded pursuit of wisdom.** A father hands on *his own father's* charge: "**Get wisdom**; get insight… The beginning of wisdom is this: **Get wisdom**, and whatever you get, **get insight**. **Prize her highly**, and she will exalt you; **embrace** her" (vv.5,7–8). The finding: wisdom is pursued as **the one acquisition worth everything** — "whatever you get, get insight" makes it the *priority over all gain* — and it is **loved and embraced** (v.6, *love her*), a beloved to be held *(stated)*. The operation: **the whole self bent on acquiring one thing**, and that acquiring is *affectionate* (prize, embrace, love) not merely diligent *(inferred; the single-minded pursuit, cross-book with Ps 27:4's "one thing")*. *Validation:* the imperative-with-object is now fully captured — *Get→target=wisdom/insight* (repeated), *Hear→sons*, *gain→insight*. *Hidden:* **transmission across three generations** (grandfather→father→son, vv.3–4) — wisdom is *handed down*, formation is inherited. *Surfaced:* single-minded pursuit of wisdom (new, cf. Ps one-thing); affectionate acquisition (love/embrace wisdom); transmission of the inner life.

**PRO-04-B · 4:10–19 · [D, multi] — evil as an inner compulsion that cannot rest.** The two paths: "the path of the righteous is like the **light of dawn**, shining **brighter and brighter**," but of the wicked — "they **cannot sleep** unless they have **done wrong**; they are **robbed of sleep** unless they have made someone **stumble**. For they **eat the bread of wickedness** and **drink the wine of violence**" (vv.16–18). The finding: wickedness is not occasional but a **compulsion** — the wicked *cannot rest* until they have done evil; doing wrong is their food and drink *(stated)*. The operation: evil has become the self's **appetite and its insomnia** — a driven interior that is *restless without sin* *(inferred; the darkest portrait of the captured will, cross-book with Ps 36:4 "he plots trouble on his bed")*. *Validation:* the paths now specifier-tagged — way→*of wisdom*, paths→*of uprightness*, path→*of the wicked*; bread→*of wickedness*, wine→*of violence*. *Hidden:* **evil as insomnia/appetite** (a compulsive interior). *Surfaced:* the two paths (frame); the compulsive-evil self (new — sharper than Ps).

**PRO-04-C · 4:20–27 · [D, multi] — keep the heart, the source of life.** The chapter's cornerstone: "**Keep your heart with all vigilance, for from it flow the springs of life**" (v.23); then the gates — "put away **crooked speech**… let your **eyes look directly forward**… **ponder the path of your feet**" (vv.24–26). The finding: the **heart is the *source*** from which the whole life flows, and therefore the object of the most vigilant **guarding** *(stated)*. The operation: the self is **the sentinel of its own heart** — because everything issues *from* the heart, guarding it is guarding the springs of the entire life; and that guarding extends to the *gates* (mouth, eyes, feet) through which the heart acts *(inferred; the master inner-being datum of Proverbs — the heart as origin, cross-book with Ps 51:10, 141:3–4, 119:9)*. *Validation (strong):* the enrichment captures it — *heart→specifier=of all* + intensity=all ("with ALL vigilance"), *all→of vigilance* welded to *Keep*, *springs→of life*. *Hidden:* **the heart as the *origin* of the life, not just a faculty** — vigilance is required *because* it is the source. *Surfaced:* guard-the-heart / the heart as source of life (★ cornerstone, cross-book w/ Ps); governing the gates (speech/eyes/feet).

---
**Chapter notes.** Validation: v1.1 substrate strongly supports — the "get wisdom" objects and the "keep the heart with all vigilance" intensity/specifier are now fully pair-tagged; residuals unchanged. **New characteristics:** single-minded/affectionate pursuit of wisdom; transmission of the inner life; evil-as-compulsion (insomnia/appetite). **Shared/cornerstone:** ★ guard-the-heart (heart as source of life); the two paths; governing the gates.

---

## Proverbs 5 - inner-being unit synthesis

# Proverbs 5 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 5:1–23, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation** (arena = the forbidden woman / the wife of youth).

---

**PRO-05-A · 5:1–6 · [D] — discernment of the sweet surface that ends bitter.** "The lips of a forbidden woman **drip honey**, and her speech is **smoother than oil**, but in the end she is **bitter as wormwood**… her steps follow the **path to Sheol**; she does not ponder the **path of life**" (vv.3–6). The finding: the inner being must learn to **read past the sweet surface to the end** — honey now, wormwood after *(stated)*. The operation: **discernment as looking-to-the-end** — the self weighs allure not by its present sweetness but by *where its path goes* (Sheol vs life) *(inferred; the anti-type of the naive who cannot see the end, cf. 14:12)*. *Validation:* *keep→discretion*, *guard→knowledge* (the discretion that protects); *drip→honey*, *go-down→death*, *path→Sheol* vs *path→of life* (the two ends captured). *Surfaced:* discernment-as-reading-the-end (new).

**PRO-05-B · 5:7–14 · [D, multi] — the retrospective regret of the un-teachable self.** The ruin of yielding is voiced *from its far end*: "at the end of your life you **groan**, when your **flesh and body are consumed**, and you say, '**How I hated discipline, and my heart despised reproof!** I did not listen to the voice of my teachers'" (vv.11–13). The finding — the sharpest inner-being note in the chapter: the self's undoing is traced to a **prior hatred of correction** — "how I *hated* discipline… my heart *despised* reproof… I did not *listen*" *(stated)*. The operation: the un-teachable interior **reaps regret** — the closed heart that despised reproof now *groans* at what it became, in a retrospective self-indictment *(inferred; teachability as life-or-death, the mirror of Ps 32:9's "be not like a horse without understanding")*. *Validation:* the enrichment names the objects precisely — *hated→target=discipline*, *despised→target=reproof*; *flesh→of body*. *Hidden:* **regret as the wage of un-teachability** (the self indicting its own past closedness). *Surfaced:* the un-teachable/despising heart (new — cross-book w/ Ps 32); retrospective self-indictment.

**PRO-05-C · 5:15–20 · [D] — rightly ordered, not extinguished, desire.** Against the adulteress: "**rejoice** in the wife of your youth… let her breasts **fill you at all times with delight**; be **intoxicated always in her love**" (vv.18–19). The finding: the answer to disordered desire is **not the killing of desire but its right direction** — the same intoxication (*shagah*) that would ruin the self with a stranger is *commanded* toward the wife *(stated)*. The operation: **desire redirected, not repressed** — the inner being's capacity for delight/intoxication is *good* when rightly aimed *(inferred; cross-book with the ordered-desire thread, Ps 37:4 "delight in the LORD")*. *Validation:* *all→of times* welded to *fill* ("fill you at all times"), *intoxicated→always*. *Hidden:* **the same passion is ruin or joy by its object** (desire is morally neutral, decided by direction). *Surfaced:* rightly-ordered desire (new — a Proverbs sharpening).

**PRO-05-D · 5:21–23 · [S] — the self bound in the cords of its own sin.** "A man's ways are before the **eyes of the LORD**… The **iniquities of the wicked ensnare him**, and he is **held fast in the cords of his sin**. He **dies for lack of discipline**" (vv.21–23). The finding: sin is **self-binding** — the wicked is *caught and held fast* not by an external trap but by *his own iniquity* *(stated)*. The operation: **iniquity as self-imposed bondage** — the sinning self *weaves the cords that hold it*; freedom is lost from within *(inferred; the self-ensnaring wicked, cross-book with Ps 7:15, 9:15, and Pro 1:18's greed recoiling)*. *Validation:* *iniquities→of wicked*, *held-fast→wicked*, **cords→specifier=of sin** — the substrate now captures "the cords *of his sin*". *Surfaced:* sin as self-binding bondage (shared thread, cross-book).

---
**Chapter notes.** Validation: v1.1 enrichment supplies the objects the readings turn on (hated→discipline, cords→of-sin); residuals unchanged. **New characteristics:** discernment-as-reading-the-end; regret-of-the-un-teachable; rightly-ordered (not repressed) desire; the same-passion-ruin-or-joy-by-object. **Shared:** the un-teachable heart (w/ Ps 32); sin as self-binding (w/ Ps 7/9).

---

## Proverbs 7 - inner-being unit synthesis

# Proverbs 7 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 7:1–27, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**.

---

**PRO-07-A · 7:1–5 · [D, multi] — wisdom held as beloved kin.** "Keep my commandments as the **apple of your eye**… Say to wisdom, '**You are my sister**,' and call insight your **intimate friend**" (vv.2,4). The finding: wisdom is to be held not as a rule but as a **beloved relation** — sister, intimate friend, guarded like the eye's pupil *(stated)*. The operation: **intimacy with wisdom** — the self is to *love* wisdom into the family, so that closeness to her keeps it from the stranger-woman *(inferred; affection as the guard, cross-book with Ps 119:97 "oh how I love your law")*. *Validation:* *teaching→of apple* ("keep as the apple of the eye"). *Surfaced:* intimacy/kinship with wisdom (new).

**PRO-07-B · 7:6–23 · [D, multi] — the anatomy of a naive heart yielding.** The long narrative of "a young man **lacking sense**" (v.7) taken step by step: she is "**wily of heart**" (v.10); "with **much seductive speech** she persuades him; with her **smooth talk** she compels him. **All at once** he follows her, as an ox goes to the **slaughter**… he **does not know** that it will cost him his **life**" (vv.21–23). The finding: the psalm-like narrative **anatomises the collapse of the naive self** — the sense-lacking heart, worked by *smooth speech*, yields "all at once" and *does not know* the cost *(stated)*. The operation: **the un-guarded interior overwhelmed** — persuasion works on a heart with no discernment until the will follows *unknowing* to its ruin; the tragedy is the *not-knowing* *(inferred; the mirror of the discerning self of 5:1–6; cross-book with the naive vs prudent, and Ps 19:12 "who can discern his errors")*. *Validation:* *wily→target=heart* ("wily of heart"), *much→of seductive speech*, *smooth→persuades*, *fill→target=love* — the enrichment captures the seduction's mechanics. *Hidden:* **ruin through not-knowing** (the naive self's fatal unawareness). *Surfaced:* the collapse of the un-discerning heart (new — the anti-type of discernment).

**PRO-07-C · 7:24–27 · [D] — guarding the heart against turning aside.** "**Let not your heart turn aside** to her ways; do not stray into her paths" (v.25). The finding: the defence is set at the **heart's inclination** — the danger is the *heart turning aside* *(stated)*. The operation: **the self guards the *direction* of its own heart** — the well-trodden path to death is entered by an inward *turning*, so the guarding is of the heart's leaning, before the feet move *(inferred; the same interiorised guard as 4:23, 6:25)*. *Surfaced:* guarding the heart's inclination (shared w/ 4:23; the turned-aside heart).

---
**Chapter notes.** Validation: v1.1 enrichment captures the seduction's mechanics (wily-of-heart, seductive-speech, fill-with-love). **New characteristics:** intimacy/kinship with wisdom; the collapse of the un-discerning heart (ruin through not-knowing). **Shared:** guarding the heart's inclination (w/ 4:23, 6:25).

---
