## Proverbs 9 - inner-being unit synthesis

# Proverbs 9 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 9:1–18, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**. (Closes the ch 1–9 discourses; two rival banquets — Wisdom and Folly.)

---

**PRO-09-A · 9:1–6 · [D] — the summons to leave simplicity and live.** Wisdom's feast: "Whoever is **simple**, let him **turn in** here!… **Leave your simple ways, and live, and walk in the way of insight**" (vv.4,6). The finding: the call is to **abandon a settled inner condition** — "*leave* your simple ways" — as the price of life *(stated)*. The operation: **the self must renounce its own simplicity** — simplicity here is not innocence but a *chosen ease* the self is asked to *walk out of*; turning toward wisdom means turning *from* a former self *(inferred; cross-book with the "leave/turn" that begins the wise life)*. *Validation:* *Leave→target=ways*, way→*of insight*. *Surfaced:* renouncing one's own simplicity (new).

**PRO-09-B · 9:7–9 · [S, multi] — the response to reproof reveals the heart.** The chapter's gem: "**Reprove a scoffer, and he will hate you; reprove a wise man, and he will love you.** Give instruction to a wise man, and he will be **still wiser**" (vv.8–9). The finding: **the same reproof divides two hearts** — one *hates* the reprover, the other *loves* him *(stated)*. The operation: **the reaction to correction is the diagnostic of the inner being** — teachability is not measured by knowledge but by whether reproof is met with *hatred* or *love*; and the teachable heart *compounds* ("still wiser") while the closed heart only hardens *(inferred; the master teachability datum, cross-book with Ps 141:5 "let a righteous man strike me… it is a kindness")*. *Validation:* *increase→target=learning*; the aheb (love, 9:8) now tags characteristic under the v1.1/aheb rule — the *love* of the reproved wise. *Hidden:* **correction as the test that sorts the heart** (love-vs-hate of the reprover). *Surfaced:* teachability as the diagnostic of the heart (★ cornerstone, cross-book w/ Ps 141:5).

**PRO-09-C · 9:10–12 · [S] — the fear of the LORD, the beginning of wisdom.** "**The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom**, and the knowledge of the Holy One is insight" (v.10). The motto restated at the discourses' close (bookending 1:7). The finding: reverent fear is the **root** of the whole wise inner life *(stated)*. *Validation:* *fear→specifier=of Lord*; *added→target=life*. *Surfaced:* fear of the LORD (★ shared cornerstone — re-attested, bookends ch 1).

**PRO-09-D · 9:13–18 · [D] — the counterfeit allure of Folly.** Folly, Wisdom's mirror-image, calls from the same "highest places": "**Stolen water is sweet, and bread eaten in secret is pleasant.** But he does not know that the **dead are there**, that her guests are in the **depths of Sheol**" (vv.17–18). The finding: Folly's appeal is the **sweetness of the illicit** — *stolen*, *secret* — and its victim, like the naive of ch 7, **does not know** the end *(stated)*. The operation: **the allure of the forbidden precisely *because* it is forbidden** ("stolen… secret" are the selling points), working on a self that will not look to the end *(inferred; the counterfeit feast set exactly against Wisdom's, so the whole discourse-section closes on a *choice of two tables* — two loves, two ends)*. *Validation:* *woman→of Folly*, *bread→of secret*, *depths→of Sheol*. *Hidden:* **the forbidden desired *as* forbidden** (illicitness as the attraction). *Surfaced:* the counterfeit allure / the sweetness of the illicit (new); ruin-through-not-knowing (shared w/ 7:23).

---
**Chapter notes.** Validation: enrichment supplies fear→of-Lord and the feast-objects; the aheb love (9:8) now correctly a characteristic. **New characteristics:** renouncing one's own simplicity; teachability-as-diagnostic (★); the counterfeit allure of the illicit. **Shared:** ★ fear of the LORD (bookends ch 1); ruin-through-not-knowing (w/ ch 7). **This closes the ch 1–9 discourses — the whole section frames the inner life as a choice between two tables (Wisdom vs Folly), two loves, two ends.**

---

## Proverbs 12 - inner-being unit synthesis

# Proverbs 12 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 12, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**; righteous⇄wicked = arena.

---

**PRO-12-F · 12:2–28 · [F]** — the moral-poles frame. Arena.

**PRO-12-teachable · 12:1,15 · [S, multi] — loving discipline vs the self right in its own eyes.** "Whoever **loves discipline loves knowledge**, but he who **hates reproof is stupid**" (v.1); "the way of a fool is **right in his own eyes**, but a wise man **listens to advice**" (v.15). Finding: teachability is an *affection* — to love knowledge is to *love the discipline* that gives it; and the fool's fault is **self-certainty** ("right in his own eyes") *(stated)*. Operation: **the self that cannot see past its own view cannot learn** — self-certainty seals the heart, while the wise *hold their view open* to advice *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 36:2 self-flattery, and the teachability thread)*. *Hidden:* **self-certainty ("right in his own eyes") as the seal against wisdom** — recurs at 3:7, 26:12, 30:12. *Surfaced:* teachability-as-affection; self-certainty as the closed heart (new thread).

**PRO-12-speech · 12:6,13–14,17–19,22–23 · [T, multi] — the tongue that wounds or heals; truth that endures.** "**Rash words** are like **sword thrusts**, but the **tongue of the wise brings healing**"; "**truthful lips endure forever**, but a lying tongue is but for a **moment**"; "a **prudent man conceals** knowledge, but the **heart of fools proclaims folly**" (vv.18–19,23). Finding: speech wounds or heals, endures or vanishes, by its truth — and the *prudent conceal* while *fools broadcast* *(stated)*. Operation: **the governed tongue as healing and enduring** — truth in speech has a *permanence* the lie lacks; and prudence *withholds* what folly *spills* *(inferred; the speech-legibility thread, + the endurance-of-truth note)*. *Validation:* v1.1 supplies the fruit-of-the-mouth objects (12:14 "satisfied with good"). *Surfaced:* speech-legibility (shared); the endurance of truthful speech (new); prudent concealment vs folly's broadcast.

**PRO-12-heart-thoughts · 12:5,20 · [S, multi] — the heart's thoughts and plans.** "The **thoughts of the righteous are just**; the counsels of the wicked are deceitful"; "**deceit is in the heart** of those who devise evil, but those who **plan peace have joy**" (vv.5,20). Finding: the inner *thoughts/plans* are the moral root — deceit or peace lives *in the heart* before it acts, and *planning peace* carries joy *(stated)*. Operation: **the heart's inner counsel as the seat of character** — what the self *thinks/plans* is who it is *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 19:14 "meditation of my heart", 139:23 "know my thoughts")*. *Hidden:* **planning peace *has joy* now** — the disposition is already its own reward. *Surfaced:* the heart's thoughts/plans as character (shared w/ Ps).

**PRO-12-anxiety · 12:25 · [S, multi] — anxiety weighs the heart; a good word lifts it.** "**Anxiety in a man's heart weighs him down, but a good word makes him glad**" (v.25). Finding: anxiety is a *weight* on the heart, relieved by a kind word *(stated)*. Operation: **the felt interior — the heavy heart lightened from outside** (a good word) *(inferred; the felt-heart thread, cross-book w/ Ps 94:19 "when the cares of my heart are many, your consolations cheer my soul")*. *Surfaced:* the felt heart (weighed/gladdened) — ★ shared cross-book thread.

**PRO-12-diligence · 12:11,24,27 · [T] — diligence rules, sloth is enslaved.** "The **hand of the diligent will rule**, while the **slothful will be put to forced labor**" (v.24). Finding: diligence and sloth end in mastery vs servitude *(stated)*. *Surfaced:* diligence vs sloth (shared Proverbs thread).

---
**Chapter notes.** Validation: enrichment consistent (fruit-of-mouth, deceit-in-heart objects). **New:** self-certainty as the closed heart; endurance-of-truthful-speech; planning-peace-has-joy. **Shared:** the felt heart (★ w/ Ps 94:19); the heart's thoughts as character (w/ Ps 139); speech-legibility; diligence/sloth.

---

## Proverbs 13 - inner-being unit synthesis

# Proverbs 13 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 13, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**; righteous⇄wicked = arena.

---

**PRO-13-F · 13:5–25 · [F]** — the moral-poles frame. Arena.

**PRO-13-desire-hope · 13:4,12,19,25 · [T, multi] — craving, hope deferred, desire fulfilled.** The chapter's felt-interior cluster: "the **soul of the sluggard craves and gets nothing**, while the **soul of the diligent is richly supplied**" (v.4); "**HOPE DEFERRED makes the heart sick, but a desire fulfilled is a tree of life**" (v.12); "**a desire fulfilled is sweet to the soul**" (v.19). Finding: the inner being is a **creature of longing whose deferral *sickens* the heart and whose fulfilment is *life and sweetness*** *(stated)*. Operation: **hope has a bodily register — deferred, it makes the heart *sick*; met, it is a *tree of life*** — the timing of fulfilment is itself an inner-being event *(inferred; a cornerstone of the felt interior, cross-book w/ Ps 42:1–2's thirst, 130:5–6's aching wait, and the desire-met thread 145:19)*. *Hidden:* **the *sickness* of deferred hope** — waiting is not neutral; unmet longing *wounds* the heart (the shadow-side of the Psalter's hopeful waiting). *Surfaced:* hope-deferred/fulfilled (★ shared cornerstone, cross-book); the craving vs satisfied soul.

**PRO-13-speech · 13:2,3 · [S] — guarding the mouth guards the life.** "Whoever **guards his mouth preserves his life**; he who **opens wide his lips comes to ruin**" (v.3). Finding: speech-restraint is **self-preservation** — the guarded mouth guards the whole self *(stated; the self-governance-of-the-tongue thread, cross-book w/ Ps 141:3)*. *Surfaced:* restraint of the tongue as self-preservation (shared).

**PRO-13-teachable · 13:1,10,13,18 · [T, multi] — hearing, revering the word, heeding reproof.** "A wise son **hears** instruction, but a scoffer does not listen"; "by **insolence** comes strife, but with those who **take advice** is wisdom"; "whoever **despises the word** brings destruction, but he who **reveres the commandment** will be rewarded" (vv.1,10,13). Finding: teachability spans *hearing*, *taking advice*, and *revering the word* — insolence (pride) is its enemy *(stated)*. Operation: **reverence for the word vs contempt for it** as the fork of the inner life *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 119's love of the word)*. *Surfaced:* teachability / reverence-vs-contempt-for-the-word (shared w/ Ps 119).

**PRO-13-company · 13:20 · [S] — formation by company.** "**Whoever walks with the wise becomes wise, but the companion of fools will suffer harm**" (v.20). Finding: the self is **shaped by the company it keeps** — one *becomes* like one's companions *(stated)*. Operation: **formation-by-association** — a law of the inner life (you become your company), the same formation-principle as "you become what you trust" (Ps 115:8) applied to human company *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 1:1's refused seat, 26:4–5)*. *Hidden:* **the formation-law extended to company** — a Proverbs parallel to the trust-formation datum. *Surfaced:* formation-by-company (★ new — the formation-law applied to company, cross-book w/ Ps 1/115).

---
**Chapter notes.** Validation: enrichment consistent (craving/desire objects, soul-of-sluggard). **New/cornerstone:** hope-deferred-makes-the-heart-sick (★ felt interior); formation-by-company (★). **Shared:** the felt interior (w/ Ps 42/130); restraint-of-tongue; teachability/reverence-for-the-word (w/ Ps 119).

## Proverbs 14 - inner-being unit synthesis

# Proverbs 14 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 14, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**; wise⇄fool = arena.

---

**PRO-14-F · 14:1–35 · [F]** — the moral-poles frame. Arena.

**PRO-14-heart-known · 14:10,13 · [S, multi] — the heart's incommunicable interior.** "**The heart knows its own bitterness, and no stranger shares its joy**" (v.10); "**even in laughter the heart may ache, and the end of joy may be grief**" (v.13). Finding — a cornerstone of the felt interior: the heart's deepest states are **private and incommunicable** — its bitterness *known only to itself*, its joy *unshared*, and its surface (laughter) may *mask* an inward ache *(stated)*. Operation: **the inner life is finally solitary** — no one else fully enters the heart's grief or gladness, and the outward face can *contradict* the inward state *(inferred; the most explicit statement in Scripture of the *privacy* of the inner being; cross-book w/ Ps 38:8–9 "the tumult of my heart… my sighing is not hidden from you" — only God enters where no stranger can)*. *Hidden:* **the mask — laughter over ache** (the outward may belie the inward). *Surfaced:* the incommunicable/private heart (★ cornerstone — new to the corpus, deepens the felt-interior thread); the masking surface.

**PRO-14-temper · 14:17,29,30 · [T, multi] — anger vs the tranquil heart.** "Whoever is **slow to anger has great understanding**, but he who has a **hasty temper exalts folly**"; "**A tranquil heart gives life to the flesh, but envy makes the bones rot**" (vv.29–30). Finding: temper is a *cognitive* matter (slow-to-anger = *understanding*), and the **tranquil heart is bodily *life* while envy *rots the bones*** *(stated)*. Operation: **inner tranquillity as physical health, envy/rage as physical decay** — the emotional interior writes itself on the body *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 32:3 "my bones wasted", 38:3; the felt interior embodied)*. *Hidden:* **the heart's peace as *somatic*** (tranquil heart → life to the flesh). *Surfaced:* self-mastery/slow-to-anger (shared, cross-book w/ Ps); the tranquil-vs-envious heart embodied (★ new).

**PRO-14-fear · 14:26,27 · [T, multi] — the fear of the LORD as confidence and fountain of life.** "In the **fear of the LORD one has strong confidence**… the **fear of the LORD is a fountain of life**" (vv.26–27). Finding: reverent fear yields **confidence and life** — not dread but a *strong assurance* *(stated; the fear-of-LORD thread, cross-book w/ Ps 112, 27:1)*. *Surfaced:* fear of the LORD → confidence/life (shared cornerstone).

**PRO-14-self-deception · 14:12 · [S] — the way that seems right.** "**There is a way that seems right to a man, but its end is the way to death**" (v.12). Finding: the self can **misread its own path** — subjective rightness is no guide to the true end *(stated)*. Operation: **self-deception about one's own way** — the inner sense of being right can be fatally wrong *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 19:12 "who can discern his errors")*. *Surfaced:* self-deception / the way-that-seems-right (★ new — recurs 16:25).

**PRO-14-simple · 14:15 · [S] — credulity vs considered steps.** "**The simple believes everything, but the prudent gives thought to his steps**" (v.15). Finding: the naive *believes all*, the prudent *weighs* — discernment as considered attention *(stated)*. *Surfaced:* discernment vs credulity (shared w/ ch 7's naive self).

**PRO-14-generosity · 14:21,31 · [S, multi] — regard for the poor as regard for the Maker.** "Whoever **oppresses a poor man insults his Maker**, but he who is **generous to the needy honors him**" (v.31). Finding: one's disposition toward the poor is a disposition **toward God** *(stated; the neighbour-facing heart, cross-book w/ Ps 41:1)*. *Surfaced:* regard-for-the-poor-as-regard-for-God (shared).

---
**Chapter notes.** Validation: enrichment consistent. **New/cornerstone:** the incommunicable/private heart (★ 14:10); the tranquil-vs-envious heart embodied (★ 14:30); self-deception (★ 14:12). **Shared:** self-mastery/slow-to-anger; fear-of-LORD→confidence; discernment; the neighbour-facing heart.

## Proverbs 15 - inner-being unit synthesis

# Proverbs 15 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 15, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**; righteous⇄wicked = arena.

---

**PRO-15-F · 15:2–33 · [F]** — the moral-poles frame. Arena.

**PRO-15-anger · 15:1,18 · [S, multi] — the soft answer; slow-to-anger quiets strife.** "**A soft answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger**"; "a **hot-tempered man stirs up strife, but he who is slow to anger quiets contention**" (vv.1,18). Finding: the inner being can **de-escalate or inflame** by the temper of its speech — gentleness *turns away* wrath *(stated)*. Operation: **self-mastery expressed as gentleness** — the slow-to-anger self *quiets* what the hot-tempered *kindles* *(inferred; the self-mastery thread, cross-book w/ Ps 4:4 "be angry and do not sin")*. *Surfaced:* self-mastery / the soft answer (shared).

**PRO-15-heart-states · 15:13,15,30 · [T, multi] — the felt heart: glad, crushed, cheerful.** "**A glad heart makes a cheerful face, but by sorrow of heart the spirit is crushed**"; "the **cheerful of heart has a continual feast**"; "the **light of the eyes rejoices the heart**, and good news refreshes the bones" (vv.13,15,30). Finding — a felt-interior cornerstone: the heart's state **shows on the face**, *crushes the spirit* in sorrow, and the cheerful heart lives in a **continual feast** regardless of circumstance *(stated)*. Operation: **the inner disposition *colours all of life*** — "a continual feast" is not about events but about a *cheerful heart*; the interior sets the taste of existence *(inferred; the felt-interior thread at its fullest, cross-book w/ Ps 4:7 "more joy… than when grain and wine abound", 34:5 "radiant faces")*. *Hidden:* **the cheerful heart makes a *continual feast* out of ordinary days** — inner state over outer circumstance. *Surfaced:* the felt heart (glad/crushed/cheerful) — ★ shared cornerstone; the crushed spirit (w/ 17:22, Ps).

**PRO-15-god-sees-heart · 15:3,11 · [T, multi] — God sees the hearts.** "The **eyes of the LORD are in every place, keeping watch** on evil and good"; "**Sheol and Abaddon lie open before the LORD; how much more the hearts of the children of man!**" (vv.3,11). Finding: the inner being is **wholly open to God's sight** — if even the realm of the dead lies open, *how much more the heart* *(stated)*. Operation (of the self): **living before an all-seeing gaze** — the heart is never unobserved *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 139 "you have searched me", 33:13–15 "he fashions their hearts and observes all their deeds")*. *Surfaced:* being-known/seen by God (★ shared cornerstone, cross-book w/ Ps 139).

**PRO-15-teachable · 15:14,31,32 · [T, multi] — the seeking heart, the listening ear.** "The **heart of him who has understanding seeks knowledge**"; "the **ear that listens to life-giving reproof will dwell among the wise**"; "whoever **ignores instruction despises himself**" (vv.14,31–32). Finding: the wise heart is **actively seeking**, and heeding reproof is **self-respect** ("ignores instruction *despises himself*") *(stated)*. Operation: **the seeking heart + the self-valuing that heeds correction** *(inferred; teachability as self-love, cross-book w/ 19:8)*. *Surfaced:* the seeking heart; heeding-reproof-as-self-respect (new).

**PRO-15-contentment · 15:16,17 · [S, multi] — the little with fear/love better than much with trouble.** "**Better is a little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure and trouble**… better a **dinner of herbs where love is** than a fattened ox and **hatred**" (vv.16–17). Finding: **contentment is a function of the inner condition** (fear, love), not the quantity of goods *(stated)*. Operation: **the inner good (fear/love) outvalues the outer abundance** *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 37:16 "better is the little of the righteous than the abundance of many wicked")*. *Surfaced:* contentment (inner-condition over abundance) — shared w/ Ps 37.

**PRO-15-ponder · 15:28 · [S] — the heart that ponders before answering.** "**The heart of the righteous ponders how to answer, but the mouth of the wicked pours out evil**" (v.28). Finding: the righteous heart **weighs before it speaks** — considered vs impulsive interior *(stated; the ponder/restraint thread)*. *Surfaced:* the pondering (vs impulsive) heart (new).

**PRO-15-humility · 15:33 · [S, multi] — fear and humility before honour.** "The **fear of the LORD is instruction in wisdom, and humility comes before honour**" (v.33). Finding: humility *precedes* honour — the lowered self is the one lifted *(stated; pride/humility thread, cross-book w/ Ps 138:6)*. *Surfaced:* humility-before-honour (shared cornerstone).

---
**Chapter notes.** Validation: enrichment consistent. **New/cornerstone:** the felt heart / cheerful-heart-as-continual-feast (★ 15:15); heeding-reproof-as-self-respect; the pondering heart. **Shared:** self-mastery/soft-answer; being-seen-by-God (★ 15:11, w/ Ps 139); contentment (w/ Ps 37); humility-before-honour.

---

## Proverbs 31 - inner-being unit synthesis

# Proverbs 31 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 31 (Lemuel + the woman of valour), per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**. (Closes the book.)

---

**PRO-31-charge · 31:2–9 · [D, multi] — self-mastery for the sake of the voiceless.** The mother's charge to the king: "**do not give your strength to women**… **it is not for kings to drink wine**… lest they **drink and forget** what has been decreed and **pervert the rights of the afflicted**… **Open your mouth for the mute**, for the rights of all who are destitute" (vv.3–5,8). Finding: **self-mastery is charged for the sake of *others*** — the king must govern appetite (women, wine) *lest* he *forget* justice and fail the voiceless *(stated)*. Operation: **appetite-restraint in service of justice** — self-control is not private virtue only but the condition of *not forgetting* one's duty to the afflicted *(inferred; self-mastery + the neighbour-facing heart joined; cross-book w/ Ps 72:2–4)*. *Surfaced:* self-mastery-for-the-sake-of-the-voiceless (new — self-control as a *public* fidelity).

**PRO-31-noble-wife · 31:10–31 · [D, multi] — the woman who fears the LORD: trust, strength, fearless hope, the book's crown.** The acrostic portrait, read for the inner being: "the **heart of her husband trusts in her**" (v.11 — she is *trustworthy*); "she **dresses herself with strength**… **strength and dignity are her clothing, and she laughs at the time to come**" (vv.17,25 — inner strength and **fearless hope**); "she **opens her mouth with wisdom, and the teaching of kindness is on her tongue**" (v.26 — wise, kind speech); and the crown: "**charm is deceitful, and beauty is vain, but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised**" (v.30). Finding — the book's closing cornerstone: the whole excellence is finally reduced to **the fear of the LORD** — over charm and beauty (which are *deceitful* and *vain*) — and it *shows* as **trustworthiness, inner strength, fearless laughter at the future, and wise-kind speech** *(stated)*. Operation: **the fear of the LORD *embodied* as a life** — the abstract root of 1:7 is here *lived out* in a whole person: an inner being so settled it **laughs at the time to come** (the opposite of dread), so reliable that a heart *trusts* in her, so strengthened it needs no charm *(inferred; the book's frame closes — fear-of-the-LORD opened it (1:7) and crowns it here (31:30); cross-book w/ Ps 112 the God-fearer whose "heart is firm… not afraid of bad news", and the fearless-security thread)*. *Hidden:* **"she laughs at the time to come"** — fearless hope as the *affect* of the God-fearing self (the antithesis of anxiety about the future, cf. 27:1's refused presumption; here a *settled* facing of the future). *Surfaced:* fear-of-the-LORD embodied (★ book-closing cornerstone, bookends 1:7, cross-book w/ Ps 112); trustworthiness; inner strength + fearless hope ("laughs at the time to come"); wise-kind speech.

---
**Chapter notes.** **Book-closing cornerstone:** the fear of the LORD *embodied* as a whole life (★ 31:30, bookending 1:7). **New:** self-mastery-for-the-voiceless; fearless-hope ("laughs at the time to come"). **Shared:** the fear of the LORD (★ frame); trust/trustworthiness; inner strength; wise-kind speech.

---
*This completes the Proverbs unit meaning-synthesis (all 31 chapters, 150 units). The book's inner-being frame: it opens (1:7) and closes (31:30) on the **fear of the LORD** — abstract root, then embodied life — and between them maps the inner being as a **heart to be guarded, given, weighed, searched, and ruled**, its wisdom a matter of what it fears, trusts, desires, and how it governs itself.*

---

## Ecclesiastes 1 - inner-being unit readings

# Ecclesiastes 1 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Ecc 1:1–18, read **per segmentation unit** (`segment_unit`, provenance `ecclesiastes-segmentation-v1-20260703`). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**; the vanity/God-relation is the arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Method (unit meaning-synthesis):** each unit is read for its inner-being meaning, and that reading **reads back and validates the Phase-1 lexical** — checking roles, **pairs** (bearer / manner / coupling / target / specifier / seat) and flags for sensibility, and **isolating hidden characteristics** the provisional segmentation did not name. Ecclesiastes is a first-person meditation, so the "self" doing the observing is itself a persistent inner-being datum.

---

## ECC-01-A · Ecc 1:2–11 · [F, multi, thread] — the perception of futility; weariness; the insatiable eye/ear; oblivion

**The reading.** Before the book argues anything it establishes an *arena the inner being must live inside*: a world of ceaseless motion that never arrives. Generations go and come, the sun races back to where it rose, the wind wheels "around and around," the streams run to a sea "not full" (vv.4–7). The finding is not a doctrine of futility but a **perception seated in a watching self** — the person who sees the cycles and feels their weight: "all things are **full of weariness**; a man cannot **utter** it" (v.8) *(stated)*. Three inner-being operations are folded together here. (1) **Weariness** — the exhaustion of watching motion without progress. (2) The **insatiable senses** — "the **eye is not satisfied** with seeing, nor the **ear filled** with hearing" (v.8): the taking-in faculties that never reach *enough*, the first sounding of the never-satisfied thread that runs the whole book. (3) **Oblivion** — "there is **no remembrance** of former things, nor will there be any remembrance of later things" (v.11): the self faces not only a wearying world but a *forgetting* one, where its own trace will not hold *(inferred: the three together define the pressure the rest of the book's inner life answers to — a self that tires, cannot be filled, and will be forgotten)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** The substrate carries the cycle-verbs (*goes, comes, rises, returns, run, flow*) correctly as `standalone` actions of the world, not the self — right, since the finding is the *observer's* response, not the sun's motion. Two notes. (1) **Positional-target over-stamp:** the v1.1 unmarked-object rule fires repeatedly here (e.g. *says*→*Preacher*, *goes*→*generation*, *comes*→*earth*), each flagged `discovery=target positional (unverified)` — these are the poetry's adjacent nouns, not real objects; correctly self-flagged, and the reading ignores them. (2) **`seat=spirit` on H7307 (v.6, "wind")** — the lexical tags the physical *wind* with `seat=spirit` because H7307 = *ruach*. Here it is plainly the meteorological wind, not the human spirit; a lemma-level seat-stamp to discount (the ruach/wind ambiguity, flagged for the rule-adjustment list — *seat=spirit* should not fire where the surface is elemental wind). The genuinely inner terms — *weariness* (H3023, v.8), the *eye* and *ear* not satisfied/filled — sit in gate-2 content; the reading is read from the verse structure, correctly.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** (1) **The watching self as a fixed datum** — the whole unit is *someone observing*; the observing-and-weighing self (not yet named) is the book's most persistent characteristic and begins here. (2) **The un-utterable** — "a man cannot utter it" (v.8): a distinct inner state, the surplus of weariness that overflows speech (kin to the Psalter's "too deep for words," but here negative).

**Characteristics surfaced:** *the perception of futility / weariness* (new — Ecclesiastes' distinctive arena); *the insatiable senses (eye/ear never filled)* (new thread — never-satisfied); *oblivion / being-forgotten* (thread, shared w/ the book's later 2:16, 9:15); *the watching-and-weighing self* (new — the book's frame-characteristic).

---

## ECC-01-B · Ecc 1:12–15 · [D, multi, thread] — the searching self (heart applied to seek out); the unhappy business

**The reading.** The Preacher names his method, and the method is an *inner-being posture*: "I **applied my heart** to **seek** and to **search out** by wisdom all that is done under heaven" (v.13). The finding is the **directed, effortful heart** — the self that deliberately sets its interior to investigation *(stated)*; this "applied heart" recurs as the engine of the whole book (2:3, 7:25, 8:16). What it finds recoils on it: the seeking is "an **unhappy business** that God has given" (v.13), and its object resists — "what is **crooked cannot be made straight**, and what is **lacking cannot be counted**" (v.15). The operation is **the seeking heart meeting resistance** — investigation that returns not mastery but the discovery of an unfixable, unfillable reality *(inferred: the "crooked/lacking" pair frames the search's limit; the heart can seek exhaustively and still not straighten the world)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *applied* / *seek* / *search out* (vv.13) carry the directed-heart finding; the lexical tags the seeking-verbs as actions, sound. The phrase "my heart" (the *leb* seat) is the bearer of the searching — the reading rests here. *unhappy business* (H6045, v.13) sits as content. No systemic residual beyond the recurring positional-target flags; pairs sensible.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** **The seeking as self-assigned burden** — it is "given by God to be busy with" (v.13): the searching heart is not idle curiosity but an *appointed labour*, a hidden note that the inner drive to understand is itself experienced as a weight, not a freedom.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *the searching/seeking self (the applied heart)* (new thread — recurs 2:3, 7:25, 8:16); *the seeking heart meeting an unfixable reality* (new).

---

## ECC-01-C · Ecc 1:16–18 · [D, multi] — knowing as grief; the heart's great experience of wisdom

**The reading.** The self takes stock of what it has become: "I have **acquired great wisdom**… my **heart has had great experience** of wisdom and knowledge" (v.16) — a heart *enlarged* by learning. Then the gem, stated flatly as a law of the interior: "in **much wisdom is much vexation**, and he who **increases knowledge increases sorrow**" (v.18). The finding is **understanding that deepens grief** — the inner being does not find that knowledge soothes; the more it takes in, the more it aches *(stated)*. Set against the ordinary hope that wisdom brings peace, this is a counter-finding: the growing mind is a *grieving* mind, because it sees more of the crooked and the lacking it cannot mend *(inferred: v.18 completes v.15 — the searching heart of 1:13 not only fails to straighten the world but is *pained in proportion to its sight*)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *wisdom, knowledge, experience* correctly carried; the pivot terms *vexation* (H3708, v.18) and *sorrow* (H4341, v.18) sit as the grief-content the reading rests on. The "I said in my heart" of v.16 correctly places the utterance in the *leb* — the dialogical self speaking to itself, a form the book shares with the Psalter (Ps 4, 42). Sound; no material mis-tag.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** (1) **The self-addressing heart** — "I said in my heart" (v.16): the interior conversation, the self reporting to itself, recurs through the book and is a genuine characteristic (the reflexive/dialogical self, shared w/ the Psalter's self-address). (2) **Wisdom as a *quantity* that scales with pain** — "in *much*… *increases*… *increases*": the finding is proportional, not binary; a hidden precision the segmentation's "knowing as grief" flattens.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *knowing as grief (wisdom deepening sorrow)* (new — a Qoheleth counter-finding); *the self-addressing / dialogical heart* (shared w/ Ps); *the enlarged heart (great experience of wisdom)* (new).

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Validation summary:** Phase-1 substrate is sound for reading. Two residuals to add to the rule-adjustment list: (1) **`seat=spirit` mis-fires on elemental *ruach*/wind** (v.6) — seat should gate on human-interior surface, not the lemma; (2) the **positional-target rule** fires on poetic adjacent nouns throughout (correctly self-flagged `unverified`) — for Ecclesiastes' verb-heavy meditation it produces many false objects; candidate to tighten for poetic genre. Neither touches the readings.
- **New characteristics this chapter (for the fork-b control table):** *the perception of futility / weariness*; *the insatiable senses (never-satisfied)*; *oblivion / being-forgotten*; *the watching-and-weighing self*; *the searching/seeking heart*; *knowing as grief*. **Shared with the Psalter/Proverbs:** *the self-addressing/dialogical heart*.
- **Threads opened:** *never-satisfied* (1:8 → 4:8, 5:10, 6:7); *the seeking heart* (1:13 → 2:3, 7:25, 8:16); *oblivion* (1:11 → 2:16, 9:15); *the joy refrain* not yet sounded (first at 2:24).

---

## Ecclesiastes 2 - inner-being unit readings

# Ecclesiastes 2 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** Phase-1 lexicals for Ecc 2:1–26, read per `segment_unit` (provenance `ecclesiastes-segmentation-v1-20260703`). Complete chapter. Cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the inner-being **operation** is the finding; wealth/toil/God-relation is the arena.

---

## ECC-02-A · Ecc 2:1–11 · [D, multi] — the self-experimenting, appetite-indulging heart; pleasure tested and found empty

**The reading.** This is the book's great *experiment on the self*, and the experimenter and the subject are the same person. "I said in my **heart**, 'Come now, I will **test** you with **pleasure**; enjoy yourself'" (v.1) — the self deliberately turns its own interior into a laboratory *(stated)*. Everything the appetite could want is supplied: houses, vineyards, gardens, pools, slaves, herds, silver and gold, singers (vv.4–8). The crucial inner-being line: "**whatever my eyes desired** I did not keep from them; I **kept my heart from no pleasure**, for my heart **found pleasure** in all my toil" (v.10) — desire is not denied but *fully granted*, the eyes given everything they reach for. And the verdict, after total indulgence: "behold, **all was vanity** and a striving after wind, and there was nothing to be gained" (v.11). The finding is the **appetite that is satisfied and still comes up empty** — the self discovers experimentally that having-everything does not fill it *(inferred: the experiment is designed to test whether pleasure can be the soul's rest; the answer is no — the heart that withheld nothing still found "nothing to be gained")*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** The substrate is strong here. *heart* (H3820, *leb*) is correctly seated (`seat=heart`) as the bearer of both the test (v.1) and the finding of pleasure (v.10). *desired* (H7592, v.10) and *found pleasure* (H8056, v.10) are correctly `characteristic` — the desiring and delighting operations the reading rests on. *body* (H1320, v.3) carries `seat=flesh` — right, "cheer my **body** with wine" is the fleshly seat. Note the recurring **`seat=spirit` on H7307 ("striving after wind," v.11)**: the *ruach* here is elemental wind in an idiom, not the human spirit — the same lemma-level seat mis-fire flagged in ch.1, to discount. Pairs otherwise sensible (the construct *of wine*, *of toil* correctly specifier-tagged).

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** (1) **The self as its own experimental subject** — "I will test *you*": the interior split into examiner and examined, a reflexive structure distinct from mere introspection (the self *runs a trial* on itself). (2) **Wisdom retained *inside* the indulgence** — "my heart still **guiding me with wisdom**" (v.3): the experiment is conducted *soberly*, not lost in it; the observing self never fully dissolves into the pleasure it tests — which is precisely why it can report the emptiness.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *the appetite fully indulged yet unfilled* (new — the sharpest form of the never-satisfied thread); *the self-experimenting / self-testing heart* (new — Ecclesiastes' distinctive reflexive move); *desire (the eyes that reach)* (shared w/ the Psalter's desire cluster); *the sober observer inside the experience* (new).

---

## ECC-02-B · Ecc 2:12–17 · [D, multi] — the hatred of life; the leveling of the wise and the fool

**The reading.** The self grants wisdom its real superiority — "there is more gain in **wisdom** than in **folly**, as there is more gain in **light** than in **darkness**; the wise person has his **eyes in his head**, but the fool **walks in darkness**" (vv.13–14). Then the finding that overturns it: "**the same event happens to all** of them" (v.14) — wise and fool arrive at the one death and the one forgetting (v.16). Out of this comes a raw inner-being state, named without hedging: "**so I hated life**, because what is done under the sun was grievous to me" (v.17) *(stated)*. The operation is **the collapse of meaning into the hatred of life** — not depression as mood but a *reasoned revulsion*: if the best thing the self can be (wise) ends identically to the worst (fool), then the ground under the self's striving gives way *(inferred: the hatred is the felt cost of the leveling; the observing self of 2:1–11, having proven pleasure empty, now finds even wisdom's advantage cancelled at the grave)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *hated* (H8130, v.17) is correctly `characteristic` with the reading's object — "hated **life**" (target H2416, sound). *wise/wisdom* and *folly/madness* correctly carried; the *leb* self-address of v.15 ("I said in my heart") again correctly seated. The reading is clean off the substrate; no material mis-tag beyond the *ruach*-wind seat at v.17.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** **Hatred directed at *life itself*, not at God or circumstance** — the object of the revulsion is the self's own existence-under-the-sun; a distinct and startling inner-being datum (the Psalter's laments cry *out* of trouble; here the self recoils from *living as such*). It is honest despair held open, not yet resolved — the book will not answer it with argument but with the joy-refrain (2:24).

**Characteristics surfaced:** *the hatred of life (meaning's collapse at the grave's leveling)* (new — Ecclesiastes' darkest inner state); *the wise/fool distinction felt and then cancelled* (new).

---

## ECC-02-C · Ecc 2:18–23 · [D, multi] — the restless, despairing heart over toil

**The reading.** The revulsion narrows onto labour: "**I hated all my toil**… seeing that I must **leave it** to the man who will come after me — and who knows whether he will be **wise or a fool**?" (vv.18–19). The self cannot even secure the meaning of its own work, since an unknown heir will inherit it. So "I **gave my heart up to despair** over all the toil" (v.20) *(stated)*. The unit's gem is the somatic close: "all his days are full of **sorrow**, and his work is a **vexation**. Even in the **night his heart does not rest**" (v.23). The finding is **the toiling heart that cannot rest even in sleep** — anxiety that has colonised the one place meant for release; the interior churns through the night *(inferred: the despair of v.20 becomes the sleeplessness of v.23 — the same restless heart the Psalter answers with "he gives to his beloved sleep," here left un-answered under the sun)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *hated* (H8130, v.18, target *all*), *despair* (H2976, v.20, target *heart*), *sorrow* (H4341), *vexation* (H3708) all correctly `characteristic` — the grief-cluster the reading names. *heart* (H3820) seated throughout; "his heart does not rest" (v.23) carries the `prohibition=forbidden` neg-particle stamp — here the negation is real ("does *not* rest"), so the stamp is not spurious, though it spreads to adjacent tokens (a mild over-reach). The reading is well-supported.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** (1) **The heir-anxiety** — a specific inner-being operation: dread not of losing one's work but of *not controlling who receives it and whether they deserve it* (v.19); the self's meaning held hostage to an unknown other. (2) **Night as the exposure of the unrested heart** — "even in the night": the finding that daytime toil's vexation *does not switch off*, isolating the sleepless interior as the true site of the vanity.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *the sleepless, unrested heart* (new — kin to but darker than the Psalter's restless soul, here without the "he gives sleep" resolution); *heir-anxiety (meaning surrendered to an unknown successor)* (new); *despair as a deliberate act of the heart ("gave my heart up to despair")* (new).

---

## ECC-02-D · Ecc 2:24–26 · [T, thread] — joy/enjoyment as the gift of God (first sounding of the refrain)

**The reading.** Against everything just said, the first sounding of the refrain that will recur seven times and carry the book's one positive answer: "There is nothing **better** for a person than that he should **eat and drink and find enjoyment** in his toil. This also, I saw, is **from the hand of God**" (v.24). The finding is **enjoyment received as gift, not achieved as gain** — the very toil that produced despair (2:18–23) becomes, when taken *as given*, a site of enjoyment *(stated)*. Crucially the enjoyment is not a different activity from the toil but the *same* activity received differently — "find enjoyment **in his toil**." And it is not self-generated: "apart from him who can eat or who can have enjoyment?" (v.25); "to the one who **pleases him** God has given wisdom and knowledge and **joy**" (v.26). The operation is **the reframing of the same life as gift** — the inner shift from grasping-for-gain to receiving-with-joy *(inferred: the refrain does not solve the vanity by argument; it relocates the self's posture from acquisition to reception, which is where joy becomes possible)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *joy* (H8057, v.26), *enjoyment/better/pleases* (H2896/H8056 family) correctly `characteristic`. *given* (H5414, v.26) correctly carries the gift-operation (targets *wisdom*, *knowledge*). The theological weight sits in the phrase "from the hand of God," correctly `standalone`. Sound.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** **Joy as a *capacity granted*, not a mood chosen** — "apart from him who can *have enjoyment*?" (v.25): the ability to enjoy is itself the gift, a subtle and important inner-being finding (later made explicit in 6:2, where wealth is given but the *power to enjoy* withheld). The refrain's joy is thus not stoic resignation but a *received competence* of the soul.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *joy/enjoyment as received gift (the refrain)* (new thread — the book's one positive answer; recurs 3:12–13, 3:22, 5:18–20, 8:15, 9:7–10, 11:7–9); *the capacity-to-enjoy as itself a gift* (new — the hidden precision under the refrain).

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Validation summary:** substrate strong; *leb* (heart) seating consistently correct and load-bearing (the whole chapter is the heart examining itself). One systemic residual persists: **`seat=spirit` on elemental *ruach*** in the "striving after wind" idiom (vv.11,17,26) — to discount. The neg-particle `prohibition` stamp at v.23 is *correct in trigger* (real negation) but over-spreads to neighbours.
- **New characteristics this chapter:** *the appetite fully indulged yet unfilled*; *the self-experimenting heart*; *the hatred of life*; *the sleepless/unrested heart*; *heir-anxiety*; *joy-as-received-gift (refrain)*; *the capacity-to-enjoy as gift*. **Shared:** *desire (the reaching eyes)*; *the self-addressing heart*.
- **Threads:** *never-satisfied* deepened (2:10–11 — the fullest indulgence still empty); *joy refrain* opened (2:24); *oblivion* recurs (2:16 "no enduring remembrance").

---

## Ecclesiastes 3 - inner-being unit readings

# Ecclesiastes 3 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** Phase-1 lexicals for Ecc 3:1–22, read per `segment_unit` (provenance `ecclesiastes-segmentation-v1-20260703`). Complete chapter. Cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the inner-being **operation** is the finding; time/God's providence is the arena.

---

## ECC-03-A · Ecc 3:1–8 · [D, multi] — the appointed rhythms of the affections; a time for everything

**The reading.** The famous seasons poem is usually read as cosmology; read through the inner-being lens it is a *catalogue of the affections placed under time*. Among the twenty-eight paired times, a whole cluster is emotional and relational: "a time to **weep** and a time to **laugh**; a time to **mourn** and a time to **dance**… a time to **embrace** and a time to refrain from embracing… a time to **love** and a time to **hate**; a time for war and a time for **peace**" (vv.4,5,8). The finding is **the inner life's movements as seasoned, not sovereign** — weeping, laughing, mourning, loving, hating each has *its* time, appointed rather than willed *(stated)*. The operation the unit foregrounds is **the affections as timed** — the self does not simply *have* a feeling; the feeling belongs to a season it does not set, so that grief and joy are neither to be manufactured nor refused but *met when they come* *(inferred: set against the chapter's later "eternity in the heart" (v.11), the poem says the interior lives inside a rhythm larger than itself — the emotions are answerable to a time the self did not choose)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** Notably, the emotion-verbs here are correctly promoted to `characteristic`: *weep* (H1058), *mourn* (H5594), *love* (H0157, *aheb*), *hate* (H8130), *seek* (H1245), *keep* (H8104), *keep silence* (H2814), plus *peace* (H7965). This is exactly right — each names an inner-being movement. The recurring **positional-target mis-fire** attaches *time* (H6256) as the "object" of each verb (*weep→time*, *love→time*, flagged `unverified`) — these are false objects (the verbs are intransitive here, "a time to weep"); correctly self-flagged, and the reading discounts them. The *aheb* promotion (love as characteristic) is the fix working as intended.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** (1) **The pairing of every affection with its opposite** — weep/laugh, love/hate, embrace/refrain: the poem holds that no inner movement is the whole truth; each has a countervailing season, so the mature self is *not* fixed in one register (a hidden characteristic — the affectively balanced, non-absolutising interior). (2) **"A time to keep silence and a time to speak"** (v.7) — silence itself named as an inner-being discipline with its season, kin to the guarded mouth of 5:1–7.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *the affections placed under time (seasoned, not sovereign)* (new — Ecclesiastes' distinctive framing of emotion); *the balancing of each affection with its opposite* (new); *love / hate / grief / joy as timed movements* (shared vocab w/ Ps, reframed).

---

## ECC-03-B · Ecc 3:9–15 · [D, multi, thread] — eternity set in the heart; the God-given limit of knowing; joy and fear

**The reading.** The chapter's gem, and one of the deepest inner-being lines in Scripture: "**he has put eternity into man's heart**, yet so that he **cannot find out** what God has done from the beginning to the end" (v.11). The finding is a *structural ache built into the interior* — the human heart is fitted with a sense of the eternal, a reach beyond the moment, and simultaneously **fenced from the very knowledge that reach craves** *(stated)*. This is not a defect to fix but the designed condition of the self: made for eternity, denied the overview. Out of it the unit draws two responses. First the joy-refrain again — "nothing better than to be **joyful** and to **do good**… **eat and drink and take pleasure** in all his toil — this is God's gift" (vv.12–13). Second, fear: God's work "**endures forever**… so that people **fear before him**" (v.14). The operation is **the heart stretched between eternity and its limit, and steadied by joy and fear** — the ache is not resolved by more knowledge (which is withheld) but held livable by present enjoyment and reverence *(inferred: v.11 diagnoses the restlessness the whole book feels; vv.12–14 prescribe not answers but postures — receive joy, revere God — for a heart that cannot see the whole)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *joyful* (H8055), *fear* (H3372), *good* (H2896), *seeks* (H1245) correctly `characteristic`. The pivotal "eternity into man's heart" — *heart* (H3820) correctly seated (`seat=heart`); the phrase sits partly in gate-2 content, and the reading rests on the verse structure. *fear before him* (v.14) correctly carries the reverence-operation. Sound; no material mis-tag.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** (1) **The eternity-shaped heart** — a characteristic in its own right, and arguably the diagnostic key to the whole book: the never-satisfied thread (1:8, 4:8, 6:7) may be *this* — a heart built for the eternal cannot be filled by the temporal. (2) **Knowing deliberately withheld as part of the gift** — "*yet so that* he cannot find out": the limit is *given*, not merely encountered; the self's ignorance is designed, which reframes the frustration of 1:13–18 as a condition to be lived reverently, not a failure.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *the eternity-shaped heart (made for the eternal, fenced from the overview)* (new — a candidate organising insight); *the God-given limit of knowing* (new); *joy and fear as the postures that make the limit livable* (new); *fear of God* (shared cornerstone w/ Ps/Pro).

---

## ECC-03-C · Ecc 3:16–22 · [D, multi] — the self facing judgment and its own creatureliness

**The reading.** The observer turns to injustice — "in the place of **justice**, even there was **wickedness**" (v.16) — and steadies on the thought "God will **judge** the righteous and the wicked" (v.17). Then a hard reflection on what the human being *is*: God "is **testing** them that they may see that they themselves are but **beasts**" (v.18); "as one **dies**, so dies the other. They all have the **same breath**, and man has no advantage over the beasts" (v.19); "all are from the **dust**, and to dust all **return**" (v.20). The finding is **the self confronting its own creatureliness** — the same breath as the animal, the same dust, the same death *(stated)*. The open question is left genuinely open: "**who knows** whether the spirit of man goes upward and the spirit of the beast goes down?" (v.21). The unit resolves not in dread but back to the refrain: "**rejoice in his work**, for that is his **lot**" (v.22). The operation is **the self sized against death and returned to present work** — humbled to dust, uncertain of what lies beyond, it is directed once more to joy in the task at hand *(inferred: creatureliness is not despair here but a *right-sizing*; the unknown afterlife (v.21) is met, again, not with speculation but with present rejoicing (v.22))*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *judge* (H8199, target *wicked*), *justice* (H4941), *righteousness* (H6664), *knows* (H3045), *rejoice* (H8055) correctly `characteristic`. The two *ruach* tags here are the **genuinely human** ones: "same **breath**" (H7307, v.19) and "the **spirit** of man / of beast" (H7307, v.21) — here `seat=spirit` is *correct* (contrast the elemental-wind mis-fires of chs.1–2), and the construct pairs *of man* / *of beast* are rightly specifier-tagged. The reading rests on these. Sound.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** (1) **Creatureliness as a deliberately administered lesson** — "God is *testing* them *that they may see*… they are but beasts" (v.18): the self's humbling is a *pedagogy*, not merely a fact; the inner-being operation is *being brought to see one's own dust*. (2) **The open afterlife question held without resolution** — "who knows?" (v.21): the honest agnosticism is itself an inner-being posture the book models — reverent not-knowing rather than false certainty.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *the self confronting its creatureliness (dust, beast, same breath)* (new); *being humbled as a divine pedagogy* (new); *reverent not-knowing (the held-open afterlife question)* (new); *rejoicing in one's lot / work* (thread w/ the joy refrain).

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Validation summary:** substrate strong; the *aheb*/emotion promotions in the seasons poem (v.8) confirm the characteristic-fix. Key validation win: the **`seat=spirit` tag is correct at 3:19,21** (human *ruach* — breath/spirit) and *mis-fires at the "striving after wind" idiom* elsewhere — the contrast is now sharp evidence for the rule-adjustment (seat=spirit should gate on surface/context, firing for breath/spirit-of-man, not for elemental wind). Positional-target mis-fires abundant in the seasons poem (intransitive verbs + *time*), all self-flagged.
- **New characteristics this chapter:** *the affections placed under time*; *the eternity-shaped heart*; *the God-given limit of knowing*; *the self confronting creatureliness*; *reverent not-knowing*. **Shared:** *fear of God*; *love/hate/grief/joy*; *joy refrain (3:12–13, 3:22)*.
- **Threads:** *joy refrain* (3:12–13, 3:22); *the never-satisfied* possibly *explained* here by the eternity-shaped heart (3:11) — a candidate cross-unit link to carry into Phase-2 synthesis.

---

## Ecclesiastes 4 - inner-being unit readings

# Ecclesiastes 4 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** Phase-1 lexicals for Ecc 4:1–16, read per `segment_unit` (provenance `ecclesiastes-segmentation-v1-20260703`). Complete chapter. Cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the inner-being **operation** is the finding; oppression/toil/society is the arena.

---

## ECC-04-A · Ecc 4:1–3 · [D, multi] — the tears of the oppressed with no comforter; the observer's grief

**The reading.** The observer looks at the oppressed and the line lands twice, deliberately: "the **tears of the oppressed**, and they had **no one to comfort them**… and there was **no one to comfort them**" (v.1). The finding is **uncomforted suffering** — not the oppression alone but the *absence of a comforter*, the isolation inside the pain, named as the sharpest edge of it *(stated)*. On the oppressors' side "there was **power**," and against that power no counter-comfort. So bitter is the observer's grief that he judges "the **dead** who are already dead more fortunate than the **living**" (v.2), and better still the never-born who has not seen the evil (v.3). The operation is **grief so deep it inverts the value of living** — the compassionate observer, absorbing the uncomforted tears, arrives at a preference for non-existence over a world this cruel *(inferred: the doubled "no comforter" is the load-bearing phrase — the wound is the *aloneness* in suffering; the observer's own inner state (a grief that would rather not exist) is the finding, distinct from the oppression that occasions it)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *tears* (H1832), *comfort* (H5162, twice, target *all*), *power* (H3581), *living/alive* (H2416) correctly carried. *comfort* rightly `characteristic` — and its *negation* is the finding (no comforter), which the reading takes from the verse. Sound; the doubling in the lexical (comfort appearing twice) matches the text's deliberate repetition.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** (1) **The comforter-shaped absence** — the inner-being datum is a *lack*: the self needs a comforter and finds none; this makes "comfort" a relational operation whose failure is itself a wound (contrast the Psalter, where "you comfort me," Ps 23:4, 71:21 — here the comfort never comes). (2) **Compassion that turns into a death-wish** — the observer's grief is not detached; absorbing others' tears bends his own valuation of life toward the grave (a distinct and dark inner-being movement, kin to but sharper than 2:17's hatred of life — here caused by *others'* pain, not his own leveling).

**Characteristics surfaced:** *uncomforted suffering (the missing comforter)* (new — the failure of a relational operation); *compassion that inverts the value of living* (new); *the grieving observer* (thread w/ the watching-self frame).

---

## ECC-04-B · Ecc 4:4–6 · [D, multi] — envy-driven toil vs the quiet handful

**The reading.** A piercing diagnosis of achievement's hidden motive: "all **toil** and all skill in work come from a man's **envy** of his neighbor" (v.4). The finding is **industry rooted in rivalry** — the drive that looks like excellence is, underneath, comparison and envy; the self works not from love of the work but from measuring itself against another *(stated)*. Against both the envious striver and the opposite folly (the fool who "folds his hands and eats his own flesh," v.5), the unit sets its resolution: "**better is a handful of quietness** than two hands full of toil and a striving after wind" (v.6). The operation is **restful sufficiency chosen over envious striving** — the deliberate preference for *less held peacefully* over *more grasped anxiously* *(inferred: the "handful of quietness" names an inner state (menuchah — rest/quiet) as the true good, exposing the envy-engine of v.4 as the thing that makes "two hands full" worthless)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *envy* (H7068, v.4, specifier *of neighbor*) correctly `characteristic` — the reading's spine, and correctly bound to its object (envy *of the neighbour*) via the specifier pair. *quietness* (H5183, v.6), *toil* (H5999), *flesh* (H1320, `seat=flesh` — "eats his own flesh," correct fleshly seat), *better* (H2896) correctly carried. The "striving after wind" *ruach* seat mis-fire recurs (discount). Strong substrate.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** (1) **Envy as the secret engine of excellence** — not envy as an occasional sin but as the *systemic driver* of "all toil and all skill": a radical inner-being claim that much of human achievement is comparison in disguise (a hidden characteristic sharper than any Psalter treatment). (2) **Quietness (menuchah) as a *possessed* good** — "a *handful* of quietness": rest imagined as something the self can hold in the hand, a small sufficiency actively chosen; the contented interior as an alternative economy to the envious one.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *envy-driven toil (achievement as disguised rivalry)* (new — a Qoheleth diagnosis); *restful sufficiency / quietness chosen over striving* (new — kin to the Psalter's stilled soul, Ps 131); *envy* (shared vocab, sharpened).

---

## ECC-04-C · Ecc 4:7–8 · [D, multi, thread] — the insatiable, isolated toiler

**The reading.** A single figure carries the never-satisfied thread to its loneliest point: a man "who has **no other**, either son or brother, yet there is **no end** to all his toil, and his **eyes are never satisfied** with riches" (v.8). The finding is **accumulation emptied of a why** — endless toil and un-satisfiable eyes, with no one to accumulate *for* *(stated)*. The self even hears its own question and cannot answer it: "'**For whom am I toiling** and depriving myself of pleasure?'" (v.8). The operation is **the insatiable eye compounded by isolation** — the never-filled appetite (1:8, 6:7) here made unbearable because there is no relationship to give it meaning; the toiler *deprives his own soul* of pleasure for the sake of nothing *(inferred: "depriving **myself** (nephesh — soul) of pleasure" makes explicit that the never-satisfied eye actively starves the soul; the unit binds insatiability to aloneness — the appetite that cannot be filled is worst when there is no one it serves)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *riches* (H6239), *toil* (H5999), *unhappy* (H7451) carried. Crucially *myself* (H5315, v.8) correctly carries `seat=soul` (nephesh) — "depriving my **soul** of pleasure": the reading rests on this, the soul as the deprived seat. *pleasure* (H2896) correctly the thing withheld. The neg-particle `prohibition` stamp on *toil*/*riches* reflects the real "never satisfied / no end"; over-spreads mildly. Sound.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** **The self depriving its own soul** — the reflexive cruelty of "depriving *myself* (nephesh)": the insatiable toiler is not merely unfulfilled, he *actively withholds good from his own soul*, a self-starving operation. This is the never-satisfied thread turned inward and made tragic — the appetite that cannot be filled ends by refusing the soul the very pleasure it could have.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *the insatiable eye + isolation (accumulation without a why)* (new — the loneliest form of never-satisfied); *the self that deprives its own soul* (new — reflexive self-starvation); *never-satisfied* (thread, 1:8 → here → 5:10, 6:7).

---

## ECC-04-D · Ecc 4:9–12 · [D] — the self's need of another; companionship against aloneness

**The reading.** Directly answering the isolated toiler of 4:8, the unit turns to bond: "**two are better than one**, because they have a good reward for their toil. For if they **fall**, one will **lift up his fellow**… **woe to him who is alone** when he falls" (vv.9–10). Warmth, defence, and endurance all flow from the bond — "a **threefold cord is not quickly broken**" (v.12). The finding is **the self as constituted for relationship, exposed in isolation** — the human being is not self-sufficient; it needs another to lift it, warm it, stand with it *(stated)*. The operation is **the vulnerability of the alone self and the strength of the joined self** — aloneness is named not as freedom but as *danger* ("woe to him who is alone") *(inferred: read against 4:8, this unit is the diagnosis's remedy — the insatiable toiler's real poverty was that he had "no other"; here the good is precisely the "other" he lacked)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *better* (H2896), *good* (H2896), *toil* (H5999), *fellow* (H2270), *prevail* (H8630) carried. The relational nouns (*fellow*, the *one/two*) correctly `standalone`/`characteristic`; the reading is structural (the "two vs one" contrast) and well-supported. Sound.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** **Aloneness as danger, not autonomy** — the modern reflex hears "independence" as strength; the unit hears it as *woe* ("woe to him who is alone when he falls"). The inner-being finding is that the self's resilience is *relational*, held up from outside; a hidden characteristic that reframes the whole book's solitary observer as itself a kind of exposure.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *the self constituted for relationship (two better than one)* (new — the relational answer to isolation); *aloneness as exposure/danger* (new); *the bond as resilience (the threefold cord)* (new).

---

## ECC-04-E · Ecc 4:13–16 · [D, multi] — the un-teachable old king; the fickle favour of the crowd

**The reading.** Two inner-being notes in a small political parable. First, unteachability: "**better was a poor and wise youth** than an old and foolish king who **no longer knew how to take advice**" (v.13) — age and power have not made the king wise; they have made him *closed*, unable to receive counsel *(stated)*. Second, the fickleness of favour: the crowd who followed the rising youth, "those who come later will **not rejoice in him**" (v.16). The finding is **unteachability as the true poverty, and the crowd's love as unreliable** — the closed heart that "no longer knew how to take advice" is worse off than youth and poverty; and the applause it might crave is itself unstable *(inferred: the two combine into a warning against the inner postures that power breeds — a heart shut to correction, and a hunger for a favour that will not last; the reading keeps the lens on the *dispositions* (closedness, the craving for and instability of approval), not the political mechanics)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *better* (H2896), *wise* (H2450), *knew* (H3045, with real negation "no longer knew"), *living* (H2416), *rejoice* (H8055, with negation "will not rejoice") correctly carried. The two negations are genuine (unteachability, un-rejoicing), so the `prohibition` stamps are trigger-correct. The *ruach*-wind seat recurs at v.16 ("striving after wind," discount). Sound.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** (1) **Unteachability as an acquired closedness** — "*no longer* knew how to take advice": the king *once* could and has *lost* the capacity; teachability is framed as something that can atrophy with age and power (a hidden dynamic — the closing of a once-open heart, kin to Proverbs' scoffer but here a *decline*, not a type). (2) **The instability of received favour** — the crowd's love as a thing that comes and goes independent of the self's worth; a warning against staking the interior on approval.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *unteachability as acquired closedness (the heart that can no longer take advice)* (new — a *decline* of teachability); *the instability of the crowd's favour* (new); *teachability* (shared thread w/ Pro).

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Validation summary:** substrate strong; two seat-validation points of note — **`seat=soul` (nephesh) correct at 4:8** ("depriving myself/soul") and **`seat=flesh` correct at 4:5** ("eats his own flesh"), both load-bearing for the readings; the *ruach*-wind seat mis-fire recurs (vv.4,6,16). Negation-`prohibition` stamps at 4:8,13,16 are trigger-correct (real negations) though they over-spread.
- **New characteristics this chapter:** *uncomforted suffering*; *compassion inverting the value of living*; *envy-driven toil*; *restful sufficiency*; *the self that deprives its own soul*; *the self constituted for relationship*; *aloneness as exposure*; *unteachability as acquired closedness*; *the instability of favour*. **Shared:** *envy*; *never-satisfied thread*; *teachability*.
- **Threads:** *never-satisfied* (4:8); the chapter forms a **diagnosis→remedy arc** (4:7–8 isolated insatiable toiler → 4:9–12 the relational answer) worth carrying into synthesis.

---

## Ecclesiastes 5 - inner-being unit readings

# Ecclesiastes 5 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** Phase-1 lexicals for Ecc 5:1–20, read per `segment_unit` (provenance `ecclesiastes-segmentation-v1-20260703`). Complete chapter. Cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the inner-being **operation** is the finding; worship, money and toil are the arena.

---

## ECC-05-A · Ecc 5:1–7 · [D, multi] — reverent restraint before God; the guarded mouth and few words

**The reading.** The one sustained passage on worship in the book makes reverence a matter of *inner restraint*: "**Guard your steps** when you go to the house of God. To draw near to **listen** is better than to offer the sacrifice of fools" (v.1) — reverence begins as *listening*, not performing *(stated)*. Then the heart and mouth: "**be not rash with your mouth**, nor let your **heart be hasty** to utter a word before God, for God is in heaven and you are on earth; therefore let your **words be few**" (v.2). The finding is **awe expressed as the restraint of speech and heart** — the properly reverent interior is *slow*, *quiet*, *listening*, aware of the distance between earth and heaven *(stated)*. The unit closes by naming the ground of it: "**God is the one you must fear**" (v.7). The operation is **reverent fear enacted as verbal and inner economy** — the fearing self does not fill the silence before God with words but holds itself in listening restraint *(inferred: the rash mouth and hasty heart (v.2) are the failures of a self that does not feel the earth/heaven gap; the fear of God (v.7) is what quiets them — reverence as the discipline of the tongue and the racing heart)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *Guard* (H8104), *listen* (H8085), *know* (H3045), *rash* (H0926), *fear* (H3372) correctly `characteristic`. *heart* (H3820) seated (`seat=heart`) as the thing not to let be hasty — load-bearing. Note *mouth* (H6310) tagged variously `seat=heart` (v.2) and `seat=flesh` (v.6) — the mouth is the *outlet* of heart and flesh, a reasonable seat-attribution though the mouth is properly the organ of speech, not itself a seat; a mild over-attribution, not affecting the reading. The neg-particle `prohibition` stamps (v.2 "be *not* rash," v.6 "let *not* your mouth") are trigger-correct (real prohibitions — this *is* imperative instruction). Sound.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** (1) **Listening as the first act of worship** — "to draw near to *listen*" (v.1): reverence is receptive before it is expressive; the inner posture is an *open ear*, not an offered sacrifice (a hidden characteristic — worship as intake, kin to Ps 40:6 "an ear you have dug for me"). (2) **The earth/heaven gap as the regulator of speech** — "God is in heaven and you are on earth" (v.2): the self's *sense of its own smallness before God* is what produces the few words; awe felt as spatial distance, disciplining the tongue.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *reverent restraint (the guarded mouth, the un-hasty heart)* (new — worship as inner economy); *listening as the first posture of worship* (new); *the fear of God* (shared cornerstone, here enacted as verbal restraint); *the sense of the earth/heaven gap* (new).

---

## ECC-05-B · Ecc 5:8–9 · [S] — the oppression of the poor observed; tiers of watching power

**The reading.** A brief observer's note: seeing "the **oppression of the poor** and the violation of justice and righteousness in a province, **do not be amazed** at the matter, for the high official is **watched by a higher**, and there are yet higher ones over them" (v.8). The inner-being finding is slight but real: **the steadying of the self against outrage** — "do not be amazed" counsels a composure that does not come undone at systemic injustice, because the tiers of power watch each other *(stated)*. The operation is **composure before a rigged order** — not approval of the oppression, but a refusal to let it destabilise the interior *(inferred: the observer, who elsewhere grieves the oppressed to the point of a death-wish (4:1–3), here counsels a different response — not shock but a sober, un-amazed recognition of how power is layered; the two responses (grief in ch.4, composure here) are both honest inner-being postures toward the same evil)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *justice* (H4941), *righteousness* (H6664), *amazed* (H8539), *watched* (H8104), *high official/higher* (H1364) carried. *amazed* correctly `characteristic` — the inner reaction the verse counsels against (with real negation "do *not* be amazed"). The bulk is social observation sitting `standalone`; the reading extracts the thin inner-being thread (composure), correctly.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** **Two legitimate inner responses to the same injustice** — the book holds *both* the grief of 4:1 and the composure of 5:8 without resolving them; the inner-being datum is that a mature interior can weep at oppression *and* refuse to be destabilised by it, depending on the season (cf. the seasoned affections of 3:1–8).

**Characteristics surfaced:** *composure before a rigged order (the un-amazed self)* (new — thin but real); *the coexistence of grief and composure toward injustice* (new — a cross-unit note w/ 4:1).

---

## ECC-05-C · Ecc 5:10–17 · [D, multi, thread] — the money-lover never satisfied; riches held to one's own hurt

**The reading.** The never-satisfied thread meets money directly: "he who **loves money** will **not be satisfied** with money, nor he who **loves wealth** with his income" (v.10). The finding is **desire that its own object cannot fill** — loving money guarantees dissatisfaction *with money*, because the appetite is not for the thing but is bottomless *(stated)*. Then the somatic cost: "the **full stomach** of the rich will **not let him sleep**" (v.12) — abundance producing insomnia, where the labourer's sleep is "sweet." And the tragedy of hoarding: "riches were **kept by their owner to his hurt**" then lost, leaving "**nothing in his hand**" (vv.13–14); "all his days he **eats in darkness**, in much **vexation and sickness and anger**" (v.17). The operation is **the money-loving self consuming itself** — the appetite that cannot be satisfied turns abundance into sleeplessness, hoarding into loss, and the whole life into a dark, vexed, angry consumption *(inferred: v.10 states the law (love of money is structurally un-fillable); vv.12–17 trace its bodily and emotional wages — the never-satisfied thread here produces not just emptiness but active torment, "vexation and sickness and anger")*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *loves* (H0157, *aheb* — "loves money," the misdirected affection, correctly `characteristic` under the aheb-fix), *vexation* (H3708), *sickness* (H2483), *anger* (H7110), *grievous* (H2470), *evil* (H7451), *riches* (H6239) all carried. The love-of-money as *characteristic* is exactly the aheb promotion working — desire fastened on the wrong object. Sound; strong substrate for the reading.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** (1) **The self-defeating structure of money-love** — not "money is bad" but "*loving* money guarantees dissatisfaction *with money*": the appetite is mis-calibrated to an object that cannot answer it (the same shape as the eternity-shaped heart of 3:11 — a reach the temporal cannot fill, here fastened destructively on wealth). (2) **Abundance as insomnia** — "the full stomach will not let him sleep" (v.12): the finding that *having more* actively steals rest, inverting the ordinary assumption; the anxious rich interior.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *money-love as structurally un-fillable desire* (new — the never-satisfied thread fastened on wealth); *abundance as sleeplessness / the anxious rich* (new); *the self consumed by vexation, sickness and anger* (new); *misdirected love (aheb on money)* (shared w/ Ps 4:2 "love vanity," Pro 1:22).

---

## ECC-05-D · Ecc 5:18–20 · [T, multi, thread] — joy as the gift of God (refrain); the occupied heart

**The reading.** The refrain returns, now with a crucial addition. The good is "to **eat and drink and find enjoyment** in all the toil" (v.18); but the fuller gift is when God gives wealth "**and power to enjoy them**, and to **accept his lot** and **rejoice** in his toil — this is the **gift of God**" (v.19). The finding is **enjoyment as a granted capacity plus an accepted lot** — not merely having good things but the God-given *power to enjoy* them and the inner willingness to *accept one's portion* *(stated)*. The gem is the last verse: "he will **not much remember** the days of his life because God **keeps him occupied with joy in his heart**" (v.20). The operation is **joy that occupies the heart and quiets the reckoning** — the enjoying self is so filled with present gladness that it stops tallying the days (the very tallying that produced the vanity-verdict elsewhere) *(inferred: joy here is not distraction but a divine *occupation* of the interior — "occupied with joy in his heart"; against the ruminating, day-counting, never-satisfied self of 5:10–17, this is its healed opposite — a heart so engaged by present joy it is released from anxious remembrance)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *enjoyment/good* (H2896), *rejoice* (H8055), *given* (H5414, the gift-operation, twice), *wealth* (H6239), *remember* (H2142), *occupied* (H6031), *heart* (H3820, seated) correctly carried. The pivot *occupied* (H6031, v.20) is correctly `characteristic` — God occupying the heart with joy; load-bearing for the reading. Sound.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** (1) **The power-to-enjoy as distinct from the goods enjoyed** — "wealth *and power to enjoy them*" (v.19): the inner capacity for enjoyment is itself the gift, set up here for its tragic negation in 6:2 (wealth given, power-to-enjoy withheld). (2) **Joy as release from the day-counting mind** — "he will not much remember the days… because God keeps him occupied with joy" (v.20): joy that *displaces* anxious rumination; the healed interior is not one that has answered the vanity-question but one so occupied with present gladness it no longer asks it.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *joy as granted capacity + accepted lot (the refrain deepened)* (thread, w/ 2:24, 3:12); *the power-to-enjoy as gift* (new — set against 6:2); *joy that occupies the heart and quiets the reckoning* (new — the healed opposite of the ruminating self).

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Validation summary:** substrate strong; the *aheb* "loves money" (5:10) is a clean characteristic-promotion (misdirected affection). Seat notes: *heart* (leb) consistently correct and load-bearing; a mild **mouth-as-seat over-attribution** (5:2,6 — mouth tagged seat=heart/flesh) worth flagging (the mouth is an organ/outlet, not a seat). Neg-particle `prohibition` stamps at 5:1–6 are trigger-correct (genuine imperatives).
- **New characteristics this chapter:** *reverent restraint (worship as inner economy)*; *listening as worship*; *composure before a rigged order*; *money-love as un-fillable desire*; *abundance as sleeplessness*; *joy that occupies the heart*; *the power-to-enjoy as gift*. **Shared:** *fear of God*; *misdirected love (aheb)*; *joy refrain*; *never-satisfied thread*.
- **Threads:** *never-satisfied* (5:10, fastened on money); *joy refrain* (5:18–20, deepened with "power to enjoy"); a cross-unit **contrast pair** — the sleepless money-lover (5:12) vs the joy-occupied heart that forgets to count its days (5:20).

---
