## Lamentations 5 - inner-being unit readings

# Lamentations 5 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** Phase-1 lexicals for Lam 5:1–22, read per `segment_unit` (provenance `lamentations-segmentation-v1-20260703`). Complete chapter. Cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the inner-being **operation**; the community's closing prayer is the arena. Not an acrostic — a bare, direct plea.

---

## LAM-05-A · Lam 5:1–18 · [D, multi, thread] — the communal lament; the sick heart; joy ceased; guilt owned

**The reading.** The final poem drops the acrostic form and becomes a plain communal prayer: "**Remember, O LORD, what has befallen us; look, and see our disgrace!**" (v.1). It catalogues the loss — orphaned, weary ("we are given **no rest**", v.5), enslaved, hungry. The interior toll: "the **joy of our hearts has ceased**; our **dancing has been turned to mourning**" (v.15); "for this our **heart has become sick**, for these things our **eyes have grown dim**" (v.17); and the confession, "**woe to us, for we have sinned**!" (v.16). The finding is **a whole community's grief — joy ceased, heart sick, rest gone — owned with confession** *(stated)*. The operation is **the corporate self naming its collective sickness of heart and turning it Godward with "Remember"** *(inferred: the shift to "us/our" (the community) makes this a *shared* interior — "the joy of our hearts has ceased… our heart has become sick" (vv.15,17): the finding is that grief here is corporate, a whole people's joylessness and heart-sickness; and it opens (as ch.1 did) with the plea to be *seen* — "Remember, O LORD… look, and see" (v.1), the same recourse of the comfortless self; the confession "we have sinned" (v.16) keeps the honest posture of the whole book (owned guilt, not protested innocence); "we are given no rest" (v.5) echoes the lost *nuach* of 1:3 — the community, like the city, can find no place to lay itself down; the inner-being datum is the shared sick heart, joy ceased, turning its collective disgrace Godward)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *Remember* (H2142, zakar — "Remember, O LORD"), *disgrace* (H2781, cherpah), *rest* (H5117, nuach — "given no rest"), *sinned* (H2398, chata — twice), *iniquities* (H5771, avon), *raped* (H6031, anah), *joy* (H4885, masos — "the joy of our hearts has ceased"), *hearts/heart* (H3820, leb — twice), *become sick* (H1739, daveh — "our heart has become sick"), *desolate* (H8074, shamem) carried. *masos*/*leb*/*daveh* (joy ceased / heart / sick) carry the interior toll; *zakar* (Remember) the plea; *nuach* (no rest, echoing 1:3) the lost rest; correctly tagged. Sound.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** (1) **The corporate sick heart (grief as shared)** — "the joy of our hearts has ceased… our heart has become sick" (vv.15,17): the finding that this grief is *collective* — a whole community's joylessness and heart-sickness, not one individual's (as ch.3 was); the shared interior naming its condition. (2) **"Remember, O LORD" as the comfortless community's recourse** — "Remember… look, and see our disgrace" (v.1): the finding that the corporate self, like the personified city (1:9,11), can still do one thing — ask God to *see and remember* — the minimal act of a faith that has lost everything but the address. And "no rest" (v.5, nuach) echoes 1:3 — the lost *nuach* is corporate too.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *the corporate sick heart (grief as shared)* (new — the communal interior, joy ceased, heart sick); *"Remember, O LORD" as the comfortless community's recourse (the plea to be seen)* (thread — 1:9,11 → 5:1); *owned guilt in corporate grief (we have sinned)* (thread — the confessing lament); *no rest / lost nuach, corporate* (thread w/ 1:3, Job 3:13).

---

## LAM-05-B · Lam 5:19–22 · [D, multi, thread] — the final prayer: restore us — held against an unresolved dread

**The reading.** The book ends not in resolution but in a prayer suspended over a fear: "**but you, O LORD, reign forever**; your throne endures to all generations" (v.19); "why do you **forget us** forever, why do you **forsake us** for so many days?" (v.20); "**Restore us to yourself, O LORD, that we may be restored! Renew our days as of old** — **unless you have utterly rejected us**, and you remain exceedingly angry with us" (vv.21–22). The finding is **a plea for restoration grounded in God's eternal reign, held open against an unresolved dread of final rejection** *(stated)*. The operation is **the self reaching for restoration it cannot presume, ending on a plea rather than an assurance** *(inferred: the ending is remarkable for its *honesty* — after the turn of ch.3 (hope re-kindled), the book does *not* close with triumphant assurance but with "restore us… *unless* you have utterly rejected us" (vv.21–22); the finding is that faith can hold a real hope (grounded in "you, O LORD, reign forever", v.19, and the memory of God's chesed, 3:22) *together with* an unresolved fear (the "unless" of v.22) — it prays for restoration it cannot presume; and the theology of restoration is precise — "Restore us *to yourself*… that we may be restored" (v.21): the return is God's work (he must restore us before we can be restored), and its goal is *God himself* ("to yourself"), not merely improved circumstances (the same "God as portion" of 3:24); the inner-being datum: mature faith prays honestly into an open future — it hopes without presuming, holds the "unless", and rests its whole plea on God's eternal reign and its own longing to be restored *to him*)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *angry* (H7107, qatsaph — "you remain exceedingly angry") carried; the reign/forget/forsake/restore language sits in gate-2 content, read structurally. *qatsaph* (angry) carries the unresolved dread of v.22; the "restore us to yourself" rests on the verse structure (shuv — return, doubled), unambiguous. Sound (sparse substrate, structural reading of a bare prayer).

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** (1) **Hope holding an unresolved "unless"** — "restore us… unless you have utterly rejected us" (vv.21–22): the finding that mature faith can pray a real hope (grounded in God's eternal reign, v.19) *together with* an honest, unresolved dread — it hopes without presuming, ending on a plea, not an assurance. The book's refusal of a tidy resolution is itself a profound inner-being witness: faith prays truthfully into an open future. (2) **Restoration as God's work, toward God himself** — "restore us *to yourself*, that we may be restored" (v.21): the finding that the return is God's doing (he must restore before we can be restored) and its *goal* is God himself (the "God as portion" of 3:24), not merely better circumstances — the deepest longing is not relief but *re-union*.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *hope holding an unresolved "unless" (faith praying into an open future)* (new — the book's honest ending; hope without presumption); *restoration as God's work toward God himself (restore us TO yourself)* (thread — God as the goal/portion, w/ 3:24); *the plea grounded in God's eternal reign* (new — the one fixed point).

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Validation summary:** substrate solid at 5:1–18 (sparser at the bare closing prayer, 5:19–22); *masos/leb/daveh* (joy ceased / sick heart, 5:15,17), *zakar* (Remember, 5:1), *nuach* (no rest, 5:5, echoing 1:3), and *qatsaph* (angry, 5:22) cleanly carried. The final prayer is read structurally. No new residuals.
- **New characteristics:** *the corporate sick heart*; *"Remember, O LORD" as the comfortless community's recourse*; *hope holding an unresolved "unless"*; *restoration as God's work toward God himself*. **Shared:** *the plea to be seen (1:9,11)*; *no rest / nuach (1:3, Job 3:13)*; *God as portion/goal (3:24)*.
- **Threads CLOSED / held here:** *the plea to be seen* recurs to the end (5:1); *lost nuach-rest* (5:5, from 1:3); *God as the goal of restoration* (5:21, from 3:24) — the deepest longing is re-union, not relief; and the book's signature honesty — it ends on a *plea* (5:22, "unless you have utterly rejected us"), holding real hope and unresolved dread together. The whole book: grief fully voiced (1–2), the turn to God's unfailing chesed at the centre (3:22–24), and a final honest prayer that hopes without presuming (5:21–22).

---

## Proverbs 3 - inner-being unit readings

# Proverbs 3 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 3:1–35, per `segment_unit`. Complete chapter. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation** (God/wisdom = arena).

---

**PRO-03-A · 3:1–4 · [D] — the heart as a writing-surface.** "Let your **heart keep** my commandments… **bind** steadfast love and faithfulness around your neck; **write them on the tablet of your heart**" (vv.1–3). The finding: internalisation is figured as **inscription** — the self *engraves* the teaching (and *chesed* + faithfulness) *onto its own heart* *(stated)*; a distinct image of the interior as a **tablet that can be written on** *(inferred; cf. Ps 40:8 "your law is within my heart")*. *Validation:* clean; *years→of life*, *sight→of God* (specifiers) confirm the arena. *Hidden:* **the heart as inscribable surface** (a new image of receptivity). *Surfaced:* internalisation-as-inscription (new); receptivity (shared).

**PRO-03-B · 3:5–8 · [D, multi] — trust as the renunciation of self-reliance.** "**Trust** in the LORD with **all your heart**, and **do not lean on your own understanding**… **fear** the LORD, and **turn away from evil**" (vv.5–7). The cornerstone. The finding: whole-hearted trust is defined by what it **refuses** — *leaning on one's own understanding* — so trust is an **abdication of self-sufficiency**, not merely confidence *(stated: the two halves are set against each other)*. *(inferred: the inner posture is constituted negatively — to trust God is to stop trusting the self; cf. Ps 131:1's un-over-reaching heart, and the trust cluster.)* *Validation (strong):* the v1.1 substrate nails it — *all* → seat=heart, **specifier=of heart**, intensity=all ("with ALL your heart"); *fear* (H3372) → **target=Lord** ("fear the LORD"). *Hidden:* **trust as self-distrust** (the renunciation of one's own understanding). *Surfaced:* trust vs self-reliance (shared cornerstone, sharpened); fear of the LORD (shared).

**PRO-03-C · 3:9–12 · [D, multi] — receiving correction as fatherly love.** "Do not **despise** the LORD's **discipline**… for the LORD **reproves** him whom he **loves**, as a **father** the son in whom he **delights**" (vv.11–12). The finding: the inner being is asked to **re-read discipline as love** — not rejection but the mark of being a cherished son *(stated)*. The operation: an **interpretive act** — the self must construe painful reproof as *delight*, which requires trust to perform *(inferred; the same reframe as Ps 94:12, Heb 12:6)*. *Validation:* *delights→target=son* captures the object; sound. *Hidden:* **discipline received requires an interpretive trust** (construing pain as love). *Surfaced:* correction-received-as-love (shared w/ Ps); honoring God with wealth (arena).

**PRO-03-D · 3:13–18 · [D] — wisdom as the desire that relativises all desire.** "She is more **precious than jewels**, and **nothing you desire can compare** with her… her ways are ways of **pleasantness**, and all her paths are **peace**; she is a **tree of life**" (vv.15–18). The finding: wisdom is **valued above every other object of desire** — it *out-ranks* all the self wants *(stated)*. The operation: wisdom **orders the hierarchy of desire**, sitting at its top, so that possessing it is *gain* beyond silver/gold *(inferred; the prizing operation, cf. Ps 119:72,127)*. *Validation:* the specifiers now enumerate wisdom's yields — *nothing→of desire*, *ways→of pleasantness*, *paths→of peace*, *tree→of life*. *Hidden:* **the desire that relativises desire.** *Surfaced:* prizing/desiring wisdom above all (shared w/ Ps word-thread).

**PRO-03-E · 3:21–26 · [D, multi] — the fearless rest of the wise.** "You will **walk securely**, and your foot will not stumble. If you **lie down**, you will **not be afraid**; your **sleep will be sweet**. Do **not be afraid** of sudden **terror**… for the LORD will be your **confidence**" (vv.23–26). The finding: internalised wisdom produces **security that shows as *sweet sleep* and *unafraid* rest** *(stated)* — the inner-being fruit is bodily repose and the absence of dread *(inferred; the same fearless-sleep datum as Ps 3:5, 4:8, and 1:33's "dwell secure without dread")*. *Validation:* *soul→of adornment* (wisdom as life/ornament to the soul); *ruin→of wicked*; prohibition over-stamp on "not afraid" (residual). *Hidden:* **sleep as the emblem of the un-anxious wise self** (cross-book w/ Ps 127:2). *Surfaced:* fearless security/rest (shared cornerstone).

**PRO-03-F · 3:27–31 · [D, multi] — the outward-facing heart.** "Do **not withhold good**… do **not plan evil** against your neighbor, who **dwells trustingly** beside you… do **not envy** a man of violence" (vv.27–31). The finding: the inner being's integrity is worked out **toward the neighbour** — generosity not withheld, no evil *plotted* against the trusting, no *envy* of the violent *(stated)*. The operation: the self **governs its dispositions toward others** — especially the temptation to **envy the violent** (to want the aggressor's gains) *(inferred; the refused envy, cf. Ps 37:1, 73:3)*. *Validation:* *plan→target=evil*, *man→of violence* (envy welded). *Hidden:* **envy of the violent as an inner temptation refused** (cross-book w/ Ps 37/73). *Surfaced:* the neighbour-facing heart (new); refused envy of the wicked (shared w/ Ps).

---
**Chapter notes.** Validation: v1.1 enrichment strongly supports this chapter — the trust-with-all-the-heart (v.5) and the wisdom-yields (vv.17–18) are now fully pair-tagged; residuals unchanged (prohibition over-stamp on negated appeals). **New characteristics:** internalisation-as-inscription; trust-as-self-distrust; discipline-received-as-love (interpretive); wisdom-relativising-desire; the neighbour-facing heart. **Shared:** trust vs self-reliance; fear of the LORD; fearless rest; refused envy.

---

## Catch-up units (2026-07-04) — loose study-term verses bound to units

**PRO-03-G · Prov 3:19–20 · [S] — wisdom as the LORD's creative attribute (arena, thin IB).** "The LORD by **wisdom founded the earth**; by **understanding** he established the heavens; by his **knowledge** the deeps broke open" (vv.19–20). This is the *cosmic scope* of wisdom — a divine attribute in creation, not a human inner-being movement. Finding (thin): the same wisdom the disciple is urged to prize (3:13–18) is shown to be *the LORD's own*, the fabric of creation — so pursuing it is aligning with the grain of reality *(inferred; the IB content is oblique — this is the arena/ground of the wisdom theme, not a finding about the human interior)*. *Surfaced:* wisdom as divine-and-cosmic (arena; grounds the value-of-wisdom thread, low IB).

**PRO-03-H · Prov 3:32–35 · [D, multi] — the two inner postures the LORD draws near or turns from.** "The **devious** person is an **abomination** to the LORD, but the **upright are in his confidence**" (v.32); "toward the **scorners** he is scornful, but to the **humble** he gives **favor**" (v.34). Finding: the LORD responds to *interior postures* — deviousness/scorn meet his turning-away, uprightness/humility meet his confidence and favour *(stated)*. Operation: the inner disposition **positions the self toward or away from God's nearness** — "the upright are in his **confidence** (sod — intimate counsel)"; humility is the posture that *receives* favour, scorn the one that forfeits it *(inferred; the sod-intimacy links to Job 29:4 "the friendship of God"; scorn/humility as the hinge)*. *Surfaced:* the interior posture that gains or forfeits God's intimacy (new — w/ Job 29:4); scorn vs humility as the receptive/closed self.

---

## Proverbs 6 - inner-being unit readings

# Proverbs 6 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 6:1–35, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**.

---

**PRO-06-A · 6:6–11 · [D] — sloth as the self's drift into ruin.** "Go to the **ant**, O **sluggard**… How long will you **lie there**? A **little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands** to rest, and **poverty will come** upon you like a robber" (vv.6,9–11). The finding: sloth is an **inner disposition**, not a single act — the *incremental* yielding ("a little… a little… a little") by which the self *drifts* into ruin without deciding to *(stated)*. The operation: **ruin by degrees** — the slothful interior does not choose poverty but *fails to rouse*, and the small surrenders accumulate into catastrophe *(inferred; a Proverbs-distinctive characteristic, faintly echoed in Ps 127:2's contrast of toil and rest)*. *Validation:* *little→of sleep/of slumber*, *folding→of hands* (the enrichment strings the incremental phrase). *Surfaced:* sloth as incremental drift (new — Proverbs-distinctive).

**PRO-06-B · 6:12–15 · [D, multi] — the malicious heart legible in the body.** "A worthless person… goes about with **crooked speech**, **winks** with his eyes, **signals** with his feet, points with his finger, **with perverted heart devises evil, continually sowing discord**" (vv.12–14). The finding: malice is **read off the body** — the *perverted heart* within *shows* in winking eyes, signalling feet, pointing fingers *(stated)*. The operation: the inner corruption **leaks through the whole body's gestures** — the heart that "devises evil" cannot keep itself hidden; its scheming animates the limbs *(inferred; the inner condition legible not only in speech (ch 10) but in *gesture*, a bodily extension of the speech-legibility thread)*. *Validation:* *crooked→of speech*, *sowing→target=discord* (the perverted heart's product). *Hidden:* **malice legible in gesture** (extends the speech-legibility characteristic to the whole body). *Surfaced:* the inner condition legible in body/gesture (new extension of the Ps speech thread).

**PRO-06-C · 6:16–19 · [S, multi] — the catalogue of inner-being evils.** The seven the LORD hates: "**haughty eyes**, a **lying tongue**… a **heart that devises wicked plans**, **feet that make haste to run to evil**, a **false witness** who breathes out lies, and one who **sows discord** among brothers" (vv.17–19). The finding: an explicit **enumeration of the inner being's abominations** — pride (eyes), falsehood (tongue), a *scheming heart*, an *eager will* (feet swift to evil), and the *discord-sowing* disposition *(stated)*. The operation: the list **maps the self's evils onto its organs** — each abomination is an inner disposition expressed through a body-part; the *heart that devises wicked plans* is the centre *(inferred; a compact anthropology of evil, cross-book with Ps 36:1–4)*. *Validation:* *devises→target=wicked* (heart devises wicked plans), *plans→of feet*, *breathes-out→lies*, *sows→discord*. *Surfaced:* catalogue of inner evils (new); the scheming heart as the centre.

**PRO-06-D · 6:20–35 · [D, multi] — desire guarded at the heart; adultery as self-destruction.** "Bind them on your **heart always**… **do not desire her beauty in your heart**, and do not let her **capture** you… He who commits adultery **lacks sense**; he who does it **destroys himself**" (vv.21,25,32). The finding: the guard against adultery is set **at the level of *desire in the heart*** — not merely the act but the *wanting* is to be refused ("do not desire her beauty *in your heart*") *(stated)*; and the act is **self-destruction** — "he *destroys himself*" *(stated)*. The operation: **the heart as the front line of purity** — the battle is fought where desire forms, before the deed; and yielding is not a gain but a *self-annihilation* *(inferred; the interiorised command, cross-book with Ps 119:37 "turn my eyes from worthless things", and Matt 5:28)*. *Validation:* the enrichment is precise — *beauty→seat=heart, specifier=of heart* ("desire her beauty *in your heart*"); *heart→of always*. *Hidden:* **purity contested at the point of desire, not the act** (the interiorised battle). *Surfaced:* desire-guarded-in-the-heart (new — the interiorised command, cross-book w/ Ps 119:37); adultery as self-destruction; jealousy's fury (v.34, the passion arena).

---
**Chapter notes.** Validation: v1.1 enrichment supplies the key objects/seats — *beauty→of-heart* (the interiorised desire) and the seven-abominations' organ-mappings; residuals unchanged. **New characteristics:** sloth-as-incremental-drift; malice-legible-in-gesture; the catalogue of inner evils / the scheming heart; purity-contested-at-desire (interiorised). **Shared:** the inner condition legible (extended to gesture); the guarded eye/heart (w/ Ps 119:37).

---

## Catch-up units (2026-07-04) — loose study-term verses bound to units

**PRO-06-E · Prov 6:3–4 · [S] — the urgent self-humbling that escapes a snare.** Having become surety for a neighbour, the counsel is immediate and self-lowering: "**save yourself**… go, **hasten**, and **plead urgently** with your neighbour. **Give your eyes no sleep** and your eyelids no slumber" (vv.3–4). Finding: the self caught in a trap must act with **urgency and self-humbling** — pleading, not standing on pride, and refusing rest until free *(stated)*. Operation: **the interior mobilised to self-rescue** — the pride that would delay or refuse to plead is set aside; the whole self (no sleep) bent on release *(inferred; humbling-to-escape as an inner-being movement, kin to the urgency of repentance)*. *Surfaced:* urgent self-humbling to escape a self-made bind (new); the pride laid down to plead.

---

## Proverbs 8 - inner-being unit readings

# Proverbs 8 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 8:1–36, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation** (Wisdom personified = the arena/speaker; the findings are the self's relation to her).

---

**PRO-08-A · 8:1–11 · [D, multi] — wisdom's truthful self-commendation and its value.** Wisdom cries at the crossroads: "my mouth will **utter truth**; wickedness is an **abomination to my lips**… take my instruction rather than **silver**… **wisdom is better than jewels**, and all that you may **desire** cannot compare with her" (vv.7,10–11). The finding: wisdom presents herself as **truth that outbids every desire** — she cannot be compared to what the self wants *(stated)*. The operation (of the self): the inner being is summoned to **re-rank its desires** with wisdom above all treasure — the same prizing as 3:15 *(inferred)*. *Validation:* *utter→target=truth*, *abomination→of lips* (wisdom's own hatred of wicked speech), *all→of desire* ("nothing you desire compares"). *Surfaced:* prizing wisdom above desire (shared w/ 3:13, Ps 119).

**PRO-08-B · 8:12–21 · [D, multi] — the fear that hates evil; the mutual love of self and wisdom.** "**The fear of the LORD is hatred of evil**. Pride and arrogance and the way of evil and perverted speech **I hate**… **I love those who love me**, and those who **seek me diligently find me**" (vv.13,17). Two findings. (1) **Reverent fear is a *hatred of evil*** — fear of God is not only awe but an *aversion*, an affective turning-against wickedness *(stated)*; a hidden dimension of the fear-of-the-LORD characteristic. (2) **Love is reciprocal and seeking is rewarded** — "I love those who *love* me… those who *seek* me diligently *find* me": the self's love and diligent seeking of wisdom is *met and answered* *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's affection for wisdom is **returned**, and its diligent search **succeeds** — a relationship of mutual love, not one-way effort *(inferred; cross-book with the seek-and-find of Ps 9:10, 27:8, and the desire-met thread)*. *Validation:* *fear→specifier=of Lord*; *knowledge→of discretion*; the govern/decree/walk objects tagged. *Hidden:* **fear-of-the-LORD as *hatred of evil*** (an affective, not merely reverent, dimension). *Surfaced:* fear as hatred of evil (new dimension of the shared fear-thread); the mutual love of the self and wisdom; seeking rewarded with finding (shared w/ Ps).

**PRO-08-C · 8:32–36 · [D, multi] — watching daily at wisdom's doors; life vs death.** "**Blessed is the one who listens** to me, **watching daily at my gates, waiting beside my doors**. For whoever **finds me finds life**… but he who **fails to find me injures himself**; **all who hate me love death**" (vv.34–36). The finding: the devoted self **watches and waits** at wisdom's door — a posture of daily, expectant attendance — and the stakes are *life or death* *(stated)*. The operation: **expectant watching/waiting for wisdom** (the same posture as the Psalter's wait-on-the-LORD, 130:6, here at wisdom's gates); and the terrible inversion — those who reject wisdom **love death** — evil as a *perverse love of one's own ruin* *(inferred)*. *Hidden:* **"all who hate me love death"** — the refusal of wisdom is not neutral but an *affection for self-destruction* (the deepest form of misdirected love, cross-book with the aheb-fixed "love vanity/simplicity" of Ps 4:2, Pro 1:22). *Surfaced:* watching/waiting for wisdom (shared w/ Ps wait-thread); the love of death (new — misdirected affection at its extreme).

---
**Chapter notes.** Validation: enrichment supplies fear→of-Lord and the operation-objects; residuals unchanged. **New characteristics:** fear-as-hatred-of-evil (a new dimension); mutual love of self and wisdom; the love-of-death (misdirected affection at the extreme). **Shared:** prizing wisdom above desire; seeking-rewarded-with-finding; watching/waiting (w/ Ps 130).

---

## Catch-up units (2026-07-04) — loose study-term verses bound to units

**PRO-08-D · Prov 8:24, 28, 30–31 · [D, multi] — wisdom's delight and rejoicing (the joy at the heart of creation).** Wisdom, present before the depths (vv.24,28 — the cosmic *arena*), describes its own affect: "I was daily his **delight**, **rejoicing** before him always, **rejoicing** in his inhabited world and **delighting in the children of man**" (vv.30–31). Finding: wisdom's mode of being is **joy** — a daily delight *before God* that overflows *toward humanity* *(stated)*. Operation: **delight as the atmosphere of wisdom** — not sober utility but gladness, directed both Godward ("his delight… before him") and manward ("delighting in the children of man") *(inferred; the cosmology of vv.24–28 is arena, but 30–31 is a real inner-being note — the joy that is wisdom's native climate, cross-book w/ the joy-refrain of Ecc and Ps 16:11)*. *Surfaced:* delight/rejoicing as wisdom's native climate (new — Godward and manward); joy as wisdom's atmosphere. *(vv.24,28 = cosmic arena, thin IB.)*

---

## Proverbs 10 - inner-being unit readings

# Proverbs 10 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Pro 10:1–32, read **per segmentation unit**. Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**; the righteous⇄wicked antithesis is the arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Method:** as PRO-01 — unit reading + **lexical read-back/validation** (roles, pairs, flags) + **hidden-characteristic isolation**. This chapter demonstrates the **thread (T)** handling: characteristics whose couplets are *scattered* across the chapter are gathered and read together.

---

## PRO-10-F · Prov 10:2–32 · [F] — the moral-poles frame (arena)

The chapter runs almost entirely on the **righteous⇄wicked** antithesis. This is the *arena* in which the specific inner-being findings sit — noted once here so it does not get re-counted as a finding in each couplet. The lexical correctly tags *righteous* (H6662) and *wicked* (H7563) as recurring poles throughout; the reading treats them as the moral field, not as the operation.

---

## PRO-10-speech · Prov 10:11,13–14,18–21,31–32 · [T, multi] — the inner condition legible in speech

**The reading.** Proverbs' dominant inner-being thread, gathered from across the chapter: **the mouth reveals the heart**. "The **mouth of the righteous** is a **fountain of life**, but the mouth of the wicked **conceals violence**" (v.11); "the one who **conceals hatred** has **lying lips**" (v.18); "when **words are many**, transgression is not lacking, but whoever **restrains his lips** is prudent" (v.19); "the **tongue of the righteous** is choice silver; the **heart of the wicked** is of little worth" (v.20). The finding: **speech is the outflow and the exposure of the inner being** — what is in the heart *comes out* the mouth, so that the lips *diagnose* the heart *(stated: the mouth conceals violence / reveals life)*. Two operations run under it: **concealment** (the wicked's mouth *hides* what is within — v.11, v.18) and **restraint** (the prudent *governs* the outflow — v.19); the un-governed tongue *leaks* transgression, the governed tongue *guards* the self *(inferred: v.19–20 make restraint an inner-being act, not mere silence — the self mastering its own outflow; cf. the Psalter's "inner condition legible in speech", Ps 5:9, 12, 141:3)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** The thread is well-supported: *righteous, wicked, life, hatred, lying, prudent* all tagged **characteristics**; the organs (*mouth, lips, tongue* — H6310/H8193) sit `standalone` gate-2, correctly (the reading reads the inner condition *off* them). Two notes. (1) **Under-tag:** v.19 "whoever **restrains** his lips" (H2820) is tagged `standalone`, but restraint-of-speech is a genuine **inner-being characteristic** (self-governance) — the reading promotes it (a correction candidate). (2) **Prohibition over-stamp** at v.19 ("transgression is *not* lacking") bleeds `prohibition` across the whole clause — a known residual. **Pair note:** v.13 *back* (H1460) is welded `manner-of found` to "wisdom is found"; it is really the body-part target of "a rod for the *back*" — a recipient-as-manner slippage, harmless to the thread.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** (1) **Restraint of speech as self-governance** (v.19) — under-tagged, but a real operation that ties this thread to the self-mastery thread (16:32, 29:11, 25:28). (2) **Concealment** — the wicked mouth that *hides* the heart (vv.11,18) is a distinct operation (the masking self), which surfaces fully at 26:23–26; a cross-chapter thread starts here.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *the inner condition legible in speech* (shared w/ Ps); *restraint of speech / self-governance of the tongue* (new — under-tagged in the substrate); *concealment / the masking self* (new thread).

---

## PRO-10-desire · Prov 10:3,24,28 · [T, multi] — desire, dread, and the hope that brings joy

**The reading.** A scattered thread on the **appetite and expectation of the inner being**: "the LORD… **thwarts the craving of the wicked**" (v.3); "what the wicked **dreads** will come upon him, but the **desire of the righteous** will be granted" (v.24); "the **hope of the righteous** brings **joy**, but the expectation of the wicked will perish" (v.28). The finding: the inner being is a **creature of desire, dread, and hope** — and the *object/direction* of that desire decides its end *(stated: the righteous's desire granted, the wicked's craving thwarted)*. The operation: **hope issues in joy** (v.28) — expectation rightly placed is already a species of gladness, while the wicked's expectation is a *dread* that materialises *(inferred: v.24 pairs the wicked's dread with the righteous's desire as two futures the inner posture is already living toward; cf. Ps 112:7–8 the fearless vs the dread-filled, and the desire-met-in-God thread, Ps 145:19)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *desire, dread, hope, joy* carry the thread; sound. The wicked's *craving* (v.3) and the righteous's *desire* (v.24) are correctly distinguished — the same faculty (desire), opposite direction, exactly the Psalter's finding (honest longing met vs disordered craving thwarted, Ps 107:9 vs 106:14). Pairs sensible.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** **Dread as a lived future** (v.24) — "what the wicked dreads will come" — the inner being's fear is not merely felt but *anticipatory*, already inhabiting the feared outcome; a subtle characteristic (the self living toward what it dreads) distinct from present fear.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *desire / craving (directional)* (shared w/ Ps); *hope issuing in joy* (shared); *anticipatory dread (living toward the feared)* (new/less-obvious).

---

## PRO-10-diligence · Prov 10:4–5,26 · [T] — diligence vs sloth

**The reading.** "A **slack hand** causes poverty, but the hand of the **diligent** makes rich" (v.4); "he who **gathers in summer** is prudent, but he who **sleeps in harvest** brings shame" (v.5). The finding: diligence and sloth are **inner dispositions** (not merely behaviours) — a *slackness* vs an *industry* of the self that shows in timing (gather in summer / sleep in harvest) *(inferred: the contrast is of inner orientation toward one's work, the self that applies itself vs the self that lets the moment pass; a Proverbs-distinctive characteristic, lightly present in Ps 127:2's anxious-toil-vs-rest but here about industriousness itself)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *diligent* (H2742) tagged characteristic; *slack/sleeps/gathers* largely gate-2, read from structure. Sound; a thin but clear thread.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** **Timing/seasonality of the diligent self** (v.5) — not just "works hard" but *acts at the right season*; a discernment-of-the-moment folded into diligence.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *diligence vs sloth* (new — Proverbs-distinctive); *discernment of the season* (new/less-obvious).

---

## PRO-10-teachable · Prov 10:8,17 · [T] — receptivity / heeding instruction

**The reading.** "The **wise of heart** will **receive** commandments, but a babbling fool comes to ruin" (v.8); "whoever **heeds instruction** is on the **path to life**, but he who **rejects reproof** leads others astray" (v.17). The finding: **receptivity is a condition of the heart** — the "wise of heart" *receives*, the fool cannot; teachability is an inner posture, not an intellectual capacity *(stated: wise of heart receives)*. The operation: **heeding vs rejecting reproof** sets the very direction of the life ("path to life") — the self's openness to correction is life-or-death *(inferred; cf. the Psalter's teachable/asking-to-be-searched thread, Ps 139:23, 25:4–5)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *wise* (H2450), *heart* (H3820, seat) tagged; the "wise of heart" pair (wisdom seated in the heart) is sensible. Sound.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** **Receptivity as a *heart-condition*** (v.8, "wise of *heart* receives") — the substrate seats it in the heart; teachability is located *in the heart*, not the ears — a Proverbs sharpening.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *receptivity / teachability (heart-seated)* (shared w/ Ps, sharpened here).

---

## PRO-10-v12 · Prov 10:12 · [S, multi] — love vs hate as relational drivers

**The reading.** A self-contained gem: "**Hatred** stirs up strife, but **love** covers all offenses." The finding: **hatred and love are the two engines of relational life** — hatred *generates* conflict, love *absorbs* it *(stated)*. The operation: **love as a covering** — not merely a feeling but an act that *takes up and hides another's offense* rather than exposing it *(inferred: "covers" makes love active and self-giving — the opposite of the concealing/masking self of the speech thread, which hides its *own* evil; love hides *another's* fault; cf. Ps 32:1 "sin covered", 1 Pet 4:8)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *hatred* (H8135) and *love* (H0157, *aheb*) both tagged **characteristics** — the aheb-fix correctly makes "love" a characteristic here (relational love, not misdirected). Clean.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** The **covering** operation contrasts pointedly with the speech thread's *concealment*: the same motion (hiding) is love when it covers *another's* offense and wickedness when it hides *one's own* — a subtle inner-being distinction worth carrying.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *love vs hate as relational drivers* (shared w/ Ps); *love-as-covering* (new/less-obvious).

---

## PRO-10-fear · Prov 10:27 · [S] — the fear of the LORD lengthens life

**The reading.** "The **fear of the LORD** prolongs life, but the years of the wicked will be short." The finding: reverent fear is **life-extending** — the same root-characteristic as 1:7, here tied to the *duration* of the life it grounds *(stated)*. A brief re-attestation of the book's spine (fear-of-the-LORD thread).

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *fear* (H3374) tagged characteristic; sound (bearer bleed on "LORD" is cosmetic here).

**Characteristics surfaced:** *the fear of the LORD (root)* (shared cornerstone — re-attested).

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Validation summary:** substrate sound for reading. Recurring residuals: **prohibition over-stamp** (v.19) and minor **bearer bleed**. One **under-tag** worth promoting: *restrains his lips* (v.19) → a self-governance characteristic. One **pair note:** recipient-as-manner at v.13 (*back*→*found*). Same rule-adjustment candidates as the Psalter run.
- **Thread method demonstrated:** the speech, desire, diligence, and teachable characteristics were each *gathered from scattered couplets* within the chapter and read as single units — the sentence-collection handling working as designed.
- **New characteristics this chapter (for the fork-b control table):** *restraint/self-governance of the tongue*; *concealment / the masking self*; *diligence vs sloth*; *discernment of the season*; *anticipatory dread*; *love-as-covering*. **Shared with the Psalter:** *inner condition legible in speech*; *desire (directional)*; *hope→joy*; *receptivity/teachability*; *love vs hate*; *fear of the LORD (root)*.

---

## Catch-up unit (2026-07-04) — loose study-term verse bound to a unit

**PRO-10-parents · Prov 10:1 · [S] — the child's wisdom or folly felt in the parent's heart.** "A **wise son makes a glad father**, but a **foolish son is a sorrow to his mother**" (v.1). Finding: a child's inner character registers as **joy or grief in the parent's interior** — wisdom gladdens, folly sorrows *(stated)*. Operation: **the interior bound across the generational tie** — one person's wisdom/folly is *felt* as another's gladness/sorrow; the inner life is not sealed but shared through love *(inferred; the relational transmission of inner states, recurs 17:21,25, 23:24–25; the heading proverb of the collection)*. *Surfaced:* the child's character felt in the parent's heart (new — inner states shared through the bond).

---

## Proverbs 11 - inner-being unit readings

# Proverbs 11 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 11, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**; the righteous⇄wicked antithesis = arena.

---

**PRO-11-F · 11:3–31 · [F]** — the moral-poles frame (righteous/upright vs wicked/treacherous). Arena; the units below are the specific findings within it.

**PRO-11-pride · 11:2 · [S, multi] — pride and its shame; humility and wisdom.** "When **pride** comes, then comes **disgrace**, but with the **humble is wisdom**" (v.2). Finding: pride *carries its own disgrace*, and wisdom keeps company with the humble — the inner posture *determines* the outcome *(stated)*. Operation: **pride as self-defeating, humility as the seat of wisdom** *(inferred; the pride/humility thread, cross-book w/ Ps 138:6, and Pro 16:18, 29:23)*. *Surfaced:* pride vs humility (★ shared cornerstone thread).

**PRO-11-speech · 11:9,11,12,13 · [T, multi] — speech that destroys or keeps.** "With his **mouth** the godless would **destroy his neighbor**"; "whoever **belittles** his neighbor lacks sense, but a man of understanding **remains silent**"; "whoever goes about **slandering reveals secrets**, but he who is **trustworthy in spirit keeps** a thing **covered**" (vv.9,12,13). Finding: speech is the outflow that either *destroys* or *guards* — and the guarding takes two forms: **restrained silence** and **trustworthy discretion** (keeping secrets) *(stated)*. Operation: **the trustworthy-in-spirit self *keeps covered*** — discretion as an inner reliability, the opposite of the leaking, belittling tongue *(inferred; the speech-legibility thread + a new note on confidentiality as inner trustworthiness)*. *Validation:* *mouth→of wicked*, and the destroy/belittle/slander objects tagged. *Hidden:* **trustworthiness-of-spirit as discretion** (keeping a confidence = an inner-being fidelity). *Surfaced:* speech-legibility (shared); trustworthy discretion (new).

**PRO-11-generosity · 11:17,24,25,26 · [T, multi] — kindness/generosity that returns on the self.** "A man who is **kind benefits himself**, but a **cruel man hurts himself**"; "one **gives freely, yet grows all the richer**; another **withholds** and only **suffers want**… whoever **waters** will himself be **watered**" (vv.17,24–25). Finding: kindness and cruelty are **self-affecting** — the disposition toward others *returns upon the self* *(stated)*. Operation: **generosity as self-enriching, cruelty as self-harming** — the inner posture toward others is, by a moral reciprocity, a posture toward oneself *(inferred; the outward-facing heart of 3:27, now with the boomerang principle)*. *Validation:* kind/cruel with reflexive objects; *give/withhold/water* tagged. *Surfaced:* generosity vs withholding (new); the disposition-toward-others-returns-on-self (new).

**PRO-11-trust-riches · 11:28 · [S] — trust misplaced in riches.** "Whoever **trusts in his riches** will **fall**, but the righteous will **flourish** like a green leaf" (v.28). Finding: **mis-placed trust collapses** — leaning on wealth topples the self *(stated)*. Operation: trust in riches vs the flourishing of the God-rooted self *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 49:6, 52:7, 62:10 — the same mis-placed-trust datum)*. *Surfaced:* mis-placed trust in riches (shared w/ Ps).

**PRO-11-desire · 11:23 · [S] — the direction of desire decides its end.** "The **desire of the righteous** ends only in **good**, the **expectation of the wicked** in wrath" (v.23). Finding: desire and expectation carry opposite ends by their moral direction *(stated; the directional-desire thread)*. *Validation:* *expectation→of wealth* (elsewhere); desire/expectation with poles. *Surfaced:* directional desire/expectation (shared w/ Ps hope-thread).

---
**Chapter notes.** Validation: v1.1 enrichment supplies the mouth-of-wicked, expectation-of-wealth, and reflexive kindness/cruelty objects. **New:** trustworthy-discretion; generosity-returns-on-self. **Shared:** pride/humility (★); speech-legibility; mis-placed trust in riches; directional desire.

---

## Catch-up unit (2026-07-04) — loose study-term verse bound to a unit

**PRO-11-honesty · Prov 11:1 · [S] — honesty as what the LORD delights in.** "A **false balance is an abomination** to the LORD, but a **just weight is his delight**" (v.1). Finding: the interior disposition behind honest dealing is what **God delights in** — integrity in the unseen (the weighing) is a delight to him, deceit an abomination *(stated)*. Operation: **integrity located in the hidden practice** — the balance and weights are where cheating hides; God's delight/abomination attaches to that concealed honesty or fraud *(inferred; the heart tested where no one sees, cross-book w/ Job 31:6 "let me be weighed in a just balance"; the heading of ch.11's collection)*. *Surfaced:* honesty-in-the-hidden as God's delight (new — w/ Job 31:6); integrity at the concealed weighing.

---

## Proverbs 16 - inner-being unit readings

# Proverbs 16 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 16, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**.

---

**PRO-16-heart-sovereignty · 16:1,3,9,33 · [T, multi] — the heart plans, the LORD establishes.** "The **plans of the heart belong to man, but the answer of the tongue is from the LORD**"; "**commit your work to the LORD, and your plans will be established**"; "**the heart of man plans his way, but the LORD establishes his steps**" (vv.1,3,9). Finding — a cornerstone: the inner being genuinely **plans and purposes**, yet the *outcome* is God's — human deliberation and divine sovereignty are held together, not against each other *(stated)*. Operation: **the planning heart that *commits its plans* to God** — the self is neither passive (it plans) nor autonomous (God establishes); the resolving move is to *entrust* the planning to the LORD (v.3) *(inferred; a distinctive Proverbs datum on the will, cross-book w/ Ps 37:5 "commit your way", 31:15 "my times are in your hand")*. *Surfaced:* the planning heart + entrusting plans to God (★ new cornerstone — human agency under divine sovereignty).

**PRO-16-weighed · 16:2 · [S, multi] — pure in one's own eyes; the LORD weighs the spirit.** "**All the ways of a man are pure in his own eyes, but the LORD weighs the spirit**" (v.2). Finding: the self's self-assessment is **unreliable** — it looks *pure to itself*; only God *weighs the spirit* truly *(stated)*. Operation: **self-blindness corrected by divine assay** *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 139, and 21:2, 30:12)*. *Surfaced:* self-blindness vs God's weighing of the spirit (shared w/ Ps 139).

**PRO-16-pride · 16:5,18,19 · [T, multi] — pride before the fall; the lowly spirit.** "**Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall**"; "better to be of a **lowly spirit with the poor** than divide spoil with the proud" (vv.18–19). Finding: the proud heart **carries its own collapse** *(stated)*. Operation: **pride as self-destruction, lowliness as the safer good** *(inferred; the pride/humility cornerstone, cross-book w/ Ps 18:27, 138:6)*. *Surfaced:* pride/humility (★ shared cornerstone).

**PRO-16-self-rule · 16:32 · [S, multi] — ruling one's own spirit.** "**Whoever is slow to anger is better than the mighty, and he who rules his spirit than he who takes a city**" (v.32). Finding — a cornerstone: the conquest of the *self* outranks the conquest of a *city* *(stated)*. Operation: **self-mastery as the supreme strength** — governing one's own spirit is a greater might than military conquest *(inferred; the self-government thread at its clearest, cross-book w/ the Psalter's self-address/self-quieting, Ps 131:2, and 25:28, 29:11)*. *Surfaced:* self-mastery / ruling one's spirit (★ cornerstone — the inner conquest above the outer).

**PRO-16-fear · 16:6,20 · [S, multi] — fear turns from evil; trust discovers good.** "By the **fear of the LORD one turns away from evil**"; "blessed is he who **trusts in the LORD**" (vv.6,20). *Surfaced:* fear-of-LORD; trust (shared).

**PRO-16-speech-heart · 16:21,23,24 · [T, multi] — the heart makes the speech; gracious words sweeten the soul.** "The **heart of the wise makes his speech judicious**"; "**gracious words are like a honeycomb, sweetness to the soul and health to the body**" (vv.23–24). Finding: wise speech *originates in the heart*, and gracious words are **sweet to the soul and healing to the body** *(stated)*. Operation: **speech as the heart's outflow, and kind speech as somatic medicine** *(inferred; the speech-legibility + felt-interior threads joined; cross-book w/ Ps 19:14)*. *Surfaced:* the heart-sourced tongue; gracious-words-heal (new).

**PRO-16-self-deception · 16:25 · [S] — the way that seems right (= 14:12).** "There is a way that seems right to a man, but its end is the way to death." *Surfaced:* self-deception (shared, recurs).

---
**Chapter notes.** **New/cornerstone:** heart-plans-God-establishes / entrusting-plans-to-God (★); self-mastery (★ 16:32). **Shared:** pride/humility (★); self-blindness vs God's weighing (w/ Ps 139); fear/trust; the heart-sourced tongue; self-deception.

---

## Catch-up units (2026-07-04) — loose study-term verses bound to units

**PRO-16-A · Prov 16:4, 7, 11 · [D, multi] — the LORD who orders all, and the self aligned to him.** "The LORD has made **everything for its purpose**" (v.4); "when a man's ways **please the LORD**, he makes even his **enemies to be at peace** with him" (v.7); "a **just balance** and scales are the LORD's" (v.11). Finding: the ordering LORD is the ground, and the self that *pleases* him is brought into peace even with enemies *(stated)*. Operation: **the God-pleasing interior as the source of peace** — inner alignment with God (not managing enemies directly) is what pacifies the outer world *(inferred; peace as a by-product of a pleasing inner life, cross-book w/ the trust-security thread)*. *Surfaced:* the God-pleasing self drawing peace (new); honesty as the LORD's (w/ 11:1).

**PRO-16-king · Prov 16:10, 12–15 · [D, multi] — the king's disposition and the self that navigates power.** The king's mouth "does not sin in judgment" (v.10); "righteous lips are the **delight of a king**, and he **loves** him who speaks what is right" (v.13); "a king's **wrath is a messenger of death**, and a wise man will **appease** it" (v.14); "in the **light of a king's face there is life**" (v.15). Finding: the king's inner favour/wrath governs life and death, and the wise interior *reads and appeases* it *(stated)*. Operation: **the discerning self that navigates another's disposition** — perceiving the wrath and defusing it, courting the favour by right speech *(inferred; the wise reading of power, kin to Ecc 10:4 calmness before a ruler's anger)*. *Surfaced:* the self that reads and appeases power (new — w/ Ecc 10:4); right speech as what wins favour.

**PRO-16-value · Prov 16:8, 16 · [S, multi] — valuing righteousness and wisdom over gain.** "**Better is a little with righteousness** than great revenues with injustice" (v.8); "how much **better to get wisdom than gold**!" (v.16). Finding: the ordered interior **prefers the right/wise to the profitable** — little-with-righteousness over much-with-injustice, wisdom over gold *(stated)*. Operation: **the value-ranking of the inner being** — a self whose deepest preference is set on righteousness and wisdom, not gain *(inferred; the reordered desire, cross-book w/ Ps 119:72 "the law is better than gold")*. *Surfaced:* the interior that values the right over the profitable (w/ Ps 119:72).

**PRO-16-guard · Prov 16:17, 22, 31 · [D, multi] — the self-guarding righteous life.** "The **highway of the upright turns aside from evil**; whoever **guards his way preserves his life**" (v.17); "**good sense is a fountain of life** to him who has it" (v.22); "gray hair is a crown of glory, gained in a **righteous life**" (v.31). Finding: the upright interior **guards its own way** and so preserves and crowns the life *(stated)*. Operation: **self-preservation through vigilance over the way** — good sense is a living spring within; the guarded path leads to an honoured old age *(inferred; the self as keeper of its own road, w/ 4:23 "keep your heart")*. *Surfaced:* the self-guarding, self-preserving righteous life (w/ 4:23); good sense as an inner spring.

**PRO-16-malice · Prov 16:26–30 · [D, multi] — malice legible in speech and gesture.** "A worker's **appetite works for him**" (v.26); "a worthless man plots evil, and his speech is like a **scorching fire**" (v.27); "a dishonest man **spreads strife**, and a **whisperer separates close friends**" (v.28); "a man of violence **entices** his neighbour" (v.29); "whoever **winks his eyes** plans dishonest things" (v.30). Finding: the malicious interior is **read off its speech and gesture** — scorching words, whispering, enticing, the winking eye *(stated)*. Operation: **the inner malice made visible** — the plotting heart betrays itself in inflammatory speech, secret whispering, and the tell-tale wink *(inferred; the interior legible in the body, w/ 6:12–14 the worthless person's gestures)*. *Surfaced:* malice legible in speech/gesture (w/ 6:12–14); the whisperer who separates friends; driving appetite (26).

---

## Proverbs 17 - inner-being unit readings

# Proverbs 17 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 17, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**.

---

**PRO-17-tests-hearts · 17:3 · [S] — the LORD tests hearts.** "**The crucible is for silver, and the furnace is for gold, and the LORD tests hearts**" (v.3). Finding — a cornerstone: the heart is **assayed by God as metal by fire** — refined and proved *(stated)*. Operation: **the tested/refined heart** — God's testing is a *smelting*, purifying not merely inspecting *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 7:9, 26:2, 66:10 "you have tried us as silver is tried")*. *Surfaced:* the tested/assayed heart (★ shared cornerstone, cross-book w/ Ps).

**PRO-17-felt-heart · 17:22 · [S, multi] — the joyful heart as medicine; the crushed spirit.** "**A joyful heart is good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones**" (v.22). Finding — a felt-interior cornerstone: inner gladness is **medicinal to the body**, and a *crushed spirit desiccates the bones* *(stated)*. Operation: **the emotional interior as physical health or decay** *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 32:3–4, 51:8 "let the bones you have broken rejoice"; and Pro 14:30, 15:13, 18:14)*. *Surfaced:* the felt heart / joyful-heart-as-medicine + the crushed spirit (★ shared cornerstone).

**PRO-17-teachable · 17:10 · [S] — the depth a rebuke reaches.** "**A rebuke goes deeper into a man of understanding than a hundred blows into a fool**" (v.10). Finding: the teachable heart is *penetrable* by a word where the fool is unmoved by a hundred blows *(stated)*. Operation: **receptivity measured by how *deep* a rebuke reaches** *(inferred; the teachability thread)*. *Surfaced:* receptivity / the penetrable vs impervious heart (shared).

**PRO-17-restraint · 17:27,28 · [T, multi] — restrained words, the cool spirit.** "Whoever **restrains his words has knowledge**, and he who has a **cool spirit is a man of understanding**; even a fool who **keeps silent** is considered wise" (vv.27–28). Finding: **restraint and coolness of spirit** are the marks of understanding *(stated)*. Operation: **self-governance of speech and temperature** — the "cool spirit" (opposite of hot temper) is an inner mastery *(inferred; the self-mastery + tongue-restraint threads; cross-book w/ Ps 39:1 "I will guard my ways… I will muzzle my mouth")*. *Surfaced:* restraint of words / the cool spirit (shared self-mastery).

**PRO-17-love-friend · 17:9,17 · [S, multi] — love covers; the friend for adversity.** "Whoever **covers an offense seeks love**"; "**a friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity**" (vv.9,17). Finding: love **covers** offenses (as 10:12) and is **constant** ("at all times"), proving itself in adversity *(stated)*. Operation: **love as covering + steadfastness** *(inferred; the love-as-covering datum + the constancy of true love)*. *Surfaced:* love-as-covering (shared w/ 10:12); the steadfast friend (new).

---
**Chapter notes.** **Cornerstones:** the tested heart (★ 17:3, w/ Ps); joyful-heart/crushed-spirit (★ 17:22). **Shared:** receptivity; self-mastery/restraint/cool-spirit; love-as-covering.

---

## Catch-up units (2026-07-04) — loose study-term verses bound to units

**PRO-17-quiet · Prov 17:1 · [S] — peace over plenty.** "**Better is a dry morsel with quiet** than a house full of feasting with strife" (v.1). Finding: the interior prizes **quiet over abundance** — a bare meal in peace outweighs a full house in conflict *(stated)*. Operation: **the self that ranks inner peace above material plenty** *(inferred; contentment as tranquillity, w/ Ecc 4:6 "a handful of quietness")*. *Surfaced:* peace prized over plenty (w/ Ecc 4:6).

**PRO-17-speech-heart · Prov 17:4, 7, 20 · [D, multi] — the interior legible in speech.** "An **evildoer listens to wicked lips**" (v.4); "**fine speech is not becoming to a fool**" (v.7); "a man of **crooked heart does not discover good**, and one with a **dishonest tongue falls into calamity**" (v.20). Finding: the heart is **read off what it listens to and how it speaks** — the evil ear drawn to wicked lips, the crooked heart self-trapped by its dishonest tongue *(stated)*. Operation: **the interior disclosed and self-ensnared by speech** — the crooked heart's own tongue delivers it to calamity *(inferred; speech as the heart's outflow that recoils, w/ Ecc 10:12 the fool's lips consume him)*. *Surfaced:* the heart legible in what it hears/speaks (w/ Ecc 10:12); the self-ensnaring dishonest tongue.

**PRO-17-Maker · Prov 17:5 · [S, multi] — mocking the poor insults the Maker; gladness at calamity.** "Whoever **mocks the poor insults his Maker**; he who is **glad at calamity** will not go unpunished" (v.5). Finding: contempt for the poor is an **affront to God who made them**, and *gladness at another's ruin* is culpable *(stated)*. Operation: **the shared-Maker conscience, and the perversity of schadenfreude** — to scorn the poor is to scorn the Maker; to rejoice at calamity is a punishable inner posture *(inferred; the common-creation ethic w/ Job 31:15; schadenfreude as a named inner-being fault w/ Job 31:29)*. *Surfaced:* the shared-Maker conscience (w/ Job 31:15); gladness-at-calamity as a fault (w/ Job 31:29).

**PRO-17-bribe · Prov 17:8, 23 · [D] — the bribe as a corrupted self-perception.** "A **bribe is like a magic stone in the eyes of the one who gives it**; wherever he turns he prospers" (v.8); "the wicked accepts a **bribe in secret to pervert** the ways of justice" (v.23). Finding: the bribe **warps the giver's own seeing** — in *his eyes* it works magic — and, taken in secret, perverts justice *(stated)*. Operation: **corruption that distorts the interior's perception** — the bribe does not just buy an outcome, it re-colours how the briber sees reality (everything looks like it prospers) *(inferred; the self deceived by its own corruption)*. *Surfaced:* the bribe as corrupted self-perception (new); secret corruption perverting justice.

**PRO-17-strife · Prov 17:11–14, 19 · [D, multi] — the contentious, rebellion-seeking heart.** "An **evil man seeks only rebellion**" (v.11); better meet a **she-bear robbed of her cubs than a fool in his folly** (v.12); "if anyone **returns evil for good**, evil will not depart from his house" (v.13); "the **beginning of strife is like letting out water**, so quit before the quarrel breaks out" (v.14); "whoever **loves transgression loves strife**" (v.19). Finding: the contentious interior **seeks rebellion, repays good with evil, and loves strife** — and strife, once begun, floods uncontrollably *(stated)*. Operation: **the strife-loving heart and the un-damming of conflict** — quarrel is a breach that, once opened, cannot be recalled; the wise self quits before the flood *(inferred; loving-transgression-loves-strife as one disposition; the flood-image for conflict's irreversibility)*. *Surfaced:* the strife-loving/rebellion-seeking heart (new); strife as an un-dammable flood; returning-evil-for-good.

**PRO-17-justice · Prov 17:15, 26 · [S, multi] — perverted justice as an abomination.** "He who **justifies the wicked** and he who **condemns the righteous** are both alike an **abomination to the LORD**" (v.15); "to **impose a fine on a righteous man is not good**" (v.26). Finding: **inverting justice** — acquitting the guilty, condemning the innocent — is what God abhors *(stated)*. Operation: **the moral revulsion at inverted judgment** — the interior that calls evil good and good evil is an abomination; punishing the righteous offends the moral order *(inferred; the perverted moral sense, w/ Isa 5:20)*. *Surfaced:* inverted justice as abomination (w/ Isa 5:20).

**PRO-17-fool-family · Prov 17:2, 16, 21, 25 · [D, multi] — folly's grief in the family, and the wise servant.** "A **servant who deals wisely** will rule over a son who acts shamefully" (v.2); "why should a fool have **money in his hand to buy wisdom when he has no sense**?" (v.16); "he who **sires a fool gets himself sorrow**… the father of a fool has **no joy**" (v.21); "a **foolish son is a grief to his father and bitterness to her who bore him**" (v.25). Finding: folly **grieves the family's interior** — a fool son is his parents' sorrow and bitterness — while wisdom, even in a servant, rises *(stated)*. Operation: **the child's folly felt as the parent's grief; wisdom as the true inheritance** — character, not birth, orders the household; the fool cannot buy the sense he lacks *(inferred; the relational grief-thread w/ 10:1, 23:24–25; wisdom un-purchasable, w/ Job 28:15)*. *Surfaced:* folly as the family's grief (thread w/ 10:1); wisdom un-purchasable / not birth-bound (w/ Job 28:15).

**PRO-17-surety · Prov 17:18 · [S] — the senseless self-binding.** "One who **lacks sense gives a pledge** and puts up security in the presence of his neighbour" (v.18). Finding: to stand surety is a **want of sense** — the self binding itself to another's debt *(stated)*. Operation: **the imprudent self-binding** (w/ 6:1–5, the surety-snare) *(inferred)*. *Surfaced:* senseless self-binding (thread w/ 6:1–5).

---

## Proverbs 18 - inner-being unit readings

# Proverbs 18 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 18, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**.

---

**PRO-18-tongue-lifedeath · 18:4,6,7,8,20,21 · [T, multi] — the tongue: deep waters, life and death.** "The **words of a man's mouth are deep waters**; the fountain of wisdom a **bubbling brook**"; "a fool's **mouth is his ruin**, and his lips are a **snare to his soul**"; "the words of a **whisperer** go down into the **inner parts**"; "**death and life are in the power of the tongue**" (vv.4,7,8,21). Finding — a speech cornerstone: the tongue holds **death and life**; words are *deep waters* (springing from the depths of the self) that can *ruin the soul* or *nourish* *(stated)*. Operation: **speech as the deep self surfacing, with power over life and death** — and the whisperer's words *penetrate to the inner parts* of the hearer *(inferred; the speech-legibility thread at its most weighty; cross-book w/ Ps 5:9, 52:2–4, 64:3)*. *Hidden:* **words *penetrate the hearer's inner parts*** (speech acts on the interior, not just conveys). *Surfaced:* the tongue's power of life/death (★ shared cornerstone); words-penetrate-the-inner-parts (new).

**PRO-18-refuge · 18:10,11 · [S, multi] — the true tower vs the imagined wall.** "The **name of the LORD is a strong tower**; the righteous **runs into it and is safe**"; "a rich man's wealth is his strong city, and like a high wall **in his imagination**" (vv.10–11). Finding: two refuges — one *real* (God's name), one *imagined* (wealth) *(stated)*. Operation: **the self runs to God as to a tower** — real security is a *fleeing-to* a person, while the trust in wealth is a wall that exists only *in the imagination* *(inferred; the refuge thread + the illusion of wealth-security; cross-book w/ Ps 61:3, 18:2, and 52:7)*. *Hidden:* **wealth-security as *imagined*** — the substrate/text names it a wall "in his imagination," an inner fiction. *Surfaced:* God-as-refuge/tower (shared w/ Ps); the imagined refuge of wealth (new).

**PRO-18-haughty-heart · 18:12 · [S, multi] — the haughty heart before the fall.** "**Before destruction a man's heart is haughty, but humility comes before honour**" (v.12). *Surfaced:* pride/humility (shared cornerstone).

**PRO-18-crushed-spirit · 18:14 · [S] — the unbearable crushed spirit.** "**A man's spirit will endure sickness, but a crushed spirit who can bear?**" (v.14). Finding — a cornerstone: the *spirit* is the self's load-bearing capacity — it can carry bodily illness, but if the *spirit itself* is crushed, nothing remains to bear it *(stated)*. Operation: **the spirit as the bearer of the self; its crushing is the limit of endurance** *(inferred; the deepest statement of the felt interior's floor; cross-book w/ Ps 42:5–6, 143:4 "my spirit faints within me", and Pro 17:22, 15:13)*. *Surfaced:* the crushed spirit as the limit of endurance (★ cornerstone — the spirit as load-bearer).

**PRO-18-hearing · 18:1,2,13,15 · [T, multi] — hearing before answering; the seeking heart.** "A **fool takes no pleasure in understanding, but only in expressing his opinion**"; "if one **answers before he hears**, it is his folly"; "an **intelligent heart acquires knowledge**, and the ear of the wise **seeks** knowledge" (vv.2,13,15). Finding: the fool loves *only his own opinion*; wisdom **hears before it answers** and *seeks* knowledge *(stated)*. Operation: **listening as a discipline against the self's rush to speak** *(inferred; teachability + tongue-restraint; cross-book w/ Ps 141:3)*. *Hidden:* **the fool's *pleasure in his own opinion*** — a self-referential closure. *Surfaced:* hearing-before-answering (new); the self-enclosed opinion-lover (new).

---
**Chapter notes.** **Cornerstones:** the tongue's life/death power (★ 18:21); the crushed spirit / spirit-as-load-bearer (★ 18:14). **New:** words-penetrate-the-inner-parts; the imagined refuge of wealth; hearing-before-answering. **Shared:** God-as-refuge (w/ Ps 61); pride/humility; teachability.

---

## Catch-up units (2026-07-04) — loose study-term verses bound to units

**PRO-18-offended · Prov 18:19, 24 · [D, multi] — the fortified offended heart; the friend closer than a brother.** "A **brother offended is more unyielding than a strong city**, and quarrelling is like the bars of a castle" (v.19); "a man of many companions may come to ruin, but there is a **friend who sticks closer than a brother**" (v.24). Finding: the **offended interior fortifies itself** like a barred castle — harder to breach than a walled city — while true friendship is depth, not number *(stated)*. Operation: **the heart that walls itself in offence, vs the bond that holds** — a grievance turns the self into a fortress; against it stands the rare friend who *sticks* *(inferred; the offended heart's self-fortification is a sharp inner-being image)*. *Surfaced:* the fortified offended heart (new); the deep friend vs many shallow companions.

**PRO-18-partiality · Prov 18:5, 17, 18 · [D] — the bias of first impressions, and the impartial lot.** "It is not good to be **partial to the wicked** or to deprive the righteous of justice" (v.5); "the one who **states his case first seems right, until the other comes and examines him**" (v.17); "the **lot puts an end to quarrels** and decides between powerful contenders" (v.18). Finding: judgment is skewed by **partiality and by whoever speaks first** — the interior leans to the first account until it is tested; the lot cuts through by removing the human bias *(stated)*. Operation: **the self's susceptibility to premature conviction** — the mind settles on the first-heard case, a bias only cross-examination (or an impartial lot) corrects *(inferred; a shrewd note on how the interior forms judgments)*. *Surfaced:* the bias toward the first-stated case (new); partiality as injustice; the lot as impartial decider.

**PRO-18-slack · Prov 18:9 · [S] — the slack worker kin to the destroyer.** "Whoever is **slack in his work is a brother to him who destroys**" (v.9). Finding: **negligence is a form of destruction** — the slack hand and the ruining hand are kin *(stated)*. Operation: **sloth reframed as active harm**, not mere absence *(inferred; w/ the sluggard thread)*. *Surfaced:* slackness as kin to destruction (new).

**PRO-18-wife · Prov 18:22 · [S] — the wife as a good and a favour from the LORD.** "He who **finds a wife finds a good thing** and obtains **favor from the LORD**" (v.22). Finding: a spouse is received as **a good and a divine favour** — a gift, not an achievement *(stated)*. Operation: **the good received as favour** (w/ 19:14, the prudent wife from the LORD) *(inferred)*. *Surfaced:* the wife/relationship as received favour (thread w/ 19:14).

**PRO-18-estate · Prov 18:3, 23 · [S, multi] — the dispositions of low and high estate.** "When **wickedness comes, contempt comes** also, and with dishonour comes disgrace" (v.3); "the **poor use entreaties, but the rich answer roughly**" (v.23). Finding: estate shapes bearing — wickedness drags contempt with it; poverty pleads while wealth answers hard *(stated)*. Operation: **the postures bred by condition** — the roughness of the secure, the entreaty of the low (the contempt-of-the-comfortable, w/ Job 12:5, Ecc 5:8) *(inferred)*. *Surfaced:* the roughness of the secure vs the entreaty of the poor (w/ Job 12:5).

---

## Proverbs 19 - inner-being unit readings

# Proverbs 19 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 19, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**.

---

**PRO-19-self-love · 19:8 · [S] — getting sense is loving one's own soul.** "**Whoever gets sense loves his own soul**; he who keeps understanding will discover good" (v.8). Finding: acquiring wisdom is an act of **self-love / self-care** — to seek sense is to love one's own soul *(stated)*. Operation: **wisdom as care for the self** — the pursuit of understanding is not duty but *self-benefit* rightly understood *(inferred; a distinctive reframe, cross-book w/ the self-preservation of 13:3)*. *Surfaced:* wisdom-as-self-love (new).

**PRO-19-heart-rages · 19:3 · [S] — the heart that rages at God for self-caused ruin.** "**When a man's folly brings his way to ruin, his heart rages against the LORD**" (v.3). Finding — a sharp inner-being note: the self **blames God for ruin it caused itself** — folly wrecks the way, and the heart *rages against the LORD* *(stated)*. Operation: **mis-directed blame** — the inner being deflects responsibility for self-inflicted ruin onto God *(inferred; a rare diagnosis of the resentful heart; cross-book contrast w/ Ps 51:4 "against you… have I sinned" — the opposite, honest owning)*. *Hidden:* **rage-at-God as displaced self-blame.** *Surfaced:* the heart raging at God (self-caused ruin blamed on God) — ★ new (the resentful/deflecting heart).

**PRO-19-anger · 19:11,19 · [T, multi] — slow to anger; overlooking an offense.** "**Good sense makes one slow to anger, and it is his glory to overlook an offense**" (v.11). Finding: to *overlook* an offense is a **glory**, not a weakness — a chosen, honourable restraint *(stated)*. Operation: **anger governed by the *choice to overlook*** — a positive act of the will *(inferred; self-mastery thread)*. *Surfaced:* slow-to-anger / overlooking-as-glory (shared, sharpened).

**PRO-19-fear-satisfied · 19:23 · [S, multi] — the fear that rests satisfied.** "**The fear of the LORD leads to life, and whoever has it rests satisfied**; he will not be visited by harm" (v.23). Finding: reverent fear issues in a **satisfied rest** *(stated; fear-of-LORD → contentment/rest, cross-book w/ Ps 4:8, 34:9)*. *Surfaced:* fear-of-LORD → satisfied rest (shared).

**PRO-19-plans-purpose · 19:21 · [S, multi] — the heart's plans vs the LORD's purpose.** "**Many are the plans in the mind of a man, but it is the purpose of the LORD that will stand**" (v.21). *Surfaced:* planning heart under divine sovereignty (shared w/ 16:9).

**PRO-19-desired-chesed · 19:22 · [S] — steadfast love is what is desired in a person.** "**What is desired in a man is steadfast love**, and a poor man is better than a liar" (v.22). Finding: the quality *prized* in a person is **loyal love (chesed)** — faithfulness over wealth *(stated)*. *Surfaced:* chesed as the prized inner quality (shared w/ Ps chesed thread).

---
**Chapter notes.** **New:** wisdom-as-self-love; the heart raging at God (★ displaced self-blame). **Shared:** slow-to-anger; fear→satisfied rest; planning-heart under sovereignty; chesed prized.

---

## Catch-up units (2026-07-04) — loose study-term verses bound to units

**PRO-19-integrity-desire · Prov 19:1–2 · [D, multi] — integrity over status; desire that needs knowledge.** "**Better is a poor person who walks in his integrity** than one who is crooked in speech and is a fool" (v.1); "**desire without knowledge is not good**, and whoever makes haste with his feet misses his way" (v.2). Finding: **integrity outranks status**, and **desire uninformed by knowledge misfires** — zeal without direction misses the way *(stated)*. Operation: **the rightly-ordered and rightly-directed interior** — integrity over standing, and desire that must be *guided*, not merely felt; haste without knowledge is a wrong turn *(inferred; the un-guided desire, cross-book w/ Ecc 6:9 the wandering appetite)*. *Surfaced:* integrity over status; desire needing knowledge/direction (w/ Ecc 6:9).

**PRO-19-fickle-friends · Prov 19:4, 6, 7 · [D, multi] — friendship keyed to wealth; the deserted poor.** "**Wealth brings many new friends, but a poor man is deserted** by his friend" (v.4); "everyone is a friend to a man who gives gifts" (v.6); "all a poor man's **brothers hate him**; how much more do his friends go far… he pursues them with words, but does not have them" (v.7). Finding: friendship that tracks **wealth** deserts the poor — even brothers withdraw; the poor man chases with words and grasps nothing *(stated)*. Operation: **the fickleness of interested affection** — bonds keyed to gain evaporate in need (the false-friend theme, w/ Job 19:13–19) *(inferred)*. *Surfaced:* interested friendship that deserts the poor (w/ Job 19:14); the poor pursuing with words.

**PRO-19-witness · Prov 19:5, 9, 28, 29 · [D] — the lying witness who mocks justice.** "A **false witness will not go unpunished**… he who breathes out lies will perish" (vv.5,9); "a **worthless witness mocks at justice**, and the mouth of the wicked **devours iniquity**" (v.28). Finding: the false witness **breathes lies and mocks justice**, feeding on iniquity as if it were food *(stated)*. Operation: **the interior that consumes iniquity** — "the mouth of the wicked devours iniquity" images an appetite *for* wrong; lying as an outbreathing of the self *(inferred; iniquity as the wicked's food)*. *Surfaced:* the lie as the self's outbreathing; iniquity devoured as food (new).

**PRO-19-son-discipline · Prov 19:13, 16, 18, 26, 27 · [D, multi] — the son, discipline, and the keeping/despising of one's way.** "A **foolish son is ruin to his father**" (v.13); "whoever **keeps the commandment keeps his life**; he who despises his ways will die" (v.16); "**discipline your son, for there is hope**" (v.18); the son "who does **violence to his father and chases away his mother**" (v.26); "**cease to hear instruction… and you will stray**" (v.27). Finding: the son's character is **ruin or hope** to the family; keeping/despising one's *way* is life or death; ceasing to hear is straying *(stated)*. Operation: **formation through received discipline, and the drift of the un-listening self** — discipline is administered *in hope*; the self that stops hearing instruction wanders off the way *(inferred; receptivity as life-keeping, w/ the teachability thread)*. *Surfaced:* discipline-in-hope; keeping-one's-way as keeping life; the un-listening self's drift.

**PRO-19-teachable · Prov 19:20, 25 · [D] — the teachable interior vs the scoffer.** "**Listen to advice and accept instruction**, that you may gain wisdom" (v.20); "**strike a scoffer, and the simple learn prudence; reprove a man of understanding, and he gains knowledge**" (v.25). Finding: the interior **grows by receiving correction** — the understanding gain from a word what the scoffer only feels as a blow *(stated)*. Operation: **teachability as the capacity to profit from reproof** — the same correction educates the wise and merely warns the simple; the scoffer is unreachable except by the rod *(inferred; the teachable/unteachable heart, w/ 9:7–9)*. *Surfaced:* teachability as profiting from reproof (thread w/ 9:7–9); the reachable vs unreachable self.

**PRO-19-sloth-luxury · Prov 19:10, 15, 24 · [D, multi] — the sluggard and the misfit of ease.** "**Slothfulness casts into a deep sleep**, and an idle person will suffer hunger" (v.15); "the **sluggard buries his hand in the dish and will not even bring it back to his mouth**" (v.24); "it is **not fitting for a fool to live in luxury**" (v.10). Finding: sloth **sinks the self into torpor and hunger**, so paralysed it will not lift food to its own mouth; and ease ill-fits folly *(stated)*. Operation: **the self-defeating inertia of the sluggard** — a torpor so deep it starves the self that could feed itself *(inferred; sloth as self-starving paralysis)*. *Surfaced:* sloth as self-starving torpor (new); ease unfit for folly.

**PRO-19-from-the-Lord · Prov 19:12, 14, 17 · [D, multi] — what is from the LORD's hand, and what returns to it.** "A **king's wrath is like the growling of a lion, but his favour is like dew** on the grass" (v.12); "house and wealth are inherited, but a **prudent wife is from the LORD**" (v.14); "whoever is **generous to the poor lends to the LORD**, and he will repay" (v.17). Finding: the deepest goods (a prudent spouse) come **from the LORD**, and generosity to the poor is a **loan to the LORD** he repays *(stated)*. Operation: **the interior that sees God behind the good and within the gift** — the truest goods are received from his hand, and mercy to the poor is transacted *with him* *(inferred; generosity re-framed as lending to God)*. *Surfaced:* the good as from-the-LORD (thread w/ 18:22); generosity as lending to God (new). *(v.12 = the king's disposition one lives under, arena.)*

---
