## Proverbs 20 - inner-being unit readings

# Proverbs 20 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 20, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**.

---

**PRO-20-spirit-lamp · 20:27 · [S] — the spirit as the lamp of the LORD searching the innermost.** "**The spirit of man is the lamp of the LORD, searching all his innermost parts**" (v.27). Finding — a cornerstone: the human *spirit* is God's **lamp** by which the self's **innermost parts** are searched and lit *(stated)*. Operation: **the self illumined and searched to its depths** — the conscience/spirit is a divine light *inside* the person, exposing what is hidden even from the self *(inferred; the being-searched cornerstone at its most interior; cross-book w/ Ps 139:23 "search me… know my heart", 20:27 the deepest interiorisation of that datum)*. *Surfaced:* the spirit as God's lamp searching the innermost (★ cornerstone, cross-book w/ Ps 139).

**PRO-20-heart-opaque · 20:5 · [S] — the heart's deep, drawable purpose.** "**The purpose in a man's heart is like deep water, but a man of understanding will draw it out**" (v.5). Finding: the heart's purpose is **deep and hidden** — yet a discerning person can *draw it up* like water from a well *(stated)*. Operation: **the opacity *and* the drawability of the inner life** — the depths are real but not wholly sealed; understanding can reach them *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 42:7 "deep calls to deep", the unsearchable-yet-reachable heart; and 25:3)*. *Hidden:* **the inner life as *drawable* by the discerning** (opacity is not total). *Surfaced:* the deep/opaque-yet-drawable heart (★ new — the interior's depth and its reachability).

**PRO-20-pure-heart · 20:9 · [S] — who can say "I have made my heart pure"?** "**Who can say, 'I have made my heart pure; I am clean from my sin'?**" (v.9). Finding — a cornerstone: no one can claim to have **self-cleansed the heart** — the interior cannot be purified by its own effort *(stated)*. Operation: **the heart's un-self-cleansability** — a confession of the limit of self-reform, throwing the self on mercy *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 51:10 "*create* in me a clean heart" — precisely because the self cannot make one; and 19:12 "who can discern his errors")*. *Surfaced:* the heart cannot self-cleanse (★ cornerstone, cross-book w/ Ps 51).

**PRO-20-wait · 20:22 · [S, multi] — do not repay; wait for the LORD.** "**Do not say, 'I will repay evil'; wait for the LORD, and he will deliver you**" (v.22). Finding — a cornerstone: the wronged self is to **renounce repayment and *wait*** *(stated)*. Operation: **entrusting the grievance to God rather than avenging** — the same move as the Psalter's wronged-self-becomes-prayer (Ps 109:4) and wait-on-the-LORD (Ps 27:14); vengeance handed over *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 37, Rom 12:19)*. *Surfaced:* not-repaying / waiting on the LORD (★ shared cornerstone, cross-book w/ Ps 37/109).

---
**Chapter notes.** **Cornerstones (cross-book w/ Ps):** the spirit as God's lamp searching the innermost (★ 20:27, w/ Ps 139); the heart cannot self-cleanse (★ 20:9, w/ Ps 51); not-repaying/waiting (★ 20:22, w/ Ps 37/109). **New:** the deep-opaque-yet-drawable heart (20:5).

---

## Catch-up units (2026-07-04) — loose study-term verses bound to units

**PRO-20-king · Prov 20:2, 8, 26, 28 · [D, multi] — the king's winnowing eye, upheld by steadfast love.** "The **terror of a king is like the growling of a lion**" (v.2); "a king who sits on the throne of judgment **winnows all evil with his eyes**" (v.8); "a wise king **winnows the wicked**" (v.26); "**steadfast love and faithfulness preserve the king**, and by steadfast love his throne is upheld" (v.28). Finding: the king's discerning eye **sifts evil**, and his throne stands not on force but on **steadfast love and faithfulness** *(stated)*. Operation: **the discerning gaze that sifts, and chesed as the throne's true support** — power endures on covenant-love, not terror alone *(inferred; the winnowing eye + love-upheld rule)*. *Surfaced:* the sifting discerning gaze; steadfast-love-and-faithfulness as what upholds authority (w/ the chesed/emunah thread).

**PRO-20-faithful-rare · Prov 20:6 · [S] — the rarity of true faithfulness.** "**Many a man proclaims his own steadfast love, but a faithful man who can find?**" (v.6). Finding: **self-proclaimed loyalty is common; actual faithfulness is rare** — the mouth advertises a chesed the life does not deliver *(stated)*. Operation: **the gap between professed and real faithfulness** — the interior that announces its own loyalty is not the one that keeps it *(inferred; a sharp gem on self-advertised virtue, w/ Job 20:2's self-display)*. *Surfaced:* professed vs real faithfulness (new — a gem); the rarity of the truly faithful self.

**PRO-20-integrity-generative · Prov 20:7, 11 · [D, multi] — integrity that blesses forward; character legible early.** "The **righteous who walks in his integrity — blessed are his children after him!**" (v.7); "even a **child makes himself known by his acts**, by whether his conduct is **pure and upright**" (v.11). Finding: integrity **blesses the next generation**, and character is **legible even in a child** by its acts *(stated)*. Operation: **the interior that shows itself in conduct and transmits forward** — the walk of integrity is read off the deeds and reaches the children *(inferred; character self-disclosing early, and generative)*. *Surfaced:* integrity blessing forward; character legible in a child's acts (new).

**PRO-20-honesty · Prov 20:10, 14, 17, 21, 23 · [D, multi] — dishonesty and its recoil.** "**Unequal weights and measures** are both an **abomination to the LORD**" (vv.10,23); "'Bad, bad,' says the **buyer, but then he boasts**" (v.14); "**bread gained by deceit is sweet**… but afterward his mouth will be full of **gravel**" (v.17); "an inheritance **gained hastily** will not be blessed" (v.21). Finding: dishonest dealing is God's abomination, and its sweetness **turns to gravel** — the fraud that gratifies now recoils later *(stated)*. Operation: **deceit that pleases then punishes the interior** — the buyer's disparaging lie, the sweet-then-gritty bread of fraud; ill-gotten gain un-blessed *(inferred; sin's recoil, w/ Job 20:12–14 "sweet in his mouth… venom within")*. *Surfaced:* the sweet-then-gravel recoil of deceit (w/ Job 20:12); the buyer's disparaging lie.

**PRO-20-given-faculties · Prov 20:12, 24 · [D, multi] — the God-given senses and the limits of self-knowledge.** "The **hearing ear and the seeing eye, the LORD has made them both**" (v.12); "a **man's steps are from the LORD; how then can man understand his way?**" (v.24). Finding: the very **faculties of perception are God's making**, and the self **cannot fully understand its own way** — its steps are ordered beyond its sight *(stated)*. Operation: **the interior's dependence and its self-opacity** — the ear and eye are given, and the path is directed by God past the self's comprehension *(inferred; the limit of self-knowledge, cross-book w/ Job 38:36 "who put wisdom in the inward parts?", Ecc 3:11)*. *Surfaced:* the God-given faculties (w/ Job 38:36); the self opaque to its own way (w/ Ecc 3:11).

**PRO-20-prudence-speech · Prov 20:3, 4, 15, 16, 18, 19, 25, 29 · [D, multi] — strife-avoidance, prudence, and guarded speech.** "It is an **honour to keep aloof from strife**, but every fool will be quarrelling" (v.3); the **sluggard does not plow** (v.4); "there is gold… but the **lips of knowledge are a precious jewel**" (v.15); take a pledge from the reckless surety (v.16); "**plans are established by counsel**" (v.18); "**whoever goes about slandering reveals secrets**" (v.19); "it is a **snare to say rashly, 'It is holy,'** and to reflect only after making vows" (v.25). Finding: the wise interior **avoids strife, plans by counsel, guards its tongue** (no slander, no rash vows), and works in season — and **wise speech is a rarer jewel than gold** *(stated)*. Operation: **the prudent, self-governing interior** — honour in refusing the quarrel, deliberation before commitment, restraint of the secret-spilling and vow-rushing mouth; the lips of knowledge prized above wealth *(inferred; rash vows w/ Ecc 5:2–6; strife-avoidance as honour)*. *Surfaced:* strife-avoidance as honour; the rash vow as a snare (w/ Ecc 5:2–6); slander that spills secrets; wise speech as a jewel above gold. *(v.29 the glory of youth/age = arena.)*

---

## Proverbs 21 - inner-being unit readings

# Proverbs 21 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 21, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**.

---

**PRO-21-king-heart · 21:1,2,30,31 · [T, multi] — the heart in the LORD's hand; the weighed heart.** "**The king's heart is a stream of water in the hand of the LORD; he turns it wherever he will**"; "every way of a man is **right in his own eyes, but the LORD weighs the heart**"; "**no wisdom… can avail against the LORD**" (vv.1,2,30). Finding — a cornerstone: even the most powerful heart is **directable by God** (a stream he channels), the self's self-assessment is unreliable (God *weighs the heart*), and no inner cleverness prevails against God *(stated)*. Operation: **the heart held and turned within God's sovereignty** — the deepest statement that the *will itself* is in God's hand *(inferred; cross-book w/ 16:9, and Ps 33:15 "he fashions the hearts of them all")*. *Surfaced:* the heart in the LORD's hand (★ cornerstone); self-blindness vs God's weighing (shared w/ 16:2, Ps 139).

**PRO-21-proud-heart · 21:4 · [S] — haughty eyes, a proud heart.** "**Haughty eyes and a proud heart, the lamp of the wicked, are sin**" (v.4). *Surfaced:* pride (shared).

**PRO-21-desire-craving · 21:10,17,25,26 · [T, multi] — the craving that kills; the giving self.** "The **soul of the wicked desires evil**"; "**the desire of the sluggard kills him, for his hands refuse to labor. All day long he craves and craves, but the righteous gives and does not hold back**" (vv.10,25–26). Finding: disordered desire is **self-killing** — the sluggard's *craving* consumes him because it never issues in action, set against the *righteous who gives* *(stated)*. Operation: **craving that devours the self vs desire that pours out** — the wicked/sluggard's appetite turns inward and lethal; the righteous's outward-giving is life *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 106:14–15 the craving answered to ruin, and the insatiable eye 27:20)*. *Hidden:* **craving that *kills* because it never acts** (desire without labour is self-destroying). *Surfaced:* the self-killing craving (★ new — desire that devours its owner); the giving vs grasping self.

**PRO-21-mouth-keep · 21:23 · [S] — keeping the mouth keeps the self.** "**Whoever keeps his mouth and his tongue keeps himself out of trouble**" (v.23). *Surfaced:* tongue-restraint as self-preservation (shared w/ 13:3, Ps 141:3).

**PRO-21-bold-face · 21:29 · [S, multi] — bravado vs self-examination.** "**A wicked man puts on a bold face, but the upright gives thought to his ways**" (v.29). Finding: the wicked **projects a bold front**; the upright **examines his own way** *(stated)*. Operation: **bravado (an outward front) vs the self-examining interior** *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 139:23–24 "search me… see if there be any grievous way")*. *Hidden:* **the bold face as a mask over an un-examined self.** *Surfaced:* bravado-vs-self-examination (new).

---
**Chapter notes.** **Cornerstone:** the heart in the LORD's hand (★ 21:1). **New:** the self-killing craving (21:25); bravado-vs-self-examination (21:29). **Shared:** pride; self-blindness vs God's weighing; tongue-restraint.

---

## Catch-up units (2026-07-04) — loose study-term verses bound to units

**PRO-21-righteousness-over-ritual · Prov 21:3, 27 · [S, multi] — the LORD prefers righteousness to sacrifice.** "To do **righteousness and justice is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice**" (v.3); "the **sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination**; how much more when he brings it with **evil intent**" (v.27). Finding: God weighs the **doing of justice above ritual**, and reads the *intent* behind the offering — the wicked's sacrifice, worse with evil intent, is abomination *(stated)*. Operation: **the interior weighed above the rite** — what God receives is righteousness enacted, not sacrifice offered; the heart's intent qualifies the act *(inferred; the moral interior over ritual, w/ Ecc 5:1 "to listen is better than the sacrifice of fools", 1 Sam 15:22)*. *Surfaced:* righteousness above ritual (w/ Ecc 5:1); intent qualifying the offering.

**PRO-21-diligence · Prov 21:5, 20 · [S, multi] — diligence stores, haste and folly squander.** "The **plans of the diligent lead surely to abundance**, but everyone who is **hasty comes only to poverty**" (v.5); "precious treasure and oil are in a wise man's dwelling, but a **foolish man devours it**" (v.20). Finding: the diligent, deliberate interior **accumulates**; the hasty and the foolish **squander** *(stated)*. Operation: **foresight that stores vs impulse that consumes** — planning gathers, haste and folly devour what is gathered *(inferred; the deferring vs devouring self)*. *Surfaced:* diligence-stores / folly-devours (new); haste as the road to poverty.

**PRO-21-crooked-way · Prov 21:6, 7, 8, 16, 18 · [D, multi] — the crooked way and its recoil.** "Treasure by a **lying tongue is a fleeting vapour and a snare of death**" (v.6); "the **violence of the wicked will sweep them away**, because they refuse to do what is just" (v.7); "the **way of the guilty is crooked, but the conduct of the pure is upright**" (v.8); "one who **wanders from the way of good sense will rest in the assembly of the dead**" (v.16). Finding: the guilty interior's **way is crooked** and its gains are vapour — its own violence sweeps it off, its wandering ends among the dead *(stated)*. Operation: **the self-destroying trajectory of the crooked way** — lying-gotten treasure is a death-snare; refusing justice becomes the flood that carries the wicked away *(inferred; the way as destiny, w/ the two-paths thread)*. *Surfaced:* the crooked way as self-destroying (thread); lying-gain as a death-snare; wandering to the assembly of the dead.

**PRO-21-quarrelsome-home · Prov 21:9, 19 · [S] — the strife-filled household.** "**Better to live in a corner of the housetop** than in a house shared with a **quarrelsome wife**" (v.9); "better to live in a **desert land** than with a quarrelsome and fretful woman" (v.19). Finding: **constant strife makes home unlivable** — a rooftop corner or a desert is preferable to a house of quarrelling *(stated)*. Operation: **the intolerable weight of chronic contention** on the shared interior of a home *(inferred; strife as what drives the self to solitude, w/ 17:1)*. *Surfaced:* the strife-filled home the self flees (w/ 17:1).

**PRO-21-scoffer · Prov 21:11, 24 · [S] — the scoffer, and how the simple learn.** "When a **scoffer is punished, the simple becomes wise**; when a wise man is instructed, he gains knowledge" (v.11); "'**Scoffer**' is the name of the **arrogant, haughty man** who acts with arrogant pride" (v.24). Finding: the **scoffer is the arrogant, proud self** — unteachable except as a warning; the simple learn from his punishment what the wise learn from a word *(stated)*. Operation: **arrogance as the closed, only-by-example-teachable interior** (w/ 19:25, 9:7–9) *(inferred)*. *Surfaced:* the scoffer as arrogant pride (thread w/ 19:25); learning by another's punishment.

**PRO-21-God-watch-mercy · Prov 21:12, 13, 14, 15 · [D, multi] — God's watch, mercy's reciprocity, and the divided response to justice.** "The **Righteous One observes the house of the wicked**" (v.12); "whoever **closes his ear to the cry of the poor will himself call out and not be answered**" (v.13); "a **gift in secret averts anger**" (v.14); "when **justice is done, it is a joy to the righteous but terror to evildoers**" (v.15). Finding: God **watches** the wicked's house; mercy is **reciprocal** — deafness to the poor earns a deaf heaven; and the same justice is **joy or terror** by the state of the heart *(stated)*. Operation: **the interior mirrored back — the closed ear meets a closed heaven; justice gladdens or terrifies by what one is** *(inferred; mercy's reciprocity, w/ Matt 5:7; justice read oppositely by the righteous and the guilty)*. *Surfaced:* mercy's reciprocity (the closed ear, w/ Matt 5:7); justice as joy-or-terror by the heart's state; God's watch on the wicked's house.

**PRO-21-pursuit · Prov 21:21, 22, 28 · [D, multi] — the pursuit that finds life; wisdom over might; the enduring word.** "Whoever **pursues righteousness and kindness will find life, righteousness, and honour**" (v.21); "a **wise man scales the city of the mighty** and brings down the stronghold in which they trust" (v.22); "a false witness will perish, but the **word of a man who hears will endure**" (v.28). Finding: the **pursuit of righteousness-and-kindness finds life**; wisdom **overtops might**; and the word of the *listening* self endures where the false witness perishes *(stated)*. Operation: **the seeking interior rewarded with life; the listening self's durable word** — what is pursued (righteousness, kindness) is found; wisdom breaches what force trusts in *(inferred; seeking-rewarded-with-finding, w/ 8:17; wisdom>might w/ Ecc 9:16)*. *Surfaced:* the pursuit of righteousness-and-kindness finding life (w/ 8:17); wisdom over might (w/ Ecc 9:16); the listening self's enduring word.

---

## Proverbs 22 - inner-being unit readings

# Proverbs 22 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 22, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**. (vv.17ff open the "Thirty Sayings.")

---

**PRO-22-humility-fear · 22:4 · [S, multi] — humility and fear rewarded.** "**The reward for humility and fear of the LORD is riches and honour and life**" (v.4). *Surfaced:* humility + fear-of-LORD (shared cornerstone thread).

**PRO-22-purity-heart · 22:11 · [S, multi] — loving purity of heart.** "**He who loves purity of heart, and whose speech is gracious, will have the king as his friend**" (v.11). Finding: the inner being can **love purity of heart** — desire *cleanness itself* — joined to gracious speech *(stated)*. Operation: **the loved clean heart** — purity is not only commanded but *desired*; the self can be in love with its own inward cleanness *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 24:4 "clean hands and a pure heart", 51:10)*. *Hidden:* **purity of heart as an *object of love*** (not just a duty). *Surfaced:* loving-purity-of-heart (new).

**PRO-22-prudent-sees · 22:3,5 · [S, multi] — foreseeing danger; guarding the soul.** "**The prudent sees danger and hides himself, but the simple go on and suffer**"; "**whoever guards his soul will keep far**" from thorns and snares (vv.3,5). Finding: prudence is **foresight that acts** — seeing danger *ahead* and protecting the *soul* *(stated)*. Operation: **the self-guarding foresight** (vs the naive who go on unheeding) *(inferred; discernment thread, cross-book w/ Ps 39:1)*. *Surfaced:* prudent foresight / guarding the soul (shared discernment).

**PRO-22-trust-appeal · 22:17–21 · [D, multi] — the aim of instruction is trust.** "**Incline your ear, and hear the words of the wise, and apply your heart** to my knowledge… keep them **within you**… **that your trust may be in the LORD**" (vv.17–19). Finding: the *purpose* of all the internalising (incline the ear, apply the heart, keep them within) is stated: **that your trust may be in the LORD** *(stated)*. Operation: **instruction internalised → trust** — the whole educational movement of Proverbs is *for* the sake of an inner posture of trust; wisdom is not an end but the road to trusting God *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 119's internalised word, and the trust cluster)*. *Hidden:* **the *telos* of wisdom is trust** — the reading of the whole book's aim. *Surfaced:* instruction-internalised-for-trust (★ new — names the book's inner-being telos).

**PRO-22-anger-company · 22:24,25 · [S, multi] — anger is caught from company.** "**Make no friendship with a man given to anger… lest you learn his ways and entangle yourself in a snare**" (vv.24–25). Finding: dispositions are **contagious** — befriend the wrathful and you *learn his ways* *(stated)*. Operation: **formation-by-company applied to *temper*** — anger is caught, so the self guards its associations *(inferred; the formation-by-company thread, 13:20)*. *Surfaced:* formation-by-company / anger-is-caught (shared w/ 13:20).

---
**Chapter notes.** **New/cornerstone:** instruction-internalised-*for-trust* (★ 22:19 — the book's telos); loving-purity-of-heart. **Shared:** humility+fear; prudent foresight; formation-by-company (anger caught).

---

## Catch-up units (2026-07-04) — loose study-term verses bound to units

**PRO-22-good-name · Prov 22:1 · [S] — a good name prized above wealth.** "A **good name is to be chosen rather than great riches**, and **favour is better than silver or gold**" (v.1). Finding: the interior **values reputation and favour above wealth** — the intangible good of a name outranks the material *(stated)*. Operation: **the value-ranking that prizes the intangible** (w/ 16:16, wisdom over gold) *(inferred)*. *Surfaced:* a good name valued above riches (thread — the interior's value-ranking).

**PRO-22-shared-Maker · Prov 22:2, 12 · [S, multi] — rich and poor of one Maker, under God's watching eyes.** "The **rich and the poor meet together; the LORD is the Maker of them all**" (v.2); "the **eyes of the LORD keep watch over knowledge**, but he overthrows the words of the traitor" (v.12). Finding: rich and poor are **level before their common Maker**, and God's **watching eyes** guard truth and overthrow treachery *(stated)*. Operation: **the leveling of shared createdness, under a watching God** — status collapses before the one Maker; the interior lives under eyes that keep and overthrow *(inferred; shared-createdness ethic w/ Job 31:15, Pro 17:5; the all-seeing God w/ Pro 15:3)*. *Surfaced:* rich-and-poor of one Maker (w/ Job 31:15); God's watching eyes over truth (w/ 15:3).

**PRO-22-formation · Prov 22:6, 15 · [D, multi] — the shaping of the young interior.** "**Train up a child in the way he should go**; even when he is old he will not depart from it" (v.6); "**folly is bound up in the heart of a child**, but the rod of discipline drives it far from him" (v.15). Finding: early **formation sets the lifelong way**, and **folly, native to the child's heart**, is driven out by discipline *(stated)*. Operation: **the malleable young interior shaped by training** — folly is *bound up* in the heart from the start; discipline is the loosing of it, and the trained way holds for life *(inferred; formation as the deep work on the interior, w/ the receptivity thread)*. *Surfaced:* early formation setting the lifelong way (new); folly native to the child's heart, driven out by discipline.

**PRO-22-poor-advocate · Prov 22:7, 16, 22, 23 · [D, multi] — the poor, and the LORD who pleads their cause.** "The **rich rules over the poor**, and the borrower is the slave of the lender" (v.7); "whoever **oppresses the poor to increase his wealth… will only come to poverty**" (v.16); "**do not rob the poor** because he is poor, or crush the afflicted at the gate, for the **LORD will plead their cause** and rob of life those who rob them" (vv.22–23). Finding: exploiting the poor **recoils into poverty**, for the **LORD himself is their advocate**, pleading their cause against the oppressor *(stated)*. Operation: **the interior warned by a God who takes the poor's side** — oppression is not merely unjust but *self-defeating*, met by a divine advocate *(inferred; God as the poor's go'el, w/ 23:11, Job 31:13–15)*. *Surfaced:* the LORD as advocate of the poor (w/ 23:11); oppression's recoil into poverty.

**PRO-22-generous-eye · Prov 22:8, 9 · [S, multi] — the bountiful eye vs the sowing of injustice.** "Whoever **sows injustice will reap calamity**, and the rod of his fury will fail" (v.8); "whoever has a **bountiful eye will be blessed, for he shares his bread with the poor**" (v.9). Finding: **injustice sown reaps calamity**; the **generous ("bountiful") eye** that shares bread is blessed *(stated)*. Operation: **the eye as the index of an open or grasping interior** — the "good eye" gives and is blessed; sown injustice returns as calamity *(inferred; the generous vs grudging eye, w/ 23:6 the stingy eye)*. *Surfaced:* the bountiful/generous eye (w/ 23:6); injustice reaping calamity.

**PRO-22-scoffer-sloth-snare · Prov 22:10, 13, 14 · [D, multi] — the strife-source, the excuse-maker, and the seductive pit.** "**Drive out a scoffer, and strife will go out**, and quarrelling and abuse cease" (v.10); "the **sluggard says, 'There is a lion outside!'**" (v.13); "the **mouth of forbidden women is a deep pit**" (v.14). Finding: the **scoffer is the fount of strife** (remove him, peace returns); the **sluggard invents danger** to justify inaction; the seductive mouth is a **pit** one falls into *(stated)*. Operation: **three self-betraying interiors** — the scoffer whose removal quiets a room, the sluggard's fear-shaped excuse, the seduced self falling into the pit *(inferred; sloth's imagined lion, a wry note on fear-as-excuse)*. *Surfaced:* the scoffer as strife's fount; the sluggard's invented danger (new); the seductive mouth as a pit (thread).

---

## Proverbs 23 - inner-being unit readings

# Proverbs 23 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 23, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**.

---

**PRO-23-appetite · 23:1–7 · [T, multi] — appetite governed; the calculating host.** "Put a **knife to your throat if you are given to appetite**… Do not eat the bread of a **stingy** man… for he is like one who is **inwardly calculating**. 'Eat and drink!' he says, but **his heart is not with you**" (vv.2,6–7). Finding: appetite is to be **violently checked**, and the host's warm words *mask an unwilling heart* — speech and heart **contradict** *(stated)*. Operation: **self-restraint of appetite + the discrepancy between spoken warmth and inner reserve** *(inferred; the masking-self thread, cross-book w/ Ps 55:21 "his speech was smooth… but war was in his heart")*. *Surfaced:* appetite-restraint; the calculating heart behind warm words (shared masking-self).

**PRO-23-give-heart · 23:12,19,26 · [T, multi] — apply / direct / give the heart.** "**Apply your heart to instruction**… **direct your heart in the way**… **My son, give me your heart**, and let your eyes observe my ways" (vv.12,19,26). Finding — a cornerstone: the heart is the thing to be **applied, directed, and *given*** — "give me your heart" is the deepest appeal *(stated)*. Operation: **the heart as the self's core offering** — instruction finally asks not for behaviour but for *the heart itself*, given over *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 51:17 "a broken and contrite heart", and the whole-hearted devotion of Ps 9:1, 119:10)*. *Surfaced:* give/direct the heart (★ cornerstone — the heart as the self's central offering).

**PRO-23-inmost-joy · 23:15,16 · [S, multi] — the parent's inmost joy at a child's wisdom.** "If your heart is wise, **my heart too will be glad**; **my inmost being will exult** when your lips speak what is right" (vv.15–16). Finding: another's wisdom produces **inmost exultation** in the one who loves them *(stated)*. Operation: **joy at another's inner good** — a relational inner-being movement (love rejoicing in the beloved's wisdom) *(inferred)*. *Surfaced:* relational inmost-joy (new).

**PRO-23-envy-fear · 23:17,18 · [S, multi] — the heart guarded from envy; the fear that sustains hope.** "**Let not your heart envy sinners, but continue in the fear of the LORD all the day**… your **hope will not be cut off**" (vv.17–18). Finding: envy of sinners is refused, replaced by *continuing in the fear of the LORD*, which secures **hope** *(stated; refused-envy + fear + hope, cross-book w/ Ps 37:1, 73:3)*. *Surfaced:* refused-envy-of-sinners (shared w/ Ps 37/73).

**PRO-23-drunkard · 23:29–35 · [D, multi] — the enslaved will.** The drunkard: "your heart will **utter perverse things**… 'They struck me, but I was not hurt… **When shall I awake? I must have another drink**'" (vv.33,35). Finding: addiction is a **captured will** — the self, insensible to pain, *returns to the very thing that ruins it* *(stated)*. Operation: **the will enslaved to appetite** — the self cannot free itself; craving *re-commands* it even after harm *(inferred; the compulsive interior, cross-book w/ the captured self of Ps 32:9 unbridled)*. *Hidden:* **the addicted self's insensibility** ("I was not hurt") and its self-re-binding. *Surfaced:* the enslaved will / addiction (new — the compulsive interior at its most vivid).

---
**Chapter notes.** **Cornerstone:** give-me-your-heart (★ 23:26). **New:** relational inmost-joy; the enslaved will (addiction). **Shared:** masking-self; refused-envy (w/ Ps 37/73); appetite-restraint.

---

## Catch-up units (2026-07-04) — loose study-term verses bound to units

**PRO-23-unreceptive · Prov 23:8, 9 · [S, multi] — words wasted on the unreceptive.** "You will **vomit up the morsels** that you have eaten, and **waste your pleasant words**" (v.8); "**do not speak in the hearing of a fool, for he will despise the good sense of your words**" (v.9). Finding: good words spent on the **unreceptive are wasted** — the fool despises them, and even hospitality with a grudging host turns the stomach *(stated)*. Operation: **the futility of pouring wisdom into a closed interior** — the fool's contempt makes counsel pointless; speak, and it is despised *(inferred; the closed self that cannot receive, w/ the pearls-before-swine principle)*. *Surfaced:* words wasted on the closed/unreceptive self (new).

**PRO-23-Redeemer · Prov 23:11 · [S] — the strong Redeemer who pleads their cause.** "Their **Redeemer is strong; he will plead their cause against you**" (v.11). Finding: the defenceless (the fatherless, the poor) have a **strong Redeemer (go'el)** who takes up their case *(stated)*. Operation: **God as the advocate-kinsman of the defenceless** — the interior warned that behind the powerless stands their champion *(inferred; God as go'el, w/ Job 19:25, Pro 22:23)*. *Surfaced:* the strong Redeemer/advocate of the defenceless (thread w/ Job 19:25).

**PRO-23-discipline-honour · Prov 23:14, 22 · [S, multi] — discipline that saves; honour to the aged parent.** "If you **strike him with the rod, you will save his soul from Sheol**" (v.14); "**listen to your father who gave you life, and do not despise your mother when she is old**" (v.22). Finding: **discipline is a rescue** — the rod saves the soul from Sheol; and the source of one's life is to be **honoured, not despised, in age** *(stated)*. Operation: **correction as life-saving love, and filial reverence across the years** — discipline aimed at the *soul*, not mere behaviour; the parent honoured to the end *(inferred; discipline-as-rescue w/ 19:18; honour to the aged)*. *Surfaced:* discipline as soul-rescue (w/ 19:18); reverence for the aged parent.

**PRO-23-parents-joy · Prov 23:24, 25 · [S] — the parent's joy in a wise child.** "The **father of the righteous will greatly rejoice**; he who fathers a wise son will be glad in him. Let your father and mother be glad; **let her who bore you rejoice**" (vv.24–25). Finding: a child's wisdom becomes the **parent's deep joy** — the appeal is to *live so as to gladden* those who bore you *(stated)*. Operation: **the child's character felt as the parent's rejoicing** (the joyful pole of the grief-thread, w/ 10:1, 17:21) *(inferred)*. *Surfaced:* the parent's joy in a wise child (thread w/ 10:1 — the glad pole).

**PRO-23-appetite-truth · Prov 23:20, 23 · [S, multi] — restraint of appetite; prizing truth.** "Be **not among drunkards or among gluttonous eaters** of meat" (v.20); "**buy truth, and do not sell it**; buy wisdom, instruction, and understanding" (v.23). Finding: the ordered interior **restrains appetite** (no drunkenness or gluttony) and **acquires truth at any cost, never trading it away** *(stated)*. Operation: **the self-governed appetite and the treasuring of truth** — truth is to be *bought and held*, wisdom acquired; the belly is not to rule *(inferred; appetite-restraint w/ the never-satisfied thread; truth prized w/ Job 28:15–18)*. *Surfaced:* restraint of appetite (thread); truth bought-and-never-sold (w/ Job 28:15).

**PRO-23-snare · Prov 23:27, 28 · [S] — the seductive pit that lies in wait.** "A **prostitute is a deep pit; an adulteress is a narrow well**. She **lies in wait like a robber** and increases the traitors" (vv.27–28). Finding: illicit desire is a **pit and an ambush** — a snare that lies in wait to trap the self *(stated)*. Operation: **the seductive trap as a lurking predator** (the forbidden-woman snare, thread w/ 22:14, 5–7) *(inferred)*. *Surfaced:* the seductive pit that ambushes (thread w/ 22:14).

---

## Proverbs 24 - inner-being unit readings

# Proverbs 24 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 24, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**.

---

**PRO-24-faint · 24:10 · [S] — fainting reveals the measure of one's strength.** "**If you faint in the day of adversity, your strength is small**" (v.10). Finding: adversity **exposes** the true size of the inner strength — fainting under pressure *measures* it *(stated)*. Operation: **adversity as the test of inner strength** *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 27:13–14 "let your heart take courage")*. *Surfaced:* adversity as the measure of inner strength (new).

**PRO-24-weighs-heart · 24:11,12 · [S, multi] — God weighs the heart and sees the excuse.** "If you say, 'Behold, we did not know this,' **does not he who weighs the heart perceive it?** Does not **he who keeps watch over your soul know it**?" (v.12). Finding — a cornerstone: the plea of ignorance is **seen through** — God *weighs the heart* and *knows* the real motive behind the excuse *(stated)*. Operation: **the pretended-ignorance exposed by the heart-weigher** — the self cannot hide its evasions from the One who weighs the heart *(inferred; the being-known cornerstone, cross-book w/ Ps 44:21 "he knows the secrets of the heart", 139)*. *Surfaced:* God weighs the heart / sees through the excuse (★ shared cornerstone, w/ Ps 139).

**PRO-24-resilience · 24:16 · [S] — the righteous rises again.** "**The righteous falls seven times and rises again**, but the wicked stumble in calamity" (v.16). Finding: righteousness is not the absence of falling but the **capacity to rise** *(stated)*. Operation: **resilience — the repeated rising** *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 37:24 "though he fall, he shall not be cast headlong", 34:19)*. *Surfaced:* resilience / rising-again (shared w/ Ps 37).

**PRO-24-enemy-fall · 24:17,18,19,29 · [T, multi] — the heart guarded against gloating and revenge.** "**Do not rejoice when your enemy falls, and let not your heart be glad** when he stumbles… **Fret not** yourself because of evildoers… **Do not say, 'I will do to him as he has done to me'**" (vv.17–19,29). Finding: the inner being is to **govern its response to an enemy's fall** — no *gladness of heart* at it, no *fretting* over evildoers, no *repayment* *(stated)*. Operation: **the heart guarded against schadenfreude and vengeance** — even the *feeling* of gladness at a foe's ruin is refused *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 35:13–14, and the not-repaying of 20:22, Ps 37)*. *Hidden:* **the interior policed at the level of *feeling*** (not merely act) — "let not your heart be glad." *Surfaced:* the heart guarded against gloating/revenge (★ shared, cross-book w/ Ps 35).

---
**Chapter notes.** **Cornerstone:** God-weighs-the-heart/sees-the-excuse (★ 24:12, w/ Ps 139). **New:** adversity-measures-inner-strength. **Shared:** resilience (w/ Ps 37); the heart guarded against gloating/revenge (w/ Ps 35).

---

## Catch-up units (2026-07-04) — loose study-term verses bound to units

**PRO-24-no-envy · Prov 24:1–2 · [S, multi] — the refused envy of the wicked.** "Be **not envious of evil men, nor desire to be with them**, for their **hearts devise violence**, and their lips talk of trouble" (vv.1–2). Finding: the self **refuses to envy or desire the company of the wicked** — because their interior is a violence-devising heart *(stated)*. Operation: **the disciplined redirection of envy/desire away from the evil** — seeing the wicked's inner content (a heart plotting violence) disarms the envy their prosperity might provoke *(inferred; refused envy, thread w/ Ps 37:1, 73:3)*. *Surfaced:* refused envy of the wicked (thread w/ Ps 37:1, 73); the violence-devising heart seen behind the appeal.

**PRO-24-wisdom-builds · Prov 24:3–6 · [D, multi] — wisdom builds, fills, and strengthens.** "By **wisdom a house is built**, and by understanding it is established; by knowledge the rooms are **filled** with precious riches" (vv.3–4); "a **wise man is full of strength**, and a man of knowledge **enhances his might**… in abundance of counsellors there is victory" (vv.5–6). Finding: wisdom is **constructive and empowering** — it builds and fills the house, and multiplies a man's strength *(stated)*. Operation: **wisdom as the interior's building and strengthening power** — understanding establishes what is built; knowledge is might, and counsel wins wars *(inferred; wisdom > brute strength, w/ Ecc 9:16, Pro 21:22)*. *Surfaced:* wisdom as building/strengthening (new — w/ Ecc 9:16); counsel as victory.

**PRO-24-folly-scheme · Prov 24:7–9 · [D, multi] — folly out of reach; the scheming, abominable interior.** "**Wisdom is too high for a fool**; in the gate he does not open his mouth" (v.7); "whoever **plans to do evil will be called a schemer**" (v.8); "the **devising of folly is sin**, and the scoffer is an **abomination**" (v.9). Finding: wisdom is **beyond the fool's reach**, and the **devising of folly is itself sin** — the plotting interior is named schemer, the scoffer abomination *(stated)*. Operation: **the interior judged at the level of its devising** — evil is sin already in the *planning*, before the act; folly is a scheming, not merely a lack *(inferred; sin located in the devising heart, w/ Ecc 8:11, the heart set on evil)*. *Surfaced:* sin in the devising (w/ the scheming-heart thread); wisdom beyond the fool.

**PRO-24-wicked-nofuture · Prov 24:15, 20 · [S, multi] — the wicked's snuffed-out future.** "Lie **not in wait as a wicked man against the dwelling of the righteous**" (v.15); "the **evil man has no future; the lamp of the wicked will be put out**" (v.20). Finding: the wicked's ambush is futile, for **he has no future** — his lamp goes out *(stated)*. Operation: **the foreclosed horizon of the wicked** (the no-future/extinguished-lamp thread, w/ 13:9, Job 18:5–6) *(inferred)*. *Surfaced:* the wicked's snuffed-out future (thread w/ Job 18:5).

**PRO-24-fear-Lord-king · Prov 24:21–22 · [S] — the dual reverence, and refusal of rebellion.** "My son, **fear the LORD and the king**, and do not join with those who do otherwise, for **disaster will arise suddenly** from them" (vv.21–22). Finding: the ordered self **reveres God and lawful authority** and refuses the company of rebels, whose ruin is sudden *(stated)*. Operation: **reverence as ordering loyalty** (w/ the fear-of-the-LORD thread) *(inferred)*. *Surfaced:* the dual reverence (God and king); refusal of rebellion.

**PRO-24-impartial-rebuke · Prov 24:23–26 · [D, multi] — impartial judgment and the honest word.** "**Partiality in judging is not good**" (v.23); "whoever says to the wicked, 'You are in the **right**,' will be **cursed by peoples**" (v.24); "those who **rebuke the wicked** will have **delight**, and a good blessing" (v.25); "whoever gives an **honest answer kisses the lips**" (v.26). Finding: **impartial judgment and honest rebuke** are blessed; calling the wicked right is cursed; an honest answer is as intimate as a kiss *(stated)*. Operation: **the interior that judges without partiality and speaks the true word** — rebuke of the wicked brings delight; the honest answer is felt as affection *(inferred; the honest word as intimacy, a striking image; impartiality w/ 18:5)*. *Surfaced:* impartial judgment; the honest answer as a kiss (new); rebuke of evil as delight.

**PRO-24-sluggard-lesson · Prov 24:30, 32 · [S] — learning from what one observes.** "I **passed by the field of a sluggard**… then I **saw and considered it; I looked and received instruction**" (vv.30,32). Finding: the wise self **learns by observing** — the sluggard's overgrown field becomes a lesson taken to heart *(stated)*. Operation: **the reflective interior that turns observation into instruction** — looking is not idle; it is receiving teaching *(inferred; the self-teaching by reflection, w/ Ecc's "I saw / I considered")*. *Surfaced:* learning by observation/reflection (new — w/ Ecc's watching self).

## Proverbs 25 - inner-being unit readings

# Proverbs 25 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 25, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**.

---

**PRO-25-heart-unsearchable · 25:2,3 · [S] — the unsearchable depth of the heart.** "As the **heavens for height and the earth for depth, so the heart of kings is unsearchable**" (v.3). Finding: the heart's depth is likened to the *unsearchable* heights and depths of creation *(stated; the opaque-heart thread, cross-book w/ 20:5, Ps 64:6 "the inward mind and heart… are deep")*. *Surfaced:* the unsearchable-deep heart (shared w/ 20:5).

**PRO-25-heavy-heart · 25:20 · [S] — comfort mistimed wounds the heavy heart.** "**Whoever sings songs to a heavy heart is like vinegar on soda**" (v.20). Finding: the **heavy heart** is a real felt state that *ill-timed cheer* only aggravates *(stated)*. Operation: **the felt heaviness that cannot be jollied out of** — comfort must match the heart's state or it *stings* *(inferred; the felt-interior thread, cross-book w/ Ps 137:2–4 refusing to sing in grief)*. *Surfaced:* the heavy heart / mistimed comfort (shared felt-interior).

**PRO-25-enemy-bread · 25:21,22 · [S, multi] — good done to the enemy.** "**If your enemy is hungry, give him bread… you will heap burning coals on his head, and the LORD will reward you**" (vv.21–22). Finding — a cornerstone: the disposition toward the enemy is **active good**, not merely restrained revenge *(stated)*. Operation: **love of enemy expressed as provision** — the self *feeds* the one who wronged it, leaving the outcome to God *(inferred; the fullest positive form of the not-repaying thread, cross-book w/ Ps 35:13, Rom 12:20)*. *Surfaced:* good-done-to-the-enemy / love-of-enemy (★ cornerstone, w/ Ps 35).

**PRO-25-thirsty-soul · 25:25 · [S] — the thirsting soul refreshed by good news.** "**Like cold water to a thirsty soul, so is good news from a far country**" (v.25). Finding: the soul **thirsts**, and good news is *cold water* to it *(stated; the thirsting-soul thread, cross-book w/ Ps 42:1–2, 63:1, 143:6)*. *Surfaced:* the thirsting soul (★ shared cross-book w/ Ps 42/63).

**PRO-25-self-control · 25:28 · [S] — self-control as the wall of the self.** "**A man without self-control is like a city broken into and left without walls**" (v.28). Finding — a cornerstone: the un-governed self is **defenceless**, a breached city *(stated)*. Operation: **self-control as the *wall* that makes a self defensible** — without it the interior lies open to every incursion *(inferred; the self-mastery cornerstone, cross-book w/ 16:32, 29:11, and the Psalter's self-governing self)*. *Surfaced:* self-control as the wall of the self (★ cornerstone).

---
**Chapter notes.** **Cornerstones:** love-of-enemy/good-done (★ 25:21, w/ Ps 35); the thirsting soul (★ 25:25, w/ Ps 42/63); self-control-as-wall (★ 25:28). **Shared:** the unsearchable heart; the heavy heart / mistimed comfort.

---

## Catch-up units (2026-07-04) — loose study-term verses bound to units

**PRO-25-humility-before-great · Prov 25:5, 6, 7 · [D] — self-lowering before the great.** "Take away the **wicked from the presence of the king**, and his throne will be established in righteousness" (v.5); "**do not put yourself forward** in the king's presence or stand in the place of the great, for it is **better to be told, 'Come up here,'** than to be put lower" (vv.6–7). Finding: the wise self **does not exalt itself** before the great — it is better to be *raised* than to be *lowered* *(stated)*. Operation: **the humility that declines self-promotion** — taking the low place and being invited up, rather than grasping honour and being demoted *(inferred; self-lowering as wisdom, w/ Luke 14:8–10; the un-self-promoting interior)*. *Surfaced:* the humility that declines self-promotion (new — w/ Luke 14:8).

**PRO-25-prudent-dispute · Prov 25:8, 9, 10 · [D, multi] — restraint in conflict.** "Do **not hastily bring** a matter into court… what will you do when your neighbour puts you to shame?" (v.8); "**argue your case with your neighbour himself, and do not reveal another's secret**, lest… your **ill repute have no end**" (vv.9–10). Finding: the prudent self **handles disputes directly and discreetly** — not rushing to court, not betraying confidences *(stated)*. Operation: **the self-restraint that keeps conflict contained and confidences kept** — haste and secret-telling both recoil into lasting shame *(inferred; discretion in dispute)*. *Surfaced:* restraint in conflict; keeping a confidence even in a quarrel (new).

**PRO-25-listening-faithful · Prov 25:12, 13 · [S, multi] — the listening ear and the refreshing faithful.** "Like a **gold ring… is a wise reprover to a listening ear**" (v.12); "like the **cold of snow in harvest is a faithful messenger** to those who send him; he **refreshes the soul** of his masters" (v.13). Finding: wise reproof meeting a **listening ear** is an ornament; a **faithful messenger refreshes the soul** *(stated)*. Operation: **the receptive interior that adorns reproof, and faithfulness as refreshment** — the reproof is beautiful only where there is an ear to receive it; the faithful one cools like snow *(inferred; receptivity as what makes correction golden, w/ the teachability thread)*. *Surfaced:* the listening ear that makes reproof golden (thread); faithfulness that refreshes the soul (new).

**PRO-25-empty-betrayal · Prov 25:14, 18, 19 · [D, multi] — empty words and unreliable trust.** "Like **clouds and wind without rain is a man who boasts of a gift he does not give**" (v.14); "a man who **bears false witness** against his neighbour is like a **war club, a sword, a sharp arrow**" (v.18); "**trusting in a treacherous man in time of trouble is like a bad tooth or a foot that slips**" (v.19). Finding: the **empty boaster** promises rain and gives none; false witness is a weapon; and **misplaced trust fails exactly when needed** *(stated)*. Operation: **the interior that promises and does not deliver, and the pain of trust betrayed in crisis** — the treacherous man is a tooth that breaks on the very bite that needs it *(inferred; the felt failure of false trust, w/ Job 6:15 the dry-wadi friends)*. *Surfaced:* the empty boaster (new); trust that fails in the crisis (w/ Job 6:15).

**PRO-25-restraint · Prov 25:17, 23, 27 · [D, multi] — restraint of presence, tongue, and self-glory.** "Let your **foot be seldom in your neighbour's house**, lest he have his fill of you and **hate** you" (v.17); "the north wind brings rain, and a **backbiting tongue, angry looks**" (v.23); "it is not good to eat much honey, **nor is it glorious to seek one's own glory**" (v.27). Finding: the self exercises **restraint** — of its presence (don't wear out welcome), its tongue (backbiting breeds anger), and its self-seeking (glory-hunting is not glorious) *(stated)*. Operation: **the self-limiting interior** — knowing when enough is enough, in company, in speech, and in appetite for honour *(inferred; self-restraint across domains; the glory-seeking self checked, w/ Ecc 1's vanity of self-exalting)*. *Surfaced:* restraint of presence/tongue/self-glory (new); glory-seeking as not glorious.

**PRO-25-compromised-righteous · Prov 25:26 · [S] — the righteous who gives way.** "Like a **muddied spring or a polluted fountain is a righteous man who gives way before the wicked**" (v.26). Finding: a righteous man who **caves before the wicked** becomes a *fouled source* — his compromise pollutes what should be pure *(stated)*. Operation: **integrity's failure imaged as a polluted spring** — the righteous is meant to be a clean fountain; yielding to evil muddies it *(inferred; a sharp image of compromised integrity)*. *Surfaced:* the compromised righteous as a fouled spring (new — a gem).

**PRO-25-quarrelsome · Prov 25:24 · [S] — the strife-filled home (again).** "It is **better to live in a corner of the housetop than in a house shared with a quarrelsome wife**" (v.24). Finding: chronic strife makes the home unlivable *(stated; repeated from 21:9)*. Operation: strife driving the self to solitude (thread w/ 21:9, 17:1) *(inferred)*. *Surfaced:* the strife-filled home (thread w/ 21:9).

## Proverbs 26 - inner-being unit readings

# Proverbs 26 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 26, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**.

---

**PRO-26-wise-own-eyes · 26:12 · [S] — self-conceit worse than folly.** "**Do you see a man who is wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him**" (v.12). Finding: **self-conceit is more hopeless than folly** — the self certain of its own wisdom cannot be helped *(stated; the self-certainty thread, cross-book w/ 3:7, 12:15, Ps 36:2)*. *Surfaced:* self-conceit as the most hopeless closure (★ shared thread, sharpened).

**PRO-26-sluggard · 26:13,14,15,16 · [T, multi] — the self-justifying sloth.** "The sluggard says, '**There is a lion in the road!**'… As a **door turns on its hinges, so the sluggard on his bed**… The sluggard is **wiser in his own eyes than seven men** who can answer sensibly" (vv.13,14,16). Finding: sloth **manufactures excuses** (a lion!), turns endlessly without progress, and is *self-certain* about its own sense *(stated)*. Operation: **the self-justifying inertia** — the slothful interior *rationalises* its inaction and cannot see itself *(inferred; sloth + self-conceit joined)*. *Hidden:* **sloth's self-justification** (excuse-making as an inner operation). *Surfaced:* self-justifying sloth (new — sloth wedded to self-conceit).

**PRO-26-concealing-heart · 26:23,24,25,26 · [T, multi] — the masking self exposed.** "**Fervent lips with an evil heart** are like the **glaze covering an earthen vessel**… whoever **hates disguises himself with his lips and harbors deceit in his heart**; when he **speaks graciously, believe him not, for there are seven abominations in his heart**; though his hatred be **covered with deception**, his wickedness will be **exposed**" (vv.23–26). Finding — a cornerstone of the masking self: the wicked **coats an evil heart with gracious speech** (glaze over cheap clay), *disguising hatred with the lips* — but the concealment *fails*, the heart is exposed *(stated)*. Operation: **the split between mouth and heart made into a strategy** — the self deliberately *masks* its interior with fair speech, and the reading's warning is *not to believe the surface*; yet the hidden heart is finally *uncoverable to God/the assembly* *(inferred; the masking-self thread at its fullest, cross-book w/ Ps 28:3 "who speak peace… while evil is in their hearts", 55:21, 62:4)*. *Hidden:* **concealment as a *deliberate craft*** (the glaze) — and its ultimate failure. *Surfaced:* the masking/concealing heart (★ cornerstone, cross-book w/ Ps 28/55); "believe not the fair surface."

---
**Chapter notes.** **Cornerstone:** the masking/concealing heart (★ 26:24–26, w/ Ps 28/55). **New:** self-justifying sloth. **Shared:** self-conceit ("wise in his own eyes").

---

## Catch-up units (2026-07-04) — loose study-term verses bound to units

**PRO-26-fool-honor · Prov 26:1, 8, 11 · [D, multi] — honour misplaced on a fool; folly's return.** "Like snow in summer… **honour is not fitting for a fool**" (v.1); "like one who **binds the stone in the sling is one who gives honour to a fool**" (v.8); "like a **dog that returns to his vomit is a fool who repeats his folly**" (v.11). Finding: honour on a fool is **as absurd and dangerous as arming a sling with the stone still bound**; and the fool **cannot leave his folly** — he returns to it like a dog to its vomit *(stated)*. Operation: **the fixity of folly** — it is not a passing mistake but a *returning*, a compulsion the fool circles back to *(inferred; folly as compulsive repetition, the un-teachable self at its most fixed)*. *Surfaced:* folly as compulsive return (new); honour absurd on a fool.

**PRO-26-answer-fool · Prov 26:4, 5 · [S, multi] — the discernment of when to engage folly.** "**Answer not a fool according to his folly, lest you be like him**" (v.4); "**answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own eyes**" (v.5). Finding: the paired paradox — **whether to engage folly depends on the moment**: silence to avoid becoming a fool, engagement to puncture his self-conceit *(stated)*. Operation: **the discerning interior that reads which folly needs silence and which needs answer** — no rule fits both; wisdom is knowing which risk (imitation vs his self-conceit) is live *(inferred; a gem on situational discernment — the same act right or wrong by the moment)*. *Surfaced:* situational discernment in engaging folly (new — a gem); the two risks (becoming like him / confirming his conceit).

**PRO-26-meddle-strife · Prov 26:17, 21 · [S, multi] — meddling and the kindling of strife.** "Whoever **meddles in a quarrel not his own** is like one who takes a **passing dog by the ears**" (v.17); "as charcoal to embers… so is a **quarrelsome man for kindling strife**" (v.21). Finding: **meddling in others' quarrels invites needless injury**, and the contentious self **feeds strife** as fuel feeds fire *(stated)*. Operation: **the strife-kindling interior, and the folly of grabbing another's quarrel** — some conflicts the self should not seize; the quarrelsome man is the fuel that keeps them burning *(inferred; the strife-thread)*. *Surfaced:* meddling as self-injury (new); the quarrelsome man as strife's fuel (thread).

**PRO-26-deceit · Prov 26:19, 28 · [S, multi] — the deceiver's "joke" and the flattering, hating mouth.** "So is the man who **deceives his neighbour and says, 'I am only joking!'**" (v.19); "a **lying tongue hates its victims, and a flattering mouth works ruin**" (v.28). Finding: deceit **hides behind 'just joking,'** and beneath the flattering mouth is **hatred** — flattery ruins *(stated)*. Operation: **the malice masked as jest or flattery** — the lying tongue *hates* the very ones it addresses; the smooth mouth is a weapon *(inferred; flattery as concealed hatred, a sharp inner-being diagnosis)*. *Surfaced:* deceit masked as joking (new); flattery as concealed hatred (new).

## Proverbs 27 - inner-being unit readings

# Proverbs 27 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 27, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**.

---

**PRO-27-boast-tomorrow · 27:1,2 · [S, multi] — presumption and self-praise.** "**Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring**"; "**let another praise you, and not your own mouth**" (vv.1–2). Finding: the self is to refuse **presumption over the future** and **self-praise** — two forms of over-reaching *(stated; cross-book w/ Ps 30:6 "I said in my prosperity, I shall never be moved")*. *Surfaced:* presumption / self-praise refused (shared w/ Ps 30).

**PRO-27-passions · 27:4 · [S] — the ranking of the passions.** "**Wrath is cruel, anger is overwhelming, but who can stand before jealousy?**" (v.4). Finding: the passions are **weighed against each other** — jealousy the most irresistible *(stated)*. Operation: **a taxonomy of the overwhelming passions** (wrath < anger < jealousy) *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps's fierce affections)*. *Surfaced:* the ranked passions / jealousy strongest (new).

**PRO-27-friend-wounds · 27:5,6,9 · [T, multi] — the honest friend; the gladdened heart.** "**Better is open rebuke than hidden love**. **Faithful are the wounds of a friend**; profuse the kisses of an enemy"; "**oil and perfume make the heart glad**, and the sweetness of a friend comes from his earnest counsel" (vv.5–6,9). Finding: love is **better shown in honest wounding** than in hidden fondness or flattering kisses; and a friend's *earnest counsel* **gladdens the heart** *(stated)*. Operation: **love as honest correction** (the friend's wounds are *faithful*) and **the heart gladdened by true counsel** *(inferred; teachability + the felt heart; cross-book w/ Ps 141:5 "let a righteous man strike me")*. *Hidden:* **love that *wounds faithfully* over love that *hides***. *Surfaced:* the honest-wounding friend (★ cross-book w/ Ps 141:5); the heart gladdened by counsel.

**PRO-27-iron-sharpens · 27:17 · [S] — formation by another.** "**Iron sharpens iron, and one man sharpens another**" (v.17). Finding — a cornerstone: the self is **honed by another self** *(stated)*. Operation: **mutual formation — the self shaped sharper by contact with another** *(inferred; the formation-by-company thread, cross-book w/ 13:20, and the trust-formation law of Ps 115:8)*. *Surfaced:* formation-by-another / iron-sharpens-iron (★ cornerstone — mutual formation).

**PRO-27-heart-mirror · 27:19 · [S] — the heart is the true self.** "**As in water face reflects face, so the heart of man reflects the man**" (v.19). Finding — a cornerstone: the **heart *is* the true self** — what a person really is shows in the heart as a face in water *(stated)*. Operation: **the heart as the mirror/identity of the person** — the deepest Proverbs statement that the self *is* its heart *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 7:9 "the minds and hearts", the heart as the self's core)*. *Surfaced:* the heart as the true self (★ cornerstone — the heart = the person).

**PRO-27-insatiable · 27:20 · [S] — the never-satisfied eye.** "**Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied, and never satisfied are the eyes of man**" (v.20). Finding — a cornerstone: human desire (the *eyes*) is **structurally insatiable**, like the grave *(stated)*. Operation: **the unfillable appetite** — the self's wanting has no natural floor; it is *never satisfied* *(inferred; the shadow-side of the desire thread, cross-book w/ Ps 106:14–15, and the only-God-satisfies datum of Ps 107:9, 145:16)*. *Surfaced:* the insatiable eye/desire (★ cornerstone — the unfillable appetite).

**PRO-27-tested-praise · 27:21 · [S] — a man is tested by his praise.** "The crucible for silver… **and a man is tested by his praise**" (v.21). Finding: how one **handles praise** assays the self — praise is a furnace *(stated)*. *Surfaced:* praise as a test of the self (new).

---
**Chapter notes.** **Cornerstones:** iron-sharpens-iron / formation-by-another (★ 27:17); the heart as the true self (★ 27:19); the insatiable eye (★ 27:20). **New:** the ranked passions; praise-as-test. **Shared:** presumption/self-praise (w/ Ps 30); the honest-wounding friend (w/ Ps 141:5).

---

## Catch-up units (2026-07-04) — loose study-term verses bound to units

**PRO-27-fool-weight · Prov 27:3, 22 · [S, multi] — the weight and fixity of a fool's folly.** "A stone is heavy… but a **fool's provocation is heavier than both**" (v.3); "**crush a fool in a mortar** with a pestle… yet his **folly will not depart** from him" (v.22). Finding: a fool's vexation is a **crushing weight**, and his folly is so **fixed** that even pulverising will not remove it *(stated)*. Operation: **folly as an ineradicable interior set** — not a surface fault correction can grind out, but the grain of the self *(inferred; folly's fixity, w/ 26:11 the returning dog)*. *Surfaced:* the crushing weight of a fool's provocation (new); folly as ineradicable (thread w/ 26:11).

**PRO-27-appetite · Prov 27:7 · [S] — appetite conditioned by fullness and hunger.** "One who is **full loathes honey**, but to one who is **hungry everything bitter is sweet**" (v.7). Finding: **satisfaction and need re-colour the same thing** — honey cloys the full, and bitterness sweetens for the hungry *(stated)*. Operation: **the interior's valuation set by its own state of fullness** — desire is not fixed to the object but to the appetite's condition *(inferred; the never-satisfied thread's mirror — fullness dulls, hunger sweetens, w/ Ecc 6:7)*. *Surfaced:* appetite conditioned by fullness/hunger (new — w/ Ecc 6:7); the state of the self colouring the object.

**PRO-27-strayer-friend · Prov 27:8, 10 · [S, multi] — the strayer, and the near friend.** "Like a **bird that strays from its nest is a man who strays from his home**" (v.8); "**do not forsake your friend**… better is a **neighbour who is near than a brother who is far away**" (v.10). Finding: to wander from one's place is a **displacement** like a bird from its nest; and a **near friend outvalues a distant brother** *(stated)*. Operation: **rootedness and proximate loyalty** — the self belongs somewhere, and the friend who is *near in calamity* is worth more than kin who are far *(inferred; the value of the present friend, w/ 18:24)*. *Surfaced:* the strayer displaced from his place (new); the near friend over the distant brother (w/ 18:24).

**PRO-27-child-glad · Prov 27:11 · [S] — the child's wisdom that gladdens and vindicates.** "Be **wise, my son, and make my heart glad**, that I may answer him who reproaches me" (v.11). Finding: a child's wisdom **gladdens the parent's heart** and even **vindicates** him before critics *(stated)*. Operation: **the child's character as the parent's joy and defence** (the glad pole, w/ 10:1, 23:24) *(inferred)*. *Surfaced:* the child's wisdom gladdening and vindicating the parent (thread w/ 10:1).

**PRO-27-prudence-service · Prov 27:12, 18 · [S, multi] — foresight, and faithful service rewarded.** "The **prudent sees danger and hides himself**, but the simple go on and suffer" (v.12); "whoever **tends a fig tree will eat its fruit**, and he who **guards his master will be honoured**" (v.18). Finding: prudence **foresees and takes cover**; faithful tending is **rewarded** — the fruit to the keeper, honour to the guard *(stated)*. Operation: **the anticipating self and the fidelity that reaps** — foresight spares suffering; steady service earns its fruit and honour *(inferred; prudence w/ 22:3; faithful service)*. *Surfaced:* foresight that takes cover (thread w/ 22:3); faithful service rewarded (new).

**PRO-27-praise-contention · Prov 27:14, 16 · [S, multi] — excessive praise as curse; the un-restrainable contentious.** "Whoever **blesses his neighbour with a loud voice, rising early**… will be counted as **cursing**" (v.14); "to **restrain her** [the contentious woman] is to **restrain the wind** or grasp oil in the hand" (v.16). Finding: **over-loud praise curdles into a curse**, and the chronically contentious is **as un-restrainable as the wind** *(stated)*. Operation: **the excess that inverts its intent, and the ungovernable contentious interior** — praise too loud reads as mockery; the quarrelsome cannot be gripped any more than wind or oil *(inferred; the un-restrainable contentious, w/ 21:9,19)*. *Surfaced:* over-loud praise as curse (new); the ungovernable contentious (thread w/ 21:9).

**PRO-27-stewardship · Prov 27:23, 24, 27 · [D, multi] — diligent stewardship against impermanent riches.** "**Know well the condition of your flocks**… for **riches do not last forever**; does a crown endure to all generations?" (vv.23–24); "there will be **enough goats' milk** for your food… and maintenance for your girls" (v.27). Finding: attentive **stewardship** sustains the household, because **riches are impermanent** — the diligent care, not the hoard, provides *(stated)*. Operation: **the interior that tends rather than trusts wealth** — knowing the flock's condition, aware that riches and crowns pass, so care is ongoing *(inferred; diligence over hoarding, w/ the impermanence-of-riches thread, Ecc)*. *Surfaced:* attentive stewardship (new); the impermanence of riches (w/ Ecc).

**PRO-27-surety · Prov 27:13 · [S] — the senseless surety (again).** "**Take a man's garment when he has put up security for a stranger**" (v.13). Finding: standing surety for a stranger is folly to be guarded against *(stated; thread w/ 6:1–5, 17:18, 22:26)*. Operation: the imprudent self-binding *(inferred)*. *Surfaced:* the surety-snare (thread w/ 6:1).

---

## Proverbs 28 - inner-being unit readings

# Proverbs 28 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 28, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**.

---

**PRO-28-bold-lion · 28:1 · [S] — the guilty flee, the righteous are bold.** "**The wicked flee when no one pursues, but the righteous are bold as a lion**" (v.1). Finding: the inner state of **guilt manufactures pursuers** where none exist, while a clear conscience is **fearless** *(stated)*. Operation: **conscience as the source of dread or boldness** — the wicked's fear is *self-generated* (no one pursues), the righteous's courage is *conscience-born* *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 53:5 "there they are in great terror, where there was no terror", 27:1)*. *Hidden:* **fear conjured by a guilty conscience** (dread with no external cause). *Surfaced:* conscience → dread-or-boldness (★ new — the self-generated fear of guilt).

**PRO-28-confess · 28:13 · [S, multi] — concealment vs confession of sin.** "**Whoever conceals his transgressions will not prosper, but he who confesses and forsakes them will obtain mercy**" (v.13). Finding — a cornerstone: **hiding sin fails; confessing-and-forsaking obtains mercy** *(stated)*. Operation: **confession as the release of the concealed self** — the interior that *hides* its sin stays bound; the one that *owns and forsakes* is freed to mercy *(inferred; the exact Proverbs parallel to Ps 32:3–5 "when I kept silent, my bones wasted… I acknowledged my sin… and you forgave")*. *Surfaced:* confession-vs-concealment (★ cornerstone, cross-book w/ Ps 32).

**PRO-28-fear-harden · 28:14 · [S, multi] — fearing always vs the hardened heart.** "**Blessed is the one who fears the LORD always, but whoever hardens his heart will fall into calamity**" (v.14). Finding: continual reverent fear vs the **hardened heart** — the self that *hardens* falls *(stated)*. Operation: **the hardening of the heart as the opposite of the fear of the LORD** *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 95:8 "do not harden your hearts")*. *Hidden:* **the heart-hardening operation** (a self-inflicted callousing). *Surfaced:* the hardened heart vs continual fear (★ new — the hardening operation, cross-book w/ Ps 95).

**PRO-28-trust · 28:25,26 · [T, multi] — trust in the LORD vs greed vs self-reliance.** "A **greedy man stirs up strife, but the one who trusts in the LORD will be enriched**"; "**whoever trusts in his own mind is a fool**, but he who walks in wisdom will be delivered" (vv.25–26). Finding: trust is set against **greed** and against **self-reliance** ("trusts in his own mind") *(stated)*. Operation: **trust as the alternative to grasping and to self-confidence** — the two great rivals to trusting God are *greed* and *the self's own mind* *(inferred; cross-book w/ 3:5 "lean not on your own understanding", Ps 62:8–10)*. *Surfaced:* trust vs greed vs self-reliance (shared, sharpened w/ 3:5).

---
**Chapter notes.** **Cornerstones:** confession-vs-concealment (★ 28:13, w/ Ps 32); the hardened heart (★ 28:14, w/ Ps 95). **New:** conscience→dread-or-boldness (28:1). **Shared:** trust vs greed/self-reliance (w/ 3:5, Ps 62).

---

## Catch-up units (2026-07-04) — loose study-term verses bound to units

**PRO-28-rule-public · Prov 28:2, 12, 28 · [D, multi] — the public weather of righteous vs wicked ascendancy.** "When a land transgresses, it has **many rulers**, but with a **man of understanding… stability** continues" (v.2); "when the **righteous triumph, great glory**, but when the wicked rise, **people hide themselves**" (vv.12,28). Finding: the ascendancy of righteousness or wickedness **changes the public atmosphere** — glory and stability, or a people in hiding *(stated)*. Operation: **the collective interior shaped by who rules** — the same people flourish or hide depending on the moral character in power *(inferred; the corporate mood, w/ 29:2)*. *Surfaced:* the public atmosphere set by righteous/wicked rule (thread w/ 29:2).

**PRO-28-law-ear · Prov 28:4, 7, 9 · [D, multi] — the law and the hearing (or turned-away) ear.** "Those who **forsake the law praise the wicked**, but those who keep it strive against them" (v.4); "the one who **keeps the law is a son with understanding**" (v.7); "if one **turns away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer is an abomination**" (v.9). Finding: keeping the law forms an understanding self; **turning the ear from it corrupts even prayer** *(stated)*. Operation: **the ear's orientation determining the whole interior** — refuse to hear instruction, and even worship sours; the receptive ear is the root of understanding *(inferred; the hearing ear, w/ the teachability thread; unheard-law makes prayer abomination — a striking link of receptivity and worship)*. *Surfaced:* the turned-away ear corrupting even prayer (new); law-keeping as understanding.

**PRO-28-seek-understand · Prov 28:5 · [S] — seeking the LORD as the key to understanding justice.** "**Evil men do not understand justice, but those who seek the LORD understand it completely**" (v.5). Finding: moral understanding is **unlocked by seeking God** — the evil are blind to justice; the God-seeker sees it fully *(stated)*. Operation: **the God-ward orientation that opens moral perception** (w/ the fear-of-the-LORD-as-wisdom thread, Job 28:28) *(inferred)*. *Surfaced:* seeking-God as the key to understanding justice (w/ Job 28:28).

**PRO-28-integrity-way · Prov 28:6, 10, 18 · [D, multi] — the two ways; the pit-digger.** "**Better a poor man who walks in his integrity** than a rich man crooked in his ways" (v.6); "whoever **misleads the upright into an evil way will fall into his own pit**" (v.10); "whoever **walks in integrity will be delivered**, but he who is crooked will **suddenly fall**" (v.18). Finding: **integrity delivers and outranks crooked wealth**; the one who lays a trap for the upright **falls into it himself** *(stated)*. Operation: **the self-recoiling crooked way** — the pit dug for another swallows the digger; the straight walk is preserved *(inferred; the pit-digger, w/ Ps 7:15; integrity over status, w/ 19:1)*. *Surfaced:* the pit-digger self-trapped (w/ Ps 7:15); integrity delivering (thread).

**PRO-28-wealth-greed · Prov 28:8, 11, 19, 20, 22, 27 · [D, multi] — wealth, self-conceit, greed, and generosity.** "Whoever **multiplies wealth by interest… gathers it for him who is generous to the poor**" (v.8); "a **rich man is wise in his own eyes**, but a poor man of understanding **finds him out**" (v.11); "**works his land → plenty of bread**; follows worthless pursuits → poverty" (v.19); "a **faithful man abounds with blessings**, but whoever **hastens to be rich** will not go unpunished" (v.20); "a **stingy man hastens after wealth** and does not know that poverty will come" (v.22); "whoever **gives to the poor will not want**, but he who **hides his eyes** gets many a curse" (v.27). Finding: **greedy haste for wealth self-defeats** (unpunished it is not, and poverty overtakes it), the rich are **self-deceived**, and **generosity to the poor** is the blessed path *(stated)*. Operation: **the grasping vs the open interior** — the hastening, stingy, self-conceited self toward poverty and curse; the faithful, generous, land-working self toward plenty and blessing *(inferred; the never-satisfied greed, w/ Ecc 5:10; generosity as un-wanting, w/ 11:24)*. *Surfaced:* greedy haste self-defeating (w/ Ecc 5:10); the rich self-deceived; generosity as the un-wanting path.

**PRO-28-oppressor · Prov 28:15, 16 · [S, multi] — the oppressive ruler.** "Like a **roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a poor people**" (v.15); "a **ruler who lacks understanding is a cruel oppressor**, but he who **hates unjust gain will prolong his days**" (v.16). Finding: the understanding-lacking ruler becomes a **predatory oppressor**; the one who **hates unjust gain** endures *(stated)*. Operation: **power without understanding turning predatory** — the interior that hates ill-gotten gain is what makes rule bearable and lasting *(inferred)*. *Surfaced:* the predatory ruler (new); hating unjust gain as what preserves.

**PRO-28-guilt-theft · Prov 28:17, 21, 24 · [D, multi] — guilt's flight, cheap corruption, the self-justified thief.** "One **burdened with the blood of another** will be a **fugitive until death**" (v.17); "to show **partiality is not good**, but for a **piece of bread a man will do wrong**" (v.21); "whoever **robs his father or mother and says, 'That is no transgression,'** is a companion to a destroyer" (v.24). Finding: bloodguilt makes a lifelong **fugitive**; corruption comes **cheap** (a piece of bread); and the thief who **denies his sin** is kin to a destroyer *(stated)*. Operation: **the fleeing conscience, and the self that renames its theft as innocence** — guilt cannot rest; the self-justified robber calls his sin "no transgression" *(inferred; guilt's flight, w/ Gen 4:12; self-justified sin, the un-owned wrong)*. *Surfaced:* guilt's lifelong flight (w/ Gen 4:12); corruption bought cheap; the self-justified thief (new).

**PRO-28-rebuke · Prov 28:23 · [S] — honest rebuke over flattery.** "Whoever **rebukes a man will afterward find more favour** than he who **flatters** with his tongue" (v.23). Finding: **honest rebuke earns deeper favour** than flattery — the truth-teller is finally more loved than the flatterer *(stated)*. Operation: **the reproof that is valued over time** (w/ 27:5–6 "faithful are the wounds of a friend") *(inferred)*. *Surfaced:* honest rebuke outlasting flattery (thread w/ 27:5).

---
