## Proverbs 29 - inner-being unit readings

# Proverbs 29 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 29, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**.

---

**PRO-29-stiff-neck · 29:1 · [S] — the hardened, unteachable self broken.** "**He who is often reproved, yet stiffens his neck, will suddenly be broken beyond healing**" (v.1). Finding: repeated reproof *refused* — the **stiffened neck** — ends in sudden, unhealable breaking *(stated)*. Operation: **the un-teachable self hardening past repair** — each refused reproof calcifies until nothing can bend it *(inferred; the terminal form of the closed heart, cross-book w/ Ps 95:8, and the teachability thread)*. *Surfaced:* the hardened/unteachable self (★ shared — the terminal closed heart).

**PRO-29-vent-spirit · 29:11 · [S] — venting vs holding back the spirit.** "**A fool gives full vent to his spirit, but a wise man quietly holds it back**" (v.11). Finding — a cornerstone: the fool **discharges** his whole spirit; the wise **restrains** it *(stated)*. Operation: **self-restraint as the holding-back of the spirit** — the mastered self does not spill its every impulse; it *quietly holds it back* *(inferred; the self-mastery thread, cross-book w/ 16:32, 25:28, and the Psalter's self-quieting, Ps 62:1, 131:2)*. *Surfaced:* self-restraint / holding-back-the-spirit (★ cornerstone, cross-book w/ Ps 131).

**PRO-29-pride-lowly · 29:23 · [S, multi] — pride brings low; the lowly are lifted.** "**One's pride will bring him low, but he who is lowly in spirit will obtain honour**" (v.23). Finding: pride **lowers**, lowliness **lifts** — the inversion *(stated; pride/humility cornerstone, cross-book w/ Ps 138:6, 18:27)*. *Surfaced:* pride/humility (★ shared cornerstone).

**PRO-29-fear-man · 29:25 · [S, multi] — the fear of man vs trust in the LORD.** "**The fear of man lays a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is safe**" (v.25). Finding — a cornerstone: **fear of man is a *snare*** to the self; trust in the LORD is safety *(stated)*. Operation: **the fear of man as an inner trap, dissolved by trust** — the dread of people *ensnares* the self, and only Godward trust frees it *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 56:11, 118:6 "the LORD is on my side; I will not fear. What can man do to me?")*. *Surfaced:* fear-of-man-vs-trust (★ cornerstone, cross-book w/ Ps 56/118).

**PRO-29-anger · 29:22 · [S] — the wrathful stir strife.** "**A man of wrath stirs up strife, and one given to anger causes much transgression**" (v.22). *Surfaced:* anger (shared thread).

---
**Chapter notes.** **Cornerstones:** self-restraint/holding-back-the-spirit (★ 29:11, w/ Ps 131); fear-of-man-vs-trust (★ 29:25, w/ Ps 56/118). **Shared:** pride/humility (★); the hardened/unteachable self; anger.

---

## Catch-up units (2026-07-04) — loose study-term verses bound to units

**PRO-29-rule-public · Prov 29:2, 4, 14, 16 · [D, multi] — just rule and the people's mood.** "When the **righteous increase, the people rejoice**, but when the **wicked rule, the people groan**" (v.2); "by **justice a king builds up the land**" (v.4); "if a **king faithfully judges the poor, his throne** will be established forever" (v.14); "when the wicked increase, transgression increases, but the **righteous will look upon their downfall**" (v.16). Finding: righteousness in power **makes a people rejoice and a throne endure**; wickedness makes them **groan** *(stated)*. Operation: **the corporate interior rising or sinking with the justice of its rulers** — the king who judges the poor faithfully secures his throne *(inferred; the public mood, w/ 28:12,28)*. *Surfaced:* the people's joy/groaning under just/unjust rule (thread w/ 28:12); faithful judgment of the poor as what establishes.

**PRO-29-snare-song · Prov 29:6, 27 · [S, multi] — the snare and the song; the mutual abomination of the two ways.** "An **evil man is ensnared in his transgression, but a righteous man sings and rejoices**" (v.6); "an **unjust man is an abomination to the righteous, but one whose way is straight is an abomination to the wicked**" (v.27). Finding: the two ways issue in **a snare and a song** — the evil trapped in his own sin, the righteous free enough to *sing* — and each way is **abhorrent to the other** *(stated)*. Operation: **the self ensnared by its own transgression vs the self at liberty to rejoice** — sin is a net that closes on its doer; righteousness opens into song *(inferred; sin as self-snaring, w/ 5:22; the incompatible interiors)*. *Surfaced:* the snare of one's own sin vs the freed song (new gem — w/ 5:22); the mutual abomination of the two ways.

**PRO-29-child-discipline · Prov 29:3, 15, 17, 19 · [D, multi] — the child, the rod, and what mere words cannot do.** "He who **loves wisdom makes his father glad**, but a companion of prostitutes squanders" (v.3); "the **rod and reproof give wisdom**, but a child left to himself shames his mother" (v.15); "**discipline your son, and he will give you rest**… delight to your heart" (v.17); "by **mere words a servant is not disciplined**, for though he understands, he will not respond" (v.19). Finding: **loving wisdom gladdens; discipline gives wisdom and rest**; and some are not moved by words alone *(stated)*. Operation: **formation through loving correction, and the limit of words** — the child left to himself drifts to shame; discipline returns *rest and delight*; but understanding without will does not respond *(inferred; discipline-as-rest, w/ 19:18; the gap between understanding and responding)*. *Surfaced:* discipline yielding rest and delight (new); the will that words alone cannot move.

**PRO-29-poor-justice · Prov 29:7, 26 · [S, multi] — the righteous knowing the poor's cause; justice from the LORD.** "A **righteous man knows the rights of the poor**; a wicked man does not understand such knowledge" (v.7); "**many seek the face of a ruler, but it is from the LORD** that a man gets justice" (v.26). Finding: righteousness includes **knowing the poor's cause** (which the wicked cannot grasp), and true justice comes **from God**, not the ruler's favour *(stated)*. Operation: **the interior attuned to the poor, and the eye that looks past power to God for justice** *(inferred; the poor's cause, w/ 28:5; justice from the LORD)*. *Surfaced:* knowing the poor's rights as righteousness (thread w/ 28:5); justice from God over the ruler's face.

**PRO-29-inflaming-speech · Prov 29:8, 9, 20 · [D, multi] — the inflaming scoffer, the raging fool, the hasty tongue.** "**Scoffers set a city aflame, but the wise turn away wrath**" (v.8); "if a wise man argues with a fool, the **fool only rages and laughs, and there is no quiet**" (v.9); "do you see a man **hasty in his words**? There is **more hope for a fool** than for him" (v.20). Finding: scoffers **inflame**, the wise **defuse**; arguing with a fool yields **no quiet**; and the **hasty tongue** is worse than folly *(stated)*. Operation: **speech that ignites vs speech that cools; the futility of reasoning with rage** — the scoffer is a fire-setter, the fool un-quietable, the hasty-worded beyond hope *(inferred; the peacemaker vs the inflamer, w/ 15:1; hasty speech, w/ Ecc 5:2)*. *Surfaced:* the scoffer as fire-setter / the wise as wrath-turner (new); the futility of arguing with a raging fool; the hasty tongue below folly.

**PRO-29-hatred-complicity · Prov 29:10, 12, 24 · [S, multi] — hatred of the blameless; complicity from the top and bottom.** "**Bloodthirsty men hate one who is blameless** and seek the life of the upright" (v.10); "if a **ruler listens to falsehood, all his officials will be wicked**" (v.12); "the **partner of a thief hates his own life**; he hears the curse but discloses nothing" (v.24). Finding: the violent **hate the blameless**; a ruler's ear for lies **corrupts his whole court**; and the thief's silent partner **hates his own life** *(stated)*. Operation: **corruption spread from the ruler's ear down, and complicity as self-hatred** — heeding falsehood makes wicked officials; the accomplice who will not disclose destroys himself *(inferred; the ruler's ear shaping the court; complicity as self-harm)*. *Surfaced:* the ruler's ear corrupting the court (new); complicity as self-hatred; hatred of the blameless.

**PRO-29-restraint · Prov 29:18 · [S] — vision and the restraint it gives.** "Where there is **no prophetic vision the people cast off restraint**, but blessed is he who **keeps the law**" (v.18). Finding: without revelatory **vision the people run unrestrained**; the law-keeper is blessed *(stated)*. Operation: **restraint as a gift of vision/law** — the interior needs a revealed word to hold it in bounds; without it, it unravels *(inferred; the restraining word, w/ the law-ear thread 28:9)*. *Surfaced:* vision/law as what restrains the self (thread w/ 28:9).

---

## Proverbs 30 - inner-being unit readings

# Proverbs 30 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 30 (Agur), per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**.

---

**PRO-30-humility · 30:1–4 · [D, multi] — the seeker's self-emptying before the unknowable God.** "I am **weary**, O God… **Surely I am too stupid to be a man**. I have **not the understanding of a man**. I have **not learned wisdom**, nor have knowledge of the Holy One… **Who has ascended to heaven?**" (vv.1–4). Finding — a cornerstone: the wisdom-seeker begins in **exhausted self-emptying** — confessing his own stupidity before the God he cannot comprehend *(stated)*. Operation: **intellectual humility as the floor of wisdom** — the truest sage *unknows* himself before God's unsearchable greatness; the confession of ignorance *is* the beginning of insight *(inferred; the deepest form of the fear-of-the-LORD-as-beginning; cross-book w/ Ps 73:22 "I was brutish and ignorant… like a beast toward you", 131:1)*. *Surfaced:* intellectual humility / self-emptying before God (★ cornerstone — the sage's un-knowing).

**PRO-30-middle · 30:7–9 · [D, multi] — the prayer for the middle; self-knowledge of the heart's dangers.** "**Give me neither poverty nor riches**; feed me with the food that is needful, **lest I be full and deny you** and say, 'Who is the LORD?' **or lest I be poor and steal** and profane the name of my God" (vv.8–9). Finding — a cornerstone: the self prays for the *mean* out of a sober **knowledge of its own heart** — knowing that *fullness* tempts to *forget God* and *want* tempts to *steal* *(stated)*. Operation: **self-knowledge as the ground of a prayer for limits** — the inner being, aware that *both excess and lack* imperil its fidelity, asks God to guard it from *its own* likely failures *(inferred; a rare, honest self-diagnosis; cross-book w/ Ps 19:13 "keep back your servant from presumptuous sins", 131:1–2's contentment)*. *Hidden:* **the two opposite dangers to fidelity** (fullness→forgetting, want→theft) — a mapped self-knowledge. *Surfaced:* self-knowledge / the prayer-for-the-middle (★ cornerstone — contentment grounded in self-diagnosis).

**PRO-30-self-clean · 30:12,13 · [S, multi] — clean in one's own eyes.** "There are those who are **clean in their own eyes but are not washed of their filth**… how **lofty are their eyes**" (vv.12–13). *Surfaced:* self-deception + pride (shared w/ 20:9, 16:2).

**PRO-30-insatiable · 30:15,16,20 · [S, multi] — the never-satisfied; the seared conscience.** "The **leech has two daughters: Give and Give**. Three things are **never satisfied**… the adulteress **eats and wipes her mouth and says, 'I have done no wrong'**" (vv.15–16,20). Finding: the **insatiable** appetite (never says "Enough"), and the **seared conscience** that feels no guilt after wrong *(stated)*. Operation: **the unfillable want + the conscience that registers no sin** *(inferred; the insatiable-eye thread of 27:20, and the numbed conscience; cross-book w/ the hardened heart, Ps 36:1–2)*. *Hidden:* **the seared conscience** ("I have done no wrong" — no inner registration of guilt). *Surfaced:* the insatiable (shared w/ 27:20); the seared conscience (★ new — guilt un-registered).

**PRO-30-restraint · 30:32,33 · [S] — checking the self before it spills.** "If you have been **foolish, exalting yourself**… **put your hand on your mouth**. For… **pressing anger produces strife**" (vv.32–33). *Surfaced:* self-restraint (shared w/ 29:11).

---
**Chapter notes.** **Cornerstones:** intellectual humility / self-emptying (★ 30:1–4); the prayer-for-the-middle / self-knowledge (★ 30:7–9). **New:** the seared conscience (30:20). **Shared:** self-deception/pride; the insatiable; self-restraint.

---

## Catch-up units (2026-07-04) — loose study-term verses bound to units

**PRO-30-refuge · Prov 30:5 · [S] — God's word proven, a shield to those who take refuge.** "**Every word of God proves true; he is a shield to those who take refuge in him**" (v.5). Finding: God's word is **tested and true**, and he is a **shield** to the one who **takes refuge** in him *(stated)*. Operation: **the interior that shelters in the tried word of God** — refuge-taking as the trusting movement toward a proven shield *(inferred; take-refuge/shield, cross-book w/ Ps 18:30 which this quotes, Ps 2:12)*. *Surfaced:* taking refuge in the proven word (thread w/ Ps 18:30 — the trust/refuge cluster).

**PRO-30-parent-honour · Prov 30:10, 11, 17 · [D, multi] — the dishonoured parent and the mocking eye.** "Do **not slander a servant** to his master" (v.10); "there are those who **curse their fathers and do not bless their mothers**" (v.11); "the **eye that mocks a father and scorns to obey a mother** will be picked out by the ravens" (v.17). Finding: **contempt for parents** — cursing, refusing blessing, the **mocking eye** — is marked for a dishonourable end *(stated)*. Operation: **the scorn legible in the eye, and the dishonouring interior** — the mocking eye betrays a heart that scorns its origin, and meets a fitting ruin *(inferred; the contemptuous eye, w/ 6:17 haughty eyes; dishonour of parents inverting the honour-thread)*. *Surfaced:* the mocking eye that scorns a parent (new — w/ 6:17); the dishonoured parent (inverting the honour thread).

**PRO-30-wonder · Prov 30:18, 19, 21, 23 · [D, multi] — wonder at the unsearchable, and the destabilising reversals.** "**Three things are too wonderful for me; four I do not understand**: the way of an eagle… a serpent… a ship… and the **way of a man with a virgin**" (vv.18–19); "under three things the earth **trembles**… an **unloved woman when she gets a husband**, and a **maidservant who displaces her mistress**" (vv.21,23). Finding: some things exceed understanding — the mysterious **way of love** among them — and certain **reversals unsettle the world** (the long-unloved suddenly powerful, the servant supplanting the mistress) *(stated)*. Operation: **the interior that owns the limits of its understanding, and reads which reversals destabilise** — wonder ("too wonderful… I do not understand") as an honest posture; the note on reversals that the human order cannot bear *(inferred; owned not-knowing, w/ Job 42:3, Ecc 3:11; the way of a man and a maid as the unsearchable inner mystery of love)*. *Surfaced:* owned wonder at the unsearchable (w/ Job 42:3); the way of love as too-wonderful; the destabilising reversal.

**PRO-30-small-wise · Prov 30:24, 25, 26, 29 · [D, multi] — the wisdom of the small.** "**Four things on earth are small, but they are exceedingly wise**": the **ants**, "a people not strong, yet they **provide their food in summer**"; the **rock badgers**, "not mighty, yet they **make their homes in the cliffs**" (vv.24–26); and "**three things are stately in their tread**" (v.29). Finding: **wisdom is not a function of strength** — the small creatures are "exceedingly wise" in *provision* (the ant's foresight) and *security* (the badger's cliff-home) *(stated)*. Operation: **prudent foresight and shelter-seeking as wisdom available to the weak** — strength is not required; the ant stores against winter, the badger builds beyond reach *(inferred; the ant's foresight, w/ 6:6–8; wisdom in the small, not the mighty)*. *Surfaced:* wisdom-in-the-small (foresight and security without strength, w/ 6:6); provision-in-season / shelter-in-the-cliff as the weak's wisdom.

---

## Malachi 1 - inner-being oracle readings

# Malachi 1 — inner-being oracle readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** Phase-1 lexicals for Mal 1:1–2:9, read per **disputation-oracle** (`segment_unit`, provenance `malachi-oracle-segmentation-v1-20260704`). Prophetic book processed by **oracle-passage, not chapter** — oracles cross chapter lines (Disputation 2 spans 1:6–2:9). Cited; grounded; *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the inner-being **operation** the oracle stages; the covenant dispute is the arena. Malachi's form is the **disputation** — God's claim → the people's objection ("But you say…") → God's answer — so each unit's spine is an **exposed inner posture**.
- *(Mal 1:1 superscription = genre metadata, not a unit — skipped, as Ecc 1:1.)*

---

## MAL-disp1 · Mal 1:2–5 · [D, multi] — God's elective love met by a doubting heart

**The reading.** The book opens on the interior directly: "'**I have loved you**,' says the LORD. **But you say, 'How have you loved us?'**" (v.2). The very first thing exposed is a **heart that cannot feel the love it is told it has received** — God asserts love, the people answer with a question that is really a complaint *(stated)*. God's answer is election: "Is not Esau Jacob's brother? Yet I have **loved Jacob** but **Esau I have hated**" (vv.2–3). The finding is **love asserted against a doubting interior, grounded not in the people's experience but in God's choosing** *(inferred: the disputation form makes the *doubt itself* the datum — "how have you loved us?" is the interior of a people whose circumstances (post-exilic disappointment) have eclipsed their sense of being loved; God does not argue from their feelings but relocates the ground of love to his own election (Jacob/Esau); the inner-being operation is the gap between *being loved* and *feeling loved*, and the reorientation of assurance from experience to God's prior choice)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *loved* (H0157, aheb — the divine love, correctly `characteristic`), *hated* (H8130, sane — "Esau I have hated"), *Great* (H1431 — "great is the LORD"), *wicked* (H7563), *angry* (H2194) carried. The aheb/sane pair (love/hate as election language) is the reading's spine; correctly tagged (covenant-election idiom, not emotional caprice). Sound.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** **The gap between being loved and feeling it** — "I have loved you / How have you loved us?" (v.2): the finding that the interior can be genuinely loved and yet *not perceive it*, its doubt shaped by disappointing circumstances; God's remedy is not proof-by-experience but a summons to rest assurance on his election. A distinct inner-being movement (assurance re-grounded outside the self's feelings).

**Characteristics surfaced:** *the doubting heart that cannot feel the love it is given* (new — the disputation's exposed interior); *love/assurance re-grounded in God's election, not experience* (new); *divine love (aheb)* (shared vocab, here covenantal).

---

## MAL-disp2 · Mal 1:6–2:9 · [D, multi] — honour and fear withheld from God; the corrupted priestly covenant

**The reading.** The longest oracle (crossing the chapter line) stages the priests' interior. God's claim: "**a son honours his father**, and a servant his master. If then I am a father, **where is my honour**? And if I am a master, **where is my fear**? says the LORD… to you, O priests, who **despise my name**. **But you say, 'How have we despised your name?'**" (1:6). The answer: by polluted, blind, lame offerings (1:7–8) — giving God what they would not dare give the governor (1:8). The finding is **reverence — honour and fear — owed to God and withheld**; contempt shown not in words but in the *carelessness of the offering* *(stated)*. Against the priests stands the ideal, the **covenant with Levi**: "my covenant with him was one of **life and peace**… a covenant of **fear**, and he **feared me**. He **stood in awe of my name**. **True instruction was in his mouth**, and no wrong on his lips… and he **turned many from iniquity**" (2:5–6). The operation is **the priestly interior that should embody reverent, truthful covenant-keeping, now hollowed into contempt** *(inferred: the disputation's genius is that the priests do not *know* they despise God — "how have we despised your name?"; contempt has become invisible to them, lodged in routine (the blemished offering that "will do"); the Levi-ideal (2:5–7) names what the interior owes — fear, awe, true instruction, a mouth that guards knowledge — the reverence that has drained out; the finding is reverence *decayed into unconscious contempt*, the most dangerous kind because the self cannot see it (cf. the heart set on evil, Ecc 8:11, but here in the religious professional))*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *honor* (H3519, twice — the honour owed), *fear* (H4172/H3374, morah/yare — "where is my fear", "he feared me"), *despise* (H0959, bazah — the priests despising the name, repeated), *covenant* (H1285, berith — the Levi covenant), *life* (H2416)/*peace* (H7965)/*awe* (H2865, "stood in awe"), *True* (H0571, emeth — "true instruction"), *iniquity* (H5771 — "turned many from iniquity") carried. The honour/fear/despise cluster is the reading's spine; the Levi-covenant terms (berith, life, peace, fear, emeth) carry the ideal; correctly tagged. Sound.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** (1) **Contempt that has become invisible to itself** — "how have we despised your name?" (1:6): the finding that irreverence can be so routinised the self no longer perceives it — the blemished offering feels normal; a distinct and sobering inner-being state (unconscious contempt). (2) **Reverence as the whole priestly interior** — the Levi covenant (2:5–7) defines it as *fear + awe + true instruction + a knowledge-guarding mouth + turning others from iniquity*: reverence is not a feeling but an integrated life; its decay is measured against this fullness. (3) **The measure of contempt: what you would not give the governor** (1:8) — God exposes the interior by comparison; the self reveres in proportion to whom it fears, and giving God the reject shows where he actually ranks.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *reverence (honour + fear) owed and withheld* (new — the oracle's spine; shared cornerstone w/ the fear-of-God thread); *contempt invisible to itself (routinised irreverence)* (new — a sobering gem); *the priestly interior as integrated reverence (the Levi ideal: fear/awe/true instruction)* (new); *the self's true valuation exposed by what it dares offer* (new).

---

## Chapter-level notes (oracle-anchored: disputations 1–2)
- **Method note:** Malachi processed **by oracle-passage, not chapter** — Disputation 2 spans **1:6–2:9** (18 verses across the chapter line), filed here under its anchor chapter (1). This is the prophetic unit (the disputation), rhetorically marked by the recurring "But you say" objection-seam.
- **Validation summary:** substrate strong; *aheb/sane* (election-love, 1:2–3), the honour/fear/despise cluster (1:6), and the Levi-covenant terms (berith/life/peace/emeth, 2:5–7) all cleanly carried. The disputation form makes each unit's finding an *exposed inner posture* (the doubting heart 1:2; the unconsciously-contemptuous priest 1:6).
- **New characteristics:** *the doubting heart that cannot feel God's love*; *assurance re-grounded in election*; *reverence owed and withheld*; *contempt invisible to itself*; *the priestly interior as integrated reverence*; *the self's valuation exposed by its offering*. **Shared:** *fear of God* (cornerstone); *divine love (aheb)*.
- **Threads opened:** the disputation-exposed interior (doubt → contempt → to come: faithlessness, cynicism, withholding, the fearing remnant) — Malachi's whole method is the staging of the people's heart and its answer by God.

---

## Malachi 2 - inner-being oracle readings

# Malachi 2 — inner-being oracle readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** Phase-1 lexicals for Mal 2:10–3:5, read per **disputation-oracle** (provenance `malachi-oracle-segmentation-v1-20260704`). Disputation 4 spans **2:17–3:5** (crosses the chapter line), anchored here. Cited; grounded; *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the inner-being **operation** each disputation stages; the covenant dispute is the arena.

---

## MAL-disp3 · Mal 2:10–16 · [D, multi] — faithlessness vs covenant-faithfulness; guarding one's spirit

**The reading.** The oracle grounds ethics in a shared interior origin: "**Have we not all one Father? Has not one God created us? Why then are we faithless to one another**, profaning the covenant of our fathers?" (v.10). The charge is marital faithlessness (vv.11,14–16): "the LORD was **witness between you and the wife of your youth**, to whom you have been **faithless**, though she is your **companion** and your wife **by covenant**" (v.14). The refrain that carries the finding: "so **guard yourselves in your spirit**, and let none of you be **faithless** to the wife of your youth" (vv.15–16). The finding is **covenant-faithfulness as an inner watch — faithlessness as a betrayal of a witnessed bond** *(stated)*. The operation is **the interior guarding itself against faithlessness** — "guard yourselves in your spirit" (nishmartem be-ruachakem) makes fidelity a *vigilance over one's own spirit*, not merely an external rule *(inferred: the disputation exposes a people faithless in the most intimate covenant (marriage) and infers the same faithlessness runs through their whole relationship with God (v.10, "faithless to one another… profaning the covenant"); the finding is that faithfulness is *one disposition* worked out horizontally and vertically — and its keeping is an inward guard ("guard your spirit"), the self watching its own tendency to betray; the tenderness of "the wife of your youth… your companion" locates the betrayed bond in a shared history the faithless self has discarded)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *faithless* (H0898, bagad — repeated, the oracle's key verb), *covenant* (H1285, berith — the marriage covenant, repeated), *companion* (H2278, chaberet), *witness* (H5749), *guard* (H8104, shamar — "guard yourselves in your spirit"), *spirit* (H7307, ruach — the seat of the guard), *love* (H0157 — "the man who does not love his wife"), *created* (H1254, bara — "one God created us") carried. *bagad* (faithless) + *shamar* + *ruach* (guard your spirit) are the reading's spine; correctly tagged. Sound.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** (1) **Faithfulness as one disposition, vertical and horizontal** — "one Father… faithless to one another… faithless to the wife of your youth" (vv.10,14): the finding that betrayal of God and betrayal of spouse are the *same* inner failure; fidelity is not compartmentalised. (2) **Guarding the spirit** — "guard yourselves in your spirit" (vv.15–16): the finding that faithfulness is kept by an *inward vigilance* over one's own spirit's drift toward betrayal — the self set as watchman over its own ruach (kin to Pro 4:23 "keep your heart"). (3) **The discarded shared history** — "the wife of your *youth*, your *companion*": the betrayed bond is weighted with a shared past the faithless self treats as nothing; faithlessness as the erasure of a history.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *covenant-faithfulness as an inner watch (guard your spirit)* (new — w/ Pro 4:23); *faithlessness (bagad) as one disposition vertical and horizontal* (new); *the discarded shared history of a covenant* (new); *the God-witnessed bond* (new).

---

## MAL-disp4 · Mal 2:17–3:5 · [D, multi] — wearying God with cynicism; the doubted justice; the refiner

**The reading.** The oracle names a posture that *tires* God: "**You have wearied the LORD with your words. But you say, 'How have we wearied him?'** By saying, '**Everyone who does evil is good in the sight of the LORD, and he delights in them**,' or by asking, '**Where is the God of justice?**'" (2:17). The finding is **moral cynicism as what wearies God** — the interior that has decided evil pays and justice is absent *(stated)*. The answer is the coming refiner: "the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come… he is like a **refiner's fire**… he will **purify the sons of Levi and refine them like gold**" (3:1–3); then "I will be a **swift witness against** the sorcerers, adulterers… those who **do not fear me**" (3:5). The operation is **the cynical heart met not by argument but by a coming purification and reckoning** *(inferred: "where is the God of justice?" (2:17) is the interior of a people who have concluded, from the prospering of the wicked, that God is indifferent (the same crisis as Job 21, Ecc 8:14, Ps 73) — and the disputation shows this cynicism *wearies* God (it is not neutral doubt but an accusation that corrodes); the answer is that justice is *coming* (the refiner, the swift witness) — but note it is a *refining* fire that falls first on the sons of Levi (the religious), not only the obvious sinners; the finding is that the cure for cynicism about justice is not a debate but the promise of a purifying God who will himself come, and whose refining begins with the doubters' own house)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *wearied* (H3021, yaga — "you have wearied the LORD"), *justice* (H4941, mishpat — "the God of justice"), *delights* (H2654, chaphets), *seek* (H1245, baqash — "the Lord whom you seek"), *delight* (H2656, chephets — "the messenger in whom you delight"), *purify/refine* (H2891/H2212, taher/tsaraph), *righteousness* (H6666), *witness* (H5707, ed), *fear* (H3372) carried. *yaga* (wearied) + *mishpat* (justice doubted) and *tsaraph/taher* (refine/purify) are the reading's spine; correctly tagged. Sound.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** (1) **Cynicism that wearies God** — "you have wearied the LORD… 'Where is the God of justice?'" (2:17): the finding that moral cynicism is not passive doubt but an *active accusation* that (anthropomorphically) tires God — the corrosive interior that has given up on justice and half-envies the wicked. (2) **Purification beginning with the religious** — the refiner falls first on "the sons of Levi" (3:3): the finding that the answer to cynicism about justice includes the *doubter's own purification* — judgment starts at the house of God, not only on the obvious wicked. The cynical heart wants justice *on others*; God's refining fire comes for the self first.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *moral cynicism that wearies God (the doubted justice)* (new — w/ Job 21, Ecc 8:14, Ps 73); *the refiner who purifies the doubters' own house first* (new — judgment beginning with the religious); *justice as coming, not absent (the swift witness)* (new).

---

## Chapter-level notes (oracle-anchored: disputations 3–4)
- **Validation summary:** substrate strong; *bagad/shamar/ruach* (faithless / guard-your-spirit, 2:14–16) and *yaga/mishpat/tsaraph* (wearied / justice / refine, 2:17–3:3) cleanly carried. Disputation 4 spans **2:17–3:5** across the chapter line, filed under anchor chapter 2.
- **New characteristics:** *covenant-faithfulness as inner watch*; *faithlessness as one disposition*; *the discarded shared history*; *moral cynicism that wearies God*; *the refiner who purifies the doubters first*. **Shared:** *guard your heart/spirit (Pro 4:23)*; *the justice-crisis (Job 21, Ecc 8:14, Ps 73)*.
- **Threads:** the disputation-exposed interior continues — from doubt (1:2) and contempt (1:6) to *faithlessness* (2:14) and *cynicism* (2:17); the justice-crisis links Malachi to the wisdom corpus's central problem, answered here by a *coming refiner* rather than by argument.

---

## Malachi 3 - inner-being oracle readings

# Malachi 3 — inner-being oracle readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** Phase-1 lexicals for Mal 3:6–4:3, read per **disputation-oracle** (provenance `malachi-oracle-segmentation-v1-20260704`). Disputation 6 spans **3:13–4:3** (crosses the chapter line), anchored here. Cited; grounded; *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the inner-being **operation** each disputation stages.

---

## MAL-disp5 · Mal 3:6–12 · [D, multi] — the withholding heart; "return to me"; the test of trust

**The reading.** The oracle turns on a summons and an objection: "**Return to me, and I will return to you**, says the LORD… **But you say, 'How shall we return?'**" (v.7). The concrete form of the un-returned heart is withholding: "**Will man rob God?** Yet you are robbing me… **In your tithes and contributions**" (v.8). Then the astonishing invitation: "Bring the full tithe into the storehouse… and thereby **put me to the test**, says the LORD… if I will not **open the windows of heaven** for you and pour down a blessing" (v.10). The finding is **the withholding, grasping interior invited into a trust that will prove God** *(stated)*. The operation is **return enacted as open-handed trust — the self that stops clutching and, in giving, tests and finds God faithful** *(inferred: "how shall we return?" (v.7) exposes a people who do not even know *how* to come back — repentance has become opaque to them; God answers concretely: return looks like *releasing the withheld* (the tithe), and — uniquely in Scripture — he invites them to *test* him (bachan), promising to open heaven; the finding is that the cure for the grasping heart is an *experiment in generosity*: the self that has been robbing God (holding back) is asked to give and discover God's overflow; trust here is not a feeling but an *act of release* that proves itself; and the withholding is named as *robbery* — the grasping interior is not merely cautious but is taking what is God's)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *Return* (H7725, shuv — twice, "return to me / I will return"), *rob* (H6906, qaba — "rob God", repeated), *test* (H0974, bachan — "put me to the test"), *blessing* (H1293, berakah), *delight* (H2656, chephets — "a land of delight"), *cursed* (H0779) carried. *shuv* (return) + *bachan* (test) + the rob/blessing pair are the reading's spine; correctly tagged. Sound.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** (1) **Repentance gone opaque** — "How shall we return?" (v.7): the finding that a people can drift so far that they no longer *know how* to come back; return itself has to be re-taught (concretely — release the withheld). (2) **Withholding as robbery** — "will man rob God? … in your tithes" (v.8): the finding that the grasping/withholding interior is not neutral prudence but *taking what is God's* — a reframing of stinginess as theft. (3) **Trust as an invited experiment** — "put me to the test… I will open the windows of heaven" (v.10): the unique inner-being move — God invites the doubting, withholding self to *prove him by giving*; trust demonstrated in the act of release, not asked as blind feeling.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *the withholding heart reframed as robbery of God* (new); *return/repentance gone opaque ("how shall we return?")* (new); *trust as an invited experiment in open-handed giving* (new — a gem); *return (shuv) as concrete release* (new).

---

## MAL-disp6 · Mal 3:13–4:3 · [D, multi] — the God-doubting heart vs those who feared the LORD; the book of remembrance

**The reading.** The final disputation stages the sharpest division of interiors. The cynical: "**Your words have been hard against me**… **But you say, 'How have we spoken against you?'** You have said, '**It is vain to serve God. What is the profit** of keeping his charge…? And now we call the **arrogant blessed. Evildoers not only prosper but they put God to the test and they escape**'" (3:13–15). Against them, the reverent remnant: "**Then those who feared the LORD spoke with one another**. The LORD **paid attention and heard** them, and a **book of remembrance was written** before him of those who **feared the LORD and esteemed his name**" (3:16). And the outcome: "they shall be mine… I will **spare them as a man spares his son who serves him**. Then once more you shall **see the distinction between the righteous and the wicked**, between one who serves God and one who does not" (3:17–18); the day burns the arrogant (4:1) but "for you who **fear my name**, the **sun of righteousness shall rise with healing** in its wings" (4:2). The finding is **two interiors under the same delayed justice — the cynic who concludes serving God is vain, and the God-fearer who reveres and is remembered** *(stated)*. The operation is **reverent fear that holds through the appearance of futility, and is remembered by God** *(inferred: the cynical heart draws the "logical" conclusion from the prospering wicked — "it is vain to serve God" (3:14), the exact opposite conclusion Job and Ps 73 wrestle toward; against pure argument, the answer is a *community of the reverent* who "spoke with one another" and "feared the LORD" (3:16) — reverence sustained relationally, and *heard and written down* by God (the book of remembrance); the finding is that the difference between the two interiors is not their circumstances (both watch the wicked prosper) but whether they *hold reverence through the appearance of futility*; and the reward is deeply personal — to be *remembered*, *spared as a son*, and healed ("the sun of righteousness with healing", 4:2); the God-fearing self, which the cynic calls foolish, is the one written in God's book)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *serve* (H5647, abad — "vain to serve God", repeated), *feared* (H3372, yare — "those who feared the LORD", repeated), *attention/heard* (H7181/H8085, qashab/shama — God attending), *remembrance* (H2146, zikkaron — the book), *esteemed* (H2803, chashab — "esteemed his name"), *spare* (H2550, chamal — "spare them as a son"), *righteous/wicked* (H6662/H7563), *arrogant* (H2086, zed), *righteousness* (H6666 — "sun of righteousness") carried. *yare* (feared) + *zikkaron* (book of remembrance) + *abad* (serve, called vain) are the reading's spine; correctly tagged. Sound.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** (1) **"It is vain to serve God" as the cynic's conclusion** — 3:14: the finding that the doubting interior reasons from the wicked's prosperity to the *pointlessness of reverence* — the terminal form of the justice-crisis, the conclusion Job and Ps 73 refuse. (2) **Reverence sustained relationally** — "those who feared the LORD **spoke with one another**" (3:16): the finding that fear-of-God is held not in isolation but in a *company* of the reverent who strengthen one another against the surrounding cynicism. (3) **Being remembered as the reward** — the "book of remembrance" (3:16), "spared as a son" (3:17): the finding that the deepest answer to the God-fearer is not vindication-by-argument but *being remembered and treasured by God* — the reverent self, which the cynic calls foolish, is the one written in God's book and healed (4:2).

**Characteristics surfaced:** *"it is vain to serve God" (the cynic's terminal conclusion)* (new — the justice-crisis's endpoint, refused by Job/Ps 73); *reverence sustained relationally (the fearers spoke together)* (new); *being remembered/treasured as the God-fearer's reward (the book of remembrance)* (new — a gem); *two interiors under the same delayed justice* (new).

---

## Chapter-level notes (oracle-anchored: disputations 5–6)
- **Validation summary:** substrate strong; *shuv/bachan* (return / test, 3:7–10), and decisively *yare/zikkaron/abad* (feared / book of remembrance / serve-called-vain, 3:14–16) cleanly carried. Disputation 6 spans **3:13–4:3** across the chapter line, filed under anchor chapter 3.
- **New characteristics:** *the withholding heart as robbery*; *repentance gone opaque*; *trust as an invited experiment*; *"it is vain to serve God"*; *reverence sustained relationally*; *being remembered as the reward*. **Shared:** *the justice-crisis (Job 21, Ps 73, Ecc 8:14)*; *fear of God*.
- **Threads:** the disputation-exposed interior reaches its climax — the cynical heart ("it is vain to serve God") set against the God-fearing remnant who are *heard and remembered*; Malachi answers the wisdom corpus's justice-crisis not by argument but by the *book of remembrance* and the coming *sun of righteousness*.

---

## Malachi 4 - inner-being oracle readings

# Malachi 4 — inner-being oracle reading (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** Phase-1 lexicals for Mal 4:4–6, read as the book's **epilogue** (provenance `malachi-oracle-segmentation-v1-20260704`). *(4:1–3 belongs to Disputation 6, read under Malachi 3.)* Cited; grounded; *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the inner-being **operation**; the close of the prophetic corpus is the arena.

---

## MAL-epilogue · Mal 4:4–6 · [D, multi] — remember the law; the turning of hearts

**The reading.** The book — and the OT prophetic canon — closes on two interior commands: "**Remember the law of my servant Moses**… that I commanded him at Horeb" (v.4); and the promise of Elijah, who "will **turn the hearts of fathers to their children and the hearts of children to their fathers**, lest I come and strike the land with a decree of utter destruction" (vv.5–6). The finding is **memory and reconciliation as the closing inner-being work** — the self is to *remember* the given law, and hearts are to be *turned* toward one another across the generations *(stated)*. The operation is **the interior re-anchored by remembrance and re-bound by the turning of hearts** *(inferred: after six disputations exposing a people's doubt, contempt, faithlessness, cynicism, and withholding, the remedy offered at the close is not new revelation but *remembrance* — "remember the law" (zakar) — the same tether-to-the-given that Ecclesiastes reached ("remember your Creator", Ecc 12:1); and the final promised work is *relational* — "turn the hearts (leb) of fathers to children and children to fathers" (v.6): the healing of the estranged interior between generations, without which the land falls under a curse; the finding is that the whole prophetic word ends by pointing the interior back to *memory* and *reconciled relationship* — the two movements that gather a scattered, doubting people; and the last word of the OT is a heart-word, leb, "the hearts… turned")*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *Remember* (H2142, zakar — "remember the law"), *hearts* (H3820, leb — twice, "turn the hearts of fathers… children"), *awesome* (H3372-linked, yare — "the great and awesome day"), *rules* (H2706, choq) carried. *zakar* (remember) + *leb* (the hearts turned) are the reading's spine — memory and the reconciled interior; correctly tagged. The prophetic canon closing on *leb* ("the hearts") is a fitting datum. Sound.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** (1) **Remembrance as the gathering remedy** — "remember the law of Moses" (v.4): the finding that after all the exposed failures, the interior is re-anchored not by novelty but by *recalling the given* (zakar) — the same tether as Ecc 12:1 "remember your Creator"; memory as what steadies a doubting people. (2) **The reconciled interior across generations** — "turn the hearts of fathers to children and children to fathers" (v.6): the finding that the final promised work is *relational healing* — estranged hearts (leb) turned back toward one another; the alternative is a cursed land. The OT ends on the turning of hearts.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *remembrance as the gathering remedy (remember the law)* (thread — w/ Ecc 12:1 "remember your Creator"); *the reconciled interior across generations (hearts turned)* (new); *the prophetic canon closing on leb ("the hearts")* (new).

---

## Chapter-level / book-level notes
- **Validation summary:** substrate clean; *zakar* (remember, 4:4) and *leb* (the hearts turned, 4:6) cleanly carried. The epilogue is short; the bulk of chapter 4 (4:1–3, the burning day / sun of righteousness) belongs to Disputation 6 and is read under Malachi 3.
- **Book-level synthesis (Malachi as a whole):** Malachi is a sequence of **six disputations** that successively *stage the people's interior* and answer it — the **doubting heart** that cannot feel God's love (1:2), the **unconsciously contemptuous** priest (1:6), the **faithless** spouse/covenant-breaker (2:14), the **cynic** who wearies God with "where is justice?" (2:17), the **withholding** heart that robs God (3:8), and the **"it is vain to serve God"** conclusion set against the **God-fearing remnant** who are *remembered* (3:14–16). The book's answers are not arguments but **God's own coming** (the refiner, 3:1–3), his **invited test** of trust (3:10), his **book of remembrance** (3:16), and the closing call to **remember** and to **turn hearts** (4:4–6). Its distinctive inner-being form is the **disputation** — the objection-seam ("But you say…") that exposes the interior the whole book is about.
- **Method validation:** processing **by oracle-passage** (not chapter) was correct — three of the six disputations cross chapter lines; the reading rests on whole oracles. The cross-chapter segmentation (`verse_refs`) is now a reusable capability for the prophets.

---

## Hosea 1 - inner-being oracle readings

# Hosea 1 — inner-being oracle readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** Phase-1 lexicals read per **oracle-passage** (`segment_unit`, provenance `hosea-oracle-segmentation-v1-20260704`). Prophetic book processed **by oracle, not chapter**; the reversal oracle spans 1:10–2:1. Cited; grounded; *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the inner-being **operation**; Hosea's marriage metaphor makes the nation's *faithlessness* an interior condition. *(1:1 superscription skipped.)*

---

## HOS-marriage-signs · Hos 1:2–9 · [D, multi] — whoredom as the faithless interior, named in the children

**The reading.** God's first word is an enacted sign: "take to yourself a **wife of whoredom**… for the land commits **great whoredom by forsaking the LORD**" (v.2). The three children are named as verdicts: **Jezreel** (judgment), **No Mercy** ("I will no more have mercy"), **Not My People** ("you are not my people, and I am not your God", vv.4–9). The finding is **unfaithfulness as the nation's inner condition** — "whoredom" names not merely idol-acts but a *heart that forsakes* its covenant-partner *(stated)*. The operation is **the interior betrayal made visible and named** — God dramatises Israel's inner adultery in a marriage and its bitter fruit (a broken relationship, "not my people") *(inferred: "whoredom" (zenunim) is the book's governing image for the divided, faithless interior — a heart given to other loves; the child-names trace the relational consequence of that inner betrayal — mercy withdrawn, belonging severed; the finding is that spiritual unfaithfulness is a *heart-condition* (forsaking) whose fruit is the rupture of the deepest bond)*.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *whoredom / spiritual unfaithfulness as a heart forsaking its covenant-partner* (new — the book's governing interior image); *the relational fruit of inner betrayal (No Mercy / Not My People)* (new).

---

## HOS-reversal · Hos 1:10–2:1 · [D, multi] — rejection reversed by grace

**The reading.** Immediately the verdict is overturned: "in the place where it was said, '**You are not my people**,' it shall be said, '**Children of the living God**'" (1:10); No Mercy becomes "you have received **mercy**," Not My People becomes "you are **my people**" (2:1). The finding is **the severed belonging restored by sheer grace** — the very names of judgment are reversed *(stated)*. The operation is **grace that reaches past the verdict to re-adopt** — the rejected are re-named children of the *living* God *(inferred: the reversal is not earned (nothing changes in Israel between v.9 and v.10) but declared — the finding is a grace that *precedes* repentance, re-establishing the belonging that unfaithfulness forfeited; the interior note is the sheer un-deservedness of restored sonship)*.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *severed belonging restored by unearned grace (Not-My-People → Children of the living God)* (new); *grace preceding repentance* (thread — recurs 11:8, 14:4).

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Method:** processed by oracle; the reversal oracle spans **1:10–2:1**. The marriage metaphor frames the whole book — faithlessness as the interior.
- **Surfaced:** whoredom as the forsaking heart; the fruit of betrayal; grace-reversed belonging. **Threads opened:** unfaithfulness/whoredom (→ chs 2–13); grace-preceding-repentance (→ 11:8, 14:4).

---

## Hosea 2 - inner-being oracle readings

# Hosea 2 — inner-being oracle readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** Phase-1 lexicals per oracle-passage (provenance `hosea-oracle-segmentation-v1-20260704`). Cited; grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being operation.

---

## HOS-the-case · Hos 2:2–13 · [D, multi] — the heart chasing lovers, forgetting the Giver

**The reading.** The LORD's case against the adulterous wife exposes a specific inner error: "she said, '**I will go after my lovers**, who give me my bread and my water… my oil and my drink'" (v.5); "and she **did not know that it was I who gave** her the grain, the wine, and the oil… which they used for Baal" (v.8); "she… **went after her lovers and forgot me**" (v.13). The finding is **desire misattributed — the gifts loved while the Giver is forgotten** *(stated)*. The operation is **the interior that chases the gift back to the wrong source** — Israel credits Baal (the "lovers") for what the LORD gave, so gratitude and love run to the wrong object *(inferred: the sin is not the enjoyment of grain, wine, oil but the *misattribution* — "she did not know that it was I who gave" (v.8); the finding is a precise inner-being fault: the heart traces its blessings to a false source and so gives its love away; God's remedy is severe (hedging her way with thorns, v.6, taking back the gifts, v.9) — a deprivation designed to expose the true Giver, so the wife will say "I will return to my first husband, for it was better for me then" (v.7); the finding is that God will strip the gifts to recover the heart that mistook them)*.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *desire misattributed — loving the gift, forgetting the Giver* (new — a precise inner-being fault); *the hedged way / stripped gifts as God's exposure of the true source* (new).

---

## HOS-allure-betroth · Hos 2:14–23 · [D, multi] — the wooing back; the restored covenant-knowledge

**The reading.** The tone turns from case to courtship: "I will **allure her**, and bring her into the wilderness, and **speak tenderly** to her" (v.14); the Valley of Achor (trouble) becomes "a **door of hope**" (v.15); "you will call me '**My Husband**,' and no longer… '**My Baal**'" (v.16). The climax: "I will **betroth you to me forever**… in **righteousness and in justice, in steadfast love and in mercy… in faithfulness. And you shall know the LORD**" (vv.19–20). The finding is **God re-wooing the unfaithful heart into a covenant defined by his own character, ending in true knowledge of him** *(stated)*. The operation is **love that allures rather than coerces, re-founding the bond on righteousness, justice, chesed, mercy, faithfulness — and issuing in *knowing* God** *(inferred: God's remedy for whoredom is not only judgment (2:2–13) but *seduction* — "allure… speak tenderly" (v.14, dabar al-lev, "speak to the heart"); the finding is that the faithless interior is re-won by tenderness, and the new covenant is not a contract but a marriage grounded in five divine attributes (tsedeq, mishpat, chesed, rachamim, emunah) — the very graces Israel lacked (4:1); and its telos is relational knowledge — "you shall know the LORD" (v.20, yada), the intimate knowing whose absence was the nation's ruin (4:6); the finding is that the whole movement from whoredom to betrothal is God re-teaching a heart to *know* him)*.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *God alluring/wooing the unfaithful heart (speaking to the heart)* (new — love that woos, not coerces); *the covenant grounded in God's character (righteousness/justice/chesed/mercy/faithfulness)* (new — w/ 4:1's missing graces); *knowing the LORD as the telos of restored covenant (yada)* (thread — w/ 6:6, 4:6).

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced:** misattributed desire; the stripped gifts; God's allure; the character-founded covenant; knowing the LORD. **Threads:** whoredom → betrothal; *knowledge of God* (2:20 → 4:6, 6:6); grace-that-woos (→ 11, 14).

---

## Hosea 3 - inner-being oracle readings

# Hosea 3 — inner-being oracle reading (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** Phase-1 lexicals per oracle-passage (provenance `hosea-oracle-segmentation-v1-20260704`). Cited; grounded; *stated* | *inferred*.

---

## HOS-buy-back · Hos 3:1–5 · [D, multi] — redeeming love for the unfaithful

**The reading.** The sign is re-enacted at cost: "**Go again, love a woman who is loved by another man and is an adulteress, even as the LORD loves the children of Israel, though they turn to other gods** and love cakes of raisins" (v.1); "so I **bought her** for fifteen shekels…" (v.2). The finding is **a love that pursues and *purchases back* the unfaithful — love directed precisely at the one who has betrayed it** *(stated)*. The operation is **redeeming love that is not conditional on the beloved's fidelity** — Hosea loves and buys back an adulteress *because* that is how the LORD loves Israel "though they turn to other gods" *(inferred: the "even as" (v.1) makes Hosea's costly, humiliating love a live enactment of God's — love that *precedes and outlasts* the beloved's faithfulness, and pays to reclaim it; the finding is that divine love is not a response to the loveliness or loyalty of its object but a *choice that redeems the unworthy*; the "many days" of disciplined waiting (v.3) images a love that also *restrains* itself, holding the beloved to fidelity without abandoning her; the outcome is a chastened return "in fear to the LORD and to his goodness" (v.5) — awe re-awakened by being redeemed)*.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *redeeming love for the unfaithful (love that pays to reclaim the betrayer)* (new — the enacted heart of God's love, w/ 11:8, 14:4); *love that precedes and outlasts fidelity* (new); *awe re-awakened by being redeemed ("in fear to his goodness")* (new).

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced:** redeeming love; love before fidelity; awe at redemption. Closes the marriage-sign cycle (chs 1–3): whoredom → the case → betrothal → buy-back. The oracles of chs 4–14 apply this to the nation's interior.

---

## Hosea 4 - inner-being oracle readings

# Hosea 4 — inner-being oracle readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** Phase-1 lexicals per oracle-passage (provenance `hosea-oracle-segmentation-v1-20260704`). Cited; grounded; *stated* | *inferred*.

---

## HOS-controversy · Hos 4:1–3 · [D, multi] — the three missing interior graces

**The reading.** The LORD's lawsuit against the land names exactly what is absent: "there is **no faithfulness or steadfast love, and no knowledge of God** in the land" (v.1) — and out of that absence flow swearing, lying, murder, theft, adultery (v.2), so that "the **land mourns**, and all who dwell in it **languish**" (v.3). The finding is **three interior graces — faithfulness (emeth), steadfast love (chesed), and the knowledge of God (da'at elohim) — whose absence unravels the whole moral and even natural order** *(stated)*. The operation is **the collapse of ethics traced to a missing interior** — the crimes of v.2 are symptoms; the disease is the absence of covenant-truth, covenant-love, and knowing God *(inferred: the finding puts the *inner* graces first and the *outer* crimes second — lying and murder are what a land does when it has lost emeth, chesed, and the knowledge of God; and the land itself "mourns and languishes" (v.3), as if creation registers the missing interior; the three graces are precisely the ones the betrothal restores (2:19–20) — so the controversy names the void the covenant will fill)*.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *the three foundational interior graces (faithfulness, chesed, knowledge of God) and the collapse when they are absent* (thread — w/ 2:19–20, 6:6); *ethics as downstream of the interior* (new — the crimes symptomatic of a lost heart).

---

## HOS-priests-knowledge · Hos 4:4–19 · [D, multi] — the lost knowledge of God; the whoring spirit

**The reading.** The oracle centres on a shattering diagnosis: "**My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge**; because you have **rejected knowledge**… you have **forgotten the law** of your God" (v.6). The mechanism of the loss: "**whoredom, wine, and new wine take away the understanding**" (v.11); "a **spirit of whoredom** has led them astray, and they have **left their God** to play the whore" (v.12). "**Ephraim is joined to idols**; leave him alone" (v.17). The finding is **a people ruined not by ignorance of facts but by *rejected* knowledge of God — a knowing deliberately let go, its faculties dulled by indulgence** *(stated)*. The operation is **the interior that has un-learned God — knowledge rejected, understanding drugged, the self bonded to idols** *(inferred: "destroyed for lack of knowledge" (v.6) is not a failure of information but a *rejection* (ma'as) — the priests who should teach have let the knowledge of God lapse, and the people's understanding is *taken away* by whoredom and wine (v.11), appetites that erode the faculty of knowing God; the finding is that the knowledge of God is not merely intellectual but a *held relationship* that can be forsaken and whose loss *destroys*; and "Ephraim is joined to idols" (v.17, chabur) names the settled bond of a heart welded to what is not God — "leave him alone" is the terrible verdict of a self past appeal)*.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *rejected knowledge of God as ruin (not ignorance but forsaking)* (thread — w/ 6:6, 2:20); *understanding dulled by indulgence (whoredom/wine take away the mind)* (new); *the self welded to idols ("joined to idols")* (new — the bonded, un-appealable heart).

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced:** the three graces and their collapse; rejected knowledge of God; indulgence-dulled understanding; the idol-welded self. **Threads:** *knowledge of God* (4:1,6 → 6:6); whoredom (→ chs 5–9).

---

## Hosea 5 - inner-being oracle readings

# Hosea 5 — inner-being oracle reading (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** Phase-1 lexicals per oracle-passage (provenance `hosea-oracle-segmentation-v1-20260704`). Cited; grounded; *stated* | *inferred*.

---

## HOS-withdrawn · Hos 5:1–15 · [D, multi] — the God who withdraws until the heart seeks his face

**The reading.** The oracle names why return is blocked: "their **deeds do not permit them to return** to their God. For the **spirit of whoredom is within them, and they know not the LORD**" (v.4); so "they shall go to **seek the LORD, but they will not find him; he has withdrawn** from them" (v.6). The oracle's hinge: "**I will return again to my place, until they acknowledge their guilt and seek my face, and in their distress earnestly seek me**" (v.15). The finding is **a God who deliberately withdraws — making himself un-findable — until the heart is driven to *earnestly* seek his face** *(stated)*. The operation is **the divine hiding that is itself a summons — absence engineered to provoke a real seeking** *(inferred: two inner-being data sit together — (1) sin as a *disabling* condition ("their deeds do not permit them to return", v.4; the spirit of whoredom *within*): the faithless heart cannot simply turn, it is bound; (2) God's remedy is *withdrawal* (v.15) — he removes himself "until they… seek my face… in their distress earnestly seek me": the finding is that God's felt absence is not abandonment but a *provocation* to genuine seeking (baqash), the affliction that finally turns a heart that comfort could not; this is the same pattern as Lamentations (the hidden face that drives the cry) and answers the *shallow* seeking of the next oracle (6:1–3) — real seeking is what distress produces, not what ease presumes)*.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *the God who withdraws to provoke a real seeking (engineered absence as summons)* (thread — the hidden face, w/ Lam 3, Job 23:8); *sin as a disabling bond ("deeds do not permit them to return")* (new — the heart that cannot simply turn); *distress as what produces earnest seeking* (thread — w/ 6:1–3, the shallow contrast).

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced:** the withdrawing God; the disabled will; distress-driven seeking. **Threads:** the hidden face (w/ Lam/Job); sets up the shallow-vs-true return (6:1–3 vs 14).

---

## Hosea 6 - inner-being oracle readings

# Hosea 6 — inner-being oracle readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** Phase-1 lexicals per oracle-passage (provenance `hosea-oracle-segmentation-v1-20260704`). Cited; grounded; *stated* | *inferred*.

---

## HOS-shallow-return · Hos 6:1–3 · [D] — the shallow, presumptuous return

**The reading.** The people rehearse a repentance that sounds right: "**Come, let us return to the LORD; for he has torn us, that he may heal us**… after two days he will revive us; on the third day he will **raise us up**… let us **press on to know the LORD**" (vv.1–3). The finding is **a return that presumes on easy, automatic restoration** — right words, but a heart that assumes God's healing follows repentance mechanically *(stated)*. The operation is **repentance as presumption — the interior that says the words of return while expecting a quick, guaranteed revival** *(inferred: read against God's answer (6:4, "your love is a morning cloud"), this seeking is exposed as *shallow* — it has the vocabulary of return ("let us know the LORD", the very telos of 2:20) but treats God's healing as a formula ("after two days… on the third day"); the finding is the subtle fault of a repentance that is confident of the outcome but light on the heart — the difference between saying "let us return" and the earnest, distress-driven seeking God actually requires (5:15); it is not hypocrisy exactly but *presumption*, a return that skips the cost)*.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *the shallow/presumptuous return (right words, assumed restoration)* (thread — contrast w/ 5:15's earnest seeking, 14's true return); *repentance that skips the cost* (new).

---

## HOS-morning-cloud · Hos 6:4–11 · [D, multi] — evanescent love; what God desires

**The reading.** God's answer exposes the fault: "**Your love is like a morning cloud, like the dew that goes early away**" (v.4). Then the book's most quoted line: "**I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings**" (v.6). "But like Adam they **transgressed the covenant**; there they dealt **faithlessly** with me" (v.7). The finding is **love that evaporates, set against the two things God actually desires — steadfast love (chesed) and the knowledge of God, not ritual** *(stated)*. The operation is **the interior that offers sacrifice while withholding the durable love and knowing God wants** *(inferred: "your love is a morning cloud" (v.4) diagnoses the people's *chesed* as evanescent — real in the moment, gone by mid-morning (the same fault as the shallow return, 6:1–3); and v.6 states the whole prophetic priority — God desires *chesed* (steadfast, covenant love) and *da'at elohim* (the knowledge of him), not the sacrifices they multiply; the finding is that the interior graces (durable love, knowing God) are what God is after, and ritual cannot substitute for them; "transgressed like Adam" (v.7) roots the faithlessness in the first covenant-breaking — the human bent to betray the bond)*.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *evanescent love (chesed like a morning cloud)* (new — love real but not durable); *what God desires: steadfast love and the knowledge of God over sacrifice* (thread climax — the book's priority, w/ 4:1, 2:20; and Ecc 5:1, Pro 21:3, 1 Sam 15:22); *ritual as no substitute for the interior graces* (new).

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced:** the presumptuous return; evanescent love; chesed-and-knowledge over sacrifice. **Threads:** *chesed / knowledge of God* (6:6 — the book's centre, w/ 2:20, 4:1); shallow-vs-true return.

---

## Hosea 7 - inner-being oracle readings

# Hosea 7 — inner-being oracle reading (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** Phase-1 lexicals per oracle-passage (provenance `hosea-oracle-segmentation-v1-20260704`). Cited; grounded; *stated* | *inferred*.

---

## HOS-not-from-heart · Hos 7:1–16 · [D, multi] — the un-hearted cry; the half-baked, divided self

**The reading.** A cluster of images anatomises a divided interior. Their passions: "with **hearts like an oven** they approach their intrigue; all night their anger smoulders; in the morning it **blazes**" (v.6). Their double-mindedness: "**Ephraim is a cake not turned**" (v.8) — half-baked, burnt one side and raw the other. Their self-oblivion: "**strangers devour his strength, and he knows it not**; gray hairs are sprinkled on him, and he knows it not" (v.9). And the core: "they **do not cry to me from the heart**, but they **wail upon their beds**… **they return, but not upward**" (vv.14,16). The finding is **religion and distress without the heart — a self that wails but does not cry to God from within, half-committed, unaware of its own decay** *(stated)*. The operation is **the divided, un-hearted interior** — passions hot as an oven, faith a cake unturned, grief real but not God-directed, return that goes sideways ("not upward") *(inferred: the string of images all name a *split* interior — the oven-heart (consumed by intrigue and anger), the unturned cake (half-cooked commitment), the return "not upward" (motion without ascent to God); the decisive one is v.14 — "they do not cry to me *from the heart*" (mi-libbam): they wail (over lost grain and wine) but the cry is not *to God from within*; the finding is that the fatal fault is not the absence of religious emotion but its *mis-direction* — grief and heat aplenty, none of it the heart turned Godward; and the self-oblivion (v.9, "he knows it not") compounds it — the divided interior cannot even see its own graying decline)*.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *the un-hearted cry (wailing, but not crying to God from the heart)* (new — mis-directed distress, w/ the shallow return 6:1); *the half-baked/divided self (the cake not turned)* (new — double-mindedness); *self-oblivious decay ("he knows it not")* (new); *return "not upward" (motion without ascent to God)* (new).

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced:** the un-hearted cry; the divided oven-heart / unturned cake; self-oblivious decline; sideways return. **Threads:** the heart mis-directed (w/ 6:1, 5:15); return-that-is-not-return (→ 14's true return).

---

## Hosea 8 - inner-being oracle readings

# Hosea 8 — inner-being oracle reading (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** Phase-1 lexicals per oracle-passage (provenance `hosea-oracle-segmentation-v1-20260704`). Cited; grounded; *stated* | *inferred*.

---

## HOS-sow-wind · Hos 8:1–14 · [D, multi] — self-destroying autonomy; forgetting the Maker

**The reading.** The oracle's proverb frames it: "for they **sow the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind**" (v.7). The autonomy behind it: "they **made kings, but not through me**. They set up princes, but I knew it not. With their silver and gold they **made idols for their own destruction**" (v.4). And the root: "**Israel has forgotten his Maker** and built palaces" (v.14). The finding is **an autonomy that acts without God — self-made kings, self-made gods — recoiling as self-destruction, because the Maker himself is forgotten** *(stated)*. The operation is **the self that constructs its own supports (rulers, idols, fortresses) apart from God and reaps ruin** *(inferred: "sow the wind, reap the whirlwind" (v.7) names the *amplifying recoil* of autonomous action — emptiness sown returns as a storm; and the taproot is v.14, "Israel has forgotten his Maker" — the interior that no longer references its origin builds frantically (palaces, fortified cities) on nothing; the finding is that forgetting the Maker is the source-fault from which self-made religion and politics grow, and that such self-supply is self-defeating; this "forgot his Maker" is the same fullness-forgetting that recurs at 13:6 and echoes Ecclesiastes' "remember your Creator")*.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *self-destroying autonomy (self-made kings and idols recoiling as ruin)* (new — sow-wind/reap-whirlwind); *forgetting the Maker as the source-fault* (thread — w/ 13:6, Ecc 12:1's "remember your Creator" inverted); *frantic self-supply built on nothing* (new).

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced:** autonomous self-supply and its recoil; the forgotten Maker. **Threads:** *forgetting the Maker/Creator* (8:14 → 13:6); idolatry (→ chs 9–13).

---

## Hosea 9 - inner-being oracle readings

# Hosea 9 — inner-being oracle reading (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** Phase-1 lexicals per oracle-passage (provenance `hosea-oracle-segmentation-v1-20260704`). Cited; grounded; *stated* | *inferred*.

---

## HOS-days-punishment · Hos 9:1–17 · [D, multi] — becoming what you love; the days of reckoning

**The reading.** Amid the exile-oracle sits one of Scripture's deepest inner-being laws: "they came to **Baal-peor** and consecrated themselves to the thing of shame, and **became detestable like the thing they loved**" (v.10). Around it, the reckoning: "the **days of punishment have come**" (v.7); "**I will love them no more**" (v.15); and the terrible "**Woe to them when I depart from them!**" (v.12). The finding is **the formation-law — the self becomes like what it loves and worships** — set inside the sorrow of a God whose love is at last withdrawn *(stated)*. The operation is **worship as self-transformation: consecrating oneself to an object *conforms* the self to it** *(inferred: "became detestable like the thing they loved" (v.10) is the same law as Ps 115:8 ("those who make idols become like them") — the finding that *love conforms the lover to the beloved*; devotion is never neutral, it *shapes* the interior into the likeness of its object, so loving a "thing of shame" makes the self shameful; this is the positive betrothal-telos (2:20, "you shall know the LORD") turned dark — as knowing/loving God would form them into his likeness, loving Baal deforms them into its; and the withdrawal ("I will love them no more", "when I depart", vv.12,15) is the gravest note — not new judgment but the felt *absence* of the God whose presence was their life)*.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *the formation-law — becoming like what you love/worship* (thread — w/ Ps 115:8; the study's candidate organising law; the dark mirror of 2:20's "know the LORD"); *worship as self-transformation (devotion conforms the self to its object)* (new); *the withdrawn love / departed God as the gravest loss* (thread — w/ 5:15, Lam).

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced:** the formation-law (becoming what you love); worship as self-conforming; the departed God. **Threads:** *formation-by-love* (9:10 → the organising-law candidate, w/ Ps 115:8, 2:20); the withdrawing God (w/ 5:15).

---

## Hosea 10 - inner-being oracle readings

# Hosea 10 — inner-being oracle reading (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** Phase-1 lexicals per oracle-passage (provenance `hosea-oracle-segmentation-v1-20260704`). Cited; grounded; *stated* | *inferred*.

---

## HOS-false-heart · Hos 10:1–15 · [D, multi] — the false/divided heart; the summons to seek

**The reading.** The oracle diagnoses the interior and prescribes the remedy. Diagnosis: "**their heart is false**; now they must bear their guilt" (v.2, chalaq — divided/smooth); "you have **trusted in your own way** and in the multitude of your warriors" (v.13). The prescription, its gem: "**Sow for yourselves righteousness; reap steadfast love; break up your fallow ground, for it is the time to seek the LORD**, that he may come and rain righteousness upon you" (v.12). The finding is **the divided heart summoned to *break up its fallow ground* and sow righteousness, so as to reap steadfast love** *(stated)*. The operation is **the interior re-cultivated — the hardened, false heart broken open like unplowed ground to seek God in season** *(inferred: "their heart is false" (v.2, leb chalaq — a *divided/slippery* heart) names the same double-mindedness as the unturned cake (7:8); against it, v.12 offers a striking agricultural inner-being image — "break up your fallow ground" (nir lakem nir): the hardened, un-worked heart must be *plowed open* before righteousness can be sown and chesed reaped; the finding is that return is not a moment but a *cultivation* — the self breaking its own hard ground and sowing, "for it is the time to seek the LORD"; and the alternative is named: "you have trusted in your own way" (v.13) — the false heart's self-reliance, which reaps injustice)*.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *the false/divided heart (leb chalaq)* (thread — w/ 7:8 the unturned cake); *breaking up the fallow ground (the hardened heart plowed open to seek God)* (new — a gem; return as cultivation); *sowing righteousness to reap steadfast love* (new — w/ Pro 11:18); *trusting one's own way (the false heart's self-reliance)* (new).

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced:** the false heart; the fallow ground to break; sowing righteousness; self-reliance. **Threads:** the divided heart (w/ 7:8); the summons to seek (w/ 5:15, "time to seek the LORD").

---

## Hosea 11 - inner-being oracle readings

# Hosea 11 — inner-being oracle reading (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** Phase-1 lexicals per oracle-passage (provenance `hosea-oracle-segmentation-v1-20260704`). Cited; grounded; *stated* | *inferred*.

---

## HOS-fathers-heart · Hos 11:1–12 · [D, multi] — the divine parental interior; the recoiling heart of compassion

**The reading.** The oracle opens the *heart of God* as tenderly as anywhere in Scripture. The memory: "**When Israel was a child, I loved him**, and out of Egypt I called my son" (v.1); "it was I who **taught Ephraim to walk**; I took them up by their arms… I led them with **cords of kindness, with the bands of love**… I **bent down to them and fed them**" (vv.3–4). Then the astonishing inner conflict: "**How can I give you up, O Ephraim?**… **My heart recoils within me; my compassion grows warm and tender**. I will not execute my burning anger… **for I am God and not a man**, the Holy One in your midst" (vv.8–9). The finding is **God's own interior — a father's love that taught the child to walk, and a heart that *recoils* from destroying, compassion overruling wrath** *(stated)*. The operation is **the divine heart torn between deserved judgment and unquenchable love, and love prevailing** *(inferred: this is the summit of the book's inner-being disclosure — not the human heart but *God's*; the parental images (teaching to walk, cords of kindness, bending to feed) portray a tenderness the rebellion has not extinguished; and v.8 stages an actual *inner conflict* in God — "my heart recoils (nehpak libbi, is overturned) within me; my compassion (nichumim) grows warm" — the finding is that God's love is not serene detachment but a *felt turmoil* in which compassion wins; and the ground is startling: "for I am God and not a man" (v.9) — God's *refusal* to destroy is precisely what makes him *God* rather than man, inverting the human assumption that mercy is weakness; the finding is that the deepest thing in Hosea's God is a compassion that overrules his own just wrath)*.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *the divine parental heart (taught to walk, cords of kindness)* (new — God's tenderness toward the rebel); *God's inner conflict, compassion overruling wrath ("my heart recoils")* (new — the book's summit; the felt turmoil of divine love); *mercy as what makes God God, not weakness ("I am God and not a man")* (new — inverts the human view of mercy). **Shared:** grace-preceding-repentance (w/ 1:10, 14:4).

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced:** the parental heart of God; compassion overruling wrath; mercy as divine strength. This is the theological/emotional centre of Hosea — the whoredom of Israel answered, at the last, by the recoiling heart of God.

---

## Hosea 12 - inner-being oracle readings

# Hosea 12 — inner-being oracle reading (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** Phase-1 lexicals per oracle-passage (provenance `hosea-oracle-segmentation-v1-20260704`). Cited; grounded; *stated* | *inferred*.

---

## HOS-jacob-return · Hos 12:1–14 · [D, multi] — Jacob's striving; return, hold fast, wait

**The reading.** The oracle reaches back to Jacob as a mirror: "in the womb he took his brother by the heel, and in his manhood he **strove with God**. He strove with the angel and prevailed; he **wept and sought his favour**" (vv.3–4). The word to the present: "**So you, by the help of your God, return, hold fast to love and justice, and wait continually for your God**" (v.6). Against it, the self-deceived merchant: "Ephraim said, 'Ah, but **I am rich; I have found wealth for myself; in all my labours they cannot find in me iniquity or sin**'" (v.8). The finding is **the summons to return and *hold fast* to steadfast love and justice, and to *wait continually* for God — set against a self-satisfied heart that sees no sin in itself** *(stated)*. The operation is **the interior called to a sustained, waiting fidelity (return + hold-fast chesed and justice + wait), against the complacent self that thinks itself innocent** *(inferred: v.6 is a compact rule for the returned interior — three sustained postures: *return* (shuv), *hold fast to chesed and mishpat* (the covenant graces, again), and *wait continually* (qavah tamid) for God — fidelity as a *durable, expectant* orientation, not a moment; and Jacob is the pattern: one who *strove* with God and *wept and sought his favour* (v.4) — struggle and tears that end in seeking, not in self-sufficiency; the counter-figure is the merchant who says "I am rich… they cannot find iniquity in me" (v.8) — the complacent interior blind to its own sin (cf. Rev 3:17), the exact opposite of Jacob's weeping struggle; the finding is that true return is a *sustained holding-fast and waiting*, and its enemy is the self-satisfied heart)*.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *return as sustained holding-fast to chesed and justice + continual waiting* (thread — w/ Lam 3:25's waiting, Mic 6:8's do-justice-love-kindness; the durable returned interior); *Jacob's striving-and-weeping that ends in seeking* (new — struggle resolved in seeking God's favour); *the self-satisfied heart blind to its own sin ("they cannot find iniquity in me")* (new — the complacent interior, w/ Rev 3:17).

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced:** return/hold-fast/wait; Jacob's striving; the complacent self. **Threads:** *hold fast to love and justice* (12:6 — anticipates Micah 6:8); waiting (w/ Lam 3:25).

---
