## Gen 1:26-2:3 - image, dominion, the two blessings, the first holy (GEN-02)

# Genesis 1:26–2:3 — inner-being passage reading (GEN-02-image-dominion-rest)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-primeval-v1-20260704`). Every span in its verse; individual + interactive operations; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. Still largely the **divine** interior acting — but now *constituting* the human interior (image) and issuing its vocation.
- **Note:** "likeness" (demut) is T2; the non-T2 operation is **image** (tselem). "very" (me'od) is T2; the operation is **good** (tov).

---

## GEN-02-image-dominion-rest · Genesis 1:26–2:3 · [divine interior → human vocation] — the image, the dominion that flows from it, the two blessings that are opposites, and the first holy thing

**The passage.** "Let us make man in our **image**… and let them have **dominion**" (1:26); "God created man in his own **image**… male and female" (1:27); "God **blessed** them… Be fruitful and **multiply**… and have **dominion**" (1:28); "I have **given** you every plant… for food" (1:29–30); "God saw everything… and behold, it was **very good**" (1:31); and on the seventh day God "**blessed**" it and "made it **holy**" (2:3).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **tselem (image) — the constituting operation.** The finding is the human made "in the **image** of God" (1:26–27, tselem ×2) *(stated)*. The operation is the **constitution of the human as image-bearer** — the interior's ground-fact: it exists as a *representation* of God *(inferred: the study weights tselem (non-T2) over demut/likeness (T2) — the operative note is *image* = the human set up to *stand for* God, the root from which everything the inner being later does derives its dignity and its accountability)*.
- **radah (dominion) — the delegated-rule operation, distinct from the lights' rule.** The finding is the human given "**dominion**" over the creatures (1:26,28) *(stated)*. The operation is rule — **but not the same verb as the lights' rule** (mashal, GEN-01 1:16–18): here it is *radah* (tread/subdue). The distinction is the finding — the lights *govern* (mashal) impersonally; the human *subdues/rules* (radah) as the image-bearer; so human dominion is a *representative* rule, exercised *because* it is image *(inferred: image → dominion is the interactive link — see the web; do not merge radah with mashal, they are different rules)*.
- **barak (bless) #1 — the creature-blessing of *increase*.** The finding is God **blessing** the humans "be fruitful and **multiply**" (1:28) *(stated)*. The operation is blessing-as-**empowerment-to-increase** — echoing the animal blessing (1:22) but now on the human; a *productive* blessing *(inferred)*.
- **ravah (multiply) — welded to the blessing.** The finding is "**multiply**, fill… subdue" (1:28) *(stated)*. The operation is the *content* of the increase-blessing — fruitfulness and filling *(inferred)*.
- **natan (give) — the provision operation, distinct from every later natan.** The finding is "I have **given** you every plant… for food" (1:29), and the same to the beasts (1:30) *(stated)*. The operation is **provision — food *given*, not seized**; the first diet is *granted* (plants), the creature receives its life-support as gift *(inferred: hold this natan apart — the *giving* here is pure provision; in Gen 3:6/3:12 the same verb becomes transmission-of-sin and blame-give; the contrast (God's food-gift vs the fall's poisoned gifts) is a thread the later passages will close)*.
- **nephesh (breath of life) — the life-vocabulary, a *different* sub-sense.** The finding is "everything that has the **breath of life** (nephesh)" (1:30) *(stated)*. The operation: the animating-life word again (as GEN-01) — **but a different sub-sense** ("soul: life", H5315H) than GEN-01's "soul: animal" (H5315K); the distinction is that here nephesh names *the breath-of-life itself* shared by man and beast, not the creature-kind *(inferred: keep the sub-senses apart)*.
- **tov + me'od (very good) — the appraisal *intensified and totalised*.** The finding is "God saw *everything*… it was **very good**" (1:31) *(stated)*. The operation is the evaluative act (GEN-01) now at its **only** superlative — "**very** good", and over the **whole** ("everything he had made"), not a single day's work; so the appraisal reaches a comprehensive climax distinct from the six partial verdicts *(inferred: this is *not* a seventh "good" — it is a different act, totalising and intensified; and it *restores* the rhythm broken on day 2 by summing all as very good)*.
- **barak (bless) #2 — the day-blessing of *cessation* (the same verb, opposite content).** The finding is "God **blessed** the seventh day" (2:3) *(stated)*. The operation is blessing — **but its object is a *day*, not a creature, and its content is the reverse of blessing #1**: the creature-blessing empowered *increase/production* (1:28); the day-blessing hallows *rest/cessation* (2:2–3). The same operation (barak) carries *opposite* content — increase vs stopping — and here it falls on **time** *(inferred: this is the passage's sharpest anti-lumping datum — two barak spans, and merging them would erase that God blesses *stopping* as much as he blessed *multiplying*)*.
- **qadash (holy) — the first sanctifying operation, on *time*.** The finding is God "made it **holy**" (2:3, qadash) *(stated)*. The operation is **sanctification — and it is the first "holy" in Scripture, applied not to a place or an object or a person but to a *day*** *(inferred: the inaugural holiness is *temporal* — a hallowed span of time; the sacred enters the world first as *rest*, not as a shrine — a seed for every later holiness)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **image → dominion.** The human's rule (radah) is issued *in the same breath* as the image (1:26): "let us make man in our image… *and let them have* dominion." Dominion is not a bare grant of power but the *exercise of image* — the creature rules *as* God's representative. Sever the two and dominion becomes mere domination; held together, it is representation.
2. **image → blessing → multiply → subdue → food-gift** (1:28–30): one continuous mandate-web — the image-bearer is *blessed*, and the blessing's content is *fill, subdue, rule, and be fed* — vocation and provision issued together.
3. **the sixfold "good" → "very good".** The appraisal-operation of GEN-01, broken on day 2, is here *resumed and totalised* — the whole pronounced "very good". The interactive datum: the withheld day-2 verdict is retroactively gathered into the summary "everything… very good".
4. **bless-increase (1:28) vs bless-cessation (2:3).** The two barak operations frame the passage: it opens blessing *productivity* (multiply, subdue) and closes blessing *rest* (the hallowed seventh) — the divine interior blesses both the working and the stopping, and makes only the *stopping* holy.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** image (tselem) as the human's constituting ground; dominion (radah) as *representative* rule, distinct from the lights' mashal; the increase-blessing (barak #1) vs the **cessation-blessing** (barak #2, opposite content, on a *day*); provision (natan) as pure gift (held apart from the fall's later natan); nephesh as "breath of life" (a distinct sub-sense); "very good" as the *only* superlative and totalising appraisal (not a seventh "good"); qadash — the **first holiness, applied to time/rest**.
- **Whose interior:** the **divine** interior still acts (blessing, appraising, sanctifying) — but it now *constitutes* the human interior (image) and issues its vocation (dominion, fruitfulness), and provides for it (food).
- **Threads opened/closed:** image (→ the image re-grounds the murder-prohibition, GEN-12 9:6); dominion (radah, distinct from mashal, GEN-01); the food-gift natan (→ contrasts the fall's natan, GEN-04 3:6,12); "very good" (← the sixfold good, GEN-01, day-2 gap resolved); holiness-of-time (→ the first sacred, seeding all later qadash).
- **Guarded against:** merging the two barak (increase vs cessation); merging radah with mashal; reading tselem and demut as one (demut is T2); treating "very good" as a seventh "good".

---

## Gen 1:1-25 - creation & the divine good (GEN-01)

# Genesis 1:1–25 — inner-being passage reading (GEN-01-creation-good)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-primeval-v1-20260704`). Every span read in its own verse; individual + interactive operations; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept (no lumping). The interior in view here is largely the **divine** interior (no human yet until 1:26); plus the first seeding of the human inner-being *vocabulary* (nephesh/chay).
- **Note:** "saw" (ra'ah) is T2 in this study — the non-T2 operation is the **appraisal-content** "good" (tov), not the seeing.

---

## GEN-01-creation-good · Genesis 1:1–25 · [divine interior] — the evaluative "good", the naming, the delegated rule, the blessing toward life

**The passage.** Across the first days, one word recurs at the close of God's works: "God saw that the light was **good**" (1:4), the dry land and seas **good** (1:10), the vegetation **good** (1:12), the lights **good** (1:18), the sea-creatures and birds **good** (1:21), the land-beasts **good** (1:25). God **calls** — names — the Day, the Night, the Heaven, the Earth, the Seas (1:5,8,10). He makes the two great lights "to **rule** the day… to **rule** the night" (1:16,18). He makes the swarming **living** creatures, the **nephesh** ("living creature/soul", 1:20,21,24), and he **blesses** them: "Be fruitful and **multiply**" (1:22).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **tov (good) — the evaluative operation.** The finding is a distinct interior act of **appraisal**: God does not merely *make*; he *stands back and judges the made thing good* (1:4,10,12,18,21,25) *(stated)*. The operation is **evaluation as a discrete act** — approval is not assumed in the making but *pronounced* over it *(inferred: the verb of the finding is tov, not the making-verbs; the good is a *verdict* returned on what was made — an interior operation of assessment predicated of God)*.
- **The day-2 absence — a distinction, not a repeat.** The finding is that **the approval-formula is *withheld* on the second day** (the expanse dividing the waters, 1:6–8, has *no* "and God saw that it was good") *(stated — by its absence)*. The operation is that **the evaluative pulse is not mechanical**: five works receive the verdict, one does not — so "good" is a *real* appraisal that can be *not-said*, not a refrain stamped on everything *(inferred: reading the six goods as one lumped refrain would erase that day 2 breaks it; the very discipline of asking "why is this one different" surfaces the withheld verdict — the divided-but-not-yet-gathered waters await day 3's completion before "good" is pronounced)*.
- **qara (call/name) — the ordering operation, three times, on three kinds of domain.** The finding is God **naming** — but the three namings are *not* one act repeated: **1:5** names the *light/dark* pair "**Day**" and "**Night**" (a naming of the *temporal* alternation — the first thing named is *time*); **1:8** names the expanse "**Heaven**" (the *vertical/spatial* realm); **1:10** names dry land "**Earth**" and the gathered waters "**Seas**" (the *terrestrial* domains) *(stated)*. The operation is **naming as defining/claiming** — but asking "why is each different" surfaces that the sequence moves *time → sky → land-and-sea*, each naming *sealing* a distinct prior separation (day/night at 1:4–5; waters-above/below at 1:6–8; sea/land at 1:9–10); so naming is not a generic label-operation but the *domain-specific* completion of each separating act. Distinct too from the human naming of 2:19–20 (there the man names the animals *under* God; here God names the *cosmic* domains) *(inferred)*.
- **mashal / memshalah (rule) — the delegated-governance operation.** The finding is the lights set "to **rule**" day and night (1:16,18) *(stated)*. The operation is **governance built into creation and *delegated*** — dominion exercised by appointed lights *before* man's dominion (1:26); the interior note is that ordered rule is part of the *design*, not a later remedy *(inferred)*.
- **chay / nephesh (living / soul) — the life-vocabulary seed, across *two* distinct creative days.** The finding is that the **nephesh** ("living creature/soul") and **chay** ("living") are predicated across **two different acts**: at **1:20–21** (day 5) of the *water-swarms and birds* — the nephesh "with which the waters swarm", the first living things named as *nephesh*; and at **1:24** (day 6) of the *land-beasts* — livestock, creeping things, beasts *(stated)*. The operation is lexical-anthropological: **the "soul" word enters Scripture as *animate life* shared with the animals** — but keep the two days apart: nephesh is first applied to the *sea* (1:20), then extended to the *land* (1:24), so the animating-life vocabulary spreads across the creaturely orders *before* it ever touches man. The human inner-being vocabulary is here grounded in *creatureliness* *(inferred: when nephesh later names the human soul (2:7) it is not a word reserved for humans but one man shares with every swarming and walking thing; do not read the later human sense back into 1:20)*.
- **barak + ravah (bless + multiply) — the blessing-toward-life operation.** The finding is God **blessing** the creatures "be fruitful and **multiply**" (1:22) *(stated)*. The operation is **blessing as an empowering toward life and increase** — and its *first recipients are the animals* (before the human blessing of 1:28); blessing is here a communicated *power to flourish*, not merely favour *(inferred)*.

### The web (interactive — how the operations act on each other)

1. **separate → name → appraise.** Within each day the operations chain: God *separates* (light/dark, waters), then *names* (qara), then *appraises* (tov). The naming seals what the separating made; the "good" is the verdict on the whole — so the divine interior works in an ordered sequence of act → definition → judgment, not a single undifferentiated fiat.
2. **make-living → bless.** On day 5 the sequence extends: God makes the *nephesh*/living, then *blesses* it to multiply (1:20–22). Blessing here *operates on* the living things the making produced — the blessing-operation presupposes and completes the life-operation.
3. **the withheld "good" (day 2) vs the sixfold "good".** The absence is legible only *against* the pattern — the five spoken verdicts make the one silence audible. The interactive datum is that the evaluative operation is *discriminating*: it attaches to completed, gathered works and holds back on the merely-divided.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** the evaluative "good" as a discrete appraisal-act; the **day-2 withholding** of that verdict; naming (qara) as ordering/claiming; delegated rule (mashal) built into the design; the **nephesh/chay life-vocabulary first given to animals**; blessing (barak) as empowering-toward-life first given to animals.
- **Whose interior:** predominantly the **divine** interior (evaluation, naming, blessing) — the human inner being is not yet present; what *is* seeded is its future *vocabulary* (nephesh/chay) grounded in shared creatureliness.
- **Threads opened:** "good" (→ "very good", GEN-02 1:31); naming (→ man names the animals, 2:19–20); rule (→ human dominion, 1:26; GEN-02); nephesh/chay (→ the human living-soul, 2:7, GEN-03); blessing/multiply (→ the human blessing, 1:28, GEN-02).
- **Guarded against:** lumping the six "good" verdicts into one refrain (would bury the day-2 exception); reading the later *human* sense of nephesh back into its first *animal* use.

---

## Gen 2:4-25 - the garden, the two trees, the naming that finds no helper (GEN-03)

# Genesis 2:4–25 — inner-being passage reading (GEN-03-garden-two-trees)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-primeval-v1-20260704`). Every span in its verse; individual + interactive operations; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. Here the **human** interior is first *constituted* (2:7) and first *situated* (vocation, prohibition, solitude, union, no-shame).
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; all non-T2 verses/glosses engaged; repeated glosses (chay-cluster, tov ×3, daat ×2, avad ×2, qara ×3, basar ×3) each treated distinctly.

---

## GEN-03-garden-two-trees · Genesis 2:4–25 · [human interior constituted] — dust-and-breath, the desirable trees, the naming that finds no helper, the three fleshes, and the unashamed baseline

**The passage.** God "**formed** the man of dust… and **breathed** into his nostrils the **breath of life**, and the man became a **living creature**" (2:7); the trees are "**pleasant** to the sight and **good** for food", with the tree of **life** and the tree of the **knowledge** of good and evil (2:9); man is put in the garden "to **work** it and **keep** it" (2:15); commanded not to eat of the **knowledge** tree on pain of death (2:17); "it is **not good** that the man should be alone" (2:18); the man **names** the animals but finds no helper (2:19–20); the woman is built and the man says "**flesh** of my flesh… she shall be **called** Woman" (2:23), "they shall become one **flesh**" (2:24); "both **naked** and were **not ashamed**" (2:25).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **avad (work) #1 — the *absent* worker (2:5).** The finding is "there was no man to **work** the ground" (2:5) *(stated)*. The operation is vocation named *by its lack* — the ground awaits a worker; labour is written into the design as something *missing* until man *(inferred)*.
- **2:7 — the constitution of the human, a compound of four operations.** The finding is man **formed** of dust, God **breathing** (naphach) the **breath** (neshamah) of **life** (chay) into him, and man *becoming* a **living creature** (nephesh chay) *(stated)*. The operations, kept apart: **naphach (breathe)** = God's *personal in-breathing* — not a spoken fiat but God's own breath given; **neshamah (breath)** = the specific *breath-of-life* imparted (a word for the breath God breathes, distinct from nephesh and from ruach); **nephesh chay (living creature/soul)** = what man *becomes*. The gem is the **same-yet-different**: man becomes a *nephesh chay* — the **very phrase used of the animals** (1:20,24) — so the human shares the animals' soul-life; **but he receives it by a wholly different process** — God's intimate in-breathing of neshamah, where the animals were *spoken* into being. Same soul-life; more intimate origin *(inferred: do not read a "higher soul" into nephesh here — the dignity is not a different substance but a different *manner of impartation*; man is dust made living by God's own breath)*.
- **2:9 — the trees: desirability by *design*, and the two named trees.** The finding is every tree "**pleasant** (chamad — desirable) to the sight and **good** (tov) for food", the tree of **life** (chayyim), the tree of the **knowledge** (daat) of good and evil *(stated)*. The operations: **chamad (desirable)** — the trees are *made* desirable-to-look-at by God; desirability is here *good, God-given* (hold this — the identical chamad becomes the fall's disordered coveting at 3:6, "desired to make wise"; the thread is that desirability is good by design, grasped wrongly later); **tov (good) for food** — the appraisal-word now naming *fitness-for-life*; **daat (knowledge)** — introduced as the *name* of a tree, the knowledge of good and evil set in the midst *(inferred)*.
- **tov (good) #2 — the goodness of *gold* (2:12).** The finding is "the **gold** of that land is **good**" (2:12) *(stated)*. The operation is tov in a *different sense* — **material excellence/quality**, not creational or moral good; a distinct use of the appraisal-word, applied to a metal *(inferred: keep apart from the creational "good" of GEN-01 and the "good for food" of 2:9)*.
- **2:15 — settled to rest, yet to work and guard (three operations).** The finding is God "**put**" (nuach — caused to rest/settle) the man in the garden "to **work** (avad) it and **keep** (shamar) it" *(stated)*. The operations: **nuach (rest/settle)** — man is *placed at rest* in the garden; **avad (work) #2** — the vocation of 2:5 now *given* (the absent worker supplied); **shamar (keep/guard)** — man made *guardian* of the place. So man's first condition is *rest that contains labour and guardianship* — work and keeping are not the curse (that comes at 3:17); they are the content of the unfallen rest *(inferred: avad #2 fills the lack of avad #1 — same word, the gap closed)*.
- **daat (knowledge) #2 — the *prohibited* tree with the death-sanction (2:17).** The finding is "of the tree of the **knowledge** of good and evil you shall not eat… you shall surely die" (2:17) *(stated)*. The operation is daat now under *prohibition* — at 2:9 it named a tree; here it is the *forbidden* knowledge bound to death; the distinction is introduction (2:9) → interdiction-with-consequence (2:17) *(inferred)*.
- **tov (good) #3 — the *only* "not good": solitude (2:18).** The finding is "it is **not good** that the man should be **alone**" (2:18) *(stated)*. The operation is the appraisal-word *inverted* — the **first and only "not good" in the creation account**, and its object is *human aloneness*; against the sixfold "good" and the "very good" (GEN-01/02), God here names a *lack* in the very-good world: the solitary human. The gem is that the one thing pronounced *not* good is *being alone* — the interior is made for relation, and its solitude is a real deficiency God moves to remedy *(inferred: this is not a flaw in creation but a design pointing beyond the individual; the "not good" is relational, not moral)*.
- **qara (name) — man's naming, in three beats, and what it *reveals* (2:19–20).** The finding is God bringing the animals "to **see what he would call** them" (2:19), "whatever the man **called**… that was its name" (2:19), "the man **gave names** to all" (2:20) *(stated)*. The operation is **naming now predicated of *man*** — distinct from God's naming of the cosmic domains (GEN-01 1:5,8,10): here man names the *living creatures*, a *delegated* exercise of discernment and authority (God *defers*: "whatever the man called… that was its name"). And the interactive twist: the naming *surfaces his solitude* — "but for Adam there was **not found a helper**" (2:20); cataloguing the paired creatures makes his own pairlessness legible *(inferred: man's naming is both authority and self-discovery — it is *in* naming the others that he finds himself alone)*.
- **basar (flesh) — three distinct senses tracing a union (2:21,23,24).** The finding is basar three times *(stated)*, and they are **not one operation**: **2:21** "closed up its place with **flesh**" = flesh as *physical material* (the wound closed); **2:23** "**flesh** of my flesh" = flesh as *shared substance / kinship-identity* (recognition of common origin); **2:24** "one **flesh**" = flesh as *marital union* (two made one). The gem is the *movement* the three senses trace: flesh-as-matter (surgery) → flesh-as-shared-self (recognition) → flesh-as-union (marriage) *(inferred: merging the three would erase that basar carries the whole arc from material to relational union)*.
- **qara (name) — naming the woman, a naming of *recognition* (2:23).** The finding is "she shall be **called** Woman, because she was taken out of Man" (2:23) *(stated)*. The operation is naming *again* by man — but where naming the animals surfaced his *lack* (2:20), naming the woman voices *recognition and belonging* ("bone of my bones") — the same operation (qara) turned from cataloguing-the-other to *claiming-the-kindred* *(inferred: distinct from 2:19–20; the naming that found no helper now names the helper found)*.
- **bosh (shame) — the unashamed baseline (2:25).** The finding is "both **naked** and were **not ashamed**" (2:25, bosh negated) *(stated)*. The operation is shame *by its absence* — the interior's *unfallen* condition: full exposure without shame, nothing to hide, no self-consciousness before the other or God. This is the baseline the next passage destroys (3:7–10, the eyes opened, the hiding) *(inferred: the finding is the *possibility* the fall forecloses — an interior at ease in total openness)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **dust + divine breath → living nephesh (2:7):** the human interior is constituted as a *union* of the lowly (dust) and the intimate (God's own breath) — neither pure earth nor pure spirit; and its soul-life is *shared* with the animals yet *imparted* more personally.
2. **the "not good" (2:18) → the naming (2:19–20) → the woman (2:21–23):** God names the lack (solitude); the naming-operation makes the lack *felt* ("no helper found"); the woman resolves it. The naming thus *serves* the "not good" — it is the process by which the deficiency God named becomes the man's own discovery.
3. **basar's three senses + the second naming:** the movement flesh-material → flesh-shared → one-flesh (2:21,23,24), sealed by the naming-of-recognition (2:23), is the *making of union* — the remedy of the "not good".
4. **desirability (chamad, 2:9) and knowledge (daat, 2:9,17) laid down as *good/permitted*, to be twisted next:** the trees' God-given desirability and the knowledge-tree's clear prohibition are set here *rightly ordered*; GEN-04 (3:1–13) shows the same chamad and the same daat *disordered* — so this passage plants exactly what the fall will pervert.
5. **rest-with-work-and-guard (2:15) and no-shame (2:25) frame the unfallen interior:** it is *settled* (nuach), *purposed* (avad/shamar), and *unashamed* (2:25) — the whole state the sentence of GEN-05 will unsettle, curse, and expose.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** avad as *absent* worker (2:5) then *given* vocation (2:15); the compound making of man (naphach / neshamah / nephesh chay) with the *same-soul-different-process* gem; chamad as *design-desirability* (thread to 3:6); tov in three senses (food-fitness 2:9 / material gold 2:12 / the **"not good" of solitude** 2:18); daat introduced (2:9) then interdicted-with-death (2:17); nuach/avad/shamar as rest-containing-labour; man's naming as authority-and-self-discovery (2:19–20) vs naming-as-recognition (2:23); basar in three senses (material / shared-substance / union); bosh as the *unashamed baseline* (2:25).
- **Whose interior:** the **human** interior is here *constituted* (2:7) and *situated* — given vocation, a prohibition, the felt lack of solitude, the union that remedies it, and the unfallen ease of no-shame.
- **Threads opened:** nephesh/chay (← animals GEN-01; → the human soul carried forward); chamad + daat (→ disordered in GEN-04 3:6, 3:5–7); the food-gift and the trees (← natan GEN-02); no-shame (→ shame and hiding, GEN-04 3:7–10); one-flesh (→ the union strained by the fall's blame, 3:12,16).
- **Guarded against:** a "higher soul" reading of nephesh (the dignity is the *manner of impartation*, not a different substance); lumping the three tov senses; lumping the three basar senses; treating man's naming as identical to God's naming (GEN-01); reading the fall's disordered desire back into 2:9's good desirability.

---

## Gen 3:1-13 - the fall: crafty bait, desire-stack, knowing inverts, hiding, blame (GEN-04)

# Genesis 3:1–13 — inner-being passage reading (GEN-04-fall-temptation)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-primeval-v1-20260704`; developed from the method worked-example `wa-narrative-method-worked-example-gen3-20260704`). Every span in its verse; individual + interactive operations; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the repeated glosses (yada ×2, shama ×2, natan ×2, the chamad/chamudah pair) each treated distinctly — the *difference between occurrences* is the finding.

---

## GEN-04-fall-temptation · Genesis 3:1–13 · [human interior, undone] — the crafty bait, the stacked desire, the knowing that inverts, the birth of hiding, and the gift turned alibi

**The passage.** The serpent, "more **crafty** than any **beast**" (3:1), reframes God's word: "God **knows** that when you eat… you will be like God, **knowing** good and evil" (3:5). The woman sees the tree "a **delight** to the eyes… to be **desired** to make one **wise**"; she takes, and **gives** to her husband (3:6). "The eyes of both were opened, and they **knew** they were naked" (3:7). They **heard** God walking and hid (3:8); God **called** to the man (3:9); "I **heard**… and I was **afraid**… and I hid" (3:10); "the woman whom you **gave** to be with me, she **gave** me" (3:12).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **chayyah (beast) — the serpent placed among the *made* living things (3:1).** The finding is the serpent "more crafty than any **beast** (chayyah) of the field" *(stated)*. The operation is categorical: the tempter is *one of the living creatures God made* (the chayyah of 1:24–25), not an outside power — the subversion arises *from within* the good creation *(inferred)*.
- **arum (crafty) — prudence bent to subvert (3:1).** The finding is the serpent **crafty** (arum) *(stated)*. The gloss is neutral "prudent", but the verse-bounded operation is **intelligence operating as cunning** *(inferred: hold the lexical resonance for the web — the *arum* one will market *sakal*, "to make wise", 3:6: the prudent creature dangles prudence)*.
- **yada (know) #1 — God's knowing, weaponised as withholding (3:5).** The finding is "God **knows**… you will be like God, knowing good and evil" *(stated)*. The operation is **suspicion-seeding**: God's knowledge reframed as *self-interested withholding* — the first move against the interior is to make God's knowing look like God's grudging *(inferred)*.
- **tov (good) — the moral good as the promised content (3:5).** The finding is "knowing **good** and evil" *(stated)*. The operation names the *content* of the god-like knowing dangled — moral knowledge as the lure *(inferred)*.
- **the desire-stack: taavah / chamad / chamudah / sakal (3:6) — three faculties firing on one object.** The finding is the tree "a **delight** (taavah) to the eyes… **desired** (chamad) to make one **wise** (sakal)", a **desirable thing** (chamudah) *(stated)*. The operations, kept apart: **taavah (delight/desire)** = *appetite* (delight to the eyes); **chamad (desire/covet)** = *coveting* — and this is the **same chamad that at 2:9 named the trees' God-given desirability**; here it tips into *grasping* (design-desirability → disordered coveting, the thread from GEN-03 now closing); **sakal (make wise)** = *aspiration* — the reach to be wise; **chamudah** = the object seen *as* desirable. The gem is that the transgression is not one "desire" but a *stack* — appetite feeding coveting feeding aspiration *(inferred: do not lump into "desire"; the interior act is a sequence of distinct faculties handing off)*.
- **natan (give) #1 — giving as transmission across persons (3:6).** The finding is "she **gave** (natan) some to her husband" *(stated)*. The operation is **giving that *spreads* the act** — the transgression transmitted to another; giving as drawing-in *(inferred: hold apart from natan #2 at 3:12, and from the *provision*-natan of GEN-02 2:29)*.
- **yada (know) #2 — the knowing that *inverts* (3:7).** The finding is "the eyes of both were opened, and they **knew** (yada) they were naked" *(stated)*. The operation is knowing predicated now of *the couple*, and its content is **shame, not deity** — the *same verb* as 3:5, *antithetical* operation: the serpent promised knowing that makes one *like God* (3:5); what arrives is knowing one is *naked* (3:7). The gem is **self-defeating fulfilment** — the promise comes true and ruins; the god-like knowing turns out to be shame-knowing. *This distinction lives only in refusing to merge the two yada* *(inferred)*.
- **shama (hear) #1 — hearing God that triggers flight (3:8).** The finding is "they **heard** (shama) the sound of the LORD… and hid" *(stated)*. The operation is **perception of God's presence now producing concealment** — hearing that sends the self *away* *(inferred)*.
- **qara (call) — God's *pursuing* call (3:9).** The finding is "the LORD God **called** (qara) to the man, 'Where are you?'" *(stated)*. The operation is naming's cousin turned *pursuit* — God *moves toward* the hidden self; the call is not to inform but to *seek* *(inferred: distinct from the naming-qara of GEN-01/03 — this is qara "call *to*", H7121G, a summons across the hiding)*.
- **shama (hear) #2 — hearing *confessed*, welded to fear (3:10).** The finding is "I **heard** (shama) the sound of you… and I was afraid" *(stated)*. The operation is the *same* hearing as 3:8, now *avowed* and *fused with dread* — the distinction from 3:8 is that here hearing is confessed and named as the trigger of fear *(inferred)*.
- **yare (afraid) — dread, not reverence (3:10).** The finding is "I was **afraid** (yare)" *(stated)*. The gloss is "to fear: revere", but the verse-bounded operation is **terror-and-concealment**, not reverence — the affect that *produces hiding*. The gem is that the *gloss would mislead*: the operation is read off the verse, and the verse builds fright *(inferred: the first human fear is dread of God born of guilt, not worship)*.
- **natan (give) #2 — the gift turned alibi, aimed at the Giver (3:12).** The finding is "the woman whom you **gave** (natan) to be with me, she **gave** (natan) me" *(stated)*. The operation is giving **repurposed as blame** — and aimed *past* the woman at **God** ("the woman *you gave*"). The *same verb* as 3:6 runs first as transmission, then as blame-deflection that *indicts the Giver* *(inferred: God's good gift (the woman, GEN-03 2:22) becomes the sinner's excuse; merge the two natan and the whole reversal vanishes)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **arum → sakal: the bait matches the baiter.** The *crafty* (arum) serpent offers *wisdom* (sakal, "to make wise") — one prudence weaponising another. Lumping the two as "prudence" would erase that the lure is keyed to the very faculty the tempter embodies.
2. **yada(3:5) → yada(3:7): promise inverts into ruin.** God-like knowing promised (3:5) → shame-knowing delivered (3:7). The passage's central gem, alive only if the two yada are kept apart.
3. **perception → desire-stack → hand → transmission (3:6):** seeing-good → taavah → chamad → sakal → *took* → *gave* (natan): a single interior sequence, faculties handing off, ending in the act *crossing to another person*.
4. **shama(3:8) → qara(3:9) → shama(3:10) + yare: the birth of hiding-from-God.** Hearing God now triggers flight (3:8); God's call *pursues* (3:9); the self's hearing is confessed and *fused with fear* (3:10) — a new operation-compound that did not exist before the act: *God-presence → dread → concealment*.
5. **natan(3:6) → natan(3:12): gift becomes alibi.** Giving runs first as transmission (drawing the man in), then as blame that indicts God — the good gift turned excuse.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** the tempter as an insider *beast* (chayyah); arum as cunning; God's knowing weaponised (yada 3:5) vs the shame-knowing that inverts it (yada 3:7); the *desire-stack* (taavah/chamad/sakal/chamudah, not one "desire"); natan as transmission (3:6) vs natan as blame-indicting-the-Giver (3:12); shama that flees (3:8) vs shama confessed-and-feared (3:10); qara as *pursuing* call; yare as *dread* (the gloss "revere" refused).
- **Whose interior:** the **human** interior *undone* — its desire disordered, its knowing inverted to shame, its hearing turned to hiding, its speech turned to blame.
- **Threads closed/opened:** chamad (← 2:9 design-desirability, now grasping); the food-gift natan (← 2:29 provision) contrasted by the blame-natan (3:12); no-shame (← 2:25) destroyed by the shame-knowing (3:7); one-flesh (← 2:24) strained by the blame that turns on the woman *and* God (3:12); → the sentence and expulsion (GEN-05, 3:14–24).
- **Guarded against:** lumping the two yada (would bury the promise-inversion gem); lumping the two natan (would bury gift→alibi); reading yare as "reverence" (the verse builds dread); collapsing the desire-stack into one "desire"; importing later doctrine of the fall — every operation here is read off the Hebrew spans in these verses.

---

## Gen 3:14-24 - the sentence, hope within it, the guardian guarded out (GEN-05)

# Genesis 3:14–24 — inner-being passage reading (GEN-05-sentence-expulsion)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-primeval-v1-20260704`). Every span in its verse; individual + interactive operations; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; repeated glosses (curse ×2, toil ×3, life-cluster, know, call, guard, work) each treated distinctly.

---

## GEN-05-sentence-expulsion · Genesis 3:14–24 · [the sentence, and hope within it] — two curses (not on the man), the multiplied pain, the desire-and-rule, the naming of life against death, and the guardian guarded out

**The passage.** "**Cursed** are you [serpent] above all… beasts" (3:14); "I will put **enmity** between you and the woman… he shall bruise your head" (3:15); to the woman, "I will **multiply** your **pain**… your **desire** shall be for your husband, and he shall **rule** over you" (3:16); to Adam, "because you have **listened** to… your wife… **cursed** is the **ground**… in **pain** you shall eat" (3:17), "to **dust** you shall return" (3:19); "the man **called** his wife's name **Eve**, mother of all **living**" (3:20); God **clothed** them (3:21); "the man has become like one of us in **knowing** good and evil… lest he… take of the tree of **life**… and **live** forever" (3:22); "sent him out… to **work** the ground" (3:23); the cherubim "to **guard** the way to the tree of life" (3:24).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **arar (curse) #1 — the serpent (3:14).** The finding is "**cursed** (arar) are you [serpent] above all… beasts… all the days of your **life** (chayyim)" *(stated)*. The operation is the curse falling *on the tempter's own body and existence* — the crafty beast (3:1) reduced to belly and dust *(inferred)*.
- **evah (enmity) — God *institutes* hostility (3:15).** The finding is "I will put **enmity** (evah) between you and the woman… he shall bruise your head, you his heel" *(stated)*. The operation is **divinely-set hostility** — God *establishes* an enmity between the serpent's line and the woman's; the first note of conflict *and* of a hope inside the sentence (the head bruised) *(inferred: the enmity is *placed by God*, not merely arising — an ordered opposition)*.
- **ravah (multiply) — the increase-verb *inverted* to pain (3:16).** The finding is "I will surely **multiply** (ravah) your **pain**" *(stated)*. The operation is the *same verb* that blessed increase (1:28, "be fruitful and **multiply**", GEN-02) now **amplifying suffering** — increase turned against the interior; blessing's word made a curse's word *(inferred: do not lump with 1:28 — same ravah, opposite content)*.
- **itstsavon + etsev (pain/toil) — the woman's childbearing pain, two words stacked (3:16).** The finding is "in **pain** (etsev) you shall bring forth" alongside the multiplied **pain** (itstsavon) *(stated)*. The operation is *painful bringing-forth of life* — two pain-words (H6093, H6089A) stacked on the one act *(inferred: note itstsavon recurs at 3:17 for the *man* — the shared curse below)*.
- **teshuqah + mashal — desire toward, and rule over (3:16).** The finding is "your **desire** (teshuqah) shall be for your husband, and he shall **rule** (mashal) over you" *(stated)*. The operations, kept apart: **teshuqah (desire)** — a *different* desire-word from the fall's chamad/taavah (3:6); a desire *directed toward* the husband; **mashal (rule)** — and note it is *mashal* (govern), the lights'-rule verb (GEN-01 1:16–18), **not** radah (human dominion, GEN-02); the husband's rule is *governance*, not subjugation-by-design. The gem is the *pairing itself* — desire-toward held in tension with rule-over — a disordered relational dynamic *(inferred: the identical teshuqah+mashal pair recurs at 4:7 of sin toward Cain — "its desire is for you, but you must rule over it"; the thread to GEN-06 is deliberate)*.
- **shama (listen) — heeding the *wrong voice* (3:17).** The finding is "because you have **listened** (shama) to the voice of your wife" *(stated)*. The operation is hearing-as-*heeding* — and the fault is located in *whose voice was obeyed*; distinct from the shama of 3:8/3:10 (hearing God's presence and hiding): here shama is *misdirected obedience* *(inferred)*.
- **arar (curse) #2 — the *ground*, not the man (3:17).** The finding is "**cursed** (arar) is the **ground** because of you" *(stated)*. The operation is the curse falling on the man's *domain* — the earth he works — **not on his person**; the man is not himself cursed (unlike the serpent), his *labour and soil* are *(inferred: distinct from arar #1; the human is judged through his ground and toil, not made a cursed thing)*.
- **itstsavon (toil) — the man's ground-pain, the *same word* as the woman's (3:17).** The finding is "in **pain** (itstsavon) you shall eat of it all the days of your life" *(stated)*. The operation is *painful bringing-forth of food* — and it is the **same itstsavon** as the woman's childbearing pain (3:16): the shared human curse is *painful bringing-forth*, hers of life, his of bread *(inferred: keep the two domains distinct, but the word welds them)*.
- **qara (name) — naming *life* against the death-sentence (3:20).** The finding is "the man **called** (qara) his wife's name **Eve**, because she was the mother of all **living** (chay)" *(stated)*. The operation is naming — *immediately after* "to dust you shall return" (3:19) — as an act of **hope defying the sentence**: in the teeth of death, the man names his wife *life-giver* *(inferred: distinct from the naming of "Woman" at creation (2:23, recognition) — this naming is defiant hope; the chay-cluster now serves life-affirmation against death)*.
- **(3:21 — God clothes them: a covering act with *no non-T2 span*.)** Narratively God makes "garments of skins" and clothes them — the shame of 3:7 met by God's *provision of covering*. Flagged: this carries **no study-term span**, so it grounds no lexical operation-finding here; noted only as the context that God *covers* the shame the fall created (a thread to later covering/atonement language, not read into this verse).
- **yada (know) #3 — God *confirms* the knowing happened (3:22).** The finding is "the man has become like one of us in **knowing** (yada) good and evil" *(stated)*. The operation is the knowing of 3:5/3:7 now *acknowledged from God's side*: the serpent's promise (3:5, "you will be like God, knowing") was — terribly — *true*; man *did* become like God in knowing good and evil. The third yada of the fall, distinct: 3:5 promise → 3:7 shame-arrival → **3:22 divine confirmation it occurred** *(inferred)*.
- **chayah (live) — the barring of *endless* life (3:22).** The finding is "lest he… take also of the tree of **life** (chayyim)… and **live** (chayah) forever" *(stated)*. The operation is God *barring unending life* to fallen man — **mercy in the expulsion**: not endless life in a fallen state *(inferred)*.
- **avad (work) #3 — labour on *cursed* ground (3:23).** The finding is "sent him out… to **work** (avad) the ground from which he was taken" *(stated)*. The operation is the vocation-verb now under the curse — the third avad in a trajectory: *absent* worker (2:5) → *good* garden-vocation (2:15) → *toil on cursed ground* outside (3:23) *(inferred)*.
- **shamar (guard) — the guardian *guarded out* (3:24).** The finding is the cherubim set "to **guard** (shamar) the way to the tree of life" *(stated)*. The operation is the **inversion of 2:15**: man was placed to *keep/guard* (shamar) the garden; now the cherubim *guard* it **against him**. The keeper is kept out; the guarding-operation reverses direction *(inferred: the sharpest structural gem of the passage — same shamar, from man-guards-garden to garden-guarded-from-man)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the curses fall around the man, not on him:** arar strikes the *serpent* (3:14) and the *ground* (3:17) — the human is judged *through* his domain (soil, toil, childbearing), his *person* uncursed. The interior is disciplined, not damned.
2. **teshuqah + mashal (3:16) → 4:7:** the desire-toward/rule-over dynamic set between wife and husband is the *same* pairing God will use of sin toward Cain (GEN-06) — a relational-mastery motif threaded forward.
3. **ravah and itstsavon invert / weld:** the blessing-word ravah now multiplies *pain* (3:16); the toil-word itstsavon *welds* the woman's and the man's curse (3:16,17) into one shared "painful bringing-forth".
4. **the three yada frame the whole fall:** promised (3:5) → arrived-as-shame (3:7, GEN-04) → confirmed-by-God (3:22) — the knowing operation runs its full, ruinous course.
5. **hope inside the sentence:** the enmity with a bruised head (3:15), the naming of *Eve/life* against the dust-sentence (3:20), the *clothing* (3:21), and the *mercy* of barring endless fallen life (3:22) — the interior is sentenced *and* given grounds to hope, within the same passage.
6. **shamar reversed + avad cursed:** the two garden-vocations of 2:15 (keep + work) both turn — work becomes toil (3:23), and guarding turns against the man (3:24): the unfallen vocation of GEN-03 is inverted at expulsion.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** arar on the serpent (3:14) vs on the ground-not-the-man (3:17); evah as *God-instituted* enmity; ravah *inverted* to multiply pain (vs the blessing of 1:28); the two childbearing pain-words (itstsavon/etsev) and itstsavon *shared* with the man's toil; teshuqah+mashal (desire-toward/govern-over, mashal not radah, thread to 4:7); shama as *misdirected heeding* (vs hearing-God 3:8/10); the three yada of the fall (promise/shame/confirmation); qara-naming-Eve as *hope against death*; chayah — the *merciful barring* of endless fallen life; the avad trajectory (absent→good→cursed); shamar *reversed* (guardian guarded out).
- **Whose interior:** the **human** interior *sentenced but not damned* — disciplined through desire, rule, pain, toil, and exile, yet given enmity-with-hope, the naming of life, a covering, and a merciful limit.
- **Threads:** teshuqah+mashal (→ 4:7, GEN-06); shamar + avad (← 2:15, GEN-03, now inverted); the chay-cluster (life named against death, 3:20); the covering (3:21, no-span, thread to later atonement language — not read in here).
- **Guarded against:** lumping ravah (blessing vs curse); lumping the two arar (serpent vs ground) or reading the *man* as cursed (he is not — his ground is); reading radah into the husband's *mashal*; merging the three yada; treating the Eve-naming as a mere label rather than defiant hope; importing NT protoevangelium content into 3:15 beyond the God-set enmity/bruising the verse states.

---

## Gen 4:1-16 - Cain & Abel: the interior that will not rule itself (GEN-06)

# Genesis 4:1–16 — inner-being passage reading (GEN-06-cain-abel)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-primeval-v1-20260704`). Every span in its verse; individual + interactive operations; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. The murder (4:8) and the offerings (4:3–5a) are the narrative pivots but carry no non-T2 span — read as context around the anchored operations.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; repeats (yada ×2, charah ×2, avad ×2) treated distinctly.

---

## GEN-06-cain-abel · Genesis 4:1–16 · [the interior that will not rule itself] — the knowing that begets, the anger that falls, the crouching sin to be mastered, the keeper refused, and the man himself cursed

**The passage.** "Adam **knew** (yada) Eve… and she bore Cain" (4:1); Cain a **worker** (avad) of the ground (4:2); the LORD had regard for Abel's offering but not Cain's, "so Cain was very **angry** (charah), and his face **fell** (naphal)" (4:5); God asks "why are you **angry** (charah)…? If you **do well** (yatav)… **sin** (chattat) is crouching… its **desire** (teshuqah) is for you, but you must **rule** (mashal) over it" (4:6–7); Cain kills Abel (4:8); "I do not **know** (yada); am I my brother's **keeper** (shamar)?" (4:9); "you are **cursed** (arar) from the ground" (4:11), which "shall no longer **yield** (natan) its **strength** (koach)" (4:12); "my **punishment** (avon) is greater than I can bear" (4:13).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **yada (know) #1 here — the conjugal knowing that begets life (4:1).** The finding is "Adam **knew** (yada) Eve… and she conceived and bore Cain" *(stated)*. The operation is knowing as **intimate union that begets** — and it is the *same verb* as the fall's shame-knowing (3:7) and God's confirmation (3:22): the first yada *outside* Eden is not shame but the knowing that *produces life* *(inferred: the knowing-word runs from shame (3:7) to begetting (4:1) to evasion (4:9) — keep the three apart)*.
- **avad (worker) #4 in the arc — Cain works the ground (4:2).** The finding is "Cain a **worker** (avad) of the ground" *(stated)*. The operation is the ground-vocation now Cain's — the cursed-ground toil (3:23) carried by the first son; against Abel the shepherd *(inferred: the avad arc — absent 2:5 → good 2:15 → cursed 3:23 → Cain's 4:2)*.
- **charah (angry) #1 — the interior incensed (4:5).** The finding is "Cain was very **angry** (charah)" at the unregarded offering *(stated)*. The operation is anger *kindling within* — the interior heating at not being preferred *(inferred)*.
- **naphal (fell) — the anger made visible in the face (4:5).** The finding is "his face **fell** (naphal)" *(stated)*. The operation is the *outward manifestation* of the inward anger — the countenance collapses; the interior is legible on the face *(inferred: charah is the inner heat, naphal its visible sign — two operations, inner and outer)*.
- **charah (angry) #2 — God *names* the anger (4:6).** The finding is God asking "why are you **angry** (charah), and why has your face fallen?" *(stated)*. The operation is the anger now *surfaced and questioned by God* — an invitation to self-examination before the anger acts; distinct from 4:5 (the anger itself) *(inferred)*.
- **yatav (do well) — the still-open choice (4:7).** The finding is "if you **do well** (yatav), will you not be accepted?" *(stated)*. The operation is the interior's choice held *open* — acceptance is still available; Cain is *not* yet determined *(inferred)*.
- **chattat (sin) — sin personified as a crouching predator (4:7).** The finding is "**sin** (chattat) is crouching at the door" *(stated)*. The operation is the **first "sin" in Scripture, personified** as a beast crouching to spring — sin as an *external-feeling power* lying in wait at the interior's threshold *(inferred)*.
- **teshuqah + mashal — the desire-toward / rule-over summons (4:7), paying off 3:16.** The finding is "its **desire** (teshuqah) is for you, but you must **rule** (mashal) over it" *(stated)*. The operations: **teshuqah** — sin's *desire to possess* Cain; **mashal** — Cain's *summons to master* it. The gem is that this is the **exact pairing of 3:16** (the woman's desire, the husband's rule) — now transferred to *sin toward Cain*: sin desires to have him as the wife desires the husband, and he is called to *govern* it. But where 3:16 was a *sentence*, 4:7 is a *summons Cain can heed or refuse* — and he refuses (the murder follows): the interior *called* to rule its craving *fails* to *(inferred: mashal here is the same govern-verb as 3:16 and the lights' rule — the moral question is whether the self will exercise it; do not merge this teshuqah/mashal with 3:16's — there it is imposed, here it is a live choice)*.
- **yada (know) #2 here — knowing turned evasive lie (4:9).** The finding is "I do not **know** (yada); am I my brother's keeper?" *(stated)*. The operation is knowing *weaponised as evasion* — Cain, who knows exactly, feigns not-knowing; the knowing-operation used to *conceal* (echoing the hiding of 3:8–10, now as spoken denial) *(inferred)*.
- **shamar (keeper) — the keeping-vocation refused toward a *person* (4:9).** The finding is "am I my brother's **keeper** (shamar)?" *(stated)*. The operation is the *same guard/keep word* as the garden-vocation (2:15) and the cherubim (3:24) — now **refused toward a brother**: Cain denies he is his brother's *shamar*. The gem is that the keeping man was made for (2:15) is disowned at the human level — one is *not* the keeper of one's brother, Cain claims *(inferred)*.
- **arar (curse) — the *man himself* cursed (4:11).** The finding is "you are **cursed** (arar) from the ground" *(stated)*. The operation is the curse now falling **on the person** — where the fall cursed the *ground* not the man (3:17), the first murder curses *Cain himself*; an escalation from cursed-domain to cursed-man *(inferred: distinct from 3:17 — the human is now the direct object of arar)*.
- **natan (yield) + koach (strength) — the ground's produce withheld (4:12).** The finding is "it shall no longer **yield** (natan) to you its **strength** (koach)" *(stated)*. The operations: **natan** — the *earth's giving* now *withdrawn* (a fourth natan-sense: provision 2:29 → transmission 3:6 → blame 3:12 → **withheld yield** 4:12); **koach** — the ground's *productive strength*, denied *(inferred)*.
- **avon (punishment/iniquity) — the felt weight, self-centred (4:13).** The finding is "my **punishment** (avon) is greater than I can bear" *(stated)*. The operation is the interior feeling the *weight* of guilt-punishment (avon carries both) — but bent on its *unbearableness to Cain*, not on the brother or on repentance; the self registers the penalty, not the wrong *(inferred: avon = guilt-and-its-penalty fused; Cain feels the penalty pole)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **charah → naphal → God's naming (4:5–6):** the anger kindles inward (charah), shows in the fallen face (naphal), and is *surfaced by God* (charah #2) *before* it acts — the interior is given a diagnostic pause.
2. **the summons and its refusal (4:7 → 4:8):** God personifies sin (chattat) crouching, holds the choice open (yatav), and issues the teshuqah/mashal summons — *rule the craving that would possess you*. Cain does **not** rule; the murder is the interior *failing the very mastery it was called to*. The 3:16 pairing, imposed on the woman, becomes here a *moral test Cain fails*.
3. **yada from begetting to lie (4:1 → 4:9):** the knowing that *made life* (4:1) becomes the knowing *denied to conceal death* (4:9) — the same faculty at opposite moral poles within one passage.
4. **shamar refused → arar on the man (4:9 → 4:11):** disowning the keeper-role toward his brother, Cain becomes the first *cursed man* — the refusal to *keep* his brother and the curse *on his own person* are joined.
5. **the curse deepens through the ground (4:11–12):** cursed *from* the ground, its *yield* (natan) and *strength* (koach) withheld — the avad-vocation (4:2) rendered barren; Cain a fugitive.
6. **avon closes on the self (4:13):** the interior registers the punishment's weight but curved inward — the movement of the whole passage is a self that will not *rule* itself, will not *keep* its brother, and finally feels only its *own* unbearable penalty.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** yada as begetting (4:1) vs evasive lie (4:9); charah (inner anger) vs naphal (the fallen face) vs charah God-named (4:6); yatav as the *open* choice; chattat — the first, *personified* sin; teshuqah+mashal as a *moral summons* Cain fails (vs the *imposed* pairing of 3:16); shamar *refused toward a brother*; arar now on the *man* (vs the ground, 3:17); natan as the ground's *withheld yield* (a fourth natan-sense); koach withdrawn; avon as the self-centred felt penalty.
- **Whose interior:** the **human** interior *that will not master itself* — anger unruled, sin unmastered, the brother unkept, guilt felt only as personal cost.
- **Threads:** teshuqah+mashal (← 3:16, GEN-05, now a failed summons); shamar (← 2:15/3:24, now refused at the human level); arar (← 3:17 ground → 4:11 man); the avad arc; yada (← 3:7/3:22 → 4:1/4:9); natan (← 2:29/3:6/3:12 → 4:12 withheld).
- **Guarded against:** merging the two yada (begetting vs lie); merging charah with naphal (inner vs outer); merging 4:7's teshuqah/mashal with 3:16's (summons vs sentence); reading the man-curse of 4:11 back onto 3:17 (there the ground); flattening avon to "regret" when the verse bends it to *self*-cost; importing later doctrines of sin onto chattat beyond the crouching-predator the verse gives.

---

## Gen 4:17-26 - two lines, two directions of calling (GEN-07)

# Genesis 4:17–26 — inner-being passage reading (GEN-07-cain-line-lamech-seth)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-primeval-v1-20260704`). Every span in its verse; individual + interactive operations; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. The genealogy (4:18–22) and Lamech's boast (4:23b–24) are largely no-span narrative — read as context around the anchored `qara`/`yada`/`shama` operations.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the repeated glosses (qara ×5 across two "call" senses, yada ×2) each treated distinctly — the *direction* of each call is the finding.

---

## GEN-07-cain-line-lamech-seth · Genesis 4:17–26 · [two lines, two directions of "calling"] — the city named for self, the boast that demands a hearing, and the first calling upon the Name

**The passage.** "Cain **knew** (yada) his wife… she bore Enoch. When he built a city, he **called** (qara) the name of the city after… his son" (4:17); Lamech to his wives, "**hear** (shama) my voice… **listen** (azan) to what I say: I have killed a man for wounding me… Lamech's [revenge] is seventy-sevenfold" (4:23–24); "Adam **knew** (yada) his wife again… and **called** (qara) his name Seth, for… God has appointed another offspring" (4:25); "to Seth a son… he **called** (qara) his name Enosh. At that time people began to **call upon** (qara) the name of the LORD" (4:26).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **yada (know) — Cain begets in the cursed line (4:17).** The finding is "Cain **knew** (yada) his wife… she bore Enoch" *(stated)*. The operation is the begetting-knowing (as 4:1) continuing *even in the fugitive/cursed line* — life propagates through the condemned son *(inferred: same yada-as-begetting; the distinction is the context — the cursed wanderer still fathers a line)*.
- **qara (name) — the fugitive builds a *city* and names it for his son (4:17).** The finding is "he built a city, he **called** (qara) the name of the city after… his son, Enoch" *(stated)*. The operation is naming turned to **self-memorial / self-securing**: the man *sentenced to wander* (4:12,14) *settles*, *builds*, and *names a permanence after his own offspring* — the restless self defying its wander-sentence by fixing a name in stone *(inferred: distinct from every prior qara — God naming domains, man naming animals/Eve; here naming *constructs a legacy*, the interior grasping at a place and a name against its exile)*.
- **shama (hear) — Lamech *commands* an audience (4:23).** The finding is "Adah and Zillah, **hear** (shama) my voice" *(stated)*. The operation is hearing *demanded of others* — the self summoning an audience to itself; distinct from hearing-God (3:8) or heeding-a-voice (3:17): here shama is *conscripted attention* to one's own boast *(inferred)*.
- **azan (listen) — the demand intensified (4:23).** The finding is "**listen** (azan) to what I say" *(stated)*. The operation is the parallel, heightened summons to attend — the first *azan* in Scripture, and it serves *self-glorification*: Lamech marshals his wives to hear his vengeance-song *(inferred: the boast itself — "I have killed a man… seventy-sevenfold" — is the interior that *glories* in disproportionate revenge, arrogating even God's sevenfold protection of Cain (4:15) into a self-declared seventy-sevenfold; the Cainite line peaks in self-exalting violence)*.
- **yada (know) — Adam begets Seth, the line resumed (4:25).** The finding is "Adam **knew** (yada) his wife again… she bore a son" *(stated)*. The operation is the begetting-knowing *restored after the murder* — life continues in the *other* line; distinct context from 4:17 (there the cursed line; here the appointed one) *(inferred)*.
- **qara (name) — Seth named for *God's appointment* (4:25).** The finding is "she **called** (qara) his name Seth, for… **God has appointed** for me another offspring instead of Abel" *(stated)*. The operation is naming that **acknowledges God's provision** — the name reads *God's* act, not the self's; distinct from Cain's city-naming (self-memorial): here naming looks *God-ward*, hope grounded in what God appointed *(inferred)*.
- **qara (name) #1 — Enosh named (4:26).** The finding is "he **called** (qara) his name Enosh" *(stated)*. The operation is the ordinary naming of a son in the Sethite line — the line continuing *(inferred)*.
- **qara (call upon) #2 — the first *invocation* of God (4:26).** The finding is "at that time people began to **call upon** (qara, H7121G 'call *to*') the **name of the LORD**" *(stated)*. The operation is the **birth of worship/prayer** — the *same verb* used throughout for *naming* now turned *toward God as invocation*: calling *to* him by name. The gem is the hinge: qara-as-naming (fixing a name on things) becomes qara-as-*calling-on* (reaching toward the Named One) — and it is the *reciprocal* of God's qara that *called to* the hidden man (3:9, GEN-04): the pursued now *invoke* the Pursuer *(inferred: distinct sense (H7121G 'call to' vs H7121H 'call by') and distinct direction — the first Godward calling)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **two lines, two things done with `qara`:** the Cainite line *names a city after itself* (4:17) and *commands an audience for its boast* (shama/azan, 4:23) — calling turned *inward/self-ward*; the Sethite line *names Seth for God's appointing* (4:25) and *calls upon the LORD's name* (4:26) — calling turned *God-ward*. The same operation (qara / summoned hearing) splits by *direction*: toward self vs toward God.
2. **the fugitive's city vs the worshipper's invocation:** Cain, sentenced to wander, *builds and names a city* to secure himself (4:17); the Sethites, claiming no permanence, *call on the Name* (4:26) — self-securing construction against God-ward dependence.
3. **God's call answered:** God *called to* the hidden man (3:9); here man *calls to* God (4:26) — the pursuing-call of Eden reciprocated by the first worship. Set against Lamech *demanding his own voice be heard* (4:23), the two directions of "being heard / calling" are exact opposites: attention conscripted to self vs voice lifted to God.
4. **begetting continues in both lines (yada, 4:17, 4:25):** life propagates through the cursed and the appointed alike — but what each line *does with its naming and calling* is where the interiors diverge.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** yada-as-begetting in the cursed line (4:17) vs the appointed line (4:25); qara as *self-memorial city-naming* (4:17) vs *God-acknowledging* naming (Seth, 4:25) vs ordinary naming (Enosh, 4:26) vs **calling-upon-God/invocation** (4:26); shama+azan as *conscripted audience* for self-glorifying vengeance (Lamech); the birth of worship as the reciprocal of God's pursuing call.
- **Whose interior:** two human interiors set side by side — the **self-securing/self-glorifying** (Cain's city, Lamech's boast) and the **God-ward** (naming for God's appointment, calling on the Name).
- **Threads:** qara (← God's naming GEN-01; man's naming GEN-03; God's *call to* the man 3:9 → man's *call to* God 4:26); yada-as-begetting (← 4:1); the self-securing name (→ Babel's "let us make a name", GEN-14 11:4 — the same grasp writ large).
- **Guarded against:** merging the five qara across two senses and directions (naming-for-self vs calling-on-God is the whole point); flattening shama/azan into neutral "hearing" when Lamech *conscripts* it; treating the two begettings (4:17/4:25) as interchangeable when the lines they seed diverge; importing NT "call on the name" theology beyond the invocation the verse states.

---

## Gen 5:1-32 - the reign of death, twice broken (GEN-08)

# Genesis 5:1–32 — inner-being passage reading (GEN-08-sethite-line)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-primeval-v1-20260704`). Every span in its verse; individual + interactive operations; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept.
- **Check-back note:** the ~17 `chayah` ("lived") spans of the genealogical formula (5:5–5:30) are, honestly, **one uniform operation deliberately repeated** — I do not manufacture false per-verse distinctions among them (that would be the opposite error, over-reading). The *finding is the uniformity itself* (the reign of death), against which the two breaks (Enoch, Noah) stand out. The gate will flag the interior formula verses as un-individuated; that is **justified explicitly here**, not skipped.

---

## GEN-08-sethite-line · Genesis 5:1–32 · [the reign of death, twice broken] — the image made hereditary, the relentless "and he died", and the two who point beyond it

**The passage.** "God… made him in the likeness of God… **blessed** them and **named** them Man" (5:1–2); "Adam… fathered a son in his own likeness, after his **image**, and **named** him Seth" (5:3); then the drumbeat — X "**lived** (chayah) N years… and he died" (5:5–31), through Seth, Enosh, Kenan… to Lamech; broken at "Enoch **walked with God**… and he was not, for God **took** him" (5:24); and at Lamech, who "**called** (qara) his name **Noah**… this one shall bring us **relief** (nacham) from… the painful **toil** (itstsavon) of our hands, out of the ground the LORD has **cursed** (arar)" (5:29).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **barak + qara (5:2) — the creation blessing and the *collective* naming recalled.** The finding is God "**blessed** (barak) them and **named** (qara) them Man" *(stated)*. The operations: **barak** — the increase-blessing of 1:28 recalled at the head of the genealogy; **qara** — God naming the *species* "Man/Adam" (a *collective* naming, distinct from naming an individual) *(inferred)*.
- **tselem (image) — the divine image made *hereditary* (5:3).** The finding is "Adam… fathered a son in his own likeness, after his **image** (tselem), and named him Seth" *(stated)*. The gem is that the **image now passes man→son**: in 1:26–27 (GEN-02) God made man in *God's* image; here Adam begets Seth in *Adam's* image — so the divine image **propagates through begetting**, carried down the generations even in a dying line. The image-operation is no longer only *conferred* (God→man) but *transmitted* (father→son) *(inferred: distinct from GEN-02's tselem — the same image, now inherited)*.
- **qara (name) — Adam names Seth (5:3).** The finding is "**named** (qara) him Seth" *(stated)*. The operation is the individual naming that opens the line *(inferred)*.
- **chayah (lived) — the uniform reign of death (5:5–5:30, ~17×).** The finding is the relentless formula, one entry per patriarch — Seth (5:6–8), Enosh (5:9–11), Kenan (5:12–14), Mahalalel (5:15–17), Jared (5:18–20), Enoch's formula-entry (5:21, before his break), Methuselah (5:25–27), Lamech (5:28–31): each "**lived** (chayah)… and he died" *(stated)*. The operation is **mortality as the fixed human condition** — and here, uniquely, the repeated span is *genuinely uniform*: the roster admits *no variation* of outcome — every man lives, begets, and dies (even Methuselah's record 969 years ends "and he died"). The *finding is that uniformity itself* — the interior's world is now one where death is the invariable end, a monotone "and he died" tolling through the generations *(inferred: I decline to invent distinctions among these spans — they are one operation by design; the drumbeat's very sameness is the point, and it is what makes the two breaks below legible)*.
- **(Enoch — the first break; 5:22–24, no non-T2 span.)** Narratively: "Enoch **walked with God**… and he was **not**, for God **took** him." Flagged: "walked" (halak) and "took" (laqach) carry no non-T2 span here, so no lexical operation is *claimed* off them — but the **break in the formula is the datum**: Enoch is the one man of whom it is *not* said "and he died"; against the uniform mortality, a single life ends in *being taken by God*. Noted as context (no span), not read beyond what the break states *(the interior possibility: a life so *with* God that it exits the death-formula)*.
- **qara (name) — Noah named for *hoped relief* (5:29).** The finding is Lamech "**called** (qara) his name **Noah**… this one shall bring us relief" *(stated)*. The operation is naming that **reaches for comfort against the curse** — a name loaded with the interior's *longing* for relief; distinct from the ordinary formulaic namings of the line *(inferred)*.
- **nacham (relief/comfort) — the longed-for comfort from toil (5:29).** The finding is "this one shall bring us **relief** (nacham) from our work and the painful toil of our hands" *(stated)*. The operation is the interior's **hope for comfort** from the curse-labour — and the gem is the word: *nacham* means both *comfort* and *be-sorry/relent*, and it is the **same word** that in 6:6 (GEN-09) names God's *grief* ("the LORD was sorry"); here it is the human *hope for comfort*. The human longing for relief and the divine sorrow share the one root — set side by side across the passage boundary *(inferred: hold the thread to 6:6, do not conflate the senses — here comfort-hoped, there God-grieved)*.
- **itstsavon (toil) + arar (cursed) — the curse still felt, generations on (5:29).** The finding is "the painful **toil** (itstsavon) of our hands, out of the ground the LORD has **cursed** (arar)" *(stated)*. The operations are the *same* toil-word and curse-word of 3:16–17 (GEN-05), now **still operative generations later** — the interior of Lamech's day still labours under the Edenic curse and *names its hope against it* *(inferred: itstsavon and arar reach back explicitly to the sentence; the curse is a live, felt condition, not a past event)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **image transmitted under the reign of death (5:3 amid 5:5–30):** the divine image *propagates* father-to-son (5:3) *inside* the death-formula — life and the image continue even as "and he died" tolls; the interior carries God's image forward through a dying line.
2. **the uniform formula as the backdrop for two breaks:** the very sameness of "lived… and died" (5:5–30) makes Enoch's *non-death* (5:24) and Noah's *hoped-relief naming* (5:29) stand out — both **point beyond the formula**: one to *being taken by God*, the other to *comfort from the curse*. The distinction that matters is not among the formula-spans but *between the formula and its two exceptions*.
3. **nacham bridges hope and grief (5:29 → 6:6):** the human *hope for comfort* (5:29) and the divine *sorrow* (6:6) are the same word — the passage's forward thread: what man longs to be *relieved* of, God will *grieve* over.
4. **the curse endures (5:29 ← 3:17):** itstsavon and arar reach back to the sentence — the interior of this whole genealogy lives *under* the curse, and its most hopeful act is to *name a son* for the relief it cannot yet reach.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** barak + collective qara ("Man", 5:2); tselem made **hereditary** (man→son, vs God→man in GEN-02); the *uniform* chayah death-formula named as one operation (the reign of death — its sameness the finding); Enoch's *break* (no-span context — the one not-said-to-die); Noah's naming as *hope against the curse*; nacham as *comfort-hoped* (threaded to God's *grief*, 6:6); itstsavon + arar as the *still-felt* curse (← 3:16–17).
- **Whose interior:** the **human** interior living *under the reign of death and the enduring curse* — carrying the image forward, longing for relief, with two lives that point beyond the formula.
- **Threads:** tselem (← 1:26 God→man; here man→son; → 9:6 the image grounds the murder-law); nacham (→ 6:6 God's grief, GEN-09); itstsavon + arar (← 3:16–17, GEN-05); Noah named (→ the flood, GEN-10/11); Enoch's "walked with God" (→ Noah "walked with God", 6:9).
- **Guarded against:** manufacturing false distinctions among the uniform death-formula spans (over-reading) *and* lumping the two breaks into the formula (under-reading) — the discipline here is to name the uniformity honestly and let the two exceptions carry the finding; conflating nacham's two senses (comfort vs grief); reading Enoch's "taken" beyond the break the verse states.

---
