## Gen 14:1-24 - the corrected interior; the oath that refuses gain (ABR-04)

# Genesis 14:1–24 — inner-being passage reading (ABR-04-melchizedek-refuse-spoil)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-abraham-v1-20260704`). Every span in its verse; individual + interactive operations; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. The war-report (14:1–11) is largely political; the inner-being centre is Abram's rescue, the priest's blessing, and the refusal of gain.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the two `barak` (14:19, 14:20) and three `natan` (14:20, 14:20, 14:21) treated distinctly.

---

## ABR-04-melchizedek-refuse-spoil · Genesis 14:1–24 · [the corrected interior] — the rescue of the one who left, the priest's double blessing, and the oath that refuses to owe its wealth to a man

**The passage.** Kings "**served** (avad)… **rebelled** (marad)" and "**joined** (arakh) battle" (14:4,8); Abram's "**allies** (baalei berit)" (14:13); "when Abram **heard** (shama) that his kinsman was taken captive" he pursued and rescued (14:14); the king of Sodom went to **meet** (qara) him (14:17); Melchizedek "**blessed** (barak) him: Blessed be Abram… and **blessed** (barak) be God Most High, who has **delivered** (natan) your **enemies** (tsar) into your hand," and Abram "**gave** (natan) a tenth" (14:19–20); "**Give** (natan) me the **persons** (nephesh), but take the goods" (14:21); "I have **lifted** (rum) my hand to the LORD… I would not take a thread… lest you say, 'I have made Abram **rich** (ashar)'" (14:22–23).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **avad (served) + marad (rebelled) — servitude and revolt, at the national level (14:4).** The finding is "twelve years they **served** (avad) Chedorlaomer, and in the thirteenth they **rebelled** (marad)" *(stated)*. The operations are *subjection* (avad) and *revolt* (marad) — the political interior of vassal peoples; limited inner-being weight, noted as the war's occasion (avad here = servitude, a distinct sense from the garden-vocation avad) *(inferred: near-context; the interior of subjection/rebellion at the collective level)*.
- **arakh (joined battle) — the array (14:8).** The finding is the kings "**joined** (arakh) battle" *(stated)*. The operation is *setting in array* — a military ordering; near-null inner-being weight, noted for coverage *(honest near-null)*.
- **berit (allies) — a *human* alliance (14:13).** The finding is Abram's "**allies** (baalei berit — lords of covenant)" *(stated)*. The operation is berit as a *human confederacy* — distinct from God's covenant (6:18; 9:9); here men *bound to Abram* by pact *(inferred)*.
- **shama (heard) — hearing that moves to *rescue* (14:14).** The finding is "when Abram **heard** (shama) that his kinsman had been taken captive, he led out his trained men" *(stated)*. The gem is *shama that acts*: Abram *hears* Lot is captive and *rescues him* — **despite** Lot's grasping departure (ABR-03); loyalty and generosity persist toward the one who left him. Distinct from the primeval shama-senses — here hearing *moves the interior to costly rescue* *(inferred)*.
- **qara (meet/encounter) — the kings come out to him (14:17).** The finding is "the king of Sodom went out to **meet** (qara, encounter) him" *(stated)*. The operation is qara in its *encounter*-sense (H7122G) — near-null inner-being weight, the scene-setting for the two kings who meet Abram *(honest near-null; distinct qara-sense)*.
- **barak (bless) #1 — the priest blesses *Abram* (14:19).** The finding is Melchizedek "**blessed** (barak) him: Blessed be Abram by God Most High, Possessor of heaven and earth" *(stated)*. The operation is *priestly blessing on the man* — Abram *receives* blessing mediated by a priest of God Most High *(inferred)*.
- **barak (bless) #2 — the priest blesses *God* (14:20).** The finding is "**blessed** (barak) be God Most High, who has delivered your enemies" *(stated)*. The gem is barak *reversed* to doxology (as 9:26, man blesses God) — the priest *praises God* for the victory; the same operation turned from man-blessed to God-praised in adjacent verses *(inferred: barak #1 on the man, #2 on God — distinct directions)*.
- **tsar (enemies) + natan (delivered) — God hands over the foes (14:20).** The finding is God "**delivered** (natan) your **enemies** (tsar) into your hand" *(stated)*. The operations: **tsar** — the *foes*; **natan** — God's *handing-over* of them (as the animals *delivered* into man's hand, 9:2) — victory ascribed to God's giving, not Abram's might *(inferred)*.
- **natan (gave) — Abram's *tithe*, giving back to God (14:20).** The finding is "Abram **gave** (natan) him a tenth of everything" *(stated)*. The gem is the *response*: having *received* victory (God's natan) and blessing, Abram *gives* (natan) a tenth — grateful worship-giving, the interior returning a portion to God through the priest; distinct from God's delivering natan — this is *man's giving to God* *(inferred)*.
- **natan (give) + nephesh (persons) — the king's bargain (14:21).** The finding is "the king of Sodom said, **Give** (natan) me the **persons** (nephesh), but take the goods for yourself" *(stated)*. The operations: **natan** — the king's *demand* (a third natan-sense in the verse-cluster); **nephesh** — the *persons/souls* (← 12:5) the king wants back; the pagan's transaction offering Abram wealth *(inferred)*.
- **rum (lifted my hand) — the oath-gesture (14:22).** The finding is "I have **lifted** (rum) my hand to the LORD, God Most High" *(stated)*. The operation is rum (exalt/lift) as the *sworn gesture* — the raised hand of an **oath**: Abram *binds himself to God* before answering the king; distinct rum from the flood's "waters rose" (7:17) — here the interior's *vow-gesture* *(inferred)*.
- **ashar (make rich) — the refusal of *tainted* gain (14:23).** The finding is "I would not take a thread… **lest you say, 'I have made Abram rich (ashar)'**" *(stated)*. The gem is the *corrected* interior: Abram **refuses** the king of Sodom's spoil so that *no man* can claim to have *enriched* him — his wealth must come from *God* (who promised to bless him, 12:2), not from a pagan king. The operation is trusting *God as enricher* and refusing to *owe one's wealth to a man*. **Contrast ABR-02**: there Abram was made rich *by Pharaoh* through Sarai's endangerment; here he *refuses* riches from a king — the fear-and-gain interior of Egypt corrected into faith-and-refusal *(inferred: ashar — the enriching Abram will only receive from God)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **loyalty to the one who left (shama 14:14):** Abram *hears* and *rescues* Lot despite Lot's self-serving departure (ABR-03) — the un-grasping interior now *risks itself* for the grasper.
2. **received blessing → returned tithe (barak/natan 14:19–20):** Melchizedek blesses Abram and praises God; Abram, having *received* victory (God's natan) and blessing, *gives* a tenth (natan) — the interior's grateful giving-back to God.
3. **the oath that refuses gain (rum/ashar 14:22–23):** Abram *binds himself by oath* (rum) and *refuses* the spoil so no man can say he *enriched* him (ashar) — grounding his refusal in "God Most High, Possessor of heaven and earth" (so he needs nothing a king can give).
4. **the Egypt correction:** ABR-02's interior *feared* and was *enriched by a pagan king* through compromise; ABR-04's interior *swears to God* and *refuses to be enriched by a pagan king* — the same temptation (gain from a king), now met by faith. The cycle is teaching the interior to receive only from God.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** avad (servitude) / marad (revolt) as the *political* interior; arakh, qara(encounter) as *near-nulls*; berit as *human alliance*; **shama that moves to rescue** the one who left; barak on *Abram* (14:19) vs barak on *God* (14:20, doxology); tsar/natan as God's *delivering*; natan as Abram's *tithe* (giving back); natan as the king's *demand*; nephesh as *persons*; rum as the *oath-gesture*; **ashar — the refusal to be *made rich by a man*** (the Egypt correction).
- **Whose interior:** the **human** interior *corrected* — loyal (rescuing Lot), grateful (tithing), and *refusing tainted gain* by oath; against the *pagan* interiors (the king's transaction) and receiving *priestly* blessing.
- **Threads:** shama (← the primeval senses; here hearing-that-rescues); barak (← 9:26 man blesses God; here priestly); natan (the many senses; here delivering / tithing / demanding); ashar/gain (← ABR-02 enriched-by-Pharaoh, now *refused*); the oath (rum → the oaths of ABR-13, ABR-16); God Most High as Possessor (the ground of needing nothing from men).
- **Guarded against:** over-reading the political spans (avad/marad/arakh — limited weight, honestly flagged); merging the two barak (man vs God) or the three natan (deliver/tithe/demand); flattening rum into "exalt" when it is the *oath-gesture*; missing the *ABR-02 correction* that ashar carries; importing later Melchizedek/priesthood typology beyond the blessing and tithe the verses state.

---

## Gen 15:1-21 - faith reckoned righteous; the covenant God swears alone (ABR-05)

# Genesis 15:1–21 — inner-being passage reading (ABR-05-believed-covenant)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-abraham-v1-20260704`). Every span in its verse; individual + interactive operations; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. The pivot of the cycle — faith reckoned righteous.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; repeats (natan ×4, yada ×2, avad ×2, the two fears yare/emah) treated distinctly.

---

## ABR-05-believed-covenant · Genesis 15:1–21 · [faith reckoned righteous] — the fear dispelled, the honest complaint, the trust credited as righteousness, and the covenant God swears alone

**The passage.** "**Fear not** (yare), Abram, I am your shield; your reward shall be very **great** (ravah)" (15:1); "what will you **give** (natan) me, for I continue childless… you have **given** (natan) me no offspring" (15:2–3); "number the stars, if you are **able** (yakhol)… so shall your offspring be" (15:5); "he **believed** (aman) the LORD, and he **counted** (chashav) it to him as **righteousness** (tsedaqah)" (15:6); "how am I to **know** (yada) that I shall possess it?" (15:8); the pieces laid "**against** (qara) the other" (15:10); "a deep sleep fell… **dreadful** (emah) and great darkness" (15:12); "**know** (yada) for certain… your offspring will be **servants** (avad)… **afflicted** (anah)… the nation they **serve** (avad) I will **judge** (din)" (15:13–14); "you shall go… in **peace** (shalom)… a **good** (tov) old age" (15:15); "the **iniquity** (avon) of the Amorites is not yet complete" (15:16); "the LORD **made** (karat) a **covenant** (berit)… to your offspring I **give** (natan) this land" (15:18).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **yare (fear-not) — the *first* "fear not", the interior's fear *dispelled* (15:1).** The finding is "**Fear not** (yare), Abram, I am your shield" *(stated)*. The gem is the **first "fear not" in Scripture** — and it *negates* the very word of the fall's dread (3:10, "I was **afraid** (yare)"): there guilt-dread; here God *dispels* fear by *self-gift* ("I am your shield… your reward"). And it *answers* ABR-04: the interior that *refused* the king's reward is told **God himself** is its reward *(inferred: the fear God removes — of harm/loss — cured by God-as-shield-and-reward)*.
- **ravah (great) — the magnitude of the reward (15:1).** The finding is "your reward shall be very **great** (ravah)" *(stated)*. The operation is ravah (the increase/greatness word) now measuring *the reward that is God himself* — a further ravah-sense (vs blessing 1:28, pain 3:16, flood 7:17) *(inferred)*.
- **natan (give) ×2 — the honest complaint of the *un-given* gift (15:2, 15:3).** The finding is "what will you **give** (natan) me, for I continue childless (15:2)… behold, you have **given** (natan) me no offspring (15:3)" *(stated)*. The gem is *faith that argues*: Abram *laments* the promise not yet kept — the believing interior is not passive but *presses God honestly* about the withheld gift; distinct from the land-gift natan — here natan is the *offspring not yet given*, the ground of complaint *(inferred)*.
- **yakhol (able) — the *uncountable* offspring (15:5).** The finding is "number the stars, if you are **able** (yakhol) to number them" *(stated)*. The operation is *inability as superabundance* (← 13:16, the uncountable dust) — the promise measured by what the interior *cannot* count *(inferred: same yakhol-as-superabundance)*.
- **aman (believed) — the *first* believing-faith (15:6).** The finding is "he **believed** (aman) the LORD" *(stated)*. The gem is the **first "believe/faith" predicated of a person** — *aman* (to be firm, to rely; the root of "amen"): Abram *trusts* the promise (uncountable offspring) *against the evidence* (childless, aged). The operation is **faith as firm reliance on God's word over sight** — the pivot of the whole cycle *(inferred)*.
- **chashav (counted) — God's gracious *reckoning*, the root of "devising" inverted (15:6).** The finding is "he **counted** (chashav) it to him" *(stated)*. The gem is that *chashav* (reckon/impute) shares the root of *machashavah* — the heart's evil **devisings** of 6:5 ("every intention of the **thoughts** [machashavah] only evil"). At 6:5 the human reckoning-faculty *devised only evil*; here **God's** reckoning *credits faith as righteousness* — the same imputing-faculty *inverted from evil-devising (man) to grace-crediting (God)* *(inferred: chashav = God's imputation; distinct from and inverting the human machashavah)*.
- **tsedaqah (righteousness) — righteousness *reckoned*, not achieved (15:6).** The finding is "as **righteousness** (tsedaqah)" *(stated)*. The gem is the **first "righteousness" as a reckoned *status*** — Abram's *trust* is *counted* righteous; righteousness *given* to faith, not *earned* by works *(inferred: the interior justified by aman, credited by chashav, as tsedaqah — the three-span pivot)*.
- **yada (know) #1 — the believer *asks for assurance* (15:8).** The finding is "how am I to **know** (yada) that I shall possess it?" *(stated)*. The gem is that *right after believing* (15:6), Abram *asks to know* — **not doubt but the request for confirmation**: faith and the desire for assurance *coexist* in the same interior; believing does not abolish the longing for a sign *(inferred)*.
- **qara (against) — the covenant pieces arranged (15:10).** The finding is "laid each half **against** (qara, toward) the other" *(stated)*. The operation is qara in its *encounter/opposite* sense (H7122H) — near-null inner-being weight, the arranging of the covenant pieces *(honest near-null)*.
- **emah (dreadful) — the *holy dread* of the covenant-presence (15:12).** The finding is "a deep sleep fell… **dreadful** (emah) and great darkness fell on him" *(stated)*. The gem is a *second, distinct fear*: God said "**fear not**" (yare, 15:1), yet as he comes to covenant a **terror** (emah) falls — not the fear of harm (dispelled) but the **awe/dread of the divine covenant-presence**. Two fears kept apart: the fear God *removes* (yare, 15:1) and the holy *emah* of God drawing near *(inferred)*.
- **yada (know) #2 — God *grants* certain knowledge, including the hard future (15:13).** The finding is "**know** (yada) for certain that your offspring will be sojourners… servants… afflicted" *(stated)*. The gem is God *answering* the request of 15:8 — the assurance *given*, but including *slavery and affliction*: the knowledge granted is *certain and sobering* — faith is confirmed with truth, not comfort only *(inferred: distinct from 15:8 — there the asking, here the certain revelation)*.
- **avad (servants) + anah (afflicted) — the foretold servitude and affliction (15:13).** The finding is the offspring "**servants** (avad)… and **afflicted** (anah)" *(stated)*. The operations: **avad** — *enslavement* (← 14:4 servitude); **anah** — *affliction/oppression* (first occurrence; the root of Hagar's affliction, 16:11) — the suffering woven into the promise's fulfilment *(inferred)*.
- **avad (serve) + din (judge) — judgment on the oppressor (15:14).** The finding is "the nation they **serve** (avad) I will **judge** (din)" *(stated)*. The operations: **avad #2** — the serving *of the oppressor*; **din** — God's *judgment* (← 6:3 the Spirit's striving) now *on the enslaving nation* — the oppression will be *requited* *(inferred: two avad — enslaved (13) and the nation served (14); din = judgment on the latter)*.
- **shalom (peace) + tov (good) — the interior's *peaceful* end (15:15).** The finding is "you shall go to your fathers in **peace** (shalom)… buried in a **good** (tov) old age" *(stated)*. The gem is the **first "peace" (shalom) in Scripture** — the *manner of Abram's death*: the interior's *wholeness/rest* at the end, a "good" old age *(inferred: shalom's first appearance names a *peaceful death* — the believer's rest)*.
- **avon (iniquity) — the oppressor's *filling* guilt, divine patience (15:16).** The finding is "the **iniquity** (avon) of the Amorites is not yet complete" *(stated)*. The operation is avon (← 4:13 Cain's) now naming an *accumulating* guilt — God *waits* until it is "complete" before judging: **divine patience and justice** — the interior of God deferring judgment until it is just *(inferred)*.
- **karat + berit + natan — the covenant God *swears alone* (15:18).** The finding is "the LORD **made** (karat — cut) a **covenant** (berit)… to your offspring I **give** (natan) this land" *(stated)*. The gem is the **unilateral covenant**: God alone (the smoking pot and torch, while Abram sleeps in dread) passes *between the pieces* — the covenant "cut" (karat) rests on **God's self-binding**, not Abram's performance; the land *given* (natan) on God's oath alone *(inferred: karat — the covenant-cutting; God binds himself, the sleeping Abram a witness not a party)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **two fears (yare 15:1 / emah 15:12):** God *dispels* the fear of harm ("fear not, I am your shield") — the fall's dread (3:10) reversed — yet the covenant-making brings a *holy dread* (emah); the interior is freed from fearing loss and *awed* by God's nearness.
2. **honest complaint → promise → faith → reckoning (15:2–6):** Abram *laments* the un-given gift (natan), God answers with the *uncountable* stars (yakhol), Abram *believes* (aman), and God *counts* it (chashav) as *righteousness* (tsedaqah) — the interior's argued faith met by promise and *credited* — the reckoning-faculty (chashav) turned from man's evil devising (6:5) to God's grace.
3. **believing yet asking to know (aman 15:6 → yada 15:8 → yada 15:13):** faith does not silence the request for assurance; Abram *asks how he shall know*, and God *gives certain knowledge* — including slavery and affliction (avad/anah). Faith is confirmed with *sobering truth*, and the oppressor's judgment (din) and the interior's *peaceful* end (shalom) are promised together.
4. **the covenant sworn alone (karat/berit 15:18):** the whole rests not on Abram (asleep, in dread) but on *God passing between the pieces* — the land *given* (natan) on God's self-binding; faith's righteousness (15:6) and the land's gift (15:18) both *grounded in God's oath, not man's work*.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** **yare** — the *first* "fear not", fear *dispelled* (reversing 3:10) vs **emah** — the *holy dread* of the covenant-presence; ravah as the *great reward*; natan as the *un-given* offspring complained-of (15:2–3) vs the *land-gift* (15:7,18); yakhol as *uncountable* offspring; **aman** — the *first believing-faith*; **chashav** — God's *reckoning* (inverting the machashavah of 6:5); **tsedaqah** — the *first reckoned righteousness*; yada as *asking assurance* (15:8) vs *granted certain knowledge* (15:13); avad (enslaved / nation-served) + anah (affliction); din (judgment on the oppressor); **shalom** — the *first peace*, a *peaceful death*; avon as *filling* guilt (divine patience); karat/berit — the *unilateral* covenant.
- **Whose interior:** the **human** interior *believing against sight* (aman) yet *honestly complaining* and *asking to know*; and the **divine** interior *dispelling fear, crediting faith as righteousness, swearing the covenant alone*, and *patient in justice*.
- **Threads:** yare (← 3:10 dread, now "fear not"); chashav (← machashavah 6:5, inverted); aman/tsedaqah (the pivot — faith and reckoned righteousness, foundational for the cycle and beyond); natan land-gift (← 12:7); anah (→ Hagar's affliction, ABR-06 16:11); shalom (first here → the peace-motif); karat/berit (God's self-binding, ← 15's unilateral oath).
- **Guarded against:** merging the two fears (yare dispelled vs emah the holy dread); merging the four natan or two yada or two avad; flattening aman/chashav/tsedaqah into one "justification" abstraction rather than three distinct spans (trust / reckoning / righteousness); reading the chashav↔machashavah link as fanciful (both are H-root reckon/devise — the inversion is real); importing NT justification doctrine onto 15:6 beyond the trust-reckoned-righteous the verse states (the operations, not the epistle).

---

## Gen 16:1-16 - the promise seized, and the outcast seen (ABR-06)

# Genesis 16:1–16 — inner-being passage reading (ABR-06-hagar-el-roi)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-abraham-v1-20260704`). Every span in its verse; individual + interactive operations; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; repeats (anah ×2, shama ×2, natan ×2, qara ×4) treated distinctly — the anah-root (afflict / submit / affliction) is the thread.

---

## ABR-06-hagar-el-roi · Genesis 16:1–16 · [the promise seized, and the outcast seen] — the scheme that heeds the wrong voice, the affliction that recoils, and the fleeing slave who names the God who sees

**The passage.** "The LORD has **prevented** (atsar) me from bearing… go in to my servant"; "Abram **listened** (shama) to the voice of Sarai" (16:2); Sarai "**gave** (natan) Hagar… as a wife" (16:3); "I **gave** (natan) my servant to your **embrace** (cheq)… may the LORD **judge** (shaphat)" (16:5); "do as you **please** (tov)… Sarai dealt **harshly** (anah) with her" (16:6); "Return… and **submit** (anah) to her" (16:9); "I will **multiply** (ravah) your offspring… for **multitude** (rov)" (16:10); "the LORD has **listened** (shama) to your **affliction** (oni)… **call** (qara) his name Ishmael" (16:11); she "**called** (qara) the name of the LORD… You are a God of **seeing**" (16:13).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **atsar (prevented) — the divinely-closed womb (16:2).** The finding is "the LORD has **prevented** (atsar) me from bearing" *(stated)*. The operation is Sarai's *reading of providence* — she rightly sees God has *restrained* her womb, but draws from it a *scheme* rather than *waiting* *(inferred: atsar = God's restraint, the fact the scheme reacts against)*.
- **shama (listened) — heeding the *wrong voice*, the fall's fault echoed (16:2).** The finding is "Abram **listened** (shama) to the voice of Sarai" *(stated)*. The gem is that this is the *exact construction* of the fall's verdict — 3:17, "because you have **listened** (shama) to the voice of your wife" (GEN-05). Abram again *heeds his wife's voice* into a scheme that *bypasses God's timing*; distinct from the primeval shama-senses — here **heeding-the-wrong-counsel**, and *pointedly* the same fault as Eden *(inferred: the thread to 3:17 is deliberate — the interior taking the promise into its own hands)*.
- **natan (gave) #1 — the surrogate handed over (16:3).** The finding is "Sarai… **gave** (natan) her to Abram as a wife" *(stated)*. The operation is *the human scheme enacted* — giving the servant to secure the promise by contrivance; a natan of *self-help* (distinct from God's promissory land-gift) *(inferred)*.
- **cheq (embrace) + natan (gave) #2 + shaphat (judge) — the grievance and its appeal (16:5).** The finding is "I **gave** (natan) my servant to your **embrace** (cheq)… may the LORD **judge** (shaphat) between you and me" *(stated)*. The operations: **cheq** — the *intimacy* given (near-context); **natan #2** — Sarai *restates* her giving (now as grievance); **shaphat** — the **first "judge" (shaphat)**, Sarai *invoking God as arbiter* of the conflict *she* engineered — the interior appealing to divine justice while blind to its own part *(inferred: shaphat = judicial arbitration, distinct from din)*.
- **tov (please) — the subjective "as is good in your eyes" (16:6).** The finding is Abram's "do to her as you **please** (tov — as is good in your eyes)" *(stated)*. The operation is tov as *personal discretion* handed to Sarai — the appraisal-word as *self-referential license* (echoing the eye-driven "good" of the fall) *(inferred)*.
- **anah (harshly) #1 — affliction, the Egypt-word, roles reversed (16:6).** The finding is "Sarai dealt **harshly** (anah) with her, and she fled" *(stated)*. The gem is that *anah* is the **very word foretold of Israel's Egyptian bondage** — 15:13 (ABR-05), "they will be **afflicted** (anah)". Here a *Hebrew afflicts an Egyptian* (Hagar) — the affliction-operation *recurs with roles reversed*; the scheme's fruit is oppression *(inferred: anah = affliction-done-to; the thread to 15:13 is pointed)*.
- **anah (submit) #2 — the same root turned reflexive: *humble yourself* (16:9).** The finding is "Return to your mistress and **submit** (anah, hithpael) to her" *(stated)*. The gem is the *same root* anah — Sarai *afflicted* (piel, 16:6), Hagar is told to *afflict/humble herself* (hithpael, 16:9): the operation is **self-humbling under the affliction** — a hard word, distinct from 16:6 (affliction *done to* her) — here *accepting* the lowly place, with the promise attached *(inferred: anah done-to vs anah self-imposed submission)*.
- **ravah (multiply) + rov (multitude) — Abraham's promise given to the *outcast* (16:10).** The finding is "I will surely **multiply** (ravah) your offspring… for **multitude** (rov)" *(stated)*. The gem is that the *same multiply-promise given to Abram* (15:5) is here given to **Hagar** — the afflicted foreign slave-woman receives the Abrahamic *ravah*; the promise reaches the *cast-out* *(inferred: ravah extended to the outcast; rov = the abundance)*.
- **oni (affliction) + shama (listened) #2 — God *hears the afflicted* (16:11).** The finding is "the LORD has **listened** (shama) to your **affliction** (oni)" — the son named Ishmael ("God hears") *(stated)*. The gem is the *counter* to 16:2: **Abram heeded Sarai** (shama, into the mess); **God hears Hagar's affliction** (shama, to rescue). The operations: **oni** — Hagar's *state of affliction* (the noun of the anah-root); **shama** — *God's hearing* of it. The interior's affliction is *heard by God*, and the son's very name records it *(inferred: two shama — man's wrong-heeding vs God's rescuing-hearing)*.
- **qara (call) — naming Ishmael, then *naming God*, then the well, then the son (16:11,13,14,15).** The finding is the fourfold **qara**: "**call** (qara) his name Ishmael" (16:11); she "**called** (qara) the name of the LORD… You are a God of **seeing**" (16:13); the well "**called** (qara) Beer-lahai-roi" (16:14); "Abram **called** (qara) his son's name Ishmael" (16:15) *(stated)*. The gem is 16:13: **Hagar *names God*** — "El Roi, the God who sees me" — *the only person in Scripture to give God a name*, and it is the *afflicted fleeing slave*. The distinct qara-acts: naming the son "God hears" (16:11); **naming God "the God who sees"** (16:13, unique — the invocation-qara turned to *naming God himself*); naming the well for the seeing (16:14); Abram's naming of Ishmael (16:15) *(inferred: the seen-and-heard outcast responds by naming the God-who-sees — the interior's answer to being seen)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the promise *seized* (atsar → shama → natan, 16:2–3):** Sarai reads God's restraint (atsar) but, instead of *waiting* on the promise Abram just *believed* (ABR-05, aman), the household *schemes*; Abram *heeds the wrong voice* (shama, the fall's fault, 3:17); Hagar is *given* (natan) — faith's promise taken into human hands.
2. **the affliction recoils (anah 16:6 ← 15:13):** the scheme yields contempt, grievance (shaphat), and *affliction* (anah) — a Hebrew *afflicting* an Egyptian in the very word of Israel's future *Egyptian* affliction; self-help breeds oppression.
3. **the hard word *with* the promise (anah 16:9 / ravah 16:10):** the outcast is told to *humble herself* (anah, hithpael) *and* is given Abraham's *multiply*-promise (ravah) — submission and blessing joined.
4. **God hears and sees the outcast (oni/shama 16:11 → qara/El-Roi 16:13):** against Abram's wrong-*heeding* (16:2), **God hears** Hagar's *affliction* (shama/oni) and **is seen** by her; the *lowest* character — a fleeing foreign slave — receives the revelation of the *seeing-hearing* God and *names* him. The interior no one else regards is *regarded by God*, and answers by naming him.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** atsar (God's restraint of the womb); **shama — Abram heeding Sarai (← the fall's 3:17)** vs **shama — God hearing Hagar's affliction (16:11)**; natan as the *surrogate scheme* (16:3) and Sarai's *grievance* (16:5); shaphat (first "judge", invoked by the one who caused the conflict); tov as *subjective license*; **anah — affliction *done-to* (16:6, ← Israel's Egypt-word 15:13, roles reversed)** vs **anah — *self-humbling* submission (16:9)**; oni (the affliction God heard); ravah — Abraham's *multiply*-promise given to the *outcast*; **qara — Hagar *naming God* "El Roi" (the only human to name God)**, alongside the naming of Ishmael and the well.
- **Whose interior:** the **human** interior *seizing the promise* (Sarai/Abram) and *afflicting the weak*; and the **outcast** interior *afflicted, humbled, heard, and seen* — answering by *naming the God who sees*; with the **divine** interior *hearing and seeing the one no one regards*.
- **Threads:** shama (← 3:17 the fall's fault, echoed in Abram; God's rescuing hearing); anah/oni (← 15:13 the foretold affliction, roles reversed; → the affliction-and-hearing motif); ravah (← 15:5, extended to Hagar); qara — *naming God* (unique); aman (← ABR-05 — believed, yet here the household does not *wait*); the promise seized vs the promise given.
- **Guarded against:** softening the 3:17↔16:2 echo (the same "listened to the voice of his wife" — a deliberate thread, not coincidence); merging the two anah (afflict vs submit) or two shama (wrong-heeding vs God-hearing) or the qara-acts; missing that the *outcast* names God; moralising the scheme beyond what the text shows (it *narrates* the seizing and its recoil, and God's regard of Hagar, without a stated verdict); importing later Hagar/Sarah allegory (Gal 4) — the operations, not the epistle.

---

## Gen 17:1-27 - the re-named interior; covenant in the flesh (ABR-07)

# Genesis 17:1–27 — inner-being passage reading (ABR-07-circumcision-new-names)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-abraham-v1-20260704`). Every span in its verse; individual + interactive operations; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept.
- **Check-back note:** `berit` (covenant) recurs ~11× — one covenant *hammered home* (as GEN-12's rainbow), the repetition itself the emphasis; and `basar` (flesh) recurs for the *circumcision-sign* — I name these once and reference the verses, without false per-verse distinctions. Repeats otherwise (qara ×3-renaming, ravah ×2, natan ×2, barak ×2, shamar ×2, basar) treated distinctly.

---

## ABR-07-circumcision-new-names · Genesis 17:1–27 · [the re-named interior] — the command to wholeness, the covenant borne in the flesh, the new names, and the inward laugh

**The passage.** "I am God Almighty; walk before me, and be **blameless** (tamim)" (17:1); "I will **multiply** (ravah) you greatly… my **covenant** (berit)" (17:2); "no longer shall your name be **called** (qara) Abram, but **Abraham**" (17:5); "I will **give** (natan)… the land" (17:8); "you shall **keep** (shamar) my covenant… circumcised in the **flesh** (basar)" (17:9–14); "that **person** (nephesh) shall be cut off" (17:14); "you shall not **call** (qara) her Sarai, but **Sarah**… I will **bless** (barak) her and **give** (natan) you a son" (17:15–16); "Abraham fell on his face and laughed and said in his **heart** (lev)" (17:17); "Oh that Ishmael might **live** (chayah)!" (17:18); "you shall **call** (qara) his name **Isaac**" (17:19); "as for Ishmael, I have **heard** (shama) you; I will **bless** (barak) and **multiply** (ravah) him" (17:20).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **tamim (blameless) — the command to *wholeness of walk* (17:1).** The finding is "walk before me, and be **blameless** (tamim)" *(stated)*. The gem is that tamim — the *given* quality of Noah (6:9, "righteous, **blameless**", GEN-10) — is here a **command** to Abraham: *integrity/wholeness of walk* demanded before God; distinct from Noah's descriptive tamim — this is the interior *called* to be whole *(inferred)*.
- **berit (covenant) — the covenant *hammered*, of circumcision (17:2, 17:4, 17:7, 17:9, 17:10, 17:11, 17:13, 17:14, 17:19, 17:21).** The finding is God establishing "my **covenant** (berit)" — an *everlasting* covenant (17:7), "between me and you" (17:4), restated ~11× *(stated)*. The operation is God's *self-binding pledge* driven home (as GEN-12's rainbow) — one covenant, its certainty emphasised by repetition; here bearing a new *sign in the flesh* *(inferred: one covenant hammered, not eleven; the repetition = certainty)*.
- **ravah (multiply) #1 — the multiply-promise to Abraham (17:2).** The finding is "I will **multiply** (ravah) you greatly" *(stated)*. The operation is the promise (← 15:5) — the offspring multiplied *(inferred)*.
- **qara (call) — God *renames* Abram → Abraham (17:5).** The finding is "no longer… Abram, but **Abraham**, for I have made you the father of a multitude" *(stated)*. The gem is *God renaming the man*: the name *changed* to embody the destiny (father of a multitude) — the interior given a **new identity by God** (against Babel's self-made name 11:4; beyond the name *made great* at 12:2 — now the name itself *transformed*) *(inferred)*.
- **natan (give) — the land-gift (17:8).** The finding is "I will **give** (natan)… the land of your sojournings" *(stated)*. The operation is the promissory land-gift (← 12:7, 15:18) *(inferred)*.
- **shamar (keep) — covenant *obedience* (17:9,10).** The finding is "you shall **keep** (shamar) my covenant… every male shall be circumcised" *(stated)*. The gem is *shamar* — the garden-*keeping* word (2:15) and the cherubim's *guarding* (3:24) — now **covenant-keeping/obedience**: the interior's task is to *keep* (obey) the covenant; distinct from guarding a place *(inferred)*.
- **basar (flesh) — the covenant *borne in the flesh*, then *enacted* (17:11, 17:13, 17:14; obeyed 17:23, 17:24, 17:25).** The finding is "circumcised in the **flesh** (basar) of your foreskin… my covenant in your flesh" (17:11, 17:13, 17:14), and that very day Abraham circumcised the flesh of his household and himself (17:23, 17:24, 17:25) *(stated)*. The gem is basar — the material/union/corrupt/frail flesh of the primeval block — now the **flesh cut as the covenant-sign**: the covenant *marked bodily*, borne *in* the flesh; a new basar-sense (the covenant-bearer). And the sign is *enacted the same day* (17:23–25) — the shamar (keeping/obedience) *done at once*, not deferred *(inferred: the command-basar (17:11-14) and the obeyed-basar (17:23-25) are one covenant-sign, commanded then kept)*.
- **nephesh (person) — the uncircumcised *cut off* (17:14).** The finding is "that **person** (nephesh) shall be cut off from his people" *(stated)*. The operation is nephesh as *the person* (← 12:5) — the covenant's *seriousness*: the unsigned person severed *(inferred)*.
- **qara (call) — God *renames* Sarai → Sarah (17:15).** The finding is "you shall not **call** (qara) her Sarai, but **Sarah** (princess)" *(stated)*. The operation is the *second renaming* — the barren wife given a new name/destiny too; both partners re-named for the promise *(inferred)*.
- **barak (bless) + natan (give) — the *barren* wife blessed to bear (17:16).** The finding is "I will **bless** (barak) her and **give** (natan) you a son by her… she shall become nations" *(stated)*. The gem is *Sarah blessed*: the womb God *restrained* (atsar, 16:2, ABR-06) is now **blessed** (barak) to bear — the closed womb reversed by blessing *(inferred: barak = the blessing on Sarah; natan = the son given)*.
- **lev (heart) — the *inward laugh* at the impossible promise (17:17).** The finding is "Abraham fell on his face and laughed and said **in his heart** (lev): shall a child be born to a man 100 years old?" *(stated)*. The gem is the *interior* response — the laugh *in the heart* (lev): **incredulous wonder** at the impossible promise (the seed of Isaac's name, "he laughs"); the believing interior (ABR-05) now *laughs inwardly* at the promise's sheer impossibility — awe and disbelief mingled, read as the heart's astonished laugh *(inferred: lev = the seat of the inward laugh; the text leaves the laugh's exact valence — I read the heart's astonishment, not import a verdict)*.
- **chayah (live) — the father's heart for *Ishmael* (17:18).** The finding is "Oh that Ishmael might **live** (chayah) before you!" *(stated)*. The gem is the *father's plea for the son already born*: given the promise of Isaac, Abraham's heart turns to *Ishmael* — "that he might live/be blessed"; the interior's love for the existing son *(inferred)*.
- **qara (call) — God names *Isaac* ("he laughs") (17:19).** The finding is "you shall **call** (qara) his name **Isaac** (he laughs)" *(stated)*. The operation is the naming that *records Abraham's laugh* (17:17) — the covenant-son's name *carries* the interior's astonishment *(inferred)*.
- **shama (heard) + barak + ravah #2 — God *hears* the father, blesses the outcast-son (17:20).** The finding is "as for Ishmael, I have **heard** (shama) you; I will **bless** (barak) him and **multiply** (ravah) him… twelve princes" *(stated)*. The gem is *God hears Abraham's plea* (shama, answering 17:18) — as he *heard Hagar* for Ishmael (16:11): Ishmael *twice heard-for*; and Ishmael is **blessed and multiplied** (barak/ravah) — but *not* the covenant-line (17:21, the covenant with Isaac). The distinction: Ishmael *blessed* (temporal abundance) vs Isaac the *covenant-bearer* *(inferred)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **wholeness commanded, covenant borne in flesh (tamim/berit/shamar/basar):** the interior is *called to wholeness* (tamim), *bound* in an everlasting covenant (berit), tasked to *keep/obey* it (shamar), and *marked* in the flesh (basar) — the covenant is *inward calling and outward sign* together.
2. **the re-named interior (qara 17:5,15,19):** God *renames* Abram, Sarai, and names Isaac — new identities *given* to embody the promise; the self that grasped a name at Babel now *receives* transformed names from God.
3. **the barren blessed, the promise laughed at (barak 17:16 / lev 17:17):** the *restrained* womb (atsar 16:2) is *blessed* to bear (barak), and Abraham *laughs in his heart* (lev) at the impossibility — belief (ABR-05) and astonished incredulity coexisting; the laugh becomes the son's *name* (Isaac).
4. **the father's plea heard (chayah 17:18 → shama 17:20):** Abraham pleads that *Ishmael* live; God *hears* (shama, as he heard Hagar, 16:11) and *blesses* Ishmael — the father's heart honoured — while the *covenant* is set on Isaac; love for the son-already-born and the covenant-line held distinct.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** tamim as *commanded wholeness* (← Noah's given tamim 6:9); berit *hammered* (the circumcision-covenant); ravah to Abraham (17:2) and to Ishmael (17:20); **qara — God *renaming* Abram→Abraham, Sarai→Sarah, naming Isaac** (new identities); natan (land / the son); **shamar — covenant *obedience*** (← garden-keeping 2:15); **basar — the covenant *borne in the flesh*** (new sign-sense); nephesh (the person cut off); **barak — the *barren* Sarah blessed to bear** (atsar 16:2 reversed); **lev — the *inward laugh*** at the impossible (→ Isaac's name); chayah — the father's *plea for Ishmael*; **shama — God *hears* Abraham for Ishmael** (← 16:11).
- **Whose interior:** the **human** interior *re-named, called to wholeness, obeying (circumcising that day), laughing inwardly at the impossible, pleading for his other son*; and the **divine** interior *binding covenant, blessing the barren, renaming, and hearing the father*.
- **Threads:** tamim (← 6:9 Noah); qara-renaming (← the name grasped at Babel / made great 12:2, now transformed); shamar (← 2:15, now covenant-obedience); basar (← the primeval flesh-senses, now covenant-sign); barak on Sarah (atsar 16:2 reversed); lev/laugh (→ Isaac "he laughs", ABR-08 Sarah laughs, ABR-12 the laugh of joy); shama for Ishmael (← 16:11, → 21:17).
- **Guarded against:** inventing eleven covenants from the hammered berit (repetition = emphasis); manufacturing per-verse distinctions among the basar-sign occurrences (17:11-14,23-25 = one enacted obedience); reading a settled verdict into Abraham's *lev*-laugh (the text leaves its valence — I read the heart's astonishment); merging the two ravah/barak/shama (Abraham vs Ishmael); importing NT circumcision-of-the-heart theology beyond the flesh-sign the chapter states.

---

## Gen 18:1-15 - the known interior; nothing too wonderful (ABR-08)

# Genesis 18:1–15 — inner-being passage reading (ABR-08-visitors-sarah-laughs)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-abraham-v1-20260704`). Every span in its verse; individual + interactive operations; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. The *laugh* (tsachaq, 18:12–15) carries no non-T2 span — read as the scene's centre-context, anchored by shama/pala/yare.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the chay time-idiom (18:10, 18:14) noted distinctly.

---

## ABR-08-visitors-sarah-laughs · Genesis 18:1–15 · [the known interior] — the eager hospitality, the overheard promise, the inward laugh, and "nothing too wonderful for the LORD"

**The passage.** Abraham "ran to **meet** (qara) them… if I have found **favor** (chen)… do not pass by" (18:2–3); "**rest** (shaan) yourselves… refresh your **hearts** (lev)" (18:4–5); "a calf, tender and **good** (tov)… he **gave** (natan) it" (18:7); "I will return… **next year** (chay), and Sarah shall have a son; and Sarah was **listening** (shama) at the tent door" (18:10); "Sarah **laughed** to herself… shall I have pleasure?" (18:12); "Is anything too **hard** (pala) for the LORD?" (18:14); "Sarah denied it… for she was **afraid** (yare)" (18:15).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **qara (meet) — the eager run to the guests (18:2).** The finding is "he **ran to meet** (qara, encounter) them and bowed" *(stated)*. The operation is qara in its *encounter*-sense (← 14:17; 15:10) — here charged with *eagerness*: the host *runs* to the strangers; the opening move of lavish hospitality *(inferred)*.
- **chen (favor) — the host *seeking the guests'* favor (18:3).** The finding is "if I have found **favor** (chen) in your sight, do not pass by your servant" *(stated)*. The gem is the *inversion of status*: Abraham, the host, addresses the guests as those whose *favor he seeks* — a courteous *self-lowering* (chen ← 6:8 Noah's favor from God; here Abraham seeks *their* favor). The interior's hospitality as *humility* *(inferred)*.
- **shaan (rest) — rest offered to the wayfarer (18:4).** The finding is "**rest** (shaan) yourselves under the tree" *(stated)*. The operation is the **first shaan** — *lean/rest/support oneself* — the host inviting the guests to *rest* on him and the shade; (shaan later becomes the *trust*-word "lean on"; here the physical rest offered) *(inferred: shaan = rest/leaning offered)*.
- **lev (heart) — the heart *refreshed* by hospitality (18:5).** The finding is "refresh yourselves (lit. **sustain your heart**, lev)" *(stated)*. The gem is the idiom: bread *sustains the heart* (lev) — the heart as that which food *refreshes*; a distinct lev-use (against the evil heart 6:5, the grieved heart 6:6, the inward-laugh heart 17:17) — here **the heart nourished by welcome** *(inferred)*.
- **natan (gave) + tov (good) — the lavish gift of food (18:7).** The finding is "a calf, tender and **good** (tov)… he **gave** (natan) it" *(stated)*. The operations: **tov** — the *choice/good* calf; **natan** — the host's *generous giving* — hospitality as *open-handed provision* (a natan of welcome, distinct from the schemes/covenant-gifts) *(inferred)*.
- **chay (next year) + shama (listening) — the promise timed, and *overheard* (18:10).** The finding is "I will return… **next year** (ke'et chay — 'when the time revives') and Sarah shall have a son; and Sarah was **listening** (shama) at the tent door" *(stated)*. The operations: **chay** — the *reviving/living time* (next year), the promise's timing (near-idiom); **shama** — Sarah *secretly overhearing* the promise from behind the tent door — the interior *listening in* and about to react *(inferred: shama = Sarah's covert overhearing)*.
- **(18:12 — Sarah *laughs to herself*: the inward laugh, no span.)** Flagged: the laugh (tsachaq) carries no non-T2 span, but it is the scene's *centre* — Sarah, like Abraham (lev-laugh, 17:17), **laughs *within herself*** at the impossible ("after I am worn out… shall I have pleasure?"): the interior's *secret incredulity* at the dead womb revived. Read as context, anchored by shama (18:10) and answered by pala (18:14) *(no-span context; the inward laugh of disbelief)*.
- **pala (too hard/wonderful) — nothing beyond God (18:14).** The finding is "Is anything too **hard** (pala) for the LORD?" *(stated)*. The gem is the **first pala** — *be wonderful / extraordinary / beyond-ability*: the theological *centre* of the whole cycle — **nothing is too *pala* for God**; the impossibility Sarah *laughs* at (a dead womb bearing) is *not beyond* the LORD. The operation grounds the promise in God's power over the *wonderful/impossible* — and it comes as God's *answer to her secret laugh* *(inferred: pala = the impossible-for-man that is not-impossible for God)*.
- **yare (afraid) — the fear-denial of the *exposed* interior (18:15).** The finding is "Sarah denied it, 'I did not laugh,' for she was **afraid** (yare)" *(stated)*. The gem is that God *read her secret laugh* ("Why did Sarah laugh?", 18:13) — the **inward** interior *known* — and Sarah, *exposed*, **denies out of fear** (yare): the fear-driven lie of the caught self, echoing Adam's fear-and-hiding (3:10) and Cain's evasion (4:9). And it *fails*: "No, but you did laugh." The interior *cannot hide its inward laugh from God* *(inferred: yare = the fear of exposure; the secret self is known)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **lavish, humble hospitality (qara/chen/shaan/lev/natan/tov, 18:2–8):** the interior *runs* to the strangers, *seeks their favor* (self-lowering), offers *rest* and *food to refresh the heart*, *gives* the *good* calf — hospitality as eager humility and open-handed provision (a foil to the inhospitality of Sodom, ABR-10).
2. **the overheard promise → the inward laugh (shama 18:10 → laugh 18:12):** Sarah *secretly listens* and *laughs within herself* at the impossible — as Abraham did (17:17); both partners *laugh* at the promise, and the laugh will become Isaac's *name*.
3. **the known interior answered (laugh → pala 18:14):** God *reads* the secret laugh and answers it with the question that grounds everything — *"Is anything too pala for the LORD?"* — the impossibility that provoked the laugh is *not beyond* God; the incredulous interior met by the God of the wonderful.
4. **exposure and fear-denial (yare 18:15):** caught, Sarah *denies out of fear* — the secret self *known* by God, the fear-lie *failing*; the interior learns it cannot conceal its inward laugh — the fall's fear-and-hiding (3:10) surfacing even in the household of promise.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** qara (the eager *run to meet*); chen (the host *seeking the guests'* favor — hospitality as humility); shaan (the *first* "rest/lean" — rest offered); lev (the heart *refreshed* by welcome); natan/tov (the *lavish gift* of food); chay (the reviving *time* of the promise); shama (Sarah's *covert overhearing*); the *inward laugh* (no-span, ← 17:17); **pala — the first "wonderful", nothing too hard for God** (the cycle's theological centre); **yare — the fear-denial of the *exposed* interior** (← 3:10, 4:9).
- **Whose interior:** the **human** interior *hospitable and humble* (Abraham) and *secretly incredulous, then afraid and denying* (Sarah); and the **divine** interior *reading the secret laugh* and *answering incredulity with the wonderful*.
- **Threads:** the laugh (← Abraham's lev-laugh 17:17; → Isaac "he laughs", ABR-12 the laugh of joy); shama (Sarah overhearing; ← the many shama-senses); pala (→ the impossible-for-God-nothing motif); yare (← 3:10 fear-and-hiding, 4:9 evasion — the exposed self); chen (← 6:8; → 19:19 Lot); hospitality (foil to Sodom, ABR-10).
- **Guarded against:** claiming an operation off the no-span laugh (read as context, anchored by shama/pala/yare); flattening chen into generic "favor" when it is the *host lowering himself*; reading a settled verdict into the laugh's valence (incredulity is what the text shows — Sarah's own "shall I have pleasure?" and her fear-denial); merging Sarah's yare with reverence (the verse states *fear of exposure*); importing NT "Sarah's faith" (Heb 11) over the incredulity the passage narrates — the operations, not the epistle.

---

## Gen 18:16-33 - the interceding interior; the Judge of all the earth (ABR-09)

# Genesis 18:16–33 — inner-being passage reading (ABR-09-intercession-sodom)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-abraham-v1-20260704`). Every span in its verse; individual + interactive operations; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept.
- **Check-back note:** `tsaddiq` (righteous) recurs 5× through the descending bargain (50→10) — one *principle* (the righteous few sparing the wicked many) pressed at each number; I name it once and reference the verses, without inventing five distinct "righteous". Repeats otherwise (yada ×2, shachat ×3, charah ×2, yaal ×2, rasha ×2, mishpat ×2) treated distinctly.

---

## ABR-09-intercession-sodom · Genesis 18:16–33 · [the interceding interior] — God's disclosure to his chosen, the outcry against grave sin, and the humble boldness that holds the Judge to his own justice

**The passage.** "Shall I hide from Abraham…?" (18:17); "Abraham shall become a great and **mighty** (atsum) nation… all **blessed** (barak) in him" (18:18); "I have **chosen** (yada) him, that he may command his children to **keep** (shamar) the way of the LORD by doing **righteousness** (tsedaqah) and **justice** (mishpat)" (18:19); "their **sin** (chattat) is very **grave** (kaved)… the **outcry** (zeaqah)" (18:20); "I will go down… and **know** (yada)" (18:21); "will you sweep away the **righteous** (tsaddiq) with the **wicked** (rasha)?… Shall not the **Judge** (shaphat) of all the earth do **justice** (mishpat)?" (18:23–25); "I have **undertaken** (yaal) to speak… I who am but dust and ashes" (18:27); "will you **destroy** (shachat)…?" (18:28); "let not the Lord be **angry** (charah)" (18:30,32).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **atsum (mighty) + barak (blessed) — the ground of God's disclosure (18:18).** The finding is "Abraham shall become a great and **mighty** (atsum) nation, and all… **blessed** (barak) in him" *(stated)*. The operation names *why* God discloses: Abraham is the *blessing-bearer* (← 12:3) — the mighty nation-to-be; the disclosure flows from his election *(inferred)*.
- **yada (chosen) #1 — God's *electing* knowledge (18:19).** The finding is "I have **chosen** (yada — 'known') him" *(stated)*. The gem is *yada as election*: to "know" here is to *choose intimately* — God's *elective knowing* of Abraham (distinct from the primeval yada-senses) — the interior *chosen/known* by God *(inferred)*.
- **shamar (keep) + tsedaqah + mishpat — the *way* Abraham must teach (18:19).** The finding is "that he may command his children… to **keep** (shamar) the way of the LORD by doing **righteousness** (tsedaqah) and **justice** (mishpat)" *(stated)*. The gem is that **tsedaqah — the righteousness *reckoned* to Abram (15:6)** — is now the righteousness Abraham must *do and teach*: the *reckoned* becomes the *practiced and transmitted*; paired with **mishpat** (first "justice") as the content of "the way"; and *shamar* (keeping, ← 2:15/17:9) is now *keeping the moral way* *(inferred: reckoned righteousness → taught righteousness)*.
- **chattat + kaved + zeaqah — the grave sin and the outcry (18:20).** The finding is "their **sin** (chattat) is very **grave** (kaved)… the **outcry** (zeaqah) against Sodom is great" *(stated)*. The operations: **chattat** — Sodom's *sin* (← 4:7 crouching sin; 13:13 sinners); **kaved** — its *weight/gravity* (heavy; kaved later "glory") — sin as a *weight*; **zeaqah** — the *outcry* (first occurrence) of victims rising to God (as Abel's blood cried, 4:10) — the *cry of the oppressed provoking judgment* *(inferred: the outcry is the ground; sin's weight is measured)*.
- **yada (know) #2 — God's *investigative* knowledge (18:21).** The finding is "I will go down to see… and **know** (yada)" *(stated)*. The gem is *yada as investigation*: God *condescends to verify* before judging — distinct from the electing yada (18:19); the Judge does not act on the outcry alone but *goes down to know* *(inferred: two yada — electing vs investigating)*.
- **tsaddiq / rasha / shaphat / mishpat — the intercession's *moral distinction* (18:23, 18:24, 18:25, 18:26, 18:28).** The finding is "will you sweep away the **righteous** (tsaddiq) with the **wicked** (rasha)? (18:23)… Far be it from you to slay the righteous with the wicked… Shall not the **Judge** (shaphat) of all the earth do **justice** (mishpat)? (18:25)" — pressed through 50, 45, 40, 30, 20, 10 (18:24, 18:26, 18:28…) *(stated)*. The gem is the *principle*: Abraham presses the *distinction* between **tsaddiq** (← 6:9 Noah; here the righteous *few*) and **rasha** (first "wicked" as a class), and holds God to his *own character* — **the Judge (shaphat) of all the earth must do justice (mishpat)**. The operation is the interior *appealing to God's justice* that the *righteous few might spare the wicked many*; the fivefold tsaddiq is *one principle* pressed at each descending number, not five findings *(inferred: shaphat — God as universal Judge, held to mishpat; the righteous as the ground of sparing)*.
- **yaal (undertaken) — the *humble boldness* of venturing to intercede (18:27,31).** The finding is "I have **undertaken** (yaal) to speak to the Lord, I who am but dust and ashes" (18:27), and again (18:31) *(stated)*. The gem is *yaal* — to *venture/presume* — held together with "dust and ashes": **audacious enough to bargain with God, humble enough to know he is dust**. The operation is intercession as *bold-yet-lowly persistence* *(inferred: yaal = the venturing to plead; the interior's humble audacity)*.
- **shachat (destroy) ×3 — the destruction *pleaded against* (18:28,31,32).** The finding is "will you **destroy** (shachat) the whole city for lack of five?… I will not **destroy** it… for the ten's sake" (18:28,31,32) *(stated)*. The gem is *shachat* — the flood-ruin word (GEN-10; renounced 9:11; Sodom's doom foreshadowed 13:10) — now the *object of Abraham's plea*: he intercedes *against* the shachat, and God *concedes each step* — the Judge *willing to spare the many for the few* *(inferred: shachat = the destruction averted/limited by intercession)*.
- **charah (angry) ×2 — the deference not to provoke wrath (18:30,32).** The finding is "let not the Lord be **angry** (charah), and I will speak" (18:30, 18:32) *(stated)*. The gem is *charah* — the anger-word (← 4:5 Cain's) — now the *divine anger Abraham is careful not to provoke*: pressing boldly *yet fearing to overstep*; the interior's *reverent restraint within its audacity* *(inferred: charah = the wrath the intercessor defers to, marking the limit of his boldness)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **election → disclosure → transmission (18:17–19):** God will not *hide* his counsel from the one he has *chosen* (yada), *because* Abraham is to *teach* righteousness and justice (tsedaqah/mishpat) — the *reckoned*-righteous man (15:6) entrusted to *transmit* the way; election *for the sake of* teaching.
2. **outcry and investigation (zeaqah/chattat/kaved → yada, 18:20–21):** the victims' *outcry* rises, the *sin* is *heavy*, and God *goes down to know* — judgment grounded in the cry and *verified*, not arbitrary.
3. **holding the Judge to his justice (tsaddiq/rasha/shaphat/mishpat, 18:23–25):** Abraham presses the *moral distinction* and appeals to God's *own character* — the Judge must *do justice*; the *righteous few* the ground on which the *wicked many* might be spared.
4. **humble boldness against the destruction (yaal/shachat/charah, 18:27–32):** the interior *ventures* (yaal), calling itself *dust and ashes*, bargains God *down* against the *shachat*, and *defers to his wrath* (charah) — audacity and reverence together; and God *concedes* — the Judge *more willing to spare* than the intercessor dares hope.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** atsum/barak (the blessing-bearer, ground of disclosure); **yada — *electing* (18:19) vs *investigating* (18:21)**; shamar (keeping the *way*); **tsedaqah — the *reckoned* righteousness (15:6) now *taught*** + mishpat (first "justice"); chattat/kaved/zeaqah (grave sin, its weight, the outcry); **tsaddiq vs rasha** (righteous/wicked, the intercession's distinction); **shaphat — God as *Judge of all the earth*** held to mishpat; **yaal — humble *venturing*** ("dust and ashes"); shachat *pleaded against* (×3); **charah — the wrath *deferred to*** (the limit of boldness).
- **Whose interior:** the **human** interior *interceding* — bold, humble, persistent, appealing to God's justice for mercy on the wicked; and the **divine** interior *disclosing to his friend, investigating before judging, and willing to spare the many for the few*.
- **Threads:** tsedaqah (← 15:6 reckoned, now taught); yada (electing/investigating — new senses); shaphat (← 16:5 Sarai's appeal, now Abraham's; God as Judge); shachat (← GEN-10 / 13:10 Sodom foreshadowed → ABR-10 the destruction); zeaqah (the outcry motif); charah (← 4:5, now divine wrath deferred to).
- **Guarded against:** inventing five distinct "righteous" from the bargaining tsaddiq (one principle pressed down the numbers); merging the two yada (electing vs investigating); flattening kaved (weight of sin) toward its later "glory" sense; reading Abraham's yaal as mere presumption *or* mere humility (it is *both* — audacity *and* dust-and-ashes); importing later intercession/substitution theology beyond the righteous-spare-the-wicked the passage states.

---

## Gen 19:1-38 - the interior that clings to the condemned (ABR-10)

# Genesis 19:1–38 — inner-being passage reading (ABR-10-sodom-lot)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-abraham-v1-20260704`). Every span in its verse; individual + interactive operations; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. The lingering (19:16) and the backward look (19:26) are narrative centres carried by chazaq/nuach and by context.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; repeats (yada ×4, chayah ×4, nephesh ×3, sur ×2, raa ×2, shachat ×3, yakhol ×2, chesed ×2, gadal ×2, qara ×5) treated distinctly.

---

## ABR-10-sodom-lot · Genesis 19:1–38 · [the interior that clings to the condemned] — the perverted knowing, grace seizing the lingerer, the backward look, and rescue for Abraham's sake

**The passage.** Lot "**met** (qara) them… **turn aside** (sur)" (19:1–2); the mob: "that we may **know** (yada) them… **called** (qara) out" (19:5); "do not act **wickedly** (raa)… do to them as is **good** (tov) in your eyes… who have not **known** (yada) a man" (19:7–8); "he plays the **judge** (shaphat)… **break** (shavar) the door… deal **worse** (raa)" (19:9); they "**wore themselves out** (laah)" (19:11); "we will **destroy** (shachat)… the outcry is **great** (gadal)" (19:13); "about to **destroy** (shachat)" (19:14); "the **punishment** (avon)" (19:15); "he lingered… the men **seized** (chazaq) him, the LORD being **merciful** (chemlah)… **set** (nuach) him outside" (19:16); "escape for your **life** (nephesh)" (19:17); "**favor** (chen)… great **kindness** (chesed)… **saving** (chayah) my **life** (nephesh)… I **cannot** (yakhol)… lest **disaster** (raah)" (19:19); "Lot's wife looked back… pillar of salt" (19:26); "God **destroyed** (shachat)… God **remembered** (zakhar) Abraham" (19:29); "Lot was **afraid** (yare)" (19:30); "**preserve** (chayah) offspring… he did not **know** (yada)" (19:32–35).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **qara (met) + sur (turn aside) — hospitality *in the wicked city* (19:1, 19:2, 19:3).** The finding is Lot "**met** (qara) them" (19:1) and pressed "**turn aside** (sur, 19:2)… to your servant's house", and they "**turned aside** (sur, 19:3) to him" *(stated)*. The operation is hospitality *echoing Abraham's* (18:2) — but in *Sodom*: Lot *insists* (sur, urging them to lodge, 19:2) and they at last *turn in* (19:3) — the righteous impulse *in the corrupt place* *(inferred: qara-encounter + sur = the urging to shelter, offered and accepted)*.
- **yada (know) #1 — the conjugal word *perverted into assault* (19:5).** The finding is the mob's "bring them out, that we may **know** (yada) them" *(stated)*. The gem is *yada* — the *begetting* knowing of 4:1 — now **perverted into intended rape/violence**: the city's depravity turns the intimate-knowing word into assault *(inferred: knowing-as-violation; the conjugal yada corrupted)*.
- **raa (wickedly) — Lot names the evil (19:7).** The finding is "do not act so **wickedly** (raa)" *(stated)*. The operation is *raa* (be/do evil, ← 6:5 the heart's evil) — Lot *pleading against* the wickedness *(inferred)*.
- **tov (good) + yada (known) — Lot's *monstrous* offer (19:8).** The finding is "I have two daughters who have not **known** (yada) a man… do to them as is **good** (tov) in your eyes" *(stated)*. The operations: **yada** — the daughters *unrealized* conjugally (virgins); **tov** — the *subjective* "good in your eyes" (← 16:6) — Lot's hospitality *curdled into monstrosity*: offering his daughters to protect the guests. The compromised interior *(inferred: tov handed to the mob's discretion; hospitality gone wrong)*.
- **shaphat (judge) + shavar (break) + raa (worse) — the mob's escalation (19:9).** The finding is "this fellow… plays the **judge** (shaphat)… we will deal **worse** (raa) with you… they pressed to **break** (shavar) the door" *(stated)*. The operations: **shaphat** — the mob *mocking Lot's moral judgment* (← 18:25 the Judge; here men resenting judgment); **raa #2** — the *escalating* evil; **shavar** — the *breaking* violence *(inferred)*.
- **laah (wore themselves out) — depravity that *persists past blindness* (19:11).** The finding is the men struck blind "**wore themselves out** (laah) groping for the door" *(stated)*. The gem is *laah* (weary/exhaust) — even *blinded*, the mob *exhausts itself* seeking the door: **sin that persists past all restraint** — the hardened interior (← the fall's hardening) *(inferred)*.
- **shachat (destroy) ×2 + gadal + avon — the judgment announced, unheeded (19:13–15).** The finding is "we will **destroy** (shachat) this place, for the **outcry** has become **great** (gadal)" (19:13); "the LORD is about to **destroy** (shachat)" — but Lot "seemed to be jesting" (19:14); "swept away in the **punishment** (avon)" (19:15) *(stated)*. The operations: **shachat** — the *destruction* (← GEN-10; the shachat Abraham pleaded against, 18:28); **gadal** — the *great* outcry (← 18:20 zeaqah); **avon** — the *punishment* (← 4:13; 15:16); and the warning *unheeded* (the sons-in-law think Lot *jests*) *(inferred)*.
- **chazaq + chemlah + nuach — grace *seizes the lingerer* (19:16).** The finding is "he **lingered**. So the men **seized** (chazaq) him… the LORD being **merciful** (chemlah)… and **set** (nuach) him outside" *(stated)*. The gem is the whole rescue: Lot *lingers* (attached to the doomed city); God's **compassion** (chemlah — first occurrence) **seizes** (chazaq — firm grip) his hand and **sets** (nuach — places at rest, ← 2:15/8:4) him *out*. **Mercy drags the reluctant interior to safety** — salvation *against* the self's clinging *(inferred: chemlah = divine pity; chazaq = the grip of rescue; nuach = set in safety)*.
- **nephesh (life) — the life to be saved (19:17).** The finding is "escape for your **life** (nephesh)" *(stated)*. The operation is nephesh as *Lot's life* (← 12:5; life-sense) — the thing the flight is *for* *(inferred)*.
- **chen + chesed + chayah + nephesh + yakhol + raah — Lot's fearful bargaining (19:19).** The finding is "your servant has found **favor** (chen)… you have shown great **kindness** (chesed) in **saving** (chayah) my **life** (nephesh); but I **cannot** (yakhol) escape to the hills, lest **disaster** (raah) overtake me" *(stated)*. The gem is **chesed — the first "steadfast kindness/love" in Scripture** — God's *loyal mercy* in saving Lot; alongside **chen** (favor, ← 6:8; 18:3), **chayah** (life-saving), **nephesh** (the life), **yakhol** (Lot's *fearful inability* — "I cannot reach the hills", ← 13:6 scarcity, here *fear*), and **raah** (the *disaster* feared). The rescued interior, *even in grace, bargains from fear* — pleading for the little city rather than the hills *(inferred: chesed = the great loyal-love word, here first; Lot's fear qualifies even his gratitude)*.
- **chayah (saved) + nephesh + yakhol + qara — Zoar, the little refuge (19:20, 19:22).** The finding is "let me escape there… my **life** (nephesh) may be **saved** (chayah) (19:20)… I **can** (yakhol) do nothing till you arrive… the city was **called** (qara) Zoar (19:22)" *(stated)*. The operations: chayah/nephesh — the life saved in the little city (19:20); **yakhol** — now the *angel's* "I **cannot** do anything till you arrive" (19:22 — the rescue *waits* on Lot); qara — the place *named* Zoar ("little", 19:22) for its littleness *(inferred)*.
- **(19:26 — Lot's wife looks back: the backward look, no span.)** Flagged: "looked back" (nabat) carries no non-T2 span, but it is the passage's *emblem*: told "do not look back" (19:17), she **looks back** and becomes salt — **the heart still turned to the condemned**, the interior that *cannot leave behind* what God destroys, *frozen* in its backward attachment *(no-span context; the clinging look)*.
- **zakhar + shachat — rescue *for Abraham's sake* (19:29).** The finding is "when God **destroyed** (shachat) the cities… God **remembered** (zakhar) Abraham and sent Lot out" *(stated)*. The gem is *zakhar* (← 8:1 God remembered Noah): **Lot is saved because God *remembered Abraham*** — the intercession (ABR-09, 18:22–33) *bears fruit*; the righteous man's prayer saves his kin. Lot's rescue rests *not on Lot's merit* but on *God's remembering the intercessor* *(inferred: intercession's fruit; the destruction (shachat) executed, yet the nephew spared for the uncle's sake)*.
- **yare — Lot's *fear*, and the irony of the hills (19:30).** The finding is "Lot was **afraid** (yare) to live in Zoar, so he lived in the hills" *(stated)*. The gem is the irony: Lot *refused* the hills (he *couldn't*, yakhol, 19:19) — now *fear* (yare) drives him *to* them; the fearful interior contradicting itself *(inferred)*.
- **chayah (preserve) + yada — the *corrupted line*, and its naming (19:32, 19:33, 19:34, 19:35, 19:37, 19:38).** The finding is the daughters' "let us… **preserve** (chayah, 19:32) offspring through our father… he did not **know** (yada, 19:33) when she lay down"; the second night "**preserve** (chayah, 19:34) offspring… he did not **know** (yada, 19:35)"; and the sons **called** (qara) Moab (19:37) and Ben-ammi (19:38) *(stated)*. The gem is the double corruption: **chayah** — *"preserving seed"* twisted into *incest* (the daughters, thinking the world ended, contrive to continue the line, both nights, 19:32,34); **yada** — the *conjugal* knowing (4:1) now in *drunken darkness*, "he did not know" (19:33,35) — begetting-in-oblivion; and the *naming* (qara) of Moab and Ben-ammi (19:37–38) records the line's shameful origin. The Sodom-corrupted interior *produces corruption even in its escape* *(inferred: chayah-preserve perverted; yada-in-oblivion; the qara-naming fixing the origin)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the depraved city (yada-assault 19:5, laah 19:11, raa/shavar 19:9):** the intimate-knowing word *perverted into rape*, evil that *persists past blindness*, the door *broken* — total depravity; and Lot's hospitality *curdles* (offering his daughters, tov 19:8) — the compromised righteous man *in* the corruption.
2. **grace seizes the lingerer (chazaq/chemlah/nuach 19:16):** Lot *clings* to the doomed city; God's *compassion* (chemlah) *seizes* (chazaq) and *sets him out* (nuach) — mercy saving *against* the self's reluctance.
3. **fear qualifies even the rescued (chen/chesed/yakhol/yare 19:19,30):** saved by *steadfast kindness* (chesed, first), Lot still *bargains from fear* (yakhol, "I cannot") for the little city — then *fears* (yare) it and flees to the very hills he refused; the fearful interior contradicting itself.
4. **the backward look vs the forward rescue (19:26):** told to flee and not look back, Lot's wife *looks back* — the heart *turned to the condemned* — and is *frozen*; the interior that will not leave what God judges.
5. **saved for the intercessor's sake (zakhar 19:29):** the *shachat* Abraham pleaded against *falls* — yet Lot is spared because *God remembered Abraham*; the intercession bears fruit even as the judgment lands.
6. **corruption survives the escape (chayah/yada 19:32–35):** rescued *from* Sodom, Lot's family *carries Sodom out* — "preserving seed" through incest, begetting *in oblivion*; deliverance from the place is not deliverance from its corruption.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** qara/sur (hospitality *in* the wicked city); **yada — the conjugal word *perverted*** (assault 19:5; the incest-in-oblivion 19:33–35) vs the daughters *unrealized* (19:8); tov as *monstrous* discretion; shaphat (the mob *mocking* judgment); laah — *depravity persisting past blindness*; shachat (announced/unheeded/executed) + gadal + avon; **chazaq/chemlah/nuach — grace *seizing the lingerer*** (chemlah first); **chesed — the *first* steadfast-kindness**; chen/chayah/nephesh/yakhol/raah — *fearful* bargaining; the *backward look* (no-span); **zakhar — Lot saved because *God remembered Abraham*** (intercession's fruit); yare — Lot's *self-contradicting* fear; **chayah-preserve + yada — the *corrupted line*** (Moab/Ammon).
- **Whose interior:** the **human** interior *clinging to the condemned* (Lot lingering, his wife looking back) and *carrying corruption out of judgment*; the *depraved* city; and the **divine** interior *merciful* (chemlah, chesed), *seizing to save*, and *remembering the intercessor*.
- **Threads:** yada (← 4:1 conjugal, here perverted); chemlah/chesed (first here — the mercy/steadfast-love words → carried through the study); zakhar (← 8:1; intercession's fruit ← ABR-09); shachat (← GEN-10; 13:10 foreshadowed; 18:28 pleaded-against, now fallen); yare (← 3:10; Lot's fear); the backward look (→ the clinging-to-the-judged motif); tov "good in your eyes" (← 16:6).
- **Guarded against:** claiming operations off the no-span backward look (read as emblem-context); merging the four yada (assault / unrealized / oblivion) or the four chayah (saving-life / preserving-seed); flattening chesed's first appearance; missing that Lot is saved *for Abraham's sake* (zakhar, not Lot's merit); moralising beyond the text (the narrator *shows* Lot's compromise, his wife's look, the incest, without a stated verdict — I read the operations); importing NT "remember Lot's wife" (Luke 17) — the operation the verse gives.

---
