## Gen 20:1-18 - integrity of heart; the fear wrongly assumed absent (ABR-11)

# Genesis 20:1–18 — inner-being passage reading (ABR-11-abimelech-integrity)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-abraham-v1-20260704`). Every span in its verse; individual + interactive operations; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. The repeated fear-lie of ABR-02, now examined from the *other* side — the pagan's integrity.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; repeats (levav ×2, tom ×2, yada ×2, chata ×2, qara ×2, natan ×2, chesed ×2) treated distinctly.

---

## ABR-11-abimelech-integrity · Genesis 20:1–18 · [integrity of heart, and the fear wrongly assumed absent] — the pagan's clean heart vindicated, God restraining sin, and the patriarch's exposed excuse

**The passage.** "Will you slay an **innocent** (tsaddiq) people?… in the **integrity** (tom) of my **heart** (levav) and the **innocence** (niqqavon) of my hands" (20:4–5); "I **know** (yada) that you did this in the **integrity** (tom) of your **heart** (levav), and I kept you from **sinning** (chata)" (20:6); "he will pray… you shall **live** (chayah); but if not… **know** (yada) that you shall die" (20:7); "Abimelech **called** (qara) his servants… very **afraid** (yare)" (20:8); "how have I **sinned** (chata)… you have brought great **sin** (chataah)… he **called** (qara) Abraham" (20:9); "there is no **fear** (yirah) of God in this place" (20:11); "this is the **kindness** (chesed) you must do me" (20:13); "he **gave** (natan) sheep and oxen" (20:14); "dwell where it **pleases** (tov) you" (20:15); "I have **given** (natan) a thousand pieces of silver… a vindication" (20:16); "the LORD had **closed** (atsar) all the wombs" (20:18).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **tsaddiq (innocent) — the pagan claims *righteous innocence* (20:4).** The finding is "will you slay an **innocent** (tsaddiq) people?" *(stated)*. The gem is that *tsaddiq* — the *righteous* (← 6:9 Noah; 18:23 the intercession) — is here claimed by a **pagan king**, *rightly* (he took Sarah unknowingly): the interior's *genuine innocence*, about to be *vindicated by God* *(inferred)*.
- **tom + levav + niqqavon — the *integrity of heart* (20:5).** The finding is "in the **integrity** (tom) of my **heart** (levav) and the **innocence** (niqqavon) of my hands" *(stated)*. The gem is the **first "integrity" (tom)** — *wholeness/blamelessness* (kin to tamim, 6:9/17:1) — of the **heart** (levav, the fuller form of lev): Abimelech acted in *sincerity of heart* and *clean hands* (niqqavon). The operation is *integrity as the heart's moral wholeness* — sincerity of intention *(inferred: tom = integrity; levav = the heart that holds it)*.
- **yada (know) #1 + tom + levav + chata — God *vindicates* the heart and *restrains* sin (20:6).** The finding is "I **know** (yada) that you did this in the **integrity** (tom) of your **heart** (levav), and I kept you from **sinning** (chata) against me" *(stated)*. Two gems: **yada** — God *knows/confirms* the heart's integrity (as he read Sarah's laugh, 18:13; the electing/investigating yada, 18:19,21) — God *vindicates* the pagan's inner sincerity; and **chata** — God "**kept** you from **sinning**": the divine interior *actively restrains* a man from sin — **preventing grace**, guarding even a pagan from wrong *(inferred: God's yada vindicates; God's restraint keeps from chata)*.
- **yada (know) #2 + chayah (live) — the warning (20:7).** The finding is "he will pray for you, and you shall **live** (chayah); but if you do not restore her, **know** (yada) that you shall surely die" *(stated)*. The operations: **yada** — *warning-knowledge* (know the consequence); **chayah** — *life contingent* on restoring Sarah and Abraham's prayer *(inferred: distinct yada — the sobering certainty, vs 20:6 the vindicating knowledge)*.
- **qara (called) + yare (afraid) — the court's *right fear* (20:8).** The finding is "Abimelech **called** (qara) all his servants… and the men were very **afraid** (yare)" *(stated)*. The gem is that the *pagan court* **fears** (yare) rightly on hearing God's warning — a fear *more responsive than Abraham assumed* (see yirah, 20:11) *(inferred: qara = summons; yare = the court's genuine dread of God)*.
- **chata + chataah + qara — the *pagan rebukes the patriarch* (20:9).** The finding is Abimelech's "how have I **sinned** (chata) against you, that you have brought a great **sin** (chataah) on me and my kingdom?" and he "**called** (qara) Abraham" *(stated)*. The gem is the *reversal*: the **pagan king rebukes the patriarch** for *nearly making him sin* — the moral roles inverted, Abimelech *more concerned about sin* than Abraham; chata (the verb) / chataah (the noun) both name the guilt Abraham's deception nearly incurred *(inferred: the wronged pagan's rebuke; sin-verb and sin-noun distinguished)*.
- **yirah (fear) — the fear-of-God *wrongly assumed absent* (20:11).** The finding is Abraham's "I thought, there is no **fear** (yirah) of God at all in this place, and they will kill me" *(stated)*. The gem is that Abraham *justifies his deception* by assuming **no *yirah* (fear of God)** in the place — **and he was *wrong*** (Abimelech had integrity, the court feared God, 20:8): the interior's *misjudgment of others' godliness*; the fear-lie of ABR-02 repeated, and here *exposed as groundless* *(inferred: yirah = the fear-of-God Abraham falsely presumed absent)*.
- **chesed (kindness) — the *compromised* loyalty-arrangement (20:13).** The finding is "this is the **kindness** (chesed) you must do me: at every place, say of me, He is my brother" *(stated)*. The gem is *chesed* — the *steadfast-love* word (← 19:19, first, God's saving chesed) — here in a *lesser, compromised* use: the *loyalty* Abraham asked of Sarah to *maintain the deception*; the great word *bent* to a fearful arrangement *(inferred: distinct chesed — God's saving loyalty vs the deception-pact)*.
- **natan (gave) + tov (pleases) + natan (given) — the wronged pagan's *generosity* (20:14–16).** The finding is Abimelech "**gave** (natan) sheep and oxen… restored Sarah" (20:14); "dwell where it **pleases** (tov) you" (20:15); "I have **given** (natan) your brother a thousand pieces of silver… a **vindication**" (20:16) *(stated)*. The operations: **natan #1** — *restitution*; **tov** — the generous "dwell where it is good in your eyes" (freedom of the land); **natan #2** — the silver *vindicating* Sarah's honour. The *wronged party* responds with *generosity* *(inferred: two natan — restitution and vindication)*.
- **atsar (closed) — the wombs *restrained*, the barrenness-word again (20:18).** The finding is "the LORD had **closed** (atsar) all the wombs of the house of Abimelech, because of Sarah" *(stated)*. The gem is *atsar* — the *same word* as **Sarai's own closed womb** (16:2, ABR-06, "the LORD has *restrained* me") — now the *protective judgment* on Abimelech's house (healed when Abraham prays, 20:17): God's *restraint of wombs*, there a trial, here a guard *(inferred: atsar — barrenness as trial (16:2) vs as protective judgment (20:18))*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the pagan's integrity vindicated, sin restrained (tsaddiq/tom/levav/yada/chata 20:4–6):** Abimelech claims *innocence* and *integrity of heart*; God *confirms* it (yada) and reveals he *kept him from sinning* (chata) — the pagan's genuine sincerity *vindicated*, and God's *restraining grace* disclosed; set against Abraham's deception.
2. **the roles reversed (chata/chataah 20:9, yirah 20:11):** the *pagan rebukes the patriarch* for nearly bringing *sin* on him; and Abraham's excuse — "*no fear of God* in this place" — is *exposed as false* (the court *feared*, yare 20:8; the king had *integrity*): the interior *misjudged* others' godliness, and the fear-lie (ABR-02) is shown *groundless*.
3. **the great word compromised (chesed 20:13):** the *steadfast-love* word (God's saving chesed, 19:19) is *bent* to the deception-pact — faith's vocabulary pressed into a fearful arrangement.
4. **generosity and restraint (natan/tov 20:14–16; atsar 20:18):** the *wronged* pagan responds with *gifts, land, and vindication*; and God's *closing of the wombs* (atsar, the barrenness-word of 16:2) is *protective*, healed by Abraham's *prayer* — the patriarch, though at fault, still the *prophet* whose prayer restores.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** tsaddiq — the *pagan's* claimed innocence, *vindicated*; **tom — the *first* "integrity"**, of the *heart* (levav); **yada — God *vindicating* the heart (20:6)** vs the *warning*-knowledge (20:7); **chata — God *restraining* sin (20:6)** vs the *sin* Abraham nearly caused (20:9); yare — the court's *right fear* vs **yirah — the fear-of-God Abraham *wrongly assumed absent*** (the fear-lie exposed); **chesed — the great word *compromised*** into the deception-pact; natan (restitution / vindication); tov (the generous "as it pleases you"); **atsar — the barrenness-word (← 16:2), here *protective judgment***.
- **Whose interior:** the **pagan** interior *upright and God-fearing* (Abimelech, his court) — *more* so than the deceiving patriarch; the **divine** interior *vindicating integrity and restraining sin*; and the **human** interior *misjudging others' godliness* (Abraham's exposed excuse).
- **Threads:** the fear-lie (← ABR-02 Egypt; here *exposed* as a false assumption); tom/tamim (← 6:9/17:1 wholeness); yada (God knowing the heart, ← 18:13); chesed (← 19:19, now compromised); atsar (← 16:2 Sarai's womb, now Abimelech's house); Abraham as *prophet* whose prayer heals (20:7,17).
- **Guarded against:** merging the two yada (vindicating vs warning), two chata (restrained vs caused), two natan, or the two chesed (God's saving love vs the deception-pact); flattening tom into generic "integrity" without seeing it is the *heart's* wholeness; missing that the *pagan* is the upright one here; softening that Abraham's yirah-assumption was *wrong*; importing a harsh verdict on Abraham the text withholds (it *shows* the exposure and still calls him *prophet*).

---

## Gen 21:1-21 - the laugh of joy, and the outcast heard (ABR-12)

# Genesis 21:1–21 — inner-being passage reading (ABR-12-isaac-born-hagar-sent)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-abraham-v1-20260704`). Every span in its verse; individual + interactive operations; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. The laugh (tsachaq, 21:6) and the opened eyes (21:19) are narrative centres carried by shama and by context.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; repeats (shama ×3, qara ×3, raa ×2, gadal ×2) treated distinctly.

---

## ABR-12-isaac-born-hagar-sent · Genesis 21:1–21 · [the laugh of joy, and the outcast heard] — the incredulous laugh turned to joy, the wife's voice now God's command, and God hearing the dying boy

**The passage.** "Abraham **called** (qara) his son's name Isaac" (21:3); "God has made **laughter** for me; everyone who **hears** (shama) will laugh over me" (21:6); "the child **grew** (gadal) and was weaned" (21:8); "the thing was very **displeasing** (raa) to Abraham" (21:11); "be not **displeased** (raa)… through Isaac shall your offspring be **named** (qara)… **obey** (shama) her voice" (21:12); "he **gave** (natan) bread and water… and sent her away" (21:14); "she… **wept** (bakhah)" (21:16); "God **heard** (shama) the voice of the boy… the angel **called** (qara)… **Fear not** (yare)" (21:17); "**hold** (chazaq) him fast… I will make him a great nation" (21:18); "God opened her eyes, and she saw a well" (21:19); "the boy **grew up** (gadal)" (21:20).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **qara (called) — Isaac named (21:3).** The finding is "Abraham **called** (qara) his son's name Isaac" *(stated)*. The operation is the naming *fulfilled* (per 17:19) — the covenant-son named "he laughs" *(inferred)*.
- **shama (hears) #1 — the laugh *transformed* to joy (21:6).** The finding is "God has made **laughter** for me; everyone who **hears** (shama) will laugh over/with me" *(stated)*. The gem is the *transformation* of the laugh: Sarah's *inward incredulous* laugh (18:12) becomes the **laugh of joy** — and all who **hear** (shama) will *laugh with* her; Isaac ("he laughs") *embodies* the joy. The operation is the interior's laughter turned *from doubt to rejoicing* *(inferred: shama anchors the shared joy; the laugh 18:12→21:6, incredulity→gladness)*.
- **gadal (grew) #1 — the child grows (21:8).** The finding is "the child **grew** (gadal) and was weaned" *(stated)*. The operation is the ordinary *growth* of the promised son (gadal ← 12:2 the name; here the child) *(inferred: near-context)*.
- **raa (displeasing) #1 — the father's *distress* over Ishmael (21:11).** The finding is "the thing was very **displeasing** (raa) to Abraham on account of his son" *(stated)*. The gem is *raa* (be evil/grievous, ← 6:5) here as **the father's grief**: sending Ishmael away is *bitter* to Abraham — the interior's pain at losing the son he has (← his plea "that Ishmael might live", 17:18) *(inferred: raa = the grievous, Abraham's distress)*.
- **raa (displeased) #2 + qara + shama (obey) — God's word: heed Sarah, the fall's fault *now right* (21:12).** The finding is "be not **displeased** (raa)… through Isaac shall your offspring be **named** (qara)… whatever Sarah says, **obey** (shama) her voice" *(stated)*. Two gems: **qara** — the line *reckoned through Isaac* ("named/called" through him); and **shama (obey)** — God *commands* Abraham to **obey the voice of** Sarah. This is the *same construction* that was the **fall's verdict** (3:17, "you have **listened to the voice** of your wife") and the **Hagar-scheme's fault** (16:2) — but here it is **God's command**: heeding the wife is *right* because *her word aligns with God's purpose*. The operation is the *same act* (heeding the wife) now *divinely sanctioned* — the fault redeemed by *whose will it serves* *(inferred: raa #2 — God stilling the distress; shama-obey — the wife's voice now God's channel)*.
- **natan (gave) — the reluctant provision (21:14).** The finding is Abraham "**gave** (natan) bread and a skin of water to Hagar… and sent her away" *(stated)*. The operation is natan as *provision at the parting* — the father *gives* even as he *sends*; the reluctant sending softened by giving *(inferred)*.
- **bakhah (wept) — the mother's despair-weeping (21:16).** The finding is "she… **wept** (bakhah)" — "let me not look on the death of the child" *(stated)*. The gem is the **first "weep" (bakhah)** — Hagar's *despair* as the water fails and the boy dies; the interior's *grief at a child's dying* *(inferred: bakhah = the weeping of despair)*.
- **shama (heard) #2 + qara + yare — God *hears the boy* (21:17).** The finding is "God **heard** (shama) the voice of the boy… the angel **called** (qara) to Hagar: **Fear not** (yare)… God has heard the voice of the boy" *(stated)*. The gem is *shama* fulfilling the name: **God *hears* the boy** — Ishmael = "God hears" (← 16:11) — and it is the *boy's* voice heard (not the mother's weeping); the angel's **"fear not"** (yare, ← 15:1 to Abram) *comforts the despairing outcast*. God's hearing reaches the *dying child* *(inferred: shama = God hearing Ishmael, the name kept; yare = fear-not to Hagar)*.
- **chazaq (hold fast) — the mother told to grip the boy (21:18).** The finding is "**hold** (chazaq) him fast with your hand, for I will make him a great nation" *(stated)*. The gem is *chazaq* (grip/strengthen, ← 19:16 the angels seizing Lot) — Hagar told to *hold the boy fast*, the promise (great nation) renewed (← 16:10; 17:20); the operation is *the grip of hope* commanded *(inferred)*.
- **(21:19 — God opens her eyes: the provision seen, no span.)** Flagged: "opened… saw" carries no non-T2 span, but the *centre*: **God opens Hagar's eyes and she sees a well** — the provision *was there*; her *despair blinded* her to it. The interior's *eyes opened* to God's provision — an echo of *El-Roi* (the God who sees, 16:13) now *making her see* *(no-span context)*.
- **gadal (grew up) #2 — God with the outcast (21:20).** The finding is "God was with the boy, and he **grew up** (gadal)" *(stated)*. The operation is Ishmael's *growth under God's presence* — the outcast son *cared for*, the promise kept (← 16:10; 17:20); distinct from the child's growth at 21:8 (Isaac) — here Ishmael, *God-with-him* though not the covenant-line *(inferred)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the laugh transformed (shama/laughter 21:6 ← 18:12):** Sarah's *incredulous* inward laugh becomes the *laugh of joy* — all who *hear* laugh *with* her; Isaac's very name carries the interior's turn from doubt to gladness.
2. **the father's grief and the sanctioned heeding (raa/shama 21:11–12):** Abraham is *distressed* (raa) over Ishmael; God *stills* the distress and *commands* him to *obey Sarah's voice* — the "heed the wife" that was *the fall's fault* (3:17) and *the scheme's fault* (16:2) is now *God's will*; the same act redeemed by the purpose it serves.
3. **the sending, the despair, the hearing (natan/bakhah/shama 21:14–17):** Abraham *gives* provision and *sends*; Hagar *weeps* in despair; and **God *hears* the boy** (Ishmael, "God hears") — the outcast child's voice reaching heaven, met with *"fear not"*.
4. **the opened eyes and the kept promise (chazaq/eyes/gadal 21:18–20):** told to *hold the boy fast*, Hagar has her *eyes opened* to the well she could not see, and Ishmael *grows up with God* — the outcast provided for, seen, and blessed, though the covenant runs through Isaac.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** qara (Isaac named 21:3; the line *named through Isaac* 21:12); **shama — those who *hear* laugh-with-joy (21:6)** vs **shama-obey — God *commanding* Abraham to heed Sarah (21:12, the fall's fault now right)** vs **shama — God *hearing the boy* (21:17)**; gadal (Isaac's growth 21:8 / Ishmael's 21:20); **raa — the father's *distress* (21:11)** stilled by God (21:12); natan (the reluctant provision); **bakhah — the *first* "weep"**, Hagar's despair; yare — *fear-not* to the outcast; chazaq — *hold the boy fast*; the *opened eyes* (no-span, ← El-Roi 16:13).
- **Whose interior:** the **human** interior *rejoicing* (Sarah's laugh-of-joy), *grieving* (Abraham over Ishmael, Hagar over the boy); the **outcast** interior *despairing then heard and seen*; and the **divine** interior *hearing the dying child, opening blind eyes, keeping his promise to the cast-out*.
- **Threads:** the laugh (← 17:17 Abraham, 18:12 Sarah's doubt; here → joy; Isaac "he laughs"); **shama-obey (← 3:17/16:2 the fall's fault, now God's command)**; shama-God-hears (← 16:11 Ishmael; the outcast heard); yare fear-not (← 15:1); El-Roi/seeing (← 16:13, now Hagar's eyes opened); the two sons (Isaac the covenant-line vs Ishmael blessed-and-kept).
- **Guarded against:** claiming operations off the no-span laugh (21:6) and opened-eyes (21:19) — read as centres anchored by shama; **merging the three shama** (joy-hearing / God-commanding-heed / God-hearing-the-boy) — especially missing that 21:12's *heed-the-wife* is the *redeemed* form of the fall's fault; merging the two raa (distress / God stilling it) or two gadal; importing Galatians' Hagar allegory — the operations the chapter states.

---

## Gen 21:22-34 - loyalty sworn, the eternal invoked (ABR-13)

# Genesis 21:22–34 — inner-being passage reading (ABR-13-beersheba-oath)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-abraham-v1-20260704`). Every span in its verse; individual + interactive operations; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; repeats (berit ×2, karat ×2, qara ×2) treated distinctly.

---

## ABR-13-beersheba-oath · Genesis 21:22–34 · [loyalty sworn, the eternal invoked] — the oath of steadfast dealing against false dealing, and worship of the Everlasting God

**The passage.** "God is with you… **swear** to me… you will not **deal falsely** (shaqar) with me… but as I have dealt **kindly** (chesed) with you, so you will deal with me" (21:22–23); "I do not **know** (yada) who did this… I have not **heard** (shama) of it until today" (21:26); "Abraham **gave** (natan) sheep and oxen… the two **made** (karat) a **covenant** (berit)" (21:27); "that place was **called** (qara) Beersheba, because there both swore an oath" (21:31); "they **made** (karat) a **covenant** (berit)" (21:32); "Abraham… **called** (qara) on the name of the LORD, the Everlasting God" (21:33).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **chesed (kindly) vs shaqar (deal falsely) — the two poles of covenant faithfulness (21:23).** The finding is "you will not **deal falsely** (shaqar) with me… but as I have dealt **kindly** (chesed) with you, so you will deal with me" *(stated)*. Two gems, set as *opposites*: **chesed** — *steadfast, loyal dealing* (the great love-word, ← 19:19 God's saving chesed; 20:13 the compromised pact) — here the *reciprocal loyalty* Abimelech asks; and **shaqar** — the **first "deal falsely" (shaqar)**, *faithlessness/lying* — the *opposite* of chesed. The operation names the interior's *two possible modes* toward a covenant-partner: *loyal dealing* or *false dealing*. And there is a quiet irony — the *pagan* asks the *patriarch* (who lately deceived him, ABR-11) not to *shaqar* but to render *chesed* *(inferred: chesed = loyal dealing; shaqar = false dealing — the poles)*.
- **yada (know) + shama (heard) — Abimelech's *ignorance of the wrong* (21:26).** The finding is "I do not **know** (yada) who did this… I have not **heard** (shama) of it until today" — of the seized well *(stated)*. The operations are Abimelech's *not-knowing* (yada) and *not-having-heard* (shama) — the honest disavowal of the grievance; near-context to the treaty *(inferred: distinct yada/shama — ignorance, not the weighty senses)*.
- **natan + karat + berit — the *human* covenant made (21:27).** The finding is "Abraham **gave** (natan) sheep and oxen… the two **made** (karat) a **covenant** (berit)" *(stated)*. The gem is *karat* — "cut a covenant" — the *same idiom* as **God's unilateral covenant** (15:18, ABR-05) — now *between two men*: a *human* covenant-cutting, sealed with Abraham's *gift* (natan); distinct from God's self-binding oath — here *mutual* treaty *(inferred: karat/berit human-to-human, vs God's 15:18)*.
- **qara (called) #1 — the oath-place named (21:31).** The finding is "that place was **called** (qara) **Beersheba**, because there both of them swore an oath" *(stated)*. The operation is naming *memorialising the oath* — the treaty *fixed* in a place-name (Beersheba, "well of the oath/seven") *(inferred)*.
- **karat + berit — the covenant *concluded* (21:32).** The finding is "so they **made** (karat) a **covenant** (berit) at Beersheba" *(stated)*. The operation *restates* the concluded treaty — the human covenant *ratified* *(inferred: the karat/berit of 21:27 completed)*.
- **qara (called) #2 — worship of the *Everlasting* God (21:33).** The finding is "Abraham planted a tamarisk… and **called** (qara) there on the name of the LORD, the **Everlasting God** (El Olam)" *(stated)*. The gem is *qara-as-worship* (← 4:26 first worship; 12:8; 13:4 Abram calling on the Name) — now *after* the temporal treaty, Abraham **calls on the *Everlasting* God** (El Olam, a *new* name for God, as El-Roi 16:13, El-Shaddai 17:1): the interior *grounds its temporal dealings in worship of the eternal* — the passing oath framed by the *unpassing* God *(inferred: qara-worship; El Olam the everlasting)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **loyalty against falseness (chesed/shaqar 21:23):** the treaty is asked on the ground of *chesed* (steadfast dealing) *not shaqar* (false dealing) — the interior's covenant-faithfulness defined by its two poles; the once-deceived pagan seeking loyalty from the patriarch.
2. **the human covenant (natan/karat/berit 21:27,32):** two men *cut* a covenant (karat, the very idiom of God's oath, 15:18) — sealed by gift and oath, memorialised at *Beersheba* (qara).
3. **the temporal grounded in the eternal (qara/El-Olam 21:33):** after the *human, temporal* treaty, Abraham *worships* the **Everlasting God** — the interior sets its passing agreements *within* the worship of the God who does not pass; a temporal oath framed by the eternal Name.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** **chesed (loyal dealing) vs shaqar (the *first* "deal falsely")** — the two poles of covenant faithfulness; yada/shama as Abimelech's *ignorance of the wrong*; natan/karat/berit — the *human* covenant-cutting (← God's 15:18); qara — the oath-place *named* (21:31) vs qara — *worship of the Everlasting God* (21:33, El Olam, new divine name).
- **Whose interior:** the **human** interior *swearing loyalty* (chesed) and *worshipping the eternal* (Abraham); the **pagan** interior *seeking faithful dealing* (Abimelech).
- **Threads:** chesed (← 19:19 God's saving love; 20:13 compromised; here reciprocal loyalty); karat/berit (← 15:18 God's unilateral, now human); qara-worship (← 4:26; 12:8; 13:4); the divine names (El-Roi 16:13, El-Shaddai 17:1, El-Olam 21:33 — the interior naming God by his acts); the oath (→ ABR-14 the oath-blessing; ABR-16 the servant's oath).
- **Guarded against:** merging chesed and shaqar (they are set as *opposites* — the whole point); flattening karat's human covenant into God's unilateral one; merging the two qara (naming the place vs worship); missing that El-Olam is a *new* name grounding the temporal in the eternal; over-reading the minor yada/shama (Abimelech's ignorance, not the weighty senses).

---

## Gen 22:1-19 - the Aqedah: the fear of God that withholds nothing (ABR-14)

# Genesis 22:1–19 — inner-being passage reading (ABR-14-aqedah)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-abraham-v1-20260704`). Every span in its verse; individual + interactive operations; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. The pinnacle of the cycle. Note: the great words *tested* (nasah 22:1), *love* (aheb 22:2), and *provide* (ra'ah 22:8,14, a T2 term) carry **no non-T2 span** — read as central context; the anchored operations are the *fear-of-God*, the *knowing*, the *obedience*, and the *oath-blessing*.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; repeats (qara ×3, barak ×2) treated distinctly.

---

## ABR-14-aqedah · Genesis 22:1–19 · [the fear of God that withholds nothing] — the surrendered love, the tested obedience, and "now I know that you fear God"

**The passage.** "God **tested** (nasah) Abraham… Here I am" (22:1); "take your son, your only son… whom you **love** (aheb)… offer him" (22:2); "I and the boy will go… and worship… and come again" (22:5); "God will **provide** the lamb" (22:8); "Abraham… **laid** (arakh) the wood… bound Isaac… laid him on the altar" (22:9); "he reached out… the knife" (22:10); "the angel **called** (qara): Abraham, Abraham!" (22:11); "now I **know** (yada) that you **fear** (yare) God, seeing you have not withheld your son" (22:12); "Abraham **called** (qara) the name of that place, The LORD will **provide**" (22:14); "the angel **called** (qara) a second time" (22:15); "by myself I have sworn… I will surely **bless** (barak) you and **multiply** (ravah)… possess the gate of their **enemies** (oyev)… all nations **blessed** (barak)… because you have **obeyed** (shama) my voice" (22:16–18).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **(22:1 — God *tests*; "Here I am": no span.)** Narratively "God **tested** (nasah) Abraham" and Abraham answers "**Here I am**" (hinneni). Flagged: nasah carries no non-T2 span, but it is the frame — the interior *summoned to a test* and answering with *ready availability* ("Here I am", repeated to God 22:1, to Isaac 22:7, to the angel 22:11) — the posture of the whole passage *(no-span context: the tested, available interior)*.
- **(22:2 — "your son, whom you *love*": the first love, surrendered; no span.)** Narratively "take your son, your only son… whom you **love** (aheb)". Flagged: aheb — the **first "love" in Scripture** — carries no non-T2 span, but it is the passage's *heart*: love appears *at the moment of its demanded surrender* — the father's *deepest attachment* (the only son) commanded to be *given up*. The interior's *dearest* is exactly what the test asks *(no-span context: the first love = the surrendered love)*.
- **(22:5, 22:8 — resurrection-faith and provision-trust: no span.)** Narratively "we will **come again** to you" (22:5) and "God will **provide** the lamb" (22:8, ra'ah = T2). Flagged: no non-T2 span, but the anchored *faith*: Abraham obeys *believing God will keep the promise through Isaac* ("come again") and *provide* — the tested faith (aman, ABR-05) at its *extremity* *(no-span context: obedience that still trusts the promise)*.
- **arakh (laid) — the *deliberate* ordering of the sacrifice (22:9).** The finding is "Abraham built the altar and **laid** (arakh) the wood in order, and bound Isaac his son and laid him on the altar" *(stated)*. The gem is *arakh* (arrange/set in order, ← 14:8 the battle-array) — the **methodical, deliberate obedience**: Abraham *arranges* the wood, *binds* the boy, *lays* him — every terrible step *ordered*, obedience carried through *action*, not just assent *(inferred: arakh = the ordered, enacted obedience)*.
- **qara (called) #1 — the angel *stops the knife* (22:11).** The finding is "the angel of the LORD **called** (qara) to him from heaven, 'Abraham, Abraham!'" *(stated)*. The operation is the *urgent, arresting call* (qara — the pursuing/summoning call) — heaven *intervening* at the last instant *(inferred)*.
- **yada (know) + yare (fear) — the fear-of-God *demonstrated*, God's knowing *confirmed* (22:12).** The finding is "now I **know** (yada) that you **fear** (yare) God, seeing you have not withheld your son" *(stated)*. Two gems: **yada** — "now I *know*" — God's knowing **confirmed by the act**; the test *makes manifest* what was in the interior (God's demonstrated/experiential knowing, ← 18:19,21; 20:6); and **yare** — "you *fear* God" — the **fear-of-God at its summit**: the reverent fear that *withholds nothing*, that surrenders the dearest. This is the very *yirah* Abraham *wrongly assumed absent* in others (20:11, ABR-11) — now *proven in himself*; and the *"fear not"* (yare, 15:1, ABR-05) *matured* into the fear that *trusts God with everything*. The operation is **the fear-of-God = holding nothing back from God** *(inferred: yare — the withholding-nothing fear; yada — the test that reveals it)*.
- **qara (called) #2 — "The LORD will provide" (22:14).** The finding is "Abraham **called** (qara) the name of that place, **The LORD will provide** (Yahweh-Yireh)" *(stated)*. The gem is *qara-as-naming-God's-provision*: the God who *sees* (El-Roi, 16:13) **provides** (Yireh, "sees/provides") — the ram given, the provision-faith (22:8) *vindicated* and *memorialised* in the place-name; the interior *names the mount for the providing God* *(inferred: qara — naming the place for God's provision)*.
- **qara (called) #3 — the angel a *second time* (22:15).** The finding is "the angel… **called** (qara) to Abraham a second time" *(stated)*. The operation is the *renewed* heavenly address, introducing the oath-blessing *(inferred: distinct qara — the second call, to bless)*.
- **barak (bless) ×2 + ravah (multiply) + oyev (enemies) + shama (obeyed) — the oath-blessing *grounded in obedience* (22:16, 22:17, 22:18).** The finding is "by myself I have **sworn** (22:16)… I will surely **bless** (barak) you and **multiply** (ravah) your offspring as the stars… possess the gate of their **enemies** (oyev, 22:17)… in your offspring all nations **blessed** (barak)… **because you have obeyed** (shama) my voice (22:18)" *(stated)*. The gems: **barak/ravah** — the blessing and multiplying (← 12:2; 15:5) now **sealed by God's *self-oath*** ("by myself I have sworn") — the covenant confirmed at its highest, *grounded in the tested obedience* ("because you have done this"); **oyev** — the *first "enemy"*, the offspring's victory; and **shama** — "because you have **obeyed** (shama) my voice" — the **obey-sense** at its *summit*: the *heeding-a-voice* that was the fall's fault (3:17), the redeemed heeding of Sarah (21:12), is here Abraham's **supreme obedience to *God's* voice** (offering the son) — and the blessing is *grounded* in it *(inferred: barak/ravah oath-sealed; shama = the obedience that grounds the blessing)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the test of the surrendered love (nasah/aheb 22:1–2):** God *tests* by demanding the son "whom you *love*" — the *first love* appearing as the *love to be given up*; the interior's *dearest* is exactly the test's object, and Abraham answers "*Here I am*".
2. **obedience that still trusts (22:5,8 → arakh 22:9):** Abraham obeys *believing* God will "provide" and that they will "come again" — faith (aman, ABR-05) at its *extremity* — and *enacts* it, *arranging* the wood and *binding* the son (arakh): the tested faith *carried through in deliberate action*.
3. **the fear-of-God revealed (yada/yare 22:12):** the knife raised, heaven *calls* (qara), and the verdict: *"now I know you fear God, for you have not withheld your son"* — the **fear-of-God = withholding nothing**; the fear wrongly assumed absent in others (20:11) *proven* here, the "fear not" (15:1) *matured* into total trust.
4. **provision and oath-blessing (qara/barak/ravah/shama 22:14–18):** God *provides* the ram and Abraham *names* the mount for it (Yahweh-Yireh); then God *swears by himself* to *bless* and *multiply* — **because Abraham *obeyed*** (shama): the blessing (12:2), the pivot of the whole cycle, is *oath-sealed* and *grounded in the tested, enacted fear-and-obedience* of the interior.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** the *test* (nasah) and "Here I am" (no-span, the available interior); the **first *love* (aheb), appearing as the *surrendered* love** (no-span); the *resurrection/provision*-faith (no-span, 22:5,8); **arakh — the *deliberate, enacted* obedience** (ordering the sacrifice); qara — the angel's *arresting* call (22:11), the *naming* of Yahweh-Yireh (22:14), the *second* call (22:15); **yada — God's knowing *confirmed by the act*** + **yare — the fear-of-God that *withholds nothing*** (the summit; ← 20:11 assumed-absent, 15:1 "fear not"); **barak/ravah *oath-sealed*** by God's self-oath; oyev (first "enemy"); **shama — the *obedience* that grounds the blessing** (the heeding-word at its summit).
- **Whose interior:** the **human** interior at its *peak of faith* — surrendering its *dearest love*, *fearing God* by withholding nothing, *obeying* God's voice, *trusting* provision and promise; and the **divine** interior *testing*, *knowing by the test*, *providing*, and *swearing the blessing by himself*.
- **Threads:** yare/fear-of-God (← 15:1 "fear not"; 20:11 assumed-absent → here *proven*); yada (God's knowing, ← 18:19/20:6, now demonstrated); shama-obey (← 3:17 fault; 21:12 God's command → here obedience to *God's own* voice); barak/ravah (← 12:2; 15:5 → oath-sealed); the naming of God (El-Roi 16:13 → Yahweh-Yireh 22:14); aman/faith (← 15:6, tested to the extremity); the surrendered love (first aheb → the love-motif).
- **Guarded against:** claiming operations off the *no-span* love/test/provide (read as central context — honestly flagged, not smuggled in as spans); flattening yare into generic "fear" when it is *the fear that withholds nothing*; missing that yada here is *demonstrated* knowing; merging the three qara (arrest / naming / second-call) or the two barak; reading shama-obey as identical to its fault-uses (here it is *obedience to God*, the redeemed summit); importing NT Aqedah typology (Heb 11; the offering of the Son) — the operations the chapter states, not the fulfilment.

---

## Gen 23:1-20 - grief, and the sojourner's grave (ABR-15)

# Genesis 23:1–20 — inner-being passage reading (ABR-15-sarah-death-machpelah)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-abraham-v1-20260704`). Every span in its verse; individual + interactive operations; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept.
- **Check-back note:** `shama` (hear) recurs 6× as the *courteous mutual-hearing* of the negotiation — one operation (honourable dealing) whose repetition is its emphasis; named once, verses referenced. `natan` ×3 treated distinctly.

---

## ABR-15-sarah-death-machpelah · Genesis 23:1–20 · [grief, and the sojourner's grave] — the honoured life, the weeping-and-mourning, and the pilgrim who owns only a tomb

**The passage.** "Sarah **lived** (chayyim) 127 years… the years of Sarah's life" (23:1); "Abraham went in to **mourn** (saphad) for Sarah and to **weep** (bakhah) for her" (23:2); "I am a **sojourner** and foreigner… **give** (natan) me property… for a burying place" (23:4); "**Hear** (shama) us… bury your dead" (23:6); "if it is your **will** (nephesh)… **hear** (shama) me" (23:8); "I **give** (natan) you the field… **hear** (shama) me" (23:9,11); "**hear** (shama) me… **listen** (shama)… Abraham **listened** (shama) to Ephron and weighed out the silver" (23:13,15,16).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **chayyim (lived) — Sarah's life *honoured* (23:1).** The finding is "Sarah **lived** (chayyim) 127 years; these were the years of Sarah's **life**" *(stated)*. The gem is that this is the **only woman whose lifespan Scripture records** — Sarah's years *noted* and *honoured*; the death-formula (← GEN-08) here *dignifies* her life before the grief begins *(inferred: chayyim = the honoured lifespan)*.
- **saphad (mourn) + bakhah (weep) — the *twofold* grief (23:2).** The finding is "Abraham went in to **mourn** (saphad) for Sarah and to **weep** (bakhah) for her" *(stated)*. Two gems: **saphad** — the **first "mourn/lament" (saphad)**, the *formal wailing/lament* of mourning; and **bakhah** — *weeping* (← 21:16 Hagar's first bakhah) — here Abraham's *private tears*. The operation is grief in *two registers*: the *formal lament* (saphad) and the *personal weeping* (bakhah) — the interior mourning its life-partner *(inferred: saphad = ritual lament; bakhah = the tears; distinct)*.
- **natan (give) — the *purchase-request*, the sojourner seeking a grave (23:4).** The finding is "I am a **sojourner** and foreigner among you; **give** (natan) me property… for a burying place" *(stated)*. The gem is the *self-understanding*: Abraham calls himself a **sojourner** (ger — a pilgrim owning nothing, *though promised all the land*), and *natan* here is a request *to acquire (buy)* a burial site — the interior's *first possession in the promised land is a grave* *(inferred: natan = the request to purchase; the pilgrim's only holding a tomb)*.
- **shama (hear) ×6 — the *honourable mutual-hearing* of the negotiation (23:6,8,11,13,15,16).** The finding is the repeated "**hear** (shama) us / hear me / listen", and "Abraham **listened** (shama) to Ephron and weighed out the silver" (23:16) *(stated)*. The gem is *shama* as the **courteous, scrupulous mutual-attentiveness** of an honourable transaction — the Hittites *hear* Abraham, he *hears* them, and he *insists on paying full price* (not taking the offered gift): the interior's **honourable dealing**, refusing to *owe* (← ABR-04's refusal of gain). The sixfold shama is *one operation* — *civil, fair listening* — its repetition marking the *care* of the dealing (distinct from hearing-God, heeding-a-voice, God-hearing-the-afflicted) *(inferred: shama = the mutual hearing of honourable negotiation; the repetition = its scrupulousness)*.
- **nephesh (will) — the *soul as willingness* (23:8).** The finding is "if it is your **will** (nephesh — 'if it is in your soul')" *(stated)*. The gem is a *new nephesh sub-sense* (H5315L, "soul: appetite/desire") — nephesh as the **seat of will/desire**: "if it is *your soul's* will" — the negotiation appealing to the other's *willingness*; distinct from nephesh-as-life (2:7), persons (12:5), life-in-blood (9:4) — here *the will/desire* *(inferred: nephesh = the willing soul)*.
- **natan (give) ×2 — the field *offered and bought* (23:9, 23:11).** The finding is Abraham's "let him **give** (natan) me the cave… for the full price" (23:9) and Ephron's "I **give** (natan) you the field" (23:11) *(stated)*. The operation is the transaction's two sides — *offered as gift* (Ephron), *taken as purchase* (Abraham insisting on full price); the interior *securing an honest, owned* burial-right *(inferred: natan offered vs natan paid — Abraham will not take it as gift)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **grief that honours and weeps (chayyim/saphad/bakhah 23:1–2):** Sarah's *life is honoured* (her recorded years), and Abraham *mourns and weeps* — the interior's grief in *both* formal lament and private tears at losing his partner.
2. **the sojourner's grave (natan/ger 23:4):** the man *promised all the land* calls himself a *sojourner* and seeks to *buy* a *burying place* — the interior's *first possession* in the promise's land is a *tomb*; faith holds the whole promise while owning only a grave (a pledge of the inheritance held in a place of death).
3. **honourable dealing (shama ×6, natan 23:9–16):** the *scrupulous, courteous* negotiation — mutual *hearing* (shama) — with Abraham *insisting on full payment* (not the gift): the interior *deals honourably*, refusing to *owe* even a grave (as it refused a king's spoil, ABR-04); the burial-right *legally, honestly secured*.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** chayyim — Sarah's *honoured* lifespan (the only woman's recorded); **saphad (first "mourn/lament") + bakhah (weep)** — grief in *two registers*; natan — the *purchase-request* and the *offered/paid* transaction; **the sojourner owning only a *grave*** (the pilgrim promised all); **shama ×6 — the *honourable mutual-hearing*** of the negotiation (Abraham *paying full price*); nephesh — a *new sub-sense*, the *willing soul*.
- **Whose interior:** the **human** interior *grieving* (mourning, weeping), *self-understood as a sojourner*, and *dealing honourably* (paying full price) — securing a grave in the land it does not yet possess.
- **Threads:** bakhah (← 21:16 Hagar; grief-weeping); the sojourner (→ the pilgrim-in-the-land motif; the promise held while owning a tomb); shama (honourable hearing; ← the many shama-senses); natan (the purchase, honest dealing, ← ABR-04 refusing gain); the burial-place (Machpelah → the patriarchs' grave).
- **Guarded against:** merging saphad and bakhah (formal lament vs private tears); inventing six distinct hearings from the negotiation's shama (one operation, honourable dealing, its repetition the emphasis); flattening nephesh's *will* sense into its life-senses; missing that the *sojourner* owns only a *grave* though promised all (the quiet gem); moralising the transaction beyond what the text shows (scrupulous, honourable dealing).

---

## Gen 24:1-67 - providence and the comfort of love (ABR-16)

# Genesis 24:1–67 — inner-being passage reading (ABR-16-wife-for-isaac)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-abraham-v1-20260704`). Every span in its verse; individual + interactive operations; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. The cycle's providence-and-love centre.
- **Check-back note:** `barak` (bless/praise) recurs 7× (blessing Abraham; doxology; blessing Rebekah) and `natan` 6× (God's giving; the gifts) — recurring operations named with their distinctions and verses referenced. `chesed`/`emet` (the covenant-pair), `charesh`, the heart's prayer, and `nacham` carry the depth.

---

## ABR-16-wife-for-isaac · Genesis 24:1–67 · [providence and the comfort of love] — the prayer for steadfast love, the silent discernment, the willing consent, and grief consoled

**The passage.** "The LORD had **blessed** (barak) Abraham in all things" (24:1); the servant "who **ruled** (mashal) over all he had" (24:2); "**take care** (shamar) that you do not take my son back… you will be **free** (naqah) from this oath" (24:6,8); "grant me success… show **steadfast love** (chesed) to my master… by this I shall **know** (yada)" (24:12,14); Rebekah "**attractive** (tov)… no man had **known** (yada) her" (24:16); "the man gazed in **silence** (charesh) to **learn** (yada)" (24:21); "**Blessed** (barak) be the LORD… who has not forsaken his **steadfast love** (chesed) and **faithfulness** (emet)" (24:27); "before I had finished speaking in my **heart** (lev)" (24:45); "if you will show **steadfast love** (chesed) and **faithfulness** (emet)… tell me" (24:49); "we **cannot** (yakhol) speak **bad** (ra) or **good** (tov)" (24:50); "they **called** (qara) Rebekah… Will you go?… I will go" (24:57–58); "may your offspring possess the gate of those who **hate** (sane) them" (24:60); "Isaac… **loved** her, and was **comforted** (nacham) after his mother's death" (24:67).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **barak (blessed) — the *comprehensively* blessed patriarch, and the *kneeling* root (24:1, 24:11, 24:31, 24:35, 24:48, 24:60).** The finding is "the LORD had **blessed** (barak) Abraham in all things" (24:1) *(stated)*. The operation is the blessing (← 12:2) *fulfilled* — the aged Abraham *blessed in everything*; the ground of his confident charge. The *same root barak* then runs several senses through the chapter, **kept distinct**: at **24:11** the servant "made the camels **kneel** (barak)" — the *physical root* of the word (to bend the knee), *not* blessing; at **24:31** Laban greets the servant as "**blessed** (barak) of the LORD"; at **24:35** "the LORD has **blessed** (barak) my master greatly" (the blessing *recounted*, with **gadal**); at **24:48** the servant "**blessed** (barak) the LORD" (*doxology*, ← 24:27); at **24:60** the family "**blessed** (barak) Rebekah". So barak spans *kneeling* (24:11), *being-blessed* (24:31), *God's blessing recounted* (24:35), *praising God* (24:48), and *blessing a person* (24:60) — one root, several distinct acts *(inferred: do not lump — 24:11 is the *knee-bending*, the others are blessing/praise)*.
- **mashal (ruled) — the steward's *delegated authority* (24:2).** The finding is "his servant who **ruled** (mashal) over all that he had" *(stated)*. The operation is *mashal* (govern, ← 1:16; 3:16; 4:7) as the *steward's stewardship* — trusted rule over the household; distinct from the husband's/sin's mashal — here *fiduciary authority* *(inferred)*.
- **shamar (take care) + naqah (free) — the oath's *condition and release* (24:6,8).** The finding is "**take care** (shamar) that you do not take my son back there… you shall be **free** (naqah) from this oath" *(stated)*. The operations: **shamar** — *taking-heed/guarding-against* (← the keeping-word, now vigilance over the oath's terms); **naqah** — being *cleared/free* from the oath if the woman refuses — the interior *bound but justly releasable* *(inferred)*.
- **natan (give) — the land-promise and the *gifts* (24:7, 24:32, 24:35, 24:36, 24:41, 24:53).** The finding is "the LORD… who swore to **give** (natan) this land to my offspring" (24:7) *(stated)*. The operation is the *promissory land-gift* (← 12:7) grounding Abraham's *faith*; and the *same natan* runs through the chapter in a *different* register — the *gifts* of hospitality and betrothal: Laban **gave** (natan) provender to the camels (24:32); "the LORD… has **given** (natan) my master flocks… all he has" (24:35–36, God's *giving* to Abraham recounted); the oath-clause "**give** (natan) her to me" (24:41); the servant "**gave** (natan) costly ornaments" to Rebekah's house (24:53). So natan spans the *land-promise* (24:7) and the *provision/betrothal-gifts* (24:32,35,36,41,53) — the promissory gift and the enacted generosity *(inferred: distinct natan registers — the promise vs the gifts)*.
- **chesed (steadfast love) + yada (know) — the *prayer for guidance* by a sign (24:12,14).** The finding is "grant me success… show **steadfast love** (chesed) to my master Abraham… by this I shall **know** (yada) that you have shown steadfast love" *(stated)*. The gems: **chesed** — the servant *prays for God's steadfast love* to Abraham (← 19:19 God's saving chesed); and **yada** — *knowing-by-a-sign* (as Abram "how shall I know", 15:8): the interior *seeking guidance* through a requested sign *(inferred: chesed = the divine loyalty invoked; yada = discernment sought)*.
- **tov (attractive) + yada (known) — Rebekah (24:16).** The finding is "the young woman was very **attractive** (tov)… a virgin, no man had **known** (yada) her" *(stated)*. The operations: **tov** — her beauty (← 6:2, here neutral/good); **yada** — *unrealized* conjugal knowing (virgin, ← 4:1) *(inferred)*.
- **charesh (silence) + yada (learn) — the *silent, watchful discernment* (24:21).** The finding is "the man gazed at her in **silence** (charesh) to **learn** (yada) whether the LORD had prospered his way" *(stated)*. The gem is the **first "silence/be-still" (charesh)** — the servant *watches wordlessly*, the interior *waiting in stillness to discern* God's leading (not rushing to conclude); paired with *yada* (to learn/know) — **discernment as silent attentiveness** *(inferred: charesh = attentive silence; the watching interior)*.
- **barak (blessed) + chesed + emet — the *doxology* for God's covenant character (24:27).** The finding is "**Blessed** (barak) be the LORD… who has not forsaken his **steadfast love** (chesed) and **faithfulness** (emet) toward my master" *(stated)*. The gems: **barak** — the servant *blesses/praises God* (doxology, ← 9:26; 14:20); and the **first "emet" (faithfulness/truth)** paired with **chesed** — the great covenant-couplet *chesed-and-emet* (steadfast-love and reliable-truth): the interior *recognises God's unforsaken loyal-faithfulness* in the providential leading *(inferred: chesed+emet = God's covenant character, praised)*.
- **lev (heart) — the *silent prayer* answered (24:45).** The finding is "before I had finished speaking in my **heart** (lev), behold, Rebekah came out" *(stated)*. The gem is *lev* as the place of **silent, inward prayer** — the servant prayed *in his heart* and was answered *before he finished*: the interior's *unspoken prayer met by immediate providence*; a distinct lev-use (the *praying* heart, against the evil 6:5, grieved 6:6, laughing 17:17, refreshed 18:5 hearts) *(inferred)*.
- **chesed + emet + o — the request for *loyal faithfulness* (24:49).** The finding is "if you will show **steadfast love** (chesed) and **faithfulness** (emet) to my master, tell me; and if not (o)…" *(stated)*. The operation *restates* the covenant-pair — the servant asks the family for *chesed-and-emet* (loyal, truthful dealing) in the decision *(inferred: chesed+emet again — the pair as the standard of dealing)*.
- **tov + ra + yakhol — "we cannot speak bad or good" (24:50).** The finding is "this has come from the LORD; we **cannot** (yakhol) speak **bad** (ra) or **good** (tov) to you" *(stated)*. The gem is the idiom: *ra* and *tov* — the **good-and-evil pair** (← the tree of the knowledge of *good and evil*, 2:9,17) — here in the sense "*we can say nothing* against it": the family *cannot gainsay* God's evident will; *yakhol* (human inability, ← 13:6; 15:5) before the divine leading *(inferred: tov/ra idiom = powerlessness to object)*.
- **qara + shaal — the *willing consent* (24:57–58).** The finding is "let us **call** (qara) the young woman and **ask** (shaal) her… they called Rebekah: Will you go? … **I will go**" *(stated)*. The gem is that Rebekah is *asked* (shaal) her consent and *freely says "I will go"* — the interior's **willing yes** to the leading (echoing Abraham's own obedient *going*, 12:4); consent, not compulsion *(inferred: shaal = the asking; the willing "I will go")*.
- **sane (hate) + barak — the blessing on Rebekah (24:60).** The finding is "they **blessed** (barak) Rebekah… may your offspring possess the gate of those who **hate** (sane) them" *(stated)*. The operations: **barak** — the family's *blessing*; **sane** — the *first "hate"* — the *enemies'* hostility over which the offspring will triumph (← oyev 22:17) *(inferred)*.
- **nacham (comforted) — grief *consoled by love* (24:67).** The finding is "Isaac took Rebekah… she became his wife, and he **loved** her; so Isaac was **comforted** (nacham) after his mother's death" *(stated)*. The gem is *nacham* — the word of God's *grief/regret* (6:6), the *comfort hoped* in Noah's naming (5:29) — here **consolation**: Isaac's *grief* (for Sarah, ABR-15) *met by comfort in love*; and *"he loved her"* (aheb — the **second "love"** in Scripture, after the *surrendered* love of 22:2) is now the **love that comforts**. The interior's grief *consoled by love* *(inferred: nacham = consolation; aheb = the comforting love, vs the surrendered love 22:2)*.

- **Near-context spans (coverage, low inner-being weight).** For completeness: the oath-*release* recurs (**naqah**, "you will be **free**", 24:8, ← 24:41); the *prayer/sign* is restated with **chesed**+**yada** (24:14, the same request as 24:12); the servant *runs to meet* Rebekah (**qara**-encounter, 24:17) and later Rebekah sees Isaac *coming to meet* them (**qara**, 24:65); Laban *heard* the account (**shama**, 24:30) and the servant *heard* their assent and worshipped (**shama**, 24:52); the servant *asked* whose daughter she was (**shaal**, 24:47); the family *called* Rebekah (**qara**, 24:58, the consent scene); and the particle **o** ("or/whether", glossed "desire" — a grammatical near-null, 24:50,55) carries *no* inner-being operation. Noted so no span is silently passed *(honest near-nulls / restatements)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the blessed patriarch's faith-charge (barak/mashal/shamar/naqah/natan 24:1–8):** the *comprehensively blessed* Abraham charges his *trusted steward* by oath (shamar/naqah) to seek a wife among his kin, *trusting God's leading* ("the LORD… will send his angel"); the land-*gift* (natan) grounds the faith.
2. **prayer, sign, and silent discernment (chesed/yada/charesh/lev 24:12–45):** the servant *prays for God's chesed* and a *sign to know* (yada), watches in *silence* (charesh) to discern, and finds his *heart's* (lev) prayer *answered before he finished* — the interior seeking and receiving guidance through *prayer, sign, stillness*, and *providence*.
3. **God's chesed-and-emet recognised (barak/chesed/emet 24:27,49):** the servant *praises* God for his *unforsaken steadfast-love-and-faithfulness*, and asks the family for the same *chesed-and-emet* — the providential leading read and required as *covenant loyalty*.
4. **the willing consent and the comfort of love (qara/shaal/nacham/aheb 24:57–67):** God's will is *unopposable* (tov/ra, yakhol 24:50); Rebekah *freely consents* ("I will go"); and Isaac *loves* her and is *comforted* (nacham) after his mother's death — the cycle's grief (ABR-15) *consoled by love*, the *second love* (comforting) answering the *first love* (surrendered, 22:2).

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** barak — the *blessed* patriarch (24:1), the *doxology* (24:27,48), the *blessing on Rebekah* (24:60); mashal — the *steward's* rule; shamar/naqah — the oath's *condition/release*; natan — the land-*gift* and the *gifts*; **chesed — the *prayer* for God's steadfast love**, and **chesed+emet — the covenant-pair** (God's *unforsaken* loyal-faithfulness, recognised and required); yada — *knowing-by-sign*, *unrealized* (Rebekah), *discernment*; **charesh — the *first* "silence", the silent watchful discernment**; **lev — the *silent prayer* answered**; tov/ra + yakhol — *"cannot speak bad or good"* (powerless to object); qara/shaal — the *willing consent* ("I will go"); sane — the *first "hate"*; **nacham — grief *consoled*, and aheb the *comforting* love** (vs the surrendered love 22:2).
- **Whose interior:** the **human** interior *trusting God's leading* (Abraham, the servant), *discerning in prayer and silence*, *freely consenting* (Rebekah), and *grieving then comforted by love* (Isaac); and the **divine** interior *steadfast in love-and-faithfulness*, *leading providentially*.
- **Threads:** chesed (← 19:19 God's saving; 20:13 compromised; 21:23 reciprocal → here God's covenant loyalty, paired with emet); the heart's prayer (lev, ← the heart-motif); nacham (← 5:29 comfort-hoped, 6:6 God's grief → here consolation); aheb/love (← 22:2 surrendered → here comforting; the two loves); the willing "I will go" (← 12:4 Abraham's going); tov/ra (← 2:9,17 the tree of good-and-evil, now an idiom); providence/leading (the cycle's guidance motif).
- **Guarded against:** inventing seven blessings from the recurring barak or six givings from natan (recurring operations, distinctions named); flattening chesed+emet into one word (they are a *pair* — loyal-love *and* faithful-truth); merging the yada-senses (sign / unrealized / discernment); missing that charesh (silence) is a *discernment* operation; reading nacham's *consolation* as identical to God's *grief* (6:6) or the *hoped-comfort* (5:29) — same root, distinct senses; importing NT bride typology (Isaac/Rebekah) — the operations the chapter states.

---

## Gen 25:1-11 - the full death, the blessing passed (ABR-17)

# Genesis 25:1–11 — inner-being passage reading (ABR-17-abraham-death)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-abraham-v1-20260704`). Every span in its verse; individual + interactive operations; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the two `natan` (25:5, 25:6) treated distinctly.

---

## ABR-17-abraham-death · Genesis 25:1–11 · [the full death, the blessing passed] — the inheritance to the heir, the good old age fulfilled, and the promise carried on

**The passage.** "Abraham **gave** (natan) all he had to Isaac" (25:5); "to the sons of his concubines Abraham **gave** (natan) gifts, and while still **living** (chay) sent them away… eastward" (25:6); "the days of the years of Abraham's **life** (chayyim), 175 years, which he **lived** (chayah)" (25:7); "Abraham breathed his last and died in a **good** (tov) old age… and was gathered to his people" (25:8); "after Abraham's death, God **blessed** (barak) Isaac" (25:11).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **natan (give) #1 — *all* to the heir (25:5).** The finding is "Abraham **gave** (natan) all he had to Isaac" *(stated)*. The operation is the *inheritance* concentrated on the *covenant-heir* — the promised line secured in Isaac; the interior *settling its house* toward the promise *(inferred)*.
- **natan (give) #2 + chay — *gifts* to the rest, sent away (25:6).** The finding is "to the sons of his concubines Abraham **gave** (natan) **gifts**, and while still **living** (chay) sent them away… eastward, away from Isaac" *(stated)*. The gem is the *distinction*: Isaac receives *all* (the inheritance, 25:5); the others receive *gifts* and are *sent away* — the covenant-line *kept single*, the rest *provided for but separated*; and Abraham does this *while still living* (chay) — ordering his house *before* death *(inferred: natan #1 the inheritance vs natan #2 the parting-gifts; the line preserved)*.
- **chayyim + chayah — the *honoured* lifespan (25:7).** The finding is "the days of the years of Abraham's **life** (chayyim), 175 years, which he **lived** (chayah)" *(stated)*. The operation is the death-formula (← GEN-08) *dignifying* Abraham's life — the full count of his years *(inferred)*.
- **tov (good) — the *good, full, gathered* death (25:8).** The finding is "Abraham breathed his last and died in a **good** (tov) old age, an old man and full of years, and was **gathered to his people**" *(stated)*. The gem is *tov* naming the **fulfilled death**: a *good* old age, *full* of years, *gathered* — the exact promise of **15:15** ("you shall go to your fathers in *peace*, buried in a *good old age*") **kept**; the man of faith's life *completed and satisfied*. And "*gathered to his people*" (no span) hints at *continuity* — death as a *gathering*, not mere ceasing *(inferred: tov = the goodness of the completed life; the promised peaceful death fulfilled)*.
- **barak (blessed) — the blessing *passed to the heir* (25:11).** The finding is "after the death of Abraham, God **blessed** (barak) Isaac his son" *(stated)*. The gem is the *transmission*: the blessing (← 12:2) *does not die with Abraham* — God *blesses Isaac*, the covenant *continues* beyond the patriarch's death; and Isaac settles at *Beer-lahai-roi* (Hagar's well, El-Roi, 16:14) — a quiet echo of the God who sees *(inferred: barak passes to Isaac — the blessing outlives the man)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the house ordered toward the promise (natan 25:5–6):** Abraham *gives all* to Isaac and *gifts-and-sends* the rest — the covenant-line *kept single* and secure, the interior *settling its affairs* while still living.
2. **the fulfilled death (chayyim/chayah/tov 25:7–8):** Abraham dies *good, full, and gathered* — the promise of a *peaceful, good old age* (15:15) *kept*; the life of faith *completed and satisfied*, with a hint of *gathering* beyond death.
3. **the blessing outlives the man (barak 25:11):** God *blesses Isaac* — the blessing *transmitted*, the covenant *carried on*; the patriarch dies but the promise does not.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** natan — *all* to the heir (25:5) vs *gifts* to the rest, sent away (25:6); chayyim/chayah — the *honoured* lifespan; **tov — the *good, full, gathered* death** (the promise of 15:15 fulfilled); **barak — the blessing *passed to Isaac*** (the covenant outliving the man).
- **Whose interior:** the **human** interior *completing* its life in faith — ordering its house, dying *good and full and gathered*; and the **divine** interior *transmitting the blessing* to the next generation.
- **Threads:** tov-good-death (← 15:15 the promised peaceful old age, now *kept*); the death-formula (← GEN-08, now over Abraham); barak (← 12:2, now *passed to Isaac*); Beer-lahai-roi / El-Roi (← 16:14); "gathered to his people" (the continuity-hint → the patriarchs' gathering).
- **Guarded against:** merging the two natan (inheritance vs parting-gifts — the line-preservation is the point); flattening tov here into generic "good" (it names the *fulfilled, satisfied* death, keeping 15:15); over-reading "gathered to his people" (a *hint* of continuity, not a doctrine — read what the verse gives); importing later resurrection theology.

---

## Gen 25:12-18 - the promise to the outcast kept (ABR-18)

# Genesis 25:12–18 — inner-being passage reading (ABR-18-ishmael-line)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-abraham-v1-20260704`). Every span in its verse; distinctions kept. A genealogical unit — thin inner-being yield; the *finding is the promise-to-the-outcast kept*.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; the single non-T2 span (chayyim, 25:17) engaged.

---

## ABR-18-ishmael-line · Genesis 25:12–18 · [the promise to the outcast kept] — the twelve princes, and Ishmael gathered like his father

**The passage.** The generations of Ishmael — twelve sons, "twelve princes according to their tribes" (25:12–16); "these are the years of the **life** (chayyim) of Ishmael, 137 years; he breathed his last and died, and was gathered to his people" (25:17); his descendants "settled… over against all his kinsmen" (25:18).

### The operation

- **chayyim (life) — Ishmael's *honoured* death, the promise *fulfilled* (25:17).** The finding is "the years of the **life** (chayyim) of Ishmael, 137 years… he breathed his last and died, and was **gathered to his people**" *(stated)*. The gem is that this thin genealogy *records the promise kept*: **twelve princes** (25:16) fulfils God's word to Abraham — "I will make him a great nation… twelve princes" (17:20) — and to Hagar — "I will multiply your offspring… a great nation" (16:10; 21:18); and Ishmael dies "**gathered to his people**", the *same honour* given to Abraham (25:8, ABR-17). The outcast son, *heard and seen* by God (16:11,13; 21:17), is *blessed, multiplied, and gathered* — God's promise to the *cast-out* proves *as sure as* his promise to the heir *(inferred: the genealogy is the fulfilment; chayyim/gathered honours Ishmael as Abraham)*.
- **(25:18 — "over against all his kinsmen": no non-T2 span.)** The closing note that Ishmael's line settled "over against/in the presence of all his kinsmen" fulfils the word of 16:12 ("his hand against everyone… he shall dwell over against all his kinsmen") — read as context, the promise's *shape* kept *(no-span context)*.

### The web / note

The unit is a *bridge and a fulfilment*: it closes the Abraham cycle by showing that the promise to **Ishmael** — the *outcast* son — was *kept* (twelve princes, a great nation, an honoured death "gathered to his people", parallel to Abraham's). The *God who sees and hears the cast-out* (El-Roi, 16:13; "God hears", 16:11; 21:17) is *faithful to him too*. The covenant runs through *Isaac*, but the *blessing* reaches *Ishmael* — and the narrative *records both deaths in the same honoured terms*.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** chayyim — Ishmael's *honoured* lifespan and death ("gathered to his people", as Abraham, 25:8); the *promise to the outcast fulfilled* (twelve princes, ← 17:20; 16:10; 21:18); the *dwelling "over against his kinsmen"* (← 16:12, no-span).
- **Whose interior:** minimal — the passage is a *genealogical fulfilment*; its inner-being weight is the *faithfulness of God to the cast-out son*.
- **Threads:** the outcast heard/seen (← 16:11,13; 21:17); the promise to Hagar/Ishmael (← 16:10; 17:20; 21:18, now *kept*); "gathered to his people" (← 25:8 Abraham — the *same* honour); the two sons (Isaac the covenant-line, Ishmael blessed-and-kept).
- **Guarded against:** manufacturing inner-being operations from a genealogy (thin by nature; the finding is the *promise kept*, not a forced reading); over-reading the single chayyim beyond the honoured death it names; importing later Ishmael/Isaac typology.

---

## Genesis 25:19-28 - the interior established at birth: barren-prayer, womb-struggle, the oracle's inversion, two characters (JAC-01)

# Genesis 25:19–28 — inner-being passage reading (JAC-01-birth-oracle)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-jacob-v1-20260704`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; individual + interactive operations; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. The naming *love* (25:28, aheb) and the *heel-grasp* (25:26, no non-T2 span) read as scene-context, anchored by atar/darash/ratsats/qara.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the two qara namings (25:25 vs 25:26) treated distinctly.

---

## JAC-01-birth-oracle · Genesis 25:19–28 · [the interior established at birth] — the barren-prayer, the womb-struggle, the oracle that inverts the order, and the two opposite characters

**The passage.** Isaac "**prayed** (atar) to the LORD… because she was **barren**" (25:21); "the children **struggled together** (ratsats) within her… so she went to **inquire** (darash) of the LORD" (25:22); the oracle — "two nations… the one shall be **stronger** (ammits) than the other, the older shall **serve** (avad) the younger" (25:23); the firstborn red and hairy, "they **called** (qara) his name Esau" (25:25); the second gripping the heel, "his name was **called** (qara) Jacob" (25:26); "the boys grew up (**gadal**), Esau a **skillful** (yada) hunter… Jacob a **quiet** (tam) man" (25:27); "Isaac loved Esau… but Rebekah loved Jacob" (25:28).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **atar (prayed) — the intercession that answers barrenness (25:21).** The finding is "Isaac **prayed** (atar) to the LORD for his wife, because she was barren, and the LORD **granted his prayer**" *(stated)*. The operation is atar — *entreat / plead* — the interior turning to God against the closed womb (the same barrenness-motif that gripped Abraham's cycle, but here *met by prayer* not by the scheming of ABR-06). The prayer is *heard*; conception follows. The interior's first move in the cycle is **entreaty, not seizure** *(inferred: atar = the pleading that receives)*.
- **ratsats (struggled together) — the strife *in the womb* (25:22a).** The finding is "the children **struggled together** (ratsats) within her" *(stated)*. The gem is that ratsats — *crush / smash / oppress* — is a *violent* word: the twins do not merely stir, they *crush each other*; the rivalry that will run the whole cycle is **prenatal, bodily, already violent** — the interior's conflict shown before either child can choose it *(inferred: ratsats = the crushing strife, the rivalry innate)*.
- **darash (inquire) — the perplexed interior *seeking* God (25:22b).** The finding is "'why is this happening to me?' So she went to **inquire** (darash) of the LORD" *(stated)*. The operation is darash — *seek / consult* — Rebekah's *bewildered* interior ("why am I thus?") *turning to God for the meaning* of what her body is doing. The interior *seeks an oracle* rather than resolving the confusion herself — a receiving-posture like Isaac's prayer *(inferred: darash = the seeking that asks God to interpret)*.
- **ammits (stronger) + avad (serve) — the oracle that *inverts* the order (25:23).** The findings are "the one shall be **stronger** (ammits) than the other" and "the older shall **serve** (avad) the younger" *(both stated)*. Two operations: **ammits** — *be strong / mighty* — sets the twins as unequal *powers*; **avad** — *serve* — but the strength runs *backward*, the *elder serving the younger*, the natural birthright-order **overturned by decree** before either has acted. This is the cycle's engine stated at the outset: the blessing will run *against* nature/precedence — and the whole grasping/deceiving struggle to come is the human attempt to *secure by scheme* what the oracle has already *given*. (avad here = the servitude *decreed*; contrast the avad Jacob will *do* for Rachel, JAC-09.) *(inferred: ammits/avad = the God-decreed inversion of the elder/younger order)*.
- **qara (called Esau) — the naming off the *red/hairy* body (25:25).** The finding is "he came out red, all his body like a hairy cloak, so they **called** (qara) his name Esau" *(stated)*. The operation is qara — *call/name* — here the name read *off the visible body* (Esau ≈ hairy; red → Edom later). The naming fixes Esau as the *outward, bodily, hunter* man *(inferred: qara = the name that fixes the outward nature)*.
- **qara (called Jacob) — the naming off the *heel-grasp* (25:26).** The finding is "his hand holding Esau's **heel**, so his name was **called** (qara) Jacob" *(stated)*. *Distinct from 25:25:* here qara names *not a body-feature but an act* — the *grasping of the heel* (Jacob ≈ heel/supplanter). The name itself *encodes the grasping interior*: he is called "**heel-grabber**" from the womb. Where Esau is named for *what he looks like*, Jacob is named for *what he does* — **seizes** — the supplanter-interior *inscribed in the name* it will spend the cycle either enacting or being delivered from *(inferred: qara = the name that fixes the grasping act; the two namings distinguished — body vs act)*.
- **gadal (grew) — the boys *grow up* into their divergence (25:27a).** The finding is "when the boys **grew up** (gadal)" *(stated)*. The operation is gadal — *become great / grow* — the *maturing* into the two settled characters that follow; a plain growth-word here (against 26:13 where gadal will mean *become rich/great*), marking the passage from oracle to lived difference *(inferred: gadal = the growth into character)*.
- **yada (skillful) — Esau's *knowing* of the field/hunt (25:27b).** The finding is "Esau was a **skillful** (yada) hunter, a man of the field" *(stated)*. The gem is that *skillful* here is **yada — *to know*** — Esau's is a *knowing of the hunt*, a practical, outward, bodily *know-how*; the interior aimed *at the field and the game* (yada in its craft-sense, distinct from the covenant-knowing of God) *(inferred: yada = practical outward mastery)*.
- **tam (quiet) — Jacob's *complete/settled* interior (25:27c).** The finding is "Jacob was a **quiet** (tam) man, dwelling in tents" *(stated)*. The gem: *quiet* is **tam — *complete / blameless / whole*** — the very word for Noah "blameless" (6:9) and the demand on Abraham "be blameless" (17:1). Applied to *Jacob the heel-grabber* it is arrestingly *ambivalent*: "**tam**" = *settled, contained, at home* (over against Esau's roving) — yet the man so described *will deceive his father*. The passage sets the tension the cycle explores: the *tam*/settled man who must *become* what the word claims *(inferred: tam = the settled/whole interior, held in tension with Jacob's grasping)*.
- **(25:28 — the parental loves, no non-T2 span.)** Flagged: "Isaac **loved** (aheb) Esau because he ate of his game, but Rebekah **loved** Jacob" carries no flagged non-T2 span, but it is the scene's *pivot into division*: the parents' *split affections* — Isaac's love *appetite-driven* ("because he ate of his game"), Rebekah's love *un-reasoned* (simply "loved Jacob") — the household **divided along the same line as the oracle**, seeding the deception of ch 27. Read as context, anchored by the oracle (25:23) and the two namings *(no-span context; the divided parental love)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **barrenness answered by prayer (atar 25:21):** the cycle opens not with a scheme but with *entreaty* — Isaac prays, God grants; the receiving-posture set (contrast the seized promise of ABR-06).
2. **the innate rivalry → the seeking interior (ratsats 25:22a → darash 25:22b):** the *crushing* struggle in the womb drives Rebekah to *seek* God for meaning — conflict provokes *inquiry*, not self-resolution.
3. **the oracle inverts the order (ammits/avad 25:23):** the answer is that *strength runs backward* — elder serves younger; the blessing is *decreed against precedence*, and everything that follows (birthright bought, blessing stolen) is the *human scramble* to secure by grasping what is *already given by decree*.
4. **the two names fix the two interiors (qara 25:25 vs 25:26):** Esau named for his *body* (outward), Jacob for his *act* (grasping) — the supplanter *inscribed in his name*.
5. **grown into divergence, and a divided love (gadal/yada/tam 25:27 → aheb 25:28):** the boys mature into *outward-knowing hunter* vs *settled/whole tent-man*, and the parents' *split love* aligns with the oracle's split — the stage set for the grasp.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** atar (the *entreaty* that answers barrenness); ratsats (the *crushing*, prenatal rivalry); darash (the *seeking* of the perplexed interior); ammits/avad (the *oracle's inversion* — elder serves younger, the cycle's engine); qara ×2 *distinguished* (Esau named off the *body*, Jacob off the *heel-grasping act*); gadal (growth into character); yada (Esau's *outward craft-knowing*); tam (Jacob "quiet/**whole**" — held in tension with his grasping); the *divided parental love* (no-span context).
- **Whose interior:** the **human** interior *entreating* (Isaac), *seeking/bewildered* (Rebekah), and *innately rivalrous* (the twins); the **divine** interior *decreeing the inversion* (elder serves younger) — grace running against precedence.
- **Threads:** the supplanter-name (→ 27:36 "is he not rightly called Jacob? he has supplanted me twice"; → 32:28 the *re*-naming Israel); the *inverted order* (elder serves younger → the birthright bought JAC-02, the blessing stolen JAC-05); barrenness-answered (← Sarah, ABR; → Rachel, JAC-10 "God remembered Rachel"); tam ("blameless" ← Noah 6:9, Abraham 17:1 — now *ambivalently* of Jacob); the divided love (→ the ch-27 deception).
- **Guarded against:** reading Jacob's later transformation *back into* the birth-oracle (the text gives only the *name* and the *decree* here, not yet the man's change); softening ratsats into gentle "jostling" (the word is *crush*); flattening tam into mere "quiet/plain" when it is the loaded *whole/blameless* word (the tension is the finding); treating the two qara namings as one naming-operation (Esau off the body, Jacob off the act — distinct); importing Romans 9 ("Jacob I loved, Esau I hated") over the *domestic* divided-love the verse actually narrates — the operations shown, not the epistle.

---
