## Genesis 29:1-30 - the deceiver deceived: the well, the love that made years seem days, the younger-for-elder switch turned back on the supplanter (JAC-09)

# Genesis 29:1–30 — inner-being passage reading (JAC-09-rachel-served-deceived)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-jacob-v1-20260704`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. Laban's "we do not give the younger before the firstborn" (29:26, no non-T2 span) reads as the scene's *ironic hinge*, anchored by ramah/avad.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the 6 avad and 3 natan each treated distinctly.

---

## JAC-09-rachel-served-deceived · Genesis 29:1–30 · [the deceiver deceived] — the well, the love that made years seem days, and the younger-for-elder switch turned back on the supplanter

**The passage.** Jacob asks "do you **know** (yada) Laban?… is it **well** (shalom)?" (29:5–6); "we **cannot** (yakhol) [roll the stone] until all are gathered" (29:8); Jacob rolls it, kissed Rachel and **wept** (bakhah) aloud (29:11); Laban **heard** (shama) the **news** (shema), ran to **meet** (qara) him (29:13), "you are my bone and my **flesh** (basar)" (29:14); "should you **serve** (avad) me for nothing?" (29:15); "I will **serve** (avad) seven years for Rachel" (29:18); "better (tov) I **give** (natan) her to you" (29:19); "Jacob **served** (avad) seven years… seemed a few days for the **love** (ahavah) he had" (29:20); Laban **gave** (natan) Zilpah to Leah (29:24); "it was Leah! Did I not **serve** (avad) for Rachel? Why have you **deceived** (ramah) me?" (29:25); "**serving** (avad) another seven years… **service** (avodah)" (29:27); **gave** (natan) Bilhah to Rachel (29:29); "**served** (avad) another seven years" (29:30).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **yada (know) — the *acquaintance* inquiry (29:5).** "do you **know** (yada) Laban the son of Nahor?" *(stated)* — yada in the *acquaintance* sense: Jacob *locating his kin*; a practical knowing (contrast the covenant-knowing of God) — the interior *seeking its way toward the family* *(inferred: yada = practical acquaintance-knowing)*.
- **shalom (well) — the *well-being* inquiry (29:6).** "is it **well** (shalom) with him?" *(stated)* — shalom in the *well-being* register: the customary *is-he-at-peace* question; the interior's *courteous concern* for the kinsman's welfare (distinct from the *homecoming-peace* of 28:21) *(inferred: shalom = the well-being asked after)*.
- **yakhol (cannot) — the shepherds' *constraint* (29:8).** "we **cannot** (yakhol) until all the flocks are gathered and the stone rolled" *(stated)* — yakhol in the *negated* mode: the *inability/constraint* of custom (the great stone, the waiting) — a foil to Jacob, who *singlehandedly rolls the stone* the moment he sees Rachel; the interior's *energy for love* set against the others' *cannot* *(inferred: yakhol = the constraint Jacob's love overrides)*.
- **bakhah (wept) — the fugitive's *overflow* at meeting Rachel (29:11).** "Jacob kissed Rachel and **wept** (bakhah) aloud" *(stated)* — bakhah, *weep*: the gem is *these* tears — not grief but *overwhelmed relief and love*; the *fleeing, friendless* deceiver, arriving at his mother's kin and *first sight of Rachel*, *breaks into weeping* — the interior *unguarded*, love and homecoming-relief flooding out *(inferred: bakhah = the tears of relief and love at the journey's welcome)*.
- **shama (heard) + shema (news) + qara (meet) — Laban's *eager welcome* (29:13).** "as soon as Laban **heard** (shama) the **news** (shema)… he ran to **meet** (qara) him" *(stated)*. Three spans: **shama** — Laban *hears*; **shema** — the *report* itself; **qara** — the *running to encounter*. The interior's *warm welcome* of the kinsman (echoing Rebekah's household hospitality, 24) — though Laban's eagerness will prove *self-interested* *(inferred: shama/shema/qara = the eager hearing-and-running welcome)*.
- **basar (flesh) — the *kinship bond* named (29:14).** "surely you are my bone and my **flesh** (basar)!" *(stated)* — basar, *flesh*: Laban *claims the blood-tie* (← the one-flesh 2:23–24, here kin-flesh) — the bond that *should* protect Jacob but will be *exploited* for cheap labour; the interior's kinship-claim *(inferred: basar = the flesh-kinship invoked, soon exploited)*.
- **avad (serve me for nothing?) — service framed as *owed* (29:15).** "because you are my kinsman, should you **serve** (avad) me for nothing?" *(stated)* — the *first* avad: Laban *frames the coming service* as something that *ought to be waged* — but the very framing *sets up the bargain* he will manipulate; service *monetised* from the start *(inferred: avad = service framed as owed wages — the bargain opened)*.
- **avad (I will serve seven years) — service *freely offered for love* (29:18).** *Distinct from 29:15:* "I will **serve** (avad) seven years for your younger daughter Rachel" *(stated)* — the gem: Jacob *offers* the service, *and names Rachel "the younger"* — the interior *willingly binding itself to long labour for love*; the grasper, for once, *gives* rather than seizes — *seven years* pledged for Rachel *(inferred: avad = the long service freely offered for love)*.
- **tov (better) + natan (give her) — Laban's *promise to give Rachel* (29:19).** "it is **better** (tov) that I **give** (natan) her to you than to another man" *(stated)*. **tov** — Laban judges it *good/preferable*; **natan (1st)** — the *promise to give Rachel* — which he *will break*. The interior's *fair-seeming word* that masks the coming deceit *(inferred: tov/natan = the plausible promise to give Rachel, later betrayed)*.
- **avad (served) + ahavah (love) — the *service transfigured by love* (29:20).** *Distinct from 29:15,18:* "Jacob **served** (avad) seven years… they seemed but a few days for the **love** (ahavah) he had for her" *(stated)*. **avad** — the *seven years actually served*; **ahavah** — the gem: **love** *compresses time* — the long labour *felt light*; the interior *so given to love* that *years pass as days*. The one place Jacob's grasping self is *wholly generous and patient* — love *transfigures* the service *(inferred: avad/ahavah = the long service made light by love)*.
- **natan (gave Zilpah) — the *maid given with the wrong bride* (29:24).** *Distinct from 29:19:* "Laban **gave** (natan) Zilpah to his daughter Leah as servant" *(stated)* — natan, *give*: a *quiet parenthetical* — the maid *given with Leah* (the substituted bride) — the narrator *lets the giving of Zilpah mark that it is Leah, not Rachel, being delivered*; the deception *furnished with its trappings* *(inferred: natan = the maid given, marking the wrong bride delivered)*.
- **avad (did I not serve for Rachel?) + ramah (deceived) — the *deceiver deceived* (29:25).** "in the morning, behold, it was Leah!… did I not **serve** (avad) for Rachel? Why have you **deceived** (ramah) me?" *(stated)*. **avad** — the *service invoked as grievance* (I served for *Rachel*!); **ramah** — the gem of the whole passage: **ramah — *deceive/beguile*** — the man who *deceived his blind father in the dark, exploiting senses* (27) is now *deceived in the dark by a substituted sibling*; his own outrage — "why have you **deceived** me?" — *echoes the very wrong he did*. The interior *reaps its own method*; the deceiver *deceived* *(inferred: avad/ramah = the betrayed service and the deception turned back on the deceiver)*.
- **(29:26 — "we do not give the younger before the firstborn", no non-T2 span.)** Flagged: Laban's justification carries no flagged span, but it is the *ironic hinge*: the *younger-for-elder switch* — the very *inversion Jacob seized* (birthright/blessing of the *firstborn*, 25:31; 27:19) — is now *turned against him by an appeal to firstborn-right*. The interior that *overturned the elder/younger order* is *bound by it*. Read as context, anchored by ramah/avad *(no-span context; the inversion reversed onto the supplanter)*.
- **avad (serving) + avodah (service) — the *doubled price* (29:27).** *Distinct from prior avad:* "**serve** (avad) me another seven years… in return for **service** (avodah)" *(stated)*. **avad** — the *second* seven-year term *imposed*; **avodah** — the *service* as the *price* of Rachel. The gem: the deception *costs Jacob another seven years* — the grasper made to *pay double* for what he loves *(inferred: avad/avodah = the doubled service exacted by the deceiver)*.
- **natan (gave Bilhah) — the *maid given with the right bride* (29:29).** *Distinct from 29:19,24:* "Laban **gave** (natan) Bilhah to his daughter Rachel as servant" *(stated)* — natan, *give*: the *parallel parenthetical* to 29:24, now marking *Rachel* delivered (the true bride at last) — the giving that *completes the doubled bargain* *(inferred: natan = the maid given, marking the right bride finally delivered)*.
- **avad (served another seven) — the *service resumed for Rachel* (29:30).** *Distinct — the final avad:* "he loved Rachel more than Leah, and **served** (avad) Laban another seven years" *(stated)* — the *closing* service: the interior *pays on*, love still driving the labour, but now under a *doubled yoke* — and the seed of the wives' rivalry ("loved Rachel more than Leah") *sown* *(inferred: avad = the resumed service under the doubled price)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **arrival, energy, and unguarded tears (yada/shalom 29:5–6 → yakhol 29:8 → bakhah 29:11):** the fugitive *locates his kin*, *singlehandedly rolls the stone* the others *cannot*, and *weeps* at meeting Rachel — the interior *unguarded*, love and relief overflowing.
2. **welcome and the monetised bond (shama/shema/qara 29:13 → basar 29:14 → avad 29:15):** Laban *runs to welcome* and *claims the flesh-kinship* — then *frames the service as waged*, opening the bargain the blood-tie will *exploit*.
3. **love binds itself to long service (avad 29:18 → tov/natan 29:19 → avad/ahavah 29:20):** Jacob *freely offers seven years for love*; Laban *promises Rachel*; and **love makes the seven years seem days** — the grasper *wholly generous* here.
4. **the deceiver deceived (natan-Zilpah 29:24 → avad/ramah 29:25 → [29:26 the inversion reversed] → avad/avodah 29:27 → natan-Bilhah 29:29 → avad 29:30):** in the dark, *Leah is substituted*; Jacob *cries the very word of his own crime* — "why have you **deceived** me?" — and Laban's *"we do not give the younger before the firstborn"* turns Jacob's *own inversion* against him. The supplanter *reaps his method*, *pays double*, and *serves on* — the interior *taught by its own deceit received back*.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** yada (*acquaintance*-knowing); shalom (*well-being* asked); yakhol (the *constraint* love overrides); **bakhah (the fugitive's *tears of relief and love*, not grief)**; shama/shema/qara (the *eager welcome*); basar (the *flesh-kinship* soon exploited); avad ×6 *distinguished* (29:15 service *framed as waged* / 29:18 *freely offered* for love / 29:20 *transfigured by love* — years as days / 29:25 *invoked as grievance* betrayed / 29:27 the *doubled* term imposed / 29:30 *resumed* under the doubled yoke) + avodah (the *service as price*); natan ×3 (29:19 the *promise* of Rachel, broken / 29:24 the maid marking the *wrong* bride / 29:29 the maid marking the *right* bride); tov (Laban's *plausible* word); **ahavah (the *love* that compresses time — Jacob's one unguarded generosity)**; **ramah (the *deceiver deceived*)**.
- **Whose interior:** the **human** interior *unguarded in love* (Jacob's tears, the years-as-days) and *made to reap its own deceit* (deceived in the dark, paying double); the *self-interested welcomer* (Laban — kinship claimed, then exploited). No divine word — the *moral symmetry* (deceiver deceived) works *through the events*.
- **Threads:** *the deceiver deceived* (ramah 29:25 ← Jacob's mirmah against Isaac 27:35; the dark/senses used against the user of the dark); *the inversion reversed* (29:26 "the younger before the firstborn" ← Jacob's seizure of the *firstborn's* right 25:31, 27:19); love as the interior's one generosity (ahavah 29:20 → the wives' rivalry it seeds, "loved Rachel more" 29:30 → JAC-10); service (avad → the long labour theme, → the wage-dispute JAC-11, the 20-years tally 31:41); kinship exploited (basar 29:14 → Laban's changed wages 31:7).
- **Guarded against:** collapsing the six avad or three natan into single serve/give operations (waged / offered / transfigured / betrayed / doubled / resumed; and the three natan mark *promise* vs *wrong bride* vs *right bride* — distinct); reading bakhah as grief when the context is *love and relief*; missing the *moral symmetry* by treating the Leah-substitution as mere plot (the *deceiver deceived*, and the *inversion turned back*, is the finding); importing a "Jacob's discipline/sanctification" theology over what the text *shows* — the deceit *received back* and the *doubled service*, read off ramah and the doubled avad.

---

## Genesis 29:31-30:24 - the rivalry read through the birth-namings: two women's interiors in a childbearing contest, God seeing the hated and hearing the barren (JAC-10)

# Genesis 29:31–30:24 — inner-being passage reading (JAC-10-wives-rivalry-sons)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-jacob-v1-20260704`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. **Each birth-naming is a distinct interior cry — never lumped.** The mandrakes-bargain speech (30:15, no non-T2 span) reads as scene-context, anchored by natan/qara.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the 12 qara-namings, 6 natan, 4 shama, 2 sane each treated distinctly.

---

## JAC-10-wives-rivalry-sons · Genesis 29:31–30:24 · [the rivalry read through the birth-namings] — two women's interiors locked in a childbearing contest, each cry a distinct state, God seeing the hated and hearing the barren

**The passage.** "The LORD saw Leah was **hated** (sane), opened her womb" (29:31); Reuben — "the LORD looked on my **affliction** (oni)" (29:32); Simeon — "the LORD **heard** (shama) I am **hated** (sane), **given** (natan) me this" (29:33); Levi — "my husband attached… three sons" (29:34); Judah — "I will **praise** (yadah) the LORD" (29:35); Rachel **envied** (qana), "give me children or I die!" (30:1); Jacob's anger **kindled** (charah) (30:2); she **gave** (natan) Bilhah (30:4); Dan — "God **judged** (din) me, **heard** (shama), **given** (natan) a son" (30:6); Naphtali — "I have wrestled and **prevailed** (yakhol)" (30:8); Leah **gave** (natan) Zilpah (30:9); Gad — "good fortune!" (30:11); Asher — "happy am I!" (30:13); the mandrakes — "**give** (natan) me some" (30:14); Leah went to **meet** (qara) him, "I have hired you" (30:16); God **listened** (shama) to Leah (30:17); Issachar — "God **given** (natan) my wages" (30:18); Zebulun — "a **good** (tov) endowment… honor me" (30:20); Dinah **called** (qara) (30:21); "God **remembered** (zakhar) Rachel, **listened** (shama)" (30:22); "taken away my **reproach** (cherpah)" (30:23); Joseph — "may the LORD add another" (30:24).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **sane (hated) — the *unloved* wife *seen* by God (29:31).** "the LORD **saw** that Leah was **hated** (sane), and opened her womb" *(stated)* — sane, *hated/unloved*: the gem is *God's regard for the unloved* — the *rejected* wife (the one given by deceit, less loved than Rachel, 29:30) is *seen and answered with fruitfulness*; the divine interior *takes the side of the hated* *(inferred: sane = the unloved state God regards and answers)*.
- **oni (affliction) + qara (Reuben) — the *affliction seen*, love hoped (29:32).** "the LORD looked on my **affliction** (oni)… now my husband will love me… **called** (qara) Reuben" *(stated)*. **oni** — *affliction/misery*: Leah names her *unloved suffering*; **qara (Reuben ≈ "see, a son")** — the naming *reads God's seeing into the child* and *voices the ache for love*. The interior: *affliction acknowledged, love craved* *(inferred: oni/qara = the affliction seen and the husband's love hoped for)*.
- **sane (hated) + shama (heard) + natan (given) + qara (Simeon) — being *hated*, now *heard* (29:33).** *sane distinct from 29:31:* here Leah *herself names* her hatedness ("the LORD **heard** (shama) that I am **hated** (sane)"). **shama** — God *hears* the unloved; **natan** — the son *given* as answer; **qara (Simeon ≈ "heard")**. The interior: *the hated one knows herself heard* — the second cry *(inferred: sane/shama/natan/qara = the hated wife hearing herself answered)*.
- **qara (Levi) — the *longing for attachment* (29:34).** "now my husband will be **attached** to me… three sons… **called** (qara) Levi" *(stated)* — qara (Levi ≈ "attached/joined"): the *third* cry names the *ache for the husband's attachment* — not love (Reuben), not being-heard (Simeon), but *bonding*; the interior *counting sons as leverage for closeness* *(inferred: qara = the naming that voices the longing to be joined)*.
- **yadah (praise) + qara (Judah) — the *turn from craving to praise* (29:35).** "this time I will **praise** (yadah) the LORD… **called** (qara) Judah; then she ceased bearing" *(stated)*. The gem: **yadah — *give thanks/praise*** — Leah's *fourth* cry *breaks the pattern* — no longer *"now my husband will…"* but *praise of God*; the interior *moves from grasping for love to thanksgiving* (qara, Judah ≈ "praise") — and *then rests* ("ceased bearing"). The unloved wife *finds her centre shifted to God* *(inferred: yadah/qara = the turn from love-craving to praise)*.
- **qana (envied) — Rachel's *envy* and desperation (30:1).** "Rachel **envied** (qana) her sister… 'give me children, or I shall die!'" *(stated)* — qana, *be jealous/envious* (← the Philistines 26:14): the *loved-but-barren* wife *consumed by envy* of the *unloved-but-fruitful*; the interior *at the extremity* — children-or-death; envy *turned self-destructive* *(inferred: qana = the barren wife's consuming envy)*.
- **charah (kindled) — Jacob's *anger*, deflecting to God (30:2).** "Jacob's anger was **kindled** (charah)… 'am I in the place of God, who has withheld?'" *(stated)* — charah, *burn/be incensed*: the husband's *flare of anger* at Rachel's demand — and his *pointing to God* as the withholder; the interior *refuses the god-role* but *in anger*, not comfort *(inferred: charah = the kindled anger that deflects the demand to God)*.
- **natan (gave Bilhah) — the *surrogate given* to win by proxy (30:4).** *natan distinct from the God-gives:* "she **gave** (natan) him Bilhah as a wife" *(stated)* — natan, *give*: Rachel *gives her maid* to *bear on her behalf* — the interior *seizing motherhood by proxy* (the Hagar-scheme again, ← 16:2), envy *acting* *(inferred: natan = the maid given to secure children by proxy)*.
- **din (judged) + shama (heard) + natan (given) + qara (Dan) — *vindication* claimed (30:6).** "God has **judged** (din) me, **heard** (shama) my voice, **given** (natan) a son… **called** (qara) Dan" *(stated)*. **din** — *judge/vindicate*: Rachel reads the surrogate-son as *God's verdict in her favour*; **shama** — *heard* (distinct from 29:33: now *Rachel* heard); **natan** — the son *given*; **qara (Dan ≈ "judged")**. The interior: *envy re-framed as vindication* *(inferred: din/shama/natan/qara = the barren wife claiming God's verdict for her)*.
- **yakhol (prevailed) + qara (Naphtali) — the *sister-wrestling* named (30:8).** "with mighty wrestlings I have wrestled with my sister and have **prevailed** (yakhol)… **called** (qara) Naphtali" *(stated)*. The gem: **yakhol — *be able / prevail*** — Rachel *names the rivalry itself* as a *wrestling with her sister* in which she has *prevailed*; the interior *openly frames the contest as a struggle-to-overcome*. (Note the word: *wrestled-and-prevailed* — the very verbs of Jacob at Peniel, 32:28 — the family's *struggle-to-prevail* motif in the women too.) *(inferred: yakhol/qara = the sister-rivalry named as a prevailing wrestle)*.
- **natan (gave Zilpah) — Leah's *counter-surrogate* (30:9).** *natan distinct from 30:4:* "she took Zilpah and **gave** (natan) her to Jacob as a wife" *(stated)* — Leah, *ceased bearing*, *answers Rachel's proxy with her own* — the contest *escalates by mirror-move*; the interior *matching seizure with seizure* *(inferred: natan = the counter-maid given, escalating the contest)*.
- **qara (Gad) — *fortune* acclaimed (30:11).** "'Good fortune has come!'… **called** (qara) Gad" *(stated)* — qara (Gad ≈ "fortune/troop"): Leah's cry *reads luck/fortune* into the proxy-son — the interior *celebrating a turn of fortune* (a different register from the God-claims — here *fortune*) *(inferred: qara = the naming that acclaims good fortune)*.
- **qara (Asher) — *happiness* and others' esteem (30:13).** "'Happy am I! women have called me happy'… **called** (qara) Asher" *(stated)* — qara (Asher ≈ "happy"): the interior *basks in happiness and others' regard* — the naming voices *social vindication* (women will call me happy), distinct from Gad's fortune *(inferred: qara = the naming that claims happiness and esteem)*.
- **natan (give mandrakes) — the *bargained fertility-charm* (30:14).** *natan distinct from the son-gives:* "'please **give** (natan) me some of your son's mandrakes'" *(stated)* — natan, *give*: Rachel *asks for the mandrakes* (a fertility-plant) — the interior *reaching for a natural means* to conceive; the request that *opens the husband-trade* *(inferred: natan = the mandrakes requested as a fertility-means)*.
- **qara (meet) — the *husband hired* for a night (30:16).** "Leah went out to **meet** (qara) him: 'you must come in to me, for I have **hired** you with the mandrakes'" *(stated)* — qara in the *encounter/meet* sense (distinct from all the naming-qara): Leah *goes out to claim the husband she has bartered for*; the interior — the husband *traded between the wives like a commodity*; intimacy *transacted* *(inferred: qara = the going-out to claim the bartered husband)*.
- **shama (listened) — God *hears Leah* again (30:17).** *shama distinct from 29:33, 30:6:* "God **listened** (shama) to Leah, and she conceived" *(stated)* — shama, *hear*: God *hears the unloved wife* once more — the divine *hearing* persists *beneath* the human bartering; the interior *answered by God, not by the mandrakes-scheme* *(inferred: shama = God's continued hearing of Leah)*.
- **natan (given wages) + qara (Issachar) — *reward for the surrogate* claimed (30:18).** *natan distinct again:* "God has **given** (natan) my **wages** because I gave my servant… **called** (qara) Issachar" *(stated)*. **natan** — God *gives wages*; **qara (Issachar ≈ "hire/wages")**: the gem is Leah's *hire-theology* — she reads the son as *payment for having given her maid* — the interior *casting God's gift as earned wages* (transactional, like Jacob's own bargaining, 28:20) *(inferred: natan/qara = the son read as earned wages)*.
- **tov (good) + qara (Zebulun) — the *longing for honor* (30:20).** "God has endowed me a **good** (tov) endowment; now my husband will **honor** me, six sons… **called** (qara) Zebulun" *(stated)*. **tov** — the *good* gift; **qara (Zebulun ≈ "honor/dwell")**: the interior *still craving the husband's honor* after six sons — the ache for Jacob's regard *persists* under the God-thanks; love-longing *never fully quieted* *(inferred: tov/qara = the good gift and the persistent longing for the husband's honor)*.
- **qara (Dinah) — the *daughter named without a cry* (30:21).** "she bore a daughter and **called** (qara) her name Dinah" *(stated)* — qara, *name*: the *only naming with no stated interior reason* — the daughter *simply named*; a *bare* naming (the narrator gives no cry) — noted distinctly *for its silence* (and Dinah's story comes in JAC-17) *(inferred: qara = the bare naming, no interior reason given)*.
- **zakhar (remembered) + shama (listened) — God *remembers* the barren Rachel (30:22).** "God **remembered** (zakhar) Rachel, and God **listened** (shama) to her, and opened her womb" *(stated)*. **zakhar** — *remember* (← "God remembered Noah", 8:1): the gem — the *barren, envying* Rachel is *remembered by God*; **shama** — *heard* (distinct: now Rachel *at last* heard directly, not by proxy). The interior *answered not by envy or mandrakes but by God's remembering* *(inferred: zakhar/shama = God remembering and hearing the barren wife)*.
- **cherpah (reproach) — the *reproach removed* (30:23).** "God has taken away my **reproach** (cherpah)" *(stated)* — cherpah, *reproach/disgrace*: the gem is *what barrenness was to her* — a *reproach*; its removal is the interior's *deepest relief* — the shame of childlessness *lifted* *(inferred: cherpah = the reproach of barrenness, now taken away)*.
- **qara (Joseph) — the naming that *still asks for more* (30:24).** "**called** (qara) him Joseph, saying 'may the LORD **add** to me another son!'" *(stated)* — qara (Joseph ≈ "may he add"): the gem — even *at the joy of the first son*, Rachel's cry is *"add another"* — the interior *satisfied and still reaching*; desire *never at rest* *(inferred: qara = the naming that rejoices and still asks for more)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **God sees the unloved (sane 29:31 → oni/qara Reuben 29:32 → sane/shama/natan/qara Simeon 29:33 → qara Levi 29:34):** the *hated* wife is *seen*, *heard*, and *made fruitful* — her first three cries *ache for love, being-heard, and attachment*, each name a distinct wound.
2. **the turn to praise (yadah/qara Judah 29:35):** Leah's fourth cry *breaks to thanksgiving* — from *"now my husband will…"* to *"I will praise the LORD"* — and *rests*; the interior's centre *shifted to God*.
3. **envy acts, then claims vindication (qana 30:1 → charah 30:2 → natan-Bilhah 30:4 → din/shama/natan/qara Dan 30:6 → yakhol/qara Naphtali 30:8):** the *barren, loved* wife *envies to the point of death-wish*, *seizes motherhood by proxy*, and *reads it as God's verdict* and *a wrestling-prevailed over her sister* — envy *re-narrated as triumph*.
4. **the contest escalates by mirror-moves (natan-Zilpah 30:9 → qara Gad 30:11 → qara Asher 30:13 → natan-mandrakes 30:14 → qara-meet 30:16 → shama 30:17 → natan/qara Issachar 30:18 → tov/qara Zebulun 30:20 → qara Dinah 30:21):** Leah *counters with her own maid*, acclaims *fortune* and *happiness*, the *husband is bartered* for mandrakes, God *keeps hearing Leah*, who reads sons as *earned wages* and still *craves honor* — the rivalry a *ledger of names*, each a distinct claim.
5. **God remembers the barren (zakhar/shama 30:22 → cherpah 30:23 → qara Joseph 30:24):** at last Rachel is *remembered and heard*, her *reproach lifted* — yet her joy-cry *still asks "add another"*: the interior *answered, relieved, and still reaching*.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct — each a separate cry):** the 12 birth-namings (qara): Reuben *affliction-seen/love-craved*, Simeon *hated-but-heard*, Levi *longing-for-attachment*, Judah *turn-to-praise*, Dan *vindication-claimed*, Naphtali *sister-wrestle-prevailed*, Gad *fortune*, Asher *happiness/esteem*, Issachar *son-as-wages*, Zebulun *longing-for-honor*, Dinah *bare/silent naming*, Joseph *joy-that-still-asks-more*; plus qara-meet (30:16, the *bartered husband claimed*). sane ×2 (God *sees* the hated 29:31 / Leah *names* herself hated 29:33); natan ×6 (God-*given* sons 29:33, 30:6, 30:18 / *maids* given 30:4, 30:9 / *mandrakes* requested 30:14); shama ×4 (heard-I-am-hated / heard-my-voice-Dan / listened-to-Leah / listened-to-Rachel); oni (*affliction*); yadah (*praise* — the turn); qana (*consuming envy*); charah (Jacob's *deflecting anger*); din (*vindication*); yakhol (*prevailing* — the Peniel-word in the women); tov (the *good* gift under persistent love-longing); zakhar (God *remembering* the barren); cherpah (the *reproach* of barrenness lifted).
- **Whose interior:** the **human** interiors of *two rival women* — the *unloved craving love then turning to praise* (Leah) and the *loved-but-barren consumed by envy then remembered* (Rachel) — and the *husband bartered and angry* (Jacob); the **divine** interior *seeing the hated, hearing the unloved, remembering the barren* — grace running *beneath* the rivalry, on the side of the *unregarded*.
- **Threads:** God's regard for the unregarded (sane 29:31 / zakhar 30:22 ← El-Roi sees Hagar 16:13, God hears Ishmael 21:17); the surrogate-scheme (natan-Bilhah 30:4 ← Sarai/Hagar 16:2); *wrestle-and-prevail* (yakhol 30:8 → Jacob at Peniel 32:28 — the family struggle-motif); the turn to praise (Judah, yadah 29:35 → the tribe of praise/kingship); transactional God-reading (Issachar "wages" 30:18 ← Jacob's vow 28:20 — the family's bargaining habit); Joseph/Dinah (→ JAC-17 Dinah; the Joseph cycle beyond Genesis-Jacob).
- **Guarded against:** **lumping the birth-namings** — the single strongest temptation here; each of the 12 qara is a *distinct interior cry* (I read each off its own stated reason, never "the naming of the sons" as one operation); collapsing the 6 natan or 4 shama (God-gift vs maid-giving vs mandrakes; and four *distinct* hearings); reading Leah's Judah-praise as the whole arc when her later Zebulun-cry still *craves honor* (the love-longing *persists* — I kept both); importing tribal/Messianic significance (Judah→David→Christ) over the *domestic interior cries* the verses give; treating Dinah's silent naming as an oversight rather than *noting the silence* itself.

---

## Genesis 30:25-43 - two schemers and the blessing that works through the cunning: the wage-bargain, honesty invoked, the counter-tricks, Jacob's prospering (JAC-11)

# Genesis 30:25–43 — inner-being passage reading (JAC-11-flocks-wages)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-jacob-v1-20260704`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. The peeled-sticks breeding scheme (30:37–42, no non-T2 span) reads as scene-context, anchored by tsedaqah/sur/rov.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the 2 natan, 2 yada, 2 avad, 2 barakh, 2 sur each treated distinctly.

---

## JAC-11-flocks-wages · Genesis 30:25–43 · [two schemers, and the blessing that works through the cunning] — the wage-bargain, honesty invoked, the counter-tricks, and Jacob's prospering

**The passage.** After Joseph's birth Jacob asks leave: "**Give** (natan) me my wives and children for whom I **served** (avad)… you **know** (yada) the **service** (avodah) I gave" (30:26); Laban — "if I have found **favor** (chen)… I have learned the LORD has **blessed** (barakh) me because of you" (30:27); "you **know** (yada) how I **served** (avad)" (30:29); "the LORD has **blessed** (barakh) you wherever I turned; it **increased abundantly** (rov)" (30:30); "what shall I **give** (natan)? … I will pasture and **keep** (shamar)" (30:31); "**removing** (sur) every speckled… my wages" (30:32); "my **honesty** (tsedaqah) will answer for me" (30:33); "Laban **removed** (sur) the striped… gave them to his sons" (30:35); the peeled sticks, the selective breeding, "the man **increased greatly**" (30:43).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **natan (Give me my wives) — the *claim to depart with his own* (30:26a).** "**Give** (natan) me my wives and children for whom I served" *(stated)* — natan, *give*: Jacob *asks for what is his by his labour* — the interior *claiming its earned family*; the request that opens the reckoning *(inferred: natan = the claim to leave with his own)*.
- **yada (you know) + avad (served) + avodah (service) — the *labour invoked as ground* (30:26b).** "you **know** (yada) the **service** (avodah) I have **served** (avad) you" *(stated)*. **yada** — Jacob *appeals to Laban's knowledge*; **avad**/**avodah** — the *service rendered* named as the *basis of the claim*. The interior *grounds its right in the labour done* (the fourteen years, ← JAC-09) *(inferred: yada/avad/avodah = the service invoked as the ground of the claim)*.
- **chen (favor) — Laban's *courteous, self-interested opener* (30:27a).** "if I have found **favor** (chen) in your sight" *(stated)* — chen, *favor/grace*: Laban *seeks Jacob's goodwill* — but to *keep* him, not release him; the interior's *ingratiating* move that precedes the counter-bargain *(inferred: chen = the favor sought to retain the profitable son-in-law)*.
- **barakh (blessed me because of you) — Laban's *admission* of the blessing-conduit (30:27b).** "I have learned by divination that the LORD has **blessed** (barakh) me because of you" *(stated)* — the gem: **barakh** — Laban *confesses Jacob is the channel of God's blessing* (the Abrahamic "in you… blessed", ← 12:3; 26:24 — now *even the exploiter admits it*) — though he reads it *superstitiously* ("by divination"). The interior *acknowledges the blessing it profits from* *(inferred: barakh = the blessing-conduit admitted by the exploiter)*.
- **yada (you know) + avad (served) — the *service pressed again* (30:29).** *yada/avad distinct from 30:26:* "you yourself **know** (yada) how I **served** (avad) you, how your livestock fared" *(stated)* — here yada is *of the service's quality/result* (the flocks' flourishing under Jacob), not merely its existence; the interior *presses the proof of its worth* *(inferred: yada/avad = the proven quality of the service pressed)*.
- **rov (abundantly) + barakh (blessed you) — Jacob's *assertion* of the blessing-conduit (30:30).** *barakh distinct from 30:27:* "it **increased abundantly** (rov), the LORD has **blessed** (barakh) you wherever I turned" *(stated)*. **rov** — *abundance*: the flocks *multiplied greatly*; **barakh** — where Laban *admitted* the conduit (30:27), Jacob now *asserts* it — "blessed *wherever I turned*". The interior *claims its own role in the other's prosperity* — pressing toward "when shall I provide for my own?" *(inferred: rov/barakh = the abundance and the conduit-role now asserted by Jacob)*.
- **natan (what shall I give / give me nothing) — the *wage refused* for a scheme (30:31).** *natan distinct from 30:26:* "'what shall I **give** (natan)?' 'You shall not **give** (natan) me anything'" *(stated)* — natan, *give*: Jacob *refuses a fixed wage* and *proposes the speckled-scheme* instead; the interior *declines the straightforward payment* for a *self-selected*, cunning arrangement *(inferred: natan = the fixed wage refused in favour of the scheme)*.
- **shamar (keep) — the *continued keeping* offered (30:31b).** "I will again pasture your flock and **keep** (shamar) it" *(stated)* — shamar, *keep/guard*: Jacob *offers to go on tending* — the service *sustained* as the frame for the wage-scheme *(inferred: shamar = the continued flock-keeping offered)*.
- **sur (removing) — Jacob's *self-selected wage* proposed (30:32).** "let me pass through, **removing** (sur) every speckled and spotted… they shall be my wages" *(stated)* — sur, *turn aside/remove*: the interior *proposes to take* the *odd-coloured* animals — an ostensibly *modest* wage (the minority colours) that his cunning will *turn into wealth* *(inferred: sur = the odd-coloured animals proposed as wage)*.
- **tsedaqah (honesty) — *righteousness invoked* by the schemer (30:33).** "so my **honesty** (tsedaqah) will answer for me later" *(stated)* — the gem: **tsedaqah — *righteousness/honesty*** — Jacob *appeals to his own integrity* as the *test* (any non-speckled animal found with him = stolen). The *tension*: the man of *mirmah* (27:35) *invokes tsedaqah* — and then works the *breeding trick*; the interior *claims righteousness while planning cunning* (the verse states the claim; the scheme follows). *(inferred: tsedaqah = the integrity invoked, held in tension with the scheme)*.
- **sur (removed) — Laban's *counter-trick* (30:35).** *sur distinct from 30:32:* "that day Laban **removed** (sur) the striped and spotted… gave them to his sons, three days' journey off" *(stated)* — sur, *remove*: the gem is the *reversal* — Laban *pre-emptively removes the very animals that would be Jacob's wage*, handing them away; the deceiver's father-in-law *out-schemes the scheme*; the interior *cheats first*. Two sur operations: Jacob's *proposed* removal (30:32) / Laban's *pre-emptive* removal (30:35) — cunning against cunning *(inferred: sur = Laban's counter-removal, out-manoeuvring Jacob)*.
- **(30:37–42 — the peeled sticks and selective breeding, no non-T2 span.)** Flagged: the *breeding scheme* (peeled poplar at the troughs; breeding the *stronger* for himself, leaving the *feebler* to Laban) carries no flagged non-T2 span, but it is the scene's *interior act*: Jacob *answers Laban's counter-trick with his own manipulation* — cunning *met by cunning*; the interior *building its wealth by craft*. Read as context, anchored by sur/tsedaqah/rov *(no-span context; the counter-scheme of the breeding)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the claim grounded in labour (natan 30:26a → yada/avad/avodah 30:26b → yada/avad 30:29):** Jacob *asks to leave with his own*, *grounding the claim in the service rendered* and *its proven quality* — the interior pressing its earned right.
2. **the blessing-conduit admitted, then asserted (chen 30:27a → barakh 30:27b → rov/barakh 30:30):** Laban *ingratiates* and *admits* the LORD blessed him *through Jacob*; Jacob then *asserts* the same — the Abrahamic blessing *acknowledged even by the exploiter*, and *claimed* by the exploited.
3. **the wage refused for a scheme (natan 30:31 → shamar 30:31b → sur 30:32 → tsedaqah 30:33):** Jacob *declines a fixed wage*, *offers continued keeping*, *proposes the odd-coloured animals* as wage, and *invokes his own honesty* as the test — righteousness claimed *at the threshold of a trick*.
4. **cunning against cunning (sur 30:35 → [breeding scheme 30:37–42] → rov 30:43):** Laban *out-schemes first* (removing the wage-animals); Jacob *counter-manipulates the breeding* — and *increases greatly*. The blessing *works through and despite the mutual grasping*; the interior *prospers by craft*, yet (as the next passage will say, 31:9) it is *God who gave* the flocks.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** natan ×2 (30:26 the *claim* to his own / 30:31 the *fixed wage refused*); yada ×2 (30:26 the *service known to exist* / 30:29 its *proven quality*); avad/avodah (the *labour as ground of claim*); chen (Laban's *ingratiating, retentive* favor); barakh ×2 (30:27 the conduit *admitted* by Laban / 30:30 *asserted* by Jacob); rov (the flocks' *abundance*); shamar (the *continued keeping*); sur ×2 (30:32 Jacob's *proposed* wage-removal / 30:35 Laban's *pre-emptive counter*-removal); **tsedaqah (righteousness *invoked by the schemer* — held in tension with the breeding-trick)**; the *breeding scheme* (no-span context — cunning met by cunning).
- **Whose interior:** the **human** interiors of *two schemers* — the *retentive, cheating* father-in-law (Laban) and the *claim-pressing, righteousness-invoking, counter-scheming* son-in-law (Jacob); the **divine** interior *blessing through the conduit* — the blessing operating *even amid* the mutual grasping (Jacob as the channel Laban profits from).
- **Threads:** *the grasping interior* (Jacob's cunning ← the birthright bought JAC-02, the blessing stolen JAC-05 — now *building flocks by craft*; the wealth real but *grasped*, contrast Isaac's *received* prosperity JAC-04); the deceiver deceived, continued (Laban's counter-trick ← the Leah-substitution JAC-09 — the two out-scheme each other); the blessing-conduit (barakh 30:27,30 ← 12:3 "in you… blessed"); *God gave it* (rov 30:43 → 31:9 "God has taken your father's livestock and given it to me" — the theological re-reading Jacob himself will give); tsedaqah invoked (→ the self-justifying tally of 20 years, 31:38–42).
- **Guarded against:** collapsing the pairs (two natan, two yada, two avad, two barakh, two sur) into single operations (admitted-vs-asserted blessing; proposed-vs-counter removal — the distinctions carry the *cunning-against-cunning* finding); reading Jacob's tsedaqah-claim at face value *or* condemning it — I read only that the verse *states* he invokes his honesty, and the scheme *follows* (the tension is the finding, not a verdict); crediting the breeding-magic as the cause when the passage itself will be *re-read* as God's giving (31:9) — I note the craft *and* leave the causation where 30:43/31:9 put it; importing a moral lesson the text doesn't state — the grasping and the blessing simply *coexist* here.

---

## Genesis 31:1-21 - the grievance, the God-reading of the wealth, and the stealthy departure: the sons' envy, Jacob's case, the flight by deception (JAC-12)

# Genesis 31:1–21 — inner-being passage reading (JAC-12-flight)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-jacob-v1-20260704`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. The Bethel-dream/angel (31:10–13) and Rachel's theft of the household gods (31:19, no non-T2 span) read as scene-context, anchored by natan/lev.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; no repeated gloss in this passage.

---

## JAC-12-flight · Genesis 31:1–21 · [the grievance, the God-reading of the wealth, and the stealthy departure] — the sons' envy, Jacob's case to his wives, and the flight by deception

**The passage.** Jacob **heard** (shama) Laban's sons — "he has taken all our father's, gained all this **wealth** (kavod)" (31:1); Laban's face changed; the LORD says return; Jacob **called** (qara) Rachel and Leah to the field (31:4); "you **know** (yada) I **served** (avad) your father with all my **strength** (koach)" (31:6); "he cheated me… but God did not permit him to **harm** (ra) me" (31:7); "God has taken your father's livestock and **given** (natan) them to me" (31:9); the dream of the angel of Bethel; the wives — "are we not **regarded** (chashav) as foreigners? he sold us" (31:15); "all the **wealth** (osher) God took is ours… do what God said" (31:16); Jacob fled, "**tricked** (lev) Laban" by not telling him (31:20).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **shama (heard) — the *resentment overheard* (31:1a).** "Jacob **heard** (shama) that Laban's sons were saying…" *(stated)* — shama, *hear*: the interior *catches the turning mood* — as he once was warned of Esau's threat by report (27:42), now he *hears the brothers-in-law's grievance*; the *trigger* of the departure *(inferred: shama = the resentment overheard, prompting flight)*.
- **kavod (wealth) — the gain seen by others as *their loss* (31:1b).** "he has gained all this **wealth** (kavod)" *(stated)* — kavod, *weight / glory / wealth*: the sons name Jacob's prosperity as *heavy gain stripped from their father*; the interior of the *envious* (the grasped wealth *provoking* resentment, as it did around Isaac, 26:14) *(inferred: kavod = the weighty gain that provokes the sons' envy)*.
- **qara (called) — the *private summons* for the decision (31:4).** "Jacob sent and **called** (qara) Rachel and Leah to the field" *(stated)* — qara, *call-to*: the interior *gathers his wives privately* (in the field, away from Laban) for the momentous choice — a *deliberate, secret* consultation; the departure planned in confidence *(inferred: qara = the private summons to decide the flight)*.
- **yada (know) + avad (served) + koach (strength) — the *wholehearted labour* pleaded (31:6).** "you **know** (yada) I have **served** (avad) your father with all my **strength** (koach)" *(stated)*. **yada** — the wives' *knowledge* invoked; **avad** — the *service*; **koach** — *with all my strength*: the gem is the *wholeheartedness* — Jacob pleads he *gave his full power* to the labour; the interior *asserting its unstinting service* against the charge of gain-by-theft *(inferred: yada/avad/koach = the full-strength service pleaded)*.
- **ra (harm) — the *evil intent restrained by God* (31:7).** "he cheated me and changed my wages ten times, but God did not permit him to **harm** (ra) me" *(stated)* — ra, *be evil / do harm*: the interior *reads a providence* — Laban *meant evil* (the ten changes) but *God restrained it*; the same *God-restrains-the-harmer* motif as Abimelech (20:6). Jacob *credits God's guarding* over his own cunning *(inferred: ra = Laban's evil intent, restrained by God)*.
- **natan (given) — the *cunning re-read as God's gift* (31:9).** "God has taken your father's livestock and **given** (natan) them to me" *(stated)* — the gem: **natan** — Jacob *re-narrates the breeding-scheme* (JAC-11) as **God's giving** — the flocks he *built by craft* are now confessed as *taken-from-Laban-and-given-by-God*; the interior *theologises its prosperity*, crediting the gift to God (and the dream, 31:10–13, backs it — "I have seen all Laban does to you"). Whether piety or self-justification, the *stated* reading is *God gave it* *(inferred: natan = the flocks re-read as God's gift, not Jacob's trick)*.
- **chashav (regarded) — the wives *counted as foreigners* (31:15).** "are we not **regarded** (chashav) by him as foreigners? he has sold us and devoured our money" *(stated)* — chashav, *reckon / count / regard*: the gem is the *daughters' wound* — their own father *reckons them as outsiders*, having *sold* them (the bride-service) and *consumed the price*; the interior of the *disinherited daughters*, siding against Laban *(inferred: chashav = the daughters reckoned as foreigners by their father)*.
- **osher (wealth) — the wealth *claimed as theirs* by right (31:16).** "all the **wealth** (osher) God has taken from our father belongs to us and our children" *(stated)* — osher, *riches*: the wives *claim the wealth* as *rightfully theirs* (restitution for the devoured bride-price) and *endorse the flight* — "do what God said"; the interior *aligning with Jacob and God against the father* *(inferred: osher = the wealth claimed as the daughters' due)*.
- **lev (tricked) — the departure *by deception* (31:20).** "Jacob **tricked** (lev) Laban the Aramean by not telling him he intended to flee" *(stated)* — the gem is the idiom: **lev — *heart/mind*** — "Jacob *stole the heart of* Laban" (ganav-lev = *deceive*): even the *God-commanded* return (31:3,13) is *executed by stealth*; the interior *deceives again* — the grasping/deceiving pattern *persists* into the departure (and Rachel *steals* the household gods, 31:19). The deceiver *leaves as he lived* *(inferred: lev = the heart-stealing deception of the secret flight)*.
- **(31:19 — Rachel steals the household gods, no non-T2 span.)** Flagged: "Rachel **stole** her father's household gods" carries no flagged span, but it *doubles* the departure's theme — *theft and stealth run in the family*; the wife *steals the teraphim* as the husband *steals the heart*; the interior's *acquisitive stealth* shared. Read as context, anchored by lev (31:20) *(no-span context; the parallel theft)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the mood turns and God calls (shama/kavod 31:1 → qara 31:4):** Jacob *overhears the sons' envy* of his *wealth*, sees Laban's face changed, and (God having said "return") *privately summons his wives* to decide.
2. **the case: full service, God's protection, God's gift (yada/avad/koach 31:6 → ra 31:7 → natan 31:9):** Jacob pleads his *wholehearted labour*, reads Laban's *evil intent as restrained by God*, and *re-narrates his prospering as God's giving* — the interior *theologising the wealth it built by craft*.
3. **the wives side against their father (chashav 31:15 → osher 31:16):** feeling *reckoned as foreigners and sold*, they *claim the wealth as their due* and *endorse the flight* — the daughters' wound turned to alliance.
4. **the stealthy departure (lev 31:20 → [Rachel's theft 31:19]):** the God-commanded return is *carried out by deception* — Jacob *steals Laban's heart* (deceives), Rachel *steals the gods*; the interior *leaves as it lived* — obedience to God *entangled with the old stealth*.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** shama (the *resentment overheard*); kavod (the *weighty gain* provoking the sons' envy); qara (the *private summons* to decide); yada/avad/koach (the *full-strength service* pleaded); ra (Laban's *evil intent restrained by God*); **natan (the *cunning re-read as God's gift*)**; chashav (the daughters *reckoned as foreigners* and sold); osher (the wealth *claimed as their due*); **lev (the *heart-stealing deception* of the flight — the idiom)**; Rachel's *parallel theft* of the gods (no-span context).
- **Whose interior:** the **human** interiors *aggrieved and theologising* (Jacob — full service, God's gift, yet fleeing by stealth), *wounded and allied* (the daughters — sold, foreignised, claiming their due), and *acquisitive* (Rachel's theft); the **divine** interior *restraining the harmer and calling the fugitive home* (the Bethel-God keeping the vow, 31:13).
- **Threads:** *God gave it* (natan 31:9 ← the breeding scheme 30:43 — Jacob's own theological re-reading of his craft); *God restrains the harmer* (ra 31:7 ← 20:6 Abimelech); the Bethel vow kept (31:13 ← 28:20–22 — God returns him as promised); the persisting deception (lev 31:20 ← the deceiver deceived JAC-09; → the confrontation where Laban pursues, JAC-13); envy at grasped wealth (kavod 31:1 ← 26:14 qana around Isaac); Rachel's theft (→ Jacob's rash oath "let the thief die", 31:32, JAC-13).
- **Guarded against:** deciding *for* the reader whether Jacob's "God gave it" (31:9) is piety or self-justification — I read only that he *states* it, and that it *re-frames* the craft of JAC-11 (the tension left open); flattening the lev-idiom into plain "tricked" and missing that the *deception-word* frames even the God-commanded return; importing a verdict on Rachel's theft (the text merely *reports* it; its consequence comes at 31:32); treating koach as a throwaway ("all my strength") when it *stresses the wholeheartedness* Jacob pleads; reading the wives' endorsement as pure faith when it is also *claim to their devoured inheritance* (chashav/osher — both are there).

---

## Genesis 31:22-55 - confrontation into treaty: God's guard, the aired grievances, the search, Jacob's self-vindication, the covenant of separation (JAC-13)

# Genesis 31:22–55 — inner-being passage reading (JAC-13-pursuit-mizpah)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-jacob-v1-20260704`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. Rachel's ruse (31:34–35, the hidden gods) reads as scene-context. **Note:** the `'o'` span at 31:43 (glossed "desire") is the conjunction *"or"* ("for my daughters *or* their children") — no desire-operation is in the verse; flagged as a probable mis-tag, given no inner-being reading.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the 2 tov, 2 shamar, 2 ra, 2 charah, 2 pachad, and the qara-namings each treated distinctly.

---

## JAC-13-pursuit-mizpah · Genesis 31:22–55 · [confrontation into treaty] — God's guard on the fleeing man, the aired grievances, the search, Jacob's self-vindication, and the covenant of separation

**The passage.** God warns Laban in a dream — "be **careful** (shamar) to say nothing to Jacob, **good** (tov) or **bad** (ra)" (31:24); Laban — "you **tricked** (levav) me, drove off my daughters… I'd have sent you with **mirth** (simchah)" (31:26–27); "it is in my power to **harm** (ra) you, but God warned me — say nothing **good** (tov) or **bad**" (31:29); "you **longed** (kasaph) for your father's house — but why steal my gods?" (31:30); Jacob — "I was **afraid** (yare)" (31:31); "with whomever you find your gods shall not **live** (chayah)" — Jacob did not **know** (yada) Rachel took them (31:32); Rachel "I **cannot** (yakhol) rise… let my lord not be **angry** (charah)" (31:35); Jacob **angry** (charah), **berated** (riv) him — "what is my **offense** (pesha)? my **sin** (chattat)?" (31:36); "you **required** (baqash) the **loss** (chata) from me… my sleep **fled** (nadad)" (31:39–40); "I **served** (avad) twenty years… God saw my **affliction** (oni)… the **Fear** (pachad) of Isaac rebuked you" (31:41–42); "let us **make** (karat) a **covenant** (berit)" (31:44); Jacob **set up** (rum) a pillar (31:45); Laban and Jacob **named** (qara) the heap (31:47–48); "if you **oppress** (anah) my daughters…" (31:50); "not pass over to do **harm** (raah)" (31:52); "God **judge** (shaphat)" — Jacob swore by the **Fear** (pachad) of Isaac (31:53); he **called** (qara) his kinsmen to eat (31:54); Laban **blessed** (barakh) and departed (31:55).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **shamar (careful) + tov (good) + ra (bad) — God's *guard* on the pursued (31:24).** "God came to Laban… 'be **careful** (shamar) to say nothing to Jacob, either **good** (tov) or **bad** (ra)'" *(stated)*. **shamar** — *watch/take heed*; **tov/ra** — the merism *good-or-bad* (i.e. *nothing at all* by way of power-move). The gem: *God restrains the pursuer* — the fleeing deceiver is *guarded by a divine warning*; the interior of the *hunter checked from above* (← God restrains Abimelech, 20:6; the harmer, 31:7) *(inferred: shamar/tov/ra = the divine restraint laid on the pursuer)*.
- **levav (tricked) — Laban names the *heart-theft* (31:26).** "you have **tricked** (levav) me and driven my daughters like captives" *(stated)* — the idiom again (← 31:20, ganav-lev): "you *stole my heart/mind*" = *deceived me*; now *Laban* names the deception done to him. The interior of the *deceived accuser* — the deception-word turned back on Jacob by its victim *(inferred: levav = the heart-theft named by the deceived)*.
- **simchah (mirth) — the *festive farewell* denied (31:27).** "why flee secretly… I'd have sent you with **mirth** (simchah), songs, tambourine and lyre?" *(stated)* — simchah, *joy/gladness*: Laban *claims a joyful send-off was possible* — the interior *aggrieved of the celebration it was cheated of* (whether sincere or self-serving, the *stated* complaint is lost joy) *(inferred: simchah = the festive farewell Laban claims was denied him)*.
- **ra (harm) + tov (good) + shamar (careful) — power to harm, *restrained* (31:29).** *ra/tov/shamar distinct from 31:24:* "it is in my power to do you **harm** (ra), but the God of your father… said, be **careful** (shamar), say nothing **good** (tov) or bad" *(stated)*. Here the merism is *quoted by Laban himself* — he *owns his power to harm* and *confesses the divine restraint*. Where 31:24 was *God's warning*, 31:29 is *Laban's admission* of it — the pursuer *conceding he is checked* *(inferred: ra/tov/shamar = the harm-power owned and confessed as divinely restrained)*.
- **kasaph (longed) — the *homesick longing* acknowledged (31:30).** "you have gone because you **longed** (kasaph) greatly for your father's house" *(stated)* — kasaph, *long/yearn*: Laban *grants the legitimate homesickness* — the interior's *pull toward home* (← the vow's "come again to my father's house in peace", 28:21) — before pivoting to the accusation of theft *(inferred: kasaph = the yearning for home acknowledged)*.
- **yare (afraid) — the *fear-motive* owned (31:31).** "I was **afraid** (yare), for I thought you'd take your daughters by force" *(stated)* — yare, *fear*: Jacob *confesses fear as the reason for stealth* — the *self-protecting* fear (← the sister-lie fear 26:7; his own dread of Esau 27:44) driving the secret flight; the interior *honest about its fear* *(inferred: yare = the fear that drove the secret departure)*.
- **chayah (shall not live) + yada (did not know) — the *rash death-oath* in ignorance (31:32).** "with whomever you find your gods shall not **live** (chayah)… Jacob did not **know** (yada) Rachel had stolen them" *(stated)*. **chayah** — *live*: Jacob *pronounces death* on the thief; **yada** — the dramatic gem: he *does not know* the thief is *Rachel* — the interior *curses blindly*, and the narrator's dark note lands (Rachel *will die* prematurely, 35:18). The rash oath of the *unknowing* self *(inferred: chayah/yada = the blind death-oath, unknowingly against Rachel)*.
- **yakhol (cannot) + charah (angry) — Rachel's *ruse* (31:35).** "I **cannot** (yakhol) rise… let my lord not be **angry** (charah); the way of women is on me" *(stated)*. **yakhol** — the *feigned inability* (she sits on the hidden gods); **charah** — she *pre-empts his anger*. The gem: the *daughter deceives her father* (as her husband did his) — the family's stealth in her too; the interior *lying with composure* *(inferred: yakhol/charah = the ruse that hides the theft, deflecting anger)*.
- **charah (angry) + riv (berated) + pesha (offense) + chattat (sin) — Jacob's *indignant counter-attack* (31:36).** *charah distinct from 31:35:* "Jacob became **angry** (charah) and **berated** (riv) Laban: 'what is my **offense** (pesha)? my **sin** (chattat)?'" *(stated)*. **charah** — *now Jacob's* anger (the accused turns accuser); **riv** — *contend/bring a case* (the legal-dispute word, ← the wells 26:20); **pesha** — *transgression/rebellion*; **chattat** — *sin/failure*. The gem: Jacob, *finally emboldened*, *demands to know his crime* — the interior *indignant in its (relative) innocence here*, pressing the legal question *(inferred: charah/riv/pesha/chattat = the indignant demand for the charge)*.
- **baqash (required) + chata (loss) — the *shepherd's borne loss* (31:39).** "what was torn I did not bring; I **bore the loss** (chata); from my hand you **required** (baqash) it" *(stated)*. **baqash** — *seek/demand*: Laban *exacted* every loss from Jacob; **chata** — here in the *loss/forfeit* sense (the shepherd *made good* the torn animals). The interior of the *scrupulous, over-charged shepherd* — bearing what custom would excuse *(inferred: baqash/chata = the losses demanded of and borne by the shepherd)*.
- **nadad (fled) — *sleeplessness* under the toil (31:40).** "the heat by day, the cold by night, my sleep **fled** (nadad) from my eyes" *(stated)* — nadad, *flee/wander/retreat*: the gem is *sleep itself fleeing* — the *bodily cost* of twenty years' labour; the interior *worn by exposure and sleeplessness* *(inferred: nadad = the sleep that fled — the toil's bodily toll)*.
- **avad (served) — the *twenty years* tallied (31:41).** "I **served** (avad) you fourteen years for your daughters, six for your flock, and you changed my wages ten times" *(stated)* — avad, *serve*: the *full accounting* of the service (← the doubled service JAC-09) — the interior *laying the whole ledger* of its labour before the witnesses *(inferred: avad = the twenty years' service tallied as vindication)*.
- **oni (affliction) + pachad (Fear of Isaac) — God as *vindicator* of the afflicted (31:42).** "if the God of my father, the **Fear** (pachad) of Isaac, had not been with me… God saw my **affliction** (oni) and rebuked you" *(stated)*. **oni** — *affliction/misery* (← Leah's oni 29:32; Hagar's, 16:11): Jacob names his *twenty years' affliction*; **pachad** — the gem: **the Fear/Dread of Isaac** — a *divine title*, God known as *the One Isaac reverently fears* — invoked as the *vindicator who saw and rebuked*. The interior *appeals past the human dispute to the God who saw* *(inferred: oni/pachad = the affliction seen, and God-the-Dread-of-Isaac as vindicator)*.
- **(31:43 — the `'o'`/"desire" span is the conjunction "or"; no inner-being operation. Flagged mis-tag, not read.)**
- **karat (make) + berit (covenant) — the *treaty of separation* proposed (31:44).** "let us **make** (karat) a **covenant** (berit), you and I" *(stated)* — **karat** *cut* + **berit** *covenant*: Laban *proposes a pact* — but (unlike the peace-covenants of blessing, 21:27; 26:28) this is a *boundary of mutual non-harm* between two who *cannot trust*; the interior *sealing a wary separation* *(inferred: karat/berit = the covenant of wary separation)*.
- **rum (set up) — the *pillar raised* as witness (31:45).** "Jacob took a stone and **set it up** (rum) as a pillar" *(stated)* — rum, *raise/exalt/lift*: the interior *erects a monument* (as at Bethel, 28:18) — here a *witness-stone* to the boundary *(inferred: rum = the pillar raised as covenant-witness)*.
- **qara (named the heap) — the *witness-heap named* (31:47).** "Laban **called** (qara) it Jegar-sahadutha, Jacob **called** (qara) it Galeed" *(stated)* — qara, *name*: each in his own tongue *names the witness-heap* — the interior *marking the boundary in a name* (both meaning "heap of witness") *(inferred: qara = the dual naming of the witness-heap)*.
- **qara (named Galeed) — the *name confirmed* (31:48).** *qara distinct from 31:47:* "'this heap is a witness'… therefore he **named** (qara) it Galeed" *(stated)* — the *confirming* naming, tying the name to its *witness*-function (and Mizpah, "watchpost") — the interior *fixing the boundary's meaning* *(inferred: qara = the naming that fixes the heap's witness-role)*.
- **anah (oppress) — the daughters *guarded* by the oath (31:50).** "if you **oppress** (anah) my daughters or take other wives… God is witness" *(stated)* — anah, *afflict/oppress/humble*: Laban's *one tender clause* — protecting his daughters from *affliction*; the interior's *fatherly concern* embedded in the wary treaty (anah → the same word for Dinah's violation, JAC-17) *(inferred: anah = the affliction the oath forbids against the daughters)*.
- **raah (harm) — the *boundary of non-harm* (31:52).** "I will not pass this heap to you, nor you to me, to do **harm** (raah)" *(stated)* — raah, *harm/injury* (distinct lexeme from the ra of 31:24,29): the *core term* of the treaty — *neither crosses to hurt the other*; the interior *fencing off future harm* *(inferred: raah = the mutual harm the boundary forbids)*.
- **pachad (Fear of Isaac) + shaphat (judge) — the *oath sworn by the Dread* (31:53).** *pachad distinct from 31:42:* "the God of Abraham and of Nahor **judge** (shaphat) between us; so Jacob swore by the **Fear** (pachad) of his father Isaac" *(stated)*. **shaphat** — *judge* (God invoked as arbiter); **pachad** — the gem: Jacob *swears by "the Fear of Isaac"* — where 31:42 *named* the title, here he *binds his oath to it*; the interior *anchors its sworn word in the God his father reveres* — a step in *his own* relation to that God *(inferred: pachad/shaphat = the oath sworn by, and God invoked to judge by, the Dread of Isaac)*.
- **qara (called kinsmen) — the *covenant meal* summoned (31:54).** *qara distinct from the naming-qara:* "Jacob **called** (qara) his kinsmen to eat bread" *(stated)* — qara, *call-to*: the interior *convenes the shared meal* that *seals* the covenant (as covenant-meals do, 26:30) *(inferred: qara = the summons to the covenant meal)*.
- **barakh (blessed) — the *parting blessing* (31:55).** "Laban kissed his grandchildren and daughters and **blessed** (barakh) them, and departed" *(stated)* — barakh, *bless*: the gem is the *softened parting* — the aggrieved father *blesses and leaves*; the wary confrontation *ends in a blessing and separation* — the interior *releasing its own in blessing* *(inferred: barakh = the parting blessing that closes the confrontation)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **God guards the pursued (shamar/tov/ra 31:24 → ra/tov/shamar 31:29):** the LORD *warns Laban to touch nothing*; Laban *owns his power to harm and confesses the restraint* — the fleeing deceiver *fenced by grace* from the pursuer.
2. **the grievances aired (levav 31:26 → simchah 31:27 → kasaph 31:30 → yare 31:31):** Laban charges *heart-theft*, denied *festivity*, and *stolen gods* — granting the *homesick longing*; Jacob owns his *fear* as the reason for stealth.
3. **the blind oath and the ruse (chayah/yada 31:32 → yakhol/charah 31:35):** Jacob *curses the thief unknowingly against Rachel*; Rachel *deceives her father* with composed cunning — the family's stealth in the daughter too.
4. **Jacob's self-vindication (charah/riv/pesha/chattat 31:36 → baqash/chata 31:39 → nadad 31:40 → avad/oni/pachad 31:41–42):** the accused *turns accuser*, demands his *crime*, and lays out *twenty years* of over-charged, sleepless, afflicted service — appealing to *the Fear of Isaac* who *saw and rebuked*.
5. **the covenant of separation (karat/berit 31:44 → rum 31:45 → qara 31:47–48 → anah 31:50 → raah 31:52 → pachad/shaphat 31:53 → qara 31:54 → barakh 31:55):** a *wary treaty* — a *witness-heap named*, the *daughters guarded from affliction*, a *boundary of non-harm*, an *oath by the Dread of Isaac* and *God as judge*, sealed with a *meal* and closed with a *parting blessing*. Not friendship — a *fenced peace* between two who cannot trust.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** shamar/tov/ra ×2 (31:24 God's *warning* / 31:29 Laban's *admission* of it); levav (the *heart-theft named* by the deceived); simchah (the *festive farewell* denied); kasaph (the *homesick longing* granted); yare (the *fear-motive* owned); chayah/yada (the *blind death-oath*, unknowingly against Rachel); yakhol/charah (Rachel's *composed ruse*); charah ×2 (Rachel *deflecting* anger / Jacob's *indignant* anger); riv/pesha/chattat (the *demand for the charge*); baqash/chata (the *over-charged shepherd's borne loss*); nadad (the *sleep that fled*); avad (the *twenty years* tallied); oni (the *affliction seen*); **pachad ×2 — "the Fear of Isaac" (31:42 *named* as vindicator / 31:53 *sworn by*)**; karat/berit (the *covenant of separation*); rum (the *witness-pillar*); qara (the heap *named* 31:47, *confirmed* 31:48, and the *meal summoned* 31:54); anah (the daughters guarded from *affliction*); raah (the *boundary of non-harm*); shaphat (God as *judge*); barakh (the *parting blessing*).
- **Whose interior:** the **divine** interior *restraining the pursuer* and *seeing the afflicted* (the Fear of Isaac, vindicator); the **human** interiors *aggrieved and accusing* (Laban), *fearful, indignant, and self-vindicating* (Jacob), and *deceiving with composure* (Rachel). The confrontation *resolves into a fenced peace*.
- **Threads:** God restrains the harmer (shamar 31:24 ← 20:6; 31:7); the deception-idiom (levav 31:26 ← 31:20 — now named *by* the victim); the blind oath (chayah 31:32 → Rachel's early death 35:18 — the narrator's dark irony); the Fear/Dread of Isaac (pachad 31:42, 53 ← Isaac's proven fear-of-God 22:12; Jacob *swearing by* his father's God — a step toward his own relation, → the Peniel encounter JAC-15); the affliction-God-sees (oni 31:42 ← 29:32; 16:11); covenant of separation (vs the peace-covenants 21:27; 26:28 — here *distrust fenced*).
- **Guarded against:** collapsing the paired merisms (God's *warning* vs Laban's *owned* restraint; the two angers — Rachel's *deflecting* vs Jacob's *indignant*; the two pachad — *named* vs *sworn by*); reading a "desire" operation into the mis-tagged conjunction at 31:43 (flagged, not read); taking Jacob's self-vindication as the narrator's verdict (the text lets him *plead* — his integrity *as shepherd* is real, even as his history is not clean); missing the *dark irony* of the blind oath (chayah 31:32 → Rachel's death); importing a "covenant of grace" reading over what is plainly a *wary boundary-treaty*; treating barakh (31:55) as warm reconciliation when it *closes a separation* — a blessing *and* a parting.

---

## Genesis 32:1-21 - dread turned to prayer and the appeasing gift: Mahanaim, the terror of Esau, the prayer of unworthiness, the present to cover his face (JAC-14)

# Genesis 32:1–21 — inner-being passage reading (JAC-14-fear-prayer-appease)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-jacob-v1-20260704`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. The two-camps strategy (32:7–8) reads as scene-context. **Note:** the second chesed span at 32:10 carries an alternate gloss "shame"; the verse's word is chesed = *steadfast love* (Jacob unworthy before God's *kindness*), so both are read as the deeds of chesed, not a shame-operation.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the 2 yatav, the paired chesed, and the paired kipper/kaphar each treated distinctly.

---

## JAC-14-fear-prayer-appease · Genesis 32:1–21 · [dread turned to prayer, and the appeasing gift] — Mahanaim, the terror of Esau, the prayer of unworthiness, and the present sent to cover his face

**The passage.** The angels meet him; "God's camp!" — he **called** (qara) it Mahanaim (32:2); he sends word to Esau, "that I may find **favor** (chen)" (32:5); word returns — Esau is coming to **meet** (qara) him with 400 men (32:6); Jacob "was greatly **afraid** (yare) and distressed," divides into two camps (32:7); the prayer — "you said, return, that I may **do you good** (yatav)" (32:9); "I am not worthy of all the **steadfast love** (chesed) and **faithfulness** (emet)" (32:10); "deliver me… for I **fear** (yare) him" (32:11); "you said, I will surely **do you good** (yatav), make your offspring as the sand… for **multitude** (rov)" (32:12); the present — he **handed over** (natan) droves (32:16); "when Esau **asks** (shaal)…" (32:17); "I may **appease** (kipper/kaphar) him… and afterward see his face" (32:20).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **qara (Mahanaim) — the *encouragement* named at the outset (32:2).** "when Jacob saw them: 'this is God's camp!' he **called** (qara) it Mahanaim ('two camps')" *(stated)* — qara, *name*: the interior *marks a vision of God's own host* at the very threshold of the dreaded return — a *reassurance named* before the fear strikes; the "two camps" that will *echo* in his own defensive division (32:7) *(inferred: qara = the naming of the God-encampment, a reassurance at the threshold)*.
- **chen (favor) — the *self-lowering* approach to Esau (32:5).** "I have sent to tell my lord, that I may find **favor** (chen) in your sight" *(stated)* — chen, *favor/grace*: the gem is the *inversion of the blessing* — Jacob, who *seized* lordship over Esau (27:29), now calls Esau *"my lord"* and himself *"your servant"*, *seeking favor*; the grasping interior *bowing before the brother it supplanted* *(inferred: chen = the favor sought in a deliberate self-lowering)*.
- **qara (meet) — the *ambiguous approach* of Esau (32:6).** "he is coming to **meet** (qara) you, and 400 men with him" *(stated)* — qara in the *encounter* sense: the *dread-laden report* — the meeting *could be embrace or army*; the interior *braced for the worst* by the numbers *(inferred: qara = the ominous coming-to-meet)*.
- **yare (afraid) — the *terror* that has shadowed the exile (32:7).** "Jacob was greatly **afraid** (yare) and distressed" *(stated)* — yare, *fear*: the gem is *this* fear — the *dread of Esau* that *drove the whole exile* (the murder-threat, 27:41–44) now *arrives*; "greatly afraid **and distressed**" — the interior at its *most exposed* since the flight; fear *doubled* *(inferred: yare = the long-dreaded terror of Esau, now upon him)*.
- **yatav (do you good) — God's *command-promise recalled* (32:9).** "O LORD who said, 'return… that I may **do you good** (yatav)'" *(stated)* — yatav, *be/do good*: the prayer *opens by holding God to his own command-and-promise* — *you told me to return and promised good*; the interior *grounding its plea in God's word*, not its own merit *(inferred: yatav = God's command-promise "do you good" recalled as the prayer's ground)*.
- **chesed (steadfast love) + emet (faithfulness) — the *confession of unworthiness* (32:10).** "I am **not worthy** of the least of all the **steadfast love** (chesed) and all the **faithfulness** (emet)… with my staff I crossed, now two camps" *(stated)*. **chesed** — *steadfast covenant-love/kindness* (← 24:12,27; 19:19); **emet** — *faithfulness/truth*: the gem is the ***new*** *note — Jacob **confesses unworthiness*** before God's *chesed-and-emet* (the covenant-character pair) — the grasper who *took by right-of-scheme* now says *"I am not worthy of the least"*; the interior *humbled*, measuring the distance from *lone staff* to *two camps* as sheer *kindness*. (The second chesed span's "shame" gloss aside, the verse's word is *steadfast love*: unworthiness *before* kindness, not a shame-act.) *(inferred: chesed/emet = the humbled confession of unworthiness before God's steadfast love and faithfulness)*.
- **yare (fear) — the *dread voiced in the prayer* (32:11).** *yare distinct from 32:7:* "deliver me from the hand of Esau, for I **fear** (yare) him, that he may come and attack the mothers with the children" *(stated)* — where 32:7 *narrated* the fear, here Jacob *names it to God* — the interior *bringing its terror into the prayer* and *pleading deliverance*; fear *turned toward God*, not only managed by strategy *(inferred: yare = the dread confessed to God with the plea to deliver)*.
- **yatav (do you good) + rov (multitude) — the *promise held up as leverage of faith* (32:12).** *yatav distinct from 32:9:* "you said, 'I will surely **do you good** (yatav) and make your offspring as the sand… for **multitude** (rov)'" *(stated)*. **yatav** — where 32:9 recalled the *command*'s promise, here Jacob *holds up the seed-promise itself*; **rov** — *abundance*: the interior *reminds God of his own pledge* (the children *cannot* be destroyed if the promise stands) — faith *reasoning from the promise* against the fear *(inferred: yatav/rov = the seed-promise held up to God as the ground of hope)*.
- **natan (handed over) — the *gift organised* (32:16).** "these he **handed over** (natan) to his servants, drove by drove" *(stated)* — natan, *give*: the interior *marshals a lavish present* — droves *given into his servants' charge*, spaced to *impress by waves*; the *strategic generosity* running alongside the prayer *(inferred: natan = the appeasing gift marshalled drove by drove)*.
- **shaal (asks) — the *anticipated question* scripted (32:17).** "when Esau **asks** (shaal), 'whose are these?'" *(stated)* — shaal, *ask*: Jacob *rehearses Esau's question* and scripts the deferential answer ("your servant Jacob's… a present for my lord") — the interior *planning the encounter's every word* *(inferred: shaal = the anticipated question the gift is staged to answer)*.
- **kipper (appease) + kaphar (appease) — the *covering of the brother's face* (32:20).** "I may **appease** (kipper/kaphar) him with the present… and afterward see his face; perhaps he will accept me" *(stated)*. The gem is the *doubled atonement-word*: **kipper/kaphar** — *cover / atone / pacify* — literally *"I will cover his face"* with the gift *before I see his face*; the interior *seeking to propitiate the wronged brother* — the *atonement*-language (later the priestly word) here *of a gift to a man he cheated*; covering the *offense of the stolen blessing* with lavish restitution *(inferred: kipper/kaphar = the covering/propitiation of Esau's face with the gift — atonement toward the wronged brother)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **reassurance, then the self-lowering approach (qara-Mahanaim 32:2 → chen 32:5 → qara-meet 32:6):** a *vision of God's camp* named at the threshold; Jacob *approaches Esau as "servant" to "my lord," seeking favor* — bowing before the brother he supplanted — and the *ominous report* (400 men) returns.
2. **terror to prayer (yare 32:7 → yatav 32:9 → chesed/emet 32:10 → yare 32:11 → yatav/rov 32:12):** the *long-dreaded fear* arrives; the interior *turns it into prayer* — grounding the plea in *God's command-promise*, *confessing unworthiness before God's steadfast love and faithfulness*, *voicing the fear*, and *holding up the seed-promise*. The grasper *humbled and praying*.
3. **prayer and appeasement together (natan 32:16 → shaal 32:17 → kipper/kaphar 32:20):** alongside the prayer, Jacob *marshals a lavish gift*, *scripts the deferential meeting*, and *aims to "cover Esau's face"* before seeing it — the interior *trusting and scheming at once*: prayer central, but the old strategist *still covering his approach*.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** qara ×2 senses (32:2 the *God-camp named* / 32:6 the *ominous coming-to-meet*); chen (the *self-lowering* — "my lord Esau", the supplanter bowing); **yare ×2 (32:7 the *terror narrated* / 32:11 the *dread voiced in prayer*)**; yatav ×2 (32:9 God's *command-promise* recalled / 32:12 the *seed-promise* held up as faith's leverage); **chesed/emet (the *new confession of unworthiness* before God's steadfast love and faithfulness — the grasper humbled)**; rov (the *sand-multitude* promise); natan (the *gift marshalled*); shaal (the *anticipated question* scripted); **kipper/kaphar (the *covering of the brother's face* — atonement toward the wronged Esau)**.
- **Whose interior:** the **human** interior *afraid, humbled, and praying* (Jacob — the terror of Esau turned to a prayer of unworthiness) yet *still strategising* (the gift, the scripted words); the **divine** interior present as *the God who commanded the return and promised good* and whose *chesed-and-emet* Jacob now confesses himself unworthy of.
- **Threads:** the dread of Esau (yare 32:7 ← the murder-threat 27:41; the fear that shaped the exile); the *inverted lordship* (chen 32:5 — "my lord Esau" ← Jacob made lord over Esau 27:29 — now bowing); the *first confession of unworthiness* (chesed/emet 32:10 — a real interior shift from the grasper; the bargaining vow of Bethel 28:20 now *deepened into humility*); chesed-and-emet (← 24:27 God's covenant character; asked of God here); the promise as leverage of faith (yatav/rov 32:12 ← 28:14; 22:17); atonement-language toward a brother (kipper 32:20 → the priestly "cover" — here restitution to the wronged); the gift *before* the face (→ the reconciliation JAC-16, "I have seen your face as the face of God").
- **Guarded against:** reading a "shame" operation into the mis-glossed second chesed span (the verse's word is *steadfast love*; Jacob's *unworthiness* is the note, not shame); collapsing the two yare (narrated vs prayed) or two yatav (command-promise vs seed-promise); over-claiming Jacob's humility as *completed* transformation when the *scheming gift runs alongside* (prayer *and* strategy — the shift is real but partial, the wrestling still to come JAC-15); importing the priestly doctrine of atonement over the plain *appease/cover-his-face* the verse means (restitution to a wronged brother, not cultic atonement); treating chen's "my lord Esau" as mere courtesy when it *reverses the seized lordship*.

---
