## Exodus 10:1-29 - the God-hardened heart still fully itself and the court fractures: the refusal to be humbled, the negotiated service, the final rupture (EXO-14)

# Exodus 10:1–29 — inner-being passage reading (EXO-14-locusts-darkness)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `exodus-deliverance-v1-20260705`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. **Multiple interiors**: the **adversary** (Pharaoh — God-hardened, yet still confessing, bargaining, threatening), **Pharaoh's servants** (fracturing from him), **God** (the pedagogical purpose), and **Moses** (firm). **Hardening note (per the ledger):** this is the **God-hardened phase** — 10:1 ("I have hardened"), 10:20, 10:27 all name *the LORD* as agent — yet Pharaoh remains fully himself (confession 10:16–17, bargaining, threat 10:28): the God-hardening *does not erase his agency*.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the 3 lev, 2 ot, 6 avad, 2 qara, 2 atar, 2 chazaq each treated distinctly.

---

## EXO-14-locusts-darkness · Exodus 10:1–29 · [the God-hardened heart that is still fully itself; the court fractures] — the refusal to be humbled, the negotiated service, and the final rupture

**The passage.** "I have **hardened** (kaved) his **heart** (lev) and his servants', that I may show my **signs** (ot)" (10:1); "that you may tell your son… my **signs** (ot)… that you may know" (10:2); "how long will you refuse to **humble** (anah) yourself? let my people **serve** (avad) me" (10:3); the servants: "let them **serve** (avad); do you not see Egypt is ruined?" (10:7); "go, **serve** (avad); but which ones?" (10:8); "you have some **evil** (raah) purpose" (10:10); "go, the men, **serve** (avad); that is what you **seek** (baqash)" (10:11); the locusts **settled** (nuach, 10:14); Pharaoh **called** (qara): "I have **sinned** (chata)" (10:16); "forgive my **sin** (chattat)… **plead** (atar)… **remove** (sur) this death" (10:17); Moses **pleaded** (atar, 10:18); "the LORD **hardened** (chazaq) Pharaoh's **heart** (lev)" (10:20); the darkness; Pharaoh **called** (qara): "go, **serve** (avad); only leave your flocks" (10:24); "we serve (avad) with all" (10:26); "the LORD **hardened** (chazaq) Pharaoh's **heart** (lev)" (10:27); "never see my face again, or **take care** (shamar) — you die" (10:28).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **lev (heart) + kaved (hardened) + ot (signs) — the *God-hardening with its purpose* (10:1).** "I have **hardened** (kaved) his **heart** (lev) and the heart of his servants, that I may show my **signs** (ot)" *(stated)* — the gem (per the ledger): *God* is the agent ("I have hardened"), and *corporate* ("his servants") — the God-hardened phase, *stated as purpose*: the hardening *makes room for the signs*. The divine interior *hardens toward an end* — not caprice but *the display of his acts* *(inferred: lev/kaved/ot = the God-hardening whose purpose is the display of the signs)*.
- **ot (signs) — the signs *told to the children* (10:2).** *ot distinct from 10:1:* "that you may tell in the hearing of your son and grandson… that you may know that I am the LORD" *(stated)* — the gem: the hardening's *deepest purpose* is *pedagogical* — the signs *become the story* Israel *tells its children*, that they may *know the LORD*. The interior-context: the adversary's resistance *turned into Israel's catechism* — the deliverance *remembered and re-told* *(inferred: ot = the signs told to the generations — the hardening's pedagogical end)*.
- **anah (humble) + avad (serve) — the *refusal to be humbled* (10:3).** "how long will you refuse to **humble** (anah) yourself? let my people **serve** (avad) me" *(stated)*. The gem: **anah** — the *same word* as Israel's *affliction* (1:11,12 "afflict"; 3:7 "affliction") now names *what Pharaoh will not do* — *humble himself*. The oppressor who *afflicted* (anah) Israel *will not be humbled* (anah); the two interiors *bound by one word* — the afflicter's refusal to be *brought low* *(inferred: anah/avad = the refusal to be humbled — the afflicter who will not himself be brought low)*.
- **avad (serve) — the *servants' break* (10:7).** *avad distinct from 10:3:* "Pharaoh's servants said: 'let the men go, that they may **serve** (avad) the LORD; do you not see Egypt is ruined?'" *(stated)* — the gem: *Pharaoh's own court turns* — the servants *urge release* against their king; the *split in Egypt* (← 9:20) *reaches his own advisors*; the adversary's *corporate interior fracturing* *(inferred: avad = the service now urged by Pharaoh's own fracturing court)*.
- **avad (serve) — the *bargaining opens* (10:8).** *avad distinct:* "go, **serve** (avad) the LORD; but which ones?" *(stated)* — Pharaoh *concedes the principle* but *negotiates the scope* — the interior *bargaining to retain control* *(inferred: avad = the service conceded in principle, the scope contested)*.
- **raah (evil purpose) — the *projected malice* (10:10).** "you have some **evil** (raah) purpose in mind" *(stated)* — raah, *evil/harm*: the gem is *projection* — Pharaoh *attributes evil intent* to Israel's request; the adversary *reads his own malice into the other* *(inferred: raah = the evil Pharaoh projects onto Israel's request)*.
- **avad (serve) + baqash (seek) — the *men-only concession* (10:11).** *avad distinct:* "go, the men, **serve** (avad) the LORD; that is what you **seek** (baqash)" — and they were driven out *(stated)*. **avad** — the *partial* surrender (men only); **baqash** — Pharaoh *redefines their asking* to the minimum. The interior *offering a controlled, partial service* and *expelling* the mediators *(inferred: avad/baqash = the men-only service offered, the request minimised)*.
- **nuach (settled) — the locusts *at rest* on the land (10:14).** "the locusts **settled** (nuach) on the whole country" *(stated)* — nuach, *rest/settle*: the gem is the *ironic rest* — the *rest*-word (later the Sabbath-word, the promised-land-rest) used of the *devouring swarm* that *settles* to consume; judgment *at rest* on Egypt *(inferred: nuach = the devouring swarm settled — an ironic "rest" of judgment)*.
- **qara (called) + chata (sinned) — the *urgent confession* (10:16).** "Pharaoh *hastily* **called** (qara): 'I have **sinned** (chata) against the LORD and against you'" *(stated)*. **qara** — the *hasty summons*; **chata** — the confession *(← 9:27)*, now *"against the LORD and against you"* (even naming the wrong to Moses). The interior *confessing under the locusts' pressure* — *more desperate*, still *pressure-talk* *(inferred: qara/chata = the urgent confession under the locusts)*.
- **chattat (sin) + atar (plead) + sur (remove) — the *plea to lift "this death"* (10:17).** "forgive my **sin** (chattat), only this once; **plead** (atar)… **remove** (sur) this death" *(stated)*. **chattat** — the *sin* to be forgiven; **atar** — the *plea for intercession*; **sur** — *remove* "this death" (the locusts). The gem is *"only this once"* — the interior *knows its own pattern* (it has confessed and relapsed before) and *pleads a single exception* *(inferred: chattat/atar/sur = the plea to remove the death, "only this once" — the self-aware relapse)*.
- **atar (pleaded) — the intercession *enacted* (10:18).** *atar distinct from 10:17:* "he went out and **pleaded** (atar) with the LORD" *(stated)* — Moses *intercedes* despite the pattern — the mediator *faithful* to the pleading *(inferred: atar = the intercession enacted despite the known relapse)*.
- **lev (heart) + chazaq (hardened) — *God hardens* after the locusts (10:20).** *lev/chazaq distinct from 10:1:* "the LORD **hardened** (chazaq) Pharaoh's **heart**" *(stated)* — the God-hardening *seals* the relapse (as the confession-relief pattern predicts) — the interior *fixed by God after the plea is answered* *(inferred: lev/chazaq = God's hardening sealing the post-locust relapse)*.
- **qara (called) + avad (serve) — the *flocks-bargain* (10:24).** *qara/avad distinct:* "Pharaoh **called** (qara): 'go, **serve** (avad); only leave your flocks'" *(stated)* — after the *darkness*, Pharaoh *concedes more* (the little ones may go) but *still withholds* (the flocks) — the interior *bargaining down to the last thing it can keep* *(inferred: qara/avad = the near-total concession still withholding the flocks)*.
- **avad (serve) — the *whole* service demanded (10:26).** *avad distinct:* "our livestock must go… we must **serve** (avad) the LORD, and we do not yet know with what" *(stated)* — Moses *refuses the partial* — *not a hoof left*; the service must be *whole* (the transfer *complete*, nothing left in Egypt) *(inferred: avad = the whole, un-partial service Moses insists on)*.
- **lev (heart) + chazaq (hardened) — *God hardens* after the darkness (10:27).** *lev/chazaq distinct from 10:20:* "the LORD **hardened** (chazaq) Pharaoh's **heart**, and he would not let them go" *(stated)* — the God-hardening *again*, after the flocks-refusal — the heart *fixed* through the ninth plague *(inferred: lev/chazaq = God's hardening after the darkness)*.
- **shamar (take care) — the *final threat* (10:28).** "get away… **take care** (shamar) never to see my face again, or you die" *(stated)* — shamar, *keep/watch* (here *menacing*): the gem is the *rupture* — the God-hardened Pharaoh *is still fully himself*: he *threatens the mediator's life*; the interior *at its most defiant* even under God's hardening — agency *intact* *(inferred: shamar = the menacing threat — the God-hardened adversary still fully, defiantly himself)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the God-hardening and its pedagogical purpose (lev/kaved/ot 10:1 → ot 10:2):** God hardens *for an end* — *to show his signs* and *that Israel may tell its children and know him*; the resistance *becomes the story*.
2. **the refusal to be humbled, the court fractures (anah/avad 10:3 → avad 10:7):** Pharaoh *will not be humbled* (the afflicter's `anah` refused), while *his own servants break with him* — *"Egypt is ruined"* — the split reaching his court.
3. **the negotiated, partial service (avad 10:8 → raah 10:10 → avad/baqash 10:11 → nuach 10:14 → qara/chata 10:16 → chattat/atar/sur 10:17 → atar 10:18 → lev/chazaq 10:20):** Pharaoh *concedes in principle but bargains the scope* (men only), *projecting evil*; the locusts *settle*; he *confesses urgently* ("only this once", self-aware of his relapse); Moses *pleads*; and *God hardens* — sealing the pattern.
4. **the final concession withheld and the rupture (qara/avad 10:24 → avad 10:26 → lev/chazaq 10:27 → shamar 10:28):** after the darkness Pharaoh *concedes all but the flocks*; Moses *insists on the whole* ("not a hoof"); *God hardens again*; and Pharaoh *threatens Moses' life* — the God-hardened heart *still fully, defiantly itself*.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** **lev ×3 (10:1 God-hardened *with pedagogical purpose*, corporate / 10:20 God-hardened post-locust / 10:27 God-hardened post-darkness)**; ot ×2 (the signs *shown* / *told to the children* — the hardening's pedagogical end); **anah (the *refusal to be humbled* — the afflicter's own word turned on him)**; **avad ×6 (the *demand* / the *servants' break* / the *scope bargained* / *men-only* / *flocks withheld* / the *whole* insisted on — the negotiation over the terms of service)**; raah (the *projected malice*); baqash (the request *minimised*); nuach (the *ironic rest* of the devouring swarm); qara ×2 (the *urgent confession* / the *flocks-bargain*); chata/chattat (the confession, "only this once" — *self-aware relapse*); atar ×2 (Pharaoh's *plea* / Moses' *intercession*); sur (the death *removed*); chazaq ×2 (God's hardening *sealing* each relapse); shamar (the *menacing threat* — agency intact under God's hardening).
- **Whose interior (multi-interior):** the **adversary** (Pharaoh) — *God-hardened yet fully himself*: confessing ("only this once"), bargaining the scope of service, projecting evil, and *threatening the mediator's life* (the God-hardening *does not make him a puppet* — he remains a confessing, bargaining, defiant self); **Pharaoh's servants** — *fracturing from him* ("Egypt is ruined") — the split deepening into his court; **God** — hardening *for the signs and the generational telling*; **Moses** — *insisting on the whole* service, and *pleading* despite the known relapse.
- **Threads:** the **hardening trajectory's sealed phase** (10:1,20,27 God-hardening — but note Pharaoh's *undiminished agency*: the God-hardening *confirms* a self that still *confesses, bargains, threatens* — answering "what else influenced it": the hardening does not remove responsibility); the **anah wordplay** (Israel *afflicted* 1:11 / Pharaoh *will not humble* 10:3 — the two interiors bound by one word); the **split in Egypt deepening** (servants 10:7 ← God-fearers 9:20); the **pedagogical purpose** (ot 10:1–2 → 12:26; 13:8,14 — the deliverance *told to the children*); the **negotiated service** (avad — Pharaoh trying to *limit* the transfer of service; Moses insisting it be *whole*); the **confession-relapse** (10:16–17 ← 9:27–34 — "only this once" naming his own pattern).
- **Guarded against:** lumping the three lev, six avad, two ot/qara/atar/chazaq (each a distinct beat — esp. the *six* avad, the *negotiation over the terms of service*); reading the God-hardening (10:1,20,27) as *removing* Pharaoh's agency when the same chapter shows him *confessing, bargaining, threatening* (the God-hardening *confirms* a fully-active self — do not make him a puppet); missing the **anah wordplay** (the afflicter refusing to be humbled); over-reading nuach (the swarm "settled") as anything but the *ironic* rest-of-judgment; treating the servants' break (10:7) as Israelite (they are *Pharaoh's* court — the fracture *within* Egypt).

---

## Exodus 11:1-10 - the split complete and the hardening's purpose fully stated: favor given, the mediator's hot anger, the heart the LORD hardens to the last (EXO-15)

# Exodus 11:1–10 — inner-being passage reading (EXO-15-final-warning)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `exodus-deliverance-v1-20260705`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. **Multiple interiors**: **God** (favor given; the purpose stated), **Moses** (hot anger), **Israel/Egypt** (the split complete), and the **adversary** (the final God-hardening). The firstborn foretold (11:4–7) reads as scene-context.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; no repeated gloss. **Hardening note (per the ledger):** 11:10 is the *final God-hardening before the Passover*, with the purpose stated at 11:9 — "that my wonders may be multiplied."

---

## EXO-15-final-warning · Exodus 11:1–10 · [the split complete; the hardening's purpose fully stated] — favor given, the mediator's hot anger, and the heart the LORD hardens to the last

**The passage.** "One plague more… he will drive you out completely" (11:1); "let them **ask** (shaal), each of his neighbour, for silver and gold" (11:2); "the LORD gave the people **favor** (chen)… Moses was very great in Egypt" — God **gave** (natan) it (11:3); the firstborn foretold (11:4–5); "the LORD makes a distinction between Egypt and Israel" (11:7); Moses went out "in **hot** (chori) anger" (11:8); "Pharaoh will not listen, that my wonders may be **multiplied** (ravah)" (11:9); "the LORD **hardened** (chazaq) Pharaoh's **heart** (lev)" (11:10).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **shaal (ask) — the *plunder by asking* readied (11:2).** "let them **ask** (shaal), each of his neighbour, for silver and gold" *(stated)* — shaal, *ask/request* (← 3:22): the gem is that the *spoil comes by asking*, not seizing — the interior *receives the wealth of its bondage as given*, on the eve of freedom *(inferred: shaal = the plunder received by asking, readied)*.
- **chen (favor) + natan (gave) — *Egypt disposed toward Israel* (11:3).** "the LORD **gave** (natan) the people **favor** (chen) in the sight of the Egyptians; Moses was very great" *(stated)*. **chen** — *favor*; **natan** — *give*: the gem (← 3:21 foretold, now *enacted*) — *God turns Egypt's regard toward Israel*; even *Pharaoh's servants* and *the people* hold *Moses great*. The *split in Egypt is complete*: the whole land *favors* Israel and *honours* the mediator — only Pharaoh's heart holds out *(inferred: chen/natan = the God-given favor that turns all Egypt toward Israel — the split complete)*.
- **chori (hot anger) — the mediator's *burning indignation* (11:8).** "he went out from Pharaoh in **hot** (chori) anger" *(stated)* — chori, *burning/heat* (of anger): the gem is *Moses' anger* — after the death-threat (10:28) and the final defiance, the mediator *burns* — the *same register* as God's kindled anger (charah, 4:14). The deliverer now *shares the divine indignation* at the hardened evil; the interior *aligned with God's stance* toward the oppressor *(inferred: chori = the mediator's burning anger, aligned with God's indignation)*.
- **ravah (multiplied) — the hardening's *purpose: multiplied wonders* (11:9).** "Pharaoh will not listen, that my wonders may be **multiplied** (ravah)" *(stated)* — the gem: **ravah** — *multiply* (the *same word* as *Israel's* multiplying, 1:7,12) — now *God's wonders multiply* as *Israel* multiplied. The *purpose* of the continued hardening is *stated*: the refusal *makes room for more wonders* — the fuller *display* of God's acts (→ the pedagogical telling, 10:2). The interior-context: the adversary's fixed "no" *serving* the multiplication of the signs *(inferred: ravah = the wonders multiplied through the refusal — the hardening's purpose)*.
- **lev (heart) + chazaq (hardened) — the *final God-hardening* (11:10).** "the LORD **hardened** (chazaq) Pharaoh's **heart**, and he did not let Israel go" *(stated)* — the gem (per the ledger): the *last* God-hardening *before the Passover* — the *culmination* of the sealed phase (9:12; 10:20,27); the heart *fixed to the last*, *"as the LORD had spoken"*. The trajectory's *end-point on this side of the firstborn* — the self-fixed, God-sealed refusal *held to the threshold of the final blow* *(inferred: lev/chazaq = the final God-hardening, the refusal held to the last)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the plunder readied, Egypt disposed (shaal 11:2 → chen/natan 11:3):** the *spoil by asking* prepared; *God turns all Egypt's favor toward Israel* and *honours the mediator* — the *split complete*, only Pharaoh holding out.
2. **the mediator's hot anger (chori 11:8):** after the death-threat, Moses *burns with indignation* — *aligned with God's own anger* at the hardened evil.
3. **the purpose and the final hardening (ravah 11:9 → lev/chazaq 11:10):** the refusal *serves the multiplication of wonders* (as Israel multiplied, so the signs); and *God hardens the heart to the last* — the trajectory *culminating* at the threshold of the Passover.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** shaal (the *plunder by asking* readied); **chen/natan (the *God-given favor* that turns all Egypt toward Israel — the split complete, only Pharaoh holding out)**; **chori (the mediator's *burning anger* — Moses aligned with God's indignation)**; **ravah (the hardening's *purpose* — wonders *multiplied* as Israel multiplied)**; **lev/chazaq (the *final God-hardening* — the refusal held to the last)**.
- **Whose interior (multi-interior):** **God** — *disposing Egypt's favor*, *stating the purpose* (multiplied wonders), *hardening to the last*; **Moses** — *burning anger* (the mediator sharing God's stance); **Egypt** — *favoring Israel and honouring Moses* (the split complete); the **adversary** (Pharaoh) — *alone* in his God-sealed refusal, against a land that now favors his slaves.
- **Threads:** the **hardening trajectory culminates** (11:10 final God-hardening ← 9:12; 10:20,27; the *purpose* 11:9 "wonders multiplied" ← 7:3; 10:1–2); the **favor** enacted (chen/natan 11:3 ← 3:21 → 12:36 the plunder); the **split in Egypt complete** (11:3 ← the God-fearers 9:20; the servants 10:7 — now *all* Egypt favors Israel); the **mediator's anger** (chori 11:8 ← God's charah 4:14 — Moses aligned with God); **ravah** (the wonders multiplied as *Israel* multiplied, 1:7 — the same word, God's acts and God's people); the **distinction** (11:7 ← 8:22; 9:4,26 → the Passover night); the **plunder by asking** (shaal 11:2 ← 3:22).
- **Guarded against:** reading the final God-hardening (11:10) as erasing the *long self-hardening* that grounded it (the ledger: the God-hardening *confirms* what Pharaoh fixed himself — do not read the culmination as the whole story); over-reading chori (Moses' anger) as sinful loss of control when the verse aligns it with *God's* indignation at hardened evil; missing that ravah (11:9) is the *same word* as Israel's multiplying (1:7) — the wonders *multiply* as the people did; treating the *favor* (11:3) as Israel's merit when the verse says *God gave* it (the disposing of Egypt's heart is God's, as the hardening of Pharaoh's is); importing NT atonement over the *firstborn distinction* the passage foretells.

---

## Exodus 12:1-28 - the rite that forms the interior and the service transferred: the unblemished lamb, the sheltering blood, the remembered bitterness, the memory taught (EXO-16)

# Exodus 12:1–28 — inner-being passage reading (EXO-16-passover-instituted)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `exodus-deliverance-v1-20260705`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. **Multiple interiors**: **God** (judgment and mercy in one night), **Israel** (the interior formed by the rite — sheltered, remembering, teaching). The blood-ritual detail reads as scene-context where no non-T2 span carries it.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the 4 nephesh, 3 shamar, 2 avodah, and the mashchit/shachat pair each treated distinctly.

---

## EXO-16-passover-instituted · Exodus 12:1–28 · [the rite that forms the interior; the service transferred] — the unblemished lamb, the sheltering blood, the remembered bitterness, and the memory taught

**The passage.** "According to the number of **persons** (nephesh) you shall count for the lamb" (12:4); "the lamb shall be **without blemish** (tamim)" (12:5); "eat the **flesh** (basar)… with unleavened bread and **bitter herbs** (maror)" (12:8); "on all the gods of Egypt I will execute **judgments** (shephet)" (12:12); "the blood shall be a sign… no plague will **destroy** (mashchit) you" (12:13); "that **person** (nephesh) shall be cut off" (12:15); "a **holy** (qodesh) **assembly** (miqra)… what every **person** (nephesh) needs to eat" (12:16); "you shall **observe** (shamar) this feast" (12:17); "that **person** (nephesh) will be cut off" (12:19); Moses **called** (qara) the elders (12:21); "the LORD will not allow the **destroyer** (shachat) to enter" (12:23); "**observe** (shamar) this rite" (12:24); "when you come to the land the LORD will **give** (natan)… **keep** (shamar) this **service** (avodah)" (12:25); "when your children ask, 'what is this **service** (avodah)?'" (12:26); the people bowed and worshiped (12:27).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **nephesh (persons) — the *counted community* (12:4).** "according to the number of **persons** (nephesh) you shall count for the lamb" *(stated)* — nephesh in the *census/person* sense: the gem is *belonging* — each *person* is *counted into* a household's lamb; the interior-context is *inclusion* — no one left uncovered, the community *reckoned by persons* under the blood *(inferred: nephesh = the persons counted in — the community's inclusion)*.
- **tamim (without blemish) — the *unblemished* offering (12:5).** "your lamb shall be **without blemish** (tamim)" *(stated)* — tamim, *whole/unblemished/blameless* (the root of Noah's "blameless" 6:9; Abraham's demand 17:1; Jacob "tam" 25:27): the gem is that the *sheltering life* must be *whole* — the interior-context is *the perfect substitute*; wholeness as the condition of the covering *(inferred: tamim = the unblemished lamb — wholeness as the shelter's condition)*.
- **basar (flesh) + maror (bitter herbs) — the *remembered bitterness* in the meal (12:8).** "eat the **flesh** (basar)… with unleavened bread and **bitter herbs** (maror)" *(stated)*. **basar** — the *flesh* eaten; **maror** — the gem: **bitterness** (← marar, 1:14 "made their lives **bitter**") — the *bondage's bitterness* is *built into the feast of freedom*; Israel *eats the bitterness even as it is delivered* — the interior *remembering the affliction in the very meal that marks its end* *(inferred: basar/maror = the remembered bitterness of bondage eaten into the feast)*.
- **shephet (judgments) — the *judgment on Egypt's gods* (12:12).** "on all the gods of Egypt I will execute **judgments** (shephet)" *(stated)* — shephet, *judgment* (← 6:6; 7:4): the gem is the *spiritual dimension* — the firstborn-plague is *judgment on the gods* Egypt trusts; the divine interior *overthrowing the false powers*, not merely the people *(inferred: shephet = the judgment on Egypt's gods — the spiritual victory)*.
- **mashchit (destroy) — the *destruction the blood averts* (12:13).** "when I see the blood, I will pass over… no plague will **destroy** (mashchit) you" *(stated)* — mashchit, *destruction* (← shachat, Gen 6:11): the gem is the *blood-sign* — the *destruction* that falls on Egypt is *turned aside* where the blood is *seen* (as the covenant-blood turned aside God's severity, 4:26); the interior *sheltered by a sign it did not earn* *(inferred: mashchit = the destruction the sheltering blood averts)*.
- **nephesh (person) — the *cutting off* for leaven (12:15).** *nephesh distinct from 12:4:* "that **person** (nephesh) shall be cut off from Israel" *(stated)* — where 12:4 was *inclusion* (counted in), 12:15 is *exclusion* — the *person* who eats leaven *cut off*; the interior-context is *the community's boundary* — belonging carries an *obligation* whose breach *severs* *(inferred: nephesh = the person cut off — the community's boundary)*.
- **nephesh (everyone) + miqra (assembly) + qodesh (holy) — the *holy assembly* (12:16).** *nephesh distinct:* "a **holy** (qodesh) **assembly** (miqra)… what every **person** (nephesh) needs to eat" *(stated)*. **qodesh** — *holiness*; **miqra** — *assembly/convocation*; **nephesh** — here *each person's* need. The gem: the community *gathered as holy* — the interior *set apart for God* in assembly, its ordinary *eating* provided for even in the holy day *(inferred: qodesh/miqra/nephesh = the holy assembly — the community set apart)*.
- **shamar (observe) — the *feast kept forever* (12:17).** "you shall **observe** (shamar) the Feast of Unleavened Bread… a statute forever" *(stated)* — shamar, *keep/guard/observe*: the gem is *memory made permanent* — the deliverance *kept* as a perpetual observance; the interior *bound to remember* by rite *(inferred: shamar = the feast kept as perpetual memory)*.
- **nephesh (person) — the *cutting off*, native or sojourner (12:19).** *nephesh distinct from 12:15:* "that **person** (nephesh) will be cut off… whether sojourner or native" *(stated)* — the boundary *applies to all* (sojourner and native alike) — the interior-context is *the community's boundary is not ethnic but covenantal* *(inferred: nephesh = the person cut off, native or sojourner — the covenantal, not ethnic, boundary)*.
- **qara (called) — the *elders summoned* to the rite (12:21).** "Moses **called** (qara) the elders: 'select lambs… kill the Passover'" *(stated)* — qara, *call-to*: the *rite transmitted* through the elders to the people — the interior of *obedient transmission* *(inferred: qara = the elders summoned to enact the rite)*.
- **shachat (destroyer) — the *destroyer barred* by the blood (12:23).** *shachat distinct from mashchit 12:13:* "the LORD will not allow the **destroyer** (shachat) to enter your houses" *(stated)* — shachat, *ruin/destroy* — here the gem is *personal*: the *destroyer* (the agent) *barred at the blood-marked door*; where 12:13 was the *destruction* (the event), 12:23 is the *destroyer* (the agent) *held out* — the blood a *barrier* the interior shelters behind *(inferred: shachat = the destroyer barred at the blood-marked door)*.
- **shamar (observe) — the *rite kept for the sons* (12:24).** *shamar distinct from 12:17:* "you shall **observe** (shamar) this rite… for you and your sons forever" *(stated)* — where 12:17 kept the *feast*, 12:24 keeps the *rite for the sons* — the *generational* transmission; the interior *handing the memory down* *(inferred: shamar = the rite kept for the generations)*.
- **shamar (keep) + avodah (service) + natan (give) — the *service kept in the land* (12:25).** *shamar distinct from 12:17,24:* "when you come to the land the LORD will **give** (natan)… **keep** (shamar) this **service** (avodah)" *(stated)*. **natan** — the *land given*; **shamar** — the rite *kept in the land*; **avodah** — the gem: **service** — the *same word* as Israel's *slavery* (1:14; 5:9; 6:6) — now the *worship-service* of the Passover. The *transfer of service is enacted*: the interior's *avodah to Pharaoh becomes avodah to God* *(inferred: shamar/avodah/natan = the worship-service kept in the given land — the slavery-service transferred to God)*.
- **avodah (service) — the *rite the children question* (12:26).** *avodah distinct from 12:25:* "when your children say, 'what is this **service** (avodah)?'" *(stated)* — the gem: the *rite provokes the children's question* — the interior of the *next generation* *taught* by asking; the *avodah* (worship) *carries the story* forward (← the pedagogical purpose, 10:2) *(inferred: avodah = the worship-service that provokes the children's question — the rite that teaches)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the counted community and the unblemished shelter (nephesh 12:4 → tamim 12:5 → basar/maror 12:8):** each *person counted in* under a *whole* lamb; the meal *eaten with the remembered bitterness* of bondage — freedom *tasting* its own past.
2. **judgment and the sheltering blood (shephet 12:12 → mashchit 12:13):** God *judges Egypt's gods* and *passes over* the blood-marked — the *destruction averted by a sign*.
3. **the holy community and its boundary (nephesh 12:15 → qodesh/miqra/nephesh 12:16 → nephesh 12:19):** the *person cut off* for leaven, the *holy assembly*, the boundary *covenantal not ethnic* (sojourner and native alike) — belonging *and* its obligation.
4. **the memory kept and taught (shamar 12:17 → qara 12:21 → shachat 12:23 → shamar 12:24 → shamar/avodah/natan 12:25 → avodah 12:26 → 12:27 worship):** the feast *kept forever*, the *destroyer barred*, the rite *handed to the sons*, the *service transferred* from Pharaoh to God, and the *children's question* answered — the people *bow and worship*. The interior *formed by the rite*: sheltered, remembering, teaching, serving God.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** nephesh ×4 (12:4 the persons *counted in* / 12:15 the person *cut off* for leaven / 12:16 *each person's* need in the holy assembly / 12:19 the person cut off, *native or sojourner* — the covenantal boundary); tamim (the *unblemished* shelter); **maror (the *remembered bitterness* of bondage eaten into the feast — ← marar 1:14)**; shephet (the *judgment on Egypt's gods*); mashchit / shachat *distinguished* (12:13 the *destruction* averted / 12:23 the *destroyer* barred at the door); qodesh/miqra (the *holy assembly*); shamar ×3 (the *feast* / the *rite for the sons* / the *service in the land*); **avodah ×2 (the *worship-service* kept — the slavery-word transferred to God — / the service the *children question*)**; qara (the *elders summoned*); natan (the *land given*).
- **Whose interior (multi-interior):** **God** — *judgment and mercy in one night*, distinguishing by the *blood-sign*, overthrowing *Egypt's gods*; **Israel** — the interior *formed by the rite*: *counted in* under the unblemished lamb, *remembering the bitterness*, *sheltered from the destroyer*, *keeping the memory*, *teaching the children*, and *serving God* (the avodah transferred). The rite *makes* the community's interior.
- **Threads:** the **transfer of service** *enacted* (avodah 12:25–26 ← slavery 1:14; 5:9; 6:6 → "let my people **serve** me" 3:12; 7:16 — the slavery-service *becomes worship*); the **remembered bitterness** (maror 12:8 ← marar 1:14 — the bondage tasted in the feast); the **pedagogical rite** (avodah 12:26 ← 10:2; → 13:8,14 — the story told to the children); the **covenant-blood averting destruction** (mashchit/shachat 12:13,23 ← 4:26 the bridegroom of blood; the destroyer barred); **tamim** (the unblemished ← Noah 6:9; Abraham 17:1); the **holy community** (qodesh 12:16 → Sinai, "a kingdom of priests"); the **judgment on the gods** (shephet 12:12 — the spiritual victory).
- **Guarded against:** lumping the four nephesh (counted-in / cut-off-leaven / each-person / cut-off-native-or-sojourner) or three shamar (feast / rite-for-sons / service-in-land) or two avodah (kept / questioned); merging mashchit (the destruction) with shachat (the destroyer) — event vs agent; over-reading tamim into NT lamb-Christology (1 Cor 5:7) over the *unblemished-shelter* the passage gives; importing atonement theology beyond what the *blood-sign averts destruction* text carries; missing that avodah (12:25–26) is the *slavery-word now meaning worship* — the transfer of service is the chapter's quiet climax; treating maror as a mere ritual detail when it *builds the remembered bitterness* into the feast.

---

## Exodus 12:29-51 - the hardening broken by death and the word turned: Pharaoh yields and begs a blessing, Egypt urgently expels, Israel plunders and goes out (EXO-17)

# Exodus 12:29–51 — inner-being passage reading (EXO-17-firstborn-exodus-plunder)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `exodus-deliverance-v1-20260705`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. **Multiple interiors**: the **adversary** (Pharaoh — the hardening broken by death), **Egypt** (terror-driven expulsion), and **Israel** (delivered, plundering, the community opened). The Passover ordinance (12:43–51) is a **thin** tail — read as scene-context except the one-law/flesh notes.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the 2 shaal treated distinctly. **Hardening note:** 12:31 shows the *hardening broken* — but only by the death of the firstborn (the deepest loss); and 12:33 turns the hardening-word `chazaq` on Egypt itself.

---

## EXO-17-firstborn-exodus-plunder · Exodus 12:29–51 · [the hardening broken by death; the word turned] — Pharaoh yields and begs a blessing, Egypt urgently expels, and Israel plunders and goes out

**The passage.** At midnight the firstborn struck; a great cry (12:29–30); Pharaoh **summoned** (qara) Moses: "go, **serve** (avad) the LORD… and bless me!" (12:31–32); "the Egyptians were **urgent** (chazaq)… 'we shall all be dead'" (12:33); the people **asked** (shaal) for silver and gold (12:35); "the LORD **gave** (natan) them **favor** (chen)… they let them have what they **asked** (shaal); thus they plundered Egypt" (12:36); the exodus; a mixed multitude (12:38); the night of watching (12:42); "no… of its **flesh** (basar) outside the house" (12:46); "one law for native and stranger" (12:49); "the LORD brought Israel out" (12:51).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **qara (summoned) + avad (serve) — the *hardening broken*, the service granted (12:31).** "Pharaoh **summoned** (qara) Moses by night: 'go out… **serve** (avad) the LORD, as you have said'" *(stated)*. **qara** — the gem of *reversal*: the man who said *"never see my face again"* (10:28) now *summons* Moses *by night*; **avad** — he *grants the whole demand* — *"serve the LORD, as you have said"* — the *transfer of service* finally *conceded*. But the price was the *death of his own firstborn*: the God-sealed heart *cracked only at the deepest loss* — and (12:32, "bless me also!") the adversary even *begs a blessing* from the God he defied. The interior *broken, yielding, and grasping for blessing* — too late *(inferred: qara/avad = the hardening broken by death — the service granted, a blessing begged)*.
- **chazaq (urgent) — the *hardening-word turned on Egypt* (12:33).** "the Egyptians were **urgent** (chazaq) with the people to send them out… 'we shall all be dead'" *(stated)* — the gem: **chazaq** — the *very root* that *hardened Pharaoh's heart* (7:13; 9:12; 10:20,27; 11:10) — now describes *Egypt's urgent pushing of Israel OUT*. The *strengthening/firmness* that *held Israel in* is *turned to expelling them*; and its *driver is terror* ("we shall all be dead"). The word of the hardening *recoils* — the grip that *held* now *thrusts out* *(inferred: chazaq = the hardening-word turned to Egypt's terror-driven expulsion — the grip become a thrust)*.
- **shaal (asked) — the *plunder requested* (12:35).** "the people had **asked** (shaal) the Egyptians for silver and gold and clothing" *(stated)* — shaal *(← 3:22; 11:2)*: the *spoil requested* — the interior *receiving the wealth of its bondage by asking*, on the way out *(inferred: shaal = the plunder requested)*.
- **shaal (asked) + chen (favor) + natan (given) — the *plunder granted* (12:36).** *shaal distinct from 12:35:* "the LORD **gave** (natan) them **favor** (chen)… they let them have what they **asked** (shaal); thus they plundered Egypt" *(stated)*. **natan/chen** — *God gave the favor* that *disposed Egypt to grant* the request; **shaal** — the *asking granted*. The gem: the plunder is *God-given favor*, not seizure — Egypt *willingly gives* its wealth (the oppressor's goods *transferred to the freed*, ← 3:21). The interior of *Egypt disposed* and *Israel enriched by gift* *(inferred: shaal/chen/natan = the plunder granted by God-given favor — the oppressor's wealth given)*.
- **basar (flesh) — the *Passover flesh* bounded to the house (12:46).** "you shall not take any of the **flesh** (basar) outside the house, nor break a bone" *(stated)* — basar, *flesh* (← 12:8): the ordinance *binds the meal to the household* — the interior-context is *the sheltered community's* rite kept *within its door* *(inferred: basar = the Passover flesh bounded to the sheltering house)*.
- **(12:49 — "one law for native and stranger"; no non-T2 span.)** Flagged: the *one-law* statute (with circumcision as entry, 12:48) carries no flagged span, but it *opens the community* — the *mixed multitude* (12:38) and the *sojourner* may *belong* on the *same terms* as the native; the interior-context is *a community covenantal not ethnic* (← 12:19). Read as scene-context *(no-span context; the community opened to the stranger)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the hardening broken by death (qara/avad 12:31):** the firstborn struck, and *Pharaoh summons the mediator he banished*, *grants the whole service*, and *begs a blessing* — the God-sealed heart *cracked only at the deepest loss*, and *too late*.
2. **the word turned, Egypt expels (chazaq 12:33):** the *hardening-word* now names *Egypt's terror-driven urgency to thrust Israel out* — the grip that *held* become a *thrust*, driven by "we shall all be dead."
3. **the plunder by God-given favor (shaal 12:35 → shaal/chen/natan 12:36):** Israel *asks* and *God's favor grants it* — the *oppressor's wealth given*, not seized; the freed *enriched by gift*.
4. **the exodus and the opened community (12:37–42 → basar 12:46 → 12:49):** the *hosts go out* on the *night of watching*, a *mixed multitude* with them; the rite *bounded to the sheltering house* yet *open to the stranger* on *one law* — the delivered community *formed and opened* in the going-out.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** **qara/avad (the *hardening broken by death* — Pharaoh summons the banished mediator, grants the service, begs a blessing — too late)**; **chazaq (the *hardening-word turned on Egypt* — its terror-driven expulsion; the grip become a thrust)**; shaal ×2 (the plunder *requested* / *granted*); chen/natan (the *God-given favor* disposing Egypt to give); basar (the Passover flesh *bounded to the house*); the *one-law* opening to the stranger (no-span context).
- **Whose interior (multi-interior):** the **adversary** (Pharaoh) — the *hardening finally broken*, but *only by the death of his firstborn*, and even then *grasping for a blessing* (the hard heart cracks at the deepest loss); **Egypt** — *terror-driven expulsion* (the hardening-word now *theirs*) and *willing surrender of its wealth*; **Israel** — *delivered, enriched by gift, formed by the watching-night, opened to the mixed multitude and the stranger*.
- **Threads:** the **hardening trajectory's END** — broken *at the firstborn's death* (12:31 ← the long self/God-hardening; it took the *ultimate loss* to crack it — the deeper trend: a heart that yields *only* under total judgment); the **chazaq wordplay** (12:33 the hardening-word now *Egypt's expelling* ← 7:13ff Pharaoh's heart; the grip turned to a thrust); the **plunder by favor** (shaal/chen/natan 12:35–36 ← 3:21–22; 11:2–3 — the oppressor's wealth *given*); the **transfer of service** *granted* (avad 12:31 ← 3:12; the demand finally conceded); the **opened community** (mixed multitude 12:38; one law 12:49 ← 12:19,48 — covenantal not ethnic); the **firstborn-for-firstborn** consummated (12:29 ← 4:23 "let my son go… or I kill your firstborn").
- **Guarded against:** reading Pharaoh's yield (12:31) as *repentance* when it is *collapse under the deepest loss* (and he still *grasps for a blessing*); missing the **chazaq wordplay** (the hardening-word turned to Egypt's expelling — the grip become a thrust); reading the plunder as *theft* when the verse makes it *God-given favor* granting a *request* (12:36); over-reading "not break a bone" (12:46) into NT typology (John 19:36) over the *household-bounded* rite; treating the mixed multitude / one-law as incidental when they *open the community* to the stranger (the covenantal, not ethnic, boundary — the chapter's quiet universal note).

---

## Exodus 13:1-16 - the interior formed by memory and redemption: consecrate the firstborn, remember by a strong hand, redeem the belonging (EXO-18)

# Exodus 13:1–16 — inner-being passage reading (EXO-18-consecrate-strong-hand)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `exodus-deliverance-v1-20260705`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. **Multiple interiors**: **Israel** (the interior formed by memory, redemption, teaching) and **God** (the redeemer "by a strong hand"). **Note:** 13:15 "Pharaoh **stubbornly refused**" (qashah) has no flagged span, but it places the *hardening into the catechism* — read as scene-context.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the 3 chozeq, 2 natan, 2 padah each treated distinctly.

---

## EXO-18-consecrate-strong-hand · Exodus 13:1–16 · [the interior formed by memory and redemption] — consecrate the firstborn, remember by a strong hand, and redeem the belonging

**The passage.** "**Consecrate** (qadash) to me all the firstborn… is mine" (13:2); "**Remember** (zakhar) this day… by a **strong** (chozeq) hand the LORD brought you out" (13:3); "**keep** (avad) this **service** (avodah)… the land he swore to **give** (natan)" (13:5); "**keep** (shamar) this statute yearly" (13:10); "when the LORD… shall **give** (natan) it to you" (13:11); "every firstborn of a donkey you shall **redeem** (padah)… your sons you shall redeem" (13:13); "when your son **asks** (shaal)… 'by a **strong** (chozeq) hand the LORD brought us out'" (13:14); "Pharaoh stubbornly refused… therefore… all the firstborn of my sons I **redeem** (padah)" (13:15); "by a **strong** (chozeq) hand the LORD brought us out" (13:16).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **qadash (consecrate) — the firstborn *set apart as God's* (13:2).** "**Consecrate** (qadash) to me all the firstborn… is mine" *(stated)* — qadash, *make holy/set apart/dedicate*: the gem is *belonging* — because God *spared* Israel's firstborn (and struck Egypt's), *every* firstborn is now *God's*; the interior-context is *the firstborn dedicated* — the community's *first and best set apart to God* (a claim answering the firstborn-death) *(inferred: qadash = the firstborn consecrated as God's — belonging by the sparing)*.
- **zakhar (remember) + chozeq (strong) — the *memory-command* (13:3).** "**Remember** (zakhar) this day… out of the house of slavery, for by a **strong** (chozeq) hand the LORD brought you out" *(stated)*. **zakhar** — the gem: *Israel commanded to remember* — the reciprocal of *God's remembering* (2:24 "God remembered the covenant"); now *Israel remembers the deliverance*; **chozeq** — *"by a strong hand"* — the refrain of the deliverance's *power*. The interior *bound to remember* the day of freedom *(inferred: zakhar/chozeq = the memory-command — Israel remembering the strong-handed deliverance)*.
- **avad (keep) + avodah (service) + natan (give) — the *worship-service in the land* (13:5).** "you shall **keep** (avad) this **service** (avodah)… the land he swore to **give** (natan)" *(stated)*. **avad**/**avodah** — *the worship-service* (← 12:25; the transfer of service continued — slavery-word now worship); **natan** — the *land given*. The interior *keeping God's service in the promised place* *(inferred: avad/avodah/natan = the worship-service kept in the given land)*.
- **shamar (keep) — the *statute kept yearly* (13:10).** "you shall **keep** (shamar) this statute at its appointed time year to year" *(stated)* — shamar, *keep/observe*: the *annual* keeping — the interior's *rhythm of remembrance* *(inferred: shamar = the statute kept in yearly rhythm)*.
- **natan (give) — the land *given* as sworn (13:11).** *natan distinct from 13:5:* "when the LORD… shall **give** (natan) it to you, as he swore" *(stated)* — the *land given* as the *condition* of the firstborn-consecration that follows; the interior's *inheritance* the setting of its worship *(inferred: natan = the land given, the setting of the firstborn-rite)*.
- **padah (redeem) — the *redemption law* (13:13).** "every firstborn of a donkey you shall **redeem** (padah)… your sons you shall redeem" *(stated)* — padah, *ransom/redeem*: the gem — because the firstborn *belong to God* (13:2), they must be *bought back*; the *unclean* animal *redeemed by a lamb* (or its neck broken), the *sons redeemed*. The interior-context is *the belonging bought back* — what is God's is *ransomed* to be kept *(inferred: padah = the firstborn redeemed — the belonging ransomed back)*.
- **shaal (asks) + chozeq (strong) — the *son's catechism* (13:14).** "when your son **asks** (shaal), 'what does this mean?' you shall say, 'by a **strong** (chozeq) hand the LORD brought us out'" *(stated)*. **shaal** — the gem: the *rite provokes the son's question* (← 12:26); **chozeq** *distinct from 13:3* — now the *strong hand* is the *catechism answer* (13:3 was Moses' proclamation; 13:14 is the *son taught*). The interior of the *next generation* *formed by asking and being told* *(inferred: shaal/chozeq = the son's question answered by the strong-hand deliverance — the catechism)*.
- **padah (redeem) — the redemption's *reason* (13:15).** *padah distinct from 13:13:* "Pharaoh stubbornly refused… the LORD killed all the firstborn… therefore… my sons I **redeem** (padah)" *(stated)* — where 13:13 was the *law*, 13:15 is the *reason*: the firstborn are redeemed *because* God *struck Egypt's firstborn and spared Israel's*. The gem: the catechism *includes the hardening* — *"Pharaoh stubbornly refused"* (qashah) is *taught to the child* — the adversary's hardening *woven into Israel's story*; and the redemption *grounded in the sparing* *(inferred: padah = the redemption grounded in the firstborn-sparing — the hardening taught as its cause)*.
- **chozeq (strong) — the *strong hand marked on the body* (13:16).** *chozeq distinct from 13:3,14:* "it shall be as a mark on your hand or frontlets between your eyes, for by a **strong** (chozeq) hand the LORD brought us out" *(stated)* — the *third* strong-hand refrain, now *bound to the body* (hand, eyes) — the interior's memory *made bodily and permanent* *(inferred: chozeq = the strong-hand deliverance marked on the body — memory made permanent)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the firstborn consecrated, the day remembered (qadash 13:2 → zakhar/chozeq 13:3):** because God *spared* Israel's firstborn, they are *set apart as his*; and Israel is *commanded to remember* the strong-handed deliverance — the reciprocal of God's own remembering (2:24).
2. **the service kept, the land given (avad/avodah/natan 13:5 → shamar 13:10 → natan 13:11):** the *worship-service* kept in the *given land*, in yearly rhythm — the interior's remembrance *ritualised in place and time*.
3. **the belonging redeemed and the child taught (padah 13:13 → shaal/chozeq 13:14 → padah 13:15 → chozeq 13:16):** the firstborn *redeemed* (bought back to God), the *son's question answered* by the strong-hand story — a catechism that *includes the hardening* ("Pharaoh stubbornly refused") — and the memory *marked on the body*. The interior *formed by memory, redemption, and teaching*.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** qadash (the firstborn *consecrated as God's* — belonging by the sparing); **zakhar (the *memory-command* — Israel remembering, reciprocal of God's remembering 2:24)**; chozeq ×3 (the *strong hand* — Moses' *proclamation* 13:3 / the son's *catechism answer* 13:14 / the *bodily mark* 13:16); avad/avodah (the *worship-service* — slavery-word transferred); natan ×2 (the land *given* — setting of service / setting of the firstborn-rite); shamar (the *yearly* keeping); **padah ×2 (the redemption *law* / its *reason* — the firstborn *redeemed* because spared)**; **shaal (the *son's question* — the rite that teaches)**; the hardening *in the catechism* (13:15 "stubbornly refused" — no-span context).
- **Whose interior (multi-interior):** **Israel** — the interior *formed by memory (zakhar), redemption (padah), and teaching (shaal)*: the firstborn *consecrated and redeemed* (belonging to God, bought back), the deliverance *remembered, ritualised, marked on the body, and taught to the children* — including *the adversary's hardening* as part of the story; **God** — the *redeemer "by a strong hand"* who *claims and spares the firstborn*.
- **Threads:** the **reciprocal remembering** (zakhar 13:3 ← God remembered 2:24 — God remembers the covenant, Israel remembers the deliverance); the **transfer of service** (avodah 13:5 ← 12:25; slavery 1:14 → worship); the **pedagogical rite** (shaal 13:14 ← 12:26; 10:2 — the story told to the children, *including the hardening* 13:15); the **firstborn** (qadash/padah 13:2,13 ← the firstborn-death 12:29; "Israel my firstborn" 4:22 — spared, so consecrated and redeemed); the **strong hand** refrain (chozeq 13:3,14,16 ← "with a strong hand he will drive you out" 6:1); the **hardening in the catechism** (13:15 qashah — the child *taught* the whole story, adversary included — the deeper trend: the hardening *serves the telling*, ← 10:2).
- **Guarded against:** lumping the three chozeq (proclamation / catechism / bodily-mark), two natan, two padah (law / reason); reading qadash/padah as later sacrificial theology over the *belonging-by-sparing* the passage gives; missing that the catechism (13:15) *includes* Pharaoh's hardening — the child learns the *whole* story (the hardening *serves the generational telling*, per the ledger's pedagogical thread); over-reading the frontlets (13:16) as later phylactery-law over the *memory-made-bodily* the verse states; treating the firstborn-redemption as merely legal when it enacts *Israel's own firstborn spared and bought back to God*.

---

## Exodus 15:1-21 - worship as the interior's endpoint: the freed people sing the divine warrior of power and steadfast love, the enemy's appetite drowned, the nations struck still (EXO-20)

# Exodus 15:1–21 — inner-being passage reading (EXO-20-song-of-the-sea)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `exodus-deliverance-v1-20260705`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. **Multiple interiors**: **Israel** (worship — the arc's culmination), the **divine warrior** (power + chesed), the **enemy** (greedy appetite quoted), and the **nations** (dread). **Note:** the second chesed span at 15:13 carries an alternate gloss "shame"; the word is chesed = *steadfast love*, read as such.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the 2 gaah, 2 oz, 2 oyev, 2 qodesh, the paired chesed each treated distinctly.

---

## EXO-20-song-of-the-sea · Exodus 15:1–21 · [worship as the interior's endpoint] — the freed people sing: the divine warrior of power and steadfast love, the enemy's appetite drowned, the nations struck still

**The passage.** "I will sing… he has **triumphed** (gaah) gloriously" (15:1); "the LORD is my **strength** (oz) and my **song** (zimrat)… I will **exalt** (rum) him" (15:2); "Pharaoh's **host** (chayil) he cast into the sea" (15:4); "your right hand, glorious in **power** (koach), shatters the **enemy** (oyev)" (15:6); "you send your **fury** (charon)… your **majesty** (gaon)" (15:7); "the deeps congealed in the **heart** (lev) of the sea" (15:8); "the **enemy** (oyev) said, 'I will pursue… my **desire** (nephesh) shall have its fill'" (15:9); "who is like you, **awesome** (yare) in **holiness** (qodesh)… in **praises** (tehillah), doing **wonders** (pele)?" (15:11); "you led in your **steadfast love** (chesed)… guided by your **strength** (oz) to your **holy** (qodesh) abode" (15:13); "the peoples **tremble** (ragaz)" (15:14); "**trembling** (raad)… **dismayed** (bahal)" (15:15); "**Terror** (emah) and **dread** (pachad) fall… **still** (damam) as a stone" (15:16); "the LORD will reign forever" (15:18); Miriam: "sing… he has **triumphed** (gaah)" (15:21).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **gaah (triumphed) — the *exultant opening* (15:1).** "I will sing… he has **triumphed** (gaah) gloriously; the horse and rider he threw into the sea" *(stated)* — gaah, *rise up / be exalted / triumph*: the gem is the *interior's exultation* — the freed people's first act *after* fear-and-faith (14:31) is *song*; the deliverance *overflows in praise* of God's triumph *(inferred: gaah = the exultant song of God's triumph — worship as the interior's overflow)*.
- **oz (strength) + zimrat (song) + rum (exalt) — *God made the interior's music* (15:2).** "the LORD is my **strength** (oz) and my **song** (zimrat)… I will **exalt** (rum) him" *(stated)*. **oz** — *strength* (God *is* the interior's strength); **zimrat** — *song* (God *is* the interior's music); **rum** — *exalt* (← the staff raised 14:16; the defiant exit 14:8 — now *God* lifted up). The gem: the interior *makes God its strength, its song, and lifts him high* — worship as *the whole self turned Godward* *(inferred: oz/zimrat/rum = God made the interior's strength, song, and exaltation)*.
- **chayil (host) — the *might cast down* (15:4).** "Pharaoh's chariots and **host** (chayil) he cast into the sea" *(stated)* — chayil *(← 14:4,28)*: the *mustered might*, now *sung as sunk* — the interior *recounting the adversary's power undone* *(inferred: chayil = the host cast into the sea — the might undone, sung)*.
- **koach (power) + oyev (enemy) — the *right hand that shatters* (15:6).** "your right hand, glorious in **power** (koach), shatters the **enemy** (oyev)" *(stated)*. **koach** — *power* (← 9:16, God's power shown); **oyev** — *enemy*: the divine interior *sung as the shattering power* — the strength that judged Egypt *praised* *(inferred: koach/oyev = the right hand's power shattering the enemy)*.
- **charon (fury) + gaon (majesty) — the *consuming wrath and majesty* (15:7).** "in your **majesty** (gaon) you overthrow… you send your **fury** (charon); it consumes like stubble" *(stated)*. **charon** — *burning anger*; **gaon** — *majesty/height* (God's exaltedness): the gem is the divine interior's *wrath* (charon) *and* *majesty* (gaon) *together* — the fury that *consumes the adversary* is an aspect of God's *greatness* *(inferred: charon/gaon = the consuming fury and the majesty — God's wrath as glory)*.
- **lev (heart) — the *heart of the sea* (15:8).** "the deeps congealed in the **heart** (lev) of the sea" *(stated)* — lev in the *idiomatic "midst"* sense (the sea's *core*): a *non-interior* use — the *depths of the sea* where the waters stood; noted distinctly *for its idiom* (not a heart-operation) *(inferred: lev = the "heart"/midst of the sea — the idiomatic core, not an interior)*.
- **oyev (enemy) + nephesh (desire) — the *adversary's greedy appetite quoted* (15:9).** *oyev distinct from 15:6:* "the **enemy** (oyev) said, 'I will pursue, overtake, divide the spoil; my **desire** (nephesh) shall have its fill'" *(stated)*. **oyev** — now the *enemy speaking*; **nephesh** — the gem: *appetite/craving* — the adversary's *interior quoted* — a *greedy, violent nephesh* ("my desire shall have its fill… I will destroy"). The song *voices the enemy's craving* — and then drowns it (15:10); the adversary's *appetite* is his epitaph *(inferred: oyev/nephesh = the enemy's greedy appetite quoted — the craving that is drowned)*.
- **yare (awesome) + qodesh (holiness) + tehillah (praises) + pele (wonders) — *God incomparable, the object of awe* (15:11).** "who is like you, **awesome** (yare) in **holiness** (qodesh)… in **praises** (tehillah), doing **wonders** (pele)?" *(stated)*. **yare** — the gem: *God himself is "awesome"* — the *fear-of-God* now *in worship* (the reverence the midwives had 1:17; Israel now 14:31 — here *sung*); **qodesh** — *holiness*; **tehillah** — *praises*; **pele** — *wonders* (← pala 3:20; Gen 18:14). The interior *stands in awe* — *"who is like you?"* — worship as *wonder at the incomparable God* *(inferred: yare/qodesh/tehillah/pele = God the awesome, holy, wonder-working — worship as awe at the incomparable)*.
- **chesed (steadfast love) + oz (strength) + qodesh (holy) — *the warrior who is also love* (15:13).** *oz/qodesh distinct from 15:2,11:* "you led in your **steadfast love** (chesed) the people you **redeemed**… guided by your **strength** (oz) to your **holy** (qodesh) abode" *(stated)*. **chesed** — the gem: the *divine warrior* (15:3 "a man of war") is *also* **steadfast love** — the deliverance is an act of *chesed*, and the redeemed are *led by chesed*; **oz** *distinct from 15:2* — now the *strength that guides* (not the interior's strength but God's leading); **qodesh** *distinct from 15:11* — the *holy abode* (destination). The divine interior: *power that destroys the enemy* and *steadfast love that leads the redeemed home* *(inferred: chesed/oz/qodesh = the warrior's steadfast love leading the redeemed to the holy place)*.
- **ragaz (tremble) — the *nations trembling* (15:14).** "the peoples have heard; they **tremble** (ragaz)" *(stated)* — ragaz, *tremble/quake*: the gem — the *report* of the deliverance *seizes the watching nations*; the interior of *the peoples shaken* by what God has done *(inferred: ragaz = the nations trembling at the report)*.
- **raad (trembling) + bahal (dismayed) — the *dread spreading* (15:15).** "**trembling** (raad) seizes Moab's leaders; the inhabitants of Canaan are **dismayed** (bahal)" *(stated)*. **raad** — *trembling*; **bahal** — *dismay/terror*: the dread *spreads nation by nation* (Edom, Moab, Canaan) — the interior of *the peoples melting* before the coming redeemed *(inferred: raad/bahal = the dread spreading through the nations)*.
- **emah (terror) + pachad (dread) + damam (still) — the *nations struck motionless* (15:16).** "**Terror** (emah) and **dread** (pachad) fall… they are **still** (damam) as a stone, till your people pass by" *(stated)*. **emah** — *terror*; **pachad** — *dread* (← the "Fear/Dread of Isaac", Gen 31:42); **damam** — *be silent/still*: the gem — the nations *struck motionless as stone* by *terror and dread* (contrast Israel's *charesh*-stillness of *faith*, 14:14; here the nations' *stillness of dread*). The interior of *the peoples paralysed* while the redeemed *pass* *(inferred: emah/pachad/damam = the nations struck still as stone by terror and dread)*.
- **gaah (triumphed) — the *antiphon closed* (15:21).** *gaah distinct from 15:1:* "Miriam sang: 'sing… he has **triumphed** (gaah) gloriously'" *(stated)* — where 15:1 Moses *opened*, 15:21 Miriam and the women *answer* with tambourines and dancing — the gem: worship is *communal, embodied, antiphonal* — the interior's praise *shared and danced*; the song *taken up by the women* *(inferred: gaah = the antiphonal close — communal, embodied worship)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the interior overflows in song (gaah 15:1 → oz/zimrat/rum 15:2):** the freed people, having *feared and believed* (14:31), *sing* — making God their *strength, song, and exaltation*; worship the *interior's overflow*.
2. **the warrior praised (chayil 15:4 → koach/oyev 15:6 → charon/gaon 15:7 → lev 15:8 → oyev/nephesh 15:9 → 15:10):** the song *recounts* the adversary's *might cast down*, the *right hand's power*, the *consuming fury and majesty*, and *quotes the enemy's greedy appetite* (nephesh) — which the sea *drowns*.
3. **awe at the incomparable, led by steadfast love (yare/qodesh/tehillah/pele 15:11 → chesed/oz/qodesh 15:13):** *"who is like you?"* — the interior *stands in awe*; and the *warrior* is *also steadfast love* — the redeemed *led by chesed* to the *holy place*.
4. **the nations struck still (ragaz 15:14 → raad/bahal 15:15 → emah/pachad/damam 15:16 → 15:18):** the *report* seizes the peoples with *trembling, dismay, terror, and dread* — *still as stone* — while the redeemed *pass by*; "the LORD will reign forever."
5. **the antiphon of the people (gaah 15:21):** Miriam and the women *answer* Moses' song with *tambourines and dancing* — worship *communal, embodied, shared*. The interior's endpoint: **the freed people singing.**

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** gaah ×2 (Moses' *opening* / Miriam's *antiphonal close* — communal, embodied worship); oz ×2 (God *my strength* / the *strength that guides*); zimrat/rum (God *made song*, *exalted*); chayil (the *host* sung as sunk); koach/oyev (the *power* shattering the enemy); charon/gaon (the *consuming fury and majesty*); **lev (the *idiomatic "heart"/midst* of the sea — not an interior)**; **nephesh (the *enemy's greedy appetite* quoted — the craving drowned)**; oyev ×2 (enemy *shattered* / enemy *boasting*); **yare (God himself *awesome* — the fear-of-God in worship)**; qodesh ×2 (majestic *in holiness* / the *holy abode*); tehillah/pele (praises / wonders); **chesed (the *warrior who is also steadfast love* — the redeemed led by chesed)**; the *terror-cluster* ragaz/raad/bahal/emah/pachad/damam (the *nations struck still* by dread — vs Israel's *charesh*-stillness of faith 14:14).
- **Whose interior (multi-interior):** **Israel** — the arc's *culmination in worship*: groan (2:23) → fear/faith (14:31) → *song* (15) — the interior *overflowing Godward*, *communal and embodied* (Miriam, dancing); the **divine warrior** — *power that shatters the enemy* (koach, charon) *and* *steadfast love that leads the redeemed* (chesed) — the two held together; the **enemy** — a *greedy appetite* (nephesh) quoted and drowned; the **nations** — *trembling and dread*, struck *still as stone*.
- **Threads:** **Israel's arc completed** (song 15 ← the groan 2:23; fear/faith 14:31 — the interior's journey from *bondage-groan* to *freedom-song*); the **fear-of-God in worship** (yare 15:11 — God *awesome* ← the midwives 1:17; Israel 14:31 — reverence become praise); the divine **warrior + chesed** (15:3,13 — power and steadfast love together ← the chesed of Gen 24; 32:10); **pele/wonders** (15:11 ← pala 3:20; Gen 18:14 — the wonder-working God); the **dread of God** on the nations (pachad 15:16 ← the "Dread of Isaac" Gen 31:42) drawing toward the land (15:17 "your holy abode… the sanctuary" → Sinai and beyond); the **stillness** contrast (damam 15:16 the nations' *dread*-stillness vs charesh 14:14 Israel's *faith*-stillness); the **enemy's appetite** (nephesh 15:9 — the craving that destroys itself).
- **Guarded against:** lumping the two gaah/oz/oyev/qodesh (opening/close; my-strength/guiding-strength; shattered/boasting; majestic-in-holiness/holy-abode); reading a "shame" operation into the mis-glossed second chesed (the word is *steadfast love*); treating lev (15:8) as an interior when it is the *idiomatic midst* of the sea; over-reading the Song into later liturgical/typological frames (the new-exodus, Rev 15:3) over the *worship-response* the passage is; missing that the divine interior here holds *warrior and chesed together* (not wrath *or* love, but power *and* steadfast love); noting that Israel's arc *culminates but does not end* in the song — the wilderness (15:22, Marah) tests it again the very next verse.

---

## Genesis 37:12-36 - the dream attacked, the father deceived and grieving: the murder-plot, the sale, the deceiver deceived by a goat (JOS-02)

# Genesis 37:12–36 — inner-being passage reading (JOS-02-sold-jacobs-grief)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-joseph-v1-20260705`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. **Multiple interiors**: the **brothers** (murder-plot, fractured by Reuben/Judah, deceiving), **Joseph** (obedient, silent victim), and **Jacob** (inconsolable grief). The goat-blood deception (37:31–33) reads with its Gen-27 echo.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the 2 baqash, 3 shama, 2 chayyah, 2 ra, and aval/avel each treated distinctly.

---

## JOS-02-sold-jacobs-grief · Genesis 37:12–36 · [the dream attacked; the father deceived and grieving] — the murder-plot, the sale, and the deceiver deceived by a goat

**The passage.** "See if it is **well** (shalom) with your brothers" (37:14); a man **asked** (shaal), "what are you **seeking** (baqash)?"; "I am **seeking** (baqash) my brothers" (37:15–16); "I **heard** (shama) them say, Dothan" (37:17); the plot — "let us kill him… a **fierce** (ra) **animal** (chayyah) devoured him… see what becomes of his dreams" (37:20); Reuben **heard** (shama) — "let us not take his **life** (nephesh)" (37:21); Judah — "he is our **flesh** (basar)… his brothers **listened** (shama)" (37:27); sold to Egypt; the bloodied robe; "a **fierce** (ra) **animal** (chayyah) has devoured him" (37:33); Jacob **mourned** (aval, 37:34), refused **comfort** (nacham), "I shall go down… **mourning** (avel)… he **wept** (bakhah)" (37:35).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **shalom (well) — the *errand of peace* into hatred (37:14).** "see if it is **well** (shalom) with your brothers, and bring me word" *(stated)* — shalom, *well-being/peace*: the gem is the *irony* — Joseph is sent to check his brothers' *shalom*, and walks into their *murderous hatred* (the brothers who *could not speak peaceably*, 37:4). The errand *of peace* meets the *absence of peace* *(inferred: shalom = the peace-errand walking into hatred)*.
- **shaal (asked) + baqash (seeking) — the *seeking* that leads to the pit (37:15).** "a man **asked** (shaal): 'what are you **seeking** (baqash)?'" *(stated)*. **shaal** — the stranger's *question*; **baqash** — *seek*: Joseph *seeking his brothers* — the gem is the *unwitting* seeking that *walks him toward the trap* *(inferred: shaal/baqash = the seeking that leads Joseph to his attackers)*.
- **baqash (seeking) — the *object named* (37:16).** *baqash distinct from 37:15:* "'I am **seeking** (baqash) my brothers'" *(stated)* — Joseph *names his errand* — *his brothers* — the very ones plotting his death; the interior *earnestly seeking those who hate him* *(inferred: baqash = the brothers named as the sought)*.
- **shama (heard) — the *informant's word* (37:17).** "'I **heard** (shama) them say, let us go to Dothan'" *(stated)* — shama, *hear*: the stranger's *overheard direction* *sends Joseph on* to Dothan — the providence-thread (a chance word steering the story) *(inferred: shama = the overheard word that steers Joseph on)*.
- **chayyah (animal) + ra (fierce) — the *cover-lie planned* (37:20).** "'let us kill him… a **fierce** (ra) **animal** (chayyah) has devoured him… see what becomes of his dreams'" *(stated)*. **chayyah** — *living thing/beast*; **ra** — *evil/fierce*: the gem is the *lie prepared in advance* — a *wild beast* to be blamed — *and* the motive: *"see what becomes of his dreams"* — **killing the dreamer to kill the dream**. The interior's murderous scheme *aimed at the dream itself* *(inferred: chayyah/ra = the beast-lie planned to cover the murder — the dream attacked)*.
- **shama (heard) + nephesh (life) — Reuben's *restraint* (37:21).** *shama distinct from 37:17:* "when Reuben **heard** (shama) it, he rescued him: 'let us not take his **life** (nephesh)'" *(stated)*. **shama** — Reuben *hears the plot* and it *moves him to intervene*; **nephesh** — *life*: the gem is the *partial restraint* — Reuben *stops the killing* (throw him in the pit, meaning to rescue him later). The interior of a *conscience-flicker* amid the hatred *(inferred: shama/nephesh = Reuben's hearing that restrains the killing)*.
- **basar (flesh) + shama (listened) — Judah's *mixed motive* (37:27).** *shama distinct from 37:17,21:* "'let us sell him… he is our brother, our **flesh** (basar)'… his brothers **listened** (shama)" *(stated)*. **basar** — *flesh/kin*: the gem is the *mixed motive* — Judah's *"he is our flesh"* (a kinship-flicker) *fused with* "what profit is it?" (37:26, gain) — *sell* rather than kill; **shama** — the brothers *heed Judah*. The interior *sparing the brother for profit-and-kinship both* (a lesser evil, not repentance) *(inferred: basar/shama = the kinship-and-profit motive that sells rather than kills)*.
- **chayyah (animal) + ra (fierce) — the *lie believed* (37:33).** *chayyah/ra distinct from 37:20:* "'a **fierce** (ra) **animal** (chayyah) has devoured him; Joseph is torn to pieces'" *(stated)* — where 37:20 *planned* the beast-lie, 37:33 is the *father speaking it as fact* — the deception *works*; the interior *of the deceived father* concluding exactly what the deceivers intended. And the gem-irony: the brothers deceive Jacob with a *goat's blood* (37:31) — *as Jacob deceived Isaac with goat-skins and goat-meat* (Gen 27); **the deceiver deceived by a goat, one generation on** *(inferred: chayyah/ra = the beast-lie believed — the deceiver deceived by a goat)*.
- **aval (mourned) — the *father's mourning* (37:34).** "Jacob tore his garments… and **mourned** (aval) for his son many days" *(stated)* — aval, *mourn*: the interior's *grief enacted* (torn garments, sackcloth) — the father *broken* by the (false) death *(inferred: aval = the father's enacted mourning)*.
- **avel (mourning) + nacham (comfort) + bakhah (wept) — the *grief without comfort* (37:35).** "he refused to be **comforted** (nacham): 'I shall go down to Sheol **mourning** (avel)'… he **wept** (bakhah)" *(stated)*. **nacham** — *comfort* (← Isaac comforted 24:67; here *refused*); **avel** — the *settled mourning* he expects to *die in*; **bakhah** — *weep*. The gem is the *inconsolable* grief — the father *will not be comforted*, expecting to *carry the mourning to the grave*; the interior's *bottomless sorrow* over the (unknowingly false) death *(inferred: avel/nacham/bakhah = the inconsolable grief the father will die in)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the peace-errand into the trap (shalom 37:14 → shaal/baqash 37:15 → baqash 37:16 → shama 37:17):** Joseph is *sent to check their peace* and *seeks his brothers*, steered on by a *chance word* — walking, unwitting, toward the men who hate him.
2. **the dream attacked, restrained, and sold (chayyah/ra 37:20 → shama/nephesh 37:21 → basar/shama 37:27):** the brothers plot to *kill the dreamer to kill the dream*; Reuben's *conscience restrains* the killing; Judah's *profit-and-kinship* motive *sells* him instead — the hatred *acting*, but *fractured*.
3. **the lie believed, the deceiver deceived (chayyah/ra 37:33):** the *beast-lie* the father *believes* — and by a *goat's blood* (as Jacob himself deceived Isaac): **the deceiver deceived, one generation on.**
4. **the inconsolable grief (aval 37:34 → avel/nacham/bakhah 37:35):** Jacob *mourns, refuses comfort, weeps* — expecting to *go down to Sheol mourning* — the father's *bottomless sorrow* over a death that never happened.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** shalom (the *peace-errand* into hatred); shaal/baqash (the *seeking* toward the trap — baqash ×2: the errand / the brothers named); shama ×3 (the *informant's word* / *Reuben's* restraining hearing / the brothers *heeding Judah*); chayyah/ra ×2 (the beast-lie *planned* 37:20 / *believed* 37:33); nephesh (Reuben's *restraint*); **basar (Judah's *kinship-and-profit* mixed motive — sell not kill)**; aval/avel (the father's *mourning* / the *settled* mourning he'll die in); nacham (comfort *refused*); bakhah (the father's *weeping*).
- **Whose interior (multi-interior):** the **brothers** — murderous hatred *acting*, *fractured* by Reuben's conscience and Judah's profit-and-kinship, and *deceiving* the father; **Joseph** — *obedient* ("Here I am") and *silent* (his distress voiced only later, 42:21); **Jacob** — *inconsolable grief*, refusing comfort. The dream is *attacked* ("see what becomes of his dreams").
- **Threads:** **the deceiver deceived** (the *goat-blood* deception 37:31 ← Jacob's own goat-deception of Isaac, Gen 27:16 — the family sin returns on him; and "**identify** (haker-na)" 37:32 → the *same word* turns on Judah with Tamar, 38:25); the *dream attacked* (37:20 → *fulfilled* when they bow, 42:6; JOS-08); *divided love's* fruit (← JOS-01, 37:3); the *inconsolable grief* (nacham refused 37:35 → the *comfort* that finally comes when Joseph is found, 45:27); Judah's *mixed motive* (→ his *transformation*, the substitute JOS-10); the *goat* (→ Tamar's kid, 38:17).
- **Guarded against:** lumping the two chayyah/ra (planned lie / believed lie) or three shama (informant / Reuben / brothers-heed); reading Judah's "he is our flesh" (37:27) as compassion when it is *fused with profit* ("what profit?", 37:26) — a *mixed* motive, not repentance; missing the **goat-deception irony** (the deceiver deceived, ← Gen 27); over-reading Joseph's silence as either innocence or guilt (the text gives *obedience* and *silence*, his interior withheld until 42:21); treating Jacob's refused comfort as excessive when the text presents it as *the father's bottomless, dying grief*.

---
