## Exo EXS-05-sinai-theophany - inner-being reading

# Exodus 19:1–25 — inner-being passage reading (EXS-05-sinai-theophany)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `exodus-sinai-v1-20260705`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. **Multiple interiors**: **Israel** (belief, holy dread, consecration), **Moses** (the mediator up-and-down), **God** (the covenant-offerer descending in fire). The people's "all we will do" (19:8, no non-T2 span) reads as scene-context. **Mis-tag flagged, not read:** 'o at 19:13 = the conjunction "or" (not "desire").
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the 4 qara, 4 qadash, 2 charad, 2 shamar, 2 ud each treated distinctly.

---

## EXS-05-sinai-theophany · Exodus 19:1–25 · [the covenant offered; the holy dread at the mountain] — a kingdom of priests, and the trembling of people and mountain

**The passage.** The LORD **called** (qara) from the mountain (19:3); the **covenant** (berit) offer — "if you indeed **obey** (shama) my voice and **keep** (shamar) my covenant… a **holy** (qadosh) nation" (19:5–6); Moses **called** (qara) the elders (19:7); "that they may **believe** (aman) you forever" (19:9); **consecrate** (qadash) them (19:10); "**take care** (shamar) not to go up" (19:12); **consecrated** (qadash, 19:14); the people **trembled** (charad, 19:16); Moses brought them to **meet** (qara) God (19:17); the mountain **trembled** (charad, 19:18); the trumpet grew **louder** (chazeq, 19:19); the LORD **called** (qara) Moses up (19:20); **warn** (ud) them (19:21); the priests **consecrate** (qadash, 19:22); "you **warned** (ud) us… **consecrate** (qadash) it" (19:23).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **qara (called) — the *divine summons* from the mountain (19:3).** "the LORD **called** (qara) to him out of the mountain" *(stated)* — qara, *call*: the *summons that opens the covenant* — God *initiates*, calling Moses up; the interior-context of *the LORD's address to the house of Jacob* *(inferred: qara = the divine summons opening the covenant)*.
- **berit (covenant) + shama (obey) + shamar (keep) — the *covenant offered on obedience* (19:5).** "'if you indeed **obey** (shama) my voice and **keep** (shamar) my **covenant** (berit), you shall be my treasured possession'" *(stated)*. **berit** — *covenant*; **shama** — *hearken/obey*; **shamar** — *keep*: the gem is the *conditional offer* — the *treasured possession* status *hinges on obeying and keeping*; the interior of *a people offered a covenant identity, conditioned on the heart's obedience* — *"if you will indeed obey"* — the vocation *set before the will* *(inferred: berit/shama/shamar = the covenant offered on obedience — the vocation set before the will)*.
- **qadosh (holy) — the *holy nation vocation* (19:6).** "'you shall be to me a kingdom of priests and a **holy** (qadosh) nation'" *(stated)* — qadosh, *holy/set-apart*: the gem is the *identity offered* — *set apart* as *a nation of priests*; the interior-context of *a people called to holiness* — a *mediating vocation to the peoples* *(inferred: qadosh = the holy-nation vocation — set apart as priests)*.
- **qara (called) — the *mediator's relay* to the elders (19:7).** *qara distinct from 19:3:* "Moses came and **called** (qara) the elders and set before them all these words" *(stated)* — where 19:3 was *God calling Moses*, here Moses *calls the elders* — the *summons relayed down* — the interior-context of *the covenant-offer passed to the people* *(inferred: qara = the mediator's relay of the call)*.
- **aman (believe) — the *belief established* by the theophany (19:9).** "'I am coming in a thick cloud, that the people may hear when I speak with you, and may also **believe** (aman) you forever'" *(stated)* — aman, *trust/be-faithful* (the *faith*-word, ← 14:31 "they believed"; 15:6-arc): the gem is that *God stages the theophany to establish trust* — the people will *believe Moses* (and God through him) *forever* because they *hear God speak with him*; the interior of *belief grounded in the heard presence* — *trust anchored, not asked in a vacuum* *(inferred: aman = the belief established — trust grounded in the heard presence)*.
- **qadash (consecrate) — the *making-holy before approach* (19:10).** "'**consecrate** (qadash) them today and tomorrow, and let them wash'" *(stated)* — qadash, *consecrate/make-holy*: the gem is that *approach to the holy requires consecration* — the people must be *made holy* to *stand before the descending God*; the interior-context of *preparation for the presence — the set-apartness that approach demands* *(inferred: qadash = the making-holy before approach)*.
- **shamar (take care) — the *boundary guarded* (19:12).** *shamar distinct from 19:5:* "'**take care** (shamar) not to go up into the mountain… whoever touches it shall die'" *(stated)* — where 19:5 was *keep the covenant*, here shamar is *guard yourself* against the *lethal boundary* — the gem: *the holy is dangerous* — *watchfulness against overstep*; the interior of *the dread-bounded approach — the barrier that kills* *(inferred: shamar = the boundary guarded — watchfulness against the lethal holy)*.
- **qadash (consecrated) — the *consecration enacted* (19:14).** *qadash distinct from 19:10:* "Moses **consecrated** (qadash) the people; they washed" *(stated)* — where 19:10 *commanded*, 19:14 *enacts* — the *people made holy* — the interior-context of *the preparation carried out* *(inferred: qadash = the consecration enacted)*.
- **charad (trembled) — the *people's holy dread* (19:16).** "thunders and lightnings and a thick cloud… all the people **trembled** (charad)" *(stated)* — **charad**, *tremble/shudder* (tagged fear): the gem is *the raw fear-of-God* — the people *shudder* at the storm-theophany; the interior of *holy dread* — *terror before the descending presence* (the fear the whole covenant will name a keeper-from-sin, 20:20) *(inferred: charad = the people's holy dread — trembling before the presence)*.
- **qara (meet) — the *bringing-to-encounter* (19:17).** *qara distinct from 19:3,7 (encounter sense):* "Moses brought the people out to **meet** (qara) God, at the foot of the mountain" *(stated)* — here qara is *encounter/meeting*: the *mediator leads the trembling people to the meeting-place* — the interior-context of *the people brought (still trembling) to the encounter* *(inferred: qara = the bringing-to-encounter)*.
- **charad (trembled) — the *mountain's trembling* (19:18).** *charad distinct from 19:16:* "the LORD descended in fire… the whole mountain **trembled** (charad) greatly" *(stated)* — where 19:16 was *the people*, here *the mountain itself* shudders: the gem is that *the dread is shared by creation* — *not only the people but the mountain trembles* at the descent; the interior-lesson that *the presence shakes earth as well as heart* *(inferred: charad = the mountain's trembling — the dread shared by creation)*.
- **chazeq (louder) — the *mounting intensity* (19:19).** "the trumpet grew **louder** (chazeq) and louder; Moses spoke, God answered in thunder" *(stated)* — chazeq, *strong/loud*: the *intensity rising* — the interior-context of *the encounter's mounting weight* (the same root as Pharaoh's *hardening*, here the *strengthening* of the trumpet — the theophany *intensifying*) *(inferred: chazeq = the mounting intensity of the encounter)*.
- **qara (called) — the *call to the summit* (19:20).** *qara distinct from 19:3,7,17:* "the LORD **called** (qara) Moses to the top of the mountain, and Moses went up" *(stated)* — the *fourth qara*: God *calls Moses up into the presence* (where 19:3 called from the mountain, this calls *to the top*) — the interior-context of *the mediator summoned into the fire* *(inferred: qara = the call to the summit)*.
- **ud (warn) — the *warning against overstep* (19:21).** "'go down and **warn** (ud) the people, lest they break through to look and perish'" *(stated)* — ud, *testify/warn solemnly*: the gem is the *solemn warning* — the people's *curiosity to look* would be *lethal*; the interior of *the desire-to-see checked by the holy peril* *(inferred: ud = the warning against overstep — curiosity checked by peril)*.
- **qadash (consecrate) — the *priests' consecration* (19:22).** *qadash distinct from 19:10,14:* "'let the priests who come near **consecrate** (qadash) themselves, lest the LORD break out'" *(stated)* — even *the priests* (nearer) must be *made holy* — the interior-context of *nearness demanding greater consecration* *(inferred: qadash = the priests' consecration — nearness demands holiness)*.
- **ud (warned) + qadash (consecrate) — Moses *recalls the warning* (19:23).** *ud/qadash distinct:* "'you yourself **warned** (ud) us, "set limits and **consecrate** (qadash) it"'" *(stated)* — Moses *rehearses the boundary-command back* — the *warning* and the *making-holy of the mountain* recalled; the interior-context of *the mediator holding the boundary he was given* *(inferred: ud/qadash = the warning recalled, the mountain made holy)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the covenant offered (qara 19:3 → berit/shama/shamar 19:5 → qadosh 19:6 → qara 19:7 → aman 19:9):** God *summons*, *offers a covenant conditioned on obedience*, names the *holy-nation vocation* — the offer *relayed to the people*, and the theophany staged so they *believe* — the interior of *a people offered a covenant identity, their belief grounded in the heard presence*.
2. **the consecration for approach (qadash 19:10 → shamar 19:12 → qadash 19:14):** *approach demands holiness* — the people *made holy*, the *lethal boundary guarded* — the interior of *the dread-bounded approach*.
3. **the holy dread (charad 19:16 → qara 19:17 → charad 19:18 → chazeq 19:19 → qara 19:20 → ud 19:21 → qadash 19:22 → ud/qadash 19:23):** the *people tremble*, are *brought to the encounter*, the *mountain trembles*, the *intensity mounts*, Moses is *called to the summit* — and the *warnings* against overstep, the *priests* consecrated — the interior of *holy dread shared by people and creation*, the *approach regulated by peril*.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** **qara ×4 (the *divine summons* / the *mediator's relay* / the *bringing-to-encounter* / the *call to the summit*)**; **berit/shama/shamar (the *covenant offered on obedience* — the vocation set before the will)**; **qadosh (the *holy-nation vocation*)**; **aman (the *belief established* — trust grounded in the heard presence)**; **qadash ×4 (the *making-holy* commanded / *enacted* / the *priests'* consecration / the mountain *made holy*)**; shamar (the *boundary guarded* — watchfulness against the lethal holy); **charad ×2 (the *people's* holy dread / the *mountain's* trembling — the dread shared by creation)**; chazeq (the *mounting intensity*); **ud ×2 (the *warning* against overstep / the *warning recalled*)**.
- **Whose interior (multi-interior):** **Israel** — *belief* (aman, grounded in the heard presence), *holy dread* (charad, trembling), and *consecration* (made holy to approach); **Moses** — the *mediator up-and-down*, *summoned into the fire*, holding the *boundary*; **God** — the *covenant-offerer descending in fire*, the *holy presence that must be bounded*. The *covenant offer* and the *holy dread* are the two gems.
- **Threads:** **the fear-of-God** (charad 19:16,18 — the *trembling* that the covenant will name a *keeper-from-sin*, 20:20; ← the God-fearing midwives 1:17 → "the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom"); **belief/faith** (aman 19:9 ← 14:31 "they believed"; 15:6-arc; 17:12 emunah → the faith-thread — here *established by the theophany*); **the holy** (qadash/qadosh 19:6,10,14,22,23 → the tabernacle's holiness, Lev; the set-apart people); **covenant** (berit 19:5 ← the Abrahamic covenant Gen 15,17 → the Sinai covenant, the whole Torah; the *conditional* offer distinct from the Abrahamic *promise*); **the dangerous holy** (shamar/ud 19:12,21 → Uzzah, 2 Sam 6; the ark's peril — nearness kills the unconsecrated); the *arrogance*-hardening contrast (chazeq 19:19 — the trumpet *strengthened*, same root as Pharaoh's *hardened* heart, here God's *good* intensity vs the *self-hardening*).
- **Guarded against:** lumping the four qara (summons / relay / encounter / summit), the four qadash (commanded / enacted / priests / mountain), the two charad (people / mountain — the *creation shares the dread*, the finding), the two shamar (keep-covenant / guard-boundary), the two ud (warn / recall); reading the covenant-offer as unconditional over the *"if you will indeed obey"* the text states (the vocation *set before the will*); flattening the trembling into mere spectacle over the *holy dread* it is (the raw fear-of-God); importing NT "kingdom of priests" (1 Pet 2:9) over the *holy-nation vocation* the verse offers; over-reading chazeq into the hardening-motif when here it is the *trumpet's* strengthening (the intensity, not a heart); missing that the belief (aman) is *grounded* in the heard presence (God stages it) — trust *given a foundation*, not demanded blind.

## Exo EXS-06-decalogue - inner-being reading

# Exodus 20:1–26 — inner-being passage reading (EXS-06-decalogue)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `exodus-sinai-v1-20260705`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. **Multiple interiors**: **God** (jealous, showing steadfast love), **Israel** (the coveting forbidden, the two fears, the remembering). The people's terror and "lest we die" (20:18–19, no non-T2 span) read as scene-context, anchored by the fear spans at 20:20. **Lexical note:** the second chesed span at 20:6 carries the homonym gloss "shame" — here both spans are the one *steadfast love to thousands*.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the 2 chesed, 2 avad, 2 qadash, 2 zakhar, 2 fear (yirah/yare), the covet-pair (chamad/chamudah) each treated distinctly.

---

## EXS-06-decalogue · Exodus 20:1–26 · [the law reaching the heart; the two fears] — the coveting forbidden, and the fear that keeps from sin

**The passage.** "I the LORD am **jealous** (qanna), visiting the **iniquity** (avon) of those who **hate** (sane) me, who **serve** (avad) [idols]" (20:5); "showing **steadfast love** (chesed) to thousands who love and **keep** (shamar)" (20:6); "**Remember** (zakhar) the sabbath, to keep it **holy** (qadash)" (20:8); "six days you **labor** (avad)" (20:9); "the LORD **rested** (nuach)… made it **holy** (qadash)" (20:11); "honor father and mother, that your days be **long** (arakh)… the land he is **giving** (natan)" (20:12); no **false** (sheqer) witness (20:16); "you shall not **covet** (chamad)… anything **desirable** (chamudah)" (20:17); "do not **fear** (yirah/yare)… that the **fear** of him may keep you from **sin** (chata)" (20:20); "where I cause my name to be **remembered** (zakhar) I will bless you" (20:24).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **qanna (jealous) + avon (iniquity) + sane (hate) + avad (serve) — the *jealous God and the iniquity of those who hate him* (20:5).** "'I the LORD am **jealous** (qanna), visiting the **iniquity** (avon) on the children of those who **hate** (sane) me… who **serve** (avad) [idols]'" *(stated)*. **qanna** — *jealous*; **avon** — *iniquity/guilt*; **sane** — *hate*; **avad** — *serve*: the gem is *the divine jealousy* — God's *exclusive covenant-love that will not be shared with idols*; those who *hate him* (choosing other gods, serving them) carry an *iniquity* that *runs down generations*. The interior of *God's jealousy* — not petty envy but the *fierce claim of a covenant love*; and the human interior of *idol-service as hatred of God* *(inferred: qanna/avon/sane/avad = the jealous God, and idol-service as the hatred that carries iniquity)*.
- **chesed (steadfast love) + shamar (keep) — the *steadfast love to thousands* (20:6).** "'but showing **steadfast love** (chesed) to thousands of those who love me and **keep** (shamar) my commandments'" *(stated)* — **chesed** (both spans; the second's *shame* gloss is the homonym artifact — here it is *loyal love*); **shamar** — *keep*: the gem is the *asymmetry* — iniquity visited to *three or four generations*, but *steadfast love to thousands* — *mercy vastly outweighs judgment*; the interior of *God's chesed* — a *loyal love* toward those who *love and keep*, poured out *immeasurably wider* than the judgment *(inferred: chesed/shamar = the steadfast love to thousands — mercy vastly outweighing judgment)*.
- **zakhar (remember) + qadash (holy) — the *sabbath remembered and kept holy* (20:8).** "'**Remember** (zakhar) the sabbath, to keep it **holy** (qadash)'" *(stated)*. **zakhar** — *remember*; **qadash** — *make/keep holy*: the gem is that *the sabbath is an act of memory and sanctity* — the interior *called to remember* (to hold the day in mind) and to *set it apart* — *memory and holiness joined* *(inferred: zakhar/qadash = the sabbath remembered and kept holy)*.
- **avad (labor) — the *six days' work* (20:9).** *avad distinct from 20:5:* "'six days you shall **labor** (avad) and do all your work'" *(stated)* — where 20:5 was *serving idols*, here avad is *honest labor* — the *ordinary work* framed by the sabbath; the interior-context of *the rhythm of work and rest* *(inferred: avad = the six days' honest labor)*.
- **nuach (rested) + qadash (holy) — the *rest that grounds the sabbath* (20:11).** *qadash distinct from 20:8:* "'the LORD **rested** (nuach) on the seventh day… and made it **holy** (qadash)'" *(stated)*. **nuach** — *rest*; **qadash** — where 20:8 *commanded* keeping-holy, here God *made* it holy: the gem is that *the human sabbath rests on God's own rest* (← creation, Gen 2:2–3) — the interior-lesson that *rest is grounded in the Creator's rest, and the day made holy by him* *(inferred: nuach/qadash = the rest grounding the sabbath — God's own rest, the day he made holy)*.
- **arakh (long) + natan (giving) — the *honor that lengthens days* (20:12).** "'honor father and mother, that your days may be **long** (arakh) in the land he is **giving** (natan) you'" *(stated)*. **arakh** — *prolong*; **natan** — *give*: the gem is *the promise attached to honor* — *honoring the parents* tied to *long life in the given land*; the interior of *the honor that orders generations and is met with length of days* *(inferred: arakh/natan = the honor that lengthens days in the given land)*.
- **sheqer (false) — the *false witness* (20:16).** "'you shall not bear **false** (sheqer) witness against your neighbor'" *(stated)* — sheqer, *falsehood/deception*: the gem is that *the tongue's deception* is legislated — the interior of *the lie that wounds the neighbor* forbidden — *truth in speech commanded* *(inferred: sheqer = the false witness — the deceiving tongue forbidden)*.
- **chamad (covet) + chamudah (desirable) — the *coveting: the law reaching the heart* (20:17).** "'you shall not **covet** (chamad) your neighbor's house… wife… nor anything **desirable** (chamudah) that is your neighbor's'" *(stated)*. **chamad** — *covet/crave*; **chamudah** — *a desirable thing*: the gem is *THE inward turn of the Decalogue* — after murder, adultery, theft, false witness (*acts*), the tenth word forbids the *desire itself* — the *coveting* before any deed. The law *reaches into the interior*: not the hand's theft but the heart's *craving* for what is another's; *the desire named as sin*. The interior *explicitly legislated* — the grasping wish the root the earlier acts grow from *(inferred: chamad/chamudah = the coveting — the law reaching the interior desire, the craving named as sin)*.
- **yirah (fear) + yare (fear) + chata (sin) — the *two fears, and the fear that keeps from sin* (20:20).** "'do not **fear** (yirah), for God has come to test you, that the **fear** (yare) of him may be before you, that you may not **sin** (chata)'" *(stated)*. **yirah** and **yare** — *fear* (two forms in one verse); **chata** — *sin*: the gem is the *paradox of two fears* — *"do not fear"* (the *terror* that flees and hides, 20:18–19) *yet* let *"the fear of him be before you"* (the *reverent awe* that *guards against sin*). The interior distinction: the *dread that drives away* vs the *fear that keeps near and holy*; the *reverent fear the inner guard against sin* — *the same word, opposite works* *(inferred: yirah/yare/chata = the two fears — the terror that flees vs the reverent fear that keeps from sin)*.
- **zakhar (remembered) — the *name remembered, the blessing* (20:24).** *zakhar distinct from 20:8:* "'in every place where I cause my name to be **remembered** (zakhar) I will come and bless you'" *(stated)* — where 20:8 was *remembering the sabbath*, here it is *God's name remembered* (invoked in worship) drawing his *presence and blessing* — the interior-context of *worship as remembrance, met with blessing* *(inferred: zakhar = the name remembered — worship met with blessing)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the jealous God and the steadfast love (qanna/avon/sane/avad 20:5 → chesed/shamar 20:6):** God's *jealousy* (the exclusive covenant-claim) visits the *iniquity* of those who *hate him* (serving idols) — *but* pours *steadfast love to thousands* who love and keep; the *asymmetry* — *mercy vastly outweighing judgment* — the divine interior of *jealous love and immeasurable chesed*.
2. **remembrance, rest, honor (zakhar/qadash 20:8 → avad 20:9 → nuach/qadash 20:11 → arakh/natan 20:12):** the sabbath *remembered and kept holy*, grounded in *God's own rest*; honest *labor* framing the rest; the *honor* of parents met with *length of days* — the interior ordered by *memory, rest, and honor*.
3. **the law reaching the heart (sheqer 20:16 → chamad/chamudah 20:17 → yirah/yare/chata 20:20 → zakhar 20:24):** from the *false tongue* to the *coveting heart* — the law *turns inward*, naming the *desire itself* as sin; and the *two fears* — the *terror that flees* vs the *reverent fear that keeps from sin* — the *inner guard*; the *name remembered* drawing blessing.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** **qanna (the *jealous God* — the exclusive covenant-claim)**; avon (the *iniquity* down generations); sane (the *hatred* that is idol-service); **avad ×2 (idol-*service* / honest *labor*)**; **chesed (the *steadfast love to thousands* — mercy vastly outweighing judgment; the second span's *shame* gloss the homonym artifact)**; shamar (the *keeping* of the commandments); **zakhar ×2 (the *sabbath* remembered / the *name* remembered)**; **qadash ×2 (keep-*holy* commanded / God *made* it holy)**; nuach (the *rest* grounding the sabbath — God's own); arakh/natan (the *honor* that lengthens days in the given land); sheqer (the *false witness* — the deceiving tongue); **chamad/chamudah (the *coveting* — THE law reaching the interior desire, the craving named as sin)**; **yirah/yare (the *two fears* — the terror that flees vs the reverent fear that keeps from sin)**; chata (the *sin* the reverent fear guards against).
- **Whose interior (multi-interior):** **God** — *jealous* (the exclusive covenant-love) and *showing steadfast love to thousands* (jealousy and chesed together, mercy outweighing judgment); **Israel** — the *coveting* forbidden (the heart itself legislated), the *two fears* (terror vs reverent awe), the *remembering* (sabbath and name). The two gems: the *law reaching the interior desire* (chamad) and the *reverent fear that keeps from sin* (yare 20:20).
- **Threads:** **the fear-of-God as inner guard** (yare 20:20 ← the trembling 19:16; the God-fearing midwives 1:17; Jethro's God-fearing judges 18:21 → "the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom", Prov 9:10 — the *reverent* fear that *keeps from sin*, distinct from the *terror* that flees); **the coveting named** (chamad 20:17 → Achan's coveting Josh 7; "each is tempted by his own desire", Jas 1:14 — the *interior craving* the root of the outward acts); **jealousy and chesed** (qanna/chesed 20:5–6 ← 34:6–7 "the LORD, merciful… yet visiting iniquity" — the same asymmetry restated; the covenant God *jealous and abounding in steadfast love*); **the sabbath** (nuach/zakhar 20:8,11 ← creation Gen 2:2–3; the manna-sabbath 16:23 — rest as gift and memory); **remembrance** (zakhar 20:8,24 — memory the mode of covenant-faithfulness).
- **Guarded against:** lumping the two avad (idol-service / labor), two zakhar (sabbath / name), two qadash (commanded / made), the covet-pair as separate operations when they are the *one coveting*; reading God's jealousy as petty envy over the *exclusive covenant-love* the word carries; missing the *asymmetry* (chesed to *thousands* vs iniquity to *3–4 generations* — mercy dwarfs judgment, the finding); flattening the *two fears* of 20:20 into one when the verse *sets them against each other* (do not fear / let the fear be before you — the finding); importing NT "the law is spiritual… I would not have known coveting" (Rom 7:7) over the *coveting-as-sin* the tenth word plainly legislates (though the resonance is real); over-reading the altar-laws (20:24–26) beyond the *name remembered → blessing* the verse gives.

---

## Exo EXS-07-covenant-slaves-injury - inner-being reading

# Exodus 21:1–36 — inner-being passage reading (EXS-07-covenant-slaves-injury)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `exodus-sinai-v1-20260705`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. **Multiple interiors**: **the slave** (the love-choice), **the master** (treachery vs faithfulness), **the assailant** (intent — willful vs accidental), and the **value of a life**. This is casuistic law; the inner-being is read where the statute *names a heart* (love, treachery, cunning, willful malice, the worth of a nephesh). Property/mechanical spans (the live/dead ox, the ox's flesh, marital provision) read as scene-context.
- **Mis-tags flagged, not read:** 'o "desire" at 21:4, 21:6, 21:18, 21:20, 21:21, 21:26, 21:27, 21:28, 21:29, 21:31, 21:32, 21:33, 21:36 = the conjunction *"or"* (not "desire"). The chay/chayyah glosses "kinsfolk"/"community" (21:35) are homonym artifacts — here the *living* ox.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every genuine non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the 2 avad, 2 nephesh, 2 shamar, 2 naqi, the two "flesh" (she'er/basar), the 3 mishpat each treated distinctly.

---

## EXS-07-covenant-slaves-injury · Exodus 21:1–36 · [the love-choice of service; intent legislated; the worth of a life] — "I love my master", the willful cunning distinguished, and life for life

**The passage.** The **rules** (mishpat, 21:1); the Hebrew **serves** (avad) six years (21:2); "'I love my master… I will not go out free'" — his ear bored, **slave** (avad) forever (21:6); the daughter he has no **right** (mashal) to sell, having **broken faith** (bagad), is **redeemed** (padah) (21:8); dealt with as the **rule** (mishpat, 21:9) for a daughter; her **food** (she'er) not diminished (21:10); the **willful** (zid) attacker who kills by **cunning** (ormah) taken from the altar (21:14); men **quarrel** (riv, 21:18); men **strive** (natsah) and hit a pregnant woman (21:22); **life** (nephesh) for life (21:23); the slave whose eye is **destroyed** (shachat) goes free (21:26); the ox's owner **innocent** (naqi ×2, 21:28); **warned** (ud) but the ox not **kept** (shamar) in (21:29); a ransom for his **life** (nephesh, 21:30); the same **rule** (mishpat, 21:31); the **live** (chay) ox sold (21:35); the ox not **kept** (shamar) in (21:36).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **mishpat (rules) — the *statutes framing the covenant life* (21:1).** "'these are the **rules** (mishpat) you shall set before them'" *(stated)* — mishpat, *judgement/ordinance*: the *ordered justice* the covenant people are to live by — the interior-context of *life shaped by God's rules* *(inferred: mishpat = the statutes framing the covenant life)*.
- **avad (serve) — the *bounded service* of the Hebrew slave (21:2).** "'when you buy a Hebrew **slave** (avad), he shall serve six years and go out free'" *(stated)* — avad, *serve*: the gem is that *servitude is bounded* — even bondage has a *sabbath-year release*; the interior-context of *service that does not own a person forever* (← Israel's own bondage, freed) *(inferred: avad = the bounded service — bondage with a release)*.
- **avad (slave) — the *love-choice of permanent service* (21:6).** *avad distinct from 21:2:* "'if the slave says "I love my master… I will not go out free"… his master bores his ear… he shall be his **slave** (avad) forever'" *(stated)* — where 21:2 was *bounded* service, here service *chosen out of love* becomes *permanent*: the gem is *servitude transfigured by love* — the freed man *elects* to stay, his *love for master and family* binding him more than any law; the interior of *devotion chosen* — the pierced ear the *mark of a love that gives up freedom* *(inferred: avad = the love-choice of permanent service — servitude transfigured by love)*.
- **mashal (right) + bagad (broken faith) + padah (redeemed) — the *treachery remedied by redemption* (21:8).** "'if she does not please him… he has no **right** (mashal) to sell her, since he has **broken faith** (bagad); he shall let her be **redeemed** (padah)'" *(stated)*. **mashal** — *rule/authority*; **bagad** — *act treacherously/break faith*; **padah** — *ransom/redeem*: the gem is that *breaking faith forfeits authority* — the master who *deals treacherously* with the designated woman *loses his right over her* and she must be *redeemed*; the interior of *treachery in a covenant* named and *remedied* — *faithlessness answered by release* *(inferred: mashal/bagad/padah = the treachery that forfeits authority, remedied by redemption)*.
- **mishpat (rule) — the *daughter's dignity in the statute* (21:9).** *mishpat distinct from 21:1:* "'if he designates her for his son, he shall deal with her as the **rule** (mishpat) for a daughter'" *(stated)* — the *statute protecting her as a daughter, not chattel* — the interior-context of *the law dignifying the vulnerable* *(inferred: mishpat = the rule dignifying her as a daughter)*.
- **she'er (food) — the *provision not diminished* (21:10).** "'if he takes another wife, he shall not diminish her **food** (she'er), clothing, or marital rights'" *(stated)* — she'er, *flesh/food/sustenance*: the *sustenance guarded* even when supplanted — the interior-context of *the first wife's due protected* *(inferred: she'er = the provision that may not be diminished)*.
- **zid (willfully) + ormah (cunning) — the *willful cunning distinguished from accident* (21:14).** "'if a man **willfully** (zid) attacks another to kill by **cunning** (ormah), take him from my altar to die'" *(stated)*. **zid** — *presume/boil* (the *seething* will, ← Egypt's arrogance 18:11); **ormah** — *craftiness/premeditation*: the gem is *THE inner-being turn of the injury laws* — the law *reads the heart's intent*: *willful, boiling malice* executed by *cunning* (premeditation) is *murder* (no altar-refuge), where the *unintended* killing (God "let him fall into his hand", 21:13) finds *refuge*. The interior *itself judged* — *the boiling, scheming will* the thing punished, not merely the deed; *intent the measure of the crime* *(inferred: zid/ormah = the willful cunning distinguished from accident — the heart's intent the measure)*.
- **riv (quarrel) — the *quarrel that injures* (21:18).** "'when men **quarrel** (riv) and one strikes the other with a stone'" *(stated)* — riv, *contend* (← the quarreling at Meribah 17:2): the *dispute escalating to blows* — the interior-context of *anger spilling into injury* *(inferred: riv = the quarrel that injures)*.
- **natsah (strive) + nephesh (life) — the *striving, and life for life* (21:22–23).** "'when men **strive** (natsah) and hit a pregnant woman… if there is harm, **life** (nephesh) for life'" *(stated)*. **natsah** — *struggle/fight*; **nephesh** — *life/soul*: the gem is the *worth of a life* — the *striving* that harms a life met with *life for life* — the interior-lesson that *a nephesh is answered only by a nephesh*; the *incommensurable value of a life* set in the law *(inferred: natsah/nephesh = the striving, and the life-for-life worth of a nephesh)*.
- **shachat (destroys) — the *slave's body honored* (21:26).** "'when a man **destroys** (shachat) the eye of his slave, he shall let the slave go free'" *(stated)* — shachat, *ruin/destroy*: the gem is that *the slave's body has dignity* — *maiming the slave earns the slave's freedom*; the interior-lesson that *even the bondman's flesh is protected* — *cruelty forfeits ownership* *(inferred: shachat = the slave's body honored — maiming earns freedom)*.
- **basar (flesh) + naqi (innocent) — the *goring ox and the owner's innocence* (21:28).** "'when an ox gores a man to death… its **flesh** (basar) not eaten, but the owner **innocent** (naqi ×2)'" *(stated)*. **basar** — *flesh* (the ox's, ← the fleshpots 16:3, here mechanical); **naqi** — *innocent/clear* (twice — the owner *not liable* for the first, unforeseen goring): the interior-context of *innocence where there was no negligence* — *guilt attaches to knowledge, not mischance* *(inferred: basar/naqi = the owner innocent of the unforeseen goring)*.
- **ud (warned) + shamar (kept) — the *negligence that incurs blood-guilt* (21:29).** "'if the ox was accustomed to gore and its owner **warned** (ud) but did not **keep** (shamar) it in, and it kills… the owner shall die'" *(stated)*. **ud** — *warn/testify*; **shamar** — *keep/guard*: the gem is the *contrast with 21:28* — where the first goring left the owner *innocent*, the *warned-but-negligent* owner bears *blood-guilt*; the interior of *responsibility that follows knowledge* — *the warned who fails to guard is culpable* *(inferred: ud/shamar = the negligence after warning — culpability follows knowledge)*.
- **nephesh (life) — the *ransom for a life* (21:30).** *nephesh distinct from 21:23:* "'if a ransom is imposed, he shall give for the redemption of his **life** (nephesh) whatever is imposed'" *(stated)* — here the *forfeited life* may be *ransomed* — the interior-context of *a life redeemable by price* (where 21:23 was *life for life*, here a *ransom* substitutes) *(inferred: nephesh = the ransom for a forfeited life)*.
- **mishpat (rule) — the *same statute for son or daughter* (21:31).** *mishpat distinct from 21:1,9:* "'if it gores a son or daughter, according to this same **rule** (mishpat)'" *(stated)* — the *equal application* — the interior-context of *impartial law* *(inferred: mishpat = the same rule applied impartially)*.
- **chay (live) + shamar (kept) — the *restitution of the goring ox* (21:35–36).** *shamar distinct from 21:29:* "'they shall sell the **live** (chay) ox and share… if the ox was accustomed to gore and its owner did not **keep** (shamar) it in, he shall repay ox for ox'" *(stated)*. **chay** — *living* (the surviving ox; the *kinsfolk/community* glosses homonym artifacts); **shamar** — again *the negligence*: the interior-context of *fair restitution*, and *the negligent owner again culpable* (echoing 21:29) *(inferred: chay/shamar = the restitution, the negligent owner culpable)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **service bounded, then chosen (mishpat 21:1 → avad 21:2 → avad 21:6):** the *rules* frame the life; service is *bounded* (a release) — yet love can *transfigure it into permanent devotion* ("I love my master… I will not go out free"); the interior of *servitude chosen out of love*.
2. **the vulnerable protected (mashal/bagad/padah 21:8 → mishpat 21:9 → she'er 21:10 → shachat 21:26):** *treachery forfeits authority* (the faithless master loses his right, she is redeemed); the woman *dignified as a daughter*, her *provision guarded*; the *slave's body honored* (maiming earns freedom) — the law *bending toward the powerless*.
3. **intent, negligence, and the worth of a life (zid/ormah 21:14 → riv 21:18 → natsah/nephesh 21:22–23 → basar/naqi 21:28 → ud/shamar 21:29 → nephesh 21:30 → mishpat 21:31 → chay/shamar 21:35–36):** the law *reads the heart* — *willful cunning malice* is murder, *accident* finds refuge; *quarrels and strivings* that injure; *life for life* (the worth of a nephesh), a *ransom* where allowed; *innocence* where there was no negligence, but *culpability where the warned failed to guard*; the interior of *intent and responsibility legislated*.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** **mishpat ×3 (the *statutes* framing / the *rule* dignifying the daughter / the *same rule* applied impartially)**; **avad ×2 (the *bounded* service / the *love-choice* of permanent service)**; **mashal/bagad/padah (the *treachery* that forfeits authority, *remedied by redemption*)**; she'er (the *provision* not diminished); **zid/ormah (the *willful cunning* distinguished from accident — the heart's intent the measure)**; riv (the *quarrel* that injures); natsah (the *striving* that harms); **nephesh ×2 (the *life-for-life* worth / the *ransom* for a forfeited life)**; **shachat (the *slave's body honored* — maiming earns freedom)**; basar (the ox's *flesh*, mechanical); **naqi ×2 (the owner *innocent* of the unforeseen goring)**; **ud/shamar (the *negligence after warning* — culpability follows knowledge)**; **shamar (again the *negligent* owner, 21:36)**; chay (the *living* ox, restitution).
- **Whose interior (multi-interior):** **the slave** — the *love-choice* (devotion that elects permanent service); **the master** — *treachery* (bagad) vs faithfulness (the faithless forfeits his right); **the assailant** — *intent* (willful cunning vs accident — the heart judged); **the negligent owner** — *responsibility after warning* (culpability follows knowledge); and the *worth of a life* (nephesh — life answered by life). The two gems: the *love-choice of service* (avad 21:6) and *intent legislated* (zid/ormah 21:14).
- **Threads:** **the law reaching the heart** (zid/ormah 21:14 ← the coveting 20:17 — the *interior intent* the measure of the crime, not the deed alone → the cities of refuge, Num 35; "whoever hates his brother is a murderer", 1 Jn 3:15); **bondage bounded** (avad 21:2 ← Israel's own slavery freed — service with a *release*, mercy woven into the law); **the love that gives up freedom** (avad 21:6 — the pierced-ear devotion → the servant-of-the-Lord motif, Ps 40:6 "my ear you have opened"); **the worth of a nephesh** (21:23,30 ← "life for life" — the incommensurable value of a life); **treachery/faithfulness** (bagad 21:8 ← Jacob-Laban's broken faith; → Mal 2:14 "the wife of your covenant… you have been faithless" — the covenant-treachery motif).
- **Guarded against:** lumping the three mishpat (framing / dignifying / impartial), two avad (bounded / love-choice), two nephesh (life-for-life / ransom), two shamar-negligence (21:29 / 21:36); reading the injury laws as mere retribution over the *intent* they legislate (the willful cunning vs accident — the finding); mistaking the 'o "desire" mis-tags for an inner-being motif (they are the conjunction "or"); treating the slave-laws as endorsing slavery when the text *bounds* it (release, dignity, freedom-for-maiming) — the *mercy in the law* the finding; over-reading the pierced-ear into later servant-Christology over the *love-choice* the verse gives (though the resonance is real); flattening the goring-ox laws into property when they turn on *negligence after warning* (the interior of responsibility).

---

## Exo EXS-08-covenant-property-vulnerable - inner-being reading

# Exodus 22:1–31 — inner-being passage reading (EXS-08-covenant-property-vulnerable)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `exodus-sinai-v1-20260705`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. **Multiple interiors**: **God** (compassionate, hearing the cry, wrath for the powerless — the divine heart revealed in the law), **Israel** (the ethical memory, faithful trust, consecration), **the vulnerable** (the cry that God hears). Property/mechanical spans (the living stolen beast, restitution) read as scene-context.
- **Mis-tags flagged, not read:** 'o "desire" at 22:1, 22:5, 22:6, 22:7, 22:10, 22:14 = the conjunction *"or"*. The chay/chayyah glosses "kinsfolk"/"community" (22:4) are homonym artifacts — the *living* stolen beast. chaval "be in labour" (22:26) is the homonym — here *take in pledge*.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every genuine non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the 5 natan, 2 shamar, 2 anah each treated distinctly.

---

## EXS-08-covenant-property-vulnerable · Exodus 22:1–31 · [the law reveals God's heart for the powerless] — "if he cries to me, I will hear, for I am compassionate"

**The passage.** Safekeeping (shamar) of entrusted **goods** (natan, 22:7); every **breach of trust** (pesha) — the one God **condemns** (rasha) pays double (22:9); another **keeping** (shamar) of an entrusted beast (natan, 22:10); a man **borrows** (shaal, 22:14); the seducer must **give** (natan) the bride-price (22:17); "you shall not **afflict** (anah) a widow or orphan; if you **afflict** (anah) them and they cry, I will hear; my wrath will **burn** (charah)" (22:22–24); the cloak **taken** (chaval) in pledge returned by nightfall — "if he cries, I will hear, for I am **compassionate** (channun)" (22:26–27); do not **curse** (arar) God or ruler (22:28); the firstborn **given** (natan, 22:29, 22:30); you shall be **consecrated** (qodesh), not eating torn **flesh** (basar, 22:31).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **shamar (keep safe) + natan (gives) — the *trust to be guarded* (22:7).** "'if a man **gives** (natan) his neighbor money or goods to **keep safe** (shamar), and it is stolen, the thief pays double'" *(stated)*. **natan** — *give/entrust*; **shamar** — *guard*: the gem is *the ethic of entrusted keeping* — what is *given in trust must be guarded*; the interior-context of *faithfulness with another's property* *(inferred: natan/shamar = the trust given, to be guarded)*.
- **pesha (breach of trust) + rasha (condemns) — the *transgression judged before God* (22:9).** "'for every **breach of trust** (pesha)… the case comes before God; the one God **condemns** (rasha) pays double'" *(stated)*. **pesha** — *transgression/rebellion*; **rasha** — *be wicked/condemn*: the gem is that *a breach of trust is a transgression* — not a mere civil matter but brought *before God*, who *condemns the wicked*; the interior of *faithlessness named as guilt before God* *(inferred: pesha/rasha = the breach of trust as transgression, condemned before God)*.
- **shamar (keep safe) + natan (gives) — the *entrusted beast* (22:10).** *shamar/natan distinct from 22:7:* "'if a man **gives** (natan) his neighbor a beast to **keep safe** (shamar), and it dies unseen'" *(stated)* — where 22:7 was *goods*, here a *living animal* entrusted — the *oath* settling the honest keeper's innocence; the interior-context of *trust tested where there is no witness — the oath before God the guard of honesty* *(inferred: natan/shamar = the entrusted beast — honesty under oath where none saw)*.
- **shaal (borrows) — the *borrowed thing* (22:14).** "'if a man **borrows** (shaal) anything and it is injured, he shall make restitution'" *(stated)* — shaal, *ask/borrow*: the *responsibility of the borrower* — the interior-context of *care owed for what is borrowed* *(inferred: shaal = the borrowed thing, its care owed)*.
- **natan (give) — the *bride-price for the seduced* (22:17).** *natan distinct from 22:7,10:* "'if her father refuses to **give** (natan) her, he shall pay the bride-price'" *(stated)* — here natan is *the giving in marriage* (or its price) — the *seducer bound to make right* — the interior-context of *the wronged woman's protection* *(inferred: natan = the bride-price — the seducer bound to make right)*.
- **anah (afflict) + anah (afflict) — the *widow and orphan not to be afflicted* (22:22–23).** "'you shall not **afflict** (anah) any widow or orphan; if you **afflict** (anah) them and they cry, I will surely hear'" *(stated)*. **anah** (twice) — *afflict/oppress* (the very word of *Israel's own affliction* in Egypt, 1:11–12): the gem is *the ethical memory turned to law* — *do not afflict* the powerless *as you were afflicted*; and the *conditional threat* — *if you do, and they cry, God hears*. The interior of *the powerless whose cry reaches God* — the affliction *God will not ignore* *(inferred: anah = the widow/orphan not to be afflicted — the cry God hears, the ethical memory)*.
- **charah (wrath burns) — the *divine wrath for the afflicted* (22:24).** "'my wrath will **burn** (charah), and I will kill you with the sword; your wives shall become widows'" *(stated)* — charah, *burn/be incensed*: the gem is that *God's anger burns on behalf of the powerless* — the *oppressor made to suffer what he inflicted* (his wife a widow, his children fatherless); the divine interior of *wrath as the defense of the defenseless* — *the measure returned* *(inferred: charah = the divine wrath for the afflicted — the oppressor's measure returned)*.
- **chaval (take in pledge) + channun (compassionate) — the *pledge returned, God's compassion revealed* (22:26–27).** "'if you **take** (chaval) your neighbor's cloak in pledge, return it before sunset… if he cries to me, I will hear, for I am **compassionate** (channun)'" *(stated)*. **chaval** — *take in pledge* (the *be in labour* gloss the homonym); **channun** — *gracious/compassionate*: the gem is *THE self-revelation* — the law *reveals God's own heart*: he *hears the poor man's cry* (as he heard Israel's, 2:24) *because he is COMPASSIONATE*; the divine interior *named* — *gracious, hearing, tender toward the destitute*. Even a *pledged cloak* matters to him because *he is compassionate* *(inferred: chaval/channun = the pledge returned, God's compassion revealed — "for I am compassionate")*.
- **arar (curse) — the *reverence owed to God and ruler* (22:28).** "'you shall not revile God, nor **curse** (arar) a ruler'" *(stated)* — arar, *curse*: the *reverence owed* to God and to appointed authority — the interior-context of *the tongue restrained from cursing what God has set* *(inferred: arar = the reverence owed — the curse withheld from God and ruler)*.
- **natan (give) — the *firstborn given* (22:29).** *natan distinct from 22:7,10,17:* "'the firstborn of your sons you shall **give** (natan) to me'" *(stated)* — here natan is *consecration-giving* — the *firstborn belonging to God*; the interior of *the first and best surrendered to God* *(inferred: natan = the firstborn given — the first surrendered to God)*.
- **natan (give) — the *eighth-day offering* (22:30).** *natan distinct from 22:29:* "'seven days it shall be with its mother; on the eighth day you shall **give** (natan) it to me'" *(stated)* — the *firstborn animal given* after the tender interval with its mother — the interior-context of *the offering timed with a mercy* (the days with the mother) *(inferred: natan = the eighth-day offering — given after the days with its mother)*.
- **qodesh (consecrated) + basar (flesh) — the *consecrated people* (22:31).** "'you shall be **consecrated** (qodesh) to me; you shall not eat torn **flesh** (basar)'" *(stated)*. **qodesh** — *holiness*; **basar** — *flesh*: the gem is the *identity that grounds the ethic* — *you shall be holy*, therefore *set apart even in what you eat*; the interior of *consecration shaping the whole life* *(inferred: qodesh/basar = the consecrated people — holiness shaping even the table)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **faithfulness in trust (natan/shamar 22:7 → pesha/rasha 22:9 → natan/shamar 22:10 → shaal 22:14 → natan 22:17):** what is *entrusted must be guarded*; a *breach of trust is a transgression* condemned *before God*; honesty *under oath where none saw*; the *borrower's* care; the *seducer bound to make right* — the interior of *faithfulness with what is another's*.
2. **God's heart for the powerless (anah/anah 22:22–23 → charah 22:24 → chaval/channun 22:26–27):** *do not afflict* the widow, orphan, poor (as *you were afflicted*) — for *their cry reaches God*, whose *wrath burns* in their defense and who *hears because he is COMPASSIONATE*; the law *reveals the divine interior* — *tender toward the destitute*.
3. **the consecrated life (arar 22:28 → natan 22:29 → natan 22:30 → qodesh/basar 22:31):** *reverence* to God and ruler; the *firstborn given* (the first surrendered); the offering *timed with mercy*; and the ground of it all — *you shall be holy* — consecration *shaping the whole life*.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** **natan ×5 (goods *entrusted* / beast *entrusted* / the *bride-price* / the *firstborn* given / the *eighth-day* offering)**; **shamar ×2 (the *goods* guarded / the *beast* kept under oath)**; pesha/rasha (the *breach of trust* as transgression, *condemned* before God); shaal (the *borrowed* thing); **anah ×2 (the widow/orphan not to be *afflicted* — the cry God hears, the ethical memory)**; **charah (the *divine wrath* for the afflicted — the oppressor's measure returned)**; **chaval/channun (the pledge returned, *God's compassion revealed* — "for I am compassionate")**; arar (the *reverence* owed — the curse withheld); qodesh/basar (the *consecrated people* — holiness shaping the table).
- **Whose interior (multi-interior):** **God** — *COMPASSIONATE* (channun), *hearing the cry* of the powerless, his *wrath burning* (charah) in their defense — the divine heart *revealed in the law*; **Israel** — the *ethical memory* ("you were afflicted", so do not afflict), *faithfulness* in trust, *consecration*; **the vulnerable** — the *cry* that reaches God. The gem: the law *legislates God's own inner being* — his compassion for the destitute.
- **Threads:** **the cry heard** (anah/channun 22:23,27 ← Israel's cry in Egypt, 2:23–25 "God heard their groaning"; the *same anah* of the oppression 1:11 — *do not do to others what was done to you*; God *hears* the afflicted as he heard you → "he has regard for the prayer of the destitute", Ps 102:17); **God's self-revelation as compassionate** (channun 22:27 → "the LORD, the LORD, compassionate and gracious", 34:6 — the first sounding of the great self-naming); **the ethical memory** (22:21 "you were sojourners" → "you know the heart of a sojourner", 23:9 — the *remembered affliction* the ground of mercy); **wrath for the powerless** (charah 22:24 — the divine anger *protective*, not arbitrary); **consecration** (qodesh 22:31 ← 19:6 "a holy nation" — the identity grounding the ethic); the *firstborn given* (natan 22:29 ← the Passover firstborn spared, 13:2 — the redeemed firstborn now consecrated).
- **Guarded against:** lumping the five natan (goods / beast / bride-price / firstborn / eighth-day), two shamar (goods / beast), two anah (the single *do-not-afflict*, but each occurrence its own clause — the command and the consequence); reading the vulnerable-laws as mere civil policy over the *divine heart* they reveal (God's compassion, his hearing, his wrath — the finding); missing the *anah ← Egypt* echo (the ethical memory — the finding); mistaking the 'o "desire" and chay/chaval homonym glosses for inner-being motifs; over-reading the firstborn-giving into later sacrificial theology over the *first-surrendered-to-God* the verse gives; flattening "for I am compassionate" into a legal formula when it is a *self-revelation* of God's interior — the reason the whole ethic stands.

---

## Exo EXS-09-covenant-justice-sojourner - inner-being reading

# Exodus 23:1–33 — inner-being passage reading (EXS-09-covenant-justice-sojourner)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `exodus-sinai-v1-20260705`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. **Multiple interiors**: **Israel** (impartial justice, empathy from remembered suffering, good to the enemy, the pull toward other gods), **God** (the angel, the terror, the patient dispossession). Feast/mechanical spans (the living beasts of the fallow year) read as scene-context.
- **Mis-tags flagged, not read:** 'o "desire" at 23:4 = the conjunction *"or"*. chayyah "living thing" (23:11, 23:29) = the wild beasts (scene-context).
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the 4 riv, 5 shamar, 3 avad, 3 oyev, 2 rasha, 2 shama, 2 naqi, 2 tsaddiq each treated distinctly.

---

## EXS-09-covenant-justice-sojourner · Exodus 23:1–33 · [justice from the inside; empathy from remembered suffering; good to the enemy] — "you know the heart of a sojourner"

**The passage.** No false **report** (shema) with a **wicked** (rasha) man (23:1); do not follow the many to **evil** (raah) in a **lawsuit** (riv, 23:2); not **partial** (hadar) to the poor in his **lawsuit** (riv, 23:3); bring back your **enemy's** (oyev) ox (23:4); rescue the donkey of one who **hates** (sane) you (23:5); do not pervert the **justice** (mishpat) due the poor in his **lawsuit** (riv, 23:6); do not **acquit** (tsadeq) the wicked, the **false** (sheqer) charge, the **righteous** (tsaddiq) and **innocent** (naqi ×2) not killed, the **wicked** (rasha) not acquitted (23:7); the bribe **subverts** (salaph) the **righteous** (tsaddiq, 23:8); do not oppress the sojourner — "you know his **heart** (nephesh), for you were sojourners" (23:9); the seventh-year fallow; the sabbath **rest** (nuach), the alien **refreshed** (naphash, 23:12); **attention** (shamar), no **mention** (zakhar) of other gods (23:13); **keep** (shamar) the feast (23:15); the angel to **guard** (shamar, 23:20); **obey** (shama), do not **rebel** (marar), he will not pardon **transgression** (pesha, 23:21); if you **obey** (shama), I am an enemy to your **enemies** (oyev), an adversary (ayav, 23:22); do not **serve** (avad) their gods (23:24); **serve** (avad) the LORD, I will **remove** (sur) sickness (23:25); my **terror** (emah) before you, your **enemies** (oyev) turned back (23:27); I will **give** (natan) them into your hand (23:31); make no **covenant** (berit) — **cut** (karat) none — with them (23:32); lest they make you **sin** (chata) by **serving** (avad) their gods (23:33).

### The operations, span by span (individual) — justice (23:1–9)

- **shema (report) + rasha (wicked) — the *false report refused* (23:1).** "'you shall not spread a false **report** (shema), nor join a **wicked** (rasha) man as a malicious witness'" *(stated)*. **shema** — *a report/hearing*; **rasha** — *wicked*: the interior of *the tongue refusing to carry a lie* and *the will refusing collusion with the wicked* *(inferred: shema/rasha = the false report refused, no collusion with the wicked)*.
- **raah (evil) + riv (lawsuit) — the *crowd not followed into evil* (23:2).** "'you shall not fall in with the many to do **evil** (raah), nor pervert a **lawsuit** (riv) siding with the many'" *(stated)*. **raah** — *evil*; **riv** — *dispute/suit* (← the quarreling 17:2): the gem is *justice against the crowd's pull* — the interior *refusing the herd* when the many do evil; *conscience over conformity* *(inferred: raah/riv = the crowd not followed into evil — conscience over conformity)*.
- **hadar (partial) + riv (lawsuit) — the *even the poor not favored* (23:3).** *riv distinct from 23:2:* "'nor be **partial** (hadar) to a poor man in his **lawsuit** (riv)'" *(stated)*. **hadar** — *honor/show favor*: the gem is *impartiality against sympathy* — even the *natural pity for the poor* must not *bend the judgment*; the interior of *justice so even it resists its own compassion* *(inferred: hadar/riv = even the poor not favored — impartiality against sympathy)*.
- **oyev (enemy) — the *enemy's beast recovered* (23:4).** "'if you meet your **enemy's** (oyev) ox going astray, bring it back'" *(stated)* — oyev, *enemy*: the gem is *active good to the enemy* — the interior *overcoming enmity* to *return what is his*; enmity *not licensing neglect* *(inferred: oyev = the enemy's beast recovered — good done to the enemy)*.
- **sane (hates) — the *hater's burden shared* (23:5).** "'if you see the donkey of one who **hates** (sane) you fallen, you shall rescue it with him'" *(stated)* — sane, *hate*: the gem is *the hater helped* — not only recover the beast but *labor alongside the one who hates you*; the interior *refusing to let hatred (his or yours) block mercy* *(inferred: sane = the hater's burden shared — mercy across enmity)*.
- **mishpat (justice) + riv (lawsuit) — the *poor's justice not perverted* (23:6).** *riv distinct from 23:2,3:* "'you shall not pervert the **justice** (mishpat) due your poor in his **lawsuit** (riv)'" *(stated)* — where 23:3 forbade *favoring* the poor, 23:6 forbids *denying* him justice: the gem is *the balance* — *neither favor nor deny* the poor; *justice due him as to any* — the interior of *even-handedness both ways* *(inferred: mishpat/riv = the poor's justice not perverted — the balance to 23:3)*.
- **tsadeq (acquit) + sheqer (false) + tsaddiq (righteous) + naqi (innocent ×2) + rasha (wicked) — the *innocent not condemned, the wicked not acquitted* (23:7).** "'keep far from a **false** (sheqer) charge; do not kill the **innocent** (naqi) and **righteous** (tsaddiq), for I will not **acquit** (tsadeq) the **wicked** (rasha)'" *(stated)*. **sheqer** — *falsehood*; **naqi** (twice) — *innocent*; **tsaddiq** — *righteous*; **tsadeq** — *justify/acquit*; **rasha** — *wicked*: the gem is *God's own standard* — *he will not acquit the guilty*, so neither may the judge *condemn the innocent*; the interior of *justice mirroring God's* — *the innocent shielded, the guilty unexonerated* *(inferred: the innocent not condemned, the wicked not acquitted — justice mirroring God's standard)*.
- **salaph (subverts) + tsaddiq (right) — the *bribe that blinds and subverts* (23:8).** *tsaddiq distinct from 23:7:* "'take no bribe, for a bribe blinds the clear-sighted and **subverts** (salaph) the cause of the **righteous** (tsaddiq)'" *(stated)*. **salaph** — *pervert/twist*: the gem is *the bribe's inward corruption* — it *blinds* even the clear-sighted and *twists* the righteous cause; the interior of *the gift that corrupts judgment* — *money bending the sight* *(inferred: salaph/tsaddiq = the bribe that blinds and subverts — money bending judgment)*.
- **nephesh (heart) — the *sojourner's soul known from within* (23:9).** "'you shall not oppress a sojourner; you know the **heart** (nephesh) of a sojourner, for you were sojourners in Egypt'" *(stated)* — **nephesh**, *soul/inner-self*: the gem is *THE interior turn of the justice code* — the ground of mercy is *empathy born of remembered suffering*: *you know his very soul — his inner experience — because you lived it*. The interior of *compassion grounded in shared memory* — *justice from the inside, felt not just decreed* — *"you know the nephesh of a sojourner"* *(inferred: nephesh = the sojourner's soul known from within — empathy from remembered suffering)*.

### The operations, span by span (individual) — sabbath, feasts, the angel (23:10–33)

- **nuach (rest) + naphash (refreshed) — the *rest that reaches the alien and beast* (23:12).** "'on the seventh day you shall **rest** (nuach), that your ox and the alien may be **refreshed** (naphash)'" *(stated)*. **nuach** — *rest*; **naphash** — *be refreshed / catch breath* (the verb of *nephesh*): the gem is *the sabbath's mercy reaching down* — *the servant, the alien, even the ox refreshed*; the interior-lesson that *rest is a mercy owed to the least* *(inferred: nuach/naphash = the rest reaching the alien and beast)*.
- **shamar (attention) + zakhar (mention) — the *guarded devotion, no other gods named* (23:13).** "'give **attention** (shamar) to all I said; make no **mention** (zakhar) of other gods'" *(stated)*. **shamar** — *keep/heed*; **zakhar** — *remember/mention*: the interior of *exclusive devotion* — *not even the names* of other gods on the lips *(inferred: shamar/zakhar = the guarded devotion, other gods not named)*.
- **shamar (keep) — the *feast kept* (23:15).** *shamar distinct from 23:13:* "'you shall **keep** (shamar) the Feast of Unleavened Bread… for in it you came out of Egypt'" *(stated)* — here shamar is *observance* — the *feast of the exodus kept* — the interior-context of *memory ritualized* *(inferred: shamar = the feast kept — the exodus remembered)*.
- **shamar (guard) — the *angel who guards the way* (23:20).** *shamar distinct from 23:13,15:* "'I send an angel to **guard** (shamar) you on the way'" *(stated)* — here *God's own keeping* — the interior-context of *the guarded journey, the presence going before* *(inferred: shamar = the angel who guards the way)*.
- **shama (obey) + marar (rebel) + pesha (transgression) — the *angel obeyed, not provoked* (23:21).** "'**obey** (shama) his voice; do not **rebel** (marar); he will not pardon your **transgression** (pesha), for my name is in him'" *(stated)*. **shama** — *hear/obey*; **marar** — *provoke/rebel* (bitter-root, ← Marah 15:23); **pesha** — *transgression*: the gem is *the warning against rebellion* — the angel *bears God's name* and *will not pardon* a *provoking transgression*; the interior of *the will called to obey and not embitter* *(inferred: shama/marar/pesha = the angel obeyed, not provoked — rebellion unpardoned)*.
- **shama (obey) + oyev (enemies) + ayav (hostile) — the *obedience that aligns God against your enemies* (23:22).** *shama/oyev distinct:* "'if you carefully **obey** (shama), I will be an enemy to your **enemies** (oyev) and an adversary (ayav) to your adversaries'" *(stated)*. **shama** — again *obey*; **oyev** — *enemy*; **ayav** — *be hostile*: the gem is *obedience aligning God with you* — *your enemies become his*; the interior-context of *the obedient under God's own championing* *(inferred: shama/oyev/ayav = obedience that makes God enemy to your enemies)*.
- **avad (serve) — the *idols not served* (23:24).** "'you shall not **serve** (avad) their gods nor do as they do'" *(stated)* — avad, *serve/worship*: the interior of *worship refused to idols* *(inferred: avad = the idols not served)*.
- **avad (serve) + sur (remove) — the *LORD served, sickness removed* (23:25).** *avad distinct from 23:24:* "'you shall **serve** (avad) the LORD, and he will bless your bread… I will **remove** (sur) sickness'" *(stated)*. **avad** — now *serve the LORD*; **sur** — *turn aside/remove*: the gem is the *contrast* — *serve him (not idols)*, and *blessing and health* follow; the interior of *devotion directed rightly, met with life* *(inferred: avad/sur = the LORD served, sickness removed)*.
- **emah (terror) + oyev (enemies) — the *divine terror sent ahead* (23:27).** *oyev distinct from 23:4,22:* "'I will send my **terror** (emah) before you… and make all your **enemies** (oyev) turn their backs'" *(stated)*. **emah** — *dread/terror*; **oyev** — *enemy*: the gem is *God's terror as weapon* — the *dread* he sends *unnerves the enemy* before Israel arrives; the interior (of the enemy) *broken by the sent dread* *(inferred: emah/oyev = the divine terror sent ahead — the enemy's dread)*.
- **natan (give) — the *land's inhabitants given* (23:31).** "'I will **give** (natan) the inhabitants into your hand'" *(stated)* — natan, *give*: the interior-context of *the dispossession as God's gift* — *the victory his to grant* *(inferred: natan = the inhabitants given into your hand)*.
- **berit (covenant) + karat (cut) — the *no-covenant with idols* (23:32).** "'you shall **cut** (karat) no **covenant** (berit) with them or their gods'" *(stated)*. **berit** — *covenant*; **karat** — *cut* (the covenant-making verb): the interior of *no binding to what would corrupt* — *the covenant with God exclusive* *(inferred: berit/karat = no covenant cut with idols)*.
- **chata (sin) + avad (serve) — the *snare of idol-service* (23:33).** *avad distinct from 23:24,25:* "'lest they make you **sin** (chata) against me; if you **serve** (avad) their gods it will be a snare'" *(stated)*. **chata** — *sin*; **avad** — *serve*: the gem is *the snare named* — *dwelling with idolaters* would *draw the heart to serve their gods and sin*; the interior of *the corruptible will guarded by separation* *(inferred: chata/avad = the snare of idol-service — the will guarded by separation)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **justice from the inside (shema/rasha 23:1 → raah/riv 23:2 → hadar/riv 23:3 → oyev 23:4 → sane 23:5 → mishpat/riv 23:6 → tsadeq… 23:7 → salaph 23:8 → nephesh 23:9):** the tongue *refuses the lie*, the will *refuses the crowd*, judgment *bends neither to the poor's pity nor against him*, *good is done to the enemy* (his beast, his burden), the *innocent shielded and the guilty unexonerated* (mirroring God), the *bribe's corruption refused* — and the *ground of it all*: *"you know the heart of a sojourner"* — *empathy from remembered suffering*, justice *felt from the inside*.
2. **the mercy of rest (nuach/naphash 23:12 → shamar/zakhar 23:13 → shamar 23:15):** the sabbath *refreshes even the alien and the ox*; *exclusive devotion* (no other gods named); the *feast of the exodus kept* — mercy and memory joined.
3. **the angel and the guarded heart (shamar 23:20 → shama/marar/pesha 23:21 → shama/oyev/ayav 23:22 → avad 23:24 → avad/sur 23:25 → emah/oyev 23:27 → natan 23:31 → berit/karat 23:32 → chata/avad 23:33):** the *angel guards the way*, to be *obeyed not provoked*; obedience *aligns God against your enemies*; *idols not served*, the *LORD served* (met with blessing); God's *terror* sent ahead; the land *given*; *no covenant with idols* — lest they *snare the heart to sin*; the interior of *the guarded, obedient will*.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** shema/rasha (the *false report* refused); **riv ×4 (the *lawsuit* — crowd not followed / poor not favored / poor's justice not denied / — the balance both ways)**; hadar (the *favor* withheld even from the poor); **oyev ×3 (the *enemy's* beast recovered / God *enemy* to your enemies / the *enemies* turned back by terror)**; sane (the *hater's* burden shared); mishpat (the *justice* due the poor); tsadeq/sheqer/tsaddiq/naqi/rasha (the *innocent* shielded, the *wicked* not acquitted — God's standard); salaph/tsaddiq (the *bribe* that subverts); **nephesh (the *sojourner's soul* known from within — empathy from remembered suffering)**; nuach/naphash (the *rest* reaching the alien and beast); **shamar ×5 (the *attention* / the *feast* kept / the angel's *guard* / the *careful* heed / — the angel obeyed)**; zakhar (other gods not *named*); **shama ×2 (the angel *obeyed* / the *obedience* that aligns God)**; marar/pesha (the angel not *provoked*); **avad ×3 (idols not *served* / the LORD *served* / the *snare* of idol-service)**; sur (sickness *removed*); emah (the divine *terror* sent ahead); natan (the inhabitants *given*); berit/karat (no *covenant* with idols); chata (the *sin* the snare would bring).
- **Whose interior (multi-interior):** **Israel** — *impartial justice* (unswayed by crowd, pity, or bribe), *empathy from remembered suffering* ("you know the sojourner's soul"), *good to the enemy* (his beast, his burden), and the *guarded, obedient will* (against the idol-snare); **God** — the *angel who guards*, the *terror sent ahead*, the *patient dispossession* (little by little), *enemy to your enemies*; **the enemy** — the *dread* that breaks him. The gem: justice *grounded in empathy born of Israel's own affliction* — the ethical memory made *interior*.
- **Threads:** **the ethical memory made interior** (nephesh 23:9 ← "you were sojourners" 22:21; the *anah* of Egypt 1:11; God *knew* their nephesh 2:25 — now *you know* the sojourner's nephesh → "love the sojourner, for you were sojourners", Deut 10:19); **good to the enemy** (oyev/sane 23:4–5 → "if your enemy is hungry, feed him", Prov 25:21; "love your enemies", Mt 5:44 — the proto-form here); **impartial justice** (hadar/mishpat 23:3,6 → "you shall not be partial", Deut 1:17; Lev 19:15 — neither favor nor deny → the blind-justice ideal); **the bribe** (salaph 23:8 ← Jethro's judges who *hate* a bribe 18:21 — the corruption of sight); **the fear/terror motif** (emah 23:27 ← the trembling at Sinai 19:16; the dread on Canaan → Rahab "our hearts melted" Josh 2:11); **rebellion** (marar 23:21 ← the bitter Marah 15:23; the murmurings — the embittered will → the wilderness rebellions).
- **Guarded against:** lumping the four riv (three distinct lawsuit-clauses, each its own angle — favor / deny / crowd), five shamar (attention / feast / guard / careful / heed), three avad (idols / LORD / snare), three oyev; reading the justice-code as external rule over the *empathy* that grounds it (the sojourner's *nephesh* known from within — the finding); missing the *balance* between 23:3 (don't favor the poor) and 23:6 (don't deny him) — *even-handedness both ways*; mistaking the 'o "desire" and chayyah "beasts" for inner-being motifs; over-reading "love your enemy" back into 23:4–5 beyond the *active good to the enemy* the verses state (the proto-form, not the full teaching); flattening the angel-warning (marar 23:21) into ceremony over the *will called not to embitter/rebel*.

---

## Exo EXS-10-covenant-ratified - inner-being reading

# Exodus 24:1–18 — inner-being passage reading (EXS-10-covenant-ratified)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `exodus-sinai-v1-20260705`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. **Multiple interiors**: **Israel** (the wholehearted covenant assent, the elders' vision), **Moses** (called into the glory), **God** (the glory as devouring fire, yet the vision permitted). The people's "all we will do" (24:3, anchored by mishpat) and the elders eating and drinking (24:11, no non-T2 span) read as scene-context.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the 2 berit, 2 qara, 2 kavod, 2 tohar each treated distinctly.

---

## EXS-10-covenant-ratified · Exodus 24:1–18 · [the covenant sworn and sealed; the vision of God; Moses into the glory] — "we will do and be obedient", the blood, and the pavement of clearness

**The passage.** Moses told the people the **rules** (mishpat, 24:3); read the Book of the **Covenant** (berit) — "all the LORD has spoken we will do and be **obedient** (shama)" (24:7, the **reading** qara); "the blood of the **covenant** (berit) the LORD has **cut** (karat)" (24:8); the elders saw God, under his feet sapphire like heaven for **clearness** (tohar ×2, 24:10); they beheld God, ate and drank (24:11); "I will **give** (natan) you the tablets" (24:12); the **glory** (kavod) dwelt, the cloud six days, the seventh he **called** (qara, 24:16); the **glory** (kavod) like devouring fire (24:17); Moses into the cloud forty days (24:18).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **mishpat (rules) — the *rules laid before the people* (24:3).** "Moses told the people all the words and all the **rules** (mishpat); they answered, 'all we will do'" *(stated)* — mishpat, *ordinances* (← the covenant code 21:1): the *statutes set before them for assent* — the interior-context of *the people hearing the whole covenant before answering* *(inferred: mishpat = the rules laid before the people for assent)*.
- **berit (covenant) + qara (read) + shama (obedient) — the *wholehearted assent* (24:7).** "he **read** (qara) the Book of the **Covenant** (berit) in their hearing; they said, 'all the LORD has spoken we will do and be **obedient** (shama)'" *(stated)*. **berit** — *covenant*; **qara** — *read out/proclaim*; **shama** — *hear/obey*: the gem is *the covenant assent at its fullest* — *"we will do AND be obedient"* — the people bind themselves *before* fully knowing, *doing* set even beside *hearing*; the interior of *wholehearted covenant commitment* — *a people saying yes with one voice* *(inferred: berit/qara/shama = the wholehearted assent — "we will do and be obedient")*.
- **berit (covenant) + karat (cut) — the *covenant sealed in blood* (24:8).** *berit distinct from 24:7:* "Moses threw the blood on the people: 'behold the blood of the **covenant** (berit) the LORD has **cut** (karat) with you'" *(stated)*. **berit** — now the *covenant enacted* (where 24:7 was the *words assented*, 24:8 is the *blood that seals*); **karat** — *cut* (the covenant-making verb): the gem is *the binding made blood-deep* — the covenant *not merely agreed but sealed*, the blood *thrown on the people* joining them to God's words; the interior-context of *commitment bound in blood — the covenant made irrevocable* *(inferred: berit/karat = the covenant sealed in blood — the binding made irrevocable)*.
- **tohar (clearness) + tohar (clearness) — the *vision of God in purity* (24:10).** "they saw the God of Israel; under his feet a pavement of sapphire, like heaven for **clearness** (tohar ×2)" *(stated)* — **tohar**, *purity/clearness* (both spans): the gem is *the vision granted* — the elders *see God* (the unthinkable), and what they see beneath him is *clarity, purity, brightness like heaven*; the interior of *awe before the pure vision* — *the dread of Sinai now opened into sight*; and (24:11) *"he did not lay his hand on them"* — *they see God and live, and eat and drink* — the *dread turned to communion*; the interior *permitted to behold and not be consumed* *(inferred: tohar = the vision of God in purity — the dread turned to communion, seeing God and living)*.
- **natan (give) — the *tablets to be given* (24:12).** "'come up… that I may **give** (natan) you the tablets, the law and commandment I have written'" *(stated)* — natan, *give*: the *covenant words to be given in stone* — the interior-context of *the law about to be handed down, written by God* *(inferred: natan = the tablets to be given)*.
- **kavod (glory) + qara (called) — the *glory dwelling, Moses called* (24:16).** *qara distinct from 24:7:* "the **glory** (kavod) of the LORD dwelt on Sinai; the cloud six days; the seventh he **called** (qara) Moses out of the midst" *(stated)*. **kavod** — *glory*; **qara** — now *summon* (where 24:7 was *reading aloud*, here God *calls* Moses): the gem is *the glory settling and the mediator summoned* — the *kavod dwells*, and after six days' waiting *Moses is called into it*; the interior-context of *the glory-presence and the call into it* *(inferred: kavod/qara = the glory dwelling, Moses called into it)*.
- **kavod (glory) — the *glory as devouring fire* (24:17).** *kavod distinct from 24:16:* "the appearance of the **glory** (kavod) was like a devouring fire on the top, in the sight of Israel" *(stated)* — where 24:16 was the *glory dwelling*, 24:17 names its *appearance* — *devouring fire*: the gem is *the terrible beauty of the glory* — *seen by all Israel* as *consuming fire*; the interior-context of *the glory that is both dwelling-presence and devouring fire* — *the awe held with the nearness* *(inferred: kavod = the glory as devouring fire — the terrible presence seen by all)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the covenant sworn and sealed (mishpat 24:3 → berit/qara/shama 24:7 → berit/karat 24:8):** the *rules laid before them*, the *wholehearted assent* ("we will do and be obedient"), and the *covenant sealed in blood* thrown on the people — the interior of *a people binding themselves to God, the commitment made blood-deep*.
2. **the vision and the communion (tohar 24:10 → [ate and drank 24:11]):** the elders *see God* in *clarity and purity*, and — *not struck down* — *eat and drink* in his presence; the *dread of Sinai opened into communion*; the interior *permitted to behold and live*.
3. **into the glory (natan 24:12 → kavod/qara 24:16 → kavod 24:17 → [forty days 24:18]):** the *tablets to be given*, the *glory dwelling* and *Moses called into it*, the glory *like devouring fire* seen by all — the mediator *entering the cloud* for forty days; the interior of *the mediator drawn into the terrible glory*.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** mishpat (the *rules* laid before the people); **berit ×2 (the covenant *assented* / the covenant *sealed in blood*)**; **qara ×2 (the covenant *read out* / Moses *called* into the glory)**; **shama (the *wholehearted assent* — "we will do and be obedient")**; **karat (the covenant *cut* — sealed irrevocable)**; **tohar ×2 (the vision of God in *clearness/purity* — the dread turned to communion)**; natan (the *tablets* to be given); **kavod ×2 (the glory *dwelling* / the glory as *devouring fire*)**.
- **Whose interior (multi-interior):** **Israel** — the *wholehearted covenant assent* (one voice, "we will do and be obedient"), and the elders' *vision-and-communion* (they see God, eat and drink, live); **Moses** — *called into the glory* (the mediator drawn into the devouring fire, forty days); **God** — the *glory* (dwelling-presence and devouring fire), yet *does not lay his hand* on the elders (the vision *permitted*, mercy in the beholding). The gems: the *covenant assent*, the *blood-sealed binding*, and the *dread-turned-to-communion* in the vision.
- **Threads:** **the covenant assent** (shama 24:7 ← "all we will do" 19:8; the offer 19:5 → the golden-calf breaking of this very vow, 32 — the *"we will do"* soon broken; the tragedy foreshadowed); **the blood of the covenant** (berit/karat 24:8 ← the Abrahamic covenant-cutting Gen 15:10,17; the Passover blood 12 → "this is my blood of the covenant", Mt 26:28 — the blood-sealed binding); **the vision of God** (tohar 24:10 ← "no one may see me and live" 33:20 — yet here the elders *see and live*, the exception of grace; → the beatific vision); **the glory** (kavod 24:16–17 ← the glory answering the grumbling 16:7,10; the glory to fill the tabernacle 40:34 — the *dwelling* glory → "we beheld his glory", Jn 1:14); **the dread turned to communion** (24:11 "he did not lay his hand… they ate and drank" — the fear of Sinai 19:16 now *opened into fellowship*, the covenant meal).
- **Guarded against:** lumping the two berit (assented / sealed), two qara (read / called), two kavod (dwelling / fire), the two tohar spans; reading the covenant assent as mere formality over the *wholehearted "we will do and be obedient"* the text gives (and its tragic weight — soon broken); flattening the vision (24:10–11) into symbol over the *seeing-God-and-living* the verses state (the *dread turned to communion* — the finding); importing NT eucharistic theology onto "the blood of the covenant" over the *blood-sealed binding* the verse enacts (though the resonance is real); over-reading the sapphire-pavement into cosmology over the *clearness/purity* seen; missing that the glory is *both* dwelling-presence *and* devouring fire (the awe held with the nearness — not resolved to one).

---
